title: Ricochet
description: Lindsey Jordan’s third LP of grungy, dreamy guitar rock aims for the same affective highs and lows of her previous records, but the hooks don’t sink as deep, and the production sounds frustratingly anonymous.

title: Whole World as Vigil
description: The singer and producer’s second album embraces grandiose pop balladry, which still means it’s full of unpredictable production choices and lyrics on the edge of comprehension.

title: Consecrated Abysses of Dread
description: The Italian experimentalist goes absolutely haywire on a very overwhelming, very fun half-hour of ecstatic avant metal.

title: High Cube
description: Working with strict limitations—no more than five instruments; just one hour to make each track—the two West Coast leftfield vets turn out a surprisingly expansive set of wooly electronic jams.

title: Full Moon
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we look back at Brandy’s futuristic, full-hearted 2002 record, an album so lush and expertly crafted that it became the new blueprint for the pop-R&B sound.

title: Honora
description: The Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist reignited his childhood love of the trumpet to make his first solo album: a mature, sophisticated collection of songs featuring stars of the L.A. jazz scene.

title: Sexistential
description: Robyn sounds right at home on a kooky new album that refines the luminous synth palpitations of Body Talk to explore sexuality, sentimentality, and the creation of life.

title: Creature of Habit
description: With a guest appearance from Waxahatchee and production from John Congleton, the latest from the Australian singer-songwriter gently furthers her career-long search for inner peace.

title: A Certain Smile, A Certain Sadness
description: The American band’s 1996 debut spun indie pop gold from heartache and secondhand Hammond organ. A new 30th-anniversary reissue can hardly do much to improve it.

title: Silent Way
description: On his first album for his own Plastic & Sounds label, the Japanese producer sounds pricklier than ever, lacing hypnotic house and techno with microtonal dissonance and clashing textures.

title: An Undying Love for a Burning World
description: On their surprise-released first album in 10 years, the psychedelic Bay Area metal veterans launch a vital and affirming second act with new vocalist Aaron Turner.

title: Is This All There Is? EP
description: Iggy Pop, Laurie Anderson, Perfume Genius, and Matt Berninger guest on the UK singer-songwriter’s latest EP, a moody grab bag of original songs and covers of Kraftwerk and Bonnie “Prince” Billy.

title: Beetle
description: On PC Music’s first release of new material since 2023, the North Carolina-based DJ and producer fuses the caustic energy of digital experimentalism with the raucous spirit of club music.

title: 97 EP
description: The Franco-Chilean conscious hip-hop icon reunites with collaborator DJ Dacel for a mixtape-inspired EP celebrating friendship and resilience.

title: i sure am getting sick of this bowling alley
description: On a new mini-album, the reunited Welsh noise-rock trio returns with berserk energy, jagged one-liners, and a surprisingly moving reflection on fatherhood.

title: Needle Guy EP
description: On his first solo release in eight years, 100 gecs’ mutant-pop prankster turns his attention to relatively straightforward big-tent EDM—but not without a little noise-scene provocation.

title: Dying Is the Internet
description: The French producer and the Egyptian singer and trumpeter reunite for a heavy, heady collaborative album with burnt-out 808s and a powerfully labyrinthine effect.

title: I know you’re hurting, everyone is hurting, everyone is trying, you have got to try
description: Earnest and intersectional, the spoken word artist’s debut solo album seizes upon the power of club music to preach about gender equality, personal transformation, and communal uplift.

title: ARIRANG
description: There’s a lot riding on the sensational K-pop group’s first album in four years, but its generic songs ring hollow and lack the vim and vigor of the band’s best work.

title: I Guess U Had to Be There
description: The adventurous rapper and producer take a more refined approach on a collaborative album full of wandering thoughts and odd, understated beats.

title: Runoff
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter considers new beginnings and emotional overload on an album of clean-lined folk rock crosscut with carefully chosen field recordings.

title: Assumption
description: Musician Dan Shaw and his bandmates continue to refine their jittery post-punk on the group’s fifth album, adding welcome spaciousness to their studied precision.

title: U
description: The former electro-pop enfant terrible swings big on her latest album, compressing all her split personalities and eclectic tastes into a high-gloss, high-stakes gamble to remake pop on her own terms.

title: sentence structure in the country
description: The experimental musician brings her treated vocals to the forefront on a poignant set that merges country and folk idioms with sputtering electronic production.

title: Blumenfantasie
description: The UK producer pairs two longstanding obsessions—breakneck-tempo drum’n’bass and ethereal European synthesizer music—to strike a balance between frenzied rhythms and eerie, atmospheric melodies.

artist: Whitney Johnson / Lia Kohl / Macie Stewart
title: BODY SOUND
description: Blending cello, viola, violin, voice, and manual tape processing, the Chicago trio reaffirms the pleasure of collective music-making in contemplative improvisations that are both patient and restorative.

title: Straight From the Heart
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we look back at the 1982 breakthrough from a California pianist and songwriter whose effortless fusion of R&B, disco, and jazz defied any attempts to pin her down.

title: Written Into Changes
description: On an album of spectral love songs, the DJ and producer’s misty dream pop feels bigger, bolder, and decidedly grown-up.

title: Girlfriend
description: The reigning champ of indie pop returns with a razor-sharp, refreshingly self-serious album that plays like a travelogue from disarray to recovery.

title: The Way I Am
description: Balanced between ballads and sports-bar anthems, the country singer’s sixth studio album delivers classic stories in a familiar fashion, occasionally accented by modern flourishes.

title: No Need to Be Lonely
description: Produced by Jeff Rosenstock, the new album from ex-Cayetana songwriter Augusta Koch revisits her old band’s punky power-pop with hard-hitting lyrics about self-improvement and communal uplift.

title: You’re Free to Go
description: The singer-songwriter finds emotional and creative rejuvenation on his third album, exploring vast emotional territory within conventional song structures.

title: in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music
description: The Brooklyn psych-folk artist’s 2025 debut, newly reissued by AD 93, is dissonant, ghostly, and otherworldly, summoning complex emotions with sparse tools.

title: Free Spirits
description: The Argentine duo shot to fame fueled by hooky songs and gonzo provocations. On their new album—a madcap blend of Latin pop, trance beats, and globe-trotting sampledelia—they commit fully to the bit.

title: KHAZNA
description: Sega Bodega’s new duo with singer Mayah Alkhateri takes a familiar sound, shoegaze, and refracts it through Arabic-language singing and ultra-modern club pop, to gorgeously unexpected effect.

title: BabyGoated EP
description: The London-via-Paris jazz artist embraces her neo-soul leanings and experimental impulses on an EP that explores the pleasures and perils of gassing yourself up.

title: HELP(2)
description: Thirty-one years after War Child’s first charity compilation, the nonprofit recruits a roomful of heavy hitters—Arctic Monkeys, Big Thief, Olivia Rodrigo—to raise money for kids in war-torn countries.

title: Half Blood (BloodLuxe)
description: On an expanded edition of his 2025 release, the 18-year-old Philadelphia rapper makes maximalist, crowd-pleasing rage rap that prioritizes craft over feeling.

title: How to Make a Breakfast
description: The Cuba-based band’s second album is a fusion of grunge, post-hardcore, and shoegaze that pays homage to the past without succumbing to pastiche.

title: The Weight EP
description: On its debut EP, the Louisiana quartet clouds the familiar sounds of off-kilter alt-rock with layers of static and distortion, pairing moments of euphoria with squealing dissonance.

title: Monica
description: Jack Harlow’s sexless new album demonstrates a fundamental misunderstanding of neo-soul. His coffee shop crooning is a transparent exercise in personal rebranding.

title: Extra Stars
description: The SML guitarist slides among instruments, modes, and moods on his restlessly inquisitive new solo album.
On a low-stakes follow-up to last year’s Forever, the London duo continues its evolution from wubby electroclash to toylike pop ditties and microwaved lullabies.

title: Megacity Madness (The Official Live Recordings)
description: The Toronto punks’ vinyl-only live album documents a unique hometown “tour” that took them to a range of venues throughout the city, capturing the communal catharsis at the heart of the band’s appeal.

title: Midnight Zone (Original Soundtrack)
description: On the soundtrack for a film that follows a lighthouse lens deep into the ocean, the producer’s lightless, airless drones capture the vertiginous feeling of endless freefall.

title: Hard Hearted Woman
description: The Canadian songwriter draws from gothic Americana, psychedelic folk, and ghostly bluegrass on an album of hypnotic ballads that land like incantations.

title: Music in Continuous Motion
description: Building on the approach of 2022’s Music for Four Guitars, the experimental guitarist spins time-bending drones from minimalist, melodic phrases.

title: Kyriemo Irving
description: Full of hungry day-in-the-life raps and light on gimmicks, the Philly drill rapper’s new mixtape makes a strong statement in an impossibly complicated scene.

title: I Could Live in Hope
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the epiphanic debut album from the Duluth slowcore band whose fragile, insistent sound was entirely its own from the beginning.

title: Paris in the Spring
description: On his seventh solo album, the British singer-songwriter pairs a grab bag of styles—synth-pop balladry, deep house, a Rolling Stones cover—with clearheaded lyrical introspection.

title: PLAY ME
description: Kim Gordon’s third solo album is the most populist and literalist music of her career. Her sharp style and wit remain, but absurdity and ambiguity are missed.

title: Lateral
description: The Dutch-Italian musician pays tribute to classic dub techno and leftfield ambient music on a 3xLP of ruminative rhythms and sumptuous tone colors.

title: early life crisis
description: The teen phenom’s new album faceplants with reheated rage production, Cartispeak, and faux pain rap that never quite becomes his own.

title: Exuvie
description: Finding inspiration in ancient warfare and molting insects, the pianist and sound artist dissects her influences with abandon, rendering classical forms in a visceral, digitally mangled smear.

title: Trying Times
description: On his first self-released album, the producer and songwriter draws from pop music and classic R&B for a pleasantly all-over-the-place set about love and existential dread.

title: Of the Earth
description: The jazz polymath wrote, played, produced, and mixed everything on his new solo album, weaving overlapping loops and knotty counterpoints into a dynamic suite of interconnected pieces.

title: Strictly 4 the Scythe
description: The debut mixtape from Denzel Curry’s new supergroup doesn’t quite cohere into something greater than the sum of its parts, but still offers plenty of low-stakes, high-energy fun.

title: star scum city
description: On a melodic, trance-inspired hyperpop Eurotrip, two shirtless twunk heartthrobs and co-producer Ninajirachi go searching for ecstasy.

title: Mutiny After Midnight
description: The outrageous and funky new album from the artist formerly known as Sturgill Simpson raises a simple question: What if we could fuck our way to a better world?

title: A Rush to Nowhere
description: The Los Angeles singer-songwriter’s second album is bolder and darker than her debut, refining her fusion of folk and R&B as she explores the expressive potential of her voice.

title: a short history of decay
description: Nothing are natural leaders in a revitalized shoegaze scene, but their new album is more reminiscent of its past. It works, but anyone who’s heard Loveless knows that it’s always worked.

title: Somersaults
description: On their third album, the brooding Londoners downsize their post-rock ambitions, packing lifetimes of sorrow into sharper, more conventional indie-rock songs.

title: Make-Up Is a Lie
description: The singer’s 14th album shows signs of progress and signs of regression, artful touches and leaden songwriting—it’s a new Morrissey album.

title: IOWA
description: The composer and producer casts a bleary eye upon the American Midwest on a chilling, starkly beautiful ambient album written as an homage to Bruce Springsteen’s Nebraska.

artist: The Thinking of the World Began Pounding in Our Ears the Moment We Hit Shore
title: The Thinking of the World Began Pounding in Our Ears the Moment We Hit Shore
description: Sculpted from years of collaborative sessions, the latest album from producer Florian T M Zeisig is a drifting patchwork inspired by rock music but structured like a beat tape.

title: El Niño Bola
description: The half-dissolved, Bluntian instrumentals on the Spanish singer-songwriter and Rusia-IDK affiliate’s debut hover between genuine melancholia and slog-pop demo tape.

title: Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.
description: The decaf dance-pop on Harry Styles’ fourth album is just unremarkable. Even songs about the emptiness of pop stardom succumb to tasteful restraint.

title: BIG MAMA
description: In between all his audiovisual extracurriculars, the L.A. producer found time to make a 13-minute EP of frenzied Game Boy funk that still manages to overstay its welcome.

title: Heaven 2
description: Whispered drama and propulsive synth-pop provide cover for modern anxieties on the songwriter’s new album, co-produced with Jay Som’s Melina Duterte.

title: Something We All Got
description: The Toronto indie-pop band cleans up (but not too much) for its first studio-quality album.

title: Dare Iz a Darkside
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the New Jersey rap icon’s paranoid, insular, largely self-produced 1994 album, an East Coast G-funk classic under the influence.

title: TRON Ares: Divergence
description: Arca, Danny L Harle, the Dare, and more take on Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross’ 2025 Disney score for the first NIN remix album that actually improves upon the original.

title: Live at Third Man Records
description: A new live album captures the four New Yorkers on the precipice of fame, finding their sea legs while performing material from their breakthrough 2025 album just ahead of its release.

title: In My Dreams
description: Released just before his 75th birthday and featuring five of his longtime bandmates, the jazz guitarist’s latest album takes stock of a life spent gently probing the limits of his instrument.

title: Autechre Guitar
description: In an improbable feat of dexterity, the American fingerstyle guitarist interprets the work of the UK electronic savants, finding graceful new forms in their brain-bending tangles.

title: Dreamers in Exile
description: After more than a decade on hiatus, the blog-era indie-pop band reunites for a cathartic, mature comeback record that sounds like a big-dreaming debut.

title: The Pleasure Is Yours
description: The singer and percussionist team up for an album of cosmic experimentalism and amorphous funk. Their collaborative debut has improvisational spirit and real feeling.

title: Nondi…
description: Pennsylvania producer Tatiana Triplin’s lo-fi, loop-centric approach to footwork makes her second album feel like a dreamy memory of the promise of digital connection.

title: My Name
description: The Birmingham rapper meditates on identity and working-class British culture on his latest album, finding inspiration in soulfully psychedelic beats and diaristic verses.

title: Rockie
description: The New York songwriter steps into the role of a despondent femme fatale on her debut album, an unassuming collection of indie-pop songs with the aura of a vintage cult classic.

title: TIGRAY FUNK
description: The Tigray-born, DMV-raised rapper’s latest album is a dazed survey of personal highs and lows, his stream-of-consciousness flow riding roughshod over his producers’ strangest beats.

title: DEADLINE EP
description: BLACKPINK aim to re-establish group domination on a five-song EP that incorporates K-pop’s trending electronic dance influence with help from Chris Martin, Diplo, and Dr. Luke.

title: Highway to Heavenly
description: The indie-pop cult icons return with their first new record in three decades, delivering expectedly sweet and sticky melodies while highlighting the emotional depth beneath their twee exterior.

title: Contra Madre
description: This posthumous album of free improv pairs the late pedal steel virtuoso with a metal-adjacent guitar-and-drums duo, to bracing, gravity-defying effect.

title: The Romantic
description: The nine songs on the pop showman’s first album in a decade are sleek and professional, but are so risk-averse that they mostly just sound like other, more well-known songs.

title: wonderful
description: The innovative rapper comes up way short with a record that lacks fun or curiosity. Most of these songs are fried, one-note, and tailored for Rolling Loud.

title: Silent Century
description: The singer-songwriter’s second album spotlights her wayward, darting mind and steadily droning guitar, with help from a constellation of fellow indie rockers from New York City and the Hudson Valley.

title: Designer Junkie
description: The Atlanta rapper tightens his wild experimentation on an album that spotlights his increasingly distinct voice.

title: My Days of 58
description: The once guarded singer-songwriter continues to open up on his latest album, reckoning with fatherhood, mortality, and his artistic vocation in revealing and uncharacteristically playful ways.

title: At Source
description: The Italian synthesist and the Norwegian saxophonist meld minds on their first collaborative release, finding common ground in the spatial qualities of their respective instruments.

title: Hen’s Teeth
description: A gentle companion album to Light Verse glows in the warmth of Sam Beam’s musical collective, featuring veteran collaborators, folk trio I’m With Her, and daughter Arden Beam.

title: Marathon
description: In the face of the mounting omnicrisis, the songwriter crafts threadbare folk songs marked by exhaustion, resignation, and uncommon beauty.

title: Justified
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a 2002 debut that launched a whole cultural phenomenon by borrowing the hottest R&B moves of the day to mint a shiny new pop star.

title: Andrew Bird & the Mysterious Production of Eggs (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: A 20th-anniversary reissue honors the years-long process of creating the quirky, masterful record and finds new freedom in its songs, packaging them with demos, live recordings, rarities, and a book.

title: The Mountain
description: The animated band’s ninth album gathers collaborators both living and departed for a characteristically audacious monument to grief, India, and archival memory.

title: The Mirror
description: The Big Thief guitarist lightly updates his solo sound, but he still fares best as a traditional country-rock troubadour.

title: Sub Zero
description: As the Bug, the UK producer has made some of the weightiest dub and dancehall ever committed to tape. But this reissued LP of oppressively wintry dark ambient is just as heavy.

title: The Great Satan
description: Reuniting with some old collaborators, the horror legend crafts a spiritual sequel to 1998’s Hellbilly Deluxe—but this time, the demon is speeding on cruise control.

title: Nothing’s About to Happen to Me
description: Mitski’s homebound eighth album is both theatrical and restrained, responding to her newfound visibility with sober reflections on loneliness and delusion.

title: folx
description: On a sprawling, 112-track treatise, the semi-anonymous samplers hide a compelling statement in a clusterfuck weighed down by conflicting ambitions.

title: Street Druid
description: The London saxophonist’s singular sound seems to create its own windy weather. His new album charts a strange course from synth ambiance to industrial-grade sub-bass.

title: The Refrigerator
description: The indie-punk band expands into softer palettes and slower tempos on an album that captures the restlessness and newfound wisdom of being in your late 20s.

title: Still Right Here
description: The Maryland rapper taps some of SoundCloud’s coolest producers for a full-length solo debut of atmospheric, cybernetic avant-trap. His punch-ins fill more pockets than a tactical vest.

title: Days of Ash EP
description: Breaking a long creative rut, the group returns with an EP of well-intentioned protest music: six topical songs about global injustice, plus a 54-page zine (and an Ed Sheeran cameo).

title: No Lube So Rude
description: Pearl clutchers beware: The electro-punk icon’s first album in a decade revels in raunch—as good dirty fun, but also as a celebration of human desires, human needs, and human rights.

title: Everywhere Isn’t Texas
description: On their debut album, the Texas-born, Brooklyn-based songwriter indulges both their silliness and their sentimentality alongside cozy, straightforward production.

title: Ca$ino
description: Keem reflects on his journey with a semi-autobiographical new album, but his performances lack spark and his warring pop star and rapper sensibilities work against him.

title: petal rock black
description: On a self-produced new album, the 25-year-old artist continues her restless journey into unmemorable experimentation but fares best in the subtle moments.

title: Cloud 9
description: As her star power grows, the Georgia country songwriter brings her charmingly self-aware narratives to broader stages.

title: Blasé Saint
description: The Seattle-based producer fills her debut album with staticky textures and bottomless reverb, rearranging familiar elements of dub techno, ambient, drum’n’bass, and hip-hop to transportive effect.

title: Blame the Clown
description: The New Orleans punk duo channels American country and folk music for a raw, righteous, and impressively original sound. Their second record is Southern garage rock at its best.

title: Da Realest
description: Formerly a beacon of relative calm among his hometown’s more gonzo street rappers, the Flint upstart packs his latest album with more jokes, quirks, and personality than ever before.

title: Evaporator
description: The UK producer perfected his leftfield electronic fusion years ago, and he sticks with it on his seventh album. But his melodic gifts make otherwise familiar sounds worth coming back to.

title: ALL MONSTERS
description: On its second album, the Brooklyn-based band brings a sense of humor and a spirit of community to grungy, shoegaze-inflected songs about self-destruction and maladaptation.

title: Erotica
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Madonna’s sensuous fifth album, an intimate and conflicted record that was all too easily overshadowed by controversy.

title: Kin
description: The prolific Kenyan artist’s latest release feels like a companion to his 2020 breakout. Here, the tracks’ inner complexity simmers beneath gravelly, overdriven textures.

title: luck… or something
description: On her first album since 2015, the Lizzie McGuire actress cowrites and collaborates with her husband on fizzy, centrist pop from the crossroads of autobiography and universality.

title: Prizefighter
description: The folk trio returns with producer Aaron Dessner, guest vocalists including Justin Vernon and Gracie Abrams, and newly vulnerable songwriting. But is it enough to make a comeback?

title: Beautiful Disaster
description: The New York BFFs make blingy electroclash and giddy EDM inspired by online brainrot and good ol’ fashioned blackouts.

title: Dedication
description: The veteran songwriter’s first record in seven years is a wistful account of motherhood, gratitude, and grief. Its unabashed earnestness is its greatest strength.

title: Wuthering Heights
description: On an adventurous soundtrack for the blockbuster film, Charli aims for brutal elegance, transporting herself from strobe-lit arenas to the wily, windy moors.

title: Icon
description: The R&B singer pivots from clubrat deviance to domestic devotion. When he leans into the honesty and specificity of his player music, he makes love feel like more than just a catalyst for a rebrand.

title: Deface the Currency
description: On their second album together, the post-punk trio and post-bop saxophonist display a newfound chemistry distilled across extensive touring together, harnessing a driving and invigorating sound.

title: Euphonic Sounds
description: The L.A. duo does for ragtime what Wendy Carlos’ Switched-On Bach did for Baroque, reimagining the century-old sound for synths and V-drums. It’s a zippily heartfelt take on a vaudeville staple.

title: To Whom This May Concern
description: On her first album in over 10 years, the R&B icon sings about setbacks, redemption, and Black joy while paying little mind to public approval.

title: Weekend Rockstar
description: The 19-year-old rapper ditches dreary London, and with it, the nuance that made him interesting.

title: Guitars Infernal
description: The New Zealand guitarist recorded these abrasive instrumentals a decade ago in response to personal turmoil. Dedicated now to our endangered planet, they feel as urgent now as they must have then.

title: Seeing Is Forgetting
description: The minimalist composer and jazz saxophonist collaborate for an improvisational album that thrives on melodic structure and ephemeral chemistry.

title: Laughter in Summer
description: The Canadian composer celebrates life, love, and community on a career-spanning 2024 performance after his diagnosis with dementia.

title: And So It Is
description: Composed in the wake of a harrowing medical diagnosis, the Los Angeles saxophonist’s debut album toggles between serenity and psychedelia, aided by an array of West Coast jazz heavyweights.

title: Necropalace
description: With a new focus on melody and epic scene-setting, the Florida metal band goes all in on symphonic black metal.

title: Ultra Villain
description: The Montreal producer’s pearlescent new album renders heartbreak and obsession in patient waves of ambient, dub techno, and progressive house.

title: Cupid & Psyche 85
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the ultra slick, deliciously clever record where the UK band deconstructed pop music only to build it back up even better.

title: We Gotta Groove: The Brother Studio Years (Super Deluxe Edition)
description: Exploring one of their least renowned periods—and featuring the first official release of the lost album Adult/Child—a new box set finds the Beach Boys at their best, worst, and most human.

title: COLD 2 THE TOUCH
description: Justice Tripp finds a balance between no-frills punk and acid-blotted experiments on a heavy, weary, pissed-off new album.

title: MAN BITES DOG
description: femtanyl make computer music that wants to mosh. The bitcrushed hardcore rave tracks on the duo’s debut LP are sometimes thrilling and sometimes too much.

title: Canada
description: The Ann Arbor producer dusts off an alias he used on a 1996 ambient-techno classic and gives his jazzy, atmospheric dance music a jolt of fresh energy.

title: Buckaroo
description: The young New York-based songwriter Zion Battle’s debut channels the heartfelt charm of bedroom pop and the distorted fuzz of 1990s indie rock.

title: Butterfly
description: On the latest album from his DJ alias, Caribou’s Dan Snaith ups the tempo and doubles down on big-room oomph, sacrificing some of the appealing eccentricity of his best work.

title: Cerulean
description: Crammed with digital texture and waterlogged by synthetic ocean chorales, the underground pop producer’s new album sinks under the weight of prog ambition.

title: 一包烟 (Yi Bao Yan)
description: The London-based artist maps the human-machine interface on his latest EP, wrapping a fuzzed-out wall of guitars in uncanny layers of Auto-Tuned vocals.

title: Clearly Cursed
description: The Toronto band’s third album is a headlong pop-punk sugar rush.

title: Piss in the Wind
description: The brooding R&B singer’s fourth album gets bogged down by unspecific songwriting and listless vocals, despite some compelling production choices.

title: Do You Still Love Me?
description: With a tone that's equally anxious and lovesick, the British singer confronts domestic bliss and finds her stride.

title: Paleo Sol
description: A geologist by day and pedal-steel virtuoso by night, Walker leads his bandmates in a stripped-down ambient country set attuned to the seismic forces that have shaped the Pacific Northwest.

title: blue fifty-six
description: Under her latest alias, Angel Marcloid offers a beguiling collection of modular synth experiments that cycle between harsh textures and monochromatic expanses.

title: As of Now
description: The Charlotte rapper’s latest album is the height of his ability. The vignettes of heartbreak and hustling come with absurdist wit and an outstanding selection of beats.

title: The Fall-Off
description: J. Cole’s greatest album of all time is a double-disc Alexandrian quest to conquer a wide breadth of styles and ideas. It crumples under expectations few records could hope to meet.

title: Love Is Not Enough
description: On their first proper album in nine years, the Boston metalcore veterans shift between blistering political bloodlettings and moody reckonings with mortality.

title: Dirt Buyer III
description: Youthful angst and autobiographical detail are fodder for creative inspiration on Joe Sutkowski’s cathartic third album of emo and slowcore.

title: Anata
description: The Los Thuthanaka guitarist celebrates the joy of performance through meteoric playing and unvarnished texture on a new solo album inspired by Aymara ceremony.

title: The Boy who cried Terrified .
description: The Essex-born poster boy for the 2020s zeitgeist celebrates turning 21 with a nervy, high-octane take on his bedroom rap melancholia. His reputation precedes him now and he knows it.

title: Jessica Pratt
description: The Providence songwriter covers Jessica Pratt's 2012 debut in its entirety, injecting the stark originals with a jubilant, chaotic energy.

title: Graze the Bell
description: The Bing & Ruth composer’s first album under his own name features solo piano music with larger-than-life physicality. His open-ended compositions resemble a mind in conversation with itself.

title: Behind the Magnolia Curtain
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a cult 1981 garage rock record steeped in Memphis lore. With Alex Chilton as his sideman, the provocative Tav Falco brought blues and rockabilly screaming into the post-punk era.

title: western beats
description: On a new reissue, the early PC Music release remains an absurdist plastic wonder, the broken toy that comes with an “underground dance music”-themed Happy Meal.

title: Singin’ to an Empty Chair
description: Bringing their country-tinted indie rock to boundless new landscapes, the Chicago band returns with their most emotionally affecting and compositionally advanced songs to date.

title: PLAGUE MUSIC EP
description: A noise artist who once found hidden music in the crackle of fire sounds equally incendiary on her latest EP of club music, sculpting redlining rhythms out of blocks of charred bass.

title: Rosacea
description: The Norwegian artist’s loop-based assemblages follow a strange, dreamlike logic, weaving indecipherable vocals and stray bits of texture into warped avant-pop.

title: Shadow Language
description: The South African artist emphasizes atmosphere over rhythm on a vibrant, textural album that shapeshifts between drum’n’bass and dub techno.

title: URGH
description: The noise-rock band’s second album is a breakthrough: insidiously catchy, incomprehensibly groovy, and fueled by righteous fury.

title: Tenterhooks
description: Seven albums in, the L.A. band continues to channel ’90s-inspired alt-rock. The record’s pleasant sound and seamless production only exacerbate the feeling of stasis.

title: low clouds hang, this land is on fire
description: The Asheville guitarist takes a new approach on his latest album for Drag City, using a surprisingly gentle sound to frame his customary meditations on political resistance and liberation.

title: Liturgy of Death
description: Now settled into a steady lineup, the iconic black metal band sounds reliable and reverent—but they shine when things get a little weird.

title: I Have to Get Hotter
description: Rowan Miles and Gabriella Turton’s totally sarcastic, painfully sincere songwriting parodies the lives of sexless young Brits with madcap humor and cartoonish charm.

title: Euphoria Bound
description: The Berlin-based producer’s new album brings muscular heft and mystical atmosphere to his labyrinthine rhythms and groaning sub-bass.

title: OCTANE
description: The Texas rapper manages to buoy even the most underwhelming stretches of his fifth album with sparks of personality and timely features.

title: NAK
description: After years of experimenting, the L.A. rapper and skateboarder finds his voice with an album that’s equally hyperactive and hypnotizing.

title: Xavier
description: The New York rapper’s debut is a cult rap record with big ambition. Cool, chaotic, and hyper-curious, Xav blows up his sound without losing his style.

title: Empty Hands
description: The versatile metalcore singer amplifies all her strengths on her seventh album—it’s heavier, savvier, and quirkier than ever.

title: GIRL I LOVE YOU
description: The Korean producer’s new album fortifies trance-inflected emotionality with singeli, reggaeton, and hard drum rhythms to argue that maximalism isn’t quite dead yet.

title: African Skies
description: Long a collectors’ holy grail, this searching, atmospheric soundtrack recorded for Chicago’s Adler Planetarium in 1993 mixes spiritual jazz with avant-garde pan-Africanism.

title: Warmer Than Gold
description: Power-pop shapeshifter Ben Cook explores the sounds and styles of Madchester on a new album that unabashedly prioritizes style over substance.

title: Can Such Delightful Times Go On Forever?
description: Matmos’ Drew Daniel continues to probe questions of community and solidarity on his latest LP—this time, trading electronic tropes for acoustic timbres informed by chamber music and film composition.

title: 波地獄 / Post Purgatory
description: Five years after its ostensible farewell gig, the Taiwanese duo builds on its drone-doom foundation, incorporating shorter song structures inflected with trip-hop, jazz, and synth pop.

title: Not Here Not Gone
description: Pulling from doom, black metal, and shoegaze, the group brings the palette of heavy music to the perspective of a singer-songwriter’s most intimate revelations.

title: A Walk Across the Rooftops
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 1984 debut from the Scottish trio who built towers of emotion from moody, minimalist parts.

title: Completely Necessary
description: Arthur Russell and Ernie Brooks’ late-’70s rock group has been rendered a historical footnote, but a new anthology captures the nervy brilliance of its guitar-driven new wave.

title: I Used to Go to This Bar
description: The Los Angeles pop-punk trio spends its seventh album wrestling with nostalgia, finding nuance and emotional complexity in their everyday grievances.

title: “Live” “At” “The” “BBC” EP
description: Backed by his ad hoc band The Muggers, the prolific songwriter blasts through a five-song set that feels like a pure distillation of his psychedelic chaos.

title: Can I Get a Pack of Camel Lights?
description: The Animal Collective member’s first solo album is a personal, psychedelic trip indulging his fascination with the hurdy-gurdy.

title: For the First Time, Again
description: The singer’s debut channels Roy Orbison, David Bowie, and erstwhile California greats—but even his tremendous voice can’t make it feel like more than homage.

title: Vacancy
description: The singer’s first album for Interscope is honey-sweet, grown-up R&B that’s looking for a little something missing.

title: My Ghosts Go Ghost
description: After the death of Injury Reserve’s Stepa J. Groggs, the surviving members of the hip-hop collective form a new group with a contemplative, improvisational spirit.

title: Sidings
description: The UK electronic producer communes with the modular synthesizer for immersive longform compositions that warp your perception of time.

title: Ralings ’26
description: On the Brooklyn DIY project’s first album in six years, Alex Ian Smith crafts artfully restrained industrial music that flirts with pop songcraft.
The imperturbable New York rapper is back behind the boards for a lean, mean new album with endless quotables and only one guest.

title: Death in the Business of Whaling
description: On his second album, the Portland musician adds a little mystery to his sad-boy singer-songwriter persona, favoring abstract musings and adding subtle strangeness to otherwise tasteful arrangements.

title: Full Serpent EP
description: On a conceptual new EP, the British producer leads vivid journeys through vaporous synthwork and glitchy samples.

title: EL NUEVO SONIDO
description: The Chilean musician channels the spirit of classic perreo on a reggaeton album shaped by sleek hooks and guided by the twists and turns of battle rap.

title: Peanut
description: The New York musician’s latest album, his first with vocals, is a gently psychedelic tour of his mind, pairing surrealistic lyrics with watery pop-ambient soundscaping.

title: locket
description: There are some decent pop songs on locket, but Madison Beer’s albums continue to feel like a lowest common denominator of trends.

title: The Demise of Planet X
description: The UK duo continues to rail against austerity and oppression on its 13th record. At worst, the album lapses into vague gesturing; at best, it turns diatribes into dialogues with guest vocalists.

title: My Heart Is a Room With No Cameras in It
description: Former Blood guitarist Julian McCamman’s scrappy, studio-augmented indie rock wears its heart on its sleeve.

title: Megadeth
description: With his final studio album, Dave Mustaine closes the curtains on a thrash metal institution without the communal gravitas of a proper farewell.

title: World’s Gone Wrong
description: Lucinda Williams’ world-weary new album takes comfort in rootsy rock’n’roll with a casual, authoritative swing that belies its stylistic range.

title: OVERTIME
description: The production duo’s busy, silly, next-gen footwork hashes underground rap microgenres and recognizable samples into dreamy collagist fantasies.

title: Jana Horn
description: The peripatetic singer-songwriter’s eponymous third album is a document of wandering and longing. Its acoustic arrangements are sparse and her lyrics fragmentary, but the mood is warm and inviting.

title: Ænima
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Tool’s marvelous 1996 album, a long and heady trip that ushered in a new age of hard rock.

title: The Return of the Durutti Column (Expanded & Remastered)
description: Reissued with demos, live performances, and early recordings, the full-length debut by the mercurial Factory project is as beautiful as it is cerebral, a work of radical non-provocation.

title: ATLiens
description: We’re celebrating the 30th anniversary of Pitchfork with a full week dedicated to Sunday Reviews of great albums from 1996. Today we revisit Big Boi and André 3000’s second album, a vulnerable and virtuosic record that solidified the duo’s dynamic.

title: Sexta dos Crias 2.0
description: A Brazilian funk ambassador known for his lightning-fingered DJ style blows the genre wide open on his second album-length mix.

title: Doppelgänger
description: Exploring new variations on their slowcore sound, the Brooklyn group’s first album in six years raises uneasy questions about life as an artist.

title: I Am
description: The Queens rapper’s sixth album puts a high-gloss sheen on her sharp-elbowed sound, but gets bogged down by repetitive rhyme schemes and boilerplate bravado.

title: If You’re Feeling Sinister
description: We’re celebrating the 30th anniversary of Pitchfork with a full week dedicated to Sunday Reviews of great albums from 1996. Today we revisit the marvelous, cult-forming second album from the Scottish indie-pop group: a deceptively complex set of character studies overflowing with compassion, humor, and hooks.

title: The Testament of Ann Lee (Original Soundtrack)
description: ​​For Mona Fastvold’s film about the Shaker founder, Daniel Blumberg reworked hymns, composed songs, and led a sizable chorus to mimic speaking in tongues. It’s ambitious but ultimately overbearing.

title: Dreamer+
description: The Oslo musician’s debut album is a darkly glamorous blur of trip-hop and dance pop, with copious reverb and Auto-Tune as stand-ins for yearning, uneasiness, and irresolution.

title: Alan Vega (Deluxe Remastered Edition) / Collision Drive (Remastered Edition)
description: The legendary Suicide vocalist’s early-1980s solo albums don’t illustrate his reinvention as a rockabilly artist so much as reveal that he’d always been one.

title: Richard D. James Album
description: We’re celebrating the 30th anniversary of Pitchfork with a full week dedicated to Sunday Reviews of great albums from 1996. Today we revisit Aphex Twin’s fourth album under the alias, which used naive melodies and mind-bending rhythms to explore the bliss and terror of childhood.

title: Yeah, mostly
description: After a pair of heady soundtracks, the Woodstock musician’s earnest and exploratory new album plants its feet firmly on the ground, finding poetry in black mold and standing desks.

title: CONFLICT DLC
description: On the sequel to 2023’s RAT WARS, HEALTH render the dehumanizing effects of a technologically mediated world in high-definition riffs with malevolent force.

title: Fire of God’s Love
description: This 1973 album of Christian worship music has long attracted crate-diggers like James Blake and Vegyn with its haunting synths and pseudo-dub rhythms.

title: One in a Million
description: This week we’re celebrating the 30th anniversary of Pitchfork with a full week dedicated to Sunday Reviews of great albums from 1996. Today we revisit the dire circumstances and extraordinary chemistry that produced Aaliyah’s second LP, one of the coolest records of the ’90s.

title: Don’t Be Dumb
description: Rocky’s fourth album is flawed but sharp, and contains enough moments of ingenuity to argue that he’s still an essential part of the rap ecosystem.

title: Valentine
description: The singer-songwriter’s ninth album is an earnest, aching set carried by dazzling vocal performances and rich, chamber-folk production.

title: Stand on My Shoulders
description: The multidisciplinary Tlingit/Unangax̂ artist examines kinship and political consciousness on an album that evokes the indie-rock experimentalism of TV on the Radio.

title: Legend
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the ubiquitous 1984 Bob Marley compilation Legend, a woefully incomplete portrait of the Jamaican artist that, nevertheless, became legendary.

title: Watching From a Distance (Reissue)
description: On a 20th anniversary reissue, the UK doom metal band’s second—and most recent—album remains one of the genre’s heaviest and most vulnerable statements.

title: Tragic Magic
description: On their debut album together, two longtime friends and peers synthesize their respective styles, seeking out new directions and new ways of connecting.

title: In 1,000 Agonies, I Exist
description: The Los Angeles hardcore band embraces a sludgy, chaotic sound that plays to their burgeoning strengths.

title: Quicksand Heart
description: On her debut solo album, the English singer-songwriter—and member of Let’s Eat Grandma—channels childlike wonder and joy with euphoric hooks and a nostalgic synth-pop palette.

title: Love and Fortune
description: The songwriter performs a penetrating and generous post-mortem of a lost friendship in pearlescent little showstoppers where her voice is often barely adorned at all.

title: Coke Wave 3.5: Narcos
description: Over 15 years after their original Coke Wave run, French Montana and Max B prove the classic formula still goes a long way.

title: Raquel Baby
description: On a brief new project, the Detroit rapper finds strange, adventurous territory on the outskirts of his hard-nosed sound.

title: Live
description: Collaged together out of discrete moments from the trio’s 2024 tour, their new live cassette balances their ambient inclinations with heavyweight bass and forceful rhythms.

title: Slutworld
description: The Minneapolis hardcore band’s debut is fearsomely loud and more timely than ever. Their protest punk hits like a baseball bat.

title: Bloodline
description: The Liberian American songwriter’s debut confronts his complex upbringing, combining millennial indie-folk influences with his poignant perspective on war, identity, and memory.

title: Desert So Green
description: With a lineup of experimental rock veterans, the Detroit sextet takes a psychedelic voyage that favors the collective over the individual.

title: Selfless
description: Under his latest alias, Vancouver electronic musician Tanner Matt contorts smeared synth tones and diffuse beats into an unsettling, opalescent album of minimalist ambient techno.

title: This Is My Way to Tell You That Everything Is Real and Happening Right Now
description: Having chosen family over music in his early 20s, the Quebec artist returns to songwriting more than a decade later, channeling spiritual yearning in spectral folk.

title: With Heaven on Top / With Heaven on Top (Acoustic)
description: The massively successful songwriter offers two versions of his 25-song new album: solo and full-band. At his best, he shows he’s learning to paint on a larger canvas.

title: Mrs.Key
description: On his New Year’s Day mixtape, the Atlanta artist pursues an idiosyncratic fusion of romance, spiritual inspiration, pain rap, and plugg.

title: La Dame
description: The rising Martinican star’s third album unites ballads with dancefloor heaters and makes space for a plethora of collaborators in and beyond the island’s shatta rap scene.

title: Feline’s Return
description: The UK singer-producer combines nimble vocals and innovative arrangements with the compressed drama of Y2K dance pop; her ear for detail enlivens familiar sounds.

title: t҉w҉o҉ ҉s҉h҉e҉l҉l҉
description: The mischievous UK duo reconsiders its 2024 self-titled LP with an uneven slate of remixes and new tracks, mixing moments of impressive boldness into a string of otherwise unremarkable exercises.

title: Other Girl
description: The second album from experimental musician Ulla Straus’ ambient folk project is intimate and untethered to reality.

title: Discipline
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the beautifully labyrinthian 1981 album from a prog-rock institution in search of continuous evolution.

title: The Long Sleep
description: The emo rapper-producer’s full-length debut cycles between weird ideas and accessible cuts, collaging stylistic landmarks from the early 1990s to the MySpace era to Lil Peep.

title: Secret Love
description: On their third album, Florence Shaw and co. are tapping into that sly, dry humor, working with Cate Le Bon, and breaking out of their shell.

title: Rebuilding
description: On their score for a neo-Western film, the guitarists explore emotional and geographical landscapes with downhome pastoral ambience.

title: 1 IN A MILLION
description: The Fort Myers rapper personalizes a mixtape of anonymous beats and drill-inspired clichés with geographical specificity and stylistic touches that scream Florida.

title: Light-Years
description: On their long-awaited full-length collaboration, the ’90s rap legends keep their gaze focused squarely on the rear-view mirror. It’s unabashed nostalgia bait with flashes of vintage brilliance.

title: Neverland
description: The pioneering Norwegian post-metal duo continues its career-long experimentation—this time with poetry recitations, EDM throwbacks, and balmy new age.

title: sankofa
description: The Maryland rapper fills his fourth album with cathartic melodies and sentimental tributes to family. But despite his occasionally distinctive moments, he sounds overly beholden to his influences.

title: The Spiritual Sound
description: The L.A. black metal quartet’s second album borrows widely from across the heavy-music spectrum and beyond, but their stylistic shifts are always in service of the band’s increasingly distinct voice.

title: The Sludge of the Land
description: The Italian experimental duo creates a sprawling, overstimulating work that celebrates the kitsch lurking behind a wide array of musical forms.

title: Desaceleradas
description: Experimental musician Delia Beatriz pays homage to Mexican cumbia rebajada using digital processing to manipulate archival recordings into fields of warped texture and hallucinatory drone.

title: As Above, So Below
description: On the French musician’s debut album, bleak sounds collide with cosmic mysticism—a post-punk take on new-age spirituality filled with strange, singular touches.

title: The Velvet Underground & Rowan
description: Proving that one scenester’s cringe is another’s creative gold, the London duo turns its retro-fetishizing gaze to early-’10s indie, finding both wit and pathos in their deeply uncool inspirations.

title: FEMME FATALE
description: The Chilean artist stretches her voice to virtuosic extremes on a ninth album that’s ambitious and unhinged, playful and poignant.

title: Marty Supreme (Original Soundtrack)
description: The electronic composer meets the larger-than-life film on its level, building the palette he’s honed over the years into a totalizing prism of sound.

title: Implosion
description: The dub veterans bring out the best in each other with a collaborative album that balances lumbering doom with spacey ambience.

title: Soulja Hate Repellant
description: One of MIKE’s roster of rap mavericks, Niontay probes the deepest, murkiest corners of his sound on this 454-hosted mixtape, blurring his influences and slurring his bars with abandon.

artist: Bulgarian State Radio & Television Female Vocal Choir
title: Le Mystère des Voix Bulgares
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we look back on a collection of Communist-era Bulgarian folk recordings that became an unlikely hit for 4AD in the 1980s.

title: You Want That Too!
description: With assists from Jeff Parker, Meg Duffy, and others, the versatile drummer’s latest album stakes its claim at the shifting border between jazz and electronic music.

title: Blizzard
description: The ambitious young Irish balladeer crafts a debut album that’s heavy on the drama, letting moments of anthemic beauty peak through his cryptic delivery.

title: Anywhere
description: Inspired by the American Midwest, the South Londoners’ debut album is a drifting odyssey through ambient and downtempo trance that captures the feeling of meditative drives on sprawling backroads.

title: A Spyglass to One’s Face
description: Spurred on by Charlotte producer Dirty Art Club’s spacious, hypnotic beats, the L.A.-based rapper sounds more reflective than usual, but his unflappable chill still prevails.

title: gutta child EP
description: On his debut EP, the Los Angeles-based singer and producer makes funky, homespun R&B that celebrates his Southern heritage.

title: No Control, No Glory
description: The Brooklyn rapper pushes past conventional song structures on an adventurous, emotional album that centers his stream-of-consciousness flow.

title: #FEDERAL
description: The London emcee fills his latest album with trap-inspired hellscapes that spotlight his dexterous flows. It’s one of the most exhilarating releases from the UK underground this year.

title: USB002
description: The superstar DJ recruits Floating Points, Danny Brown, and Sammy Virji for the latest update to his “infinite” album. It’s consistently banging—Fred again.. on pleasant autopilot.

title: The Pilot
description: On this prelude to an upcoming album, the rapper explores themes of sobriety with newfound clarity and confidence.

title: amnesia
description: The British rapper and New York production collective blend cloud rap, club trap, and stormy breaks to capture a slice of London life, dropping local references and conjuring the city’s hazy malaise.

title: Dentro De Mim
description: The rising batida producer refines his dark, industrial sound on a set of competent yet conventional club tracks.

title: Suburban Tours
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a DIY gem that funneled childhood nostalgia and omnivorous taste through piles of reverb and dirt-cheap equipment to become one of the great guitar records of the 21st century.

title: lost in dreams
description: The mysterious artist known as Traumprinz, Prince of Denmark, and DJ Healer explores his most guileless side on an epic, three-hour compendium of dub techno, deep house, trance, ambient, and drum’n’bass.

title: Holo Boy
description: Songwriter Nate Amos polishes up 10 tracks from his Bandcamp days and confronts humorous self-effacement with new confidence.

title: ♡ EP
description: The producer and songwriter channels pop bliss on their latest EP, which features gently reworked versions of several previously released songs.

title: Cavejaz
description: The Brazilian American composer and guitarist crafts a quietly immersive record that feels like the result of a long, inspired jam session.

title: I Tried to Tell You
description: Embellishing DMV drill with retro R&B, Southern-style storytelling, and striking moments of vulnerability, the DC rapper’s album is simultaneously regional and singular.

title: Vesper Sparrow
description: The experimental composer’s second album deepens their exploration of speech dysfluency and its musical possibilities. Here, their stutter is a pathway to probe family legacy and the passage of time.

title: Love Is a Kingdom
description: Tems’ new EP explores the many facets of love, grappling with romantic desire and spiritual surrender against a foundation of syncopated log drums and 808s.

title: Reminiscencias
description: On his debut LP, the Colombian producer trades the conceptual bent of earlier releases for bold fusions of techno, electro, and progressive house, emphasizing emotional connection above all else.

title: wet glass
description: On a set of imagistic travelogues, the North Carolina quartet finds new clarity in its dreamy, wintry sound.

title: A Series of Actions in a Sphere of Forever / Changes in Air
description: Two more full-length albums from the pianist and composer are narrow in focus and all the more compelling for it. Together, they form a treatise on the lingering note.

title: YELL AT CLOUD
description: On its second album, the San Diego supergroup—featuring members of Drive Like Jehu, Pinback, and more—channels modern gloom with haunting imagery and aggressive riffs, lifted by flashes of hope.

title: Hunched Jack Mixtape
description: On his first release for Surf Gang, the Chengdu plugg rapper embraces his outsider persona atop the strongest, most cohesive production of his career.

title: Rebel
description: The Liverpudlian’s hard-nosed depiction of streetlit debauchery has turned him into one of the hottest new faces in UK rap. He prefers to hide that face behind a mask.

title: Ruby Vroom
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 1994 debut album from a New York group that mixed up rock, jazz, hip-hop beats, and slam poetry into a brand-new sound that is inextricably linked to its era.

title: II
description: On the long-awaited follow-up to their 2012 debut, techno sorcerers Donato Dozzy and Neel return to a rich, subtly evolving sound that feels like the dance music equivalent of forest bathing.

title: Unclouded
description: On her latest album of diaphanous psych rock, the French musician’s songwriting is as ethereal as ever, but the crisp production sharpens the focus.

title: Once Upon a Time... in Shropshire
description: On his second album, the British musician—who has scored several Yorgos Lanthimos films—delivers maximalist delirium and pastoral ballads, leveraging ridiculousness to capture the terror of loss.

title: Forward
description: The Santa Cruz band’s self-released debut plants its flag for the homespun Midwest emo of the 1990s.

title: Live at Third Man Records
description: Recorded September 2024 in Nashville, this catalog-spanning, low-energy set lands with a finality that the duo perhaps didn’t intend.

title: pullup to busan 4 morE hypEr summEr it’s gonna be a fuckin moviE EP
description: Rapping fluidly over fluorescent hyperpop, the Korean artist oozes personality on her latest release, drawing equally from mainstream K-pop’s efficiency and PC Music’s experimental edge.

title: SLIDER II
description: The California R&B singer lets a little light into his vibey, moody love songs.

title: Cabin in the Sky
description: On the Daisy Age veterans’ 10th album, De La confront the loss of Trugoy the Dove, who died while making the record. But despite the sorrowful subtext, their rhymes and beats are as playful as ever.

title: KPOP B!TCH
description: The South Korean singer and producer’s high-saturation blend of hyperpop and big-tent EDM flashes back to naughty-aughties clubland.

title: ...it’s only about u if you think it is.
description: On the heels of his viral success, the shapeshifting R&B artist makes a daring but frustrating pivot to ’90s alt-rock worship.

title: Destinée
description: After backlash to her performance at the Paris Olympics, the French Malian singer’s fifth album uses her signature blend of Afrobeats, zouk, pop, and R&B to subtly reframe the narrative.

title: joy is no knocking nation EP
description: The Chicago group’s latest EP blitzes through the last half century of punk and hardcore, fusing no wave, post-rock, and ’90s screamo in a densely packed and carefully crafted 19 minutes.

title: THE LIFE OF ERG
description: The three Dominican American artists fill their collaborative album with local idiosyncrasies and evocative production, sharing tales of small-city kingpins in the New England rust belt.

title: Balloon Balloon Balloon
description: 21-year-old power-pop auteur Kai Slater is back with a deliberately constructed album that finds the sweet spot between winsome and whimsical, chaos and craft.

title: How You Been
description: A powerhouse quintet with deep ties to L.A.’s experimental music universe breaks jazz wide open on its second album, blurring the lines between live improv and post-production sorcery.

title: Red sky at morning
description: Probing the unease lurking beneath domestic comfort, the New York musician’s second album uses warm, melodic folk as the backdrop to something stranger and more macabre.

title: Strangers From the Universe
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit an essential talisman of freak music from 1994, a beautifully weird document of a beautifully weird band living out the last daydream of alternative rock.

title: What of Our Nature
description: The songwriters collaborate for a spirited and serious collection of protest folk inspired by the legacy of Woody Guthrie.

title: Shine
description: A decade after his debut, the Los Angeles singer-songwriter and feted hired gun put his session work on hold to record a comeback album with the intimacy and immediacy of a homespun demo.

title: sorry i thought you were someone else
description: The British producer’s third record is the most satisfying of his career so far, its streamlined, home-listening house driven by finely honed drums and filled with lush textures.

title: The Sword & the Soaring
description: Sage Elsesser’s sixth album is his most evocative release in years. Working with an extensive catalog of producers, the rapper reflects on grief and loss in songs that continually foreground hope.

title: Panorama
description: On her third solo album, the Montreal singer-songwriter crafts playfully disorienting art-punk without ever losing her cool.

title: Daylight Daylight
description: The Brooklyn songwriter and guitarist crafts a tender album filled with negative space and patient reflections on mortality.

title: Electric Hour
description: The Atlanta indie-rock band puts its city and its songwriting in the spotlight on a tightly focused new album.

title: Still Goin the EP
description: The veteran Atlanta producer’s new solo EP channels his familiarity with Southern rap history to celebrate a fresh lease on life.

title: Giant Steps
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 1993 masterpiece from a group of shoegazing Beatles fanatics who went up against Oasis in the battle for the soul of British rock—and lost.

title: A Jackal’s Wedding
description: After the sleek Your Hero Is Not Dead and the labyrinthine An Inbuilt Fault, the singer-songwriter finds a middle ground; it’s expansive and unpredictable but features his most polished songwriting yet.

title: Let It Be (Deluxe Edition)
description: Packaged with live recordings and studio rarities, the Mats’ 1984 masterpiece gets a thoughtful new box set that illustrates the precarity and magic of their unlikely breakthrough.

title: Riviera
description: The electronic duo moves beyond referential homage on its second album, offering a clearer definition of its own sound: scuzzy, brooding, and obsessed with open roads and Californian archetypes.

title: Retrospective Frequencies
description: Gregorio Da Silva’s debut album combines nostalgic rave sounds with Latin American folk rhythms, offering a warm, freaky introduction to the Argentinian producer’s craft.

title: Finally Over It
description: The Atlanta R&B singer takes cover in plain sight on her trilogy-capping double LP. Its 1990s-style slow jams and tame genre fusions don’t do her justice.

title: Half of What You See
description: The jazz-rap ensemble’s second album is dense, chaotic, and thrilling, with electroacoustic abstraction grounded by casual humor and intentional collaboration.

title: LaFlair
description: The emergent SoundCloud graduate’s new full-length feels like a sleeker, more idyllic take on the original plugg scene of the 2010s.

title: Station on the Hill
description: The Vancouver noise-rock band embraces overstimulation on a full-length debut that demands active listening.

title: DOGA
description: On her first album in eight years, the Argentinian musician plies a whimsically unsettling mix of sing-song melodies, ghostly electronics, and lyrics that probe the absurdity of the human condition.

title: Through This Fire Across From Peter Balkan
description: The musical tale of three shipwrecked souls makes for an unusually linear Mountain Goats record, full of powerful moments that not even the eternally moving John Darnielle can scrape into the whole it deserves.

title: Jam on Revenge
description: The Brooklyn electro crew’s 1984 debut gets a new reissue that shows how visionary and vital their work remains.

title: EUSEXUA Afterglow
description: The chaotic EUSEXUA universe is expanding and contracting with a brand new album and a reimagined version of her album from earlier in the year. But twigs sounds like she’s having a blast, so let’s roll with it.

title: Chin Up Buttercup
description: On her latest album, Katie Stelmanis processes heartbreak by embracing club-ready synth-pop. It’s an impressive leap forward after years of steadily expanding the project’s sound.

title: Warbrained
description: On the Florida musician’s gritty, back-to-basics third album, the digicore exile embraces analog oomph, mining golden-era shoegaze for corporeal pleasure.

title: Tranquilizer
description: Drawing on a cache of commercial sample CDs, Daniel Lopatin assembles an impossibly dense and transportive electronic album that takes impermanence as its inspiration.

title: Again
description: The Melbourne band’s peppy, generic indie rock represents exactly the sum of its parts.

title: My Supernova
description: The Japanese techno producer crafts a cohesive full-length that’s equally suited for home listening and the club.

title: Float
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 2000 record from the Long Island rapper, a deep, heady, and potent transmission from the splintering hip-hop underground.

title: 1985: The Miracle Year
description: A set of previously unreleased live recordings captures the Minneapolis hardcore trio at peak ferocity. It’s a welcome corrective to the tinny production of their studio albums.

title: Big city life EDITS
description: A host of artists—ML Buch, Astrid Sonne, Erika de Casier, MIKE, and more—radically rework the Norwegian duo’s songs on a remix set that flows as compellingly as an actual Smerz album.

title: COSPLAY
description: On its third album, the London band breaks free of its usual ironic tone, filling its warped rock songs with pop-culture references and alluring idiosyncrasies.

title: Lil Herb
description: Stepping into his teenage shoes for a loose concept album, the Chicago icon reflects on the original era of drill with the clarity of a scene veteran.

title: After EP / After EP 2
description: The Los Angeles duo’s bland simulations of millennial pop-rock will make you feel like it’s still 2006. Isn’t there more to life?

title: a little death
description: After the singer-songwriter slant of last year’s sentiment, the field recordist and audio diarist rebalances her emo-ambient fusion, emphasizing nuanced drones and meticulous arrangements.

title: Small Talk
description: The Chicago indie rock band soothes heartbreak with the most anonymous, uninspiring music you can possibly imagine.

title: Before You Press Play
description: On their chest-puffing joint album, the Atlanta underground rap wunderkinds sound like they’re on the precipice of growing up.

title: Queen
description: The Martinican artist helped popularize shatta, the dancehall offshoot born on her home island. She keeps the party going on her debut album, making a strong case to be the genre’s global ambassador.

title: Stardust
description: Working with a new vanguard of outsider electronic artists, the Detroit rapper lets his freak flag fry. The results are shaky but full of heart.

title: Time Flies
description: On her debut mixtape, the South London-based R&B singer shares complex portraits of love and grief.

title: Talulah’s Tape
description: The Indianapolis band’s ramshackle debut is a charming throwback to 1990s jangle pop.

title: hooke’s law
description: The Chicago singer and producer’s second album tangles with racing thoughts and unruly arrangements, narrating love and mental health in the nervous heat of real time.

title: C0FFEE!
description: Written, recorded, and occasionally set behind the wheel of his Ford Bronco WildTrak, the Chicago rapper-producer’s new EP is a loose and freewheeling break from his typically meticulous projects.

title: The Hermit
description: On her debut album, the North Carolina-born, Los Angeles-raised artist elevates straightforward songs with unconventional production choices and her singular, vibrato-laden voice.

title: Out the Blue
description: On their breakout album, the Baton Rouge rappers wear the championship belt for best duo out of the city, churning out big trash-talking tunes with fat-ass basslines made to set the clubs off.

title: Episodes
description: Released alongside a new memoir, the rapper’s latest album details his mental health struggles. Its best moments meld vulnerability and humor—but its bloated runtime leads to diminishing returns.

title: InitiatriX
description: The Manchester-based DJ’s warped experiments pack a club-shifting wallop. His debut is challenging without being overly cerebral and idiosyncratic without feeling inscrutable.

title: Horses
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Patti Smith’s unparalleled debut, an album whose raw power and incalculable legacy catalyzed a new cultural order in music.

title: Through the Open Window: The Bootleg Series Vol. 18
description: The 18th installment of Dylan’s never-ending reissue series tracks his rise from teenage rock’n’roller to new folk icon. It plays less like a box set and more like the audiobook of a Great American Novel.

title: LUX
description: The Spanish singer’s fourth record is a heartfelt offering of avant-garde classical pop that roars through genre, romance, and religion.

title: Hostile Design
description: The D.C. art-punks return with their first record in over two decades, adding a new emphasis on dub grooves to their controlled chaos and righteous indignation.

title: U      TA
description: On a collaborative record that feels anomalous for both artists, the avant-garde icon adds prickliness to the composer’s soothing sounds, achieving an overall feeling of warm vulnerability.

title: Punjabi Disco
description: Naya Beat reissues the first-ever British Asian electronic dance album—a joyous, loose-limbed romp through Punjabi-tinged disco, funk, psychedelia, and proto-acid house.

title: Mercy
description: Reuniting with the Alchemist, billy woods and Elucid renew their call to learn from history before it’s too late. Mercy represents the trio’s slickest, most exacting collaboration yet.

title: Repulsor
description: The L.A. beatmaker turns aggressive on his fourth album—dialing up the distortion, flooding his beats with overdriven synths, and pushing anxious moods into the red.

title: Iconoclasts
description: The Swedish composer and organist makes imposing, monolithic music, but the themes she addresses in her singing—love, heartache, renewal—are resolutely human in scale.

title: The Boy Who Played the Harp
description: The UK rap superstar contemplates fame, faith, and the self on a new album whose melancholy mood reflects the solitary nature of introspection.

title: Off the Record
description: Gathering and reworking a decade’s worth of blistering live jams, this compilation of four dynamic new EPs captures the recombinant spirit of the jazz drummer, bandleader, and beatmaker.

title: The Love
description: On their second album, the Denver punks look both outward and inward at once, beefing up their sound while they explore more introspective emotional terrain.

title: Harlem’s Finest: Return of the King
description: The fourth posthumous release from the New York legend has been in the works for a long time, but it still feels hollow and cobbled together.

title: Everybody Scream
description: On her sixth album, Florence Welch sings anthems of resilience with her characteristic gusto, but it’s her words of uncertainty that stand out most.

title: Cloud Time
description: The ambient artist and Florist bandleader takes inspiration from Japanese environmental music on an album culled from improvisational, solitary live performances during a trip to Japan.

title: In the Earth Again
description: On a surprisingly seamless collaborative LP, the sludge-metal band and fingerstyle guitarist push each other to vulnerable new territory.

title: Psychic Resynthesis / Nite Closures EP
description: On two recent releases, the electronic experimentalist explores new territory—recognizably classical music written for a chamber ensemble—and offers a set of quintessentially bewildering solo tracks.

title: Tremor
description: On his first album since 2022, the UK producer trades his habitual techno and ambient for a more melodic, rock-driven sound that puts guest singers like yeule and yunè pinko front and center.

title: Resurrection
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the Chicago rapper’s second album, a powerful, multidimensional record that put the MC and his hometown on the map.

title: (What’s the Story) Morning Glory? (30th Anniversary Deluxe Edition)
description: Now we enter the third decade of Oasis-mania—with all its goofy rivalries, mimicries, and cash grabs. How good do your tunes have to be to withstand all that? This good.

title: Snocaps
description: The Crutchfield twins—accompanied by MJ Lenderman and Brad Cook—reunite for a spirited new project that plays to their strengths and embraces all the miles they’ve traveled.

title: I Love My Computer
description: Moving between EDM, tech-house, speed garage, dubstep, and hyperpop, producer Nina Wilson presents an aggressively stimulating, distinctly Australian look at life online.

title: Dancin’ in the Streets
description: British DJ and producer Tom Boogizm, alongside a small group of collaborators, cloaks a set of gothic neo-folk songs in grainy textures and gauzy shadows.

title: Stereotype
description: Recorded at a friend’s parents’ house in a two-week free-for-all, this previously unreleased, proudly unpolished 1994 curio captures a teenage Tom Jenkinson at his raviest and most unrestrained.

title: Touch
description: The Chicago post-rock band’s first album in nine years was recorded between three separate cities. It’s a noisy, unstable, and strangely moving listen.

title: West End Girl
description: With an album that doubles as an insider’s account of a tabloid divorce, the singer finds a new evolution of her signature style: Lightness isn’t a foil for irony, but a vehicle for hurt.

title: CAOS
description: Eight years after his last album, the R&B heartthrob shows little interest in breaking new ground. But at his best, his vocal prowess and studio experiments place him in a class of his own.

title: Traveling Light
description: Building on the gaseous harmonies of last year’s Spectral Evolution, the Portuguese experimental guitarist dives deeper into jazz standards, piercing atmospheric drones with familiar melodies.

title: Daughters
description: On her debut, the London songwriter and producer crushes organic instrumentation and intimate vocals into a powerful statement on grief, overwhelm, and detachment.

title: Son of Spergy
description: The R&B singer explores his relationship to love and faith, but the clumsy songwriting offers more platitudes than testimonies.

title: PsychoWarrior: MG Ultra X
description: Fighting overstimulation with more overstimulation, the New York experimental band presents 14 tracks of choppy, distorted, digitally thrashed mutations of noise, EBM, and hardcore.

title: Perseverance Flow
description: Sinking their teeth into a single theme for nearly 35 minutes, weaving minimalist jazz with strands of dub and dance music, Joshua Abrams and his bandmates have never sounded more focused—or more expansive.

title: A RUPTURE A CANYON A BIRTH
description: After a tumultuous year, the Toronto-based artist embraces dance-pop on an uninhibited, unfiltered record that plays like a personal epiphany.

title: fingers crossed
description: The Ghanian British rapper fuses jerk rap, R&B, and Afrobeats on a tape that strives for luxury extravagance and coming-of-age sentimentality.

title: Rhythm Immortal
description: The Brussels-based producer fled the strictures of techno and drum’n’bass in search of a freer sound. On his astonishing debut LP under a new alias, he seems to rewrite the laws of physics.

title: Good Story
description: On her second album, the North Carolina songwriter tells candid, multi-dimensional stories where everything is on the table—including the act of storytelling.

title: How I Learned to Love What’s Gone
description: The Los Angeles band’s angsty, lovestruck pop-punk speaks to everyone’s inner teenager.

title: Korn
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a foundational nu metal album where a singer’s life of hurt and trauma gets weaponized by his band’s trailblazing sound.

title: Curiosities From the Shift
description: The experimental percussionist finds meaning in motion with a vibrant and beautiful new album built around the clave.

title: Nebraska ’82: Expanded Edition
description: A new box set, which includes the fabled Electric Nebraska sessions, tells the complete story of one of the most foundational and lonesome records in rock music.

title: Blight
description: The group’s seventh album simmers with dread about environmental catastrophe, which is addressed both sincerely and tediously.
