description: The Spanish singer’s whimsical, first-draft experimental pop marries high concept and limited resources.

title: Fancy That
description: The British singer-producer’s new mixtape is a portal into an alternate universe where UK garage blew up in America and fashion froze in 2006.

title: Even in Arcadia
description: The masked, anonymous UK quartet might be the biggest metal band in a generation—yet the group’s laborious, watered-down fusion of pop, rap, and djent amounts to very little.

title: Ill at ease
description: On the Canadian post-punks’ nervy fifth album, even apocalyptically grim lyrics feel like an appeal to humanity and romance.

title: Lifetime
description: The Danish singer shifts her gaze to ’90s classics from Janet, Madonna, and Sade on her self-produced new LP, channeling trip-hop and R&B in aqueous synths and boom-bap drums.

title: Who Will Look After the Dogs?
description: The Toronto group’s fifth album embraces self-improvement with dialed-back hooks and urgent introspection—offering a rare example of a pop-punk band learning to age with grace.

title: Jonatan
description: With a monochromatic, no-wave-inflected new studio album, the Swedish rapper and singer-songwriter attempts to merge his musical identities under one banner.

title: GOLLIWOG
description: The Brooklyn rapper’s new solo album is a twisty horrorcore masterpiece where history and nightmares are indistinguishable. The spooky backdrop is a perfect showcase for his craft.

title: Animaru
description: On her debut album, the New York-based singer-songwriter and her dexterous band combine bossa nova, indie, and J-pop. The songs are lovely and polished, but truly shine when committing to strangeness.

title: SLAYTANIC
description: No one is combining throwback Southern trap with the drama of medieval theatre quite like this Atlanta rap upstart.

title: Universal Consciousness
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we look back at Alice Coltrane’s 1971 avant-garde masterpiece, a furious and unbound collection of experimental jazz and devotional music that ascends to a higher spiritual realm.

title: From Where You Came
description: Folding together electronics, woodwind, and brass, the Canadian composer’s first solo album in eight years is her most peaceful yet; it seems to float in a state of dazed contentment.

title: Tall Tales
description: The Radiohead frontman and the esteemed electronic producer release a collaboration album. What it lacks in razzle-dazzle it makes up for with risky maneuvers.

title: 7 piano sketches
description: This low-key collection of no-fi piano improvisations is the latest step in the rapper-songwriter-producer’s new era as spiritually attuned vibesmith. It’s also more substantial than it may seem.

title: L.B. Cooper
description: The Harlem rapper and producer’s latest tape takes a fresh look at rage rap with arcade-game synths and vocal melodies that feel spontaneous, never stock.

title: The Scholars
description: In aiming to write a rock opera for the playlist era, Will Toledo crafts some of his band’s most inspired compositions—but weighs them down with a confusing plot and endless stylistic changeups.

title: Without References / Cindy Van Acker
description: In its score to an avant-garde dance piece, the Japanese group stresses the physicality of machinelike polyrhythms while using bells and gongs to heady, psychedelic effect.

title: Down on Them
description: Singing about bikes, bugs, and fragile human connection, the Brooklyn songwriter helms a modern, ecstatic New York City folk album.

title: Lake Fire
description: The Vancouver producer’s latest album uses ambient and dub techno as an ominous backdrop to the West Coast’s wildfire season. It’s road-trip music for the new normal.

title: STILL AIN NUN BIGGER
description: The Dallas rapper’s latest release of no-frills motivation rap sounds triumphant but undercooked—and, like many other #NewDallas releases, fails to help pinpoint the city’s unique hip-hop identity.

title: Joseph, What Have You Done?
description: The UK rapper and producer is part of a wave of artists mixing grime, drill, and club music into avant-garde confessional art. Here, he probes at the nexus of generational trauma and regional pride.

title: Scanners
description: The New York producer’s sixth album is his most straightforward yet: a collection of immaculately produced house and techno whose simplicity belies its considerable depth.

title: If You Asked for a Picture
description: On her second album of dreamy, ’90s-indebted alt-rock, Sabrina Teitelbaum interrogates mid-20s heartache and complex family relationships with bluntness and guarded optimism.

title: UW6
description: The DMV street rapper’s latest paints vivid scenes with cold and dour lyrics over glitzy and alluring beats.

title: Pirouette
description: The raucous Brooklyn quartet follows up its celebrated debut with an icy, crisp album that’s strikingly honest about self-consciousness in the face of desire.

title: Oh What a Beautiful World
description: The 92-year-old country legend interprets the songs of fellow Texan Rodney Crowell, whose plainspoken, deceptively catchy melodies fit as comfortably as an old pair of boots.

title: Bloodless
description: On her flinty third album, the Minneapolis singer sharpens her storytelling, lacing deceptively bright folk pop with small, evocative details.

title: Melting Moment
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we look back at the 1992 cult classic that introduced a Japanese underground icon’s intoxicating blend of trip-hop, UK club, yé-yé, and dream pop.

title: Blue Veil
description: The British cellist’s catalog includes longform drone with Kali Malone and Bach recordings on ECM; her minimalist solo debut on the instrument is rigorous, austere, and breathtaking.

title: Iris Silver Mist
description: The Norwegian avant-garde artist’s ninth album—inspired by a love of perfume—examines impermanence, transformation, and the nature of performance.

title: Face Down in the Garden
description: The indie-pop duo caps its career with a sumptuously produced, exceedingly pleasant album that coasts on vibe.

title: Taba
description: The Japanese ambient folk artist’s fourth album is awash in the sounds of the outside world—birdsong, wind, rushing water—while her hushed singing and acoustic guitar signal meditative stillness.

title: I Don’t Know How But They Found Me!
description: The Los Angeles singer-songwriter does battle with cruel exes and her own inner critic on a focused album of Y2K soft-pop that sometimes suffers from lyrical oversaturation.

title: (The) Forever Dream
description: The Virginia rapper relaxes his typical metronomic precision and adopts a shaggier, more footloose demeanor on a warm-spirited new album executive-produced by Quelle Chris.

title: Weirdo
description: Faced with unimaginable grief, the UK musician responded the only way she knew how: with an album of buoyant jazz-funk steeped in melody, vibrant color, and a sneaky sense of humor.

title: Time Indefinite
description: The Nashville guitarist’s latest album is an act of reckoning: Collaging together found sounds and field recordings with his own fingerpicking, it feels like an elegy for a nation in free fall.

title: Gloorp ’Em Up
description: Philly percussionist Garrett Burke’s new dance tape is one skull-rattling fill after another, a daisy-chained string of mulching beats that’s casual, light, and fun as hell.

title: Hex Key
description: On their third album, the Atlanta indie rockers channel a tactful self-assurance while following their trippy, idiosyncratic impulses.

title: Live at Revolution Hall
description: The Big Thief singer’s sprawling, sentimental live album presents a vivid archive of the ephemera orbiting any formal performance. Perfection is not the goal here—presence is.

title: A Complicated Woman
description: The UK star repeats some of her breakout album’s formula but little of its lacerating insight on a record where the Big Feminist Statements feel frustratingly basic.

title: E
description: The 27-year-old pianist and singer channels jazz titans like Carla Bley and Annette Peacock on her austere, haunting debut, lavishing attention on the contours of every syllable.

title: Under Tangled Silence
description: Pairing fluid improvised piano with mind-bendingly complex drum programming, the UK producer returns with a mercurial survey of what sound like his deepest emotions.

title: Fada<3of$
description: The bite-sized songs on the Brooklyn-via-Florida rapper’s debut almost feel like demos, but they sparkle with nostalgia for gold rims and TR-808s.

title: Demilitarize
description: The Angolan producer’s debut album was inspired by the country’s civil war; his new one delves into interior turmoil. It’s a gripping, destabilizing, psychedelic take on kuduro.

title: Hysteria
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we look back at the unlikely, multi-platinum smash that perfected pop metal—and brought the genre to its logical endpoint.

title: Totality
description: Nine years after their last collaborative LP, the two Chicago experimental mainstays meet up for another heady set of psychedelic drone and corkscrewing grooves.

title: Luster
description: The Irish musician’s gossamer dream pop is both mythic and real, a wild and ancient landscape in which her own figure is just barely perceptible.

title: Alex
description: Mountain Man’s Alex Sauser-Monnig applies the playful sound of early-2010s alt-pop to the more troubling realities of the mid-2020s, and mostly pulls it off.

title: Lorings
description: Lindsay Olsen’s new album trades cosmological conjecture for a spirit of inner contemplation, revealing her as an uncommonly inventive and endearing songwriter.

title: WITH A VENGEANCE
description: The British DJ's debut shifts frenetically between high-speed dance genres. Her meticulousness and evocative samples lend the record an impressively narrative, emotional quality.

title: Natural Pleasure
description: The raucous Oklahoma quartet mellows out its garage-rock grit for a hazy, introspective record that doesn’t abandon the band’s signature playfulness.

title: Chaos Practitioner EP
description: Seven months after its debut LP, the Brooklyn art-pop duo returns with a short, energetic EP crammed with more ideas than many records three times as long.

title: Noble and Godlike in Ruin
description: On its latest album, the veteran quartet sounds coarse, raucous, and refreshingly immune to the staid professionalism that tends to afflict bands in their fourth decade of existence.

title: Dance Music 4 Bad People
description: With roiling rhythms and Atlas-shouldered basslines, Chicago house veteran Jamal Moss’ new album aims to give dancefloor whiners something to really cry about.

title: Papaholic, Vol. 1
description: The New Jersey rapper and producer pair up again for a throwback East Coast hip-hop tape that doesn’t feel stuck on regional clichés.

title: Resonance
description: The cult Cleveland artist—beloved by Elliott Smith and Guided by Voices—keeps a low profile, but his classic rock influences are anything but esoteric. His first LP in 13 years feels particularly timeless.

title: Stadium Lo Champions
description: The Toronto rapper-producer duo’s new collaboration feels outside time, as if it really were recorded in the ’90s and only recently unearthed from some moldy basement in Staten Island.

title: 5ive
description: The Nigerian pop superstar’s fifth album is a show of confidence, an intoxicating breath of ocean air and amor fati.

title: Bite Down
description: The Montreal indie-rock duo formerly known as Love Language reinvents itself with a stark, stripped-down sound and potent songwriting informed by singer Tashiina Buswa’s Anishinaabe heritage.

title: Crisis Kid
description: The former SoundCloud star flits between unflappability and panic on an ambitious album that marries sunny melodies with existential exhaustion.

title: Rain Dogs
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the singer-songwriter’s inimitable 1985 album, a romantic and carnivalesque masterpiece imbued with the avant-garde sound of New York.

title: CULTURE
description: The latest from the Minneapolis producer is full of dramatic transitions and collagist sound design as he enlists a small army of underground rappers to sample his vibey, blown-out sound.

title: Send a Prayer My Way
description: The two singer-songwriters embrace their Southern roots for a country collaboration. Their folksy depictions of queer love are charming, but their humor and homage often land awkwardly.

title: A Study of Losses
description: For Zach Condon to write music for a troupe of acrobats might seem a little too on the nose, given his roots. But the results are the most effortless and surprising Beirut album in ages.

title: The Pines
description: Compressing 8,760 hours of field recordings from a single pine tree into a four-hour epic, The Pines isn’t just a nature documentary; it’s a meditation on listening and subjectivity.

title: More Chaos
description: On the sequel to his rage-rap opus A Great Chaos, Opium’s heir apparent goes through familiar motions in hopes of making lightning strike twice.

title: Thee Black Boltz
description: The TV on the Radio singer sharpens his voice on his debut solo album, using bold synth melodies and driving beats as the backdrop to some of his most nuanced performances yet.

title: E.M.O. (EVIL MOTION OVERLOAD)
description: With a combination of hyperpop abrasion and bratty punch-ins, the 19-year-old rapper’s debut EP positions her as a pop diva working on the borders of club music.

title: Take Me Out to a Bar / What Am I, Gatsby?
description: Paring back to just piano, sustain, and her scratchy alto, the wry, candid New Zealand songwriter gets reluctantly reacquainted with optimism.

title: 4EVA
description: On her most energetic release yet, the Seoul producer and member of Salamanda draws on contemporary club styles to showcase her restlessly inventive approach.

title: TANYA
description: The Buenos Aires singer winks at the devil on her shoulder, channeling romantic misadventure into feverish club maximalism.

title: Welcome to My Blue Sky
description: The Brooklyn alt-rock band rides a wave of guitar fuzz through songs about love, longing, and surviving your early 20s. It’s intimate without ever revealing too much.

title: Based on a True Story
description: The star’s first album in two decades is a pointless apology tour for the dumbest Oscar gaffe in history, treating his Chris Rock slap as a grand teachable moment. It’s as corny as it is calculating.

title: Seeking Darkness
description: The visionary, mysterious South Korean musician behind Parannoul broadens his palette for a set of cacophonous, murky compositions.

title: On a Painted Ocean
description: On his second solo album, the former Hurray for the Riff Raff and Weyes Blood collaborator might just make you think about the accordion in a whole new way.

artist: Gregory Uhlmann / Josh Johnson / Sam Wilkes
title: Uhlmann Johnson Wilkes
description: On their first album as a trio, the L.A. musicians combine complex polyrhythms and ambient cooldowns with help from a remarkable array of effects.

title: a strong desire to survive
description: The New York singer toggles between defeat and defiance on a syrupy R&B album that, though sometimes disjointed, highlights their acrobatic, powerhouse voice.

title: Underground Vol. 1: 1991-1994
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a slice of 1990s Memphis rap lore: 15 gloomy, hard-hitting, massively influential tracks from the early days of Three Six Mafia.

title: The Sacrificial Code
description: A new reissue offers a chance to revisit the experimental composer’s breakthrough 2019 album for pipe organ, an otherworldly maze of tones with a powerful emotional pull.

artist: Dirty Projectors / David Longstreth / s t a r g a z e
title: Song of the Earth
description: David Longstreth’s first major piece for a large ensemble, a commission by the Berlin-based chamber orchestra, is nearly monotonous in its restless variety.

title: NO BRING INS
description: The North London rapper’s debut signals superstar ambition, but her syncopated flows and roughneck punchlines get watered down when she tries to appease an audience.

title: When the Distance Is Blue
description: Accompanied by Lia Kohl, Whitney Johnson, and Zach Moore, the Chicago multi-instrumentalist folds prepared piano, string quartet, and field recordings into elegant expressions of nameless longing.

title: SABLE, fABLE
description: On his fifth album, Justin Vernon moves out of the shadows and into an unabashedly joyful mindset and soundscape. His music remains as compelling as ever.

title: Little House EP
description: On a sunny new EP, the British Zimbabwean pop upstart leans into her chatty, accessible style and witty songwriting.

title: Tripla
description: After publishing her memoir, the former Lush singer-guitarist returned to songwriting. Rooted in shoegaze and dream pop, her new LP is tinged with sadness—but fueled by joy of playing again.

title: Stochastic Drift
description: On his second LP, the Berlin-based musician opens himself to chance and presents a vision of techno that harnesses randomness for all its potential. He emerges a more remarkable musician than ever.

title: Bunky Becky Birthday Boy
description: You may long for 2010, but the jittery, irreverent pop-punk of the duo’s new album can’t recapture the fluorescent glow of their glory days.

title: A Requiem
description: After the dream pop of her self-titled trilogy, the Australian-born, UK-based musician explores darker ambient textures on an album rooted in ancestry, trauma, and ritual.

title: F*CK U SKRILLEX YOU THINK UR ANDY WARHOL BUT UR NOT!! <3
description: There are so many ideas packed into Sonny Moore’s whirlwind of an album—wubsmaxxing basslines, abrupt left turns, absurdist DJ tags—that it’s hard not to be bowled over by its sheer force of will.

title: Jellywish
description: Embracing a playful, almost hallucinogenic sound, the indie-folk band suffuses its fifth album with wide-eyed awe at everyday miracles.

title: The Crux
description: Actor and musician Joe Keery’s third album aspires to something big. But though it’s performed with care and craft, its frictionless blend of styles feels a bit uncanny.

title: Revengeseekerz
description: The experimental artist does a complete 180 from their previous record and unleashes an inferno of raw thoughts that pushes everything—rap, pop, voice, their artistic persona—to the breaking point.

title: Forever Howlong
description: After several years of lineup and repertoire changes, the UK group returns with an ambitious and unabashedly twee album overflowing with baroque flourishes and communal spirit.

title: OI!
description: The UK rapper’s studio debut builds on the jerk sound of his previous mixtape with playful, hard-hitting instrumentals but sacrifices some of the personality that animated his breakthrough.

title: New York Dolls
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit downtown New York in the early 1970s and the debut album by the flashy, trashy rock’n’rollers who cleared the way for punk.

title: Maintenant Jamais
description: The Montreal trio’s mix of prog excess and punk attitude landed its 2020 debut on John Dwyer’s Castle Face label. On LP no. 3, the group hones its songwriting while honoring its exploratory instincts.

title: Los Thuthanaka
description: In siblings Chuquimamani-Condori and Joshua Chuquimia Crampton’s dense, elaborate thicket of sound, traditional genres and ancestral wisdom coexist with digital ephemera and rapturous noise.

title: star
description: The internet rapper and producer’s new album is wired-up and ready to dance, confronting his growing fame through festival-ready beats that bang like post-millennial supernovae.

title: their internal diapasons
description: The Polish composer’s spectral, textural music—written on an instrument he designed from scavenged organ pipes—swarms with beautifully unruly ideas.

title: Music Can Hear Us
description: Playfully swerving through house, Afrobeats, and wistful German-language pop, Stefan Kozalla’s latest album makes good on his inextinguishable supply of curiosity and childlike wonder.

title: Watch Over My Body
description: Through a haze of ambient textures and uncanny rhythms, the Maryland artist’s insular, atmospheric struggle rap makes the familiar feel alien.

title: Gleaming Cursed
description: On their debut album, the Vancouver punks distill the urgency and anxiety of 1990s emo and post-hardcore into their own insistent, gnarly sound.

title: hexed!
description: Sound bristles, foams, bursts, and oozes as the UK artist’s daring second album confronts the terrifying crush of reality. It feels like witchcraft; maybe it is.

title: You Are Always on My Mind
description: On their fourth solo release, the Brooklyn sound artist and composer threads together downtempo rap, sound collage, and pop hooks to examine memory and self-transformation.

title: Portrait of My Heart
description: The Bay Area musician’s new album is an elegant, stormy take on the nu-metal, pop-punk, and ’90s guitar superstars who soundtracked millennial angst.

title: Dan’s Boogie
description: Dan Bejar’s 14th Destroyer record is contemplative, morning-after music par excellence: He’s putting the whole story back together, knowing it’s all going to fall apart.

title: End Beginnings
description: The techno collective once known for its unrelenting severity loosens up after a 13-year break. But while the mood has lightened, the group sometimes seems to lack its former sense of purpose.

title: Perfect Teeth (30th Anniversary Edition)
description: An expanded reissue of the indie-pop icons’ 1993 swan song highlights the contradictions—youthful innocence and teenage lust; scrappy punk and lovelorn ballads—that made the group unique.

title: Gift Songs
description: The ambient experimental musician’s latest record is cohesive, fluid, and egoless. Using an almost entirely acoustic palette, he and his collaborators channel an abiding sense of mystery.

title: Patience, Moonbeam
description: A much-anticipated follow-up to the Seattle quintet’s 2019 debut explores themes of life change with gratitude, sincerity, and an exquisite sense of drama.

title: i was put on this earth EP
description: Singing for the first time on a solo DJ Python record, Brian Piñeyro trades the reggaeton and deep house of earlier releases for softer, more abstracted sounds couched in trip-hop, shoegaze, and pop.

title: Live! at the Star-Club in Hamburg, Germany; 1962
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a storied piece of Beatles lore, a bootleg that captures—in glorious low fidelity—a band on the brink of changing the world.

title: Tonky
description: A handful of all-star contributors turn the avant-garde singer’s seventh album into a big-hearted, transcendental testimonial.

title: Forever Is a Feeling
description: On her new solo album, the songwriter and Boygenius alum makes an impassioned, all-in gamble on love. So why does the music feel hamstrung by caution and daintiness?

title: Lonely People With Power
description: Following a divisively tuneful 2021 album, the California post-metal band returns to its signature sound on its sixth album. But these heavy, soaring songs also hint at unexplored terrain.

title: IC-02 Bogotá
description: The latest in Ruban Nielson’s globe-trotting series taps into a cosmic, extroverted energy, highlighting his band’s virtuosity in a set of psychedelic jams.

title: Glory
description: Mike Hadreas’ seventh studio album brings a more elegant and capacious sound to unanswerable questions of anxiety, grief, and disconnection.

title: is
description: Veteran producer Brendan O’Brien helps craft the epitome of a modern My Morning Jacket LP. It captures their classic style and sound, but lacks the adventurousness that defines their best work.

title: Channels
description: On its debut album, the British duo stirs house, techno, and Balearic beat into a luxuriously appointed soundtrack to Mediterranean downtime that’s carefully balanced between dancefloor and lounge chair.

title: 45 Pounds
description: On their outstanding debut, the New York-based experimental rockers show up fully formed with vision, presence, and possibility.

title: Defiant Life
description: The second collaborative album by the jazz composers and instrumentalists is a searching meditation on resistance and revolutionary potential.

title: Battle Zone
description: The footwork veteran’s Planet Mu debut gathers a decade’s worth of tracks that showcase his thrillingly skewed take on the genre, drizzling pitched-down samples over woozy drum programming.

title: From the Private Collection of Saba and No ID
description: Rapper Saba and producer No ID collaborate for a master class in melodic rap that harnesses ’90s sampledelia, ’00s neo-soul, and the singsong lyricism of 2010s Chicago.

title: I Said I Love You First
description: The collaboration between the singer and her producer fiancé has big romantic appeal but mostly contains serviceable, pastiched pop songs that reveal little about their love story.

title: Moneyball
description: After the lo-fi slowcore of its first two albums, the L.A. sextet embraces a welter of instruments, some carefully chosen country influences, and sentimental feelings delivered with a wink.

title: Radio DDR
description: Lifeguard’s Kai Slater bottles the feeling of youthful, lovestruck invincibility with enough scream-a-long hooks and artful riffs that his second album feels like a greatest-hits collection.

title: No Floor
description: The Texan experimentalists reflect on their friendship and interwoven careers in a moving set of ambient pieces inspired by bars and venues they’ve visited.

title: Every Video Without Your Face, Every Sound Without Your Name
description: The California sound artist assembles bare piano, melancholy vocal melodies, and engulfing silence into a stark meditation on desire, absence, and acceptance.

title: My War
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we look at a 1984 record that rewrote the rules of punk, balancing hardcore’s jackhammer attack with dirge-like heavy metal, and helping pave the way for grunge, stoner rock, and beyond.

title: Flora
description: Never released until 2006, three years after the ambient composer’s death, this 1987 recording is an outlier in his catalog—less plainly atmospheric, more melodic and mischievous.

title: For Melancholy Brunettes (& sad women)
description: Michelle Zauner’s lovely, pensive, capital-R Romantic fourth album takes a step back from autobiography to examine the performances and peril of fame itself.

title: Affectionately
description: Where her group Good Sad Happy Bad’s post-punk sounds effortless, Raisa K’s careful soundscaping—blending lo-fi guitars, low-key vocals, and industrial clang—is immaculately controlled.

title: Elvers Pass
description: The Welsh producer’s latest mini-album gathers some of his most intricate and inventive music yet, adding elasticity, humor, and deeply plaintive moments to a classic minimal-house palette.

title: Consentrik Quartet
description: In a new quartet of seasoned New York improvisers, the Wilco guitarist reveals his range, balancing soft duets with hard grooves and ballads with bedlam.

artist: Anoushka Shankar / Alam Khan / Sarathy Korwar
title: Chapter III: We Return to Light EP
description: Alongside sarod and percussion, the sitarist and composer—daughter of virtuoso Ravi Shankar—closes out her suite of mini-albums with a record dedicated to musical heritage and blissful optimism.

title: October Country
description: The Haunted Mound founding member reunites with Sematary for a debut solo mixtape that rekindles their chemistry and sets the bar for witch house revivalism.

title: Exploding Trees & Airplane Screams
description: The Drive-By Truckers co-founder’s fourth solo album features contributions from Wednesday, Waxahatchee, and more. Surreal and cinematic, it’s his most adventurous solo release—and his best.

title: Never Catch Us
description: The New Orleans rapper and New York producer continue a fruitful partnership that goes back over a decade. Pairing extravagant boasts with sumptuous beats, it’s a thoroughly luxurious affair.

title: Georgie
description: George Lewis Jr. pares down his sound for an understated alt-R&B album that’s both beautiful and aimless.

title: MUSIC
description: Carti’s long-awaited third official album is a blockbuster event that synthesizes all of his impulses—good and bad—into a dizzying, inspired, vibes-driven, 30-track flood of everything.

title: two house
description: The post-hyperpop pranksters’ second album is music by and for people who spend too much time online, a firehose blast of memes and brainrot. But beneath the chaos lie moments of surprising sensitivity.

title: Zombie Love Kensington Paradise (Deluxe)
description: The fascinating rise of the idiosyncratic Philly rapper over the last year culminates with a solid showcase in the form of a deluxe version of his 2024 album.

title: Whatever the Weather II
description: By narrowing its focus to muted synth pads and minimalist arrangements, the second LP from Loraine James’ ambient-leaning produces some of the most direct, spontaneous music in her catalog.

title: Turnar
description: The Icelandic thereminist’s latest album finds new depths in the century-old instrument, forgoing its campy, sci-fi associations in favor of uncanny horror.

title: Blood on the Silver Screen
description: On her third album, the Los Angeles songwriter pivots to pop. When she leans into outsized production and campy hooks, she soars—but more often, her anemic songwriting falters.

title: La question
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the French singer’s arresting 1971 album, a highlight of her career, a lovelorn mélange of spare Brazilian folk and the chanteuse traditions of her youth.

title: Lonesome Drifter
description: Following in a long tradition of country singers on the skids, the Grammy-nominated Texan songwriter’s new album recounts a trail of broken promises and broken hearts.

title: Halo on the Inside
description: Created in the depth of night, Haley Fohr’s latest studio album sounds like her take on industrial dance music: sludgy, colossal, and teeming with darkness.

title: Clique City Vol. 2
description: The Chicago rapper stands out from SoundCloud rap’s nostalgia parade thanks to his strong songwriting and knack for harmonies—but his millennial revivalist gimmick works for and against him.

title: The Near End, The Dark Night, The County Line
description: The Japanese guitarist and improviser has collaborated with Haruomi Hosono and Nels Cline. His new album collects 10 years’ worth of shape-shifting dream-pop and minimalist jazz.

title: Cotton Crown
description: On his jangle-pop group’s second album, the former Joanna Gruesome singer finds unlikely inspiration in familial grief. Against his glum lyrics and cold, stricken voice, the music chugs along merrily.

title: Myrtus Myth
description: The electro-pop singer-producer’s fourth album is operatic in scope and tone, exploring grief and hopelessness in soaring vocals and epic scenes of beasts, angels, and the cosmos.

title: The Hurtless
description: Harto Falión’s vocals are an ideal match for Evilgiane’s vaporous, meditative production, but his expressions of detachment and dissociation are as hollow as the feelings themselves.

title: This Side of the Island
description: The Walkmen frontman’s third solo album is scattershot and charming, full of beachside vignettes about doomed lovers and aimless wanderers.

title: Ruby
description: The BLACKPINK singer powers her solo debut with versatility and charm, translating the group’s tough-girl sound into a blistering new style.

title: Eternal Reverie
description: On her latest album, the L.A. producer trades the grit and swung rhythms of her early work for sleek house and disco beats. The vibes are dreamy—sometimes to a fault.

title: Another Life
description: Pitched somewhere between Pinegrove and Bladee, the Swedish duo winkingly reframes contemporary indie sounds and beloved pop samples for a debut album that’s goofy yet undeniably beautiful.

title: All Worlds
description: Reuniting on a double-billed album, the Danish musicians draw on 20 years’ worth of indie dance textures for a sound that’s summery yet distant.

title: Gaman
description: The San Jose power-pop band bottles nervous energy into compact, combustible hooks and sets them off with no time to spare.

title: MAYHEM
description: On her seventh album, Lady Gaga returns to pop with the larger-than-life sound. She delves into the inner turmoil of fame while reminding you why she’s earned it.

title: Violence
description: The Montreal-via-Alberta punks solder together noise rock, sludge metal, bluegrass, and post-hardcore for a forceful—and moving—rejection of stereotypes of their prairie homeland.

title: If Not to Give a Fantasy
description: Speed begets speed as the Brooklyn-based DJ and musician applies a fresh coat of polish to her pugnacious, unrelenting industrial hardcore.

title: On How Life Is
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Macy Gray’s misunderstood 1999 debut and the unlikely story that shaped its wise songwriting and chameleonic sound.

title: Ted Lucas (Extended)
description: Half a century after its initial release, a treasure of private-press folk music finally gets an expanded reissue. Its songs remain sweet, sad, and completely enchanting.

title: A Blade Because a Blade Is Whole
description: On the British saxophonist and poet’s graceful new album, the reminders to savor each day and to forgive oneself feel less like jazz tunes than wordless hymns.

title: Sheer Hellish Miasma II
description: The Chicago sound artist follows up his landmark 2002 noise opus with a 92-minute behemoth that’s even more brutally unrelenting.

title: On the Yeah Side Deluxe
description: For the latest edition of their collaborative series, the rapper and producer invite fellow Detroit voices into the fold—but the album is at its best when highlighting the duo’s locked-in chemistry.

title: City of Clowns
description: Forget dancing like no one’s watching: The Québécois musician’s latest LP is raving under surveillance capitalism, offering pranksterish critiques over Y2K-inspired beats.

title: All Cylinders
description: The Canadian psych-pop auteur’s new album is less interested in paying homage to the golden oldies than in discovering what playful new mutations he can get away with.

title: Horses
description: With plaintive harmonies and a subdued, country-rock sound, the Chicago group sketches a vision of the nation’s hinterlands filled with strip mall vistas, diner grease, and subtle transcendence.

title: Luminescent Creatures
description: Inspired by creatures she encountered diving in the waters off a remote island, the Japanese singer-songwriter’s understated, beautiful album explores liminal worlds through softly textured ambient folk

title: Alter Ego
description: On the BLACKPINK singer and rapper’s solo debut, her various musical identities add up to the generic embodiment of a pop star.

title: Tears of Injustice
description: An acoustic reworking of Funeral for Injustice highlights the fearsome adaptability of the Nigerien singer-guitarist and his band, as well as the tensions of their position on a world stage.

title: Sinister Grift
description: Assisted by his Animal Collective bandmates, Noah Lennox’s latest solo LP is disarmingly laid-back. It might be his most straightforwardly beautiful record—and also his most emotionally complex.

title: Old Joy EP
description: The score for Kelly Reichardt's 2006 drama, written by the indie-rock veterans and session guitarist Smokey Hormel, captures the magisterial doldrums of an American road trip in countrified krautrock.

title: Billboard Heart
description: Frontwoman Jessica Dobson’s powerful voice and gnarled guitar solos grant the Seattle band’s propulsive, riff-laden indie rock a new level of yearning intensity.

title: Club Shy Room 2 EP
description: The London singer and producer builds on the mid-’00s glamor of last year’s Club Shy EP with pulsing hooks, euphoric self-assurance, and a VIP guest list of features.

title: Erotica Veronica
description: The LA songwriter scales down to a no-frills soft rock sound for a nuanced, self-aware album that takes a personal lens to relationships and queer identity.

title: Opening Night
description: ​​Recorded live at the opening gala of a Hollywood theater, the Danish duo—accompanied on one song by Laurel Halo—performs a moody, minimalist tribute to LA.

title: Album – Generic Flipper
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a 1982 album in which hardcore punk’s oppositional spirit turned on itself—a nihilistic spiral both profound and absurd.

title: Spring Board: The Early Unrecorded Songs
description: A final album from the New Zealand indie-pop vets revives decades-old compositions by its late frontman with winsome optimism and a keen eye for the passage of time.

title: Nothing
description: Guided by the idea of wiping the slate clean, Nicolás Jaar and Dave Harrington’s third album is a raw, surprisingly funky, desperately hopeful response to the chaos of the 2020s.

title: Sleepers
description: The London-via-Glasgow duo’s second album of gothic folk songs romanticizes bleakness and melancholy—which, depending on your mood, can feel like an indulgent luxury or a gloomy endurance test.

title: Mela EP
description: The New York duo channels the intensity of West Bengal’s earthshaking soundcheck battles into rowdy, celebratory bass music.

title: Jupiter
description: The British singer’s fourth LP is a light, uplifting journey through R&B and nu-disco that lands on some thin cosmic metaphors.

title: Gut
description: With a newly muscular sound, Will Wiesenfeld’s first Baths album in eight years examines the giddy, pleasure-seeking joys of queerness alongside loneliness and desperation.

title: Goodbye Horses: The Many Lives of Q Lazzarus (Music From the Motion Picture)
description: Though her song soundtracked an iconic scene in The Silence of the Lambs, the New Jersey singer stayed unknown. A new documentary explores her life on the margins of fame—and behind the wheel of a cab.

title: Shards
description: This short, varied collection of the Canadian composer’s soundtrack work feels like a short film in its own right: part sci-fi noir, part android tearjerker.

title: So Close to What
description: On her third album, the Canadian singer and dancer amps up the 2000s influence and dials up the sex. Though it’s her most mature release yet, the music still sounds tedious and reheated.

title: List of Demands
description: The musician and educator layers samples of historical audio, minimal loops, and his spoken-word poetry to lay out a vision of Black liberation rooted in community and creativity.

title: #mia
description: The British crooner’s new mini-album builds on the heartache of their breakout LP with an evocative meld of rap-rock electronica.

title: Sometimes I Forget to Breathe
description: The Philly producer takes a big leap with an album of freeform synth grooves inspired by the hyperkinetic blasts of late-’90s and early-’00s IDM.

title: Malignant Worthlessness
description: In what they’ve hinted could be their final album, the Philadelphia death-metal extremists pair pummeling riffs with otherworldly vocal experiments. It’s hypnotic, psychedelic, and brutal.

title: Rarely Do I Dream
description: On a record combining driving rhythms, cinematic synths, and snatches of home videos, Trevor Powers sketches a gothic frontier strewn with fabled characters and blood relations.

title: Food From the Gods
description: The producer and MC, longtime fixtures of Detroit rap, team back up for an album of gritty boom-bap beats and nimble wordplay. Their genuine chemistry reinvigorates familiar touchstones.

title: Horror
description: The genre-blurring indie rocker’s third album—half co-produced by Jack Antonoff—is ambitious and messy, grappling with deep-seated fears about the search for stability in a world of dread.

title: In Search of the Turtle’s Navel
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a sublime 1976 solo guitar album, a humbly brilliant record that spawned a colossal new-age music empire.

title: People Watching
description: On his third album, the UK’s own heartland rocker casts an empathetic eye on modern British life. Even as he shouts at max volume, he sometimes gets lost in the wall of sound.

title: Saya
description: On her second album, the Japanese-Canadian musician’s magpie art pop coheres into something like a traditional breakup record, but her perspective and production are far from conventional.

title: I Love You, Honeybear Demos, etc.
description: Gone are the sweeping strings and the galloping mariachi band: On demos for his breakout 2015 album, Josh Tillman’s naked vocals clip and echo as he stress-tests his home recording equipment.

title: 1000 Variations on the Same Song
description: For their sixth album of indie folk, brothers Daniel and Steve Bateman discovered this one weird trick to speed up the process: embrace the hallmarks of their songwriting.

title: Like a Ribbon
description: The London musician’s unyielding deadpan anchors a stylish debut that counters the high expectations of city hustle with nature’s eternal tranquility.

title: Love Me As I Am
description: On his second full-length, the Maryland rapper confronts real-life struggle with emo-tinged production and a sensitivity that transcends pain-rap tropes.

title: In the Blue Light
description: A masterful re-interpreter of her own songs, the future-facing singer-songwriter gives a lush, harp-assisted performance of music from across her discography at New York’s famed Blue Note Jazz Club.

title: $ome $exy $ongs 4 U
description: $ome $exy $ongs 4 U is a desperate album from one of rap’s most notorious narcissists. Oh, and PARTYNEXTDOOR is here, too.

title: Phonetics On and On
description: For their second album, produced by Cate Le Bon, the New York-via-Chicago indie rockers adopt a spirit of linguistic playfulness and a newly pared-back sound.

title: The Last Days of May
description: As part of the boutique label’s final crop of releases, the Austrian experimental musician strips back and stretches out, exploring the nuances of his guitar in real time.

title: End of the Middle
description: On a pared-back acoustic epilogue to his trilogy of solo records, the Newcastle prog-folk musician examines the way family histories repeat themselves.

title: Följd
description: In Swedish producer Thomas Bodén’s patient, minimalistic studies, an extended drone or a beatific glow conceal a world of unanticipated detail.

title: KISS (Keep It Short & Sweet) EP
description: The rapper’s debut EP puts a flirty spin on classic New Orleans bounce with sauced-up throwbacks, creative samples, and expert comedic timing.

title: Fontanelle
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Babes in Toyland’s overlooked 1992 album, a raw rock exorcism that connected grunge to the beginning of the riot grrrl sound.

title: 1991 / Delaware
description: A new remaster titled 1991 presents the demo tracks that anointed the young Boston shoegaze band in the British press and paved the way to their landmark debut, Delaware.

title: Ghostholding
description: A new album by the artist aka Jane Remover is full of sprawling, fearsome beauty, both compositionally tighter and texturally coarser than their past forays into rock.

title: The Breeze Grew a Fire
description: The Los Angeles-based singer, guitarist, and rapper finds refuge on her second solo album, buoyed by looser arrangements and immediate, declarative songwriting.

title: Another Farewell
description: The Canadian roots group romanticizes the open road on a debut album filled with weird cowboy songs, streamlined saloon rockers, big-hearted folk tracks, and pastoral psychedelia.

title: Thirteen Sense
description: The South London musician filters nu-metal and millennial pop into an enveloping noise LP—part of a broader microverse of contemporary experimental guitar music informed by modern rock radio.

title: For the Mature
description: The Philadelphia rapper’s new album positions him as an elder statesman with a Swiss Army knife skillset, even when some song concepts fall short.

title: Dim Binge
description: On a promising debut mixtape, the East London singer-producer channels Sampha, Thom Yorke, and Arthur Russell in whispered dirges and haunted soul.

title: Cowards
description: Building on the sociopolitical themes of previous LPs, the UK post-punks’ latest frames even heavier subject matter—the nature of evil itself—in darkly dazzling songs at once ominous and luxurious.

title: GetEm
description: On his latest album, the D.C. rapper attempts to separate himself from a pack of DMV rappers. The beats are beautiful chaos, but it’s missing his personality.

title: Life Is Beautiful
description: Over placid production from the Alchemist, the two rappers combine their respective styles—Larry June’s nonchalance and 2 Chainz’s spontaneity—for a record that’s pleasant but a bit underwhelming.

title: Madvillainy Demos
description: Over a year before the world heard the groundbreaking Madvillainy, a stolen demo cassette was leaked onto the internet. Now that the bootleg has been officially reissued, the arguing and comparisons can recommence.

title: Ascension
description: The French-Norwegian metal duo’s debut album showcases a style halfway between djent and dubstep. Packed with flayed tones, mutilated hooks, and textural trickery, it’s depraved yet weirdly tasteful.

title: choke enough
description: On her full-length debut, the French electronic pop darling presents a twilit fusion of Y2K worship, Baroque polyphony, and elegant, opaque ambiance.

title: Lay Low
description: On his third solo album, with production by Nick Hakim, the R&B singer contemplates life’s circuitous paths in a set of glossy, minimalist songs.

title: Leaving Home
description: The 18-year-old rapper and producer’s second solo album is a coming-of-age record that foregrounds his vulnerabilty—yet he’s never sounded so confident.

title: The Blossom Filled Streets
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a lost indie rock gem from 2000, an ethereal and luminescent highlight of the underground Bristol scene.

title: A Ghost Is Born (Deluxe Edition)
description: A mammoth 13-piece box set unpacks the origins of Wilco’s wild, ambitious fifth album, including four revelatory LPs of alternates and outtakes.

artist: Sharon Van Etten / The Attachment Theory
title: Sharon Van Etten & The Attachment Theory
description: The singer fills her stormy seventh album—billed as a collaborative effort with her bandmates—with post-punk motifs and reflections on clinging to love amid apocalyptic upheaval.

title: Dear Psilocybin
description: Created just before getting sober, the Detroit rapper’s latest album charts a path through psychosis, with appropriately psychedelic—and at times surprisingly melodic—production.

title: TUMPIT
description: Weird wrinkles are the best part of this mellow, left-field rap mixtape from the UK producer and vocalist with a catalog full of offbeat experiments.

title: A Shaw Deal
description: The Animal Collective member transforms guitar riffs by Highlife’s Doug Shaw into modular synth abstractions. Its abrasive tone may not be for everyone, but its funky, egoless spirit is infectious.

title: Ways to the Deep Meadow
description: Longtime electronic explorer Joe Tye pays tribute to classic ambient and new age with an album of billowing pads, gentle arpeggios, and wide-eyed wonder.

title: Eduardo Polonio: Obra Electroacústica 1969-1981
description: A new anthology rescues the work of the pioneering Spanish electroacoustic musician, whose breathtakingly radical work signaled a new spirit of openness after the fall of the dictatorship.

title: Humanhood
description: Written in the wake of personal crisis—and in the midst of global upheaval—Tamara Lindeman’s latest album, a lush and stirring tangle of acoustic and electronic textures, searches for meaning in chaos.

title: BLACK’!ANTIQUE
description: The rapper’s third solo LP is a community affair, gathering some two dozen friends and collaborators for a bold, noisy album that gradually settles into a soulful groove.

title: So Wavy Luciano
description: The New York City rapper pushes hedonism to the extreme, delivering paranoid self-awareness and off-kilter cadences over moody plugg production.

title: Hurry Up Tomorrow
description: Abel Tesfaye gives his sordid, heartbroken pop-star persona a long, opulent finale: He’s going out on top by hitting rock bottom.

title: Forever
description: The Nashville singer-songwriter’s latest album is an ode to the intimacy of domestic bliss that doesn’t sound intimate at all; it’s a rousing rock record steeped in the sounds of ’90s alternative.

title: Louder, Please
description: Assisted by a crew of dance-pop hitmakers, the UK singer trades past singles’ glittery diva house for a darker, seedier strain of club pop steeped in well-worn hedonistic tropes.

title: Jump Out
description: On his third album, SoundCloud rap’s new-gen torchbearer presents his most volatile and electrifying work to date. His sound is as distinct as it’s ever been.

title: Forms of Paper (2024 remaster)
description: The Los Angeles artist and composer coaxed unexpected sounds from daily life. Newly remastered, his 2001 composition made from the sounds of books offers an intensely psychedelic listening experience.

title: v.i.p. - very important pony EP
description: With a rubber horse mask and a stable full of jokes, the Berlin-based producer and DJ indulges in hardstyle, Eurodance, and happy hardcore that’s both silly and stylish.

title: Garcia
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Jerry Garcia’s 1972 debut solo album, a captivating blueprint of cosmic Americana and one of his many transcendent detours from the Dead.

artist: Ebo Taylor / Adrian Younge / Ali Shaheed Muhammad
title: Ebo Taylor JID022
description: The Jazz Is Dead series’ latest installment is a late-career gem from the Ghanaian highlife legend, backed by a well-drilled crew.

title: Showbiz!
description: The prolific Brooklyn rapper reflects on dislocation and homecoming with his most refined, spiritual-sounding album to date.

title: I recognize you from my sketches
description: The veteran producer and multi-instrumentalist—a key figure in Beirut’s independent music scene—turns samples of his peers into an ambient meditation on community.

title: I’m Just Say’n
description: On a remarkable collaboration with Swedish multi-instrumentalist Mats Gustafson, the 85-year-old free-jazz icon lays down his horn and lays into a bracing set of his own poetry.

title: The Purple Bird
description: Recorded in Nashville with seasoned locals, this is Will Oldham’s take on a country album. A sort of companion to his two previous studio LPs, it’s also his best and most focused in some time.

title: Can’t Rush Greatness
description: The ubiquitous UK rapper presents himself as success personified, the voice of a new generation. But his Columbia debut sounds market optimized and risk averse.

title: !OK!
description: One of footwork’s most exciting new artists, the Tunisian producer amasses starkly contrasting samples—trap, jazz, synth pop, lounge, video games—for a hyperactive record with a sharp sense of humor.

title: DÍA
description: The Colombian producer emerges from a period of personal upheaval with a set of brilliant, daylit dance tracks about the hard work of healing.

title: 4 Tha Freakas
description: The DMV rapper’s horndogging new tape has just one thing on its mind.

title: crazy arms
description: On an album that evokes a honky-tonk held in a punk house living room, the Olympia band finds sparks of communal joy while sorting through the stress and grief of daily life.

title: Waiting Room
description: The Oakland songwriter and field recordist’s sinister, atmospheric full-length debut is all the more unnerving for its quiet, ticking-time-bomb intensity.

title: Studio Addict
description: The Georgia rapper’s debut album adds contemporary luster to Atlanta rap’s idiosyncratic template. At its best, the record conveys artful reverence; at its worst, it sounds like glitzy cosplay.

title: DRY CRY
description: The Toronto singer and rapper steps confidently onto the global scene with a heady, party-starting blend of Brazilian funk, drill, R&B, and dancehall.

title: LOWER
description: Working with producer Kenny Segal, the New Orleans-based singer-songwriter constructs a corroded beat-centric grunge that soundtracks stories of violence and perseverance.

title: Salt River
description: The folksinger’s calling is as old as the hills. Channeling Appalachian fiddles, desert rock, Ornette Coleman, and Arthur Russell, the Vermont native keeps it moving forward, in his own inimitable style.

title: Mapambazuko
description: Peruvian electronic musician Alejandra Cárdenas and Congolese guitarist Titi Bakorta join forces on a fast-moving album that’s brightly colored, dizzyingly detailed, and wildly fun.

title: Epiphany
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the Auto-Tune king’s second album, a frivolous but memorable moment from hip-hop’s ringtone era.

title: West Coast
description: The Swedish duo’s 2006 debut still feels both familiar and futuristic, with a breezy blend of dance and indie rock that evokes both windswept landscapes and youthful freedom.

title: EUSEXUA
description: Twigs’ third album brings club music into her sensual, supernatural world. It’s a masterful pop-star moment for the artist.

title: Museum Music
description: The memelord rapper and designer’s 30-track double album is one big, cryptic troll job. It might’ve been funnier if the music were better, but mostly the joke is on him.

title: Hometown Girl
description: Under a new alias, the ambient musician Ulla Strauss shifts toward an acoustic palette for an exquisitely rendered album anchored by a generous depth of feeling.

title: The Bad Fire
description: On their 11th album, the long-running post-rockers open up disarming, uplifting new dimensions to their sound without veering too far from familiar paths.

title: Lust (1)
description: Though more compact than Voice Actor’s four-and-a-half-hour debut, the new album’s hazy blend of blown-out ambient and indecipherable murmurs taps into a similarly delirious dream state.

title: lucre EP
description: The avant-pop stalwart’s newest YouTube-only release foregrounds lovestruck guitar ballads, with Elias Rønnenfelt and Vegyn guesting.

title: Balloonerism
description: Recorded in 2014 but never released, Mac Miller’s second posthumous album is the missing link between the earnest rapper he was and the evocative songwriter he would become.

title: My Way EP
description: After moving from UK dance music to American country, the English singer hits the studio with two L.A. pop producers. It feels less like a major statement than a signpost for possible future paths.

title: Sacrifice
description: Under a new moniker, Los Angeles-based house producer Seven Davis Jr. delivers studio wizardry with a pugnacious, uncompromising spirit.

title: Weft
description: The Copenhagen-via-Dallas composer expands his instrumental palette for a radiantly tranquil album that blends drone, folk, and ambient.

title: Tune In, Turn On, Drop Out – Radio Sessions 1980-1993
description: A collection of stripped-down studio broadcasts from the idiosyncratic but influential post-punks captures them in all their unpredictable glory.

title: HEAL
description: The ambient musician Buttechno and the abstract artist Dupuy collaborate for a record whose vaporous synths and puffs of white noise summon vintage environmental records and ’90s chillout rooms.

title: Hosianna Mantra
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a 1972 meditation on faith and uncertainty by a pioneering electronic band that stepped away from its synthesizer to make it.

title: Teenager of the Year (30th Anniversary Edition)
description: The Pixies frontman’s 1994 solo LP is a relic of an era when the music industry was flush with cash, affording even the most idiosyncratic artists the freedom to indulge their most outrageous whims.

title: Murder During Drug Traffic
description: In the grim light cast by producer RichGains’ murky, distorted beats, one of Detroit’s preeminent talents shades his signature stoicism with creeping psychic torment.

title: Suntub extras
description: Though not as expansive as the Danish musician’s otherworldly 2023 masterpiece, this instrumental bonus EP still offers an engrossing snapshot of her mysterious creative universe.

title: Dlow Curry
description: Though stuffed with outlandish boasts and nonstop hustle, the Port Salerno rapper’s new album is remarkably light on its feet.

title: A Complete Unknown (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: If you haven’t seen A Complete Unknown, the soundtrack might feel like a novelty record, Chalamet’s Dylan karaoke. In context, it’s a generational actor’s portrayal of a musician who was himself constantly acting.

title: RIO FREE
description: Just a month after his release from prison, the Michigan rapper returns with an EP that’s rife with paranoia and anger while retaining his signature aloof brutality.

title: Good Sad Happy Bad: All Kinds of Days
description: On the second album under their new name, Mica Levi and co. twist rock conventions into unexpected shapes.

title: Who Let the Dogs Out
description: On an album of fast-and-loose party punk, the British duo rails against misogyny, homophobia, and all manner of institutional cruelties with righteous fury and rambunctious glee.

title: Amour
description: London’s himbo partyboy supreme delivers a sexy yet sensitive collection of queer club bangers.

title: Montalvo
description: Dream-pop and trip-hop blur like a fading memory on the misty, poignant solo debut from Chanel Beads’ Maya McGrory.

title: DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS
description: Bad Bunny synthesizes the past and present sound of Puerto Rico for an anthemic, cross-generational album. He’s a master at work to enact his vision for the future of música urbana.

title: stars fell on trench
description: The 20-year-old rapper and producer smushes Top 40 samples, idiosyncratic bars, and cartoonish quirks into a blend that’s alternately razor sharp and deep fried.

title: Unraveling in Your Hands
description: After a nearly decade-long hiatus—including joblessness, injury, and personal loss—the UK guitarist returns with a moving, virtuosic album that communicates a rare sense of purpose.

title: Perverts
description: Darker and slower than ever, the singer-songwriter’s second LP blends claustrophobic ambient textures with chilly, half-obscured songs about powerlessness, guilt, and shame.

title: Think of Mist
description: On her second album, the Toronto songwriter—known for her work with U.S. Girls—marvels at the natural world in a swooning song cycle perched between folk-pop and choral jazz.

title: Look Up
description: Making good on his legacy as the Beatles’ resident cowboy, the former Fab Four drummer teams up with T Bone Burnett on a solo album steeped in classic country.

title: Pop
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit U2’s ninth studio album, an unexpected—and contentious—zig-zag into sounds inspired by hip-hop and dance.

title: Heavy Metal
description: A world away from his band’s ecstatic classic rock, the Geese frontman’s solo debut frames his woozy baritone with a careful juxtaposition of casual virtuosity and soul-scouring catharsis.

title: Cosmic Waves Volume 1
description: The singer-songwriter spotlights under-the-radar artists and covers their songs. The compilation includes some stunning moments, though Olsen’s own contributions tend to downplay her singular voice.

title: The Human Fear
description: The Scottish band’s sixth album summons the vintage swagger and suave humor of its early work but little of the punkish exhilaration.

title: Music From the Merch Desk (2016 - 2023)
description: Richard D. James’ latest curveball is a sprawling collection of rarities originally sold to fans at gigs. The high points are dazzling, but most of it is defiantly unfocused.

title: True Music
description: The Fievel Is Glauque musician translates his jazzy improvisations and playful songwriting to a spare, homemade solo piano album.

title: Midwinter Swimmers
description: The long-running band’s thirteenth album surveys faith, longing, and middle age with the commonplace language of awe and a sense of unbarred earnestness.

title: Good Mourning
description: The reclusive R&B artist revisits her cult-favorite mixtape. The reworked version, with its crisp vocals and Y2K-indebted production, polishes her earlier work without sacrificing mystique.

title: KEEPIN IT CLOUDY
description: At his best, the divisive Atlanta rapper’s surreal black comedy feels like a snapshot of contemporary ennui. But often, his monotonous flow and stock plugg beats just feel half-assed.

title: The Brutalist (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: The needling anxieties and delicate reprieves of Daniel Blumberg’s score illuminate the darker corners of Brady Corbet’s ambitious architectural drama.

title: SOS Deluxe: Lana
description: Fifteen diaphanous new tracks balance the ambling indie R&B of CTRL and the forthright hooks of SOS. Put these songs in their own playlist and you can proudly call Lana the third SZA album.

title: REACTOR EP
description: The Toronto producer’s feral digital hardcore channels horror aesthetics through maximalist rave mayhem; behind the breakbeat onslaught lies a spirit of joyous defiance.

title: Musik (2024 Remastered)
description: Newly reissued for its 30th anniversary, DJ and producer Richie Hawtin’s 1994 album reconfigured acid house’s familiar contours to new specifications: spare, trippy, and disorientingly slow.

title: Attempted Martyr
description: Calling the Dearborn noise rockers’ debut “intense” is somehow still underselling it.

title: Daryl Johns
description: Jumping from a jazz-prodigy past to a slot on Mac DeMarco’s label, the L.A. bassist and songwriter channels his myriad influences into a loosey-goosey, feel-good universe of all-American pop.

title: Parenòstic
description: The Menorcan singer and songwriter blends folk tradition and new compositions in a series of eerie, intensely focused performances honoring the rural character of her home island.

title: Mosaic
description: Nearly a quarter century after his ambient glitch masterpiece, Endless Summer, the Viennese musician still seeks transcendence in the collision of guitar riffs and electronic treatments.

title: Cooper B. Handy’s Album, Vol. 9
description: On his ninth album, the pop outsider continues his brand of charmingly bizarro tunes. In light of the songwriter’s prolific output, what once felt spontaneous has begun to sound homogenous.

title: Something Becomes You EP
description: The New York band’s second EP funnels its influences into a scuzzier, more ambitious showcase of paranoid alt-rock.

title: The Skeleton Key
description: The duo’s second full-length collaboration is leaner and meaner, weirder and bleaker.

title: the mind is a miracle EP
description: The Queens musician and multidisciplinary artist’s brief but immersive EP sets her soft-focus mantras to a meditative blend of ambient, field recordings, and left-field soul.

title: Clues
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit an idiosyncratic, funk-infused LP caught between the album-oriented 1970s and the electronic futurism of the 1980s.

title: Squared Roots
description: Crafted from the same materials that yielded Everything Squared, the British band’s new record of cosmological dub offers new insight into its recombinant philosophy.

title: Death Jokes II
description: Damon McMahon announced the end of Amen Dunes, but not before reworking the LP’s maximalist excess into this leaner, more direct swan song.

title: Discipline
description: The Japanese producer’s latest LP blends dub techno with the sunnier house sounds of his more recent work; twinkling digital synths and idiosyncratic samples add a welcome sentimental touch.

title: The Night
description: On the beloved indie-pop trio’s 11th album, world-weary acceptance and the unending march of time take shape as cloudy ambient tones and creepy nocturnal resonance.

title: rosie
description: On her solo debut, the BLACKPINK star aims to draw listeners close. But rather than offer a fresh vision of the singer, the record leans on outdated references and thinly sketched heartache.

title: Possession EP
description: Flute voyager Shabaka Hutchings follows up his debut solo album with a shadowy, searching EP that pushes his blend of New Age, jazz, and hip-hop further afield.

title: Intrinsic Rhythm
description: Interweaving field recordings, electronic abstractions, and low-key vocals—sometimes sung, sometimes merely murmured—these ambient pieces often feel like snapshots of dreams.

title: Doesn’t Exist II: The Complete Recordings
description: A decade after the Rhode Island-born group dissolved, its entire catalog has been remastered and reissued. The box set offers a three-guitar salute for blog rock’s most relentlessly joyful band.

title: Kassie Krut EP
description: The trio’s sing-songy single “Reckless” was one of the year’s most infectious dance bangers. On their debut EP, the ex-Palm players confirm that they’re here to get down.

title: ARTWORK III
description: The DMV rapper’s scorching new tape arrives with breakneck delivery, symphonic polish, and post-Opium vitriol.

title: Shell EP
description: On a sparse and subdued EP, the UK singer-songwriter warps past and present to examine conflicted love from every possible angle.

title: Solid Air
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit John Martyn’s dazzling 1973 album, an astral-folk masterpiece that embodies the British songwriter’s mercurial artistry.

title: re:wired
description: Full of raw nerves and short circuits, the 19-year-old digicore producer’s full-length debut is a study in emo-aggro duality.

title: Rome
description: Recorded in Italy in June 2024, the National’s 21-song live album is replete with deep cuts. Its more esoteric selections emphasize the unlikeliness of this band getting this far.

title: BLUE SUPER LOVE
description: On her debut album, the Detroit singer-songwriter explores supersized feelings in songs that pair bratty pop melodies with overblown textures.

title: You Never End
description: The UK trio—rock-informed, techno-adjacent—taps friends and peers for unconventional guest vocals and finds new life in squalling guitars and asymmetrical rhythms.

title: PHANTOM BRICKWORKS (LP II)
description: Stephen Wilkinson pays tribute to Britain’s nostalgic landscapes and ruins with a second collection of ambient tone poems indebted to the likes of Brian Eno and William Basinski.

title: BAD ASS F*CKING KID
description: The 17-year-old rapper’s debut is mostly derivative and incoherent, but he does have a strange allure.

title: If a Body Meet a Body
description: David Grubbs, Wendy Eisenberg, and Kramer—under a tongue-in-cheek alias borrowed from one of Grubbs’ books—meet for a spontaneous, exploratory improv session on dual guitars and electric bass.

title: The Undisputed Truth
description: With his sheer technical wizardry on display, the L.A. rapper’s posthumous album is a culmination of what should have been a generational talent’s early-middle period.

title: I Forget Everything EP
description: Using little more than harp, violin, and voice, the New York duo makes a tranquil yet unsettling strain of ambient dream pop.

title: Nobody Loves You More
description: Nearly four decades after becoming an indie fixture, the ex-Pixies bassist and Breeders co-founder finally releases her solo debut, revealing sides of herself we’ve never seen before.

title: Everything Changes, Nothing Ends
description: After the death of his partner, the longtime Ibiza resident jettisoned his habitually balmy Balearic sounds in favor of a more tempestuous palette that might help him process his grief.

title: Imperial Bedroom
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the intricate pop of Elvis Costello’s seventh album, a lush, baroque, bitterly clever highlight in his catalog.

title: The Bricktionary
description: The prolific Detroit rapper continues his astounding run with an album of cooly delivered street chronicles that get a boost from markedly busier production.

title: Vėjula
description: Too arresting to be ambient, the Lithuanian Belgian experimental folk duo assemble elegant, many-faceted compositions with a precision that feels like a little glimpse at forever.

title: 3AM (LA LA LA)
description: The Australian band, now based in London, tries to keep the party going all night with a dance-pop record that doesn’t quite have the stamina.

title: The Holy Grail: Bill Callahan’s “Smog” Dec. 10, 2001 Peel Session EP
description: Recorded 23 years ago in BBC’s Maida Vale studios, this brief EP—featuring two Smog originals and covers of the Velvet Underground and Fleetwood Mac—highlights the sinister yet generous essence of Bill Callahan’s music.

title: Nonetheless (Expanded Edition)
description: Continuing a recent retrospective turn, the duo’s latest album pines for the countercultural promise of eras past. But its hopeful defiance—and opulent, invigorated songwriting—feel firmly of the now.

title: Petrichor
description: The New Jersey multihyphenate looks to level up with a boldly experimental album marked by arena-rock grandiosity and sudden switch-ups.

title: The Neon Gate
description: Drawing inspiration from poems by Yeats and Pushkin, the Halifax quartet cloaks supernatural questions under steady strums and familiar sonic textures.

title: Plot Twist EP
description: On the Berlin-based DJ’s debut solo release, vintage sounds like speed garage and breakbeat 2-step get a hyper-detailed, psychedelic update; it’s head music with a powerful physical pull.

title: we will be wherever the fires are lit
description: On his second album for Drag City, the Bhutan-born guitarist wordlessly articulates a time of American turmoil—and finds fits of hope in the end.

title: Small Changes
description: The UK singer-songwriter’s first album in five years is mellower and more assured than his Mercury-winning 2019 LP; he sounds like a man floating above the world rather than struggling through it.

title: Bouquet
description: The veteran diva’s fifth solo album is a collection of bland, countrified pop tunes dedicated to love and her marriage.

title: Phantasy & Reality
description: The ambient musician and experimental saxophonist reunite for a spacious album that glows with the chilly beauty of winter sun.

title: Living in the Material World (50th Anniversary)
description: Following the success of All Things Must Pass, the former Beatle’s second album frames spiritual yearning and earthly woes in a careful balance of resigned introspection and musical uplift.

title: Quiet in a World Full of Noise
description: The singer and composer scale down their collaboration for a grief-saturated set of songs filled with austere piano melodies and diaristic reflections.

title: Essential Mixtape
description: Folding murmured dialog into road-trip snapshots and blissed-out synths, the two producers meld their respective style—wistful edits, lo-fi euphoria—into a rapturous pop-ambient blur.

title: Lily of the Valley
description: Singer-songwriter Will Kennedy moves through grief in delicate and unsparing ways using the simple sounds of lo-fi indie rock.

title: GNX
description: Kendrick’s glossy, hyper-local sixth album arrives after a year of unimpeachable victories. The question is, how much do you enjoy watching him take lap after lap?

title: Trellis
description: The collective’s loosely defined blend of drifting ambient, driving funk, and buoyant electronic improv is not quite jazz, but also not not jazz.

title: Scarlet Lamb EP
description: The South London producer takes on a darker electro-pop sound with an EP that captures the joy of oblivion and the slog of creative fatigue.

title: Meaning’s Edge EP
description: The UK producer and DJ’s thrilling, destabilizing tracks unfold with mind-bending complexity and effortless sleight of hand.

title: Cosa Nuestra
description: Drawing from his Nuyorican roots and the salsa romántica greats, El Zorro makes a bid for the canon with mixed results.

title: Get Loose
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a 1982 dancefloor classic, featuring timeless production and a sparkling voice of the post-disco sound.

title: Curyman II
description: With string arrangements from bossa nova legend Arthur Verocai, the L.A.-based, Rio-born musician celebrates the vibrancy of Brazilian culture while tackling the country’s complex history.

title: The Way Out of Easy
description: The guitarist’s latest live set of exploratory, atmospheric jazz shares sensibilities with 2022’s Mondays at the Enfield Tennis Academy. The vibe is laid-back, but it rewards rapt attention.

title: Strange Meridians
description: The Dutch producer’s new album trades the clockwork precision of IDM for a more organic strain of ambient, one that sounds less programmed than hydroponically grown.

title: GRAND POP
description: The J-pop collective’s second album is a high-spirited musical ping-pong match, bouncing between guitar shredding, bubblegum bass, and twitchy experimental rap.

title: Mahashmashana
description: Josh Tillman is at his spiritual peak: The mood swings are wilder, the logic more tangential, and the songwriting might be the best it’s ever been.

title: Rocky Top Ballads
description: Danish singer-songwriter Fine Glindvad Jensen’s curious, enigmatic solo debut is suffused with the whispery enchantment of Hope Sandoval.
The Brooklyn-based cellist explores her darkest and most abstract material yet: Her brutalist compositions are an ominously muscular companion to an apocalyptic work of contemporary dance.

title: MM..FOOD (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: In 2004, DOOM dropped his funniest and most mercenary album. Reissued for its 20th anniversary, it remains a fully realized creation of rap’s greatest eccentric.

title: 王中王
description: Slurring his way through bars that conceal literary and internet-savvy references, the Chengdu plugg rapper is a regular guy speaking to the ennui of China’s urban youth.

title: Sli’merre 2
description: The riveting Atlanta MC and forward-thinking producer usually work well together. Unfortunately, their newest tape gets bogged down by vapid clichés, stale retreads, and lukewarm sex-and-drugs anthems.

title: Access All Areas
description: The UK trio’s debut delivers a confident vision of what a modern girl group can be: tender, headstrong, and unified, with a clear point of view and harmonies for days.

title: Computer and recording works for girls
description: Born from a series of spontaneous home recordings on guitars, synths, and computer, the duo’s debut collaboration is a tale of friendship translated into whimsical ambient music.

title: Desperate Youth, Blood Thirsty Babes (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: An expanded reissue calls back to the tumultuous era that produced the New York band’s landmark 2004 debut, which posed desperate pleasure as a way of making meaning in a hostile world.

title: Afrikan Alien
description: The British Gambian rapper chronicles his cellblock daydreams on family, freedom, and feeling alien in the UK while hinting at a new blueprint for pan-African pop.

title: Mister Sweet Whisper
description: On his third album, the 74-year-old Alabama poet and songwriter casts about for meaning among dreams and memories for a wise, lonely, utterly beguiling set of songs.

title: Wish You Were Here
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a timeless classic rock album from 1975, a mournful, emotionally charged mood piece that grounded a historically cosmic band.

title: KING OF THE MISCHIEVOUS SOUTH
description: On a sequel to a 2012 mixtape, the Miami rapper takes a playful romp through Southern rap history. Instead of devotional revivalism, he treats regional traditions as a springboard for stylistic play.

title: Personification
description: The Texas rapper’s new album presents itself as a moment of mid-career reflection but feels more like a facsimile of his past work.

title: Take Off From Mercy
