description: Fingerpicked guitar casts a dream-like trance around Khari Lucas’ plaintive singing on a spare, dense album with the quiet fervor of prayer.

title: CONGLOMERATE
description: Capitalizing on the UK underground’s rising profile, the three British MCs combine forces for a cosmopolitan, if slightly uneven, collaboration.

title: Saaheem
description: The Atlanta-based rapper’s self-titled album bridges the silly and the deadly serious with fresh stylistic flair.

title: Naya Beat, Vol. 2: South Asian Dance and Electronic Music 1988-1994
description: In the ’80s and ’90s, South Asian musicians around the globe blended house and dub with the sounds of their heritage, reimagining Western styles and presaging today’s diasporic club-music renaissance.

title: Come Ahead
description: The first Primal Scream album in eight years gives Bobby Gillespie’s acid-dipped grooves a funky, cinematic sheen.

title: Camelot
description: After the intimacy of 2020’s folky Monarch Season, the Ontario musician’s new album packs a country-rock kick. But behind the familiar textures lies an ambitious blend of reflection and fantasy.

title: Guetto Star
description: On his first full-length in seven years, the Lisbon-raised, Paris-based producer showcases his complex batida style with alien intensity and subtle humor.

title: Blue Desert
description: On his second album, the Mood Hut cofounder branches out from the underground house he made his name with, infusing sultry new wave and chillout with a captivating air of unease.

title: Ministerial Cafeteria
description: With an intoxicating mix of punk, grindcore, death metal, and math rock, the Nashville quartet channels both personal rage and horror movie camp to condemn corrupt systems of power.

title: Slo-Be Bryant 4
description: The first posthumous record from the Stockton rapper showcases a style so fully articulated that it seems to have sprung from everywhere and nowhere at once.

title: DREAMDROPDRAGON
description: The Brooklyn rapper offers both cosmic clarity and existential frustration over newly adventurous, fractured beats.

title: Swan Lake EP
description: The San Francisco band’s EP is a small slice of dream-pop rendered softly, simply, and elegantly.

title: Use Your Illusion I / Use Your Illusion II
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Guns N’ Roses’ twin 1991 LPs, an indulgent and maximal dispatch from the definitive rock band at its cultural apex.

title: Love, Guess Who??
description: Nine years after Age of Transparency, Arthur Ashin finally returns to close the trilogy he began with 2013’s Anxiety, pushing deeper into his customary fusion of R&B and experimental electronica.

title: Piedras 1 & 2
description: Condensed from a five-hour radio play, Jaar’s 2xLP weaves a story of Chilean colonial history, military dictatorship, and Palestinian erasure into a dizzying mixture of abstract sonics and avant pop.

title: Big Smile, Black Mire
description: The L.A. musician takes a dissociated, post-club approach to indie, folding acoustic guitars into fragments of hip-hop and electronic music; the resulting hybrid is wide-eyed and intimate.

title: Leave Another Day
description: The Belgian producer makes a hard shift into oaky, autumnal dream pop for an unusual suite of twisted love songs poisoned by toxic desire.

title: Seed of a Seed
description: On her second album, the Oregon singer-songwriter crafts patient, detailed songs in the borderlands between modernity and nature.

title: LL
description: The self-mythologizing L.A. duo’s debut album is a wanton mixture of electroclash, ’00s dance pop, and digital hyperactivity. Despite the aggressive posturing, it’s surprisingly heartfelt.

title: Groovy Steppin Sh*t
description: An unlikely meeting between the South Carolina rapper and Philadelphia producer yields thrillingly alien results. It’s the rare perfect marriage of tough underground MC and nerdy beatmaker.

title: What a Relief
description: The MUNA singer’s solo debut scales down her songwriting, replacing the band’s festival-sized choruses with down-to-earth lyrics and folksy production touches.

title: Eternal Atake 2
description: Instead of blazing a path forward, the iconoclastic rapper retreads familiar ground in a dull, remarkably safe sequel to their groundbreaking album.

title: FunHouse
description: The rapper and producer’s maximalist songs mimic the hyperactive atmosphere of Nintendo side-scrollers. On his second album of the year, he pens baby-voiced rage-rap dense with uplifting sentiments.

title: Night Palace
description: Phil Elverum’s first Mount Eerie album in five years feels like a culmination of his work over the past 25 years, making room for all his earlier selves and sounds.

title: Electric Bouquet
description: The Omaha musician writes songs frank in their directness and poignant in their imagistic details. Her ramshackle arrangements and quivering voice channel a warmly human outpouring of emotion.

title: Mirror Starts Moving Without Me
description: On her second album, Mia Berrin continues to write sugary anthems detailing early adulthood’s growing pains, but this time she trades punk for punchy, sharp-edged pop.

title: Africa Must Be Free by 1983
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the impressive 1978 debut of a teenage star, a radical piece of roots reggae defined by its innocence and the tragedy that followed.

title: Window in the Rhythm
description: In an unexpected coda to the indie-lifer trilogy that ended with 2018’s Aftering, the Ann Arbor musician again revisits his youth—but this time interrogating nostalgia, rather than indulging in it.

title: Songs of a Lost World
description: Sixteen years after their last album, Robert Smith & co. return at their own glacial pace. Sounding regal, weary, and deliciously slow, they grapple with mortality and doubt as only they could.

title: Evergreen
description: Sophie Allison’s fourth album is steeped in a loneliness darker than that of her youth, pairing raw reflections on grief with the most laid-back, pastoral music of her career.

title: Heavy Glory
description: On his solo debut, the Iceage frontman experiments with a newfound sincerity and an Americana-inspired sound, searching for beauty in the small and insular.

title: CHROMAKOPIA
description: On his eighth album, Tyler is both mask-on and mask-off. It’s an electric, revealing, and perennially odd journey back into his aging psyche.

title: Goodbye Horses
description: The teen rapper’s second album of the year is stiff and stuffy where it’s meant to feel rapturous, with flaccid hooks and verses that barely reflect his talent.

title: Two Shell
description: On its debut album, a quasi-anonymous UK duo famous for cutting-edge bass music and rascally pranks seeks a balance of mystery, mischief, and unbridled dancefloor hedonism.

title: MEGAN: ACT II
description: The deluxe edition of Megan’s album from earlier this year adds a slew of new tracks for a creative recentering that lands with refreshing lightness.

title: Cartoon Darkness
description: A defensive, chip-on-shoulder tone dominates the Australian punks’ third album, threatening to overshadow their freaky experimental flourishes and newfound melodic sophistication.

title: The Great Impersonator
description: With a muddled concept at its core, Halsey’s fifth album languishes in dull pop-rock corridors behind emotionally potent but unremarkable songwriting.

title: Lyfestyle
description: When Yeat isn’t doing caricatures of great rage tracks, he throws the occasional curveball that hardly curves.

title: Thankful
description: The experimental composer sculpts backmasked samples and towering distortion in tribute to her mentor, Peter Rehberg of Editions Mego.

title: Rong Weicknes
description: Scored for octet and collaged together out of multiple live takes, the Brooklyn art-pop group’s latest is their most giddily hyperkinetic, vividly colored, unabashedly maximalist record yet.

title: el precio de la yuca / Bexaco y rico
description: Pulling freely from punk, nu-metal, trap, hyperpop, and podcast, the Dominican producer’s alternative-minded música urbana amplifies the genre’s defiant roots.

title: Gossip
description: The former Girlpool singer’s solo debut wants to rot your brain. It is, in many respects, insufferable.

title: Da Real World
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Missy Elliott’s overlooked second album, a mind-bending showcase of her and Timbaland’s burgeoning relationship.

title: Virtual Dreams II, Ambient Explorations in the House & Techno Age, Japan 1993-1999
description: A spellbinding compilation of seldom-heard tracks from the 1990s revisits the moment when Japanese ambient music absorbed the influence of a rapidly evolving worldwide techno scene.

title: Patterns in Repeat
description: Following the birth of her daughter, the accomplished singer-songwriter carefully unspools a homey, quiet record. It’s one of the best of her career.

title: Space as an Instrument
description: Using simple raw elements—piano improvisations, field recordings, whispered poetry—the French electro-acoustic composer evokes emotional states that are alien and intense.

title: Scheduled Explosions
description: The Philly fuzz-pop band balances cute, quirky songcraft with a deep sense of paranoia and dread.

title: I Wanna Run Barefoot Through Your Hair
description: The former frontman of Girls has been through hell. His first new album in nine years is a travelogue of his journey.

title: DJ-Kicks: Honey Dijon
description: The Chicago DJ’s mix highlights her skills as a crowd-pleaser, a storyteller, and a house-music historian. She’s an expert at connecting dots, joining eras and audiences at the same time.

title: Dreamstate
description: The Welsh producer’s fourth album benefits from newfound clarity and architectural scale, stripping her sound to its essence while preserving its hypnotic air.

title: Fate & Alcohol
description: The rock duo’s final album comes ready with the booze-soaked conviction, but the keg’s finally run dry.

title: Guided Tour
description: On their third album, the UK hardcore vets add a little melody and Madchester into their hard-won anthems of hope.

title: Desde Los Oídos de un Sapo
description: The Uruguayan electronic musician smears and distorts the sounds of nature, twisting the rules of club music into unconventional shapes.

title: MG Ultra
description: A new label and more exacting sound design suggest an interest in leveling up, but for the most part, the group’s dystopian electronic hardcore is business as usual.

title: Lush Life
description: The Australian band’s debut, newly reissued by Third Man, is a classic power-pop rager that’s euphoric and greyhound-lithe.

title: Enough
description: The Brooklyn band’s guest-studded double album swaps jazzy soft-rock stylings for sample-speckled art pop and nocturnal brooding.

title: Clouds in the Sky They Will Always Be There for Me
description: Dana Margolin’s band returns with a ferocious new album about burning out and burning it down.

title: Dance of Love
description: The 83-year-old American songwriter comes out of seclusion to record an intimate, textured, homespun folk album with Big Thief as his backing band.

title: Majician
description: The veteran New York rapper’s new album features unearthed material workshopped with executive producer MF DOOM. It’s a big pair of shoes to fill.

title: You’ve Come a Long Way Baby
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Fatboy Slim’s 1998 album, a sampledelic funhouse that briefly made big beat the next big thing in dance music.

title: Even the Forest Hums: Ukrainian Sonic Archives 1971-1996
description: A lovingly curated new compilation excavates 25 years of Ukrainian music that flourished in the shadows of Soviet officialdom. The aim: to celebrate an endangered culture in all its complexity.

title: SABLE, EP
description: In a moving suite of songs about loneliness and disappointment, Justin Vernon distills the familiar pleasures of his extraordinary oeuvre with clarity and confidence.

title: Spiral in a Straight Line
description: Touché Amoré’s sixth album stays true to heartfelt post-hardcore while packing some of their strongest and most surprising hooks to date.

title: More Insane
description: The Rochester band adds newfound complexity and subtle flourishes to old-school death metal’s classic sound.

title: GLORIOUS
description: With a debut LP that’s also a comeback record, the Memphis rapper channels the music of her youth, cycling through crunk and gospel with aplomb.

title: Oasis
description: The Atlanta producer’s short and spooky-sweet new album pairs his psychedelic pluggnb sounds with an all-women roster of regional talent.

title: Beautifully Broken
description: The former rapper turned country star has the voice, the pathos, and the charisma of an American folk hero. All he needs are the songs.

title: I SHOULD CALL THEM
description: After a trilogy of shape-shifting EPs, the Sudanese American artist concentrates their style into a dusky blend of R&B, rap, and rock songs whose lyrics seesaw between swaggering and lovesick.

title: iiyo iiyo iiyo
description: For a pair of dates in Japan, the L.A. jazz bassist forged a new quintet stacked with longtime collaborators; the results sound enlivened by spontaneity, intimacy, and a sense of wonder.

title: Cool World
description: On an album that paints a panoramic view of human suffering, the Oklahoma City group sometimes sacrifices ferocity as it expands its muscular sludge-metal sound.

title: When you wake up
description: Blending bodily rhythms and shoegazing abstraction, the Danish Chilean composer and singer’s debut constructs a subtle play of perception and ambiguity.

title: Mighty Vertebrate
description: After the freeform exploration of their solo debut, the Australian bassist leads seasoned collaborators through a series of unusual creative prompts, with results as intricate as they are varied.

title: Brat and it’s completely different but also still brat
description: Quick on the heels of her blockbuster album BRAT, the pop star offers a remix album that is anything but obligatory. Like its sister album, it is unexpected, unfiltered, uncomfortably messy, and dizzyingly fun.

title: Feats of Engineering
description: The Brooklyn art-pop duo’s cheeky, ambitious debut has the shameless ambition of an arena band with the musical chops of studio veterans.

title: Mood Ring EP
description: On her first release in two years, the Kentucky singer uses elegantly understated folk arrangements to frame keenly rendered expressions of empathy.

title: Jealous One’s Envy
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Fat Joe’s hard-hitting 1995 album, a crucial sidequest for New York rap filled with his heavyweight style and vivid storytelling.

title: Leon
description: The soul singer looks backward on his fourth album, a wistful nostalgia trip that wraps its ’70s-inspired sound in sumptuous, heavily stylized production.

title: REVELATOR
description: The New Yorker’s at the peak of his powers on his stormy new album, a mix of deep-hitting bars and organic live instrumentation, with a noisy electronic edge to it all.

title: Casts of a Dreamer
description: The Florida-born rapper’s latest tape expands on the frenzy of Fast Trax 3, gushing with airy plugg positioned somewhere between Mario Kart and the skate park.

title: See You at the Maypole
description: In the aftermath of a miscarriage, Nandi Rose reckons with grief, solitude, and perseverance on songs that strike a delicate balance between pain and beauty.

title: Cutouts
description: The Radiohead spinoff’s looser, funkier second album in nine months is a thrilling testament to the near-telepathic chemistry the three musicians have spent the last three years developing.

title: Moon Music
description: Moon Music demonstrates all the reasons to be sick of Coldplay, and all the reasons they’ll be missed when they finally retire.

title: Dulling the Horns
description: The band’s poetic take on rough-hewn heartland rock is simultaneously weirder and more fun than anything in their catalog.

title: The New Sound
description: The black midi frontman’s solo debut populates his over-the-top genre workouts with a carefully drawn parade of unsubtle, unsympathetic characters. It’s exhilarating—and occasionally exhausting.

title: ANIMALS ONLY
description: The rising rapper’s new tape packs every era of Chicago drill into 12 songs. He sounds like a natural.

title: harkening critters
description: A new compilation of field recordings from animals around the world—from croaking toads to buzzing insects to bellowing bison—draws attention to the ways creatures of all sizes can speak to us.

title: The Hard Quartet
description: Stephen Malkmus, Matt Sweeney, Emmett Kelly, and Jim White’s classic-rock comfort food retains the willful eccentricity and goofball impulses of its creators.

title: “NO TITLE AS OF 13 FEBRUARY 2024 28,340 DEAD”
description: Despite the grim title, the veteran Montreal post-rockers make some of their most exultant music here, trading apocalyptic epics for camaraderie and catharsis.

title: Keep Holly Alive
description: Ten years into their career, the Richmond, Virginia hip-hop collective gets an official debut that finally puts the crew’s effortless chemistry on full display.

title: Honey
description: Dan Snaith’s new album scales his distinctive fidgety production style into huge, satisfying dancefloor heaters—and wait till you find out who’s singing them.

title: Acadia
description: Bright and gregarious yet focused, the inventive guitarist’s latest release draws on the warm camaraderie of her collaborators for an imaginative expansion of her sound.

title: Fragments of Us
description: The UK producer’s debut LP is a pocket history of British and American gay subcultures, accompanying ambient-electro grooves with the testimony of queer elders.

title: Come Away With Me
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Norah Jones’ 2002 debut, a humble, bluesy pop record that sent a previously unknown singer-songwriter to the stratosphere.

title: Machine
description: This anthology of instrumentals the industrial dub stalwart crafted for his pummeling live performances is some of his heaviest, ugliest, most damaged-sounding music yet.

title: Absolute Elsewhere
description: Following their proggy instincts to galactic new heights, the Denver quartet balances krautrock’s surreal splendor with death metal’s profane madness, finding hypnotic focus in even the heaviest riffs.

title: Highway Prayers
description: On his major-label studio debut, the bluegrass wunderkind expands his palette, exploring new textures and emotional registers while staying true to his beloved genre.

title: Pretty Side of the Ugly Life
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter’s eclectic debut blends winding Midwest emo guitars, half-mumbled vocals, glinting pedal steel, and minimalistic ’80s synths.

title: EELS
description: With deceptively lo-fi hooks and a playfully oblique approach, the Austin rock duo crafts songs that are goofy, serious, innocent, and knowing all at once.

title: Bully
description: The Queens producer and vocalist’s new mixtape is a tipsy, game-spitting New York mood piece.

title: Plays John Coltrane and Langston Hughes
description: Over the past nine years, the guitarist’s hushed, hypnotic suite of koan-like pieces has gathered a cult fan base. It’s a perfect encapsulation of his music’s mystical, spiritual energies.

title: Dunya
description: With subtly shifting production and incisive writing, the Toronto singer adapts intimate stories of pain and devotion to his worldly folk palette.

title: Whodunnit
description: Taking a whimsical and meditative approach to the breakup album, Dan Knishkowy makes the end of a marriage sound unexpectedly healing.

title: Coyote
description: After his breakout smash “Million Dollar Baby,” the honey-voiced Virginia singer struggles to find the heart and personality that comes after a viral hit.

title: Watch Me Drive Them Dogs Wild
description: The Pittsburgh native’s folk- and country-infused songwriting captures big ideas and bigger feelings in vivid imagery and unconventional turns of phrase.

title: White Roses, My God
description: With blown-out electronics and heavy vocal processing, Low’s Alan Sparhawk grapples with the death of his wife and bandmate, Mimi Parker, giving wild, feverish shape to his grief.

title: Peace of Mind EP
description: The Japanese techno producer has long struck a balance between easygoing grooves and unsettling frequencies. On his new EP, he indulges in some of his prickliest sounds in years.

title: The Natural Bridge
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit David Berman’s essential 1996 album, a uniquely dark and atmospheric entry in the Silver Jews catalog.

title: HOPECORE
description: The artist formerly known as Christine and the Queens plunges into physical abandon on an album steeped in house music, carnal pleasures, and impassioned vocal performances.

title: SOPHIE
description: The electronic pioneer’s posthumous album is bittersweet, difficult to pin down, and an unusually safe statement from one of the 21st century’s great risk-takers.

title: Throwing Bows EP
description: Unlike her strong debut, the Monaleo of these chintzy, throwaway songs is a caricature who says anything and fights for nothing.

title: Like All Before You
description: On his third album with the Voidz, Julian Casablancas details a questionably sincere quest for deeper meaning. Aiming for nirvana, he delivers a stream-of-consciousness slog instead.

title: Jazz Plates
description: After years of long-distance collaborations, the two ambient musicians finally sit down to make music together under the same roof. The result is some of their most dreamily unstructured music yet, intimate and conversational.

title: Mixtape Pluto
description: Future finds a new gear. His latest album is urgent and kinetic, filled with heartbreaking asides and tiny bursts of melodic ingenuity.

title: Sayso Says
description: The Atlanta rapper delivers escapist party anthems whose dense, maximalist sound masks a slightly hollow perspective.
The popstar confidently returns with very little to say.

title: Warm and Cool / Around / Songs and Other Things
description: An overdue reissue campaign rescues the Television frontman’s final solo albums from obscurity, spotlighting a jazzier mode of the late icon’s six-string brilliance.

title: Odyssey
description: The London saxophonist looks outward on her second album, folding in richly layered orchestral arrangements and giving free rein to her most adventurous instincts.

title: Moon in Gemini
description: The Istanbul-born, Glasgow-based musician’s new album contains featherweight songs of innocent wonder—but, as in the best children’s stories, stranger things often lurk beneath the surface.

title: How to Be Hopeful
description: On their first album in eight years, the British emo-punks’ all-encompassing angst is reconstituted as hard-earned gratitude—and even true love.

title: Version 2.0
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Garbage’s 1998 album, a uniquely synthetic electro-grunge record that rejected alt-rock for something far more grand and exquisite.

title: Toda la verdad sobre Dame Area
description: After the sleek sound of their last album, the Barcelona synth punks take up a motley set of tools—machine-like sound effects, homemade noise generators—and wreak industrial havoc.

title: In Waves
description: Ten years after his big solo debut, the UK producer goes even bigger for a well-polished record animated by the ecstatic and easy pleasures of the dancefloor.

title: Gap Year!
description: Riding the success of singles “Like That!” and “Not My Problem,” the 18-year-old New York vocalist and producer presents her own version of a throwback self-titled debut.

title: Estradas
description: On their debut collaboration, the beatmaker and the drummer search for middle ground between their respective styles, twisting programmed grooves and loose-limbed percussion into propulsive, polyrhythmic configurations.

title: LIVE DRUGS AGAIN
description: The Philly group’s second live album is a celebration of the band as a symbiotic unit and an impressive distillation of its cosmic Americana sound.

title: Viewfinder
description: Laser eye surgery enabled the guitarist to see clearly. Their new album draws on the improvisatory techniques of free jazz to explore the slippery nature of human perception.

title: My Method Actor
description: On her third album, the UK singer-songwriter sounds relaxed, confident, unflappably cool, even in moments of conflict. The result is an album of everyday luxury, lush and unhurried.

title: Shirt
description: On his heaviest, spikiest album to date, Aaron Maine’s shredded production and raw arrangements evoke existential angst and quotidian despair.

title: Think Differently
description: The New York experimental duo gets meta on a concept album about experimental music that’s littered with meme effects and shitpost irreverence. It feels like a Discord thread set to music.

title: Foxing
description: On their self-titled fifth album, the cult emo rockers construct a story of hard work, disillusionment, and nu-metal.

title: This Is BASIC
description: The Philadelphia trio pays tribute to a baffling 1984 LP of programmed drums and indulgent guitar recorded by an obstinate Lou Reed collaborator. They’re not so much imitators as acolytes.

title: Live in Amarillo, Texas
description: A December 2023 performance recorded in the guitarist’s beloved hometown displays his playing at its most expressive and expansive.

title: my anti-aircraft friend
description: On its debut LP, this trio of L.A. 20-somethings digs into au courant grunge and shoegaze influences to come up with fresh, compelling alt-rock epics rendered in miniature.

title: Carrot Season
description: The New York rappers develop the contours of their voices, adding shading and depth to what could otherwise come off as exhaustingly mechanical.

title: Sex Drive
description: The New York rapper refines his horndog anthems into a true pervert’s cocktail: crass, silly, and genuine.

title: BCD
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit an immortal 1995 dub-techno manifesto that forged links between Berlin, Detroit, and Jamaica, dissolving dance music’s throb into an ambient haze.

title: Days Before Rodeo
description: The 10th anniversary edition of Days Before Rodeo, Travis Scott’s breakout mixtape, is a time capsule of the rapper’s chameleonic production prowess and budding curatorial skill.

title: Cascade
description: Three years after exploring new dimensions in ambient jazz alongside Pharoah Sanders, Sam Shepherd refocuses his efforts on the dancefloor, with dazzling results.

title: Art of the Unseen Infinity Machine
description: The singer-songwriter completed her new album after a brush with death, filling her airy folk-rock with poetic urgency, empathetic curiosity, and a renewed respect for life.

title: Migratory
description: Through tranquil reverberations of vibraphone and shō, the Japanese experimental composer contemplates the restless urges that inspire birds (and humans) to take flight.

title: In a Landscape
description: The German composer reflects on his many years of music-making with a subtle, melancholic suite of songs that looks back to move forward.

title: WOOF.
description: The UK’s latest post-punk export has built its rep on antic live shows and costumed hijinks. But on record, Fat Dog’s arch dance-punk fusion feels more calculated than provocatively chaotic.

title: Endlessness
description: The London-based musician’s potent and intuitive second album dissolves the binaries inherent in ambient jazz and imagines a third sort of music that thrives at their midpoint.

title: Free Energy
description: On its second album, the Los Angeles band levels up its dizzying dynamic shifts and emphasizes Emma Maatman’s expressive voice. The result is a record of expertly crafted psych-pop that’s thrillingly kinetic and unbound.

title: Hole Erth
description: Chaz Bear has been on the periphery of emo-rap since 24kGoldn was in kindergarten. But the crowded, blown-out Hole Erth struggles to sound like anything but an imitation.

title: Oh My God - That’s So Me
description: The Norwegian-American songwriter’s observations about contemporary states of distraction and detachment are compassionate and closely focused.

title: GAS
description: Finally reissued in full, the 1996 debut from Wolfgang Voigt’s ambient techno project deserves every second of its 92-minute runtime. It’s music to get lost in, meditative and mind-numbing—in the best way.

title: Born Horses
description: On their first album of original material in nine years, the veteran New York rockers reinvent themselves once again. That’s where the problems begin.

title: What’s Wrong With New York?
description: Split between libido-maxxed hooks and hackneyed stabs at post-bender profundity, the Dare’s debut album is sweaty, horny, and trying really hard.

title: Belaya Polosa
description: A few years removed from TikTok virality, the Belarusian band sharpens its blend of ’80s goth rock and post-Soviet melancholia. Its latest album is more ebullient and captivating, though its energy can sometimes lag.

title: I’ll Drown on This Earth
description: The Southern California band once printed up a T-shirt proclaiming, “Shoegaze is a prison.” On their second album, they break out.

title: Rum Sodomy & the Lash
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the Pogues’ 1985 classic, a groundbreaking punk-rock fever-dream pub session led by Shane MacGowan’s unforgettable writing and performance.

title: In Dreams
description: The second act of the slowcore and space-rock band has now lasted longer than the first. On their third album since reuniting, they’re still playing the past.

title: Manning Fireworks
description: The Asheville singer-songwriter’s outstanding fourth album is loaded with zingers and losers. It’s witty and sincere, the mark of a songwriter finding his voice.

title: Baggy$$ EP
description: The very cool, very downtown New York dance trio’s debut EP is of little ambition, which isn’t to say it isn’t good.

title: LOVE LASTS FOREVER
description: The Atlanta rapper’s new album ditches the dirge-like guitars of If Looks Could Kill, but despite the flashy trap beats and flex-rap tropes, he still makes hedonism sound dreary.

title: Alligator Bites Never Heal
description: On her most ambitious and musically diverse release to date, the TDE rapper and singer meets the pressures of success with defiance and irreverence.

title: Wish on the Bone
description: Singer-songwriter Blair Howerton’s writing is full of doubt and vulnerability, but her band’s blend of shoegaze, fried country, and straight-ahead indie rock sounds more confident than ever.

title: Wild God
description: On a record originally conceived as an ode to joy, Nick Cave continues to grapple with the all-consuming nature of grief. Pushed to rapturous extremes, the album sounds as haunted as it is healing.

title: Amelia
description: The multimedia artist’s latest release is a fictionalized retelling of Amelia Earhart’s final voyage. A brisk and largely frictionless record, it’s nonetheless filled with moments of awestruck wonder.

title: Rose Main Reading Room
description: On its fourth album, the Los Angeles-based group confronts the mysteries of memory and time in richly layered songs informed by classic indie pop, classical minimalism, and gentle psychedelia.

title: Ritual
description: Following LPs for ketamine therapy and chemical voyages, the UK producer’s latest record stems from his soundtrack for a stroboscopic psychedelic gizmo. It’s his most single-mindedly epic LP.

title: Normal Sounds
description: The Chicago cellist’s new album is an ode to the din of everyday life, transforming the mundanity of buzzing fridges and clicking turn signals into moments of unlikely beauty.

title: megacity1000
description: The Australian musician better known for his indie-pop project Golden Vessel turns to crisply banging productions heavily inspired by contemporary Latin club.

title: Chocolate and Cheese
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the Ween’s landmark 1994 album, a genius pop record made by two idiots—or vice versa.

title: Troubadour
description: Originally released in 1976, the pioneering artist’s debut album is filled with countless moments of disarming beauty. It plays like a map of her musical passions, linking folk traditions with avant-garde innovation.

title: Everything Squared
description: In the ’90s, Seefeel evolved through shoegaze and post-rock to create their own unsettling brand of ambient dub. Breaking a 13-year hiatus, they’re still finding new magic in old tricks.

title: Girl
description: On their third album, cloud pop-rap stars Coco & Clair Clair’s barbed quips and cheeky attitude let you know they really care.

title: Cacophony
description: The English singer-songwriter’s debut swings big, tackling themes of death and patriarchal oppression through earthy imagery and dense alt-pop arrangements.

title: The Bed I Made
description: On their first album in 24 years, Rose Melberg and Jen Sbragia are indie-pop minimalists with the biggest of hearts, conveying complex adult emotions with the freedom and possibility of youth.

title: WATCH THE THRONE
description: Over bitcrushed, kick-heavy beats, the DMV street rapper’s scenes from everyday life reveal a more introspective take on the region’s distinctive sound.

title: The Thief Next to Jesus
description: On a stark, somber album rooted in gospel samples, the Brooklyn rapper examines the relationship between Black Americans and Christianity, while seeking a new framework for his own faith.

title: You’ll Have to Lose Something
description: The Philadelphia psych collagists’ new album approaches confusion and terror through some of their prettiest music to date.

title: Power
description: On a record of gentler, cozy indie rock, Sarah Tudzin searches for balance while confronting life’s humbling privileges, the heaviness of mourning, and all manner of recent grievances.

title: Starchris
description: Bludgeoning rage beats, glitchy sound design, and sideways R&B melodies take on corporal presence in producer and vocalist Chris Taylor’s brilliantly discombobulating debut.

title: Patio User Manual
description: Is the patio a liminal space, a threshold between the known and unknown? Cincinnati artist Alex Cobb’s minimalist ambient-glitch music suggests that it’s definitely a possibility.

title: For Every Set of Eyes
description: The Rhode Island songwriter’s ornate, bookish chamber pop has its own brand of whimsy.

title: Short n’ Sweet
description: After a summer of hit singles, Sabrina Carpenter sets a high bar for big pop with a refreshingly light album that’s cheeky, clever, and effortlessly executed.

title: Something to Write Home About (25th Anniversary Deluxe Edition)
description: A 25th anniversary reissue of the Kansas group’s 1999 breakthrough looks back at a crucial turning point for Midwestern emo—but a dozen demos offer a glimpse of paths not taken.

title: Veena
description: On his new solo album, the Queens rapper tackles his struggles with addiction and intergenerational trauma. His signature mix of smart-dumb humor is still there, but it no longer feels like a security blanket.

title: Soundbombing II
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the lodestar of independent rap, a 1999 Rawkus mixtape that captured the vital, splintering sound of New York’s underground.

title: TGCD1 / The Third Mind Movements
description: Two new reissues capture the industrial titans at strikingly different moments in their career—showing first endless and explosive potential, then the fault lines of a group at odds with itself.

title: Imaginal Disk
description: The Los Angeles duo’s second album is musically and conceptually dense, warping the fundamentally optimistic sound of pop to suit a more cynical and paranoid reality.

title: PLAY CASH COBAIN
description: The New York rapper-producer’s fluttering hi-hats soundtracked the summer of sexy drill. His new LP stamps the moment by doubling down on his city-specific sexcapades.

title: Mucho Mistrust
description: On its second album, the Bay Area band adds surrealist detours and melodic reflections to its snarling, witty post-punk.

title: Romance
description: On its fourth album, the Irish group trades steely post-punk for stadium-sized alt rock with a hefty dose of Y2K nostalgia. It’s an unexpected shift, but they handle it with panache.

title: Woodland
description: The intuitive bond between the two musicians remains at the forefront of their terrific new album, full of quiet adventures and clear empathy.

title: Forever
description: A bold, bright sound dominates the band’s third album, in which moments of emotional overload lead to some of their biggest, most ambitious pop songs yet.

title: Lover, Other
description: The British singer-songwriter’s third album embraces a daring, inventive production style that highlights the soulful power of her voice.

title: $10 Cowboy / Visions of Dallas
description: With a blend of country, folk, soul, and cover songs, the Texan singer-songwriter’s recent pair of albums outline his modern take on classic Americana.

title: F-1 Trillion
description: Post Malone’s first bona fide country album captures the sound of mainstream Nashville, made with a little help from Dolly Parton, Tim McGraw, Luke Combs, and many more.

title: Sun Glories
description: Collaborating with drummer Ryan Jewell and saxophonist Cole Pulice, the pedal steel player steers into triumphant post-rock territory on his most surprising and exploratory album yet.

title: Delicate Steve Sings
description: Guitarist Steve Marion does not, in fact, sing a note on this tenderly executed albeit bland collection of lounge-act covers and originals.

title: Sky Hundred
description: The South Korean shoegazer’s surprise new release would be called a “back to basics” album if Parannoul had ever once sounded like a typical rock band.

title: Persona EP
description: The New Jersey hardcore band returns with a five-song EP that keeps the unrelenting ferocity of their early work and adds bolder production and deeper hooks.

artist: Panda Bear / Sonic Boom / Mariachi 2000 de Cutberto Pérez
title: Reset Mariachi EP
description: Panda Bear dreamed for years of hearing his songs played by a Mexican mariachi group. He finally gets his chance.

title: Descending Moonshine Dervishes
description: A new reissue of a 1975 Berlin organ performance rescues an overlooked masterpiece of early ambient music. In its crystalline churns, conventional timekeeping melts away.

title: Quantum Baby
description: Hot off the flirty summer hit “Nasty,” the singer-songwriter delivers a lean and muscular collection of songs for the club and the road.

title: Lungu Boy
description: The third record from the Nigerian pop star has the muted thrills of a victory lap: a triumphant showcase that covers well-trodden ground.

title: BETA
description: Following a move from New Delhi to a scenic village in North Goa, the Indian indie rockers explore sunnier, more bucolic shades in their trademark fusion of sounds, eras, and cultural traditions.

title: 3rd Shift
description: The Detroit rapper teams up with Oakland’s Squadda B for some interstate madness. J.U.S rolls with every beat for a record that sounds specifically local but refreshingly timeless.

title: Disaster Trick
description: The Boston group translates its habitually dreamlike reveries into sharply focused songwriting, bringing newfound heaviness to its narcotic haze.

title: Triple Seven
description: The Indianapolis band is a standout voice in the new generation of shoegaze. Its debut album is filled with memorable hooks and blistering guitars that draw on Midwest emo and 2000s pop.

title: VULTURES 2
description: The sequel to the rappers’ collab album from February is even shoddier in construction and execution than its predecessor.

title: Sugar Honey Iced Tea
description: On the Clayton County rapper’s third album, her winking Southern charm gets lost in an abundance of anonymous beats.

title: Opus
description: Six months before his death, the composer sat down to record Opus, his final concert film and album. Slow and contemplative, it offers a moving testament to his spirit and perseverance.

title: Shadowbox
description: The rapper continues to mine heavy existential themes against a newly vaporous, kaleidoscopic palette. It’s among his darkest work, but also his most piercing and inventive.

title: Sorcs 80
description: John Dwyer’s ever-inventive psych-garage band plugs synth demos into samplers and thrashes and pulses without the aid of a single guitar. Just add saxophone.

title: This Is How Tomorrow Moves
description: Bea Kristi’s third album, co-produced by Rick Rubin, deploys a more subdued, acoustic palette to render an accurate portrait of early adulthood.

title: Life Till Bones
description: Jade Lilitri’s latest is an economical, punchy rock record about love and death that still expands the band’s core sound.

title: Another Day
description: The Toronto hardcore band’s latest builds on their previous records not by going bigger but by honing the small stuff: intricate melodies, squelching guitar loops, and Damian Abraham’s ornately aggressive performance.

title: Nice Guys
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit an essential 1979 example of self-described Great Black Music from a tight-knit collective that embraced traditional and experimental forms all at once.

title: Realistic IX
description: The New Orleans drone duo follows up its 2011 album Common Era with an unexpected pivot into shoegaze. At its best, it makes familiar formulas sound alien.

title: Bird’s Eye
description: The singer collaborates with Dahi for a genre-blending album that experiments within and beyond R&B—always guided by her expansive, cotton-candy soft soprano.

title: Doing It for Me
description: On an album filled with A-list producers and magnificent beats, the San Francisco rapper skates by with simplistic, autopilot rhymes.

artist: Google Earth / James Riotto / John Vanderslice
title: Street View
description: In a new collaboration with producer James Riotto, John Vanderslice strikes a fascinating balance between his art-rock inclinations and his newfound passion for exploratory electronic music.

title: I LAY DOWN MY LIFE FOR YOU
description: On a frenetic album that tests the limits of his trolling, JPEGMAFIA hints at the delicate balance of truth and fiction behind his confrontational mix of noise, rap, and punk.

title: Smoke & Fiction
description: Four years after an unexpected comeback LP, the Los Angeles country-punk veterans return with their final album. They sound vigorous and assured, finding fresh inspiration in familiar sounds.

title: No Name
description: The old Jack White suddenly steps out from behind the curtain with 42 minutes of amp-busting blues punk. Even the last couple of White Stripes albums weren’t this stacked.

title: Michael & the Mighty Midnight Revival, Songs for Sinners and Saints
description: Backed by his live band, the rapper remixes and elaborates the autobiographical themes and gospel uplift of 2023’s Michael.

title: AGGRO DR1FT (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: The MPC wizard’s ethereal synths are the perfect complement to Harmony Korine’s over-the-top spectacle, playing up its impressionistic textures and humanizing its hallucinatory violence.

title: Sophcore EP
description: Amid the rich textures and hushed production of this playful, soulful six-song EP, the San Bernardino native radiates sensuality—and fun.

title: Skull Dream
description: On his first solo billing in six years, the guitarist—a member of Darkside and Taper’s Choice—bids farewell to NYC. These patient, wistful explorations are heavy on both melody and collaborative spirit.

title: Cellophane Memories
description: The Texas singer uses experimental vocal collages set against actual Lynchian backdrops to create a uniquely off-kilter kind of evanescence.

title: Ultimate Love Songs Collection
description: The rapper and visual artist’s debut compilation is an intimate opus of lo-fi sampledelia, a 50-song catalog of memories, half-thoughts, and moments of discovery.

title: Kampire Presents: A Dancefloor in Ndola
description: This invigorating compilation of African dance music from the 1980s and ’90s is a nostalgic snapshot of the Ugandan DJ’s youth—and a celebration of the selector’s ability to connect disparate sounds.

title: One Day
description: Brian Leeds—aka ambient-techno maestro Huerco S.—presents a collection of dubby, foggy dance tracks where mystery feels like the main event.

title: Blackout
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the pop star’s singular 2007 album, her oft-misunderstood comeback and a defining cultural artifact of the dark, trashy, celebrity-driven essence of the aughts.

title: Resuscitate!
description: Captured in Chicago in March 2023, the singer-songwriter and his band achieve a sort of dream state, finding otherworldly new forms for familiar songs about rebirth and revelation.

title: Memoirs in Armour
description: The follow-up to the New York lyricist’s Def Jam debut is a stripped-back canvas for his searing, lived-in stories. His vision is clearer than ever.

title: G.O.D.’s Network (Reb7rth)
description: On his first album in 15 years, the trailblazer cedes the spotlight to a roster of spiritual disciples. There are flashes of magnetism, but the visionary rapper we know and love is mostly missing in action.

title: forgive too slow
description: The English and French musician makes crystalline electro-pop songs about mistakes, heartbreaks, and relationships that never got far enough to be either.

title: To the Ghosts
description: Five albums in, Cults sound just as eerie and cheery as ever but struggle to transcend the fleeting pleasantries of paint-by-numbers pop.

title: The Eternal Now
description: The underground rap vet caps a prolific mixtape run with a full-length DJ Muggs collaboration that’s loaded with the life experience to go with beats that bring to mind late-’90s Queens.

title: marked
description: The South London experimental musician shifts from her usual leftfield electronics and avant-garde R&B to an album of blistering guitar noise. She has a few more tricks up her sleeve, too.

title: Strange Burden
description: The Austin quintet’s debut fuses grimy post-punk, agit-jazz, and warped disco into a unique, oblique, and cheeky sound of their own.

title: Are Possible
description: Banjo player Nathan Bowles, double bassist Casey Toll, and drummer Rex McMurray reunite for a spacious jam session informed by Appalachian folk and modern minimalism.

title: Vertigo
description: The Los Angeles quartet reinvents its sound on its sixth album, building on the cosmic post-rock improvisations first teased on 2022’s live Spiders in the Rain.

title: Natur
description: The Kenyan artist’s new release is a stunning portrait of the electromagnetic sounds and hidden noises of his hometown. In its swelling electrical currents lies a thesis about the richness and drama of everyday sounds.

title: Kansas Anymore
description: Tucker Pillsbury’s second album turns to folksy sincerity, recounting a celebrity breakup in songs that feel competent, cutesy, and almost believable.

title: Y2K!
description: The Bronx rapper’s full-length debut leans into a hard-nosed drill sound and features some of her most dynamic and abrasive bars to date.

title: Wild Guess
description: The Vermont indie-rock quartet’s debut album pits airy dreamscapes against raw realities, frolicking in the tumult of uncertainty.

title: Barrio Fino
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Daddy Yankee’s breakthrough album, the unforgettable year of “Gasolina,” and how the Puerto Rican rapper helped make reggaeton a global sensation.

title: Live at Wembley Stadium
description: Taken from a rousing 2023 reunion show, the UK stalwarts offer another souvenir double-live album filled with aged and elegant takes from the core of their songbook.

title: SMILE! :D
description: The one-time EDM superstar’s production has never sounded shinier or sugarier, but beneath the maximalist synths and peppy rhythms lurk more complicated, bittersweet feelings.

title: Vertigo
description: The debut from the UK pop singer is a proficient study of her influences but can’t help but feel like there’s a lack of personality to the songs.

title: Total Blue
description: Decked out in wind synths and fretless bass, the L.A. trio’s debut album lovingly invokes new age and ambient jazz at their most opulent. It’s a heartfelt argument that smoothness is not a crime.

title: Manual Manic Procedures
description: The Cleveland band puts thrills front and center on its second album, slotting monster riffs into gruesomely switchbacking arrangements.

title: Rapstar*
description: Layering disaffected vocals over glitchy beats, the duo’s second LP is a deadpan testament of the terminally online. It’s both mundane and disorienting, irritating and soothing.

title: Damaged
description: The Stuttgart producer Michael Fiedler’s debut album under a new moniker distills ambient dub into a wispy, wraithlike form.

title: Bando Stone and the New World
description: Donald Glover’s final album under this moniker features eclectic and adventurous rap and R&B, but the big swings never really connect.

title: Butu
description: Congolese singer Makara Bianko and French producer Débruit craft polyglot techno-punk with a bustling, metropolitan atmosphere.

title: Harmonics
description: The Hot Chip member’s third solo album proffers empathetic pop-house as the cure to what ails us. But in a divided world, politeness only goes so far.

title: Lambda
description: The Berlin-based producer’s new album is a spellbinding fusion of atmosphere and texture, forever on the point of mutating into new shapes.

title: Ashanti
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Ashanti’s assured blockbuster debut, a lynchpin record for the new era of pop and R&B at the dawn of the century.

title: Starface
description: With a sci-fi concept and a psychedelic sensibility, the NiNE8 Collective member brings a mix of funk, ska punk, grunge, dance, and indie that’s part London, part L.A.

title: All Hell
description: Self-funded, self-released, self-produced, and self-referential, the Welsh rock band’s seventh album has a big-tent sound with all the requisite wit and panache. It is unquestionably the ultimate Los Campesinos! album.

title: True Magic
description: The UK dance producer’s effervescent debut glows from within, powered by nostalgic ’80s synth and a stacked guest list that includes Rina Sawayama, piri, and Empress Of.

title: My Light, My Destroyer
description: The New York singer’s smoldering, sophisticated songs get a little more cosmic while retaining their characteristic wit and charm.

title: Big Ideas
description: The California singer and producer’s whimsical alt-pop bounces between disco beats and reggae grooves, 1960s soul and 1990s indie folk.

title: The EyeWitness
description: On an album inspired by the psychological effects of trauma, the Detroit techno pioneer and science-fiction storyteller pursues his search for new frontiers that lie far from the dancefloor.

title: HEIS
description: On his second album, the Nigerian star pays tribute to Benin City and its history with spring-loaded rhythms and gleeful provocations.

title: When I’m Called
description: On his fifth album and first for Fat Possum, the Southern folk singer finds ingenious ways to pull old obscurities into the anxious present.

title: The Death of Slim Shady (Coup de Grâce)
description: A concept album about killing his alter ego can’t save the impishly clever Eminem from the same tired, dated, developmentally arrested material.

title: Across the Tracks
description: The Detroit rapper teams up with the Missouri producer on a muted album that plays out like a nostalgic travelogue. Despite his laid-back delivery, James’ verses burble with conflict and regret.

title: Pan the Pansexual
description: Through decayed beats and gothic atmospheres, the musician formerly known as Aristophanes transforms sexual desire into an existential threat.

title: The Great American Bar Scene
description: The country crossover star’s excellent songwriting is raw and evocative, and though he continues to hone his sound, the total emotional experience of the album sometimes wears a bit thin.

title: Paint a Room
description: The indie rock vet’s intimate songwriting comes to life in blossoming arrangements seemingly plucked straight out of a vintage California bachelor pad.

title: Macro
description: On its fourth album, the Oakland duo uses disco-fueled dance grooves and gently psychedelic atmospheres as vehicles for introspection.

title: Raqs-e-Bismil
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 2000 album from one of the most famous and influential musicians in South Asian history, a spare, heart-rending, spiritually transcendent experience.

title: Coming and Going
description: Interweaving spiritual jazz, thumping rhythms, and contributions from a tight-knit group of collaborators, the Nicaraguan Canadian musician imbues his fifth LP with the warmth of human connection.

title: Passage du Desir
description: Sturgill Simpson’s outstanding album under a new stage name expertly balances cosmic and outlaw country and reintroduces himself as the premier Nashville outsider.

title: Can You Hear Me Dreaming?
description: The Australian producer and vocalist tells stories of anguished romance over crisp drums and crystalline melodies. When she’s not dragged down by bland hooks and generic beats, she glitters.

title: Charm
description: Claire Cottrill’s third album sinks deeper into a soft-rock sound as her songwriting takes on an understated new confidence.

title: Leviathan
description: At once telegenic and slightly tongue in cheek, the Montreal composer’s ersatz chamber music is proof that you can love something and poke fun at it at the same time.

title: The weight of the world
description: The California producer’s next-gen dubstep rolls shards of digicore, hyperpop, shoegaze, and ASMR into elaborately pixelated clouds of chaos.

title: God Said No
description: The singer-songwriter’s second album sharpens the darkness of a romantic estrangement into glittering pop gems. Apollo is still full of longing, but he’s ready to show his claws.

title: Small Medium Large
description: Recorded across four nights of longform improv at L.A.’s Enfield Tennis Academy, then cut up and remixed, the quintet’s debut marks an exciting milestone in the city’s emerging jazz scene.

title: A Record Collection, Reduced to a Mixtape / And Yes, This Is My Singing Voice!
description: A double LP and CD box set collect the irascible English rockers’ studio recordings, B-sides, and live cuts. Though new material is limited, the band’s commitment to legacy is perfectly in character.

title: Algorithm
description: The prodigious singer reunites with producer D’Mile for a collection of live-band soul and future-R&B that aspires to update the classic seduction jam with a dose of modern vulnerability.

title: Walk Thru Me
description: Lou Barlow and John H. Davis’ first body of new work in 25 years applies a fresh coat of paint to the droning indie rock sound of the duo’s formative years.

title: Samurai
description: Lupe Fiasco reunites with producer Soundtrakk for a jazzy, subdued album that weighs the challenges and indignities of sustaining a career in the arts.

title: Home Constellation Study
description: The 24-year-old Providence musician’s 15th album bursts with imagination, complexity, and feeling. The abundance of ideas might seem excessive if it weren’t so carefully arranged.

title: Service Merchandise
description: The rap supergroup meditates on the passage of time on their new LP. It possesses all the intimacy and nostalgia of a ’90s parking lot cypher between friends.

title: Redd Kross
description: The eternally youthful McDonald brothers celebrate their band’s 45th anniversary with a signature blend of pristine melodic craft and garage-band insolence.

title: Notes From a Quiet Life
description: With Ernest Green’s pastoral Georgia home as its emotional backdrop, Washed Out’s fifth LP clears the haze from his structured songcraft and winds up feeling inert.

title: Birds & Beasts
description: Stretching out keys, piano, and pedal steel in wide-open space, the ambient country trio’s new album underlines the vast scale of evolutionary time.

title: Love Changes Everything
description: On its first album in 12 years, the veteran instrumental trio discovers a newfound spontaneity, summoning some of the most beautiful and emotional work of the group’s career.

title: Evil Does Not Exist
description: Following her Drive My Car soundtrack, the Japanese composer again links up with director Ryusuke Hamaguchi; this time, her ambiguous, atmospheric pieces are even more central to the narrative.

title: MEGAN
description: The Texas rap star’s new album has something for every type of Megan Thee Stallion fan—and the strain of catering to the masses has begun to crowd out the goofy charm of her best music.

title: Revival of a Friend
description: The Bay Area band’s two singer-guitarists have been friends since they were teens. On a debut album shot through with grief and tenderness, that intimacy fuels an almost telepathic interplay.

title: Bad Cameo
description: The duo’s joint project is wistful and occasionally danceable, juxtaposing steely electronica with a stadium-ready take on Yachty’s sing-rap sensibilities. But too often, they play it safe.

title: Crash
description: On their lusty new album, the L.A. singer and songwriter leapfrogs across trap-inflected R&B, countryfied ballads, and bassy pop confections.

title: Pills ‘n’ Thrills and Bellyaches
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the apex of the infamous UK band, a hedonistic and sampledelic Madchester masterpiece that reinvented post-punk for the rave era.

title: Songwriter
description: A set of recently unearthed studio recordings sheds light on the country icon’s remarkable comeback in the early 1990s.

title: C,XOXO
description: The pop star’s fourth LP is a transitional record mistakenly labeled as a statement album. Her impressionistic tale of lost love and aimless youth is electrifying but inconsistent.

title: roses are red, tears are blue — A Fountain Baby Extended Play
description: The Ghanaian American singer’s new EP bubbles and froths with Afropop effervescence. It’s a little more subdued than its predecessor, but no less fluid.

title: B_B EP
description: The Seoul producer and one-half of the electronic group Salamanda makes effervescent, maximalist music. Her new EP is her most dynamic and evocative solo release yet.

title: Sentir que no sabes
description: On her new album, the Mexico City-based cellist and singer moves from abstraction toward more familiar pop and rock silhouettes. But her lyrics remain committed to the power of opacity.

title: Hot Sun Cool Shroud EP
description: EPs have traditionally played a peripheral role in the Chicago group’s catalog, but this six-song release has both the vision and the range of their full-lengths.

title: A Dog’s Chance
description: This internet-enabled rap trio’s new collaborative album is a brief blast of unruly energy that bounces between 5G towers in New York, Atlanta, Milwaukee, and beyond.

title: Proxy Music
description: Stricken by a disease that left her unable to sing, the British songwriter recruits a cast of guest vocalists for a set of songs that toy with assumptions about authorship and interpretation.

title: #gigi
description: The UK-born, L.A.-based rapper and beatmaker vacuums up Jersey club, Brazilian funk, classic soul, and Auto-Tune melodies for a crispy, kinetic mix with a foot in every corner of the internet.

title: The Healer
description: The experimental metal trio’s four-song, 76-minute album is the peak of their career. It’s dense and invigorating, highlighting the band’s dexterity, creativity, and clarity of purpose.

title: Scream From New York, NY
description: The buzzy New York City rock quintet’s debut taps into a vivid sense of place. Their keening intensity captures a snapshot of a city coming unglued.

title: Elixa
description: The Australian trio’s zonked lo-fi electronica and dub pop beams in from an alternate dimension where the primary building blocks of pop music are melodica and drum machine.

title: ÉXODO
description: The corrido icon’s charisma shines on this sprawling double album, but La Doble P’s pop-star turn is less convincing.

title: WeirdOs
description: The saxophone-and-drum duo’s muscular, distorted, freeform tracks connect the London post-punk and jazz scenes like an arcane new subplot.

title: Salt and Sugar Look the Same
description: Assembled in a year-long process of file-swapping between Berlin and L.A., this hazy, collage-like album takes the form of a wordless conversation. It’s uncanny, familiar, and warmly evocative.

title: Welcome to the Pleasuredome
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the subversive 1984 debut from the UK synth-pop group, an exquisite-sounding album that snuck an ode to amyl nitrate and orgasms onto pop charts around the world.

title: Disconnect
description: The pair’s debut collaboration is an amorphous, droning flood that sounds like the advent of the end times. In its hopeless sound world lies a poignant condemnation of colonial violence.

title: Resort
description: Byran Müller’s latest LP plays like a guided tour of his catalog. It’s some of his warmest and most inviting music to date.

title: The Gloss
description: The former Ought members’ second album balances economy with exploration, reaffirming their place in a lineage of prickly, leftfield guitar rock.

title: Big for You
description: The singer’s debut album is an intimate, soulful project that spotlights her versatile voice and the experimental touches that give the album its unique texture.

title: As It Ever Was, So It Will Be Again
description: On their first new album in six years, the folk troubadours balance out-of-time balladry with a mature sensibility that’s attuned to melancholy and mortality in the present.

title: Grush
description: On his 17th solo album under the alias, Mike Paradinas looks fondly back upon IDM’s melodic golden age and finds sneaky ways to make familiar ideas sound fresh.

title: DOPAMINE
description: The pop singer’s long-awaited debut is also a comeback and reintroduction. With her plush voice and slick production, she plays it cool and also plays it safe.

title: Moth
description: The California singer-songwriter’s third album pulls sounds from all across the psychedelic neo-soul spectrum as she muses about matters of the heart.

title: Scattersun
description: Twinkling riffs collide with dial-up static and blown-out drums on a collaborative album from the bit-crushing electronic maximalists and the South Korean dream-pop darling.

title: Placenta
description: Assisted by players like Sam Gendel and André 3000, the ambient-jazz bandleader explores the spiritual and psychedelic aspects of human birth.

title: Santa Cruz
description: Densely packed and deeply sincere, the latest chapter of David Bazan’s musical memoir project spans a decade of life, from eighth grade into his early 20s.

title: F.U.N. T.O.Y.
description: The L.A. rapper’s dead-eyed hustler tales are grimier and druggier than ever. It’s a harsh toke, but the crackling production gives it the energy it needs.

title: Inter-Dimensional Music
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a foundational new age album from 1975, an alluring, slightly fried soundscape channeled directly to its composer from an inter-dimensional entity named Vista.

title: One Hand Clapping
description: Shelved for decades and now finally released in full, Wings’ 1974 Abbey Road sessions are intimate and exploratory, showcasing a seldom heard, anything-goes side of the former Beatle.

title: Why Lawd?
description: Anderson .Paak and Knxwledge’s sly, smooth-talking rap&B sounds older and wiser these days. The duo’s stellar second album layers doubt and insecurity into jet-setting antics and featherbed-plush beats.

title: boy
description: At a time when dance music is pop and pop is rap and rap is emo and everything is electronic, the Los Angeles-based artist synthesizes it all into a gaudy yet distinctive sound.

title: Box for Buddy, Box for Star
description: On the first proper album under his solo alias, Water From Your Eyes’ Nate Amos balances self-reflection with a sly, idiosyncratic approach to DIY pop songcraft.

title: Born in the Wild
description: On her adventurous and melancholic full-length debut, the Nigerian pop star re-asserts herself as an imaginative producer and the author of her own lore.

title: Eight Pointed Star
description: Behind the elegant sounds of Laurel Canyon, the Los Angeles singer-songwriter’s vivid and knotty lyrics evoke half-imagined landscapes with startling clarity.

title: Timeless
description: Spotlighting over a dozen vocalists on a suite of airy, upbeat collaborations, the Canadian producer’s big mainstream moment showcases his slick sound in a variety of different settings.

title: Lived Here for a While
description: The Austin band’s knowing, sharply rendered indie rock filters life on the road into songs about interpersonal angst and heartland unease.

title: with 2
description: Crazed, noisy, and barely finished, the New York rapper’s latest tape digs into his mad mind and hypnotic sound.

title: Breathe​.​.​. Godspeed EP
description: The Colombian producer’s galaxy-sized rave tracks are unsettling and exhilarating. This 21-minute EP is an essential record for the vanguard of dance music.

title: Statik
description: Composed during an extended flow state, the UK avant-techno producer’s hypnotic new album balances murky, lo-fi dread with moments of shimmering beauty.

title: Below the Waste
description: The South London band’s third album combines subtle garage-pop grooves and clanging noise-rock for the most full and refined version of the Goat Girl experience.

title: Inside the Marble
description: On her debut album, the New York singer-songwriter grapples with the big feelings and small details of young adulthood over appropriately cinematic backdrops.

title: AmeriKKKa’s Most Wanted
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Ice Cube’s 1990 debut solo record, a groundbreaking piece of hard and funky reality rap that introduced the tabloid decade.

title: What Is Not Strange?
description: The Los Angeles composer—son of late Fluxus composer Yoshi Wada—flexes his avant-garde instincts on a surprisingly song-driven new album, moving from abstraction into more expressive forms.

title: BRAT
description: With her sixth album, Charli XCX transcends all narratives and delivers a hit. Brat is imperious and cool, nuanced and vulnerable, and one of the best pop albums of the year.

title: I Hear You
description: Crowd-pleasing anthems come naturally to the Korean superstar DJ. If only her debut album had more of them.

title: The Year I Turned 21
description: The singer-songwriter’s second album is a well-curated coming-of-age tale. Full of summery R&B and glitzy amapiano, it moves beyond feel-good anthems and thoughtfully tackles the insecurities of young adulthood.

title: Where I’ve Been, Isn’t Where I’m Going
description: After a decade of searching for the intersection of hip-hop and country and a star turn on Cowboy Carter, the Virginia-born singer finds much more than a party on his third album.

title: Big Swimmer
description: At its best, Hannah Merrick’s stream-of-consciousness songwriting feels like sitting shotgun with her as she crosses the country, taking in the sublime and the absurd in equal measure.

title: The Dream of Delphi
description: The singer-songwriter’s new album tackles the tenderness of motherhood with a series of transportive, ambient-adjacent experiments.

title: Escape at Your Own Pace EP
description: Setting aside the punishing death metal of their main band, the Tomb Mold players’ side project floats a whimsical fusion of math rock and city pop festooned with sneaky metal accents.

title: Umbilical
description: The Louisiana sludge-metal giants have always professed a fondness for classic grunge; they make good on those influences on a streamlined album that’s also one of their heaviest yet.

title: In Sexyy We Trust
description: A nice little addition to last year’s breakout Hood Hottest Princess, the St. Louis native’s EP is packed again with filthy, horny, sex-fueled shenanigans.

title: She’s So Unusual
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Cyndi Lauper’s massive debut, a slyly feminist new wave pop record whose undeniable singles helped usher in the MTV era.

title: Insurrection
description: Unearthing 11 lost recordings from the late ’90s, the Suicide co-founder’s newest posthumous release frames him as a doomsday prophet of the information age.

title: Night Reign
description: The singer and composer’s wondrous fourth album deepens the sound of her boundless folk-jazz style. Its gestures are bold, romantic, and often unforgettable.

title: Dark Times
description: The Long Beach rapper threads the fables of the past with the reality of the present for another expertly written, starkly candid record.

title: The Fool
description: Reconnecting with his heartland rock roots, John Rossiter interrogates his artistic impulses and creates his most magnetic and direct record to date.

title: Sewaside III
description: After 2022’s stripped-back Sewaside II, the Montreal rapper-producer opts for stranger beats, a packed guest list, and what sound like real instruments to balance his beguiling sample flips.

title: We Have Dozens of Titles
description: In a new archival collection, Jim O’Rourke and David Grubbs have polished and stitched together every scrap and forgotten rarity into one final album, a fitting final chapter for an indescribably great band.

title: Searching
description: Using inscrutable digital techniques—randomization, automation, perhaps a little black magic—the Bay Area artist makes bewitchingly skewed techno full of tangled loops and mismatched time signatures.

title: Morning Dove White
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a lost downtempo classic from 1993, a dreamy, fascinating chimera of styles and moods produced by the legendary Andrew Weatherall.

artist: Wadada Leo Smith / Amina Claudine Myers
title: Central Park’s Mosaics of Reservoir, Lake, Paths and Gardens
description: The AACM composer pays tribute to the cultural history of a monumental work of public infrastructure in a set of elegiac pieces for trumpet and piano.

title: Frog in Boiling Water
description: The Brooklyn indie rock band’s fourth album is an anxious and sour record that copes with capitalism and its knock-on emotional effects.

title: We Could Stay
description: The Brooklyn producer’s debut album is filled with immersive, inventive reimaginings of dance music, flickering between ecstasy and decay.

title: #RICHAXXHAITIAN
description: The New Jersey rapper returns with a supreme sense of confidence. He glides effortlessly over grainy beats, putting his skill for meandering but meticulous raps on full display.

title: Please Don’t Cry
description: The North Carolina rapper’s fourth album clarifies her identity and the depth of her talent over lush blends of R&B, gospel, reggae, and trap. It’s a vivid affirmation of self and community—and a rap clinic.

title: Valedictorian
description: The latest viral rapper absorbs Black influences while marketing himself as if he doesn’t. His songs are fine, but he is a cipher, a husk, and a vacuum of taste.

title: To All Trains
description: Released just 10 days after Steve Albini’s death, the trio’s sixth record closes the book on the band and serves as a reliably excellent epitaph.

title: Room Under the Stairs
description: Co-produced with Nashville’s Dave Cobb, the onetime boy bander’s new solo album is a coming-clean, “back to basics” record that hits like background music.

title: Snake EP
description: After experiments with UK garage, club breaks, and more, the cheerfully chameleonic Atlanta producer turns his attention to dance punk; the results are as mischievous as ever.

title: HIT ME HARD AND SOFT
description: The pop star teams with her brother Finneas for their third album together, expanding the cooly dark vision of their sound. It’s an honest and ambitious album when it’s not inert and repetitive.

title: Valentino
description: The Staten Island artist’s debut full-length collects dreamy R&B and punchy pop rap, chronicling stories of heartbreak and hookups with a cool, crowd-pleasing ease.

title: What a Devastating Turn of Events
description: Recasting Y2K British alt-pop for a new generation, the South London singer-songwriter’s debut tackles heartbreak and loss with humor and conviction.

title: AMAMA
description: The New York psych-pop quartet returns with an album that finds compelling new ways to make mini-dramas of the mundane.

title: Hex Dealer
description: On their new album, the New York band collides hardcore, dance punk, and hip-hop like a little kid smashing together action figures. It’s an exhilarating, refreshing, and inventive listen.

title: P.S. Fuck You
description: The upstart Alabama rapper has big hype and a personality to match. His new full-length shows off a more human side.

title: Judy at Carnegie Hall
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Judy Garland’s mythical 1961 live album, a late-career triumph that helped to outline the shape of queer fandom for decades to come.

title: Sti.ll
description: Ambitiously remaking a 2002 ambient-glitch album with clarinet, vibraphone, cello, and other acoustic instruments, New York composer Joseph Branciforte discovers new depths in a minimalist classic.

title: Lives Outgrown
description: Thirty years after stepping into the spotlight, the Portishead singer reintroduces herself with her debut solo album. History weighs heavy on her songs, but she takes pains to avoid her musical past.

title: I AM JORDAN
description: Despite its technical mastery, the English producer’s debut full-length struggles to deliver on the emotional revelation it promises.

title: The Hollow
description: The British singer-songwriter’s harrowing, physical folk music forces you to confront an awful and awesome kind of beauty.

title: Mayday
description: The Quebecois singer and guitarist transforms French and English folk ballads into songs where hoary tradition yields boldly contemporary sounds.

title: Dust Devil
description: The expansive debut from the Berlin-based artist features many guests from the fringes of ambient electronic music. It’s a crinkly, supple, meditative opus.

title: Ten Fold
description: With singular grace and flair, Yaya Bey deepens her connection to homespun funk and R&B while transforming grief, insecurities, and depletion into a full embrace of life.

title: One of Wun
description: As hip-hop’s elite ice him out, the Atlanta star tries to keep the good times rolling. These may sound like the catchy Gunna songs of the past, but they don’t feel like them.

title: Almighty So 2
description: The long-teased sequel to his cult-classic mixtape is a highlight in the Chicago rapper’s career, bringing the first-wave drill he helped popularize screaming into the future.

title: I’m totally fine with it 👍 don’t give a fuck anymore 👍
description: On its second post-comeback album, the Scottish duo turns its narrative attention to human behavior in the digital age, to incisive and occasionally nihilistic ends.

title: Singeli Ya Maajabu
description: Nyege Nyege’s latest snapshot of Tanzanian singeli pairs an avant-garde producer with a local keyboardist; the high-BPM results sound like a loose, extremely weird jam session.

title: Death Jokes
description: Filtered through warped hip-hop beats and garbled samples, Damon McMahon’s self-produced sixth album is a characteristically oblique apocalypse tale about living for today.

title: I Am Toward You
description: On his first album in six years, Tom Krell shrouds labyrinthine songs in distortion and slips down referential rabbit holes. The extremes can be daunting, but the highs are ecstatic.

title: Romanticism
