description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a 1995 album that changed the sound of dancehall while pointing the genre in a newly reflective direction.

title: Before These Crowded Streets
description: Newly reissued on vinyl, the most experimental album from the Charlottesville jam institution explores the uneasy zone between celebratory anthems and grim lamentations.

title: Cartwheel
description: Will Anderson amplifies everyday heartbreak with towering shoegaze and supersized power-pop anthems that demand to be played loud.

title: The Masterplan (Remastered Edition)
description: Newly reissued and remastered, the Gallagher brothers’ 1998 B-sides collection remains a smartly curated, thoughtfully sequenced set that stands among their finest work.

title: Sweet Justice
description: The Australian musician chooses herself over the bullshit on a cheeky, colorful album that flexes greater musical confidence.

title: Dancing on the Edge
description: After fronting the rock band State Champion, the Louisville artist crafts a solo debut full of vivid songwriting and cosmic-slacker jams.

title: Vidrio
description: The Mexico City duo of Mabe Fratti and Héctor Tosta break with the hushed beauty of the cellist’s earlier work, exploring sprawling new directions in modern composition, jazz, and art song.

title: For Forever
description: The Austin band’s first album in 18 years puts an ever-so-slightly sharper edge on their familiar, slow-burning indie rock.

title: Half Eaten by Dogs
description: The Cincinnati synth-punk trio dials up the energy on a zippy new album.

title: Jenny From Thebes
description: John Darnielle delves into the lore of 2002’s All Hail West Texas with a soft-rock opera that adds baroque arrangements to his brutal, tender storytelling.

title: Larger Than Life
description: The Maryland R&B star’s third album is stacked with DMV-area talent and storytelling reminiscent of your most toxic ex. But how does he really feel?

title: Nekkuja
description: The Barcelona musician expands her dizzying art-pop sound with sharper hooks and a feistier spirit.

title: There Is No End
description: Vancouver’s atmospheric noisemakers team up with Norwegian dream-pop artist Tuvaband, whose luminous voice brings focus to the group’s sprawling avant-prog.

title: Desolation’s Flower
description: The Pacific Northwest metal duo’s riveting new album is a sludgy and simmering call to action.

title: Robed in Rareness
description: Flanked by a close circle of collaborators, hip-hop experimentalist Ishmael Butler takes a brief, mysterious trip through rap aesthetics past and future.

title: chaos takes the wheel and i am a passenger
description: The San Jose band’s second album is a collection of gnarly emo epics that spotlight the underbelly of being a touring musician.

title: Polygon
description: On her second album about environmental catastrophes in her native Kazakhstan, the London-based composer turns her attention to the radioactive legacy of the Semipalatinsk Test Site.

title: 1989 (Taylor’s Version)
description: Taylor keeps her re-records very close to the originals, but five previously unreleased songs add depth and context to what was then her galactic, career-shifting pop debut.

title: Lahai
description: The multi-hyphenate singer-songwriter’s second album, densely packed but light as a feather, explores life and the many leaps of faith required to truly live it.

title: Diamonds and Pearls (Super Deluxe Edition)
description: Prince’s hip-hop-influenced ’90s comeback is the subject of a new box set that offers fascinating insight into a prolific, if uneven, period in his career.

title: Action Adventure
description: Synth-rich and emotionally ambiguous, the producer’s new instrumental LP meditates on nostalgia for the sound of terrestrial radio in the 1980s.

title: Floodland
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a 1987 goth rock masterpiece, a dramatic and winkingly macabre record from the mind of a man who thought it was all sort of a joke.

title: 讨好自己 Please Myself
description: Four albums released between 1994 and 1996 showcase the Cantopop icon (and Cocteau Twins collaborator) confidently moving beyond adult-contemporary and toward her own singular voice.

title: Madres
description: The Peruvian producer’s debut album is a shimmery collection of protest chants, club rhythms, and sunlit synths that testifies to dance music’s spiritual nourishment.

title: Models
description: The UK electronic musician used neural networks to wring synthetic voices into strange, unintelligible shapes. The results are by turns funny, poignant, and frightening.

title: Hold
description: On his latest album, Jack Tatum incorporates newly vulnerable songwriting into his ’80s dreamworld.

title: A Little Touch of Schleicher in the Night
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter makes being a loser sound lush with textured, self-deprecating songs that land like punchlines.

title: RAW
description: JT and Yung Miami strive to regain their spot as the dirtiest, most provocative hitmakers in rap.

title: Spike Field
description: On their spectral new album, the Oakland musician explores the promise of connection and the terror of the past.

title: Foxy
description: Loosely keyed to a story of Hollywood hedonism in the ’70s, the second album from William Basinski’s dance-pop project taps into the teeth-grinding edginess that follows a euphoric high.

title: How To Capture Playful
description: The New England rapper celebrates the joys of gaming on a bright and bubbly collaborative album.

title: Romantic Music
description: Reuniting after a decade, ex-Abe Vigoda members Michael Vidal and Juan Velasquez make a welcome return to sighing, swirling guitar and dusky post-punk ambiance.

title: Sator Arepo
description: Inspired by traditional music and an ancient mystery, French producer Julien Hairon creates buzzing, digitized dance beats that iterate endlessly on themselves.

title: Salmon Graveyard
description: Using electric mandolin, electrified violin, pedal steel, and snare, the Baltimore group’s music tilts bluegrass and Western swing toward raga and drone; it’s both avant-garde and compellingly listenable.

title: One More Time...
description: The classic Blink-182 lineup reunites to huff the fumes of their best material.

title: Chapter I: Forever, For Now EP
description: The daughter of sitar virtuoso Ravi Shankar has spent years exploring the instrument’s possibilities. Recording in Berlin with Arooj Aftab and Nils Frahm, she zeroes in on the nexus of music and memory.

title: AUDIOBOOK
description: The Los Angeles multi-instrumentalist improvised alongside his partner while she illustrated on paper; together, they’ve created an audiovisual album bursting with bold lines and vivid colors.

title: Rosa Rugosa EP
description: The Knife producer returns with his first major solo release in over a decade, a giddy, slippery EP that explodes into the sunlight.

title: The Darker the Shadow the Brighter the Light
description: The gloomy new album from British rapper, DJ, and now filmmaker Mike Skinner echoes but doesn’t equal the narrative force of the Streets’ classic material.

title: Set It Off
description: The rapper tries to reinvent himself with his second solo album, showing off impressive range while getting hampered by personality-free songwriting.

title: A Host for All Kinds of Life
description: The Los Angeles ambient musician continues to explore the interdependence of plants and humans, but they add new wrinkles to their placid style, shifting from easy listening to dynamic soundscaping.

title: Selvutsletter
description: Jenny Hval and Håvard Volden’s second album together rejects longform epics for pop structures—yet Hval’s songs are more elusive than ever.

title: Harlem: Diary of a Summer
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the 2005 solo LP from the Dipset rapper, who rendered his brusque New York City experience in surreally unnerving style.

title: Some Kinda Love: Performing the Music of the Velvet Underground
description: The indie rockers pay tribute to their heroes with a love and abandon that can only come from living with these songs for decades.

title: Census Designated
description: The singer-producer explodes her sound with a feverish blend of shoegaze and bedroom pop.

title: Hackney Diamonds
description: Speckled with guest stars and produced by Andrew Watt, the Stones’ second original album this century is a bunch of hackneyed duds, polished until the character has disappeared.

title: Jonny
description: Jonny Pierce’s eponymous new album reflects the characteristically sunny indie pop and increasingly inward focus of the Drums’ solo incarnation.

title: The Am3rican Dream
description: The two Golden State rappers sound like naturals on their funky, easygoing collaborative album with New York producer Harry Fraud.

title: A Great Chaos
description: The Opium affiliate’s new album is a creative breakthrough, flipping the script on Atlanta rap production and funneling his hedonistic tendencies into joyously unholy music.

title: Sweet Dreamin’
description: On his second record for Mac DeMarco’s label, the Australian singer-songwriter settles into an effortlessly smooth sound perfectly suited for date-night soundtracks.

title: Attachment Figure
description: On her subdued debut album, the Tallahassee singer-songwriter constructs an eerie, beguiling world imbued with a supernatural charge.

title: Afternoon X
description: The London group dials up the psychedelia on its fourth album, swapping out retro-futurist tropes and avant-pop touchstones for uneasy atmospheres and narcotic languor.

title: Burning Desire
description: The prolific New York rapper-producer’s latest album is self-assured and clear-eyed, ushering in an ambitious new era for the hometown hero.

title: And Then You Pray for Me
description: A sprawling new album from the Buffalo rapper subtly expands his raw and luxurious sound.

title: Scriptures
description: The Massachusetts producer’s new Christianity-themed album infuses Chicago drill and Atlanta trap with an air of holiness.

title: Tomorrow’s Fire
description: The Chicago-based indie rocker beefs up her sound on her third LP. Foregrounding her confident voice and formidable guitar skills, it’s a compact, muscular record guided by a single-minded intensity.

title: nadie sabe lo que va a pasar mañana
description: El Conejo Malo’s fifth solo LP is a rap homecoming. It doesn’t possess the magic or sophistication of his best work, but it’s just as horny and cavalier.

title: Water Made Us
description: The Chicago R&B poet and singer doesn’t just write about losing or finding love: Her tender and curious new album is all about the transformative potential of the journey.

title: Paint My Bedroom Black
description: The English singer-songwriter makes her full-length debut with a charmingly melodramatic set full of earnest writing and kinetic, multi-dimensional production.

title: Something to Give Each Other
description: The Australian singer is a hedonistic pop hero on an album that pulls together club nights, tender moments, last-call horniness, and eclectic samples with remarkable finesse.

title: Goodnight Summerland
description: The Montreal songwriter shifts toward a stripped-back, folksier sound, highlighting her gossamer voice as she reflects on the ache of grief and the passage of time.

title: Eulo Cramps
description: The UK producer’s new record pulls apart the seams of dance music, trading four-on-the-floor beats for meditative chaos and boundless expansion.

title: Excelsior
description: The New York producer’s second album is a dense and dizzying suite of collages that invites close listening.

title: Wasn’t Tomorrow Wonderful?
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the Ohio new wave band’s 1982 debut, an arch yet sincere sendup of humdrum modern life.

title: Surround
description: Commissioned as the soundtrack to a line of prefab homes, this 1986 ambient masterpiece doubles as a frame for the smallest, most quotidian sounds. It’s a testament to the act of listening itself.

title: The Rest EP
description: Six months after their debut album, Julien Baker, Phoebe Bridgers, and Lucy Dacus return with a self-mythological companion EP aglow with the sense of triumph from their imperial year.

title: Archives, Vol. 3: The Asylum Years (1972-1975)
description: The latest archival set collects demos and live recordings from the pivotal years between the stark solo songs of For the Roses, her full-band masterpiece Court & Spark, and the impressionistic jazz-pop of The Hissing of Summer Lawns.

title: Running From the Chase
description: The band’s imposing, precarious new album cements them in a history of North Carolina bands making thrilling indie rock.

title: Unum
description: Gathering inspiration from Maltese folk and ’70s psych-rock, the UK-based band makes complex, ambitious post-punk with the chaotic energy of an informal jam.

title: I Killed Your Dog
description: With an elliptical and bewitching new album, Taja Cheek turns her expansive, introspective compositions toward surreal humor and playfulness.

title: So Far So Good
description: The Oakland songwriter pairs abstract imagery with elegant arrangements on her dreamy, open-ended second album.

title: Growing at the Edges
description: On his fourth album helming the Brooklyn chamber folk ensemble, Jordan Lee brings a watchmaker’s precision to a baroque sound typically associated with billowy grandeur.

title: The Music of Heatmiser
description: A new compilation explores the early days of Elliott Smith's alt-rock band, whose tight songcraft and introspective lyrics set the stage for his solo work to come.

title: The X Tape
description: On his new mixtape, the Flint rapper continues his run as a solid flagbearer for his city’s rap scene. It’s a tight and punchline-driven offering, marred by occasionally stiff delivery.

title: Hot Commodity
description: The Brooklyn rapper and former beauty influencer has charisma to spare on her swaggering, stylish debut.

title: Perspective EP
description: The Pulitzer-nominated experimental producer finesses acoustic samples from the Third Coast Percussion ensemble into dazzling rhythmic workouts.

title: Goodbye, Hotel Arkada
description: The Los Angeles-based harpist’s songs remain characteristically serene and steeped in nostalgia, though guests like the Cure’s Lol Tolhurst and Slowdive’s Rachel Goswell add nuance to her sound.

title: Permission to Land… Again (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: What exactly was the Darkness? A 20th-anniversary reissue of their meteoric debut album reaffirms their pop-metal bona fides.

title: Tonite Longhorn
description: Three shows recorded at Minneapolis club Jay’s Longhorn between 1979 and 1980 capture a raw snapshot of a young band in flux, brimming with confidence and hopped up on speed.

title: For All the Dogs
description: On his eighth album, a skillful Drake struggles to keep it interesting. His familiar concerns, while occasionally sincere or funny, have become quite boring.

title: Perfect Picture
description: Soundtracked by euphoric bubblegum synth, the PC Music star takes a deep dive into two-dimensionality.

title: The NID Tapes: Electronic Music From India 1969​-​1972
description: Gathering vintage compositions from 27 tape reels, this expansive new collection highlights the brief but fertile period, more than 50 years ago, when avant-garde electronic music took root in India.

title: Hot Fruit
description: Acoustic guitarist Dan Knishkowy is joined by an improvisational quartet for an album of autumnal instrumental folk that meditates on self-knowledge and change.

title: Gettin’ It (Album Number Ten)
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the Oakland rapper’s imperial ’90s peak with the Dangerous Crew, a slick and funky landmark of pimp rap.

title: Next Door
description: The Tokyo guitarist and pianist channels jazz, fusion, and Japanese environmental music as he deepens the emotional resonance of his music while maintaining its soothing atmosphere.

title: Changing Channels
description: The Hessle Audio cofounder’s exuberant new album is stuffed with high BPMs, ribcage-vibrating basslines, and richly hued synths. Club music this banging is rarely so nuanced.

title: Several Songs About Fire
description: On his stripped-down second solo album, the Parquet Courts frontman finalizes a messy divorce with his adopted hometown, ruminating on vanished cityscapes and piercing memories.

title: Going...Going...Gone! EP
description: The zany, ’80s-inspired debut from the 24-year-old pop singer and TikTok star showcases a promising young artist in the age of internet virality.

title: Out and About
description: The Rotterdam quartet makes sparse yet atmospheric post-punk that draws inspiration from all things dreamy and twee.

title: Javelin
description: Sufjan’s masterful new album recalls his intimate singer-songwriter days. But it also draws on his entire catalog, his dazzling musicality, and his lifelong inquiries about love and devotion.

title: I Don’t Want You Anymore
description: Clementine Creevy sifts through the muck on her new album, picking up everything from radio-friendly electro-pop to fuzzed-out garage rock.

title: Yard
description: The Chicago band motors through big emotions with clear-eyed sincerity, bubblegum hooks, and mellow arrangements that feel like a warm embrace.

title: Debbie’s Son
description: The Los Angeles rapper’s second album this year confronts the uncertainties of life with characteristically reflective rhymes and a steely new determination.

title: Dissolution Grip
description: The prolific Kenyan-born, Berlin-based electronic musician departs from his typical use of field recordings, but environmental sound still makes its mark on his immersive, long-form explorations.

title: Arepa Mixtape
description: The Miami producer and vocalist’s expertly curated, shamelessly horny new mixtape revels in reggaeton’s queer and femme club underground.

title: Shone a Rainbow Light On
description: Multi-instrumentalists Nathan Bowles, Jaime Fennelly, and Joe Westerlund combine forces on textured, stormy folk compositions that encourage deeper listening.

title: We Buy Diabetic Test Strips
description: The duo of Elucid and billy woods delivers a moody, unsettling, sharply observed album balancing moments of self-reflection with vivid snapshots of societal dysfunction.

title: No Fixed Point in Space
description: Featuring players from Spiritualized and the Necks, the hushed third album from Jack Cooper’s chamber-improv ensemble slots into a lineage of exploratory groups fusing folk, psych, and post-rock.

title: Nothing Lasts Forever
description: The Scottish power-pop band keeps things light on an album distinguished by subtle touches and twilight grooves.

title: What Is My Capacity to Love? EP
description: The Water From Your Eyes vocalist’s new solo EP is a collection of charming, heartfelt bedroom pop songs that deserve to be more fully realized.

title: Again
description: Daniel Lopatin returns with a nostalgic jam session full of proggy synth passages and ’90s alt-rock touches. It leaves a lot to admire but a little less to think about.

title: Falling or Flying
description: The UK singer’s earthy, sumptuous new album explores her ambivalent relationship to fame. It soars when it lets loose.

title: Rustin’ in the Rain
description: The Kentucky songwriter surveys the past, present, and future of country music on a thoughtful new record with deep roots.

title: Trifecta 3: the Finale
description: On the final installment of their Trifecta series, the Detroit rap trio delivers quotable after quotable. It’s cocksure and playful, like a high school lunchroom cipher.

title: The Breakthrough
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a blockbuster R&B comeback record from 2005, an unofficial marker of a more self-actualized Mary J. Blige.

title: Who’s Next : Life House (Super Deluxe)
description: An exhaustively comprehensive 11-disc box set explores a defining work by the classic rock band alongside the ambitious, shelved concept album that would become Pete Townshend's white whale.

title: Isn’t It Now?
description: On what feels like a companion to Time Skiffs, Animal Collective explore some surprisingly traditional psych-rock modes, but without abandoning their essential trickster spirit.

title: Sit Down for Dinner
description: On their first album in nearly a decade, and following a wave of viral resurgence, the NYC avant-rock vets return with their warmest, most welcoming music yet.

title: Heaven
description: The SAULT vocalist’s new album explores faith and self-love through warm, lustrous neo-soul.

title: Signs
description: The Chicago trio excels in precisely detailed ambient dub with just the right amount of reverence for turn-of-the-millennium avant-garde electronic music.

title: Cousin
description: With help from producer Cate Le Bon, the Chicago band’s 13th album flickers to life on several songs that hint at the controlled chaos of their bygone experimental era.

title: Faith Is a Rock
description: The New York rappers team up with the legendary producer for their first full-length collaboration. Over his thick, sample-heavy beats, MIKE and Wiki brandish a natural chemistry that feels like it’s existed for decades.

title: Chai
description: The Japanese quartet evolve their perspective and sound, exploring the decadent grooves of city pop as they contend with growing up.

title: Strange Disciple
description: The Brooklyn synth-pop trio expands its signature sound on its surprisingly idiosyncratic third album.

title: Gentle Confrontation
description: On her third album for Hyperdub, the UK experimental musician uses chaotic arrangements and glitchy drums to express knotty, difficult-to-name emotions.

title: The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess
description: The pop singer’s full-length debut is a bold and uproarious introduction, buoyed by sturdy songcraft and steely indifference to good taste.

title: Powders
description: The experimental musician’s radiant new album explores love’s rapture within the confines of more traditional pop structures.

title: Atlas
description: The experimental artist’s fifth solo album is among her best, a beautiful collection of minimalist ambient compositions in which no line extends for long without dissolving into an inky blot.

title: Flying Wig
description: The Venezuelan singer-songwriter’s 11th album tackles grief and melancholia with the kind of endearing eccentricity only he can.

title: La Planète Sauvage (Expanded Original Soundtrack)
description: This score to the 1973 sci-fi film was sampled by generations of hip-hop luminaries. Reissued for its 50th anniversary, it remains a dazzlingly avant-garde fusion of styles and moods.

title: Scarlet
description: In proving herself as a rapper, Doja Cat offers up an uneven album that is accomplished but gets bogged down in reactive and repetitive songs.

title: Postcards From Italia EP
description: Drawing on the sounds of ’90s Eurodance and classic rock’n’roll, these six songs are light, lush, and streaked with melancholy.

title: V
description: The Chilean band journeys through icy, alien frontiers on their mesmerizing new album.

title: Karaoke Night EP
description: On her new EP, Sophie Allison rents out a room just for herself, singing covers of Taylor Swift, Pavement, Sheryl Crow, and more.

title: One Night Stand! Live at the Harlem Square Club, 1963
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a monumental artifact of soul—one of the best live albums of all time, from the singer who wrote the 20th century’s defining civil rights anthem.

title: Tim (Let It Bleed Edition)
description: This deluxe reissue is the holy grail that fans of Tim have dreamt of: a new mix that instantly becomes the best and most definitive album in the Replacements’ catalog.

title: softscars
description: On their riveting new album, the 25-year-old singer-songwriter-producer shifts from future-shocked electronic pop to a super-sized emotional bloodletting steeped in ’90s alternative.

title: World of Hassle
description: On his first album under his own name, the artist behind Neon Indian returns with the funniest and most musically accomplished songs of his career.

title: Sorry I Haven’t Called
description: Laetitia Tamko’s bright, dewy electro-pop album depicts growing up with candor and levity.

title: Nothing’s Gonna Stand in My Way Again
description: The alt-country songwriter’s sixth album sits at the eye of the storm, matching a softer, more measured sound with a wryly humorous look at existential turmoil.

title: Tension
description: Kylie Minogue’s most relaxed album in years is a compendium of all the sounds she’s best known for: confectionary synth-pop, breezy Euro house, and propulsive EDM.

title: DIAMONDS
description: Lil Peep and iLoveMakonnen’s collaborative album reflects both the kinship they share as pop outsiders and queer rappers. It’s the rare posthumous rap album that actually honors an artist’s legacy.

title: Pretty Girls Love Slizzy
description: The Bronx rapper’s bluntness and playful ear for beats gives his sex-obsessed songs the nonchalance of a one-night stand.

title: Stone
description: For the first time ever, the Southern metal expats return with the same lineup as their previous album. A little outside input could’ve gone a long way.

title: Dreams of a Dancefloor EP
description: The New Hampshire DJ folds multiple influences—trance, drum’n’bass, breaks, acid, deep house—into shape-shifting tracks that mimic the flow of an ecstatic night of dancing.

title: Destiny
description: The pseudonymous London producer’s new album is a radiant, elastic, nearly four-hour celebration of the transportive possibilities of dance music.

title: The Beach Album
description: The New York nightlife veteran’s new album chronicles pandemic survival in the city and the difficult joy that’s followed.

title: The Enduring Spirit
description: The Toronto death metal band returns with its best album yet: an ambitious and deeply human suite that touches the sublime.

title: Supernova
description: The Spanish artist’s debut cuts and pastes from R&B, hip-hop, reggaeton, and flamenco. It’s bizarre and incongruous—but oddly satisfying.

title: Protect Your Light
description: The free jazz collective takes a more patient and self-reflective approach to politics on their new album.

title: Messages to God
description: With flutes and instrumental flair, the New Zealand singer-songwriter adds restless drama to her steadfast, plainspoken reflections on pain and personal growth.

title: Laugh Track
description: The National’s second album of 2023 extends its predecessor’s subdued mood and reclusive purview.

title: Born for Greatness
description: The reggae veteran’s new studio album doesn’t match the magic of his legacy. But when he’s not exploring grandiose thematic statements, he sounds as confident and impressive as ever.

title: Smartwoods
description: In diaphanous compositions like color field paintings, this full-band ambient album conveys relaxation, whimsy, and a vague sense of dread.

title: All Around You
description: The Singaporean band’s new album showcases a punchier indie rock sound and reinvigorated perspective on the environment.

title: Time (The Revelator)
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past. Today we revisit Gillian Welch and Dave Rawlings’ third album, an Americana masterpiece whose prophecies reverberate through modern folk and indie rock.

title: Pharoah
description: This 1977 album was obscure in its day, but it spawned a fervent cult among fans of spiritual jazz, for good reason: The no-frills recording captures a feeling of unearthly magic.

title: The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We
description: After contemplating retirement, Mitski returns with a new album that’s warmer, quieter, and more organic-sounding. For the first time in a while, she sounds like she has space to breathe.

title: Black Rainbows
description: The English singer-songwriter takes a scuzzy, loud, and political left turn on her gutsy fourth album. It sounds like a departure but feels like a renaissance.

title: 66689 Blvd Prequel
description: The Cleveland rapper’s quietly intense new album is fueled by the constant churn of unrelenting self-examination, but that heaviness is offset by his nimble, natural flow.

title: Bird Machine
description: In the year before he died, Mark Linkous hit the studio with Steve Albini. Fourteen years later, those unreleased sessions reveal a bittersweet cocktail of beauty and torment.

title: BB/ANG3L
description: At just seven songs, Tinashe’s newest album is as stylish and focused as a runway walk.

title: Drift
description: Departing from his typically electronic palette, the UK musician’s new album plunges into a maze of contradictory influences drawn from dub, post-punk, and alt rock.

title: CITTA’ ’93
description: Reissued by Temporal Drift, this recording of the mysterious Japanese psych-rock band’s loud, legendary 1993 set at Club Citta’ is the best they’ve ever sounded.

title: Hit Parade
description: The Irish artist’s full-length collaboration with DJ Koze is a showcase of everything impressive about the musician sapped of the excitement that has historically made her work feel so vital.

title: How Do You Sleep at Night?
description: On his debut, the suddenly inescapable singer goes looking for a mashup of Texas rap, pop-punk, and R&B original enough to match his fashion sense.

title: Teghnojoyg
description: Foregrounding sensory disorientation, clashing keys, and confounding meters, the Brazilian musician’s sample-based music investigates the warping effects of cultural and political memory.

title: Sidharth
description: An Indian film-music superstar raised on rap and indie, the 33-year-old singer taps Bon Iver’s Justin Vernon and producer Ryan Olson in the attempt to reconcile his transnational influences.

title: Mid Air
description: Hearkening back to her queer nightlife days, the xx singer and guitarist pays homage to the euphoric dance-pop of the 1990s and 2000s.

title: Talàn
description: In his sparse, instrumental style, the Polish guitarist channels centuries of cultural exchange. His new album is slow and reverent, as if suspended in a different measurement of time.

title: Bewitched
description: TikTok’s favorite neoclassical jazz singer gives contemporary heartache a misty, out-of-time quality.

title: Brand New Soul
description: Justice Tripp has a blast channeling the affirming and aggressive spirit of Southern California, even if it sounds a little stuck between stations.

title: GUTS
description: The pop star rocks out on her biting, charismatic second album, turning the ritual humiliations of girlhood into dazzling, over-the-top spectacles.

title: Come With Fierce Grace
description: Drawn from the same sessions as 2022’s Gold, the UK jazz poet and saxophonist’s new album counters that record’s opulence with a spare, percussive sound.

title: Techxodus
description: Considering the gap between techno’s roots and its globalized, commercialized present, the writer, curator, and musician DeForrest Brown, Jr., posits alternate futures for the genre.

title: Color Me Country
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a groundbreaking 1970 album, a lovely but tragic record led by a pioneering force in country music.

title: Music for KIDS
description: A new compendium of music Lou Barlow and John Davis created for the 1995 cult film Kids brings a piece of prescient indie rock experimentation—and sleeper hit “Natural One”—to streaming in full.

title: Playing Robots Into Heaven
description: The former dubstep balladeer and sometime pop super-producer returns to his electronic roots, working cut-up vocal samples into leftfield dancefloor material.

title: The King
description: Channeling Old Testament themes of righteous fury and justice, the indie-folk singer embraces a pared-back sound that only amplifies the drama.

title: i’m so lucky EP
description: After an intra-band breakup, the Philly noise experimentalists return with a brief, focused EP that clears away some of their elaborate studio trickery.

title: Braintrust of Fiends and Werewolves
description: On their first duo recording together, the veteran guitar improvisers find a shared language in slanted melodies and clouds of dissonance.

title: everything is alive
description: Since forming over three decades ago, the UK shoegaze band’s fifth album is the first to shoulder the weight of those years. The music is wispier, more skeletal, attuned to and aware of fading glories.

title: Through the Window
description: The Massachusetts songwriter’s ragged, tormented indie rock puts a surreal spin on the grim realities of life.

title: E3
description: The Indiana artist’s debut album builds on his hyperpop, digicore, and rage rap roots, but positions him as a pop star in his own right.

title: Careful!
description: On its third album, the Chicago band continues to refine its strain of post-punk revivalism, trotting out familiar tropes while subtly pushing at the boundaries of its sound.

title: trip9love…???
description: Tirzah and Mica Levi bore deeper into their strange and unique style of music. This time it is even more cramped and claustrophobic, a minefield of fitful rhythms and rain-filled craters.

title: The Lamb as Effigy or Three Hundred and Fifty XOXOXOS for a Spark Union With My Darling Divine
description: Fueled by frontman Alexander Kent’s raging declamations, the Los Angeles band’s sprawling, 96-minute album is an incendiary fusion of noise, post-punk, metal, prog, and drone.

title: Bad News
description: The California-based producer crew and indie rap icon’s first full-length collaboration isn’t revelatory, but it does show off their gifts as classicists.

title: HELLMODE
description: Working in a professional recording studio, the DIY lifer goes big by going small. It’s the prettiest album he’s ever made—but it still gets you riled up.

title: Rabbit Rabbit
description: On its fourth album, the Philadelphia band lets it rip behind Sadie Dupuis’ knotty, mischievous songwriting.

title: Another Triumph of Ghetto Engineering
description: Armed with advice for the next generation and lots of thank-you notes, Open Mike Eagle’s funny and reflective ninth album seeks a sense of closure within his discography.

title: Siamese Dream
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the alternative titans’ 1993 album, where Billy Corgan discovered the larger-than-life sound that would reshape rock for decades to come.

title: Sumday Twunny
description: Packaged with demos, outtakes, and a new remaster, this 20th anniversary box set presents the California indie band’s wide-open third album as a prescient meditation on the need to escape.

title: The Window
description: The Chicago quartet swings big on a Chris Walla-produced album that brings unexpected grandeur to their modest, rootsy indie rock. It sounds like a breakthrough.

title: Does It Look Like I’m Here? (Expanded Remaster)
description: With seven additional tracks and a Heba Kadry remaster, the ambient synth experimentalists’ landmark album is even more transportive than it was in 2010.

title: Private Recordings, August 1970
description: Essential for superfans, this collection of Sylvester’s earliest known recordings illuminates how he would become a disco superstar.

title: Zach Bryan
description: The rising country star from Oklahoma works with a traditionalist’s appreciation for songwriting and the intense, earnest emotion of heartland rock.

title: Hold Your Horse Is (Deluxe Reissue)
description: The Sacramento duo’s 2002 debut album might be the platonic ideal of math rock, but its real joy lies in the way it seems to escape the bounds of logic altogether.

title: Unfixed EP
description: After challenging himself to make music without kick drums, the Berlin-based producer reverses course on an innovative, high-contrast new EP.

title: I Told Them...
description: Burna Boy’s fifth album takes in the view from the top, fusing his adventurous pan-African pop with memories of 1990s hip-hop, advice from Virgil Abloh, and a little victory-lap stunting.

title: Alive People
description: Recorded in front of a live audience, the latest from the Brattleboro songwriter is a meditative, idiosyncratic set about the impermanence of all things.

title: Soul Assassins 3: Death Valley
description: The latest tape in the West Coast producer’s series is understated, but reveals how good he is at letting genre artists approach the best versions of themselves.

title: VOIR DIRE
description: The surprise album from an elite rapper-producer combo is lean and beautifully crafted. Both make excellent use of each other’s light and shadow.

title: YO NO ERA ASÍ PERO DE AHORA EN ADELANTE, SÍ
description: The Dominican producer takes a mischievous, electro-punk approach to genre fusions, mashing up the club, the rave, and the mosh pit.

title: Intercepted Message
description: From synth pop to new wave to disco, the shapeshifting rock band goes all in on its keyboard album.

title: Fly or Die Fly or Die Fly or Die ((world war))
description: The late trumpeter’s third and final album opens dazzling new paths in her work. It’s a heartbreaking glimpse of where she might have gone next, but more importantly, it’s a joy to hear.

title: Bite
description: On its first album in six years, the Austin group dreams up an elaborate fictional universe and delivers it with swaggering glam-rock panache.

title: RESET! EP
description: On a short and sprightly EP, the up-and-coming Oakland rapper and producer makes strides in both fields.

title: An Object in Motion
description: Written in the remote coastal town of Yachats, Oregon, the duo’s latest EP refashions its gloomy guitar pop as ecstatic shoegaze, complete with a cameo from Slowdive’s Rachel Goswell.

title: Jaguar II
description: The decorated pop songwriter arrives in the spotlight with a full-length debut whose plush R&B and live-band arrangements strike a tone that’s classic, sexy, and understated.

title: Perfect Saviors
description: The most mysterious group in hardcore pull back the curtain to reveal: a rock band. If their new album sounds like something you’d hear on alt radio, that’s the point.

title: Death Is Nothing to Us
description: On its third LP, the Boston post-hardcore band completes a thematic trilogy about grief, depression, and the determination to move forward in the face of loss.

title: Unreal Unearth
description: The Irish balladeer’s third album is a mishmash of mythology and past-date pop that leaves him sounding like an interloper.

title: Domino
description: Blue Broderick’s new power pop record sets her gentle thoughts against the most immediate rock Diners has ever attempted.

title: Jump for Joy
description: On a loosely conceptual project, the singer-songwriter finds his groove in smooth, soft-rock sounds and adolescent optimism.

title: SPELLLING & the Mystery School
description: Chrystia Cabral gives her old highlights new studio arrangements, lending them the immediacy and clarity of live versions.

title: El Toro 2
description: A too-cautious sequel to the Louisville rapper’s breakthrough mixtape dangles fascinating production experiments but winds up returning to the script.

title: Rocket Power
description: On his first solo album since the death of Takeoff, the Migos rapper takes an uncharacteristically vulnerable approach, looking to his past successes and pushing tentatively forward.

title: Echo the Diamond
description: On her third album, the Brooklyn musician scraps the synths and elaborate arrangements of her last LP, opting for a stripped-down combo and songs written as fast as the rush of feelings that inspired them.

title: ghetto cupid
description: The Florida teen rapper’s ambitious new project pulls together disparate strands, from plugg to shoegaze and emo balladry. It’s messy, but it works more often than not.

title: Haunted Mountain
description: The fullest solo album yet from the Big Thief guitarist is an earnest ode to getting lost.

title: Marquis
description: The underground Atlanta rap star teams with DJ Marc B, who backs his signature bouncy flows and silly punchlines with gleaming, thudding beats.

title: Ontological Mysterium
description: The Philadelphia death metal quartet has a blast on its fifth album, veering between styles with uninhibited energy and virtuosic musicianship.

title: Epoch
description: An elaborate new box set explores the evolution of Justin Vernon’s early band through pivotal live sets, avant-Americana studio experiments, and a formative solo album.

title: phantasea pharm EP
description: The New York City quartet’s 4AD debut is an entrée to a world of scuzzy, lewd, electro-punk camp.

title: ELECTRIC EP
description: The PC Music producer’s first EP in eight years is a loving paean to the earnest euphoria of 2010s EDM.

title: Pontiac
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the eclectic Texan’s 1987 album, a terrific showcase of his subversive and idiosyncratic country style.

artist: Panda Bear / Sonic Boom / Adrian Sherwood
title: Reset in Dub
description: Much as he did on last year’s remix of Spoon’s Lucifer on the Sofa, the storied dub producer uncovers a universe of detail lurking in the folds of the duo’s 2022 album Reset.

title: World Music Radio
description: The jazz multi-instrumentalist wants to unite the world in song. But his new album collapses the wide-ranging possibilities of global music into something for everyone and no one.

title: Resolve
description: Assisted by Oren Ambarchi, Konrad Sprenger, and Joachim Schütz, the iconoclastic instrument builder lays down a hypnotic set of minimalist, microtonal guitar music.

title: You’re the One
description: On her first album of all original songs, the folk polyglot seeks livelier rhythms and vocal styles infused with jazz, country, and zydeco.

title: Mr. Greg & Cass McCombs Sing and Play New Folk Songs for Children
description: On a set of originals for the hallowed Folkways label, the California singer-songwriter and his pal, a Bay Area preschool teacher, know when to honor the past and when to break from it.

title: Lord of the Shithouse
description: Spirit of the Beehive members Zack Schwartz and Corey Wichlin shift styles on a collection of warped, dissonant pop with hairpin turns and an underlying unease.

title: APPETIZER
description: Shielding vulnerability beneath layers of cranked-up bass, the Brooklyn rapper and singer’s new tape is music for baddies who keep in touch with their feelings.

title: Chrome Dreams
description: One of Neil Young’s most widely bootlegged lost albums from the ’70s gets an official release. As familiar as the material may be, its ragged, magical charm remains greater than the sum of its parts.

title: Defiant Presents: Jiggy in Jersey (ft. MCVertt)
description: The Newark rapper, Newark producer, and Bronx drill rapper join forces for a 27-track mixtape that fires on all cylinders.

title: living in memory of something sweet
description: Steeped in a mixture of indie rock, shoegaze, emo, and ambient, the L.A.-based musician’s debut album is an ambitious attempt to make something new out of familiar materials.

title: The Death of Randy Fitzsimmons
description: On their first album in over a decade, the Swedish garage-rock mainstays refuse to evolve or age—they are here for a good time and absolutely nothing else.

title: Chthonic
description: An ominous blend of drones and field recordings, the two musicians’ debut collaboration plays out like a long-distance conversation about geologic time.

title: Deliverance
description: The Fuck Buttons co-founder fills his latest solo album with familiar, quavering synth-pop, less concerned with exploring feelings than deeply expressing what he’s feeling.

title: Keeping Secrets Will Destroy You
description: On his first solo album in four years, Will Oldham dispenses the wisdom of his life and the anxiety of his present into some of his most intimate and compelling musical settings.

title: Final Boss
description: The Chicago rapper-producer’s new album blankets hedonistic flexes in a layer of frost.

title: Crazy Trip EP
description: The Oakland producer finds a middle ground between her atmospheric tendencies and her more percussive productions, pairing raw, footwork-inspired drum loops with ethereal synths.

title: Solo Concerts: Bremen/Lausanne
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a career-defining jazz masterpiece, collecting two hours of improvised solo performances from the piano virtuoso.

title: Live in Brooklyn 2011
description: Dissolving three decades of music into a 17-song noise opera, this pivotal live album captures a peerless set from a band who knew its days were numbered.

title: Sundial
description: Noname’s first album in five years is a cool and masterful interrogation of the culture. She’s taking everyone’s name—including her own.

title: Lonestar Luchador
description: The Texas rapper's new album is a brightly colored spectacle that showcases all the Lone Star state has to offer.

title: Porches
description: The California rapper is a nimble and versatile vocalist with an impressionistic, occasionally stilted writing style. Is it enough to make him TDE’s next big star?

title: End of World
description: John Lydon’s public persona remains as contrarian as ever. But on PiL’s first album in eight years, his voice remains captivating—and, occasionally, surprisingly moving.

title: RUAB
description: Touring the gritty underbelly of Ahmedabad, India to the sounds of swaggering synth and G-funk, the 25-year-old rapper’s debut makes an auteur’s plea for authenticity in a transactional world.

title: murmuring chasms of nostalgia
description: With whispery beats and spectral vocals, erstwhile dubstep DJ Jon Gooch seeks a quieter, more intimate sound.

title: Floating Into the Night
description: For three decades, this 1989 album has remained one of dream pop’s chief benchmarks. While these songs will be forever associated with David Lynch’s work, the album stands proudly on its own.

title: And Southern Star
description: On a stirring full-band album, the classically trained harpist lets her instrument become an integral part of her twangy, easygoing rock’n’roll sound.

title: The Sweat of Earth
description: The imposing, experimental 18-minute piece from the Tehran-based composer draws upon noise, drone, musique concrète, and the poetry of Xavier Villarrutia.

title: A New Reality Mind
description: The Oakland singer-songwriter looks to experimental synth and new age music on her self-produced fourth LP, a serene and reflective take on the breakup album.

title: They Live in My Head
description: The legendary no wave band honors late drummer Dee Pop on a mournful album of sludgy post-punk.

title: A Pocket Full of Rain
description: A new reissue of the Emeralds guitarist’s 2009 album captures his style in its infancy. Careful songcraft would come later; these wide-eyed jams are cosmic and sprawling.

title: The Holey Bible
description: Philadelphia singer-songwriter Francie Medosch’s band combines the weepy twang of old-school country with the cozy intimacy of DIY rock.

title: Not a Dream but a Controlled Explosion
description: The UK rapper-producer’s new album is an indelible rush of free-associative rhymes, ghostly textures, and shapeshifting vocals.

title: Soft Landing
description: Welsh songwriter Polly Mackey expands her bedroom-pop sound on her intimate and adventurous second album.

title: The Dark Side of the Moon
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit one of the biggest albums of all time: its origins, its impact, and why it remains a permanent fixture in the rock canon.

title: Rich
description: The Queens rapper’s latest album, produced in full by Mono En Stereo, offers few surprises but features plenty of charmingly diaristic, relatable songs that contrast sharply with mainstream rap.

title: INFINITY CLUB
description: The Toronto musician produces like a DJ: blending genres, playing fast and loose with BPM, and bringing club music’s promise of endless possibility to life.

title: the infinite spine
description: On her debut, the British-French experimentalist reckons with the body and the spirit in compositions so bright and ornate they feel like an inverted version of goth-pop.

title: Prestige
description: Inspired by the FX drama Pose and the flush of new love, the London indie trio uses its third album to cosplay as the house band of a fantasy discotheque.

title: At Royal Albert Hall
description: Billed as his final album, this 2016 live set by the late songwriter is a thoughtful and intimate survey of his vast catalog.

title: Natural Disaster
description: On her debut solo album, the Best Coast leader draws inspiration from classic country and glossy pop-rock. It’s the brightest her music has ever sounded but the songwriting doesn’t rise to the occasion.

title: Euphoric
description: The UK singer-producer teams up with Rostam for a collection of chilled-out electro-pop that plays it a little too safe.

title: Somewhere Down Below
description: The versatile Pittsburgh quartet polishes their scrappy, shoegaze-inspired indie rock on an album studded with references to local favorites and ’90s classics.

title: The Loveliest Time
description: Once again Carly Rae Jepsen’s B-sides are just as good if not better than her A-sides.

title: Eyeroll
description: The Berlin-based DJ’s new album relies on rototom drums and the interplay of diverse guests to build exhilarating, dynamic soundscapes.

title: Neo Seven
description: The experimental musician continues their path of dematerialization on a mostly placid set characterized by warm synths, steady tremolo pulses, and an air of unease.

title: Blackbox Life Recorder 21f / In a Room7 F760 EP
description: There’s more than meets the eye on Richard D. James’ first new EP in five years, a slim collection of percussive bruisers with a woozy, inscrutable mood.

title: Evenings at the Village Gate: John Coltrane With Eric Dolphy
description: A previously unknown recording, discovered by chance in 2017, captures the saxophonist testing the limits of his sound in the summer of 1961. It’s a snapshot of a pivotal moment in jazz’s evolution.

title: AUSTIN
description: With a focus on guitar-centric pop-rock, Posty’s latest record is a passion project that feels overstuffed and undercooked.

title: UTOPIA
description: In an attempt to give the world a true blockbuster rap album, the Houston rapper delivers a shiny, empty spectacle loaded with pop superstars who rarely make an impact.

title: Love Hallucination
description: Jessy Lanza leans into low-lit club pop (and picks up a saxophone) on an album whose breezy mood feels inspired by her new home of Los Angeles.

title: Ooh Rap I Ya
description: On the vaporwave producer and label boss’ new album, smeary synths and boyband-inspired vocals feel less like a biting subversion of nostalgia than a straight-up “remember when.”

title: The Last Remaining Light
description: The Leeds-based musician crafts a bittersweet and atmospheric record whose songs find serenity in stillness.

title: XO
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Elliott Smith’s big 1998 album, both a transformational landmark and a logical next step for the restless composer.

title: Joni Mitchell at Newport
description: The singer’s first full concert in 22 years was a joyous surprise, a moment of wonder. Led by Brandi Carlile, the live recording of the star-studded fête crowds Joni out.

title: I Am Not There Anymore
description: Marked by newfound sonic adventurousness and evocative dream-logic lyrics, the long-running UK band’s new double album is a bold quest into the vast unknown.

title: Magic 2
description: Nas and Hit-Boy cook up another collaboration, a low-stakes mid-career rap album to show that one of the genre’s icons is still in decent fighting shape.

title: The Ones Ahead
description: The Canadian composer’s first new material since the 2016 rediscovery of his 1986 LP Keyboard Fantasies is a joyous, hope-filled showcase of his singular voice and healing vision.

title: New Future City Radio
description: Cross-cutting sample collages, beat tracks, and free improv with wryly surrealist DJ banter, the Chicago musicians’ fictional mixtape celebrates the revolutionary promise of pirate radio.

title: PANICO NO SUBMUNDO
description: The São Paulo producer pushes Brazilian funk to horrorcore extremes, colliding Lil Uzi Vert and Halloween samples into a dizzying metallic symphony.

title: Outside Problems
description: An improvisatory companion to 2022’s Inside Problems, Andrew Bird’s newest instrumental album channels the warmth of its Ojai, California setting.

title: War on Drugs 2
description: On the Detroit rapper’s newest tape, lean and mean stories from the drug game take shape against ominous beats and inspired references.

title: You’ve Got to Learn (Live)
description: Recorded live at the 1966 Newport Jazz Festival, this brief but incendiary set includes a famous rendition of “Mississippi Goddam” tucked inside a handful of potent standards.

title: Infinite Psychic Depths
description: On an ambitious new album, the Pennsylvania death metal band moves in nimble, surprising directions while honing its psychedelically brutal sound.

title: Love in a Vicious Way
description: The Toronto band’s debut album brightly blurs the line between ’60s psych pop and ’90s dream pop, but its lyrical preoccupations are much darker in tone.

title: Infirmary / Unknown​ ​Summer EP
description: The Hyperdub boss and his reclusive label-mate team up on a split single that highlights their differences, contrasting Kode9’s restless rhythmic energy with Burial’s contented melancholy.

title: Pure Music
description: On an adventurous new album, the shapeshifting indie-rock band blends rave influences with larger-than-life hooks for some of its sharpest songwriting to date.

title: Virtuoso
description: On his new album, the Chicago rapper known for his muted, monklike delivery struggles to realize his full potential, even when assisted by Harry Fraud’s lush instrumentals.

title: Get Up EP
description: The girl-group’s brisk, club-inflected pop songs cement them as one of the most interesting K-pop acts working today.

title: Presenting Dionne Warwick
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the legendary singer’s 1963 debut, whose career-making collaborations with Burt Bacharach and Hal David transformed pop music into something more symphonic, boundless, and idiosyncratic.

title: Journey to the Moon and Beyond
description: Following reissues of Mother Earth’s Plantasia and other cult classics, a new anthology of the Moog pioneer’s work revolves around his groundbreaking soundtrack to the 1969 moon landing.

title: Barbie the Album
description: Curated by Mark Ronson, the pop-heavy soundtrack to the blockbuster doll movie shrivels outside of the magical world of Barbieland.

title: Hands That Bind (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: The experimental producer and composer’s score for the prairie gothic film is luminous, faintly menacing, and clouded with uncertainty.

title: The Ballad of Darren
description: The Britpop icons contemplate middle-age turbulence and inertia on a meticulously polished reunion album.

title: Everyone Else Is a Stranger
description: Steeped in multiple layers of nostalgia, the Norwegian musician’s sixth album spins his habitual vintage space disco into an enveloping fusion of dewy uplift and nocturnal danger.

title: Super Snõõper
description: The Nashville egg punks’ debut is a short, speedy trip to the world of “Devo-core.” Bring your giant puppets.

title: Everybody Good?
description: On his first new album since 2018, the longtime Detroit beatmaker unites rap, soul, funk, rock, and ghettotech with meticulous craftsmanship and a wonky-yet-smooth touch.

title: Maybe It’s Me…
description: With little to talk about aside from his girlfriend Halle Bailey, the YouTuber-turned-artist delivers an album that treats rap like just another piece of content.

title: Alchemy
description: The A-list dance-pop duo returns to the club on a new record that’s fresher and more fun than the brothers have sounded in ages.

title: Western Cum
description: The Wand frontman’s third solo album offers a funhouse-mirror take on classic rock, combining surreal lyrical vignettes and laid-back delivery with incendiary guitar shredding.

title: Eye on the Bat
description: Writing with painful exactitude, El Kempner crafts a vividly rendered breakup album that’s always threatening to explode.

title: i care so much that i dont care at all
description: The 18-year-old singer-songwriter moves away from hyperpop and digicore on his debut album, sharpening his pop instincts as he unpacks the chaotic intensity of teenage emotions.

title: Beautiful and Brutal Yard
description: The London rapper’s third album extends his carnal and philosophical investigation of masculinity against lush, robust beats that evoke a distinctly Black British take on G-funk.

title: When Horses Would Run
description: Surf-rock riffs, oddball humor, and warped Americana storytelling define the Austin band’s raucous debut.

title: Crying Crystals
description: With inventive storytelling and eclectic beats, the Toronto-based rapper constructs a breakup album that sucks everyone into the drama.

title: Little Songs
description: The Canadian country singer immerses himself in a bygone era on this spacious and dynamic full-band set.

title: Bringing Down the Horse
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a ’90s pop-rock mainstay, a warm and rootsy record where Jakob Dylan came to terms with being his father’s son.

title: PLAYA SATURNO
description: The Puerto Rican hitmaker attempts to replicate the magic of his celestial 2022 album in this summery spinoff but winds up lost in space.

title: Jelly Road
description: The singer-songwriter-superproducer teams with the Vermont jazz musician Chris Weisman for an invigorating collaborative album that’s whimsical and wistful in surprising ways.

title: Natural Wonder Beauty Concept
description: On their first album together, ambient singer-songwriter Ana Roxanne and leftfield producer DJ Python find common cause in slow-motion grooves and downbeat electronic pop.

title: Crowd Can Talk / Dressed in Trenches
description: On a pair of EPs, the young Chicago band captures the kinetic energy of its live show, walking a thrilling tightrope between abrasion and melody.

title: Rain Before Seven...
description: The Penguin Cafe Orchestra successors’ fifth album is a tribute to pandemic perseverance that’s long on uplifting strings but short on experimentation.

title: I Inside the Old Year Dying
description: In songs adapted from her book-length poem Orlam, the British singer-songwriter crafts a hallucinatory dreamworld out of folk instruments, primitive electronics, and warped field recordings.

title: Connection
description: The New York guitarist and his longtime collaborators spend a rollicking, leisurely hour imagining rock music’s role in a world more invested in social justice than commerce.

title: I Can’t Help It
description: On her new album, the Texas rapper ditches ready-made strip-club anthems for no-hook freestyles that flaunt her verbal dexterity.

title: Speak Now (Taylor’s Version)
description: Taylor Swift’s catalog re-recording campaign continues with a thoughtful version of 2010’s Speak Now that tempers teen angst with the ageless quality of lullabies and folk songs.

title: Mondo Tempo
description: The Canadian duo takes a chill, fuzzy-headed left turn but retains the bleak imagery and nuanced production of its best work.

title: I’ve Really Never Been Better
description: From knotty wordplay to hip-hop in-jokes only a head would attempt, the North Carolina rapper’s latest mixtape provides much to savor.

title: Learning in Public EP
description: Blending fuzzy guitars and 2-step beats, the UK singer’s richly textured DIY pop looks to Britpop and garage, Frank Ocean and Drake.

title: The Greater Wings
description: Completed after the death of her producer, collaborator, and close friend, the New York singer-songwriter’s album envisions mourning as a form of meditative practice and constant renewal.

title: Data
description: The Puerto Rican superproducer’s debut LP is a wellspring of new ideas for reggaeton. Even when the concepts don’t fully connect, he remains one of the genre’s most forward-thinking architects.

title: Slugs of Love
description: The Swedish quartet’s seventh album glows with carefree, mosaic pop arrangements. They sound looser and freer than ever.

title: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross
description: After 13 years, Anohni gets the band back together for a soulful and intense record that provides a safe place to grieve nothing less than the destruction of the planet.

title: Swells
description: The Brighton producer works with a light touch, resulting in subtle, pliant songs that evolve in sneaky ways.

title: Salesforce
description: Unlike the commercial soundtrack music she writes in her day job, the Los Angeles producer’s solo work is an over-the-top onslaught of electronic noise and withering anti-capitalist sarcasm.

artist: Dolly Parton / Linda Ronstadt / Emmylou Harris
title: Trio
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a historic collaboration that braided three unique histories of American music into a timeless whole.

title: Pink Tape
description: The Philadelphia rapper delivers a bloated and messy new album, struggling to live up to their reputation for imaginative, genre-blending adventures.

title: Stories From a Rock n Roll Heart
description: The masterful singer-songwriter offers her lightest, most earthbound record in years, finding newfound inspiration in the sweetly silly sound of barroom rock’n’roll.

title: If We Stayed Alive
description: Two decades after the Minneapolis alt-rock also-rans called it quits, lead singer Ryan Olcott resurrects the project, reworking abandoned demos into contemporary bedroom pop with a vintage cast.

title: Good Living Is Coming for You
description: The DIY fixtures behind Silkies, Dee-Parts, and Mini Dresses turn their attention to scuzzy, no-fi ’80s punk overflowing with pop hooks.

title: The Idol: Music From the HBO Original Series
description: The collected songs from the infamous show would have been better served as a random Weeknd posse album meant to launch the promising minor pop career of Lily-Rose Depp.

title: Flying High EP
description: The star beatmaker reunites with past collaborators like Earl Sweatshirt, billy woods, and Larry June on a breezy new EP.

title: Blowout
description: The latest album from this L.A. session player to the stars reveals him to be a fascinatingly expressive keyboardist who doesn’t take himself too seriously.

title: Fish Don’t Climb Trees
description: The St. Louis rapper’s new album showcases a fly confidence that the thin writing can’t always match.

title: Ganger
description: After years of anticipation, the idiosyncratic Detroit rapper returns with an unpredictable new album full of vocal quirks and unlikely punchlines.

title: The Happiest Times I Ever Ignored
description: The eccentric 29-year-old guitarist, artist, model, and former city council candidate’s new solo guitar album showcases his studious and inventive approach to the genre.

title: Dream Box
description: The 68-year-old guitar virtuoso compiled this understated set of solo recordings from a forgotten folder during downtime on tour. These casual experiments offer a fascinating peek into his creative mind.

title: Glockoma 2 (Deluxe)
description: Now expanded in a deluxe edition, the Memphis rapper’s blues-inflected third album keeps a tight focus while alluding to the painful loss of mentor Young Dolph.

title: Spooky
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we look back at the UK band’s 1992 debut, a deceptively hazy pop record that showcases the complementary songwriting of Emma Anderson and Miki Berenyi.

title: Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids
description: A new reissue highlights Vini Reilly’s 1998 turn towards pop, a less explored period of the guitarist’s long career as the forward-looking post-punk outfit the Durutti Column.

title: I’ve Got Me
description: The New York City songwriter meets the hardest of feelings with uncommon compassion. Their second album’s singsong ditties and openhearted ballads play like new standards.

title: Chaos for the Fly
description: The subdued solo debut from the Fontaines D.C. singer feels alluringly timeless. It’s a combination of novelty and tradition, artifice and honesty.

title: In the End It Always Does
description: Working primarily with the 1975’s George Daniel, the English songwriter crafts a breakup album that’s vibrant and playful while exploring nuanced emotional threads.

title: Systemic
description: The Naarm, Australia-based duo draws upon its Black and Indigenous heritage to make visceral instrumental metal infused with unmistakable socio-political intent.

title: Sun Arcs
description: Layering his custom-built 48-string zither with slide guitar, clarinet, and pump organ, the Texas native makes music that draws as much from drone and ambient as from jazz and Americana.

title: Go West!: The Contemporary Records Albums
description: This new box documents a pair of late-’50s albums in which the New York saxophonist left an indelible mark on West Coast jazz.

title: Be My Vengeance
description: The Denver band’s debut is 19 minutes of galvanizing, accessible hardcore with a focus on queer community and uplift.

title: Picture of Bunny Rabbit
description: Recorded at the same time as 1986’s masterpiece World of Echo, this posthumous collection offers an essential glimpse into Arthur Russell’s haunted, luminous sound.

title: Business Is Business
description: As the Atlanta rapper’s court case continues, this scrappy project is all the more compelling for its loose, improvisatory structure.

title: Texas Boy
description: The Texas artist’s second album contains sparks of brilliance, but its overreliance on generic flex raps feels stale and tedious.

title: STROBE.RIP
description: Working alongside the multidisciplinary troll Freeka Tet, Berlin experimental club duo Amnesia Scanner sound as playful as ever, but there’s a gnawing sense of anxiety behind their fits of delirium.

title: Life Under the Gun
description: On their debut album, the Los Angeles hardcore band explodes out of the basement show without abandoning its energy and essence.

title: COI
description: The rapper and singer’s endlessly imitative new album chases trendy sounds and obvious samples to mask that it has nothing to say.

title: Please Touch
description: At once immersive and disorienting, Seth Horvitz’s second album as Rrose is dance music that erases the dancefloor.

title: Every Day Like the Last
description: A short but resonant compilation from the indie rock duo navigates life’s gray areas with gentle instrumentation and hard-earned serenity.

title: Melodies On Hiatus
description: Working alongside pop songwriter Simon Wilcox, the Strokes guitarist delivers a cheerfully sprawling double album that feels less like a cohesive statement than a clearinghouse of ideas.

title: Central City
description: The New Orleans bounce icon takes a victory lap on her long-awaited second album, one of the most effective party-starting records of the year.

title: Purge
description: Returning to the apocalyptic club setting of its early-’90s work, the industrial metal duo crafts the most inviting record of its late career.

title: Tonight
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we look back at a 1984 album that exemplifies the best of Italo disco, in all its joyfully eccentric glory.

title: The Days Of Wine and Roses (40th Anniversary Expanded Edition)
description: An extensive 4xCD set celebrates the 40th anniversary of the Paisley Underground mainstays’ debut LP, chronicling the early years of the Los Angeles group’s underground rock.

title: Feed the Beast
description: Across her latest album, the pop star’s high-octane, inoffensive dance-pop plays it way too safe and never really finds a point of view.

title: Michael
description: The Atlanta rapper’s first solo record in 11 years preserves his seismic bars, but its sanctimonious undercurrent can make it hard to stomach.

title: 3D Country
description: With a newfound emphasis on dynamics and space, the Brooklyn group evolves from its gritty post-punk origins into a proudly outrageous jam band.

title: PetroDragonic Apocalypse; or, Dawn of Eternal Night: An Annihilation of Planet Earth and the Beginning of Merciless Damnation
description: The prolific Australian psych-rockers deliver a thrash-metal concept album that doesn’t shred hard enough to stave off its overwhelming campiness.

title: a Gift & a Curse
description: The Atlanta rapper tries to testify to the emotional burdens of the YSL case while staying lighthearted, resulting in an album that both lacks depth and is too absorbed in real-life drama.

title: The Omnichord Real Book
description: Meshell Ndegeocello’s sprawling new record feels like a natural synthesis of the jazz, rock, dub, and soul sounds she’s explored throughout her career.

title: Let There Be Music
description: After a stint as Waxahatchee’s backing band, the Detroit folk-rockers subtly sharpen their musicianship on a laid-back album suffused in positive vibes.

title: The Complete Dirty South
description: An expanded edition of 2004’s alarm-sounding masterpiece presents the century’s greatest Southern rock band at its most powerful and its most poignant.

title: LaVette!
description: The soul legend presents her loosest and most daring album in years, an affectionate tribute to the underappreciated blues and folk songwriter Randall Bramblett.

title: The Whaler
description: The second album from the acerbic and eclectic emo-rock band expertly bottles their energy as they sing about constantly pushing for more when given so little.

title: Átta
description: After a decade, the Icelandic band returns with an album of minimal music performed maximally, along with a 41-piece orchestra, climate despair, and Jónsi’s inimitable vocals.

title: The Onederful Nephew
description: Assisted by Brooklyn beatmaker DJ Rude One, the rambunctious rapper makes his most focused, pared-down project yet.

title: Sugar the Bruise EP
description: Meg Duffy sharpens their slow, perceptive songwriting into a vulnerable and compelling meditation on creativity and human connection.

title: Guy
description: The Canadian producer and DJ’s second album pays tribute to her father’s memory, fusing home-video recordings with ambrosial disco, soul, and dance-pop.

title: Bitter
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we return to the 1999 album from the singer and bassist, a spare and mercurial exploration of a breakup that has become her masterpiece.

title: Smash – The Singles 1985 – 2020
description: A new 55-song compilation from the UK art-pop duo is as definitive as it gets, pearl after pearl of fabulous singles from one of the best to ever do it.

title: In Times New Roman...
description: On its angriest and heaviest record in years, the rock band restores its bluesy, primitive sound as Joshua Homme confronts his recent turmoil

title: Work of Art
description: The Nigerian singer-songwriter’s second album is in constant search of innovation, fusing traditional and contemporary African music into a celebration of success and community.

title: Myuthafoo
description: The Italian synthesizer wizard follows up her 2019 album Ecstatic Computation with an instrumental set of controlled abandon and rapturous minimalism.

title: Dolphin
description: The UK jazz pianist Greg Foat deftly balances the rhythmic and ambient poles of his sound on his collaborative album with veteran Italian artist Gigi Masin.

title: Girl With Fish
description: The Pittsburgh noise-pop experimentalists come into their own on a short yet richly textured album full of fuzzy melodic hooks and beguiling left turns.

title: Hood Hottest Princess
description: The St. Louis rapper’s new mixtape channels Gucci Mane and Trina, delivering filthy, laugh-out-loud punchlines and setting the tone for the freakiest summer since the advent of the smartphone.
The irreverent Detroit rapper’s latest album reaches toward seriousness with traditional song structures and slower, more menacing production.

title: Paranoïa, Angels, True Love
description: Inspired by Angels in America, the French artist’s latest album is a raw, dreamlike, 20-song epic that still feels like a first draft.

title: Time Ain’t Accidental
description: With understated production and forceful vocal performances, the Los Angeles songwriter crafts a heartbroken road-trip record that feels like a breakthrough.

title: Joy’all
description: The veteran singer-songwriter takes inspiration from classic country on an album full of barbed wit and insight, but the music could use more of the genre’s bite.

title: Heaven Is a Junkyard
description: Trevor Powers has long shown a penchant for reinvention, but his first album as Youth Lagoon in eight years feels like a homecoming; he’s never sounded so confident or at peace with himself.

title: Animals
description: Like his last LP, the drummer-producer’s Warp debut rejects false dichotomies like jazz vs. hip-hop. But sometimes, his freeform style is too haphazard for its own good.

title: When the Poems Do What They Do
description: Backed by a prodigious jazz combo, the poet’s debut album possesses a profound and forceful clarity.

title: Further Out Than the Edge
description: Joined by a wealth of collaborators, the house band for the venerable South London spoken-word night thrives on a nearly imperceptible blend of live improvisation and studio assemblage.

title: Fountain Baby
description: The Ghanaian American singer’s dazzling second album is a confident and unconventional record that flows, saunters, and boasts its way to one of the best pop albums of the year.

title: Lost at Sea
description: At age 69, Lana Del Rey’s father—boating enthusiast, real-estate agent, domain-name investor—makes his piano-playing debut on a major label. It’s totally fine.

title: Ticket to Fame
description: Kate NV and Angel Deradoorian lock themselves in a Cologne studio with an arsenal of synths and a mutual appreciation for the absurd; tongue-in-cheek krautrock hijinks ensue.

title: Jarak Qaribak
description: The Israeli singer and the Radiohead guitarist team up with artists from across the Middle East to tackle a range of Arabic love songs, in an act of concerted musical bridge-building.

title: Crying Laughing Loving Lying
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the British singer-songwriter’s 1972 album, an intimate and delicate collection of queer folk-rock from one of the best voices in his generation.

title: Metro Boomin Presents Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (Soundtrack From and Inspired by the Motion Picture)
description: The megastar producer enlists Future, 21 Savage, James Blake, and more in a wobbly attempt to create another synergistic pop moment in the animated Spider-Man franchise.

title: The Age of Pleasure
description: Janelle Monáe’s fourth album exchanges science fiction for lusty romance, creating a rapturous Afrofuturistic sound collage for sunny days and sticky nights.

title: Space Heavy
description: On his fourth album as King Krule, Archy Marshall reckons with love and newfound fatherhood, but he still sounds beset by existential doubt.

title: O Monolith
description: The English band’s second album explores big questions with a bucolic, open-ended new sound. Where once they surged forward, now they wander.

title: Weathervanes
description: A calm breeze blows through the songwriter’s latest album, a road-ready set of tunes forged on the long journey to relaxation.

title: New Jazz
description: With restless vocals and shapeshifting beats, the Harlem rapper’s new mixtape innovates on the chaotic sound of rage-rap.

title: QWERTY EP
description: The art-pop musician’s latest EP is a bleary, semiconscious rush that invites you to get lost inside it.

title: Wandering Rebel
description: On his most introspective album to date, the everyman balladeer from Queens considers beachside sandwiches, making money from art, and what it means to be home.

title: Jam City Presents EFM
description: The UK dance producer delivers an effervescent blend of rattling garage, glitzy disco, and thumping house that invokes the idea of nightlife as an endless fantasy.

title: Zango
description: On their first album in nearly 40 years, the Zamrock pioneers prove their malleable, genre-spanning style still sounds like the future.

title: Orbs
description: The New York producer once known for muscular house and techno continues to drift into the ether, channeling ’90s chillout and dub techno into his singular vision.

title: Formal Growth in the Desert
