description: The glitch pioneer returns with his most accessible album to date: a surprisingly colorful set that sounds like he’s DJing a retrospective of his own career.

title: SUSS
description: Neither rawboned nor ramshackle, the New York group’s elegantly composed brand of ambient country stands as tall and clean as a brand-new pair of cowboy boots.

title: You Haven’t Missed Much
description: A compilation from the prolific Water From Your Eyes songwriter offers an endearing tour through their introspective, constantly evolving body of work.

title: Emergency!
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the birth of jazz fusion, a combustive 1969 album led by a prodigious drummer striking it out on his own.

title: B-Sides, Demos & Rarities
description: PJ Harvey fans have waited a long time for this: a near-exhaustive collection of the singer’s non-album tracks and orphaned gems, many of which rival her classic album cuts.

title: Senderos de luz y sombras
description: In a 16-channel piece commissioned for France’s Groupe de Recherches Musicales, the electroacoustic pioneer looks to the origins of the universe and the unconscious mind for inspiration.

title: Anyhow
description: On his solo debut, the BADBADNOTGOOD member applies jazz instrumentation and technique to compositions that approach psychedelic rock and dream pop.

title: Matter
description: Equally inspired by late Romantic symphonies and experimental electronic techniques, the Swiss composer pushes both classical tropes and ambient conventions to their breaking points.

title: Hotel Insomnia
description: The latest album from the Japanese shoegaze band shimmers with restless yearning, a sense of wonder kicking like a fluttering heartbeat in the chest.

title: Paper Route Frank
description: The Memphis rapper’s posthumous album honors his legacy by spotlighting his unmatched charisma, technical prowess, and storytelling flair.

title: Liquiddd Changesss
description: On piano and cello, this cross-generational drone partnership finds common ground in the desire to explore the fundamental malleability of sound.

title: Take Me Home EP
description: The London producer’s new three-track EP adds texture and personality to her music without quite innovating on her original, already much-imitated pop formula.

title: Four
description: The 71-year-old guitarist has long been known as a peerless interpreter of American musical forms, but on these 13 diaristic originals, he reveals more of himself than ever before.

title: Come Around
description: The Australian songwriter returns with a beachy, airborne set with subtle hints of something darker lurking underneath.

title: Beware of the Monkey
description: MIKE continues a long run of great records with his self-produced 10th album, a self-assured current of shifting emotional states.

title: My House My Rules
description: The South African producer behind 2019’s viral hit “Untold Stories” tests the limits of amapiano, fusing its trademark log drums with established club genres.

title: Jumping/Dancing/Fighting EP
description: With a menacing sound and bleak but playful lyrics, the Norwegian noise-rock trio stands out from the pack on its debut EP.

title: To Illustrate
description: With each track set around 100 BPM, this compilation from London’s Wisdom Teeth label allows the artists to stretch out and yield surprisingly dynamic results.

title: The Smile (Live at Montreux Jazz Festival, July 2022)
description: The Radiohead offshoot’s new live album is both an unexpected treat and a flex, proving the trio can replicate its gnarliest, most thrilling material onstage and sans studio trickery.

title: Niger EP Vol. 1 / Niger EP Vol. 2
description: Recorded in the Tuareg guitarist’s home country over the past five years, these live and alternate takes offer the chance to hear his music in the cultural context in which he forged it.

title: Live at The Whisky 1977
description: This four-disc set recorded just before Cheap Trick’s ascent to stardom captures the power-pop icons at their most manic and muscular, sounding more like hungry punks than arena-ready heartthrobs.

title: Live Fire
description: With a low-stakes live album, the English art-rock band showcases the playfulness that runs through even their most elaborate work.

title: Ground Groove
description: On her third album, the Los Angeles artist weaves samples of Iranian music into a rugged blend of dub and industrial.

title: Ice, Death, Planets, Lungs, Mushrooms and Lava / Laminated Denim / Changes
description: The Gizzard’s abundant crop of fall albums spans custom incidental music, nerdy compositional experiments, and one of the best front-to-back records in their catalog.

title: Solos / 4 Cuts Placed in “A First Quarter” / Having Been Built on Sand
description: In the 1970s, the Downtown saxophonist fused free jazz’s fire-breathing spirit with minimalism’s dizzying swirl. Three new reissues from Unseen Worlds document the evolution of his unique style.

title: Keep It Lit EP
description: The Oakland rapper’s new EP slows her throwback 1990s jams to a leisurely West Coast pace.

title: Full Moon Mystery Garden
description: The GothBoiClique affiliate takes a Lynchian journey through trap beats, dusty drum breaks, and shoegaze guitar; his vaguely emotive lyrics suggest horrors lurking in the shadows.

title: NO THANK YOU
description: Accolades be damned, the UK star blasts a music industry that has left her feeling drained, adding her voice to a chorus of Black British artists pushing back against the status quo.

title: Premonition
description: The Canadian punk band’s fifth and final album is a softer, more family-oriented affair, with reflections on motherhood and loss set to metallic riffs.

title: The Way It Is
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Keyshia Cole’s 2005 debut, a scrapbook of too-real breakup anthems from a pivotal moment in R&B.

title: The 7" Singles
description: A ginormous, mostly fans-only box set gathers together 80 records that tell the singular story of a man who has dedicated his entire life to the three-minute pop song.

title: Herbert
description: After a tumultuous few years, the TDE rapper gets personal and sounds reinvigorated, but his worst tendencies as a rapper consistently hold him back.

title: hypochondriac
description: Heady, self-loathing, and occasionally overwrought, the Ohio singer and producer’s new album plays like an obsessive process document of internet-mediated anxiety.

title: Call and Response
description: Reverb is the sole ingredient on the German-Bulgarian artist’s latest conceptual record, in which vintage pedals and digital processors are used to mimic the properties of sound in impossible spaces.

title: Vacabularee
description: The Chicago rapper’s new album contains a few flashes of brilliance, but the aloof flows that set him apart now feel a little too familiar.

title: Yesterday’s Tomorrow Is Not Today
description: A totemic box set from Numero Group collects the output of the Midwestern emo band, whose melodic, sentimental take on D.C. hardcore served as a microcosm of the genre’s transition.

title: Live at Budokan
description: Recorded in 1984, this live set offers a glimpse behind the fog of pot smoke and blur of whiskey when one of country music’s greatest-ever bands was performing at its peak.

title: VMAK<KOMBZ<<<DUGLAS<<6NDR7<<<
description: The longtime Tortoise bassist picks up lead guitar on his solo debut, a wayward instrumental expedition with a poker-faced sense of humor.

title: Snake Eyes EP
description: The mischief-making duo is up to its usual tricks on this three-song, six-minute EP, but it fails to deliver the thrills of the group’s debut.

title: Snake Chain
description: Mixing viral videos with synths and the unsettling screams of lead singer Kate Mahony, the London punk quartet delivers an unusual record that’s as funny as it is unhinged.

title: Watertown
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a fascinating outlier in Frank Sinatra’s catalog, an unsparing and bleak concept album from 1970.

title: Divine Symmetry
description: The new Hunky Dory-era box set offers a tantalizing peek behind the curtain of Bowie’s theatrical persona during arguably the most pivotal moment in his life and career.

title: SOS
description: SZA’s long, ambitious, luxurious new album solidifies her position as a generational talent, an artist who translates her innermost feelings into indelible moments.

title: Plasma
description: The latest collaboration from Luca Mortellaro and Seth Horvitz is a vision of techno as a luminous fog, conjuring vivid imagery with the most stone-faced drones.

title: MOB
description: With cohesive production and lyrics that veer from tender to stoic, the Detroit rapper’s latest is his most meticulous project yet.

title: Heroes & Villains
description: The hitmaking producer’s latest album brandishes his ardent ambition, attention to detail, and gift for curation.

title: All Roads Lead to the Gun (Deluxe)
description: Alternating between ruthless hardcore punk and melodic post-hardcore, the Los Angeles band seek emotional truth that still rips.

title: Lucifer on the Moon
description: On-U Sound legend Adrian Sherwood gives Spoon’s latest album a surprisingly sprightly and occasionally awkward dub reconstruction.

title: A Complete Anthology of Solo and Duo Violin Pieces
description: Reaching back to the 1950s, this collection highlights the New York School composer’s fragmented, conversational style, as well as his music’s patient, intuitive qualities.

title: Palaces of Pity EP
description: The French ambient producer uses the ocean’s duality of stillness and turbulence as inspiration to produce music that ebbs and flows eternally.

title: Live at the Fillmore (1997)
description: Compiled from a marathon run of shows at the Fillmore Auditorium, this live set is a joyful, relaxed, and abundant journey through Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers’ personal rock’n’roll history.

title: Type 4: City on the Type of Forever
description: Earnestly didactic “conscious” hip-hop is easy to mock but hard to do well. The Compton rapper’s rhyme schemes are persuasive even when his arguments don’t withstand close scrutiny.

title: Dusk
description: The capstone to Portland synthesizer musician Daryl Groetsch’s wildly productive year, Dusk runs the gamut of his sound, evoking early ambient classics as it flits between beauty and terror.

title: HIS HAPPINESS SHALL COME FIRST EVEN THOUGH WE ARE SUFFERING
description: On the final entry in a trilogy that began with her Polaris Prize-winning 2020 album, the Montreal rapper seeks elusive redemption in cacophonies of tense noise and gothic samples.

title: Back to the Woodlands
description: Where his 1975 album Neighborhoods was rooted in the sounds of community, these previously unreleased archival recordings capture the Oregon wilderness in synths, zither, and field recordings.

title: Respect the Come Up
description: On his debut mixtape, the Manchester rapper deploys his thick, graceful raps with expert precision. It’s a promising opening statement, crafted with candor, wit, and a slick sense of style.

title: Promethean Pathology
description: Featuring members of Blood Incantation, the avant-garde black metal band blends industrial and electronic elements into a seamless whole.

title: Hejira
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Joni Mitchell's eighth album, an iridescent meditation on travel and solitude, a masterpiece in her catalog and across all of music.

title: Upright and Even EP
description: The New York band’s alluring new EP of cocktail-lounge house packs a seven-and-a-half-minute dancefloor heater like a magnum of champagne.

title: 100% Galcher
description: An understated landmark of underground house, Galcher Lustwerk’s 2013 DJ mix receives a remastered 2xLP release. His defiantly unchanging beats feel charged with the knowledge that every party ends.

title: Broken Spectre
description: The experimental composer’s accompaniment for Richard Mosse’s film installation transforms the natural sounds of the Amazon rainforest into a harrowing score to environmental disaster.

title: World Record
description: Co-produced by Rick Rubin, Neil Young’s 42nd album is a mellow, off-kilter collection about the environment, mourning what’s already been lost while expressing a modicum of hope.

title: And I Have Been
description: On his third album—the first part of a projected trilogy—the singer-songwriter retains all his theatrical intensity while shifting his focus to songs about love, a subject he once spurned.

title: This Is What I Mean
description: The UK rapper’s third album is pitched as both a pious expression of worship and an earnest message of self-affirmation—but with plenty of opportunities for flexing along the way.

title: On the way to Beatenberg EP
description: The South African indie pop trio returns from hiatus sounding wiser, softer, and as virtuosic as ever.

title: Wane Into It
description: Blending slowcore, ambient, and folk with lo-fi musings on memory and entropy, Portland, Oregon musician Kyle Bates joins a grand tradition of Pacific Northwestern gloom.

title: Flipped It EP
description: Intimate and unadorned, these five recordings from the Melbourne-based artist sound like the dying embers of torch songs.

title: Flaming Swords
description: Multi-instrumentalist Zach Phillips and singer Ma Clément craft alluring jazz fusion songs in miniature. It is heady but not stuffy, precise but not rigid, dense but not cluttered.

title: SATURNO
description: With an eclectic mosaic of sounds across 1980s and ’90s freestyle, Miami bass, house, and old-school reggaeton, the Puerto Rican star’s new album delivers floor-fillers that actually try something different.

title: Feed tha Streets III
description: Still trying to capture the lightning of his star-making debut, the Compton rapper’s latest is an attempted return to form that plays it far too safe.

title: Spirit Roaming
description: Anchored by muted samples and soul-baring soliloquies, the New York rapper’s new album is an impressive, winding meditation on survival.

title: Onwards!
description: Blending weighty subject matter and loose, meandering grooves, the Charleston-based artist’s latest album moves like a raindrop down a windowpane—jagged, natural, and unpredictable.

title: foam
description: Drawn mostly from a palette of piano, guitar, and chopped vocal fragments, Ulla Straus’ new direction in ambient music represents a departure from her previous albums. It’s glitchy, but also human.

title: The Hands of Grace
description: Now 84, the celebrated novelist, poet, and playwright presents his first collection of original songs. These sweetly earnest and stirringly beautiful pieces reflect a life immersed in jazz.

title: Isomonstrosity
description: An innovative effort to produce a contemporary classical record in the piecemeal style of a rap mixtape ends up sounding both tasteful and weirdly frustrating.

title: Black Girl Magic
description: Fresh off Beyoncé’s co-sign, the house DJ and producer returns with a joyous, collaboration-filled LP that channels the buzzy, late-night feeling when affection and tenderness flow freely.

title: Back 2 Life
description: On his first album in three years, the Bangkok-based Drain Gang rapper taps into the group’s customary sentimentalism, but the rote lyrics and beats fail to convey much genuine emotion.

title: Please Have a Seat
description: The Chicago DIY star is capable of presenting even the most technically difficult music as a casual, catchy pop song. His Secretly Canadian debut makes for an ideal introduction.

title: STR4TASFEAR
description: On their second album together, London DJ Gilles Peterson and Brit-funk pioneer Jean-Paul “Bluey” Maunick pay tribute to an overlooked strain of UK dance music.

title: The Roches
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the cult-classic 1979 debut from the Roche sisters, a playful, poignant, and slyly subversive folk masterpiece.

title: Redcar les adorables étoiles (prologue)
description: Written almost entirely in French, the Parisian artist’s quietly imaginative new album pursues a sonic and lyrical interiority that doesn’t always translate to great pop.

title: Big Time Things
description: Sleek but not too sleek for slap bass, the Brooklyn quartet’s third album is a dispatch from the gray area between stoicism and comedy.

title: I Don’t Give a Fuck About This Rap Shit, Imma Just Drop Until I Don’t Feel Like It Anymore
description: Wordy, thoughtful rapping is thriving, but the Virginia-born MC makes the style feel particularly urgent. Neither his full-on delivery nor his absurdist sense of humor dilute his razor-sharp focus.

title: The Family
description: The purported final album from the chart-topping hip-hop collective chronicles their rise and accelerated decline through the lens of a mercurial Svengali.
Composed for the Guggenheim Museum’s retrospective of Maurizio Cattelan, this 2011 performance showcases a band torn between its impulse to entertain and its personal mission to challenge.

title: King’s Disease III
description: The fourth album in Nas’ ongoing series of collaborations with producer Hit-Boy locks into a straightforward groove. It’s loose and expert and finally nimble again.

title: softCORE
description: On softCORE, the New Jersey native mashes pop punk grit and airy R&B. It’s a commendable undertaking, but the execution is rough.

title: Almanac Behind
description: Nature takes center stage on the experimental guitarist’s latest album—a response to climate crisis blending fractured melodies with recordings of severe weather and emergency broadcasts.

title: Vivid
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a groundbreaking 1988 album, a crucial document in Black rock music with huge, brawny riffs and a complex socio-political message.

title: On the Impossible Past (10th Anniversary Edition)
description: This 2012 LP, newly reissued, is the Scranton punk band’s definitive album—the record that inaugurated a signature vernacular of doomed romance and self-loathing nostalgia.

title: And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow
description: Natalie Mering’s majestic fifth record is a dispatch from the center of catastrophe—an idiosyncratic set of love songs and secular hymns with lushly orchestral arrangements.

title: The Ruby Cord
description: The latest from the ambitious British musician is a grim vision of the future: a crumbling, corroding monument that feels strangely devoid of a soul.

title: Maternity Beat
description: Accompanied by the 12-person Trondheim Jazz Orchestra, the Norwegian metal-jazz guitarist explores motherhood and mayhem on nine action-packed songs full of overdriven riffs and warring counterpoints.

title: Tempus
description: On his latest project, the German electronic musician blends piano, percussion, and dying equipment into his moody ambient-dub.

title: CAZIMI
description: The Texas-born Nashvillian previously proved herself a natural translator of honky-tonk’s emotional entanglements; on her long-delayed third record, she makes a complete song cycle out of them.

title: Meeting with a Judas Tree
description: The polymath brings his signature compositional style back to the piano for an expressive album that is intimate, immediate, and, for all its ambition, easy to connect to.

title: Anyways, Life’s Great… EP
description: With the song of the summer belt around her waist, the Memphis rapper collects on the “F.N.F.” fame with a rowdy, promising debut EP.

title: Chimæra I
description: In two long, bassy, zoned-out compositions, the genre-defying saxophonist strains against the formal restrictions of drone music.

title: An Orange Colored Day
description: The Los Angeles songwriter balances autobiographical odes to love and loss with dreamlike imagery on her soft, hopeful debut.

title: RTJ Cu4tro
description: Killer Mike and El-P’s collaborative free-for-all puts the spotlight on artists from the Latin American diaspora. It’s an exciting lineup, but a little too inconsistent to work as an album.

title: What Had Happened Was
description: The Virginia crooner and sometime rapper is back with his old name and his new sensibilities—a re-re-introduction that solidifies his love for all things smooth and sappy.

title: We’re Not Here to Be Loved
description: On the Vein.fm side project’s full-length debut, these hardcore musicians melt down an entire CD binder’s worth of alt-rock classics and sculpt an alternate timeline out of the pliable remnants.

title: Hayday
description: The Pittsburgh rock quartet’s newly reissued debut is a relentless, intentionally chaotic document of twentysomething existential dread.

title: Song of Salvation
description: Exploding death metal into atmospheric and experimental new dimensions, the dream-doom duo’s monuments to melancholy have never felt so crushing or beautiful.

title: Myself in the Way
description: A patchwork of lethargic guitar riffs, dying-bulb synth glow, and generic disco beats, the Virginia band’s newest album feels strangely emotionally detached.

title: 5 to the Eye With Stars
description: Ferreira’s newest album doesn’t stray from his core sound of jazzy boom bap, but his candid writing brings out the lucidity and urgency of his music.

title: How the Light Felt
description: Carefully parsing the nuances of shoegaze, dream pop, and alt rock, the Chicago quintet’s second album amounts to a rigorous study of 1990s guitar sounds.

title: HH5
description: With its macabre textures and sinister flows, the fifth installment of CEO Trayle’s Happy Halloween series unspools the rapper’s fears and sorrows into one of the most original rap albums of the year.

title: Scarecrow (Deluxe)
description: The deluxe reissue of the heartland songwriter’s 1985 album reinforces its stature as the platonic ideal of a traditional American rock’n’roll record: It is direct, unfussy, and unpretentious.

title: MK 3.5: Die Cuts | City Planning
description: Half woozy Los Angeles beats and half lo-fi techno, Mount Kimbie’s new double album doesn’t sound much like anything they’ve done before. It’s also some of their least original work.

title: Nothing You Do Matters EP
description: The Chicago quartet play nervy post-punk with a groundedness and poise that suggests if your back is up against the wall, you might be able to lean on it for support.

title: They’re All Gonna Laugh at You!
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a 1993 comedy album full of dick and fart jokes, and the brilliant, self-effacing man who made them work.

title: Mondays at the Enfield Tennis Academy
description: Recorded across a few intimate evenings at a cozy L.A. cocktail bar, these four side-long tracks of bass, drums, sax, and guitar dissolve revelatory improvisation into mesmerizing ambient atmospheres.

title: Only the Strong Survive
description: Bruce brings heaps of feeling to a new set of some of his favorite, largely obscure soul songs, giving them a confident, faithful, and occasionally synthetic sound.

title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever - Music From and Inspired By
description: The soundtrack from the new Marvel blockbuster has a staggering sonic diversity, but the absence of a curator is felt in how loosely songs are tied to the movie.

title: Through a Room
description: On his second solo album for Drag City, the Philadelphia guitarist continues to develop his singular style, incorporating tape loops, taishōgoto, and hurdy-gurdy into his sculptural approach.

title: Comradely Objects
description: On the group’s fourth album, carefully controlled minimalism gives way to a playful expressionistic streak, suggesting a utopian balance between social harmony and personal freedom.

title: Amateurs
description: The Australian songwriter’s intermittently funny and mournful folk-pop confronts the improbable task of commercial success and decides that art is worth making anyway.

title: Alpha Zulu
description: The French indie rock stalwarts’ fun and fizzy seventh album rejuvenates a proven formula while protecting its true feelings behind glass.

title: Club Godfather
description: The first album from the breakout star of New Jersey club rap isn’t quite the revelation its title suggests, but his breakneck sound remains intoxicating.

title: Clan Way 3
description: On the third edition of Clan Way, the Los Angeles duo brings back the laugh-out-loud antics. It’s breezy and fun, bolstered by the pair’s flawless chemistry.

title: Protector
description: Inspired by the rugged yet serene beauty of Ireland’s west coast, the singer-songwriter’s tranquil psych-folk explores communion with nature, family, and ourselves.

title: Pigments
description: Setting Dawn Richard’s agile voice against Spencer Zahn’s lush chamber arrangements, the two musicians push each other into an atmospheric zone that’s new for both.

title: A Swollen River, A Well Overflowing
description: The second album from the Chicago singer-songwriter Jess Shoman brings in the band for a noise-country-ish sound that both spotlights and strengthens their vocals.

title: Animal Drowning
description: With a mixture of shoegaze and dream pop, the Philadelphia band offers a dramatic soundtrack to dark introspection.

title: Air Guitar
description: The Singaporean indie pop trio’s second album sparkles, but under all the glitter, there are somber truths about love’s uncertainties.

title: Her Loss
description: The album-length collaboration between the pop star of the North and the rap star of the South seems like a good match, but it turns into a drastically uneven project in almost every way.

title: Hadja Bangoura
description: On her debut album, the Brooklyn-based producer and singer smartly and subtly remakes her sound, meshing R&B and New York drill in melodically refined and technically daring ways.

title: SAP
description: On her third album, Kaya Wilkins’ arrangements have finally caught up with her free-roaming mind; the music has gathered weight and mass, bringing her distinctive insights into focus.

title: MEMPHIS MASSACRE III
description: The rapper’s hard-knocking horrorcore is classic Memphis trunk music, and only other artists from the 901 are invited along for the ride.

title: Back Home
description: On the UK trio’s first LP for Kill Rock Stars, the band fleshes out its riot-grrrl-meets-girl-group sound with electronics and strings while singing of strength and vulnerability.

title: Sexy
description: With a playful mood and a wide range of collaborators, the debut full-length from the outlandish pop duo subverts trends with ease.

title: Perspective
description: Layering spoken interviews about the experience of disability with pulsing minimalist fugues, Perspective is a powerful work of love and empathy that underscores the poison of ableism in American culture.

title: Fashion Nugget
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Cake’s second album, a wry, earnest, and oft-misunderstood outlier of ’90s alt-rock.

title: ( ) 20th Anniversary Edition
description: The Icelandic group celebrates the 20th anniversary of its third album with an expanded edition. Sung entirely in the made-up language of Hopelandic, it sounds as sumptuous and suggestive as ever.

title: Endure
description: On their remarkable third album, the New Orleans band pushes their sound to both its bleakest and its sweetest brinks. Pop, disco, and house all melt into their raucous, revolutionary glam punk.

title: Is It Going to Get Any Deeper Than This?
description: Matmos’ Drew Daniel extends the collaborative thrust of his solo project, imbuing dynamic, shape-shifting disco and deep-house tracks with a warm sense of community.

title: Crybaby
description: The duo’s latest album reaches back into their past but gets stuck in a strange middle ground between big-budget indie and low-budget pop.

title: human futures
description: On the follow-up to 2018’s Skulls Example, the Portland group delivers pointed late-capitalist critiques, using coarser melodies and more vivid lyrics to express gnawing existential anxiety.

title: Svengali
description: The New York rapper is known for his breathless flows and punchy hip-house beats. His second album is just as slick, but this time there’s a little tenderness.

title: Cold Cuts
description: Where 2021’s Half God was a farewell to the Manhattan of Wiki’s youth, the follow-up lacks that record’s deliberate agenda, channeling its freewheeling energy into a free-associative writing style.

title: snow flakes 2022
description: After a decade-long pause, Jaime Brooks revives her Elite Gymnastics project. The record feels like an elegy for a time when the internet provided refuge for misfit kids seeking out like-minded souls.

title: Astral Fortress
description: The apparent effortlessness (and occasional silliness) of the metal band’s 20th album could make it feel tossed off, but the duo’s enthusiasm mostly prevents that from happening.

title: Luv 4 Rent
description: The rapper’s third album is an invitation into his domestic sphere in all of its messiness, controversies, and communal joy.

title: ILYSM
description: John Ross leads his band through a richly detailed and expectedly sentimental album that wrestles with all the life and death that exists in the midst of a cancer diagnosis.

title: Bluenothing EP
description: Drawing inspiration from symphonic black metal, the enigmatic band’s new mini-album is a gothic dreamworld where virtuosic shredding rules above all.

title: OUTOFBODY
description: The Richmond-based artist collides big riffs, sweet melodies, and thick fuzz into crisp, cathartic songs about life’s uncertainties.

title: Reason in Decline
description: On their first studio album in 24 years, the long-reunited Southern indie rockers make mighty, angry songs better suited for now than then.

title: Light Moving Time
description: The full-length debut from the New York folk-rock duo addresses the nonlinear nature of healing with a gentle and deliberate touch.

title: Paste
description: The trio of drummer Valentina Magaletti and Raime’s Joe Andrews and Tom Halstead subtly reinvent post-hardcore by plundering the past and making familiar tropes sound fresh again.

title: From a Story Now Lost
description: On her solo debut, the Norwegian electronic musician uses synthesizer and piano to sketch suggestively abstracted scenes veiled in fog. The songs can feel like they’re transcribed from a forgotten language.

title: Trouble the Water
description: On an adventurous new album, the New York hardcore band populates a swamp of chugs with weird creatures of electronica and sudden clearings of melodic, galloping punk.

title: Dirt Femme
description: On her first independent release, the pop star pivots to tamer themes and gives more lethargic performances, losing a lot of her spark in the process.

title: Noon
description: The songwriter and multi-instrumentalist who’s collaborated with Big Thief, the Deslondes, and the Low Anthem returns with a sparse, earnest collection that occasionally overstates its message.

title: Nacarile
description: Adopting an oblique, exploratory approach to bolero, hip-hop, and synth pop, the Puerto Rican artist’s third studio album meditates candidly on political and personal endurance.

title: DJ-Kicks: Theo Parrish
description: On a landmark mix album, the Detroit icon gathers together multiple generations of the city’s dance-music faithful in a celebration of history, community, and possibility.

title: Actual Life 3 (January 1 - September 9 2022)
description: On his third album in 18 months, the UK hitmaker applies a scrapbooker’s instincts to festival-ready house anthems. But despite the diaristic hints, we learn little about the artist.

title: Waiting Game
description: The Canadian duo cuts out drums and vocals from long stretches of their first album in six years. That it feels of a piece with their past work is a testament to the solid foundation of their music.

title: akọle EP
description: The Nigerian-born artist collages highlife, Afrobeats, and electronics into his bravely experimental second EP. While the medley is audacious and impressive, it sometimes feels unfinished.

title: Cyclorama
description: On her debut album, the rising Chicago DJ spins thrilling, multifaceted club music into a celebration of her Belizean heritage and trans identity.

title: Wyld Love Songs
description: Both playful and spare, the second solo LP from the Red River Dialect songwriter and ordained Buddhist chaplain finds warmth and comfort in scenes of decay.

title: Streetlands EP
description: Continuing in the vein of January’s Antidawn EP, Burial’s latest three-tracker dispenses with the drums entirely, instead exploring an ambient expanse of choir and strings.

title: Dig Me In: A Dig Me Out Covers Album
description: St. Vincent, Low, Courtney Barnett, the Linda Lindas and more highlight the enduring influence of Sleater-Kinney on this track-by-track tribute to the band’s breakthrough 1997 album.

title: Malign Hex
description: The Chicago band’s new album balances punk aggression and Sisyphean striving, so wide and claustrophobic that it leaves you disoriented.

title: Guitar Music
description: The Liverpool band’s debut looks at rock music and quotidian life through their own bizarre, distorted pop lens.

title: Bolts
description: Assembled from years of recordings made on the road, the Armenian British producer’s debut LP for Four Tet’s Text label flips traditional instruments and captured moments into dancefloor thrills.

title: Building Something Beautiful for Me
description: As part of an ongoing reassessment of pioneering composer Julius Eastman’s work, the London electronic musician presents originals loosely inspired by signature pieces like “Stay On It” and “Femenine.”

title: Cometa
description: The Brooklyn-based crooner’s abundant talent vanishes behind hazy production and indistinct writing.

title: Paraglow EP
description: A new joint release from the Seoul artists feels like a true collaboration, fusing their distinct styles with shoegaze production and alt-rock guitars.

title: Se Ve Desde Aquí
description: On her new album, the Guatemalan cellist trades her lush, verdant style for moments of austere beauty. She feels more intuitive and confident than ever.

title: Stumpwork
description: The London quartet moves beyond the sardonic post-punk of its debut, exploring new sounds and moods while Florence Shaw reveals hitherto unheard subtleties in her famously low-key delivery.

title: Steady
description: On their 13th album, the Canadian indie lifers play to their strengths with classic rock worship and power-pop hooks.

title: The Liz 2
description: Sounding effortlessly in command of her money and her sexuality, the Griselda rapper’s new album oozes seductive pleasure.

title: Midnights
description: More interested in setting atmosphere than chasing trends, Taylor Swift’s 10th album pursues a newly subdued and amorphous pop sound.

title: Inner World Peace
description: With loose, psych-pop grooves and empathetic lyrics about growing up, Greta Kline and her band enter a phase of tenured inquisitiveness.

title: Amor Hardcore
description: Playful, maximalist, and flirtatious to the core, Isabella Lovestory’s debut album is a defiant celebration of sexual agency.

title: All Blue
description: The Toronto singer-songwriter channels cosmic country on her debut album. Recorded live in the studio, it’s a promising showcase of both her nimble voice and her band’s dynamic playing.

title: Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the English duo’s 1981 debut, a daring landmark of synth pop that went unexpectedly mainstream.

title: Up the Bracket (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: The London band’s thrillingly seedy 2002 debut receives a reissue, accompanied by a stack of demos and studio outtakes that illuminate its sprawling, chaotic romance.

title: Laughing so Hard, it Hurts
description: Intimate by design but expansive in scope, the rapper’s latest project is an inventive and unnerving evolution of his singular style.

title: The Loneliest Time
description: More interested in earmarking ideas than in formulating an overarching aesthetic proposition, Carly Rae Jepsen’s fifth album diversifies her portfolio of 1980s pop sounds.

title: Momentary Presence
description: Drawing on several decades of psychedelic music, the debut album from the Brooklyn project grapples with introspective feelings through expansive, transportive sounds.

title: Gris Klein
description: The French trio’s third album trends towards accessibility without losing its taste for the visceral pleasures of more technical post-hardcore.

title: PLAYGIRL
description: The pop artist’s second record is a bold attempt at lightening up her sound, featuring a cyber-future narrative and three distinct personas.

title: The Car
description: The English band returns with an adventurous, heavily orchestrated album filled with enigmatic songs of love, longing, and doubt.

title: Live in Cuxhaven 1976
description: The third installment in an ongoing series of live recordings contains some of the krautrock titans’ most unbridled moments yet, but the whittled-down highlights preclude any sense of flow.

title: Quiet the Room
description: Blending misty ambience with introspective folk songwriting, the Los Angeles artist’s full-length debut is less about specifics than the way it all smears together.

title: Only Built for Infinity Links
description: The Migos members’ new collaboration is longer than it needs to be, but Quavo and Takeoff can make most scenarios sound exciting, whether life-changing or mundane.

title: I Walked With You a Ways
description: Katie Crutchfield and Jess Williamson’s debut as Plains sends it back to the ’90s with a thoughtful, personalized interpretation of old-school country-pop.

title: Return of the Dream Canteen
description: The funk-rock band’s second album of the year is a surprisingly introspective set filled with references to forgotten actors, classic bands, and, most tellingly, decades-old Chili Peppers songs.

title: It’s Only Me
description: The Atlanta rapper sounds comfortable, uninspired, and indifferent on his latest album. It’s a missed opportunity to flaunt his talent for vocal manipulation and emotional delivery.

title: Nothing Special
description: The Okkervil River frontman has long taken a sledgehammer to the fourth wall; on his self-aware solo debut, he takes stock of the troubled state of the industry and delivers a eulogy for his band.

title: ForeverAndEverNoMore
description: Confronting the climate crisis and the prospect of humankind’s demise, the veteran experimental musician takes an unconventional approach: He gets in touch with his feelings.

title: Loose Future
description: The Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter teams up with producer Sam Evian for an assured, exploratory, and warm record that mirrors a newly opened heart.

title: Church
description: The rapper’s second album of 2022 is a dark memoir about love, memory, and faith. With a meticulous but loose style, it amplifies his capacity for vulnerability.

title: Now Is
description: The London electronic musician’s painterly, atmospheric production style yields deftly layered headphone music adorned with occasional dancefloor flourishes.

title: YTI⅃AƎЯ
description: On his third solo album in as many years, the wise and stoic singer-writer extolls the virtues of the sacred and the mundane.

title: Nicks and Grazes
description: On its third album, the Philadelphia quartet hones the studio techniques—as well as the knowledge of when to hold back—required to do justice to the group’s adventurous spirit.

title: Component System With the Auto Reverse
description: The rapper’s eighth solo album is a stroll down memory lane, summoning the ‘90s boom bap aesthetics he grew up on. It’s a nostalgic trip that further cements his witty, introspective, and singular style.

title: grow your hair long if you​’​re wanting to see something that you can change
description: Singer-songwriter Kevin Patrick Sullivan exchanges straight-to-tape simplicity for full-band arrangements, bringing a warm Americana glow to bedroom ballads full of sadness and yearning.

title: Reinventing Axl Rose
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Laura Jane Grace’s 2002 folk-punk salvo, an album that yearns for an escape from and through rock’n’roll.

title: The Velvet Rope (Deluxe Edition)
description: After three blockbusters, the megastar turned introspective on her fourth album, plumbing the depths of depression. Considered a disappointment at the time, it’s become one of her most beloved LPs.

title: Being Funny in a Foreign Language
description: Matty Healy taps Jack Antonoff to help produce a concise, meaningful, pop-focused album about love. It’s cliche, it’s obvious, it’s slyly profound—it’s the 1975.

title: Blueblue
description: On a softly melancholic new album, the Los Angeles musician offers a concentration of his strengths in service of one sharpened, sustained mood.

title: Rolling Golden Holy
description: On their second album as a trio, Anaïs Mitchell, Eric D. Johnson, and Josh Kaufman build fresh narratives from the fabled history of folk music.

title: RUFFS
description: In Kenny Mason’s world, puppies are royalty and contemporary Southern rap and rock go hand-in-hand.

title: ¡Ay!
description: The Colombian musician sketches a sci-fi vision of bolero, son, and other classic genres she grew up with. It’s philosophically daring, technically ambitious, and a joy to experience.

title: <CopingMechanism>
description: The Gen Z philosopher’s hard-rock era continues with an album about love and hurt, pain and healing, done with great nuance but not quite enough originality.

title: 3800 Degrees
description: On his fourth solo album of the year, the Louisiana rapper wears his regional roots with brash defiance. It’s a reminder of how thrilling he can be when he’s focused and cohesive.

title: Bobby Weir & Wolf Bros: Live in Colorado, Vol. 2
description: On a striking live set, the Grateful Dead rhythm guitarist and vocalist stages some of the band’s most beloved material with passion and reverence.

title: Anywhere But Here
description: On its second album, the London band folds classic pop tropes into its songwriting—just the latest surprise from a group that has always kept listeners on their toes.

title: I will not use the body’s eyes today. EP
description: On an independently released 30-minute EP, Angel Marcloid slightly recalibrates her uber-maximalist sound to be both lighter and heavier at its extreme poles.

title: Doubles
description: Having added a second drummer and a synth player since its 2018 debut, New Orleans’ self-described “free-jazz party band” vacillates between abandon and unease.

title: Languoria
description: Composer Sofie Birch’s lush ambient creations and experimental singer Antonina Nowacka’s indelible vocal melodies meet on a record that ebbs and flows as naturally as breathing.

title: Most Normal
description: The Irish band’s unrelenting third album, made with an arcade of pedals and processors, surges with electricity. Inside all of its noise is an indignant, surreal mania that gives it a twisted pop soul.

title: Orange 2
description: The second album from the enigmatic duo is equally nauseating and joyous, like binging on several decades of euphoric pop and hurling it onto the floor of a Tilt-A-Whirl.

title: Capricorn Sun
description: The UK producer casually throws house, UK garage, R&B, pop, and breakbeats into varied songs that are as emotionally relatable as they are instinctively danceable.

title: Desperately Imagining Someplace Quiet
description: The Madison, Wisconsin band’s second album melds 1960s pop melodies and ’90s indie rock distortion into feel-good tunes rich in existential angst.

title: Cherry
description: Dan Snaith’s joyous new album as Daphni lets its first-thought-best-thought spirit shine. Bar for bar, this might be the most fun there is to be had on a dance record this year.

title: Living Sky
description: A veteran of Sun Ra’s band of astral travelers, saxophonist and bandleader Marshall Allen carries on the jazz legend’s legacy of uplifting spirits and upending musical expectations.

title: En Är För Mycket och Tusen Aldrig Nog
description: The Swedish psych-rock pioneers’ songs are usually like odysseys, but their first full-length studio album in seven years is more of a pleasure cruise.

title: At Scaramouche
description: On their second collaborative album, the Toronto saxophonist and Vancouver singer find common ground in the beauty of mundane moments and minuscule gestures.

title: Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)
description: The Wu-Tang Clan’s debut album channeled their grimy New York roots and love of ’70s kung fu into an instant hip-hop classic, launching a sprawling and influential culture empire.

title: Wu-Tang Forever
description: The double-disc second album from all nine rappers can feel bloated and disjointed, but it is also the greatest distillation of the Wu at their most chaotic and functional.

title: Tical
description: Compared to the Wu-Tang Clan’s rowdy 36 Chambers and the canonized solo albums that followed it, Method Man’s solo debut is a reclusive, interior record, concerned primarily with securing refuge and dispatching threats.

title: Ironman
description: On his solo debut, Ghostface recreated the New York underworld of his adolescence in impressionistic fits over scythelike RZA beats. It is lean, vulgar, and irresistible.

title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
description: RZA made his first foray outside of hip-hop with a daring score for the 1999 Jim Jarmusch film about a lonely hitman. The movie plays like a melancholy requiem for the Wu-Tang’s golden era.

title: Let’s Have a Dream (1974 One Step Festival)
description: Released for the first time, a recording of the opening night of Ono’s 1974 Japanese tour captures her at her mischievous peak.

title: Blue Rev
description: The Toronto band’s third album is a triumph of power pop, a densely layered, blithe, and beautiful record that sets a new benchmark for the genre.

title: Hysteria
description: The Australian folk artist’s second album is glossier and broader than its predecessor, but the most stunning moments are still ones of hushed reverence.

title: Kiss the Ring
description: The New York City rapper heads upstate for a steely Westside Gunn production with all the hallmarks of a Griselda blockbuster.

title: Pocket Fantasy
description: On its second album, the Austin quartet balances complex, technical arrangements with playful moments of levity.

title: World Spirituality Classics 3: The Muslim Highlife of Alhaji Waziri Oshomah
description: The third volume in Luaka Bop’s World Spirituality Classics series spotlights a Nigerian musician who fuses traditional rhythms and pan-Nigerian highlife with the teachings of Islam.

title: Nymph
description: Sensuous, funny, and smartly produced, the London artist’s full-length debut transforms dusky electronic beats and trending pop sounds into a singular celebration of sexual agency.

title: I Got Issues
description: The veteran West Coast rapper toggles between kickback anthems and pertinent reflections on his life and growth, but he’s missing the hunger and innovation of his best work.

title: Makes Me Sick Makes Me Smile
description: Sabrina Fuentes’ debut album offers a flashback of adolescence in New York, filtering teenage themes through a studied imitation of ’90s grunge.

title: The Sun Still Seems to Move
description: Accompanied by cello, lap steel, and other acoustic instruments, the Philadelphia singer-songwriter creates abstract soundscapes that envelop even their loneliest songs in a soft, expansive warmth.

title: Entergalactic
description: Released in conjunction with an animated Netflix film, Kid Cudi’s latest is a pleasant surprise—a minor project that features some of his most purely enjoyable music in a decade.

title: $oul $old $eparately
description: Inviting producers like Kaytranada, James Blake, and DJ Paul into the fold offers a refreshing canvas for a rapper whose technical prowess and stark songwriting deserve a varied landscape to thrive in.

title: Dreamkiller
description: Producer Arthur Rizk’s band plays heavy metal in the traditional sense: catchy, operatic choruses and chugging riffs that you only need to hear once before you can air-guitar along.

title: The Will to Live
description: The New Jersey band’s seventh album is a hero’s journey powered by indomitable lifeforce and spirited, classic rock-inspired songwriting. It’s a rollicking good time and their best record in years.

title: Shebang
description: The experimental guitarist’s latest piece thrives on tension—between pulse and drone, repetition and variance, and, particularly, between the naturalism of the musicians’ playing and the artifice of the mix.

title: Spiderr
description: With celestial synth arrangements and heavy-lidded streams of consciousness, Bladee’s newest album offers a vision of pop that’s grounded in real emotion but shrouded in otherworldly mystery.

title: Solar Bridge
description: Newly reissued by Ghostly, this 2008 release from the influential experimental trio represents the zenith of their early drone excursions, and hints at the more meticulous compositions that were to come.

title: Doggerel
description: On the fourth album from their reunited lineup, the alt-rock lifers choose to embrace the slowing of their step.

title: The Bible
description: The latest from Kurt Wagner’s shapeshifting group is its darkest yet: a haunting ode to everyday American pain and the small ways we make it through.

title: Morbidity Triumphant
description: Energized by the presence of a new bassist, the death metal pioneers still stand apart from the pack.

title: Evergreen
description: The New York-based composer’s newest project with the Attacca Quartet highlights the significance of language while exploring the narrative potential of contemporary classical music.

title: Functional Designs
description: On his first album as Deepchord in four years, Rod Modell continues to refine his bustling, urban, singular take on dub techno.

title: The Charm of the Highway Strip
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Stephin Merrit’s 1994 meta-country album, an idiosyncratic, lo-fi travelogue bursting with gothic wit and pathos.

title: Older (Super Deluxe)
description: Arriving at a moment when his worldwide stardom was in eclipse, this 1996 album was the most daringly personal statement of George Michael’s career.

title: Fossora
description: With her 10th album, Björk is grounded back on earth, searching for hope in death, mushrooms, and matriarchy, and finding it in bass clarinet and gabber beats.

title: Diner Coffee
description: On an eerie new record, the anonymous collective strays from its metal roots and takes influence from jazz, telling stories of life on America’s class margins.

title: I Never Felt Nun
description: On his latest album, the Kentucky rapper addresses his demons head-on with startling bluntness and raw desperation.

title: Paradise of Replica
description: The Japanese avant-garde pop band strove to create a “sacred ambiance” on their second album, fusing unconventional arrangements with bouncing volleyballs and an eyes-wide air of wonder.

title: Cool It Down
description: The trio’s first album in nine years ushers in a patient new era for the band, gracefully shedding the electrifying hunger of its early days to make room for tempered joy.

title: The Hum Goes on Forever
description: The pop-punk band ages gracefully on a heart-achingly earnest record about parenthood.

title: Blending
description: The London quintet’s second album takes a softer approach to Britpop-infused post-punk and a more emotional perspective on working-class consciousness.

title: Last Spa on Earth
description: The Chicago-based band sheds its psychedelic garage-pop for intrepid experiments in reggaeton, synth-pop, and club music.

title: Languish Arts / Woeful Studies
description: The scars in Ka’s music come with lessons he feels duty-bound to pass on. The Brooklyn rapper’s two new albums set hard-earned wisdom to the lushest music of his career.

title: U Wasn’t There
description: The Harlem veteran’s long-promised collaboration with producer A-Trak is a laid-back shot of charisma.

title: Legendary
description: On his newest mixtape, the young Atlanta rapper succeeds at sounding like a one-note NBA YoungBoy and very little else of note.

title: Tyrannical Vibes
description: The New York singer-songwriter infuses aesthetics of indie pop with the rigor of his opera training. Sung by a small crew of friends, his cryptic lyrics feel like a snapshot of his social circle.

title: In These Times
description: The hybrid jazz drummer and producer’s latest album uses his familiar post-production techniques but feels more deftly orchestrated and rhythmically complex.

title: Est. 2003
description: Now two decades into his career, the Huddersfield native balances the brashness of bassline house with the swing of 2-step, demonstrating his own quiet mastery of UK garage’s many strands.

title: Running in Waves
description: Over flickering jungle breaks and gentle electronic soul, the London singer-songwriter who broke through with Anz’s ebullient “You Could Be” turns her focus inward.

title: Exister
description: Sharper songwriting, unbridled vocal performances, and more austere industrial textures give Luis Vasquez’s fifth album a new level of depth and candor.

title: Weather Alive
description: The eighth album from the English songwriter is the best work of her career. Soothing, immersive, and self-produced, it conjures a dreamlike atmosphere with songs that spiral out into the ether.

title: Still, Here
description: On an alternately deliberate and exploratory new record, the guitarist and composer finds flashes of beauty at the heart of each instrumental tale.

title: Harlequin
description: The Vienna-based singer and musician’s second album turns to high-concept cabaret pop, exuding a cool melancholy that complements its textured production.

title: Denim & Diamonds
description: Frank, honest, and irreverent, the songwriter’s fourth album attempts to subvert the should-bes of a woman making a country record.

title: SkinDiver
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a buried treasure, the 1989 experimental new age solo album from the R&B legend, a Black queer epic where technology mediates tenderness.

title: Yankee Hotel Foxtrot (Super Deluxe Edition)
description: A sprawling new box set full of demos and alternate takes suggests a dazzling array of paths the Chicago group might have taken on their masterpiece.

title: God Save the Animals
description: Placing its faith in the healing power of animals and Auto-Tune, Alex Giannascoli’s most hopeful record stands out for its grounded patience and moments of sharp lyrical simplicity.

title: Girl of My Dreams
description: On her debut album, Fletcher aims to champion vulnerability in queer love. Instead, she delivers generic, one-dimensional pop anthems that never fully articulate her experience of love and heartbreak.

title: Moss
description: The minimalist acoustic palette of the 24-year-old actor and singer’s second album makes a calming backdrop for her diaristic songwriting and white-smoke soprano.

title: Music for Animals
description: Trading his customary piano for a mostly electronic palette, the Berlin composer conjures an air of stillness and solitude. The results are both meditative and, at three hours long, sprawling.

title: The Mars Volta
description: On the duo’s first album in 10 years, Omar Rodríguez-López and Cedric Bixler-Zavala mellow out, abandoning their unhinged prog opuses for a kind of airy, Caribbean yacht rock.

title: Decide
description: On his second solo album, Stranger Things actor Joe Keery fights his way through the simulation with winking, off-kilter synth-pop.

title: Darklife
description: On a new double album, the experimental collective continues its journey from vaporwave toward fractured, maximalist pop music.

title: Shepherd Head
description: Following the dissolution of the group’s lineup, founding member John Rossiter plays alone for the first time, working up an intimate set of songs using just mic, laptop, and field recordings.

title: Asphalt Meadows
description: At last, the band’s 10th album restores their creative momentum. If the songs don’t feel as lived-in, at least they unlock the repressed memory of what it was like to be deeply moved by Death Cab for Cutie.

title: Born Pink
description: The K-pop quartet’s highly anticipated second album leans into an image of authority that’s undercut by familiar ideas and stale musical concepts.

title: Heaven Is No Fun
description: The New Orleans-based punk artist crafts broad caricatures of chaos and destruction with giddy hooks, flashy musicianship, and self-mythologizing humor.

title: ♡ EP
description: Pairing the Colombian singer’s voice with the New York producer’s wistful electronic hybrids, this brief but endearing EP feels like a set of missives sent from the depths of a daydream.

title: demon time
description: The London producer loosens the reins for a guest-heavy, party-starting album that doesn’t feel pressured to do or say too much.

title: That’s What Happened 1982-1985: The Bootleg Series Vol. 7
description: A new three-disc set surveys the trumpeter’s most critically reviled era. The unreleased studio material is a mixed bag, but a 1983 live recording is revelatory.

title: The Trouble With Fever
description: The musical output of Michelle Branch and Patrick Carney’s embattled partnership suffers from muddled songwriting and meandering arrangements.

title: (Self-Titled)
description: With production from Blake Mills, the Mumford & Sons frontman goes solo with a hushed, searching record anchored in trauma.

title: SPARK
description: The Chicago duo’s inert new album has a gorgeous sound, but it comes at the cost of depth and spontaneity.

title: When the Wind Forgets Your Name
description: Dotted with cool surprises and intricately plotted melodies, the veteran indie band’s Sub Pop debut shakes things up without breaking their pattern of low-key, late-period releases.

title: Mosquito
description: The Brazilian-born, Amsterdam-based producer’s new mixtape presents shapeshifting, pop-minded club tracks that showcase her dense production and versatile singing.

title: Beauty Is Useless
description: Pairing undulating synthesizers with cycling grooves, the Bay Area electronic musician’s first album in 14 years calls back to the ambient techno of the late 1990s.

title: Houdini
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the major-label debut from the sludge-metal pioneers, an album that marked their transition from rockers to experimentalists.

title: Words & Music, May 1965
description: Featuring the earliest known renditions of several Velvet Underground classics, this archival set of acoustic demos highlights a formative period in Lou Reed and John Cale’s artistic partnership.

title: Hold the Girl
description: Seeking empathy for a younger self, Rina Sawayama’s second album pirouettes through pop-punk and power ballads, trance and stadium rock. It’s ambitious in the same way as putting on all the clothes in your closet.

title: Expert in a Dying Field
description: The third album from the New Zealand quartet blends openhearted lyrics about post-breakup regret with a sugar-rush immediacy and a craftsman-like attention to detail.

title: People Helping People
description: The LA duo’s sixth album is notably abstract and eccentric, showcasing a renewed sense of possibility.

title: Butcher Brown Presents Triple Trey
description: The collective’s new album is their most focused yet, possessing the soul of a beat tape and the larger-than-life feel of big band jazz.

title: Demons Protected by Angels
description: The Canadian rapper’s latest album finds moments of real depth and humanity. The rest of the time, his verses register as monotonous and tame, his energy dictated by A-list collaborators.

title: age/sex/location
description: Grown, sexy, and horny on main, the Dreamville singer’s second album pursues pleasure without compromising on self-love.

title: Lyfë
description: Rage rap can be rote and exhausting, but in small doses—like on the Portland rapper’s new pared-down and hypnotic album—the style can be ridiculous fun, electrifying, and hyperreal.

title: Hydration
description: The Japanese ambient artist’s new album is an immersive textural exercise that demands full use of the senses. It is some of his most magnetic work yet.

title: Legend
description: On an 81-minute double album, the EGOT singer-songwriter enlists an impressive roster of guests to help bring more fun—and funk—to his music than he has in years.

title: Arrangements
description: Grim, grey, and dour, the Canadian band’s fourth album offers a bleak look at the world and delivers some new textures but lacks some of the musical tension to really create sparks.

title: Jingul
description: A revered musician in Balochistan, Pakistan, Ustad Noor Bahksh debuts internationally with a twangy, enveloping collection of reinterpreted and original compositions for the benju.

title: 2007 EP
description: The Los Angeles-based pop singer's new EP plunges into her psyche with quiet desperation, producing some of her most vulnerable music yet.

title: Spirituals
description: On her first album in six years, Santigold reimagines the type of music that can comfort people in times of grief and stagnation.

title: Hideous Bastard
description: The solo debut from the xx vocalist is a quiet work of personal exploration. Rife with growing pains, it occasionally hints at real beauty.

title: Andrew McIntosh: Little Jimmy
description: The piano-and-percussion quartet performs a series of pieces by the Los Angeles composer that wrestle with the aftermath of 2020’s wildfires; McIntosh’s own field recordings flesh out a sense of place.

title: Krökta Tankar och Brända Vanor
description: Gothenburg trio Amateur Hour translate their hometown’s DIY ethos into an hour-long dream-pop epic, balancing lo-fi scuzz with welcoming intimacy.

title: Natural Brown Prom Queen
description: With daring lyricism and technical ingenuity, singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Brittney Parks’ second album conjures a frenzied energy as emotionally soothing as it is physically crushing.

title: As Above, So Below
description: The rapper continues to explore identity and belonging on her second album. Recorded in her native Zambia, it folds together zamrock, polyrhythmic percussion, and choral harmonies.

title: Dimensional Bleed
description: With a slightly subtler approach, the post-metal band relies on familiar tricks, gesturing at widescreen emotions in an endless sea of sine wave swells.

title: Invisibility Is an Unnatural Disaster
description: The jazz supergroup of free-improvising heavyweights—Patrick Shiroishi, Jessica Ackerley, Chris Williams, Luke Stewart, and Jason Nazary—veers between frenetic roar and microscopic textures.

title: Nothing’s Shocking
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the Los Angeles band’s 1988 debut, which infused the nascent alt-rock movement with a surreal vision of Hollywood hedonism.

title: Step on Step
description: Famous for his widescreen imagination, the legendary R&B producer and arranger helped define Chicago soul. This anthology of home recordings uncovered by his daughters reveals his more intimate side.

title: Clouds of Joy
description: Enthusiastic, meticulous, and decidedly analog, Clouds of Joy is AM radio music for a late ’70s moment that may only exist in bandleader Max Turnbull’s imagination.

title: How Do You Burn?
description: Greg Dulli and co. return with an eclectic, haunted set that feels untethered to their past work. They seem less interested in living up to expectations than upending them.

title: My Boy
description: With actorly affect and an Orbinsonesque croon, the New Zealand singer-songwriter uses the bright, artificial gloss of 1980s pop to evoke an uncanny, self-protective brand of masculinity.

title: Two Sisters
description: On her new album, the Canadian artist collages 18th-century pipe organs and cavernous drone music. It is a dark encounter between the past and present, revealing the full range of her gifts as a composer.

title: White Girl Wasted
description: With appearances from MF Doom, Jay Electronica, Madlib, and DJ Premier, the full-length collaborative debut from the rapper and producer is a nostalgic ode to druggy hedonism and classic boom-bap.

title: I Love You Jennifer B
description: The full-length debut from the shapeshifting UK duo is a virtuosic display of theatrical mayhem, dazzling production, and surprisingly lustrous pop music.

title: Good Movie
description: On his third solo album, the New York producer finally proves he’s a proficient rapper, but his audacious beats take a backseat in the process.

title: Yungblud
description: The English singer’s third album promises eccentricity and personal revelation but delivers anonymous, uninspired pop-rock.

title: Diagonals
description: Nineties heads know Chicago’s Jamie Hodge for his leftfield productions on Plus 8 and Source. Sifting through his old DATs, Demdike Stare came up with a grip of vintage ambient-techno abstractions.

title: Louie
description: An in-demand beatmaker who has worked with Denzel Curry, Vince Staples, and more, the producer finally releases his solo debut—a dynamic record bursting with soul samples and complicated emotions.

title: God Did
description: DJ Khaled is a savvy curator; too often, that’s all he is. His latest collection of star-studded rap party bangers offers the rare opportunity to isolate what, exactly, he adds to a track.

title: Black Vladimir
description: Buffalo producer Daringer’s austere music spotlights Meyhem Lauren’s phonetic idiosyncrasies. For the first time in years, the Queens rapper is an unequivocal headliner.

title: Carpet Cocoon
description: Following her ambient collaboration with Cole Pulice earlier this year, Lynn Avery’s newly reissued 2020 LP is charmingly offbeat and shrouded in snowy intimacy.

title: Bajascillators
description: The Chicago psych trio’s loops and layers seem to play tricks on time: Long songs fly by quickly, and short pieces feel expansive.

title: Separation
description: The Philadelphia musician’s new album resembles the indelible emotional resonance of a dream, allowing his idiosyncrasies as a storyteller to shine.

title: MTV
description: On his fifth album, the Portland power-pop musician embraces a spontaneous, home-recorded approach that exudes a playful charm.

title: Guilty Pleasure
description: The Hartford, Connecticut five-piece repurpose what many consider the worst parts of 2000s scene culture and rap-rock into a 22-minute ode to unpretentiousness.

title: Guy
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Guy’s self-titled debut, the album that solidified the sound of new jack swing and established Teddy Riley as the most influential R&B producer of the late 1980s.

title: Pulse of the Early Brain (Switched On, Vol. 5)
description: The avant-pop group offers a comprehensive if inessential career overview on what may be the final edition of its long-running compilation series.

title: Heaven Come Crashing
description: The Brooklyn composer injects the ambient wash of her past work with flashes of dancefloor emotionality, striking a balance between reflective contemplation and the ego-melting thrills of a warehouse party.

title: Whipped Stream and Other Earthly Delights
description: Indulgent, arcane, and often hilarious, the Ohio noise-jazz improvisers’ new three-and-a-half-hour cassette collection is too weird to be boring.

title: Keep On Smiling
description: Efficient and impersonal, the rock band’s latest album is filled with sunny-side platitudes and peppy tempos that scan as forced fun.

title: Sides
description: The Virginia duo’s sparse, meditative indie folk songs grapple with the impermanence of life and the disorientation of grief, evoking an aching stillness.

title: Someday Is Today
description: The Canadian band’s third album is a wistful and familiar soundtrack to winter malaise.

title: The Forever Story
description: The Atlanta rapper’s latest LP is an ambitious and overwhelming experience, a bridge between his upbringing and his place within hip-hop canon and Black history at large.

title: Dollar Menu 4
description: Variously lively and listless, the latest entry in Mach-Hommy and Tha God Fahim’s Dollar Menu series highlights the flaws in the formula even as it celebrates their bond.

title: Touch the Lock
description: The Parisian duo’s debut full-length harnesses controlled chaos, offering an engrossing introduction to their prismatic synth pop.

title: Music for Four Guitars
description: The veteran improviser creates a virtual quartet indebted to classical minimalism and avant-garde guitar ensembles, sculpting multitracked figures into complex systems.

title: Will of the People
description: Working under the auspices of another vague, dystopian narrative, the UK band slaps a shiny new label on the grafted remains of better songs and calls it the ninth Muse album.

title: honeybee table at the butterfly feast
description: Teen Suicide return with a sprawling new album that meditates on the anxiety and indifference of love and mortality.

title: Context
description: The prolific Norwegian producer and electronic musician explores space and silence on a pair of powerful, absorbing records—one solo, the other with experimental metal vocalist Runhild Gammelsæter.

title: Icarus EP
description: Balancing the familiar sweetness of her vocals against bruised club beats, the debut EP from Kero Kero Bonito’s Sarah Midori Perry traverses newly dark emotional terrain.

A new box set collects the singer-songwriter’s 2001 debut alongside a set of live recordings from her early days in New York, showcasing the intimate performance style and vivid, theatrical lyrics that ignited her career.

title: Garden Gaia
description: On Pantha du Prince’s sixth album, the organic tumult is so thick that electronic tones and rhythms bend and buckle around it.

title: A Spirit Appears to a Pair of Lovers
description: The New York curator and multimedia artist uses droning Farfisa organs and arpeggiated synths to tap into a tripped-out spirit of wonder.

title: Significant Soil
description: Kansas City producer Iggy Romeu’s strange, evocative second album for West Mineral feels so divorced from musical convention, there’s the thrilling sense that anything could happen.

title: The Elephant Man’s Bones
description: Toned down but no less penitent, nostalgic but ready to stake a claim to a new future, the duo’s long-awaited full-length is one of the most indulgently sinister rap records of the year.

title: Let’s Turn It Into Sound
description: With tangled, stop-start arrangements that open to unexpected trap doors, the composer and synthesizer musician brings playfulness to the fore. You might call this her “pop” album.

title: Broken Gargoyles
description: Based upon early 1900s German poetry about sick patients and maimed soldiers, these two side-long tracks of experimental vocalizations highlight the singer’s conceptual, confrontational heft.

title: Evolution Here We Come
description: Taking influence from the rock music of the early 1980s, the experimental guitarist settles into the role of a traditional frontman on a sharp, guest-heavy new record.

title: Duty Now for the Future
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a spirited but uneven salvo from the Ohio pranksters’ campaign to reprogram American minds.

title: Against the Odds: 1974 - 1982
description: A new archival box set collecting Blondie’s first six albums and assorted rarities and outtakes makes the case for their singular presence in American music.

title: Pre Pleasure
description: The Australian songwriter’s empathetic, understated rock songs sift through a litany of relationships and beliefs, seeking a balance between thinking about life and actually living it.

title: The Painter
description: An icon of ’90s pop-dance crossover who produced Madonna’s Ray of Light, the UK musician returns with his first album in eight years, but the record’s endless-sunset vibes quickly turn cloying.

title: All of Us Flames
description: Returning to familiar sounds of vintage girl groups and rock’n’roll, Ezra Furman writes trans pride and existential fear into an album that feels like her most complete picture yet.

title: From There / To Here: UK / US Recordings 1974-1982
description: Animated by a sense of endless potential and patchwork charm, a new box set collects the influential British songwriter’s work during a transitional period.

title: Earth Patterns
description: On its most cohesive album to date, the improvisatory jazz trio finds new power in silence and restraint.

title: Flood
description: Grounding her second album in moments of real vulnerability, the Australian singer-songwriter zeroes in on her guiding concern as a musician: how we seek and create safety.

title: Killer in Neverland
description: Blending melodic rap, explosive pop-punk, and languid electro-pop, the Japanese singer and producer’s adventurous new album is fueled by an impassioned wish to escape reality.

title: Duo Geloso
description: Performing live in 1987, the avant-garde composers extracted complexity from simple designs and novel instrumentation. A new release captures their meditative and playful collaboration.

title: Pillow Talk
description: Collaborating with producer Hitmaka, the R&B artist abandons her concept-album ambitions for a free-flowing collage of simple, irresistible pleasures.

title: Greatest Hits ’88 - ’16
description: This collaboration between Arca and Shayne Oliver looks back at a scene where queer and trans artists of color birthed avant-garde club sounds that continue to hold sway today.

title: V O R T E X
description: The debut full-length from the celebrated filmmaker collages genres with abstract ambition, but it often lands with unnerving headiness.

title: How Do I Get That Star
description: Brooklyn songwriter Zannie Owens’ debut is a loose concept album about a lost alien—and an opaque inquiry into the shifting nature of reality.

title: Gnosis
description: On its dauntless and electrifying eighth album, the post-metal trio recharges its familiar sound.

title: Freakout/Release
description: Treating music as something like a homeopathic remedy, Freakout/Release joins doubt with deliverance over the cleansing pulse of a disco beat.

title: Bleed Out
description: John Darnielle’s band returns to visceral guitar-rock directness for a collection of songs that embrace and humanize the familiar tropes of action cinema.

title: 90 in November
description: Led by singer-songwriter Blair Howerton, the debut from the sun-baked indie band sounds cozy but yearns for open spaces.

title: Spaceships on the Blade
description: The San Francisco rapper’s laid-back presence is the perfect foil to tales of luxury rides and big-money moves. On his latest album, he slips into a more romantic mode.

title: Heartmind
description: Across a casually sublime album, Cass McCombs is at his most confident and intentional, constantly returning to the imagery of music and the casualties of a life devoted to making and sharing art.

title: Au Suisse
description: Morgan Geist and Mike Kelley’s first outing as a duo takes in a broad sweep of early-’80s reference points—disco, new romantic, sophistipop—that come together in an opalescent swirl.

title: Eli Winter
description: Joined by an illustrious lineup of players including Yasmin Williams, Ryley Walker, and jaimie branch, the Chicago-based guitarist constructs wistful, evocative psychic landscapes.

title: Physical Thrills
description: It’s no return to form, but the alt-rock band’s sixth album taps into a well of quarantine-bound inspiration for some of their most varied and carefree songs in over a decade.

title: Squeezing Out Sparks
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit an underappreciated icon of new wave and his best album, a clinic in lean, sardonic, emotive pop songwriting.

title: Unravelled: 1981-2002
description: The New Zealand duo of Chris Knox and Alec Bathgate have influenced generations of lo-fi rockers. This 55-track box set reminds us why.

title: Holy Fvck
description: Demi Lovato has long sung about rebirth. On Holy Fvck, she enacts it by jettisoning the pop-R&B palette that has defined her records for a decade.

title: Was It Ever Real?
description: On his latest EP as the Soft Pink Truth, Drew Daniel of Matmos offers a luxe version of deep house that leans into the carnal qualities of club music.

title: Success
description: The long-running experimental band ends the longest gap of its career with a set of urgent, direct, and celebratory songs.

title: Profound Mysteries II
description: The Norwegian duo sets out to honor their forebears in electronic music, but they end up falling back on derivative, uninspired clichés.

title: Only Built 4 Diamond Links
description: Following his release from jail, the Michigan rapper expands the aperture of his street tales with cinematic storytelling and post-prison clarity.

title: Get Fucked
