description: In addition to eight previously unreleased songs, this double LP remixes and remasters two early albums born from the macabre, witty, and wonderful mind of Sadie Dupuis.

title: An Evening With Silk Sonic
description: Bruno Mars and Anderson .Paak’s faithful and loving ode to ’70s R&B has a distinctly light touch, which works both for and against the project.

title: In Virus Times EP
description: A brief EP from the Sonic Youth guitarist features ruminative, unadorned acoustic performances that convey a sense of anxiety and perseverance.

title: Why Look Up, God’s in the Mirror
description: A synthesis of outerborough album rap, Five-Percenter ideology, and Southern Gothic interiority, the Memphis native’s latest album is a somber reflection on the place that made him.

title: On the Edge
description: The Berlin-based duo of Errorsmith and Fiedel push toward the extreme lower limits of danceability on a debut LP that’s stranger, woozier, and slower than anything they’ve made before.

title: Garbology
description: Backed by Blockhead’s spare production, the Long Island-bred rapper continues his creative evolution, writing more incisively about himself than ever before.

title: Doran
description: Recorded in a Virginia mountain town named Rural Retreat, the debut from this quartet of fringe-folk veterans beautifully articulates the weirdness and magic of life outside of the city.

title: Engine of Hell
description: With sparse acoustic arrangements and cryptic lyrics, the songwriter’s fifth solo album feels like a series of intimate dispatches from a personal purgatory.

title: Red (Taylor’s Version)
description: Re-recorded in meticulous detail, along with a dozen songs cut from the 2012 original, Taylor Swift’s most pivotal album has still more to say about growing up and moving forward.

title: Silk Degrees
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Boz Scaggs’ 1976 hit album, a record whose ineffable tragicomedy called for its own system of measurement.

title: Rhythm and Paranoia: The Best of Bush Tetras
description: This 3xLP box set surveys the influential New York group’s long career, reinforcing their post-punk bona fides and tracing their evolution over the course of four decades.

title: Slave to the Scalpel
description: With a pitch-black sense of humor, the Cleveland death metal quartet boils the genre down to its essence but lands just shy of its potential.

title: Things Take Time, Take Time
description: The Australian singer-songwriter’s fourth album has the directness of a collection of demos. Barnett sounds characteristically laconic; she’s at her best when she lets her guitar take the lead.

title: Public Storage
description: The Los Angeles singer and songwriter’s full-length debut is grandiose and opaque, opting for intricacy over intimacy.

title: Yellow Tape 2
description: The sequel to the Memphis rapper’s 2020 tape embodies the spirit of Southern rap without trading in nostalgic aesthetics or noticeable samples.

title: Pluperfect Mind
description: Exploring the concept of “queer time,” classically trained musician Isabelle Thorn crafts a prodigiously ambitious, suite-like album that never quite rests.

title: Zigzag Wombat
description: The Brooklyn art rock trio’s choppy harmonies and sweetly free-associative tunes are a little bit freaky and more than a little bit funny.

title: Lee “Scratch” Perry’s Guide to the Universe
description: In one of his final recorded appearances, the late dub visionary trades the mixing desk for the mic on an album fusing parallel strains of heavy, psychedelic music.

title: Make Drunk Cool Again
description: While the rapper’s latest of multiple releases this year is too scattershot to sustain itself as a project, he’s landing more darts on the board than usual, and it’s fun to hear him experiment.

title: Rhinestones
description: Over the past decade, the Melbourne group’s music has grown lighter, gentler, and more inviting with every release. Here, they trade their minimal-wave roots for unexpected forays into gothic country.

title: 9 Airs
description: The Welsh electronic musician continues his run of home-listening albums with a quiet, unassuming record that splits the difference between low-key dance music and ethereal ambient.

title: Christfucker
description: Channeling slasher flicks and Dante’s Inferno, the Austin band’s second album of 2021 is a roiling cauldron of scorched-earth sludge and hardcore that doesn’t take itself too seriously.

title: Still Over It
description: With her latest album, the singer cements herself as one of R&B’s most relatable storytellers, with an ear for melodrama that becomes monotonous. The best moments capture her soulfulness alongside her fury.

title: Thank You
description: The singer’s first album in 15 years casts a fond glance back at the vintage sounds she made her name with, but a few new songs—including a Jack Antonoff production—bring her back to the present day.

title: Elephant in the Room
description: The fiercely ambitious Chicago rapper turns in a scattered, familiar collection, ditching the epic scope of his past releases and sticking to what works.

title: both feet en th infinite
description: Isolating the rhythm at the center of their work and tapping into a new physicality, the Washington, D.C. experimental duo find joy in improvisation and liberation in the body.

title: Vi/deo
description: Liz Wendelbo and Sean McBride remain committed to their tactile brand of minimal synth with a set of nostalgic rhapsodies that embrace a newfound warmth.

title: Absolutely
description: The roaming, Americana-obsessed songwriter brings a sense of purpose to his zigzagging on his debut album, a collaborator-filled collection of heartbreak tales.

title: Hyd EP
description: Once best known best as the cryptic PC Music character QT, Hayden Dunham returns with an updated electro-pop sound that strips away some of the artifice from their previous project.

title: Preserved in Torment
description: On the Olympia death/doom band’s unrelenting second album, everything sounds beefier. This music grabs you by the shoulders and shakes you to attention.

title: Inglish
description: With an ambitious fusion of Hindustani classical, progressive rock, and jazz, the New York-based guitarist and composer offers an expansive, egalitarian vision of identity and belonging.

title: Women in Technology
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Jyoti Mishra’s 1997 major-label debut, a collection of tender homemade synth-pop that spawned an unlikely global hit.

title: New Adventures in Hi-Fi (25th Anniversary Edition)
description: R.E.M.’s most unstable album never quite arrives in any one sound for more than a track at a time. Born of a chaotic and stressful tour, it translated not only the energy of their shows but the transience and unreality of life on the road.

title: Voyage
description: Returning with their first new album in 40 years, the Swedish pop titans attempt the seemingly impossible: balancing the lure of nostalgia with the pull of the present day. Amazingly, they pull it off.

title: Raw Demoon Alchemy (A Lone Operation)
description: The New York saxophonist’s breakup album subverts what we’ve come to expect from the genre. Covering songs by Ornette Coleman, Sun Ra, and others, he finds new emotions in familiar songs.

title: Arm’s Length EP
description: The London producer’s second EP of the year is a nebulous collage of lo-fi R&B, hip-hop, and electronic. It feels like a sketchbook of ideas in search of their final forms.

title: Kid A Mnesia
description: At the turn of the century, Radiohead released two albums that forever altered their identity. Now, Kid A and Amnesiac are reissued as a pair, along with whatever worthy B-sides, alternate versions, and outtakes they can find.

title: Projector
description: With impressive performances and a few promising moments, the young Brooklyn post-punk band clearly knows all the right moves—but it’s hard to tell what moves them.

title: Pohorylle
description: The debut album from the Pacific Northwest country songwriter showcases her distinct personality with vivid lyrics and lovely, thoughtful arrangements.

title: Valentine
description: Lindsey Jordan’s exquisite second album documents love in all stages, but mostly in disrepair. She takes on a larger and poppier sound while keeping her songwriting dazzlingly sharp and passionate.

title: HOUSE OF CONFUSION
description: On his latest album of country-influenced indie rock, Dave Benton takes surprising, subtle turns in songs of indecision, introspection, and alienation.

title: Soul Controller
description: Highlighting a new corner of Michigan rap, this mixtape from the Grand Rapids rapper is a sustained rush of adrenaline that rarely loses steam.

title: Candy Racer
description: The J-pop icon and hyperpop predecessor returns with an album that looks forward even as it longs for an imagined past.

title: The Path of the Clouds
description: Inspired by true crime and accompanied by Mary Lattimore, Emma Ruth Rundle, and others, the gothic songwriter’s latest feels newly textured and symphonic.

title: Something for Thee Hotties
description: With her latest batch of unreleased freestyles and loosies, the Houston rapper reminds the world that breathless raps are her foundation.

title: Mandatory Enjoyment
description: The Los Angeles band nods to various corners of psychedelic music while transcending its influences on this blissful and spacious debut album.
Ed Sheeran is older now; he’s married and newly a father. With all this change comes a new set of trite observations about love, life, and partying amid anonymous and synthetic pop music.

title: Lily We Need to Talk Now
description: On her debut album, the New York polymath roams free across a map of the last 50 years of contemporary pop music, leading to her most accessible and purposeful record to date.

title: Reticence / Resistance
description: Recorded over two nights at London’s Café Oto in 2017, this live performance from the group showcases the band’s unique ability to fuse folk traditionalism with drone experimentation.

title: im hole
description: The boundless debut from the London-based artist is a delirious tug of war between pleasure and unease, shuttling between club sounds and psychedelic mind states with a steely, unbridled intensity.

title: Extropy
description: On the third album of an astronomically-inspired trilogy, the German producer suspends lonely, isolated instruments within a sweeping cosmos. It sounds appropriately epic and a little vacant.

title: Collected Pieces II
description: A companion piece to last year’s sparkling Silver Ladders, the harpist’s latest dip into her archives assembles improvised sessions into intricately layered songs with a powerful emotional pull.

title: Intra-I
description: Inviting guest vocalists into his fold for the first time, the London tuba player delivers a collection of taut pop songs deeply rooted in Afro-Caribbean soundsystem culture.

title: Come on Over
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Shania Twain’s 1997 blockbuster, one that showed the world the power of a true pop-country crossover.

title: Petunia
description: With a newfound sense of melancholy, the Florida jam duo has crafted its tightest studio album without losing the ambling spirit that fuels its live performances.

title: Quivering in Time
description: Born of impromptu DJ sets broadcast from a forest clearing in New Hampshire, Drew’s latest album distills decades of dance-music history into an hour of joyous new standards.

title: Far In
description: The follow-up to 2019’s This Is How You Smile is mellower and breezier than its predecessor; it feels less like a tour of Roberto Carlos Lange’s psyche than an afternoon barbecue in his backyard.

title: Hushed and Grim
description: The Atlanta metal band’s new double album is its least ambitious collection yet: an inoffensive, occasionally alluring, but overwhelmingly dull 90-minute slog.

title: I Don’t Live Here Anymore
description: The fifth album from Adam Granduciel and co. chips away some of their hazier edges in favor of sharper melodies, broadening the borders of the meticulous yet joyously simple sound he has perfected.

title: Love Black
description: The Atlanta rapper’s new album swings seamlessly from upbeat to disruptive without being one-note. It’s her best work yet.

title: Crossover EP
description: Transforming their past solemnity into swaggering confidence, the Minneapolis-based singer-songwriter and rapper returns with an EP of thunderous club music.

title: LP!
description: Though just as charged and confrontational as any of his other projects, the rapper’s latest album is uninhibited and proud of it.

title: B-Sides & Rarities (Part II)
description: Culled from a period of intense musical transition over the past decade-plus, these 27 songs offer an alternate window into the songwriter’s depravity and anxiety—and the quest to overcome both.

title: Actually, You Can
description: Through a collection of songs that range from anxious garage funk to mercurial power pop, the San Francisco experimentalists argue for an urgent remaking of the world.

title: Fun House
description: With stark, introspective lyrics and fuller production, Meg Duffy’s latest is a bold foray into poppier sounds. It feels like a fresh start.

title: A Love Supreme: Live in Seattle
description: A previously unknown recording from a small Seattle club in 1965 documents one of the saxophonist’s signature works—spiritual, searching, unstoppable—as never heard before.

title: My Morning Jacket
description: Concentrating hours of freeform takes into the baggy shape of 11 songs, My Morning Jacket’s ninth LP achieves the dubious goal of nailing a “jam band album” on the first try.

title: -io
description: Accompanied by strings, horns, and more, Haley Fohr has crafted her most expansive work to date, capturing a sprawl of emotions too complicated to be named.

title: Shade
description: Recorded over the last 15 years, and alternating between stripped-down folk and thickets of distortion, Shade takes Grouper’s careful balance between intimacy and inscrutability to a new extreme.

title: Lull
description: Writing for string octet plus soloists Nate Wooley and Brian Chase, the New York composer’s work is rooted in the ways that sound absorbed by the body can both reflect and influence emotional states.

title: Is It Time to Eat the Rich Yet?
description: The Chennai quartet are indie-rock revival survivors making an overdue play for international recognition. Their latest EP is packed with sunlit synths, neon grooves, and upbeat pop melodies.

title: Big Bend (An Original Soundtrack for Public Television)
description: On its first soundtrack in seven years, the Texas band mirrors the subtle landscape and beauty of the national park that the namesake documentary captures.

title: Source ⧺ We Move
description: Drawing on UK dance music, experimental R&B, and hip-hop, this remix album to the London saxophonist’s kaleidoscopic jazz record expands on the eclectic universe of the original.

title: Sympathy for Life
description: With sincere, resolute songwriting and a more accessible sound, the latest album from the New York quartet feels more suited than ever for the ecstasy of a crowded club.

title: Ookii Gekkou
description: Propelled by Valentina Magaletti’s masterful drumming and assisted by collaborators like Stereolab’s Laetitia Sadier, the London group ventures further into its utopian parallel universe.

title: Combat Rock
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the Clash’s famously complicated fifth album that contains some of their biggest songs as well as their moodiest and most impenetrable material.

title: Una Rosa
description: The singer-songwriter’s latest album is steeped in Caribbean texts that have influenced her musicianship. In its shades of love and grief, it sounds like life as it arrives.

title: Fast Idol
description: Chris Stewart continues his decade-long quest to rewrite ’80s synth-pop on his latest record, an enjoyable homage that struggles to reach the heights of its influences.

title: City of Mirrors
description: Approaching the rich Latinx musical tradition from intriguing new angles, the Chicago quintet’s album evokes the crisp air, soft color, and enveloping warmth of a greenhouse.

title: Blue Banisters
description: Lana Del Rey’s second album of the year is a sweeping survey of her talent as a songwriter, stripped of the aesthetic borders she often places around her work.

title: Heartbeats
description: The breakout star of the regional subgenre known as Jersey club harnesses its familiar driving grooves and libidinal energy while pushing the style forward with new sounds and moods.

title: Chameleon
description: On his first album in two years, the New York producer applies an exploratory approach to ambient techno, utilizing elements of dub and post-punk to sculpt a record that feels meditative but never maudlin.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: On their first official mix album, the Lawrence brothers broaden their horizons, focusing on a selection of classic-sounding house. It’s a far more intimate vibe than their festival-stage fare.

title: A Tear in the Fabric of Life
description: Citing death metal and Phil Spector as influences, the Kentucky metalcore band turn in an absurdly heavy EP that tells an even heavier story about death and grief.

title: Punk
description: While Young Thug’s creative choices after about 2015 have had little sway over emerging trends, Punk suggests that the place he now occupies is one that allows him more room to experiment.

title: Wayfinder
description: With a focus on the minutiae of grief and heartbreak, the latest album from songwriter Taylor Vick nestles wry, careful lyrics into quiet arrangements that reward close listening.

title: Eternal Home
description: An 80-minute epic blending screamo, jazz, prog rock, IDM, and more, the latest from producer Angel Marcloid offers some of her most focused and welcoming material amid the chaos.

title: Simple, Sweet, and Smiling
description: The Los Angeles singer-songwriter’s charming third album is full of recurring worries, but her nods to ’80s synth pop and adult contemporary imbue the music with a sense of lightness.

title: shut the fuck up talking to me
description: On his debut album, Zack Fox doubles down on the joke rap shtick, resulting in a collection of tracks that is as disjointed as it is unfunny.

title: High Dragon and Universe
description: The debut EP from the rising hyperpop artist is exhilarating and unabashedly silly but falters when adhering to genre conventions and trends.

title: Weight of the World
description: Every aspect of the Texas rapper’s personality locks into place on his latest album, the most deeply personal statement of his career.

title: Pins and Needles
description: On her second album, a country singer-songwriter accustomed to crafting songs for artists like Miranda Lambert and Lee Ann Womack finds her own voice.

title: Juno
description: In the California pop singer-songwriter’s bright, hallucinogenic world, everything glows in the dark and almost every chorus is chanted.

title: All Hours EP
description: Across six tracks channeling vintage freestyle, electro, UK garage, Baltimore club, and more, the Manchester producer pays tribute to dance music at its most joyful.

title: Sediments We Move
description: A stirring composite of choral hymns, progressive rock, and free jazz, the Brooklyn composer’s suite presents a fluid cycle of matter as sound.

title: Optimist
description: Without any of the gothic production flourishes that put him on the map, the producer and songwriter’s latest album is gloomy, on edge, and disappointingly hollow.

title: Georgia Blue
description: Released for charity, this star-studded covers album celebrates music from the state of Georgia. It is a joyful affair with sadness lurking in the shadows.

title: Seal
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Seal’s 1991 debut, a luxurious album that grew out of the UK rave scene and took his inimitable voice to the world.

title: Let It Be (Super Deluxe)
description: A new reissue of Let It Be includes four discs of live material, demos, alternate takes, and lost mixes, shining a light on the brilliant and tumultuous process of what would become the Beatles’ final album.

title: Trying Not to Think About It
description: On her rawest and most cohesive project to date, the pop singer explores themes of depression and anxiety but too often relies on familiar imagery.

title: A Night at the Little Los Angeles
description: Lo-fi and languid, these 4-track demos for 2020’s Sundowner offer an illuminating window into the songwriter’s creative process.

title: to hell with it
description: The 20-year-old UK producer broke out on TikTok with snippet-sized songs that ache with nostalgia for the recent past. Her intimate, lived-in music succeeds where cheaper imitations fail.

title: Why Do Birds Sing? (Deluxe Edition)
description: Released in 1991, the Milwaukee trio’s fifth album marked a return to the misfit anthems that had made the Femmes cult heroes in the first place.

title: Ekphrasis
description: The rap duo’s latest project fits neatly into the stately traditionalism currently dominating the independent scene.

title: Music of the Spheres
description: Here he goes again, looking at the stars, seeing how they shine.

title: I Want the Door to Open
description: Pairing her simple, unaffected vocal style with carefully synthesized arrangements, the Chicago-based musician departs from her indie-rock foundations in search of musical and personal freedom.

title: Mercurial World
description: Mica Tenenbaum and Matthew Lewin’s fuzzy, rococo synthpop confections have a magic power: They sound like whatever you grew up with, whenever that was.

title: Life of a DON
description: The Texas rapper’s latest album sounds so damn good that the emptiness of it all is an afterthought.

title: Garden of Burning Apparitions
description: Offering 12 songs in 21 minutes, the metal band refines its sound, creating an unsettled atmosphere littered with strange and memorable moments.

title: Seventeen Going Under
description: With classic rock ambition and full-hearted sincerity, the 27-year-old British songwriter hits his stride when looking inward but fumbles when casting his gaze toward society at large.

artist: The World Is a Beautiful Place & I Am No Longer Afraid to Die
title: Illusory Walls
description: The band’s dense and ornate fourth album sacrifices intimacy and warmth in favor of the most technically proficient and hard-hitting music of their career.

title: then i’ll be happy EP
description: The digicore scene’s two biggest rising stars aren’t yet distinct enough to complement each other in interesting ways.

title: Piecework
description: The Oakland-based heavy music band returns with its first album in 6 years. Concise and crystal clear, it feels almost provocatively unadorned.

title: Geist
description: The singer-songwriter’s fourth album is largely focused on spiritual shifts and ruptures. Throughout, Geist presents a quiet, lovely, undramatic rendering of the dramatic.

title: Floating Mountains
description: Working with synthesizers and samplers from the 1990s, the Tokyo producer channels the uncannily ersatz sounds of vintage video-game music into a post-vaporwave take on deep house.

title: Talk Memory
description: With nods to the likes of Miles Davis and Pharoah Sanders, the inventive Canadian band sets aside its affinity for hip-hop and kindles a love of classic jazz.

title: Amanita (25th Anniversary Edition)
description: Reissued for its 25th anniversary, this dynamic and momentous release from the Philadelphia rock band features some of their highest peaks.

title: True Love
description: On a warm and crisp new album, the Texas indie-pop duo takes up the mantle of adulthood while remaining preoccupied with the nature of memory and longing.

title: Crimson Poem
description: On her most fully realized album to date, the prolific Chinese artist serves up an enthralling blend of dread and beauty that feels quintessentially her own.

title: Crash
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the album that made the Dave Matthews Band forever famous, in search of its long-overlooked dark heart.

title: One Touch (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: At a fraught time for young women in pop, the UK trio’s 2000 debut elevated candid songs about teenage girls’ hunger for experience by the mining sounds they might actually like.

title: Friends That Break Your Heart
description: A warm and even-keeled collection of ballads, this is James Blake’s most traditional album, but it offers little in the way of emotional insight.

title: Melodi
description: The London duo’s second album boasts a sharpened, more streamlined sound while sticking to its roots in ’70s Anatolian psychedelic pop.

title: Cacerolazo
description: Built from recordings of his 2013 tour as Mister Lies, Nick Zanca’s debut under his own name is sparse experimentation in clamor and free-form percussion.

title: Vol. 3
description: Like its predecessors, the anonymous electronic musician’s third album for Los Angeles’ Peak Oil label consists of little more than dubby swirls of static; the record’s power is in its restraint.

title: one hand on the steering wheel the other sewing a garden
description: On her second album, the Montreal songwriter pens straightforward tales of escape but fares best when she’s retreating into fantasy.

title: Mod Prog Sic
description: Sounding at once meticulous and reckless, sinister and goofy, the experimental trio’s first album in nearly a decade is its most direct appeal to the pleasure center.

title: All Day Gentle Hold !
description: On his fifth album, Aaron Maine is having more fun, writing more playfully, staying out of his own head. It’s some of his most succinct and enjoyable songwriting to date.

title: CXXI
description: Structured around a grid of 121 minor chords, the English experimental musician’s 121st release injects process music with a welcome dose of beauty, chaos, and emotion.

title: Only the End
description: Assisted by frequent collaborators like Bonnie “Prince” Billy, the Vancouver singer-songwriter’s second album is a gentle testament to resilience in the face of emotional hardship.

title: Trust Fund Babies
description: The duo’s collaborative mixtape isn’t a complete disaster, and it’s nice to hear Lil Wayne rap adequately again.

title: Expensive Pain
description: Meek’s fifth album is an extended victory lap that can be thrilling and thoughtful in spots but is mostly content to aggressively spin its wheels.

title: Ma délire - Songs of love, lost & found
description: The ambitious new album from the Canadian songwriter features thoughtful and transformative interpretations of traditional music. It is both a meditation on the past and a novel step forward.

title: Girl, Buried
description: The Michigan band’s debut defaults to the moody rumble of 1990s shoegaze, but sounds best when it plows through the guardrails.

title: Prose Combat
description: Originally released in 1994, the Parisian rapper’s second album brought a particularly French sensibility to hip-hop, countering the hegemony of American artists—and the English language itself.

title: To All Sides They Will Stretch Out Their Hands
description: Huerco S.’ second album under his atmospheric alter ego is eerie and unsettling: Rhythms are frayed, harmonies are buried, and the usual reassurances of ambient music no longer apply.

title: Half God
description: Produced entirely by Navy Blue, the New York rapper’s latest is one of his greatest. A wise and angry Wiki reveals what it’s like to come of age in the city: the way it shapes, hardens, prematurely ages you.

title: Let Me Do One More
description: With poignant writing and irreverent humor, Sarah Tudzin’s second album as Illuminati Hotties plays like a demonstration in the art of persistence.

title: Liminal Soul
description: The Moscow electronic musician and vocalist’s third album treats the haphazard textures of everyday life with a refreshingly playful sensibility.

title: Moebius Strips
description: Moebius’ friend Tim Story gathers loops and samples left behind by the late krautrock pioneer and reworks them with the assistance of Hans-Joachim Roedelius, Michael Rother, Sarah Davachi, and others.

title: Molten Mirrors
description: Livity Sound displays past and present iterations of its elliptical sound on this anniversary compilation, a low-key affair that serves as a testament to the focus and consistency of the Bristol label’s approach to dance music.

title: Animal
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Kesha's whiskey-soaked 2010 debut, a ridiculously fun and somewhat fraught album whose garish aesthetic is being channeled anew.

title: Fair & Square
description: Newly reissued on vinyl, this late-career gem from the beloved songwriter highlights the hope, humor, and underdog rage that animate his best work.

title: Wilds
description: Because it’s not beholden to some overarching conceit, the latest album from the Toronto-based singer-songwriter sounds looser, a bit wilder, more lackadaisical in a sadsack sort of way.

title: Local Valley
description: After six years, the Swedish singer-songwriter returns with another soothing album of sweet indie-folk murmurs. Spare electronic beats bring a new pulse to his sound, but the voice remains the same.

title: Our Bande Apart
description: The latest album from Stephan Jenkins’ alt-rock band is full of big swings and big misses, but its best songs elicit a modest, familiar sense of nostalgia.

title: Colourgrade
description: The London songwriter’s mesmerizing second album turns towards porous, avant-garde love songs that celebrate kinship, change, and the wonder of quotidian experience.

title: The Heart Pumps Kool-Aid
description: On a collaboration between Austin’s More Eaze and Orange Milk co-founder Seth Graham, the music’s frequent rests and lacunae lend its jazz-tinged electroacoustic mesh a stony, severe quality.

title: Songwrights Apothecary Lab
description: Esperanza Spalding’s eighth album is a strangely romantic, sometimes didactic effort to mold the often private experience of listening and feeling the healing power of music.

title: A Beginner’s Mind
description: With a collection of gentle duets inspired by great-to-iffy movies, the veteran songwriter and protégé uncover mythic resonances and ugly truths.

title: Hitler Wears Hermes 8
description: The confrontationally prolific Buffalo rapper cedes space to his dynamic guests on both halves of his latest project, a supremely competent data dump that is memorable only in fits.

title: In the Meantime
description: Alessia Cara’s moving and mature album is a sleek ode to in-between states, whether they are relationships or her career track as a pop star.

title: Flux
description: Music has always been just one aspect of the former YouTuber’s cryptic multimedia experience, but Flux makes it finally feel like the most important one.

title: Crocus
description: The Cincinnati folk-rock quartet’s third album is artfully and interestingly composed, a snapshot of four people figuring out their identities both as individual humans and as a subtly defiant band.

title: Sincerely, Kentrell
description: While it carries the same flaws as his previous work, the latest album from the Baton Rouge rapper provides a clear portrait of a tragic figure who often blurs the lines between fact and fiction.

title: Lowkey Superstar Deluxe
description: The L.A. singer and rapper offers a fun-forward deluxe mixtape that exudes color and energy, pinballing between personas and styles.

title: Provisional License
description: Shaped around a loose narrative, the Birmingham drill rapper’s debut album paints an immersive picture of everyday brutality with gripping beats and detailed imagery.

title: And Then Life Was Beautiful
description: After rediscovering her creative spark, Nao turns her organic-sounding third album into a kaleidoscopic testament to the pains and pleasures of modern love and the healing process they inspire.

title: Flowerland
description: The third album from the duo of Juliette Pearl Davis and Joachim Polack takes on the soft psychedelic hues of Stereolab and Wendy Carlos, shot through with malaise and a curious sense of overstimulation.

title: Mouth Full of Glass
description: Best known as one half of art-rock duo Ohmme, the Chicago musician turns towards lush, baroque-tinged folk on a solo debut with a reverent approach to self-knowledge and growth.

title: Remember Her Name
description: The debut album from the rising country artist aspires for universality but fares best when highlighting her singular voice and defiance of the status quo.

artist: Pastor T. L. Barrett and the Youth for Christ Choir
title: I Shall Wear a Crown
description: Some may know the Chicago pastor only as the source of Kanye’s “Father Stretch My Hands.” Documenting his ’70s fusions of gospel, funk, and soul, Numero Group’s box set captures the full sweep of his legacy.

title: I’ll Be Your Mirror: A Tribute to the Velvet Underground and Nico
description: St. Vincent, Kurt Vile, Sharon Van Etten, Iggy Pop, and more contribute to this tasteful if predictable cover album, faring best when their own identities shine through the music.

title: Lewis Taylor
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a lost gem of neo-soul from 1996 made by a nascent phenom from the UK, heralded by Aaliyah and D’Angelo as one of the greats.

title: I’ve Seen Everything
description: The beloved Scottish indie rock band reissues their 1993 sophomore album, a fan favorite, one that exemplifies the band’s communal songwriting and their indelible romanticism and pop instincts.

title: Molecular Level
description: Reviving his dormant Micron Audio label, Detroit’s Sherard Ingram—also known as the chief architect of Urban Tribe—returns to the high-octane techno and electro that are his stock in trade.

title: Sable (Original Video Game Soundtrack)
description: A gentle, mostly wordless collection of ambient pop, Michelle Zauner’s soundtrack for the indie exploration game is a streamlined glimpse into her versatility as a narrative artist.

title: Máscaras
description: The Toronto-based musician explores his Nicaraguan roots on an album of drifting, ambient-adjacent songs incorporating instruments like the quena and llamador.

title: Teenage Dreams
description: The teenage South African duo build the lean rhythms and jazzy melodies of amapiano into a sprawling debut suffused with dynamic energy and tantalizing uncertainty.

title: By the Time I Get to Phoenix
description: On their first album since member Stepa J. Groggs’ death, the Phoenix rap trio reintroduces themselves as wide-eyed explorers, a rep that suits their fascination with rap’s mechanics, its margins, and its future.

title: Observation of Breath
description: Performed on a 132-year-old pipe organ, the latest project from the Australian sound artist dials up the volume and revels in the rumble.

title: No More Tears
description: Featuring contributions from Lemmy, a pair of Hot 100 hits, and a newly vulnerable outlook, this peak from the rock star’s solo career gets a 30th anniversary reissue.

title: If Orange Was a Place EP
description: The breakout Nigerian star’s second EP explores new sounds even as it returns to familiar ideas—her ongoing search for peace, love, and emotional clarity.

title: American Dreamer
description: The 8xLP box set gathers the ’60s and ’70s studio recordings of a singer-songwriter whose melodically intricate work had a profound impact on Joni Mitchell, Elton John, and Steely Dan.

title: Back in Action EP
description: On his latest EP, the Indiana-raised hyperpop upstart takes a step closer toward the mainstream, sharpening his style without losing the irreverence that makes up his volatile vision.

title: drive-by lullabies
description: Knit together with ambient passages and found sound, the teenage rapper and producer’s debut feels like a jumbled journey through folders of ideas that reveals new layers with every listen.

title: Departing Like Rivers
description: Shackleton’s first solo full-length in nine years is stripped of some of his customary idiosyncrasies, but it remains heady, beaded-curtains, incense-in-the-air music, filled with occult mystique.

title: The Gaping Mouth
description: With newly complex arrangements and more freeform songwriting, the Atlanta duo ventures from its bedroom pop origins with occasionally fascinating results.

title: Black Encyclopedia of the Air
description: Though the Philadelphia experimental poet and sound artist has called this her most “accessible” album, her aims remain as radical as ever.

title: Goldilocks X
description: The Canadian rapper and singer’s sense of playfulness is the highlight of a second album that attempts to reach beyond her raunchy sex-rap comfort zone.

title: Hey Tony
description: The first compilation album from the Brooklyn beatmaker is an entertaining ride through the sounds of one of New York’s most underappreciated producers.

title: Silence
description: With sparse arrangements and a lyrical focus on hearing loss and mortality, the latest solo album from the Hot Chip vocalist is a solemn and moving collection.

title: PICTURA DE IPSE: Musique directe
description: On his second album, the Québécois pop provocateur scales down the lavish glam rock of his debut for funky experiments with inconsistent results.

title: Montero
description: On his melodious debut album, the pop-rap icon flaunts his verve and star power, all while a sense of isolation lives at the music’s brighter edges.

title: The Convincer (20th Anniversary Reissue)
description: A new reissue of the the master craftsman’s 2001 album offers the quintessential portrait of his third act, showcasing a fascination with the places where genres intertwine.

title: Look-Ka Py Py
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit an inimitable album of New Orleans music, home to the deepest grooves and an enormous foundation for funk, rock, and rap.

title: Deja
description: Absorbing influences from the natural world and working with collaborators like Lido Pimienta, the Colombian group pushes its habitual electro-tropicalia sound into new terrain.

title: Division
description: The Miami singer moves through her debut album with a sense of self-assurance that doesn’t allow her to look into the rearview at missteps.

title: Established!
description: The footwork pioneer sets aside the obsessive minimalism of his previous album in favor of party-starting anthems and sly sample flips. But his work remains a masterclass in rhythmic dexterity.

title: Starshooter
description: The Sacramento rapper is more relaxed and nonchalant on his latest project, a mood that suits his knack for finding humanity in the darkest of situations.

title: Up 2 Më
description: The inescapable Portland rapper continues to go beyond the usual rage rap expectations, bending his voice without ever making it feel gimmicky.

title: A Beautiful Life
description: On its straightforward but deeply felt sixth album, the Ohio rock band positions music itself as a salve against the horrors of the world.

title: Space 1.8
description: The brilliant and unassuming debut from the young UK musician and composer is a benchmark in ambient jazz featuring outstanding players and delicately woven arrangements.

title: Crack Dreams
description: The latest disappointing mixtape from one of the year’s most exciting rappers proves that the best way to encounter him is his YouTube channel.

title: Texis
description: Despite its newfound musical relevance, the influential duo struggles to evolve beyond its signature template of empowering pop hooks and overdriven arrangements.

title: The Melodic Blue
description: On his expansive debut studio album, the once enigmatic rapper expands his fascination with trap and melody to feature-length with mixed results.

title: Flush Real Pharynx 2019-2021
description: Gathering a trio of EPs into a single sprawling package, the experimental club producer offers a nightmarish tour of late capitalism that’s dark, disorienting, and at times, draining.

title: K Bay
description: Filled with delightful moments of sound-craft, the third solo album from the Spacebomb auteur places him at the center of a vast musical cosmology.

title: Antiphonals
description: Using a soft instrumental palette of Mellotron and keyboards, Canadian minimalist composer Sarah Davachi welcomes listeners into her fortress of solitude.

title: Comfort to Me
description: On their second album, the Australian quartet expands into a Colossus-sized version of itself. Everything feels bigger, heavier, and more meaningful.

title: Lindsey Buckingham
description: On his first solo album in 10 years, Lindsey Buckingham’s insistent, almost irritating knack for melody suggests a resurgent talent for making his insularity accessible.

title: Before I Die
description: Singing and rapping in Korean and English, the Los Angeles-based electronic producer takes tentative steps toward reinventing herself as a songwriter.

title: Doe or Die II
description: The Brooklyn rapper follows up his 1995 debut with an ornate sequel that indulges nostalgia on its own terms.

title: You Heat Me Up, You Cool Me Down
description: This live album is an intense, electric, and sometimes uncanny exhibition of Archy Marshall’s ability to reimagine his songs on stage.

title: The Delta Sweete
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Bobbie Gentry’s 1968 album, a daring, atmospheric, and oft-overshadowed Southern classic.

title: I’ve Been Trying to Tell You
description: On their 10th studio album, the UK electro-pop heroes look back on the end of the 20th century, when hooks and choruses dissolved into blissed-out loops and vibe became paramount.

title: HEY WHAT
description: On the follow-up to 2018’s astonishing Double Negative, Mimi Parker and Alan Sparhawk push deeper into abstraction, finding fresh angles on the themes that have animated them since the beginning.

title: The Metallica Blacklist
description: Celebrating the 30th anniversary of the Black Album, Metallica enlist Phoebe Bridgers, Kamasi Washington, Moses Sumney, Weezer, J Balvin, and many more for this enormous and uneven tribute album.

title: star-crossed
description: Kacey Musgraves’ chronicle of marriage and divorce looks to the stars but takes pains to stay grounded. Writing in the plain language of someone desperate to be understood, she sounds alternately vulnerable and triumphant.

title: Honest Labour
description: A genre-spanning collection of cryptic transmissions, interludes, and asides, the Manchester duo’s second album gets at emotion in an oblique fashion, remaking your desires as it plays.

title: Italians Do It Better
description: Executive-produced by Johnny Jewel, this Madonna tribute album transports her iconic singles to the boutique label’s seedy, neon-lit lounges.

title: Mercury – Act 1
description: Despite the ostensibly humanizing presence of Rick Rubin, rock’s patron saint of prestige, these quintessentially Vegas showmen still sound like they’re firing their emotions out of a T-shirt cannon.

title: Dawn of Chromatica
description: A remix album of Lady Gaga’s 2020 dancefloor epic is less a wall-to-wall collection of club bangers than an expansion of the Chromatica cinematic universe, featuring Charli XCX, Arca, Rina Sawayama, Doss, and more.

title: gg bb xx
description: The nominally bicoastal pop trio’s fourth album is musically complacent and emotionally lifeless.

title: M Field EP
description: On this indie pop EP, the Cape Town singer and guitarist generates warmth by pairing innocent inquiry with bright instrumentation.

title: Everything
description: Chicago singer-songwriter Jessica Viscius moves through grief in a profoundly moving and generous way on her spare debut as Bnny.

title: Mirrors
description: On his first album in four years, the Swedish house producer strips away the hiss to zero in on floor-filling club tracks and big, universal emotions.

title: Certified Lover Boy
description: Drake’s sixth album sounds good but feels labored. Melancholic and often incisive, it becomes an overlong and very familiar journey through the life, mind, and heart of Drake.

title: I Died for This?!
description: The Georgia rapper’s debut for Shady Records is a gritty showcase for his creativity and versatility, even if it only works in fits and starts.

title: Baduizm
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Erykah Badu’s 1997 debut, an existential anchor of the neo-soul movement.

title: The Witness
description: By resisting the bluster of past efforts, the Montreal band emerges with its most cohesive album yet, the first that never gets lost in its own dark gravity.

title: Backwards and Forwards (The WEA Recordings 1984-1995)
description: This expansive collection follows songwriter Roddy Frame from his second album Knife through his decision to retire the Aztec Camera moniker, highlighting forays into sophistipop, electronica, and soul.

title: The Mutt’s Nuts
description: With the glow-up of a bigger indie label behind them for their second album, the UK punks ride again with burly bravado, but it’s notably the work of artists eager to show that they contain multitudes.

title: Senjutsu
description: The British metal legends return with their dark and patient 17th album. While their influence looms large in heavy music, no other band sounds quite like this.

title: Sometimes I Might Be Introvert
description: On her fourth album, the UK rapper wrestles with the split between her public persona and private self, raising broadly relatable questions about the craving for validation.

title: Screen Violence
description: On its fourth album, the Scottish trio steps back from the grandest pop aspirations and embraces a horror-movie concept without losing its signature brightness and sense of joy.

title: Any Shape You Take
description: The North Carolina songwriter’s outstanding second album spans grungy rock and colorful, hi-fi pop, illuminating her impressive voice and her ability to wring out every last drop of emotion.

title: Dissent
description: The Berlin dub-techno icon reshuffles his trio’s lineup on its first album in six years. Alongside jazz drummer Heinrich Köbberling, Laurel Halo’s electric keys provide a surprising new focal point.

title: Structure
description: The Brooklyn electro-pop duo’s fifth album breaks into two mirror-image halves of a guided tour of heartbreak, hope, and longing. They’re still making cryptic indie pop that hits like a sugar rush.

title: How Long Do You Think It’s Gonna Last?
description: Justin Vernon and Aaron Dessner’s expansive side project embraces new guests and familiar sounds, but sometimes feels lost in its own pleasant fog.

title: History of a Feeling
description: The Nashville-based singer-songwriter’s fifth album breaks through to a spare, unvarnished, and occasionally volatile style of indie rock that feels in step with the newly sharpened edge to her lyricism.

title: Fire
description: Drawing inspiration from the abject state of contemporary Britain and nourished by fantasies of righteous violence, the latest album from the UK producer is his heaviest in years.

title: Deconsecrate
description: On its second album, the Portland quartet conjures a sense of ambient horror with shapeshifting, high-velocity death metal.

title: Donda
description: Kanye West’s 10th album arrives barely finished and with a lot of baggage. Its 27 tracks include euphoric highs that lack connective tissue, a data dump of songs searching for a higher calling.

title: Feel Flows: The Sunflower & Surf’s Up Sessions 1969-1971
description: Tracing the Beach Boys’ long road back to the spotlight, this five-disc set showcases a complicated era and a creative peak.

title: Next Is Now
description: In grappling with the “mess” of our present moment, the punk legend looks relentlessly to the future, and her optimism feels alternately like a salve and a delusion.

title: Love Will Be Reborn
description: On her first album in five years, the singer-songwriter meditates on love, grief, and motherhood with vibrant melodies and newfound perspective.

title: Psalms
description: Accompanied by Joan Shelley, Will Oldham, and others, the Louisville guitarist sets Hebrew psalms and poetry to music with a comforting, candlelit atmosphere.

title: Geezyworld
description: The former Shoreline Mafia member launches his solo career with a concentrated dose of what he does best: rap music for the height of the party.

title: Other You
description: Recorded in Los Angeles, the songwriter and guitarist’s sixth solo album is ambitious yet effortless. Even his lead guitar seems almost to melt away into the delicate arrangements.

title: Everybody Else Is Doing It, So Why Can’t We?
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the 1993 debut from the Irish pop-rock band, a showcase for Dolores O’Riordan’s disarming songwriting and immaculate voice.

title: In It for the Money (Remastered Expanded Edition)
description: Originally released in 1997, the Britpop band’s second album feels like a crash course in the history of UK rock, zipping through glam, psychedelia, punk, and pop in fresh, surprising ways.

title: Cracks
description: On his second solo album, the Norwegian saxophonist continues to develop an entirely new vocabulary for his instrument, using electronic treatments to yield a curiously disembodied sound.

title: Only Up
description: Recorded with an ensemble of Toronto musicians, the fun and referential second album from Josh Korody’s indie rock project feels like a big, messy collage.

title: Lost Futures
description: Evoking the landscapes of the American Southwest, these peaceful guitar duets find the duo tapping into the serene, timeless quality of their instrument.

title: Glow On
description: The Baltimore band’s spectacular fourth record is all groove, riffs, and passion. It is not a crossover hardcore album that looks to transcend the genre, but one that tries to elevate it to its highest visibility.

title: Corinne Bailey Rae
description: Though best remembered for its biggest hit, the UK singer’s eponymous 2006 debut remains unmatched in the weighty simplicity of its stories of love pursued and lost.

title: If I Can’t Have Love, I Want Power
description: Produced by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross, Halsey’s spectral fourth album confronts the thrill and terror of getting what you want. It’s their strongest work to date.

title: No Sun
description: Written in the wake of a divorce and while working toward a PhD in musicology, the Los Angeles musician’s first album in four years is a breakup record stripped to its most elemental parts.

title: Year of the Spider
description: The Oakland rock band responds to tragedy with grace on their most musically diverse and lyrically affecting album yet.

title: America’s Sweetheart 2
description: Bear1Boss has been a breath of fresh air with his bright, melodic take on Atlanta rap. His latest and best project yet focuses purely on fun.

title: Cheers to the Best Memories
description: The trio’s collaborative debut stumbles into lovely stretches, coasting on the beauty of the singers’ voices. But it leaves you wondering why such an obviously winning combination falls short.

title: The Horses and the Hounds
description: On his expertly written 10th album, the Texas storyteller delivers some of his most intense and humane work.

title: The Long and Short of It
description: The fantastic album from the Portland-based artist Graham Jonson turns beat music and bedroom pop into a complex psychedelic world with vast emotional horizons. His songs are lush and boundless.

title: Don’t Know What I Am
description: The Portland quartet crank up the chorus and distortion pedals in service of jangly hooks and gleaming counter-melodies.

title: Aisles EP
description: The songwriter takes an uncharacteristic breather with a collection of faithful, occasionally brooding covers of 1980s hits like “Forever Young” and “The Safety Dance.”

title: Sylva Sylvarum
description: With vivid details and subtle textures, the latest collaboration between crys cole and James Rushford folds real-world sounds into a landscape of dreams.

title: Primordial Arcana
description: Working out of their home studio in the Washington woods, experimentally minded brothers Nathan and Aaron Weaver return to their roots in atmospheric black metal, but they no longer sound like pioneers.

title: Infinite Granite
description: Abandoning black metal’s harsh intensity in favor of softer, gentler sounds, Deafheaven push themselves into surprising terrain. It’s a tricky proposition.

title: ’Til I Start Speaking
description: The London-based singer’s jazzy debut album shines most brightly when she gets explosive, yet her muted moments also resonate.

title: Body Jumper
description: Filled with muted vocals and no wave melodies, the Bay Area group’s debut album uses 1980s horror tropes and video games to reflect on contemporary alienation.

title: Long Time Coming
description: The West Virginia native found fame on YouTube, but she descends from a long tradition of American roots music. Though assisted by Nashville greats, her debut retains her essential wildness.

title: A Martyr’s Reward
description: One of rap’s most inventive stylists surfaces from his memories to reflect on himself and his vocation, transforming his latest record into a searing, soulful gem in his catalog.

title: Long Term Effects of Suffering
description: Channeling the stark sound and fatalistic worldview of vintage Southern rap, the New Orleans duo takes grim pleasure in grappling with substance abuse and mental illness.

title: Rhododendron
description: The Montreal musician and former Grimes collaborator weaves synthetic woodwinds and harpsichord into a dizzying yet heartfelt fusion of classical pastiche and skewed electronic pop.

title: Solar Power
description: Lorde returns with a self-aware, scaled-back album. Its holistic beauty and revelations about the natural world are often lost in the drab music.

title: Queendom
description: The individual songs on the K-pop girl group’s mini-album are perfectly adequate, but the release itself never reaches the group’s former heights.

title: Cherrytape EP
description: The Tennessee rapper’s latest four-song EP is a concentrated burst of energy with perfectly paced flows and a vibe that’s always ready for the dancefloor.

title: Pyrex Picasso
description: The Griselda rapper’s latest album accentuates many of his strengths, highlights no unknown weaknesses, and is peppered with some of the finest tracks of what will be remembered as a golden era for The Butcher.

title: The Ballad of Dood and Juanita
description: Following two volumes of roots renditions of his own songs, the shapeshifting country musician returns with a bluegrass concept album about love among the legends of the Kentucky frontier.

title: Twin Plagues
description: On its second album, the Asheville five-piece goes big and loud, scaling up its shoegaze-indebted sound while frontwoman Karly Hartzman buries an undercurrent of anxiety beneath the clutter.

title: Dreams Still Inspire
description: Guided by detailed coaching from Kanye West, the Chicago duo embrace an urge to restore a kind of lyrical conscious rap that has never been lost.

title: Basic Tools
description: The Kingston-based dancehall crew’s fourth album presents a world of inside jokes and outsize characters set to slyly experimental beats that show exacting attention to detail.

title: Draw Down the Moon
description: The St. Louis band’s fourth album scrapes away their unwieldy experimentalism in favor of the approachable, frustratingly anonymous sounds of 2010s festival rock.

title: A Hole in the Fence
description: Taken individually, the pieces on this album from the Los Angeles-based accordion player can be moving, but their similar construction yields transcendence and tedium in equal measure.

title: Bo Jackson
description: The Detroit rapper and the famed producer rejoin forces for a spare, melancholy, and psychedelic album, solidifying their partnership as one of the most rewarding team-ups in hip-hop.

title: Don’t Get Comfy / Nowhere
description: On her solo debut, the double bassist largely lets her instrument play a supporting role for her distinctive soprano vocals, working through deep feelings via quietly adventurous songwriting.

title: Anjelitu EP
description: Bored by the status quo and excited by everything he hasn’t tried yet, the Queens rapper is unafraid to take risks and get weird on his latest EP.

title: Sweetness EP
description: Buoyed by Afrobeats producer Sarz’ nostalgic, ’80s-influenced production, the Nigerian-born, London-based singer turns his attention to romance, exploring a gentler side of his voice.

artist: A Great Big Pile of Leaves
title: Pono
description: With its wistful musings on adolescence and nostalgia, the indie rock trio’s first album in eight years picks up right where they left off.

title: Refuge
description: The songwriter and producer team for a loving, referential collection of new age music that doesn’t always color inside the lines.

title: All Dogs Go to Heaven EP
description: Recorded in a sleek L.A. studio, the Gen-Z hyperpop artist’s latest EP hides his natural talent under a layer of amorphous production.

title: Still Slipping Vol. 1
description: In his debut full-length, the UK producer puts his idiosyncratic stamp on a variety of club styles, folding in the voices of his family members to add emotional resonance.

title: Fire of Love
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the incendiary, hell-bent debut from the Los Angeles punk band who used blues and rockabilly to paint a depraved portrait of a young artist in their purest state.

title: Harmonizer
description: The tireless psych rocker’s latest is simultaneously sleek and sludgy. It’s not quite his cleanest-sounding album, nor his heaviest, but it stands close to the top of both categories.

title: Fiori Chiari, Fiori Oscuri
description: Fusing toy piano, minimalist improvisation, children’s voices, modular synthesizers, and a purring cat, among other fanciful sounds, the American composer’s 1978 album revels in the accidental music of everyday life.

title: A Sky Record
description: The duo’s latest album is a calming and tender reflection on appreciating what you have in uncertain times.

title: Complacency EP
description: The Philadelphia emo trio’s debut EP packs in a career’s worth of evolution, pulling from ’90s Midwest twinkle, Guitar Hero shredding, and the online angst of an emergent fifth wave.

title: Pressure Machine
description: Brandon Flowers dials back the pomp for an intimate, homespun, and sometimes clunky tour through the small town where he grew up.

title: Above the Fray
description: DāM-FunK’s latest is his most romantic and awestruck album. If his earlier work suggests a bleary-eyed, late-night haze, Above the Fray is a cloudless vista where you can see for miles.

title: Project X
description: The Atlanta rapper and Playboi Carti protégé aims to set himself apart with his zoned-out sing-rap.

title: fragments
description: Five months after her stunning debut album, the Brooklyn composer offers up a modest yet revealing set of sketch-like guitar pieces, drawing unexpected connections between Pat Metheny and Midwestern emo.

title: Rich Shooter
description: With tightly packed bars and adaptable, uncanny flows, the Atlanta rapper’s latest is precise and loose at the same time. Pi’erre Bourne and Coupe’s beats are showcases for his originality.

title: Sinner Get Ready
description: Kristin Hayter’s latest is an intense and frightening religious inquiry, incorporating traditional Appalachian instruments and samples from televangelist sermons.

title: Megabear
description: The London band’s full-length debut is an audacious experiment: 52 short snippets of rippling pianos and synthesized symphonics that can be shuffled in any order to create one continuous song.

title: King’s Disease II
description: The Queensbridge rapper’s sequel mythologizes his business acumen and doubles down on the formula of its predecessor to mixed effect.

title: FEMINISTA
description: The California producer’s debut album channels new-age synths and retro dance styles into a dreamlike synthesis of disparate musical modes.

title: Bloodslide EP
description: Featuring members of Protomartyr and Preoccupations, the post-punk supergroup’s debut is refreshingly blunt and ambitious.

title: Painful Enlightenment
description: The veteran Chicago footwork producer tests the genre’s stylistic limits on a bracing, sometimes harrowing album that documents her struggles with depression.

title: The Apple Drop
description: With new collaborators and a little psychedelic aid, the sculpted rhythms and dark-hued instrumentation of Angus Andrew’s long-running art-rock project feel like a summation and a fresh start.

title: Native Sons
description: A tribute to their hometown of Los Angeles, this covers album spans genre and style, showcasing Los Lobos’ versatility, taste, and strength as a rock’n’roll band.

title: Therapy
description: The British singer’s crisply rendered, competently hooky second album promises a more personal self-portrait, but she ends up disappearing into vague songwriting and anodyne dance-pop production.

title: Mood Ring
description: The latest album from Philly songwriter Zoe Reynolds embraces the synths and glitter of pop music, but it feels most luminous when it’s raw.

title: Laura Stevenson
description: The singer-songwriter’s sixth album remains enigmatic, processing trauma and joy through the force of its unvarnished arrangements.
Parlaying creative independence into her best work to date, the R&B star’s latest self-released album is a showcase for her omnivorous tastes and supremely light touch.

title: Born in the U.S.A.
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit a 1980s rock blockbuster: the bold, brilliant, and misunderstood apex of Bruce Springsteen’s imperial era.

title: Country Funk Volume III (1975-1982)
description: The third volume of Light in the Attic’s ongoing survey of this largely notional movement puts a new twist on the idea of combining two seemingly incompatible genres in one unruly sound.

title: House of Lull . House of When
description: The debut solo album from the Daughters vocalist is a left turn: an eerie, improvised collection of industrial music that places you deep in the heart of the abyss.

title: 9th & Walnut
description: The veteran California band reconstructs some of its earliest material for an unusual sort of lost album that captures an ephemeral moment in punk history.

title: GUMBO’!
description: The genre-defying rapper’s third album pays tribute to the artists who helped shape his sound—and sounds like something else altogether.

title: Razor’s Edge
description: The rapper’s latest album, a sleek modern update to a classic formula—helmed entirely by producer Futurewave—expresses a tenderness rarely seen in his catalog.

title: At Pioneer Works
description: In Tuareg culture, women rarely play guitar; this Nigerien group breaks with that tradition. Their 2019 live recording captures them at a hypnotic high, far from home but in command of an eager, inviting spirit.

title: H.R.
description: The Irish DIY artist isn’t the first to note that while pop is fun, capitalism is perhaps a bit of a downer. But she’s uncommonly committed to the bit.

title: Young Dolph Presents Paper Route Illuminati
description: Featuring Key Glock and newcomers Snupe Bandz and Joddy, this compilation from the Memphis rapper and his associates feels like the culmination of a thoroughly unique career.

title: Stand for Myself
description: The Bristol-born, Nashville-based singer-songwriter’s second album isn’t defined by genre as much as it is by Yola’s indomitable spirit.

title: Vanice
description: Following up the viral hit “Vibe (If I Back It Up),” the New Jersey singer’s official debut aims to render the fast-paced, energetic sound of Jersey club in her own image.

title: Welcome 2 America
description: Recorded in 2010, Prince’s first posthumous album of all unreleased material is a state-of-the-union concept record in which he bluntly broadcasts his opinions on taxes, technology, drugs, religion, and the music industry.

title: New Day With New Possibilities
description: Billed as a country record, the San Francisco garage-rock hero’s eighth record with the Sunsets uses the genre as a means for chronicling the lives of lonesome men.

title: Yes/And
description: The debut album from Meg Duffy and Joel Ford maps the interaction between delicate fingerpicking and precise electronic textures; it is a study in subtle, gorgeous discord.

title: Glans Intercum
description: Ben Bondy makes ambient music shot through with sharp, pristinely mixed drums. This album for Huerco S.’s label is psychedelic in a way that suggests a faint sense of nausea or discomfort.

title: Heart-Shaped Scars
description: With a tendency to drift, the Scottish songwriter’s first solo record in almost a decade is a quiet, graceful collection of autumnal folk music.

title: Debonair
description: Grating yet perversely gratifying, this King Krule-adjacent South London band’s debut also contains music of inarguable force or surprising beauty.

title: The House Is Burning
description: The TDE rapper returns with newfound poise and even joy, taking R&B, Southern rap, and his inimitable lyrical style and casting it into a sophisticated collage.

title: Happier Than Ever
description: On her second album, Billie Eilish sings with unsparing honesty about her rapid ascent to stardom and all its accompanying horrors. It’s woozy, effortlessly melodic, and showcases her command over the pop landscape.

title: SHILOH: Lost for Words
description: The East London rapper and producer’s debut has the feel of a mixtape, luxuriating in the tension between her reticent persona and raw lyricism.

title: Celestial Blues
description: Kristina Esfandiari and her band move from the darkness to light on their second album, taking liberally from post-rock, grunge, and doom to tell a tale equally inspired by a childhood brush with death and Paradise Lost.

title: Wildhund
description: On their first album in 7 years, the blackgaze innovators lighten up their sound with bountiful hooks and life-drunk enthusiasm.

title: Jesus Freak
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the story around the ’90s boom of Contemporary Christian Music and one of its biggest records.

title: Peppa’s Adventures: The Album
description: The four-year-old pop phenom and famous pig’s second album is a charming and self-assured celebration of family, friendship, and muddy puddles.

title: Âlem
description: On their second album this year, the Netherlands-based Anatolian psych rockers push deeper into electronic pop, infusing traditional Turkish melodies with the spirit of disco.

title: Take the Sadness Out of Saturday Night
description: On his third album, the in-demand producer and solo artist ends up splitting his time between careful rock songwriting and carefree pop singing, leaving a minor impression of both in the process.

title: Ngủ Ngày Ngay Ngày Tận Thế
description: The Vietnamese experimental trio’s debut album offers a breakneck onslaught of disparate styles and moods. The sounds can be thrillingly haphazard, but the vision is unmistakably focused.

title: Crowlink EP
description: Interspersed with birdsong, new age synth, and poetry recitations, a new EP from the English folk singer returns her songs to the elements that inspired them.

title: A Night at the Baths
description: The Special Interest synth player’s latest solo project is an emotional tour of the bathhouse: a celebration of defiantly queer spaces in the form of heady, hazy techno and ambient.

title: Thirstier
description: Mackenzie Scott’s latest is anthemic and euphoric, loaded with hooks and joyous reflections on love and self-discovery.

title: Amapiano Now
description: Curated by London DJs Shannen SP and Joe Cotch, this 17-track compilation takes the pulse of the quickly evolving South African genre built around log-drum grooves, bright synths, and jazz-inflected keys.

title: Moon Boy
description: The Mobile, Alabama rapper’s debut album is weighed down by streaming bait, but thankfully it does include a handful of his highest highs.

title: Change
description: The Berlin-based artist’s first full-length solo release in over a decade is a stylish, sexy record where not much happens.

title: Under the Lilac Sky
description: The Indian composer and vocalist blends Hindustani classical music with new age synth on her dreamy, meditative debut.

title: We’re All Alone in This Together
description: The British-Nigerian rapper’s second album is as ambitious, technical, and deeply felt as his first. It is sure to keep his star on the rise.

title: Seance
description: On the New Zealand singer-songwriter’s fourth album, spare acoustic arrangements make deceptively simple containers for songs charged with memory and mysticism.

title: an afternoon whine
description: Texas musicians and real-life “bffs” mari maurice and claire rousay work in the same room for the first time. More than a cool biographical detail, this fact defines the album’s lovingly meta style.

title: Yellow
description: The debut from the English bandleader and producer is a fascinating blend of spiritual jazz and brass band that can sound full-on psychedelic while staying grounded in its clever arrangements.

title: Scout EP
description: The singer-songwriter aims for a bigger sound with her new EP, a condensed whirlwind of breakups, reunions, long-distance phone calls, and long-haul road trips.

title: Van Gogh’s Left Ear
description: The Detroit rapper pays tribute to Van Gogh’s most infamous moment, extending his own recent prolific streak with a chaotic, creative album that switches styles like outfits.

title: Banned
description: A low-pressure psych-rock jam session between Canadian artists Yves Jarvis and Romy Lightman produces a few happy accidents and a lot of aimless experimentation.

title: Life, and Another
description: Erin Birgy’s delightfully freaky sixth album is dense but full of whimsy and romance, pulling in strains of folk, jazz, and chamber pop to marvel at all the odd little wonders of the world.

title: PSA
description: The Houston singer’s debut blends pop, alt-R&B, and soul into a polished and pensive account of growing into young adulthood.

title: Blind Obedience
description: The enigmatic Brooklyn rapper’s debut album is part airing of grievances, part origin story: a blood-stained portrait of the forces that made him.

title: Last Train to Paris
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Sean “Diddy” Combs’ 2010 side project: a dark and stormy concept album about one man’s transit through love.

title: Tiny Music… Songs From the Vatican Gift Shop (Super Deluxe Edition)
description: Newly reissued for its 25th anniversary, STP’s sunbaked album of glam and pop and rock ranks as one of their best, separating them from the pack of post-grunge wannabes.

title: Spiral
description: Nicolás Jaar and Dave Harrington return with a meticulous work of unexpected and even unprecedented familiarity—less a portal than a kiosk existing entirely within the boundaries set by their 2013 debut.

title: Signals in My Head
description: The South Side producer infuses footwork’s intricate syncopations with the romance of R&B; in the process, he underscores the shared lineage with Chicago house.

title: Ain’t That the Truth
description: Drakeo’s fifth full-length release in eight months is brooding and entertaining. The lesser cuts can’t help but bleed together, but there’s just enough new variations to keep things fresh.

title: Gold-Diggers Sound
description: The Texas singer delivers a smooth, risk-averse R&B album whose nostalgic trappings aim for timelessness.

title: Utopian Ashes
description: Feigning coupledom, the two singers offer a fictionalized divorce album modeled after the tear-jerking country, soul, and pop duets of yesteryear. They flirt with camp without ever succumbing to it.

title: It’s Remble
description: The Los Angeles rapper’s debut charts his development as he settles into a style that’s funny, winkingly formal, and rich in commercial potential.

title: TEMPORARY HIGHS IN THE VIOLET SKIES
description: With dreamy experimental production and standout Tyler, the Creator features, the L.A. singer’s latest is an affecting document of how pain can smolder beneath a veneer of nonchalance.

title: The Asymptotical World EP
description: Even on a brief EP, Yves Tumor’s prismatic world seems to get bigger as it mutates into certain conventions of goth rock, dream pop, and shoegaze.

title: Blue Heron
description: Chicago multi-instrumentalist Nick Levine’s solo debut will feel familiar to Pinegrove fans but struggles to expand on the band’s formula.

title: fabric presents Overmono
description: Traversing classic UK genres like 2-step and jungle, the duo’s first commercial mix doubles as a celebration of multiculturalism in modern Britain.

title: Faith
description: Pop Smoke’s second posthumous album sounds like it’s solely designed to generate clicks as a new generation of rap fans continues to be exploited for their streams.

title: lately I feel EVERYTHING
description: Willow’s fourth solo album continues to unpack her lifelong struggles with the extremes of human emotion, using a trove of pop-rock stylings from nu-metal to pop-punk to somewhat mixed effect.

title: Muvaland Vol. 2 EP
description: The no-holds-bar rapper and producer weave a tight tapestry of musical references that only hundreds of hours spent sweating to music by queer elders could produce.

title: Tell Me About Tomorrow
description: The 20-year-old TikTok personality turned punk rocker’s debut album won’t stop announcing how punk it is.

artist: Rey Sapienz / The Congo Techno Ensemble
title: Na Zala Zala
description: Powered by brittle electronic drums and buzzing synths, the Congolese musician’s debut album is simultaneously bleak and exhilarating.

title: The Soft Bulletin Companion
description: Originally released in 1999 as a promotional CD-R, this collection of alternate mixes and non-album tracks bridges the gap between the band’s experimental hijinks and pop instincts.

title: Sling
description: On her second album, reluctant Gen Z ambassador Clairo turns back the clock, embracing classic touchstones of 1970s folk.

title: TX, ’98
description: The debut EP from this reverential emo band is full of nostalgia, wonder, and autobiographical detail, like a Linklater film soundtracked by Deep Elm Records.

title: Luminol
description: With cosmos-filling drones and blazing noise, the third album from Madeline Johnston’s experimental pop project feels ambitious and communal.

title: Hideaway
description: Working with producer Dave Sitek, Nathan Williams returns with another mixed bag of combative rock songs that are straightforward to a fault.

title: Diva
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Annie Lennox’s 1992 solo debut, a joyous and liberated pop album with a prophetic message about the disillusionment of fame.

title: Kirtan: Turiya Sings
description: These 1981 devotional recordings for voice and Wurlitzer, meant to guide meditation through chanting, offer an alternate version of the cosmic jazz visionary’s synthesizer masterpiece, Turiya Sings.

title: It’s Just Wind
description: New Zealand psych rocker Connan Mockasin’s collaborative album with his dad, Ade, has bad jokes, stream-of-consciousness poetry, and an odd, undeniable appeal.

title: Dee Gees - Hail Satin
description: Dave Grohl’s six-piece finds common cause between gaudy disco-pop and willfully absurd arena rock on an album-length collection of Bee Gees covers and live-in-studio Medicine at Midnight cuts.

title: Sob Rock
description: Sob Rock is the sound of a man alone in his success. Even if this is one of John Mayer’s stronger albums, the whole thing feels self-consciously minor.

title: Banoffee Pies White Label Series 01
description: Breakout UK producer Tim Reaper and his collaborator Comfort Zone convey the power and possibility of jungle.

title: Hologram
description: With a new rhythm section and tighter performances, the noisy New York band’s latest EP moves deliberately from chaos to catharsis.

title: 20+ Piano Improvisations
description: The Monterrey-based experimental musician abandons the outward trappings of electronic music on his latest album, a hushed collection of cryptic etudes that flicker in the margin between the played and the programmed.

title: Ry Ry World
description: The 23-year-old singer’s careful observations add new profundity to her storytelling. Her second album confirms her place as one of modern R&B’s realest talkers.

title: Space Jam: A New Legacy
description: Much like the cinematic remake, which functions as nothing but an advertisement for the entire Warner Media library, the Space Jam soundtrack is soulless and gratuitous.

title: Mythopoetics
