description: Created during a residency at Gainesville’s Pulp Arts studio, Nandi Rose’s latest album as Half Waif is complex, daring, and emotionally unsettled.

title: UY Scuti
description: The Nigerian rapper and singer’s easygoing charm guides this lush and freewheeling collection.

title: Fun Is Not a Straight Line
description: Sasu Ripatti—aka Vladislav Delay and Luomo—returns to footwork with his first album-length attempt at the form, translating the genre’s fast-paced syncopations into a harsh, elemental blast.

title: Last Year Was Weird, Vol. 3
description: The Australian musician caps an adventurous trilogy of EPs with another round of plush, laid-back songs that effortlessly mix pop, rap, R&B, and reggae.

title: A Color of the Sky
description: Guided by the inquisitive lyrics of singer Audrey Kang as she narrates the process of searching for self through song, the band’s lush third album feels like a ride-along to the creative process.

title: Moot!
description: Raime’s Joe Andrews and Tom Halstead, together with percussionist Valentina Magaletti, swap their customary electronics for muscular, guitar-driven sounds influenced by bands like Slint and Unwound.

title: Sin City
description: On his new mixtape, the South Florida rapper hones the blade of his technical precision while his peers take direct stabs at crossover success.

title: Twin Shadow
description: George Lewis Jr.’s self-titled fifth album is an island of good feelings and vacuous summertime indie-pop jams.

title: Nastavi, Calliope
description: Singer and songwriter Maya Bon’s bedroom-pop dirges are both intimate and removed, filled with understated yet strangely meaningful detail.

title: Yasuragi Land
description: On his first proper full-length in three years, the Japanese electronic musician collages tiny sounds into intricate grooves that harness the wonder of everyday life.

title: Vice Versa
description: The nascent pop star attempts to move beyond reggaetón on his latest album, but he never fully commits to any particular direction.

title: Mirror II
description: The Brisbane trio immerses itself in cavernous, eerie post-punk to soundtrack the uncanny horror of young adulthood.

title: Origin of Symmetry
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the grandiose British rock band’s second album, a supranatural space odyssey powered by all-too-human emotion.

title: Exit Wounds
description: On their first album in nearly a decade, Jakob Dylan and co. return with highway ballads and Saturday afternoon rockers, sounding like the classic rock band they’ve always ached to be.

title: I LIE HERE BURIED WITH MY RINGS AND MY DRESSES
description: The Zambian Canadian rapper and producer’s third album is heavy and suffocating, cranking up the murk and intensity to reveal the relief within unbridled anger.

title: Alpha
description: On her debut album, the Toronto singer-songwriter and producer draws variously from gospel, folk, and adult-contemporary influences; no matter the style, every song is a showcase for her powerful voice.

title: Agor
description: Arriving a full 10 years after his debut single, Welsh producer Lewis Roberts’ first album is a bravura display of brain-bending editing that’s more concerned with big feelings.

title: Vince Staples
description: Produced entirely by Kenny Beats, the album’s reserved musical approach magnifies the blunt scene-setting Vince has used to build his name over the last decade.

title: The Nightmare of Being
description: On the strongest album of their unlikely second act, the Swedish melodic death metal band lets their weirder side take the reins.

title: Rain’s Break
description: The UK musician’s latest release is her most substantial work yet, adding a new sense of momentum to her ambient dream pop.

title: Golden Doubt
description: The Melbourne jangle-pop quartet hits all the right ‘80s pleasure points with an understated sense of humor and anthemic songcraft.

title: SGV1
description: The New York City rap crew’s latest is a mansion of sweet beats and vocal textures that bring a whole new level of professional polish to their sound.

title: The Hustle Still Continues
description: Three 6 Mafia’s tireless frontman has done it all as an artist and collaborator, which is why it’s disappointing to see him combat his ageless production with uninspired guest features on his new deluxe album.

title: castles / CASTLES II
description: Newly released on streaming services, the pair of mixtapes Peep and Tracy put out on SoundCloud five years ago capture the instinctive way their voices blend and break over each other.

title: Former Things
description: Manchester post-punk musician Julie Campbell’s third album is dense with possibilities, whiplashing between past and future. The maximalism isn’t big-picture, but granular: busy, hyperreal instants by the millions.

title: Será que ahora podremos entendernos
description: The Guatemalan musician’s second album explores the friction between interiority and exteriority; blooming with ecstatic synth riffs and spirited cello, the record captures the sound of a mind abuzz.

title: Let the Soil Play Its Simple Part
description: Centering her own voice for the first time, Caroline Shaw proves to be a master of collapsing boundaries, whether between her performer-composer roles or the corporeal and the immaterial.

title: Space & Time
description: The newly independent singer’s latest project is designed to make her stand out in a crowded R&B field but falls short of any singular, defining moments.

title: The Veiled Sea
description: An extended investigation of the electric guitar solo, the latest record from Ben Chasny’s experimental project is graceful and surprising.

title: Planet (i)
description: On Ella Williams’ second album as Squirrel Flower, the road is a space of intimacy and disaster. Her vivid songwriting and bright, searching voice bring both sides to life.

title: United States Live
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Laurie Anderson’s grand theatrical treatise, an avant-garde piece comprised of sound sculpture and rock music, gender and social studies, philosophy and linguistics.

title: Tezeta
description: A long-lost recording captures the Ethiopian organist and his band at the Hilton Addis Ababa in 1975, laying down deceptively breezy jazz songs steeped in nameless longing.

title: Who Hurt You? EP
description: The 23-year-old songwriter’s debut renders tales of young love and its quandaries with diaristic lyrics and anguished singing. She’s at her best when she’s plainspoken and immediate.

title: Born This Way the Tenth Anniversary
description: A decade ago, Lady Gaga created an enormous, bravura flex of electronic pop. An anniversary edition arrives with six “reimagined” versions of its songs by LGBTQ+ artists and allies.

title: Get Up Sequences Part One
description: Indie aesthetics have changed considerably in the past two decades, but the UK group is still throwing block parties for a utopia where time and genre collapse.

title: Get Lost in the Music EP
description: The New Jersey singer-songwriter’s five-song EP tries out different frames for her strikingly powerful voice, variously exploring reggaetón, futuristic Americana, and psychedelic club pop.

title: Valdez
description: The noisy, cosmic trio of Philadelphia DIY lifers returns with an unearthed studio album. It’s an upgrade in fidelity and a shit-ton of fun.

title: The Last Ride
description: Once united in their status as industry misfits, the four-man supergroup has reassembled for a fan-service album that hinges upon a certain taste for bars.

title: NINE
description: The elusive UK group’s third album in just over a year—to be made available online for only 99 days—renders Black trauma in the eerie, sing-song cadences of children’s rhymes.

title: Fat Niggas Need Love Too
description: The Flint-raised, Houston-based rapper is known for his outrageous punchlines, but the engine of his raps is the personality-filled flow and the piano-driven Michigan beat.

title: Quietly Blowing It
description: Despite its grand scope and good intentions, the latest album from M.C. Taylor is the sound of an artist beginning to repeat himself: lite music for dark times.

title: Death of a Cheerleader
description: Equally indebted to pioneering girl groups and her punk heroes, the New York singer-songwriter’s debut is a fiery exploration of love, anger, and coming-of-age.

title: Dark in Here
description: A gloomier companion to 2020’s Getting Into Knives, John Darnielle’s latest is patient, tense, and full of empathy.

title: Fate in Seven Lessons
description: The post-punk band’s new seven-song collection owes a conspicuous debt to New Order, and while the presentation begs to be called “spooky,” they’re having fun with it.

title: Fatigue
description: The Brooklyn songwriter and sound artist’s second album is a kind of spiritual accounting, a swirling blend of orchestral groans and human whispers that evokes subconscious drift.

title: Soundness of Mind
description: Informed by their study of Zen Buddhism, Danielle L. Davis and Steven Whiteley create spacious, playful synthesizer melodies that push at the boundaries of what “meditative” music can be.

title: How Much Time It Is Between You and Me?
description: Recorded in a mountain village, the Russian ambient musician’s debut album molds field recordings and hushed vocals into a form that’s richly textured and occasionally unsettling.

title: Mood Valiant
description: No longer content with merely capturing the sound of four wildly talented musicians in a room together, the Australian “future soul” group transforms on their vibrant and psychedelic third album.

title: To Enjoy Is the Only Thing
description: The Melbourne-based songwriter’s debut is sparse and hypnotic, drawing connections between her experiences of leaving a relationship and leaving a religious upbringing.

title: The Turning Wheel
description: The myth-skewing, Oakland-based artist is a chameleonic pop singer on her third album. Whimsical and urgent, these are fairy tales meant to wake us up.

title: Call Me If You Get Lost
description: With DJ Drama in tow, Tyler thrives in the realm of the rap mixtape, which allows him great freedom to explore every facet of his talent as a producer, writer, and vocalist.

title: The Stranger
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Billy Joel’s greatest album, a sublimely crafted breakthrough that finds the meeting ground of the romantic and the mundane.

title: The Golden Casket
description: The band’s first new album in six years is a procession of pinging, clanging, reverberating tactile pleasures, an inventive backdrop for Isaac Brock’s familiar blend of forced optimism and unforced paranoia.

title: Planet Her
description: The third album from the extremely chaotic pop star, battle rapper, and edgelord is a thrilling ride that puts her eclecticism on full display.

title: Icons
description: The composer and percussionist’s latest work is intricate and eerie, drawing attention to the small sounds that slip unnoticed in the chorus of a busy day.

title: I Know I’m Funny haha
description: There is so much depth to Faye Webster’s dazzling fourth album. It strikes a perfect balance between classic country stoicism and the sound of the saddest person you follow on social media.

title: Escapades
description: The French musician’s giddily maximalist solo debut maintains the spirit of his group Justice’s debut album; though inspired by ’70s prog and disco, it inhabits a singular universe of its own invention.

title: After the Storm
description: By blending everyday stories with spacey beats, the Savannah rapper makes the mundane unexpectedly entrancing.

title: Year of the Horse
description: On this elaborate concept album, initially released in monthly installments, the hardcore collective reclaims its status as the most fearless prog-punk band of them all.

title: I Love My Mom
description: The Asheville songwriter’s newly reissued debut divulges her restless thoughts through folksy garage-pop that’s both vulnerable and fierce.

title: Home Video
description: Addressing faith, young love, and nostalgia, the songwriter’s autobiographical third album is empathetic yet unsparing, catchy and finely crafted.

title: I Still Miss Theresa Benoit
description: The Oakland band’s darkly psychedelic country folk suggests things on the verge of collapse. In March 2020, as singer Sawyer Gebauer unwittingly contracted COVID-19, that was truer than anyone knew.

title: Stardust
description: Mamiffer’s Faith Coloccia pressed her music—faintly liturgical songs and sound poems about self and motherhood—onto dubplates for turntablist Philip Jeck to smear and distort, to uncanny effect.

title: Back of My Mind
description: The long-awaited debut from the lauded singer and guitarist is a fine showcase of her immense talent, though the constant balladeering doesn’t really capture what she does best.

title: Disco!
description: MIKE’s place in the vanguard of New York underground rap has invigorated him. It would be a stretch to call this album happy, but the atmosphere is undeniably warmer and more hopeful.

title: Wary + Strange
description: An intensely personal document, the Tennessee singer and guitarist’s third album examines the realities of being a Southern Black LGBTQ+ woman in songs both defiant and vulnerable.

title: The BBC Sessions EP
description: A set of intimate, in-studio performances from Matthew Houck’s creative breakthrough in the early 2010s reveals new meaning and intensity in his tough-hearted songs.

title: Delusive Tongue Shifts - Situation Based Compositions
description: His name is short for “The International Billionaire’s Secret Love Child,” and his ambient pieces are weightless as a sigh, splotchy as a bruise, both cozy and unsettling.

title: Taste of Love
description: Continuing to mature into a more grown-up image, the nine-member K-pop girl group balances self-contentment and romantic confidence with breezy summer thrill-seeking.

title: Mother Nature
description: Collaborating with artists like Mr Eazi, Burna Boy, and Sampa the Great, the Beninese icon builds upon a proudly pan-Africanist musical vision that celebrates the power of community.

title: Our Extended Play EP
description: On a collaborative EP with the 1975’s Matty Healy and George Daniel, the former TikTok phenom devotes herself to the ambiance of late-’90s guitar-pop.

title: Broken Hearts & Beauty Sleep
description: With flourishes of R&B, house, and funk, this exuberant and sweltering nine-track mini-album nails the transition from left-of-center cult favorite to bona fide diva.

title: About You
description: The Amsterdam-based electronic musician trades his habitual house and ambient productions for blissful bedroom pop influenced by the shoegaze music of his youth.

title: The Lion and the Cobra
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit an uncompromising debut, pop music that ventures to the extremes of sound and emotion.

title: Hall of Fame
description: The Chicago rapper takes a step further into the mainstream on his third album, an ultimately hopeful exploration of how trauma manifests.

title: Black Metal 2
description: The sequel to 2014’s beloved Black Metal is a brief but thrilling project from the mercurial artist, featuring the most approachable music of his career.

title: Peace or Love
description: After a 12-year hiatus, the Norwegian duo returns with an especially airbrushed take on easy-listening pop. At their best, the Kings sound deceptively effortless, but the facade is sometimes too smooth.

title: Ancient Dreams in a Modern Land
description: The unmistakably dramatic pop singer seeks the divine feminine, embracing a bold yet soft aesthetic that’s more effective than some of her lyrics.

title: Blue Weekend
description: The UK band’s enormous third album is pristine and emotionally extravagant, the platonic ideal for contemporary big-tent rock music.

title: Islomania
description: On their first album in five years, Nick Thorburn’s ever-evolving band takes a pop-friendly turn. With neon synths and disco grooves, these songs are Top 40 at heart.

title: Absence
description: In this 2015 set marking his retirement from live performance, the veteran improvising guitarist explores the simpler, starker side of his abstract, purposefully formless music.

title: Jordi
description: Maroon 5’s seventh album sets out to experiment beyond their comfort zone. It sounds like a band trying desperately to appeal to as many markets as possible.

title: Culture III
description: The rap trio’s latest, like its predecessor, can become a slog and at times seems shoddily constructed. But at its best, the album is a callback to their inspired peak.

title: Slitherman Activated
description: The Rochester rapper is at his best when he isn’t folding to the pressures of wider appeal or tightly-packaged collaborations on his latest project.

title: Path of Wellness
description: On their first self-produced record and first in 24 years without drummer Janet Weiss, Sleater-Kinney find pleasant comfort and not much else with down-the-middle rock tunes.

title: SDM​-​LA8​-​441​-​114​-​211
description: This unlikely electronic trio—featuring the Chili Peppers’ John Frusciante, Venetian Snares’ Aaron Funk, and noise musician Chris McDonald—cherry-picks from 11 years of dazzlingly complex improvisations.

title: Limitless Frame
description: Layering reverberating guitar melodies with subtle electronic sound design and foggy atmospheres, the ambient musician formerly known as Ulla Straus has a way of making the vaporous feel intimate.

title: Finally EP
description: The Los Angeles-via-Toronto singer offers a finely wrought EP that showcases her oceanic voice and her austere songwriting.

title: No Gods No Masters
description: With pop stars once again performing garish exaggerations of what seems like real personal trauma, Shirley Manson & co. have timed their return perfectly.

title: Troubled Paradise
description: The proudly campy hyperpop singer’s debut is vibrant and ridiculous, for better or worse.

title: Mommy Issues EP
description: With influences ranging from Afrobeat to choral symphonies, the Brooklyn-based group’s debut is bright and bursting with detail.

title: Bombay
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the groundbreaking 1995 soundtrack that changed Bollywood forever.

title: Degrees of Freedom Found
description: The fearless work of the late avant-garde pianist is celebrated with a momentous new anthology, showcasing his immense talent and passion.

title: Pressure
description: The Texas rapper’s second album shows a great talent struggling to find her place while focusing on what she does best: aggressive, take-no-prisoner bars.

title: time machine
description: After a viral sample made her feathery vocals famous, the singer-songwriter arrives on her own terms with a debut that flits effortlessly between guitar-based soul, alt-pop, and R&B.

title: Butterfly 3000
description: Album number 18 was recorded in the band’s homes during the pandemic, and trades psych-rock blitzes for a finely-woven sprawl of synth programming and MIDI sequences.

title: The Life of Pi’erre 5
description: The fifth installment of the rapper-producer’s long-running series lands closer to the sweet spot between beats and bars glimpsed on his previous effort.

title: SCURO CHIARO
description: Built around his new custom synthesizer, the latest from the electronic musician and Nine Inch Nails member showcases the vast potential of both the instrument and the artist behind it.

title: The Rich Are Only Defeated When Running for Their Lives
description: Backed by veteran jazz musicians and newer players, the Trinidad-born, London-based poet summons spirits of the Caribbean diaspora to ask what it might take to build a better world.

title: Hildegard
description: Montreal musicians Ouri and Helena Deland recorded their debut album together in eight days; the album’s eight songs feel like the diary of a gradual mind meld.

title: Pool
description: Compiling several years’ worth of material and spanning nearly two hours, the Munich producer’s first full-length since 2018 feels cohesive, virtuosic, and thrillingly physical.

title: Nafs at Peace
description: On their debut album, the Lahore band blends the free-form improvisation of Hindustani classical and jazz with sample-heavy production creating a musical dialogue about faith, spirituality, and the self.

title: epiphany
description: The teen rapper’s dreamy yet dark mixtape leans into gruff flows and gun-toting punchlines with a wink.

title: Jade 玉观音
description: The Berlin producer is a master of negative space and biomechanical sound, lacing her uneasy compositions with voices that excavate images of unceasing loneliness and longing.

title: Picnic
description: Connecting Kansas City and Melbourne, Picnic’s debut full-length is rounded out by a more than an hour’s worth of remixes by artists like Huerco S. and Dntel—a celebration of ambient music as a social phenomenon.

title: The Codex Necro
description: The Birmingham duo’s 2001 debut introduced their nightmarish hybrid of black metal, grindcore, and electronic music. On a new reissue, it sounds as extreme and subversive as ever.

title: Eternity
description: Drawing inspiration from narrative thrust of video-game soundtracks and sound design of trap and trance, the London producer revels in melodramatic builds and spaced-out bliss.

title: Light Armour EP
description: On his first release in six years, the UK producer trades the atmospheric grime of his debut for a more driving techno sound, lush enough for headphones but punchy enough to keep one foot on the dancefloor.

title: The Voice of the Heroes
description: While not quite a marquee work for either artist, the new team-up is reliably consistent and casts them as a natural pair, near-ideal complements to one another in writing and execution.

title: If It’s Any Constellation EP
description: On her second EP for Mark Ronson’s Zelig Records, the London multi-media artist proves herself a canny, sophisticated pop stylist with a taste for tales of millennial disaffection.

title: Jubilee
description: Michelle Zauner embraces the spotlight and goes for the brass ring on her third album, a stylish and eclectic record that feels of the moment and also steeped in classic indie sensibilities.

title: Reflection
description: The London producer’s third album tests the boundaries of dance music not just for the sake of experimentalism, but as an expression of vulnerability and a vehicle for self-knowledge.

title: Clarity
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the Arizona band’s third album, a giant canvas of rock and pop songwriting that wears its heart on its sleeve.

title: Soberish
description: The alt-rock icon returns with tasteful, timeless rock arrangements on a record about friendship, sobriety, and the love she’d like to receive.

title: This Time I’ll Be Of Use
description: The trio’s debut album shifts casually between soulful rap, textured noise, and pensive folk with grace and sometimes too much distance.

title: The Work Is Slow
description: On their debut album as a quartet, Greg Fox, Melvin Gibbs, Sasha Frere-Jones, and Grey McMurray find common ground in psychedelic post-rock jams that are both sprawling and supremely focused.

title: Avow
description: The Australian metal band’s sixth album is dense and disorienting, collapsing the boundary between the human voice and machine-made clamor.

title: Changephobia
description: The producer and songwriter’s second solo album is a romantic exploration of uncertainty, a rush of momentum softened by his trademark sounds.

title: Doomin’ Sun
description: The collaborative album by Jay Som’s Melina Duterte and Palehound’s Ellen Kempner tells compelling and rarely heard stories, but doesn’t reach the same highs as their respective solo work.

title: The Sky Is Bleeding EP
description: The latest EP from the Irish singer is a set of introspective, velvet-crushed balladry, as much a cohesive mood piece as a collection of individual songs.

title: The Fool
description: The Swedish rapper scales back some of his rave ambitions on his most distilled creative package yet as he becomes something approaching a star.

title: Feed Me Weird Things (25th Anniversary Edition)
description: First released in 1996, Tom Jenkinson’s debut album feels like a time capsule of the era’s drill’n’bass and jazzy jungle. It’s steeped in inventive rhythms, gorgeous melodies, and giddy fun.

title: The Waves Pt. 1
description: The product of lockdown recording and late-night walks through London, the Bloc Party frontman’s fifth solo album is as low-key and eccentric as he’s ever sounded.

title: Hidden Treasure
description: The veteran rapper continues to leverage the same well-worn blueprint on his latest album, which plays like a back-to-basics revue.

title: Navy’s Reprise
description: Coming on the heels of two stellar 2020 albums, one of the best new voices in underground hip-hop sounds a little looser and lighter, but still keeps his raps bracingly personal.

title: Get on Board the Soul Train: The Sound of Philadelphia International Records Vol. 1
description: The new box set examines the early years of Gamble and Huff’s Philadelphia International Records, a soul-music label that defined its city the way Stax did Memphis and Motown did Detroit.

title: 3MB feat. Magic Juan Atkins
description: This 1992 meeting of Moritz von Oswald, Thomas Fehlmann, and Juan Atkins is a monument to the improbable transatlantic alliance that techno forged between Detroit and Berlin.

title: Exodus
description: Though it’s full of guests and emotional twists and turns, the late rapper’s posthumous album is largely sloppy and inconsequential, a sour note to bookend a storied legacy.

title: 3 Sessions in a Greenhouse
description: Recorded over three long, inspired days in a studio north of Rio and newly remastered for its 15th anniversary, this is as solid a dub outing as has issued from anywhere beyond Jamaica.

title: AZEB EP
description: On this tightly curated EP, the insightful R&B singer revises the elements intrinsic to her work, providing new meditations on Blackness, womanhood, and love.

title: Live in Stuttgart 1975
description: This 1975 set captures the band reconnecting with the psych-rock fury of its primordial years, drawing from a cleaned-up recording of a super-fan’s tape.

title: Cavalcade
description: The UK band stakes out even more ground on their glorious second album. The chord changes are more elaborate, the rhythms more twisted, the pretty parts prettier, the heavy parts heavier.

title: Perfect EP
description: The Philadelphia band returns as a three-piece on a pandemic-era EP that introduces subtle shifts in sound and structure. It’s their first release that’s as tender as it is tough.

title: When Smoke Rises
description: On his debut solo album, the Toronto artist formerly known as Mustafa the Poet confronts grief and dispossession over understated production with folk-music overtones.

title: Off the Yak
description: The Brooklyn rapper’s latest project is a ready canvas for her technical skill and well-earned boasts, but she’s at her best when she digs deeper.

title: Pray for Haiti
description: On one of his most ambitious and definitive projects, Mach-Hommy reunites with Westside Gunn and puts on an unforgettable clinic with his razor-sharp bars and an exceptional eye for detail.

title: How to Leave Your Body
description: The Italian-born, London-based EBM auteur thaws out his industrial chill and embraces optimism, celebrating the fragility and strangeness of human experience with uncommon earnestness.

title: Penelope Three
description: The Australian-born, UK-based musician hones her songwriting and polishes her production without losing the atmospheric qualities that made the first two albums in this trilogy so captivating.

title: Phoenix Rise
description: The drummer builds on the transnational foundations of his last ambitious album, making the case for global citizenship and international solidarity through culture-spanning music.

title: Sensational
description: Though heavily inspired by ’90s and ’00s R&B, the Portugal-born, Danish musician grows into a quietly commanding presence of her own on her second album.

title: Between the Richness
description: Fiddlehead’s second album doesn’t stray far from the band’s foundational qualities: gruff but approachable, intense without being aggro, emo but not emo.

title: Whole Damn Body EP
description: A new EP of songs originally recorded for 2011’s Hello Sadness illustrate just how well the band’s simultaneously twee- and emo-adjacent indie rock holds up.

title: All I Know So Far: Setlist
description: The pop singer architects her legacy with a new documentary and live album from her 2019 tour. As a performer, she’s fun and loose, even as her newest music feels more like a means to an end.

title: Seeking New Gods
description: The Super Furry Animals frontman’s latest is a concept album about an ancient volcano on the China-North Korea border that ranks among his most imaginative solo records.

title: Showtunes
description: Following a string of albums deconstructing Lambchop’s sound, Kurt Wagner continues to reinvent his band, this time using MIDI-assisted piano melodies to write love songs to music itself.

title: Kommunity Service
description: The team-up between two West Coast rappers suggests an inspired combination, but it pays off only in intermittent bursts.

title: DR. EV4L
description: The Atlanta rapper does not go pop on this release, choosing instead to dive deep into his unique blend of horror tales and unsettling production.

title: WINK
description: The omnivorous Japanese band’s Sub Pop debut exudes a newfound sense of serenity, even as they remain committed to exuberant self-love.

title: Not the Girl
description: The Brighton-based singer’s second album exquisitely recreates the sound of early ’70s AOR, with songs that go straight to the despondent heart.

title: The Best of Lily Konigsberg Right Now
description: The cheekily named compilation includes songs from three solo releases, alongside unreleased tracks and bedroom demos that offer a shining mosaic of the New York singer-songwriters indie-pop acumen.

title: Sara Bug
description: On her debut album, the Nashville-based singer-songwriter and her extraordinary voice search for a place to call home.

title: No. 1 in Heaven
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the brilliant 1979 album from the Mael brothers that transformed them into future-pop prophets.

title: Sparkles & Debris
description: The Canadian singer and songwriter’s fourth album is an ambitious collage of ’90s R&B and orchestral dramatics, welded together by her versatile, gossamer voice.

title: Monastic Love Songs
description: On his solo debut, the Red River Dialect frontman explores personal, spiritual, and musical growth after his nine-month retreat at a Nova Scotia Buddhist monastery.

title: SOUR
description: Four months after “drivers license,” pop’s newest star offers a nimble and lightly chaotic collection of breakup tunes filled with melancholy and mischief.

title: A Little More Time With Reigning Sound
description: Reuniting the Memphis lineup of his long-running band, former Oblivian Greg Cartwright reveals the depth of his appreciation for classic American rock and soul sounds.

title: Black to the Future
description: Shabaka Hutchings leads his brass band on a propulsive mind- and body-moving record, advocating through music that change comes from speaking directly about collective oppression.

title: TV62
description: The Danny Brown collective’s new album is a solid extension of their brand of gully Detroit music delivered with a crooked snarl.

title: Medieval Femme
description: Following the camp-infused club music of 2017’s Shaneera, Al Qadiri once again examines questions of gender and representation in the Arab world, this time invoking women poets of the Middle Ages.

title: Afrique Victime
description: The Tuareg guitarist and his bandmates deliver the fullest picture of his gifts yet. Recorded piecemeal during tour breaks, the album captures the group’s easy chemistry and explosive energy.

title: The Alias Sessions
description: Developed in collaboration with the Alias dance company, Fernando Corona’s newest solo album is a swirling miasma of ominous drone and murky rhythm that hums like an electrical substation.

title: Be Right Back
description: With stripped-back instrumentation and poignant emotion, the English singer’s latest release is a stopgap EP that punches above its weight.

title: Blessed, I Guess
description: Amid the humble Florida rapper’s croons and raps about life and pain, there’s a unique voice that’s starting to emerge.

title: Daddy’s Home
description: Annie Clark brings the glammy sounds of the ’70s to an album about mothers and daughters, fathers and prison. It’s an audacious and deeply personal record occasionally beset by clunky choices.

title: Telephonebooth
description: The NYC rapper’s latest is a 22-minute blast of dank, dingy, experimental rhymes that feels too fleeting to be a long-term stylistic shift.

title: Love Suite
description: The South Carolina vocalist and producer presents an attainable vision of R&B on his latest EP, an unpretentious suite of pure bedroom music greater than the sum of its vibes.

title: Khaled Khaled
description: The producer and luxury furniture seller gathers the biggest names in rap once again for a market-researched album that’s as repetitive as his catchphrases.

title: The Off-Season
description: On J. Cole’s refreshing and lively new album, the rapper relaxes his grip around the mic and thrives when he’s collaborating, not when he’s making deadly serious legacy raps.

title: Dedicated 2 Disrespect EP
description: The Philadelphia-born, Berlin-based producer, a former GHE20G0TH1K affiliate, follows a run of incendiary mixtapes with a four-track EP of lacerating, irresistibly kink-positive techno.

title: Charva Anthems EP
description: The boisterous UK trio adds polish to its organ house and bassline rap, balancing lyrical economy with over-the-top boasts and catchy choruses.

title: On Tilt EP
description: Reviving Untold’s Hemlock label from a four-year slumber, the UK producer returns with an EP of stripped-down basement tracks bridging dubstep’s early years with club music’s future.

title: Mirror Guide
description: On his latest album, Keith Rankin programs a virtuosic MIDI cello, tempering awe-inspiring moments with potent reminders of its synthetic nature.

title: Discovery: Live in Rio 1994
description: Originally released as a concert film but now reissued as a live album, this cult favorite reimagines the Pet Shop Boys’ own canon and other pop hits, curating a century of pop music history in one jukebox.

title: The Score
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the 1996 album from the hip-hop trio, a socially conscious blockbuster grounded by the realities of the immigrant experience.

title: Rupt and Flex (1994-96)
description: A four-disc set looks back on the brief, fertile period in which the British band twisted conventional rock instrumentation into increasingly arcane shapes. They still inhabit a class of their own.

title: Ice Melt
description: On their second album, the Brooklyn quartet sinks deeper into their dread-filled chill-out sound, but they become sharper and more focused in the process.

title: Gayest Tits & Greyest Shits: 1998-2017 12-inches & One-offs
description: A collection of Terre Thaemlitz’s gorgeous and thought-provoking deep-house 12"s turns a critical eye on history, identity, and club culture.

title: Faygo Baby EP
description: The Ohio rapper’s new EP makes a compelling case for his brand of self-aware cynicism.

title: Delta Kream
description: As Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney breezily enter their third decade together, they pay tribute to and put their own spin on the Mississippi blues, turning it into something that sounds supple and comforting.

title: TY4FWM
description: On his feature-heavy new album, the Oakland rapper takes stock of his achievements so far while looking toward a new stratum of success with clear-eyed gratitude.

title: More Energy Fields, Current
description: Reworking improv sessions featuring frequent collaborators like Sam Gendel, Jamael Dean, and Laraaji, the L.A. bandleader and percussionist shows his contemplative side.

title: First
description: The Japanese jazz saxophonist’s debut arrived at the intersection between traditional and unfamiliar, mannerly and chaotic. A new reissue restores it to its rightful place.

title: Van Weezer
description: Rivers Cuomo’s latest is a tribute to his hair metal heroes, but it never goes all that hard.

title: Shock Power of Love EP
description: Serving up his customary collage of UK garage rhythms, forlorn vocals, sugary trance synths, and copious vinyl hiss, Burial is at his most emo on a new split EP.

title: 4 New Hit Songs
description: Veering from bubblegum house to shoegaze, the producer and singer captures the intimacy of the dancefloor.

title: Archive Series No. 5: Tallahassee Recordings
description: Sam Beam’s earliest recordings reveal a songwriter and singer already secure in his eccentricities. Far from sounding tentative, these songs are more like a lost Iron & Wine album.

title: Street Sermons
description: The Fayetteville rapper’s debut album is at its best when he shines a light on his darkest moments and traces his glow-up step-by-step, imbuing each word with purpose.

title: Watch Out! EP
description: Countering the isolation of the past year, the UK house producer draws upon classic club sounds in an EP guided by the life-giving virtues of community.

artist: Jack Ingram / Miranda Lambert / Jon Randall
title: The Marfa Tapes
description: Somewhere between a demo collection, a live album with no audience, and a lo-fi left turn, the ad-hoc country trio’s desert recording session focuses on the simple joys of songwriting.

title: The Music Industry Is Poisonous
description: Massachusetts songwriter Cooper Handy’s naive, bizarro-world pop is a portal to a dimension weirder and more vivid than this one.

title: Bright Green Field
description: The English band’s nervy debut blazes through scraps of jazz, funk, krautrock, dub, and punk. More than a canonized style, it’s their level of control that sets them apart.

title: Axacan
description: Straying from the niche where he made his name, the fingerstyle guitarist layers his playing with field recordings and electroacoustic techniques, to cryptic but compelling ends.

title: Fiver With the Atlantic School of Spontaneous Composition
description: Simone Schmidt and company navigate interior and exterior life with country-inflected improvisations that stretch out like a long summer afternoon.

title: Music for Living Spaces
description: In composing radiant new-age music inspired by plants, the Los Angeles-based musician encourages a sense of empathy with nonhuman life.

title: There Is No End
description: A posthumous album captures the legendary drummer and Afrobeat icon at his most copacetic and polished, meeting collaborators at their level even as he urges them to his.

title: The Gilded Palace of Sin
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the cosmic country rockers’ 1969 debut, a strange, short-lived truce in the long battle between hippies and squares.

title: Boogie Shoes: Live on Beale Street
description: This live set captures the former Big Star frontman for a 1999 one-off in Memphis, where he serves up a feast of soul-music staples backed by the city’s legendary Hi Rhythm Section.

title: Build a Problem
description: Although Dodie Clark came to fame for her chatty and intimate viral videos, she proves the exception to the rule about internet stars making terrible music. Her debut studio album spotlights the sparse and self-conscious folk-pop she’s been making for nearly a decade.

title: Seek Shelter
description: With production by Peter Kember and an added gospel choir, the Danish band’s fifth album completes their transformation from grim-faced nihilists to wearied soothsayers.

title: Suburban Indie Rock Star EP
description: With sharp DIY production and earnestly self-aware lyrics, Eric Reyes’ debut radiates familiar, understated emo-pop charm.

title: Latest Record Project, Vol. 1
description: It’s a terrible night for a moondance: On this risible and intermittently lovely 28-song collection, Van indulges in some of his most cherished paranoid theories and deepest-held grudges.

title: Cake Pop 2
description: Dylan Brady’s experimental pop troupe finds idiosyncratic takes on late-aughts pop, but gets bogged down by great gecspectations and its leader’s own overwhelming influence.

title: Yasuke
description: In his score to LeSean Thomas’ anime series about a Black samurai in medieval Japan, the Los Angeles musician aligns his visual obsessions with his wide-ranging musical instincts.

title: Guess Who
description: On this mini-album, the K-pop girl group struggle to maintain the audacious energy that first put them in the spotlight.

title: Gami Gang
description: Ambitious, self-referential, and packed with their signature bad puns, the D.C. emo-punk duo’s double album hones in on the nostalgia and sincerity that lies beneath all adolescent woe.

title: if i could make it go quiet
description: The 22-year-old pop songwriter’s debut captures the onslaught of young-adult emotion, longing for a state of being where noise and confusion are replaced by certainty and clarity.

title: SKA DREAM
description: The indefatigable punk icon reworks his anthemic 2020 album No Dream as ska, and wouldn’t you know, it works.

title: Play With the Changes
description: The Toronto singer’s latest is a time capsule of moody 2010s R&B, distinguished by its introspection and near-claustrophobic melancholy.

title: Shelley FKA DRAM
description: The Virginia crooner reintroduces himself with a set of sumptuous, retro R&B that’s a soothing, dapper fit for his impressive vocal range.

title: Rosegold
description: On her least country album to date, the Nashville songwriter flattens out the twang and borrows from pop and hip-hop, to mixed results.

title: Diptych
description: Across two long, imperceptibly evolving tracks, the veteran drone duo delivers a pair of luxuriant tonal sound baths.

title: Earth Man Blues
description: The garage-rock institution rolls on with a loosely conceptual album that is equally inconsistent and ingenious, containing some of Robert Pollard’s most direct lyricism.

title: Superwolves
description: 16 years after their original underground classic, Matt Sweeney and Will Oldham reunite for an album that plays like the continuation of a decades-long conversation.

title: Second Line: An Electro Revival
description: For almost two decades, Dawn Richard has been increasingly beholden to nothing but her own satisfaction as an independent artist. Her sixth album is a decadent testament to her maturation.

title: The Fellowship
description: The latest album from the Toronto saxophonist, best known for his work with Destroyer, is an inventive work of auditory storytelling exploring his own fraught religious background.

title: Pink Dogs on the Green Grass
description: The cartoonist and drummer for the post-punk quintet Pottery explores gently lysergic visions on his psych-pop solo albums.

title: Hanazono
description: Refining her approach, the Japanese musician shifts from singer-songwriter confessionalism to open-ended abstraction on this textured, ambient record.

title: Joan Armatrading
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the British folk-rock singer’s 1976 album, a brilliant display of musicianship from a songwriter attuned to the mysteries of desire and heartbreak.

title: This Is Telex
description: A new compilation recaps the career of the Belgian synth-pop trio, whose futuristic kitsch stretched from the Eurovision Song Contest to the roots of Detroit techno.

title: Rare, Forever
description: Setting aside his penchant for elaborate concept records, the UK producer zeroes in on what makes his productions so singular, balancing immaculate sound design with compelling club rhythms.

title: She Walks in Beauty
description: Faithfull pairs her forever-soothing voice with the words of the Romantic poets who inspired her, over tasteful accompaniments from Bad Seeds sonic architect Warren Ellis.

title: Endless Arcade
description: The Scottish band’s eleventh album feels uniquely pensive, even tentative. Nearly every song will have you humming along, though few seem designed to grab your attention.

title: Don’t Go Tellin’ Your Momma
description: The Montclair, NJ-based rapper follows his breakout debut with an expansive, funk-embroidered recollection of his childhood, complete with an accompanying 35-minute film.

title: Architecture III
description: For the final installment in his years-long genre study of house music, the L.A. funk prophet takes a different structural approach while maintaining a minimalist spirit.

title: A Gangsta’s Pain
description: At his best, the stalwart Memphis rapper excels at heart-on-sleeve, bluesy songwriting, and his new album shows him deepening and opening up.

title: Nurture
description: Coming seven years after his debut, the North Carolina EDM producer’s second album alternates between euphoric pop and muted ambient work, exploring the difficulty of finding fulfillment and lasting peace.

title: Crooked Machine
description: More intimate and less reverential than a traditional remix album, collaborator Richard Barratt’s full-length rework casts Róisín Machine in deeper shades of modern house and techno.

title: Inbred EP
description: In Hayden Anhedönia’s moody, gothic soundscapes, the ageless persona of Ethel Cain confronts the religion, sex, and violence lurking within the confines of small-town America.

title: Pulling Teeth EP
description: On a set of ominous club tracks billed as a dystopian concept record, the Bristol native brings an industrial edge to that city’s deeply ingrained soundsystem sensibilities.

title: Michigan Boy Boat
description: Lil Yachty consummates his unlikely relationship with Michigan rap on a mixtape pairing him with mainstays like Sada Baby and Rio da Yung OG.

title: I Can’t Explain EP
description: The DFA stalwart delivers a set of psychedelic, late-night club cuts that invoke the dancefloor at its most immersive.

title: Vulture Prince
description: The Pakistan-born, Brooklyn-based composer draws from jazz, Hindustani classical, and folk to create a heartbreaking, exquisite document of the journey from grief to acceptance.

title: Flat White Moon
description: On their eighth album in 16 years, the veteran British art rockers smooth out some of their eccentricities but lose some of their swagger in the process.

title: From tha Streets 2 tha Suites
description: Snoop’s new album, the latest in a quietly prolific period as he closes in on 50, reminds us of the simple pleasures of his still-virtuosic voice when set against booming, funk-inflected production.

title: descension (Out of Our Constrictions)
description: Joined by veteran saxophonist Evan Parker, Joshua Abrams’ exploratory jazz ensemble delves into a single piece that stretches to 75 minutes and seems to pass in no time at all.

title: Lazer Guided Melodies
description: On their debut, Spiritualized seemed to emerge from the ether perfectly realized, creating rock music that was serene, spaced-out, and shamelessly untroubled.

title: Inked in Red
description: Fronted by an Afghanistan war veteran turned firefighter and EMT, the Athens, Georgia, goths offer a take on the genre that’s both strikingly melodic and informed by the horrors of lived experience.

artist: Young Thug / Gunna / Young Stoner Life
title: Slime Language 2
description: The latest compilation from Young Thug’s YSL label is packed with appearances from rap’s biggest stars, though its flamboyant host seems content to take a backseat.

title: Ask the Ages
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we examine the monumental final album by a singularly talented guitarist with a conflicted relationship to his instrument and an ecstatic vision for his music.

title: My Parade
description: Now on his own label, the internet rap originator explores all his favorite styles—warbling rap, theatrical rock and pop—and the results are consistently joyous.

title: 9696 Dream
description: Manchester producer Evan Majumdar-Swift mines the history of club music for slippery, enigmatic electro jams that move in unexpected directions, sounding melancholy yet playful.

title: Sweep It Into Space
description: Featuring co-production from Kurt Vile, the classic trio’s latest reunion album is their breeziest and most melodically generous yet.

title: Almost Nothing Is Nearly Enough
description: Pete Kember follows up his first album under the Sonic Boom moniker in 30 years with a remixed version that stands as its own discrete work, as impassioned and cohesive as the original.

title: Crossing Over EP
description: The Bay Area trio takes several beats to slow down and expand on a nice EP that mines indie rock and slowcore for its finest components.

title: Draw Me a Silence
description: The peripatetic electronic artist takes inspiration from her Tunisian Berber heritage with her new alias. Full of yawning spaces and dembow-like rhythms, the music explores a space where body music and head music become one.

title: Tears to Grow EP
description: Channeling the scrappy ache of ’90s emo, the New York City band’s DIY rock songs voice the joy and catharsis of creating in community.

title: Exoplanet
description: Accompanied by a like-minded troupe of intergalactic travelers, the Bitchin Bajas member brings together jazz composition with far-out electronic sound design.

title: The Who Sell Out (Super Deluxe)
description: Celebrated with an elaborate new box set, their 1967 pop-art experiment remains the band’s dark-horse favorite, when they were scrappy enough to laugh at themselves but strong enough to write the music that would define their career.

title: a softer focus
description: The San Antonio-based musician brings newfound expression to her customary field recordings, folding richly harmonic elements into her typically cryptic palette of clatter and hum.

title: La Maquina
description: The Griselda rapper’s second album of 2021 is his statement of reinvention, a neat balance between glitz and grime.

title: American Spirit EP
description: The Detroit producer and vocalist leads a brief, unvarnished tour of his home city, allowing sounds and samples to function as landmarks in a woozy deep-house landscape.

title: Civilisation II EP
description: The news is hardly any less grim since 2019’s Civilisation I, but the UK pop trio’s second entry considers the emotional toll of disaster with ingenuity, wit, and a warm, bright sound.

title: Never the Right Time
description: Marking 10 years since he set off down his path of dour, slow-motion techno, the Manchester musician returns to his familiar palette of ashen moods and richly textured electronics.

title: Heaven’s Just a Flight
description: Powered by her commanding voice, the L.A. songwriter’s debut casts questions about family, relationships, aging, death, and the afterlife in buzzing neon hues.

title: Fearless (Taylor’s Version)
description: Taylor Swift’s project to re-record her albums to reclaim legal ownership of the music begins here with 2008’s Fearless, an almost identical, polished, and somewhat melancholy version of it.

title: Rakka II
description: On his second album inspired by journeys in the Arctic wilderness, Finnish electronic musician Sasu Ripatti makes even the most hostile environment feel homey.

title: Keys
description: The Chicago guitarist and the North Carolina multi-instrumentalist work wonderfully together and channel many spiritual influences with great warmth and ease.

title: Pale Horse Rider
description: The Wand frontman’s second solo record blows open the chamber pop of his first for a lysergic and unsettling take on cosmic Americana.

title: Drum Temple
description: Inspired by a panoply of club-music styles like gqom, UK funky, and tribal, the Mexican producer’s music revels in eroding barriers between percussive techniques.

title: epic Ten
description: Sharon Van Etten invites a handful of artists to cover songs from her 2010 album epic. These new versions—played by Fiona Apple, Lucinda Williams, and more—reveal the music’s healing power and complexity.

title: Married to the Money II #MTTM2
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we examine the young South Carolina rapper’s profoundly influential moment in the spotlight.

title: McCartney III Imagined
description: Sir Paul presents a resequenced, alternate-universe version of last year’s trilogy-completing release, as performed by Beck, Phoebe Bridgers, St. Vincent, Dev Hynes, Damon Albarn, and more.

title: Violence Unimagined
description: Decades into their career and on their 15th album, the death metal legends have become their genre’s Rolling Stones: iconic, verging on cartoonish, always reliable.

title: Birdy Island
description: The soundtrack to an imaginary theme park where people reconnect with nature and spirituality, the Beijing producer’s album combines traditional Chinese references with wild electronic experimentation.

title: Californian Soil
description: The UK electronic-pop trio’s third album draws on a renewed sense of extroversion and energy, which can’t always overcome its lyrical and production missteps.

title: ULTRAPOP
description: The third album from the Detroit collective is an exceptional melding of hardcore, noise, and pop. Abstract concepts aside, the Armed makes thunderous and discordant music move with great finesse.

title: Twixtustwain EP
description: After COVID foiled the tour behind their debut album, the London pop chameleons return with an EP that lurks in the shadowy spaces of claustrophobia, existential dread, and the sadness of a long pandemic winter.

title: Mommy Don’t Spank Me
description: The Drums made their name on jaunty surf pop, but a collection of little-heard songs from their early years explores themes of longing and heartbreak that guided Jonny Pierce from the start.

title: Doom Mix, Vol. V
description: The fifth annual compilation from Los Angeles’ Doom Trip label is a survey of contemporary vaporwave that doubles as a snapshot of a particularly vital corner of the electronic underground.

artist: Vijay Iyer / Linda May Han Oh / Tyshawn Sorey
title: Uneasy
description: Even as they negotiate complex parameters of rhythm and harmony, the trio’s expertly attuned playing evokes the openness of improvisation, and the urgency of justice.

title: ROADRUNNER: NEW LIGHT, NEW MACHINE
description: The hip-hop collective’s sixth album refocuses on melody and economy, resulting in the group’s most focused and impressive record yet.

title: Spotify Is Surveillance
description: The musician and activist’s new album speaks truth to streaming giants, trans exclusionists, and extremely online leftists, but hits its stride at its sweetest and most nostalgic.

title: War
description: The Ohio rapper’s new EP devours a half-decade of online scenes and styles and spits them out into a psychedelic combination that often feels overly referential.

title: Shades of Flu 2
description: In the second installment of his “COVID-themed” remix series, the Brooklyn-based drummer-producer reworks jazz classics and modern recordings.

title: Music
description: The Dutch songwriter follows behind-the-scenes work with Rex Orange County, The Free Nationals, and others with a breezy new solo record. Featuring collaborations with Mac Demarco and Emily King, the album does a good job distilling his charms into a single package.

title: NOW
description: The bandleader, composer, and pillar of Chicago arts and culture follows up the acclaimed 2019 LP he recorded with the Black Monument Ensemble with another grand and luminous statement.

title: I Became Birds EP
description: The Floridian emo band channels a sense of boundless possibility on their new LP, which has the heft of a manifesto despite its compact length.

title: The Things I Can’t Take With Me EP
description: On a stopgap EP between album projects, the Brooklyn R&B musician sloughs off emotional baggage from a soured relationship.

title: Seeds, Thy Divine Thresher
description: The experimental rapper from Richmond, Virginia raps, speaks, and sings over a strange amalgamation of beat sculptures, glitchy melodies, and found audio. The effect is dizzying and alluring.

title: Memoryland
description: The Montreal producer fondly glances back at his formative musical memories of the late 1990s: commercial electronica and alternative rock, in all their occasionally kitschy glory.

title: Broken Mirror: A Selfie Reflection
description: Taking cues from Miles Davis’ electric period, the Spacebomb Records founder and Alabama sculptor join forces on a mesmerizing album rooted in improvisation, risk-taking, and unlikely musical chemistry.

title: Pulse of Defiance
description: Fusing elements of free jazz, breakbeat, acid house, dub, ambient, and more, the Tokyo producer’s second full-length album is simultaneously comforting and destabilizing.

title: These Are Not Fall Colors
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we examine the lone and remarkable album from the Olympia, Washington band, a noisy, youthful, and chaotic expression of indie rock in the early ’90s.

title: S·F·X / The Endless Talking / Paradise View / Mercuric Dance
description: Four new reissues explore the acclaimed Japanese producer’s work c. 1984-1985, as he set aside techno-pop in favor of spacious, imaginative ambient music.

title: TRIANGLE
description: The acclaimed jazz bassist’s latest project, a three-part suite inspired by meditation and healing practices, seeks to alleviate the stress and upheaval of a pandemic year.

title: Fake Fruit
description: The Oakland band’s wide-ranging debut is a whirlwind of biting critique, nervy post-punk guitars, and absurdist humor. Rarely does a first record speak with such a trenchant voice.

title: Tabia
description: The Punjabi rapper-producer’s genre-hopping second album paints a richly detailed picture of a psyche buffeted by turmoil. Wildly ambitious in sound and scope, it raises the bar for India’s hip-hop vanguard.

title: ENTERTAINMENT, DEATH
description: The outstanding album from the Philadelphia electro-psych trio is reclusive, cryptic, late-night paranoia music. Their oblique songs can evoke an entire landscape of feeling in very few words.

title: Fuck It Up EP
description: Joyful, euphoric, and free, these new songs from the Miami party-starters are all produced by SOPHIE and are full of potential energy and the excitement of exploration.

title: Dope Game Stupid
description: The Detroit rapper’s standout debut is among the year’s most engaging rap albums so far, packed with disarming metaphors, humor, and introspection.

title: PXE EP
description: Over a fleeting 10 minutes, the Swedish artist swings between confidence and insecurity and explores an exciting new direction.

title: ARENA02
description: The 40-song label compilation from Argentina’s AGVA Records is a prismatic and circuitous immersion into the sounds and aesthetics circulating across Latin America.

title: Dancing With the Devil…The Art of Starting Over
description: After an overdose nearly ended her life, Demi Lovato sings powerfully and directly about her past and who she wants to become.

title: F\K Da World
description: The Detroit rapper’s latest mixtape is a vivid anthology of first-person vignettes driven by a deep sense of paranoia.

title: Course in Fable
description: The singer and guitarist takes a new, rangy, proggy direction with an artful touch, finding some psychedelic wisdom between the profound and the mundane.

title: Bills & Aches & Blues
description: A benefit compilation from the venerable UK label 4AD sets its roster loose on its back catalog for a varied set of covers that uphold the imprint’s exploratory spirit.

title: Year of the Orc EP
description: Channeling sugar-rush synths and bracing noise, the Philadelphia producer continues his quest to make pop music stranger and more head-spinning—and to test listeners’ ability to follow the twists and turns.

title: YDFWC?
description: The bilingual underground New York rapper with the gift of gab has put out many tapes in the last five years, but this might be his goofiest and most affable—it suits him well.

title: Paradigmes
description: The French psych rockers’ send-up of mythic American road trip fantasies is undeniably fun, even if the humor and hooks don’t approach anything like real insight.

title: Happy Birthday, Ratboy
description: To celebrate its 10th anniversary, the Chicago group pairs new recordings of songs from 2011’s RATBOY EP with a collection of early rarities, contrasting cozy nostalgia with hard-rocking instincts.

title: Head of Roses
description: Even as she surveys heartbreak and self-doubt, Jenn Wasner’s second solo album sounds confident. Textural layers of guitar and synth offer depth, yet allow her voice to lead the way.

title: Wading EP
description: Led by 19-year-old Jana Bahrich, the fiery emo duo tackle big existential questions and turbulent emotions in four short songs that throw off promising sparks of brilliance.

title: G_d’s Pee AT STATE’S END!
description: For a quarter-century, the Canadian chamber ensemble has made hold music for awaiting a revolution. Suddenly, on their seventh album, they sound hopeful it could come.

title: Bodies of Water
description: The auspicious debut from the Chicago indie rock trio has the spontaneous feel of close friends bonding before the universe has a chance to pry them apart.

title: Joyce Manor
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the influential debut from the SoCal band, a pop-punk spark that spread like wildfire in the Tumblr era.

title: Scorpion
description: On her second album, recently reissued for its 20th anniversary, the lone woman of Ruff Ryders took the reins and made the loudest statement of her career.

title: Fantas Variations
description: A diverse array of musicians reinterpret a standout from the Italian synthesizer composer’s 2019 album Ecstatic Computation, but only a handful recreate the metaphysical wonder of her work.

title: New Long Leg
description: The London art-rockers’ outstanding debut is a droll album full of surreal images, bizarre obsessions, and sense memories. The cumulative effect of Florence Shaw’s narration is inexplicably wonderful.

title: Blush
description: Moving beyond his label’s grounding in UK soundsystem styles, the Wisdom Teeth cofounder shows newfound devotion to melody, texture, and feeling.

title: Renée Reed
description: Steeped in Acadian musical heritage, the Louisiana songwriter’s sketchy four-track recordings and odd, dreamy storytelling evoke the likes of Jessica Pratt or Elliott Smith.

title: Made Out of Sound
description: Refusing to be hemmed in by quarantine, the veteran improvisers took the unusual path of recording separately: drums first, then overdubbed guitars. The results are genuinely life-affirming.

title: How Many Times
description: The New Orleans country singer’s heartsick, headstrong third album chronicles the fallout of bad breakup with sly humor and empathy.

title: $mokebreak EP
description: The pair’s second record of lo-fi rap collaborations is technically bulletproof, the bars masterfully patterned and relayed with gusto. Still, the songs don’t always fulfill their potential.

title: VISIONLAND
description: The Alabama rapper’s debut offers few worthwhile insights into him as a person and ends up stalling on its own ambition.

title: Haram
description: On their collaboration with the Alchemist, the duo of ELUCID and billy woods drag postcolonial wounds onto the examination table. They don't just embrace the darkness; they wear it as a protective cloak.

title: Half a Human EP
description: Collecting a few leftovers from their 2020 album The Main Thing, Real Estate continue to expand the sound of the band as well as their song lengths to mixed results.

title: The Longest Interlude
description: The pop singer-songwriter’s debut album leans on alluring and woozy R&B and hip-hop, yet the music forgoes most of the memorable hook-writing that Starrah has made her name on.

title: Dum and Dummer 2
description: The Memphis rap duo reunites for an impressive sequel that’s as natural and effortless as an old friendship.

title: Menneskekollektivet
description: The debut LP from the duo Jenny Hval and Håvard Volden is a warm-blooded exploration of the sensuality of the artistic process.

title: Live in… New York City
description: The Australian singer-songwriter looks to the warm, easygoing sounds of ’70s troubadours on an album that rarely demands attention, only politely asks for it.

title: Green to Gold
description: The New York band’s first album in seven years sounds like a post-rock orchestra playing around a campfire. It’s the sound of hard-won peace of mind, rendered in the lightest brushstrokes.

title: Blexxed Rec
description: Inspired by the Beatles circa Revolver, Mike Donovan’s lo-fi marauders fuse their habitual folksy garage and fantastical psych into a wily sound fleshed out with Mellotron and tape echo.

title: Cherry
description: After nearly a decade in the psych-rock group Quilt, Rochinski offers a bold, buoyant debut that mingles propulsive riffs with off-kilter instrumentation and lyrics that make heartbreak and disillusionment sound like a party.

title: DEACON
description: Josiah Wise’s second album is an eager, effervescent tale of romance, outlining a genealogy that stretches from gospel to the shiny, gossamer R&B of the ’90s and ’00s.

title: Introspection / Introspection Reimagined
description: The Los Angeles singer’s mellow, folk-inflected R&B explores give-and-take in relationships with others and with ourselves. A companion release revisits her recent EP, adding texture and emotion with live instrumentation.

title: OH NO
description: Jamie Stewart duets with more than a dozen indie, punk, and experimental music colleagues, and what results is a surprisingly sweet meditation on friendship, with nary a try-hard shock to be found.

title: Songs in A Minor
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Alicia Keys’ outstanding 2001 debut, a self-produced, Chopin-inspired R&B album that blazed a unique path to mainstream superstardom.

title: Assembly
description: This new compilation adroitly selects high-water marks from Strummer’s solo career while never quite ameliorating the “what if” questions that haunt the Clash’s legacy.

title: Collections from the Whiteout
description: Working with Aaron Dessner, the English singer-songwriter trims down his compositions and expands his comfort zone, experimenting with elements of jazz and historical fiction.

artist: Floating Points / Pharoah Sanders / The London Symphony Orchestra
title: Promises
description: The all-star collaboration between a producer, a saxophonist, and a symphony is a celestial event. But it’s Pharoah Sanders’ playing that holds it all together, a clear late-career masterpiece.

title: Statistique Synthétique / Teum (the Silvery Slit)
description: On a split LP, the German computer musician and South Korean cellist apply unusual methods to their respective instruments, approaching the synthesis of digital and acoustic from opposite sides.

title: Like a Good Old Friend EP
description: With joyful house beats and emotive production, producer Joe Thornalley’s latest EP offers a more approachable side of his sound.

title: Playground in a Lake
description: Following the recent turn toward acoustic instruments in his soundtrack work, the UK electronic polymath investigates neoclassical modes on an album inspired by climate change.

title: Voyage Out
description: The Chicago four-piece’s debut oscillates between beauty and dissonance with masterful subtlety, finding new shades of delicacy within math rock.

title: Songs for and About Ghosts
description: With help from Owen Pallett, the long-running experimental duo maps a sprawling path through seemingly unconnected musical ideas; the result is an enveloping overload of ideas and inspirations.

title: To See the Next Part of the Dream
description: The lo-fi shoegaze project from the Seoul musician is a rare find. The ambitious and alluring music expertly captures the feeling of a sound so uncannily familiar that it truly feels like a dream.

title: Under~Between
description: Andrew PM Hunt’s fourth album as Dialect blends vaporwave, field recordings, and sketch-like fragments into an unbroken whole. The result owes as much to collage as to composition, with an emphasis on flow.

title: A History of Nomadic Behavior
description: As the New Orleans sludge-metal icons clean up their act, Mike IX Williams’ once-indecipherable howls and Jimmy Bower’s detuned blues riffs come to the surface.

title: Fresia Magdalena EP
description: The Berlin-based artist pays tribute to her native Lima, Peru in bittersweet house music that wears its spiritual yearning on its sleeve.

title: Zack Snyder’s Justice League (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: The release of Zack Snyder’s Justice League offers both the director and soundtrack composer Tom Holkenborg the chance to indulge their every whim. The resulting movie and score are both aggressively long, ambitiously overstuffed, and deeply polarizing.

title: Justice
description: Underneath the ill-advised MLK quotes, you’ll find an earnest pop album that unearths the charisma and agility that helped make Bieber a star.

title: Solar Paroxysm
description: Jacob Buczarski’s cerebral, complex melodic black metal is an elegy for a dying planet. There is little hope on offer here, but plenty of silvery, well-executed riffs.

title: Alkisah
description: Mixing metal and noise with ritualistic howls, the Indonesian duo’s seventh album is a thrilling, at times ecstatic serenade to the collapse of civilization.

title: Survive EP
description: On their latest EP, the band crumples up angst and complacency and offers a simple, singular diagnosis: you may feel numb, but fight.

title: Still Woman Enough
description: The 88-year-old country icon has created a loving tribute to herself that spans generations, proving there's still vitality and relevance in her work.

title: DJ-Kicks: Special Request
description: UK house and breakbeat veteran Paul Woolford connects the dots between club-music styles from across the decades, finding a through line in lush, transporting melodies.

title: Creation Never Sleeps, Creation Never Dies: The Willie Dunn Anthology
description: The First Nations songwriter receives his overdue recognition with this brilliant and troubling anthology, which shows the breadth of his skill. Nearly every song is remarkable, and nearly any of them could have served as a breakthrough.

title: What’s Growing
description: The New Zealand indie rock band’s thoughtful, witty, and brief songs pit surrealism against the malaise of workaday life.

title: Rapture
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Anita Baker’s timeless 1986 album, a slow-burning and symphonic piece of quiet storm R&B that floods every sense.

title: The Poet / The Poet II
description: This latest reissue from the legendary soul singer features some of the greatest love songs ever made. It also reminds us of a tall and tarnished legacy left behind.

title: The Plugs I Met 2
description: On his latest nine-track triumph, the Griselda star finds an easy chemistry with Harry Fraud, whose syrupy samples lend poignancy to these stories of hustling and survivor’s remorse.

title: World’s Most Stressed Out Gardener
description: Holed up in his DIY inventor’s laboratory,  VanGaalen delivers his most abrasive, unstable collection in years. Even this notorious Canadian recluse can't stop a little apocalyptic dread from creeping in.
The Oakland rapper known for his standout scam records sinks into a more reflective mood on his latest LP. The cost of this pensive turn is a loss of personality.

title: Chemtrails Over the Country Club
description: Lana Del Rey’s sixth album dials back the grandiosity in favor of smaller, more intimate moments. It carries a roaming spirit of folk and Americana without losing the romantic melodrama of her best work.

title: Number One
description: On her dazzling solo debut, the Toronto multi-instrumentalist proves herself a musical Swiss Army knife, capable of anything and reveling in her multiplicity.

title: Theory of Ice
description: On an album with the musical charms of British art-rock, the Indigenous writer and scholar uses our connections with water to explore the revolutionary power of community.

title: Clamor
description: After a debut album that reinterpreted Iberian folk for a contemporary audience, the Catalan duo turns toward the future, adding electronics and collaborating with Holly Herndon and Kronos Quartet.

title: Do It With a Smile
description: The Nashville-based hardcore punk band’s exhilarating debut is a call-to-arms that could inspire even the most acquiescent to take action.

title: Xiao Gong
description: The Chinese-American multi-instrumentalist's works are sensuous and lively but evoke a vast loneliness.

title: The Moon and Stars: Prescriptions for Dreamers
description: On her new album, the Memphis singer-songwriter and guitarist pens her most heavy-hearted songs, treating love and loss like old scars, fondly remembered.

title: Yaral Sa Doom
description: Senegal’s Arouna Kane and Sweden’s Karl Jonas Winqvist, plus a host of musicians on two continents, spin improv sessions and long-distance overdubs into airy, dreamlike music as generous as it is joyous.

title: Poster Girl
description: Years into her solo career, Larsson is still just a disembodied voice floating over the beat. On her third album, she tries out some different sounds, but the result comes off like a Who's-Who of 2011 radio.

title: Lost Navigator
description: Filled with sampled ephemera and vintage television clips, the rapper’s latest EP looks to science fiction for a pessimistic, paranoid vision of the present.

title: Spaceman
description: To cut through and leave a lasting impression of Nick Jonas, the artist, would require a vision much bolder than what this album has to offer.

title: J Jazz Volume 3: Deep Modern Jazz From Japan
description: On the third release from its ongoing reissue series, the BBE label continues to excavate the hidden wonders of Japan’s post-WWII jazz scene.

title: All Caps EP
description: The Egyptian producer’s music is forceful, corrosive, unstable-sounding. His latest EP, a collection of six unrelenting club cuts, is his heaviest record yet.

title: Everything Nice EP
description: The Ontario band arrive full-formed on a musically polished, emotionally ragged mini-album that testifies to the enduring potency of emo and pop-punk symbiosis.

title: Gang of Four: 77-81
description: The UK post-punk pioneers’ influence always outshone their popularity, but a new box set makes a convincing case that stardom actually was within their reach.

title: Melodies in the Sand
description: Fusing early music, ambient, and folk, the Czech couple’s work has entranced fans like Sufjan Stevens and Bryce Dessner for decades. This collection is an enchanting portal into their furtive sound world.

title: Lazy
description: The London producer and label boss’ third album responds to a year of uncertainty with a mixture of club-friendly styles and melancholic touches for the lonely wee hours.

title: Nunsexmonkrock
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the iconoclastic German singer’s solo debut, an album inspired by punk rock, Jesus, aliens, and a mother’s love.

title: Do You Want More?!!!??!
description: The singular hip-hop band’s second album is a story about America and Philadelphia, memory and survival. Like a good book, it goes by quickly, yet you force yourself to linger.

title: New Music and Big Pop
description: The Philadelphia indie rock trio’s debut is gentle in both sound and spirit. Singer Michael Doherty can turn simple moments of reflection into marquee statements with his outstanding voice.

title: Immediately Remixes
description: A carefully curated set of reworks filters last year’s Set My Heart on Fire Immediately through synth pop, techno, and other electronic lenses, giving Mike Hadreas’ grit a blast of glitter.

title: Notes With Attachments
description: Two notable sidemen collaborate on an elusive instrumental album inspired by funk, West African, and Cuban music. The melodies are fleeting and the arrangements ever-shifting.

title: Really From
description: Fusing bookish indie jazz with emo and math rock, the Boston quartet explores the complications of identity while dismantling stale indie-rock paradigms.

title: As Days Get Dark
description: On their first album in 16 years, the Scottish duo situates themselves in the current moment, teasing out new modes of songwriting while remaining as wry, dark, and self-lacerating as ever.

title: Teen Week
