description: The 17-year-old digicore producer’s debut centers them as a vocalist and songwriter, mapping out feelings of insecurity and loneliness against production that is perpetually in motion.

title: End of the Earth EP
description: One of hip-hop’s brightest young minds finds himself in a state of deep reflection, maturing into adulthood in real time on his latest EP.

title: Memory Lane
description: The Baltimore rapper continues to earn his “Captain Hook” nickname on an album full of Murda Beatz’s sometimes too-spare production.

title: Eau de Bonjourno
description: The Toronto group set oddball existential queries at the center of a shapeshifting rhythm section, collaging together pop fundamentals with a vast collection of musical knick-knacks.

title: Duke Nukem
description: Quality Control’s secret weapon sticks to his crunk roots on his new album while also venturing into the most known unknown.

title: Way Down in the Rust Bucket
description: Recorded in 1990 at a small Santa Cruz club, this joyous live document flips the energy of 1991’s Weld on its head, swapping out incendiary arena rockers for oddball picks and warm, woolly vibes.

title: Thumbing Thru Foliage
description: The L.A. rapper teams with producer ewonee for a lean and low-stakes album, but its strength is in its brevity.

title: Quiet Life
description: A new reissue of the UK group’s 1979 album captures David Sylvian and his bandmates as they evolved from their glam-influenced early years into the experimental electronic pop of their final two LPs.

title: When You See Yourself
description: On their eighth album, the Followill brothers desperately cling to a sound that has stopped working, trying to write songs that soar but capable only of ones that wallow.

title: 1/f EP
description: On the heels of a new signing, the singer remerges with a four-track EP that reworks songs from her previous albums, coupling the flexibility of her original compositions with daring musicianship.

title: Only the Family - Lil Durk Presents: Loyal Bros
description: Chicago drill star Lil Durk cedes the floor to his capable crew on a 23-song victory lap that memorializes his own hard-earned fame alongside the memory of his late protégé, King Von.

title: Driver
description: Stevie Knipe’s third LP builds layered arrangements and a renewed sense of confidence without sacrificing the earnest, confessional vulnerability of their songwriting.

title: Denzel Curry & Kenny Beats: Unlocked 1.5
description: The duo’s refurbished EP gets the typical sequel treatment, with new characters and a glossy finish that makes you miss the gritty original.

title: These 13
description: On their first sustained collaboration since the Squirrel Nut Zippers disbanded, Bird and Mathus draw from a range of old styles, primarily gospel, with the ease of old friends getting together for coffee.

title: Heaven and Holy
description: Woods founder Jeremy Earl and Americana veteran Glenn Donaldson team for an effortlessly warm debut that feels alive with a sense of mutual discovery.

title: BGM
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the Japanese band’s technically masterful, tremendously expensive 1981 album, a record that looms over 40 years’ worth of electronic production.

title: Heisei No Oto: Japanese Left​-​field Pop From The CD Age, 1989​-​1996
description: A new compilation digs deep into stacks of jewel cases and explores an inflection point in Japanese pop music where changes in technology brought changes in sound.

title: The American Negro
description: The multi-instrumentalist and composer’s concept album about Black existence cites everything while saying nothing. The record collapses under its own inertia.

title: Metal Bird
description: Clearing the lo-fi haze of her previous work, the Los Angeles-based songwriter’s third album reveals astral Americana hymns that hover somewhere between the dirt and the stars.

title: flashes in time
description: Even on this brief EP, the London producer’s music is becoming more confident and idiosyncratic, moving beyond familiar club contexts in search of points unknown.

title: Show Me How You Disappear
description: Jilian Medford’s third album is bigger, brighter, cleaner, and more ambitious. Even when she’s hollering, she sounds dwarfed, standing vulnerable but unafraid amid towering emotions.

title: Yol
description: On their third album, Amsterdam’s finest Turkish psych revivalists add synths and drum machines to spirited ’70s standards from the Anatolian funk canon.

title: Vol. 4 (Super Deluxe)
description: Made in L.A. under the influence of colossal amounts of cocaine, the heavy metal legends’ fourth album, recently reissued, made room for both light and shade and featured several of their signature songs.

title: The Truth Hurts
description: Drakeo’s second project of all-new material since being released from prison is more relaxed and less bitter than his first. There’s a subtext to every flex; he’s been through the wringer, and this is his time to celebrate.

title: Fresh Bread
description: Fifty-two tracks deep, this archival compendium might seem like a catch-all. In fact, it’s a chance to peek under the hood of the multi-instrumentalist’s creative process.

title: Cheetah Bend
description: Pairing experimental sound design with varied rap and R&B features, the Detroit producer’s hyperpop-tinged LP doubles as a tribute to the spirit of SOPHIE, his late friend and collaborator.

title: K.G. / L.W.
description: On this double album, the madly prolific psych-rock band synthesizes everything they do into compact songs that still allow their weirder impulses to flourish.

title: Polydans
description: The German producer’s smooth dance-pop is meant to be played under bright festival lights—and it’s never sounded less convincing.

title: Pack Pro Nobis
description: The Catalan folk duo makes music full of unnameable longing and buzzing with portent. The remixes included, from John Talabot and Mans O, cannot compete with the simple sound of their voices.

title: The Shadow I Remember
description: As the Cleveland band returns to Electrical Audio at full force, they retain their penchant for rueful concision and world-weary chronicles of pandemic existence.

title: Tidibàbide / Turn
description: On an album generous in both spirit and proportion, the Montreal-based musician fuses traditional Algonquin influences from her upbringing with synth pop, strings, and experimental vocal techniques.

title: Music Life
description: The Los Angeles-based singer-songwriter’s 12th album is a lucid, jazzy, and unique entry in her catalog. The complex, hypnotic arrangements belie the warm simplicity of her verse.

title: Carnage
description: Nick Cave’s cinematic work with his bandmate Warren Ellis is a slight departure from last decade’s trilogy of albums. It’s defined by its stark contrasts, at turns brutal, surreal, and romantic.

title: In Ferneaux
description: On his fifth solo album, Fuck Buttons’ Benjamin John Power channels industrial menace and ambient dread to ask a timely question: What is real life, and will life ever feel real again?

title: Harlecore
description: The PC Music alum surveys the history of rave, sucking serotonin from its gleaming extremes: teeth-chattering trance, Thunderdome-worthy techno, and psychedelic chill-out.

title: AAI
description: The experimental duo have long embraced music’s anarchic potential, and their latest project, exploring the nuances of machine intelligence, might be their most confounding and ambitious.

title: 100 Miles and Walk’in
description: The Bronx rapper pulls you into his orbit with dark humor and trademark absurdity on his latest project, more focused than any of his previous work.

title: Duke
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the 1980 album from the shapeshifting UK prog band, a pivotal moment in their journey to pop-rock stardom.

title: Electrically Possessed (Switched On Vol. 4)
description: The fourth volume in the endlessly innovative group’s long-running series reminds us that they often dropped their best work away from their full-lengths.

title: Little Oblivions
description: On her third album, Julien Baker’s self-lacerating storytelling gets a more expansive canvas to work with. The big, full-band sound makes all the small moments of pain surreptitiously devastating.

title: Like Sunlit Threads
description: Departing from the high-impact electro of his Galaxian alias, Scottish producer Mark Kastner explores more contemplative strains of ambient and IDM.

title: Life Support
description: Rooted in authenticity but still layered in artifice, the rising pop singer’s debut is ambitious yet shallow, seemingly intent on proving its own seriousness.

title: Endeavor
description: The Brooklyn-based rock quartet’s mild, uptempo debut coasts on good vibes but won’t convince anyone they’re living dangerously.

title: In Spite Of
description: The Columbus quartet approaches hardcore from weird and skronky angles, but they tear shit down because they have a specific vision for what they want to see in its place.

title: Echo
description: Co-produced by Adrianne Lenker, the Australian songwriter’s debut is a dark little star of intimacy and intensity. The atmosphere is rapt, the silences charged.

title: Trench Baby
description: The 23-year-old rapper shows the most promise on his sophomore album when he dials down the menacing grit and focuses on how his emotions have shaped his current reality.

title: Believer
description: The appealingly unpredictable debut from the Norwegian duo thrives off the dueling forces of unease and temptation.

title: Forever in Your Heart
description: After their sudden dissolution last year, the Toronto noise duo return just as suddenly with a new album. Like their previous work, it’s full of pain, dissociation, and hopelessness—and surprisingly, a new tranquility.

title: The Tipping Scale
description: Drawing upon her background as a choreographer, the Brooklyn-based singer-songwriter explores the mind-body connection in her serene and dramatic synth music.

title: Dialogue.
description: With their dusky, languid jazz-rap, the Norwegian duo stakes its own territory in hip-hop’s ever-expanding diaspora.

title: Open Door Policy
description: Dark, ominous, but still marching forth with that same bar-rock passion, the Hold Steady feel more unified, making a place for each member within their music’s newfound sprawl.

title: Might Delete Later
description: On his Fools Gold debut, the anxious and acerbic rapper knows he’s rounded a corner in his career, but remains on edge, his eyes glued to the rearview mirror.

title: Nerve Bumps (A Queer Divine Dissatisfaction)
description: On his debut solo album, the Oakland experimental musician utilizes custom-built software systems that allow him to navigate around disability, with electrifying results.

title: Something Else EP
description: Across five breezy, feel-good songs, the rising Afropop star continues to explore the overlap between the sounds of Ghana and those of his native Nigeria.

title: Trauma Factory
description: The emo-rap artist rebounds from a sophomore slump with an album that glows with conviction and sometimes-uncomfortable honesty.

title: iii EP
description: Rather than packing their recordings wall-to-wall with furious riffing and tricky time signatures, these Canadian post-punks leave space for each element to build tension.

title: Ífaradá EP
description: The Nigerian-born, London-based musician pulls from blues, highlife, post-punk, and more on a short, fiery EP that details the struggle to rise above the pain of the everyday.

title: As the Love Continues
description: The Scottish band is on familiar ground, patiently building mountainous songs suffused in nameless sadness, but they sound energized by the darkness—and refreshingly resistant to self-seriousness.

title: A Billion Little Lights
description: Splitting the difference between War on Drugs and Death Cab for Cutie, the latest from the Brooklyn band offers indie rock at its most familiar and instantly gratifying.

title: Teenage Dream
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit Katy Perry’s second album, a sugary pop juggernaut with big misses and even bigger hits.

title: Legacy +
description: On the duo’s generation-spanning double album, Fela Kuti leads in spirit while the baton gets passed down the family tree.

title: Good Timing
description: Stripping back the gentle folk of last year’s Solid Love, the New York guitarist writes drifting, mostly instrumental songs marked by a profound sense of interiority.

title: An Overview on Phenomenal Nature
description: Filled with people, stories, and dialogue, the New York songwriter’s second album flows like an emotional breakthrough, tying together disparate observations into a serene and unified vision.

title: Angel Tears in Sunlight
description: The electronic composer’s first album in 33 years is also her final one—she passed away in December. The synthesizer pieces here are the lightest and most playful of her career, like beacons of hope and change.

title: times
description: The British producer’s detailed yet frictionless house bangers are full of reverence for the dancefloor, though too controlled to match its catharsis.

artist: Big Ghost Ltd / Conway the Machine
title: If It Bleeds It Can Be Killed
description: The disgruntled member of Griselda Records is often overlooked, but he remains a secret weapon. The couplet is his canvas, and few can challenge him on his turf.

title: EDNA (Deluxe)
description: The UK drill artist's debut album offers a richly drawn portrait of a young man feeling his way through life.

title: Who Am I?
description: The Manchester quartet is still stuck as an imitation act, but their love for 2000s-era singer-songwriter pop—and their star potential—comes through.

title: Judas and the Black Messiah: The Inspired Album
description: The soundtrack to the Shaka King-directed film, featuring heavyweights like JAY-Z and Nas alongside newer stars like Polo G and Pooh Shiesty, exploits Hampton’s image to peddle liberation-lite Billboard hits.

title: New Fragility
description: Alec Ounsworth’s latest album is a world of divorce, substance abuse, callous indifference to murder, and also bittersweet nostalgia for that bygone indie-rock era that gave him a platform in the first place.

title: Oh! Pardon tu dormais…
description: Singing about human complexity, channeling her past with Serge Gainsbourg, and grappling with the death of her daughter, the iconic singer-songwriter sounds battle-scarred but never defeated.

title: Lost Themes III: Alive After Death
description: The cult director’s third standalone collection of electronic music isn’t necessarily innovative, but it’s comforting, like a chilling movie you’ve seen a million times.

title: With the Shifts
description: The Brooklyn-based rapper’s latest sports heady lyricism and honest self-exploration. Her words are raw, wise, and immediate as they blaze across the dusty, sun-faded production.

title: Let My People Go
description: These live sets between the saxophonist and pianist capture a dialogue between two highly skilled and empathetic collaborators whose reverence for space matches their regard for the music itself.

title: Glowing in the Dark
description: The UK psych-rockers’ pan-genre approach benefits from a little extra curation and fun. As versatile as they are, their stylistic detours eventually feel like overkill.

title: The Complete Atlantic Singles 1968-1971
description: Featuring most the magisterial Dusty in Memphis and its lesser follow-up A Brand New Me, plus a bevy of related tracks, a new collection captures one of pop’s most fascinating personalities in her second act.

title: TYRON
description: The UK rapper’s first album since his disastrous appearance at last year’s NME Awards is split between welcome introspection and all-caps boasting. It’s a refreshingly candid self-assessment.

Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the UK duo’s striking 1988 debut, full of noise and bliss and darkness, a crucial document of dream pop.

title: Stage Fright (50th Anniversary Edition)
description: An expanded reissue of the Band’s charming, loose-limbed album from 1970 reveals its relatively small stakes are inextricable from its charm.

title: Tell Me I’m Bad
description: The Massachusetts-based trio featuring guitarist Wendy Eisenberg is a gnarled, shred-heavy, meta-comment on indie rock that also creates some pretty great indie rock songs along the way.

title: Lines Redacted
description: Rallying against aggravating, absurd political realities with passion and humor, the Leeds post-punks offer a tongue-in-cheek counterpoint to dourer contemporaries.

title: She’s Calling EP
description: After 2019’s celebratory, cathartic album Resonant Body, this 20-minute EP cleverly subverts club convention in pursuit of higher states of consciousness.

title: private LIFE
description: Expanding from a duo to a trio, complete with saxophone, the Manchester group embraces newfound production gloss without sacrificing its indie-pop roots.

title: Unfuckwitable
description: The Detroit rapper’s latest EP is more polished than anything he’s made before but shines best when he sticks to his Midwest roots.

title: FLOWERS for VASES / descansos
description: Working in isolation, the Paramore leader extends the healing narrative of last year’s Petals for Armor with a sparse, unadorned album that casts a mournful glance to the past.

title: #7DJ (7 Días En Jamaica)
description: The reggaeton of the Colombian pop star meets the reggae of Jamaica on a short and sleek album that, as far as cross-cultural projects go, just barely skims the surface.

title: Merlynn Belle
description: The Lockhart, Texas band moves easily between folky Americana and Renaissance-esque ditties, conjuring strange stories as if through a Ouija board.

title: Subconsciously
description: The veteran South African DJ and producer broadens his sound and his global reach, but his own smooth, moody grooves are more reliably rewarding than his highest-profile collaborations.

title: The Cinder Grove
description: The California pedal steel guitarist makes inventive use of space and place on a quietly mournful album where lost forests and shuttered venues endure in intangible anonymity.

title: Shiesty Season
description: On his promising solo debut, the Memphis rapper punches well above his weight class and firmly positions himself as the top dog of the New 1017.

title: Deep Fried Grandeur
description: The jam-heavy live set captured between Walker’s four-piece band and the Japanese psych-prog quintet is a heady meeting of the minds.

title: For the first time
description: Anchored by inquisitive musicianship and the mercurial vocals of Isaac Wood, the London-based group’s debut creates a post-punk safe haven for unfiltered pretension and paranoia.

title: Impostor EP
description: On her promising, impressively self-produced second EP, Margaret Sohn addresses youthful self-doubt with flair, pairing punchy indie rock with subtle electronic flourishes.

title: Kamil Manqus كَامِل مَنْقوص
description: The Ramallah-based electronic musician’s fifth album uses sampling and noise as tactics for disrupting official narratives and defending Palestinian historical memory.

title: Me and Ennui Are Friends, Baby
description: The unflinching and brutal new record from the Melbourne-based singer-songwriter is so direct that it demands your full attention for every single second.

title: Medicine at Midnight
description: Dave Grohl’s lawful-good lifestyle presents an eternal conflict between being unable to hate the guy and being unable to enjoy the music he continues to make.

title: Before Sunrise
description: On her debut, this Japanese 20-year-old takes inspiration from indie rock to craft lonely, glowing bedroom pop that relishes in the ecstatic possibilities of sound.

title: Start Walkin’ 1965-1976
description: Sinatra’s  influence can be heard everywhere from Angel Olsen to Lana Del Rey. This new compilation offers one of the only overarching retrospectives of a singular career.

title: Step II
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today we revisit the 1978 album from an icon of soul and disco, a formative record in the queer canon.

title: Good Woman
description: Working with John Congleton, the folk trio makes their most personal and energetic statement yet, sacrificing some of their clarion intimacy along the way.

title: Gestalt
description: Against dry, plucked guitar and minimal piano, the Texas songwriter creates moments of intimacy that always seem to suggest more than he’s willing to say outright.

title: Somewhere
description: The indie pop group’s second album is filled with longing for vanished times and spaces. It explores what happens when daydreaming becomes both playground and prison.

title: Ignorance
description: Tamara Lindeman’s songwriting has reached stunning new heights. With a full band supporting her, her new album draws upon the natural world to create unforgettable moments of calm and beauty.

title: Yellow River Blue
description: The Chinese-born, Vancouver-based electronic musician’s debut album fuses disparate moods, styles, and experiences into a varied set of songs that touch on ambient dub, synth pop, and left-field house.

title: Vacation Package
description: The Japanese producer makes records that are absurd and exhilarating in equal measure—behind every drum hit lies a trap door.

title: Rebirth of Wonky
description: On his 25th album, the Chilean-British techno maverick indulges his nostalgia for the dancefloor without sacrificing his habitually mind-bending sounds and textures.

title: Music for Parents
description: The Berlin sound artist explores the creative potential of vibroacoustic research, composing ambient music for therapeutic mattresses that transmit ultra-low frequencies directly to patients’ bodies.

artist: Tha God Fahim / Your Old Droog
title: Tha Wolf on Wall St
description: The duo seamlessly merges their contrasting styles on their new EP, an assured slice of underground rap.

title: Obscure Languages
description: On his second album for Barcelona’s Lapsus Records, the Tbilisi producer brings a rhapsodic melodic sensibility to rhythms that pay tribute to the golden era of IDM.

title: You've Got the Whole Night to Go EP
description: The Australian producer's latest project creates a sense of spaciousness, tracing the almost forgotten flutters and rushes of a good night out.

title: I’ve Seen All I Need to See
description: With a concussive sound and a deceptively lean setup, the doom duo returns to terrifying basics on a macabre and strangely exhilarating album about anguish.

title: Uppers
description: The charged debut from the UK post-punks evolves from a band you think you’ve heard a million times before into one you feel like you’re just getting to know.

artist: A Winged Victory for the Sullen
title: Invisible Cities
description: The neoclassical-ambient duo of Adam Wiltzie and Dustin O’Halloran offers a gorgeous, towering, and apposite score for a dance theater production based on the Italo Calvino novel of the same name.

title: Carm
description: On his solo debut—assisted by Sufjan Stevens, Justin Vernon, and Yo La Tengo’s Georgia Hubley and Ira Kaplan—the multi-instrumentalist rethinks the horn’s role as an album’s driving creative force.

title: Sound Ancestors
description: On his collaborative album with Four Tet’s Kieran Hebden, the producer, multi-instrumentalist, DJ, and archivist remains masterful by simply turning what he hears into something new and revelatory.

title: We Are Always Alone
description: With ceaseless, snarling brutality, the Texas post-hardcore trio’s second album finds a new level of confidence to express the pointlessness of existence.

title: Collapsed in Sunbeams
description: The hotly tipped 20-year-old singer-songwriter debuts with a cool, confident record that occasionally blends into pleasant monotony.

title: The Third Chimpanzee EP
description: Availing himself of his formidable array of modular-synthesizer components, the Depeche Mode songwriter indulges his darkest instincts.

title: Vertigo Days
description: The German band’s first album since 2014 revives their introspective blend of indie rock and electronica, while simultaneously looking outward for new voices and perspectives.

title: OK Human
description: Rivers Cuomo pays tribute to his hermit orchestral-pop heroes, name-checking Harry Nilsson, Serge Gainsbourg, and Pet Sounds. But of course, it's all Weezer in the end.

title: Just Tryin’ Ta Live
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the Houston rapper’s 2002 album, where stoner logic and slacker humor becomes a timeless look into the psyche of the everyman.

title: Disco Se Aagay
description: In 1984, a teenaged sibling duo in Birmingham, England recorded their unique, Urdu-language take on synth pop. The first release from the Discostan label celebrates a lost classic of new wave.

title: Los Dioses
description: Two Latin-trap stars join forces for a slickly produced and familiar-sounding Watch the Throne-style joint album.

title: On All Fours
description: Equipped with whirlpooling guitars and a newfound supply of silvery electronics, the South London band chronicles anxiety and ennui in songs full of spine-tingling dissonance.

title: Painting the Roses
description: Melding disco extravagance with Old Hollywood glamour, the Los Angeles duo’s lush, shape-shifting glam rock transcends pastiche with theatrical flair.

title: Freedom
description: In a pair of electroacoustic radio operas, the American composer addresses the horrors of the Middle Passage and the moral equivocations of the contemporary church.

title: Going to Hell
description: The Muncie Girls frontwoman’s solo debut is part self-interrogation and part community offering, serving up tiny bursts of joy and doubt as refuge for anyone navigating a similar path.

title: A Magnificent Day for an Exorcism
description: The Queens legend tests out an unwieldy rap-rock hybrid with a few promising moments that will test even his most devoted followers.

title: Urban Driftwood
description: On her second album, the 24-year-old solo guitarist’s unique style finds inspiration from unexpected places and sounds untethered to any tradition whatsoever.

title: Ninja Warrior
description: Though the Flint rapper’s latest falls slightly short of his previous mixtape, he’s still capable of delivering dumbly witty punchlines and sex-obsessed theatrics.

title: The Blue of Distance
description: Building a hypnotic counterpoint between a bright chamber-music ensemble and groaning analog synthesizers, composer Elori Saxl’s debut is an investigation of emotion and seasonal change.

title: Longway Sinatra 2
description: The Atlanta rapper makes some of his most intimate, introspective tracks yet and proves why he’s one of his city’s most dependable.

title: Cheater
description: The Norwegian quartet’s second album effortlessly waltzes between technical art-rock, dissonant post-punk, and pop’s irresponsible sugar high. It’s as daring as it is darling.

title: J.T.
description: On this poignant covers album, Steve Earle inhabits his late son’s songs of love and loss as a means of moving through pain.

title: Sketch for Winter IX: Perlita
description: Six tracks on an atmospheric new mini-album for Atlanta label Geographic North feel like dispatches from deep within a fogbank.

title: Anywhere but Here
description: The Pro Era rapper channels the adolescent moodiness of Machine Gun Kelly and the aspiration navel-gazing of J. Cole.

title: Palberta5000
description: Inspired by mainstream pop, the experimental punk trio try their hand at honed hooks and concise riffs. At their best here, they evoke not Bieber and Grande but classic Sleater-Kinney.

title: Trees (50th Anniversary Edition)
description: The UK’s Trees were not scholarly devotees of the folk tradition but enthusiastic recent converts who brazenly experimented with traditional forms and never missed the opportunity to jam.

title: Narrow Sea
description: The Pulitzer Prize-winning composer draws inspiration from shifting tides and centuries-old hymns for a piece that reckons with the unease of feeling adrift in the universe.

title: Kissing Rosy in the Rain
description: On his solo instrumental debut, the New York acoustic guitarist balances the romantic dynamics of flamenco and the meticulousness of Windham Hill with the unguarded qualities of improvised music.

title: Home
description: Rhye leader Michael Milosh remains king of the most respectable horny music possible. His new album testifies to those talents without calling too much attention to itself.

title: Witch Egg
description: John Dwyer leads an instrumental jazz-garage chimera that’s far-out enough to escape predictability and ghoulish enough to go bump in the night.

title: Infamous Angel
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the devastating and sublime debut from one of the most outstanding voices and songwriters in country music.

title: Solid State Logik 1
description: Finally available on streaming services, the UK art-pop pranksters’ throwback rave anthems, jock-jam singalongs, and mischievous myth-making prove as enduring as they are audacious.

title: Isles
description: With dancefloors gone dark, the Northern Irish DJs tailor their second album to homebound listeners, but their indoor voices don’t command the same attention as their main-stage belters.

title: Full Circle
description: The Copenhagen producer’s debut LP reaches beyond the city’s trademark fast tempos to explore woozy slow-motion jams, pensive ambient sketches, and pulse-racing breakbeat trance.

title: Cooler Returns
description: On their second album and first for Sub Pop, the Canadian indie rock group pairs shaggy guitars with sardonic observations.

title: Somewhere Between: Mutant Pop, Electronic Minimalism & Shadow Sounds of Japan 1980-1988
description: Following compilations of Japanese city pop and ambient, Light in the Attic unearths a set of songs lying outside familiar genres. It’s a vital addition to the label’s broader historical project.

title: Demidevil
description: The 24-year-old alt-pop rapper showcases her newly refined confidence, taking a step toward the pop powerhouse she's capable of becoming.

title: Two Saviors
description: While the Big Thief guitarist’s solo work makes more room for American country music than his main band, it offers much of the same warmth and whispery intimacy.

title: Screamers Demo Hollywood 1977
description: These influential but under-documented L.A. punks finally get a proper release, and the five demos here reveal an adventurous band pushing the boundaries of punk orthodoxy.

title: No Place
description: Combining the sweetness of adult contemporary pop with a college rock sensibility, the Arizona songwriter presents the raw emotions of a breakup in a familiar, comforting package.

title: The Seven Foot Tall Post-Suicidal Feel Good Blues
description: The British psych-rock provocateur pens an album-length ode to the fragile euphoria of clawing yourself back from the brink.

title: Nobody Is Listening
description: The boy band graduate remains desperate to remind you that he has sex, eager to insist that he smokes. His falsetto is beautiful, but he’s never sounded like this much of an amateur.

title: Maquishti
description: Challenging but never chaotic, contemplative yet too rigorous to be mistaken for ambient music, the experimental vibraphonist’s solo debut carves out its own place in contemporary music.

title: Griselda & BSF: Conflicted (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: One of modern rap’s most well-oiled machines has officially ventured into film. And while their debut soundtrack doesn’t hit the highs of their studio projects, it continues the tradition of bolstering an under-represented city.

title: Jailbreak
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Thin Lizzy’s greatest album, one that embodies the myth and grandeur of classic rock.

title: Complete UA Singles 1977-1980
description: A box set of the UK pop/punk quartet’s 12 7" singles comprehensively documents the band’s rapid evolution, capturing the group’s energy in short, controlled bursts.

title: Drunk Tank Pink
description: The London post-punk band’s second album is bigger, louder, and more textured as frontman Charlie Steen anxiously details the strange gap between youth and adulthood.

title: Kill Streak
description: The Atlanta rapper leaves the candy-coated comfort zone of his previous mixtape and stands out in a competitive rap lane.

title: Parallel / 871
description: Two albums—one a collection of luminous ambient textures and club grooves, the other an eclectic set of experiments from over 20 years ago—illustrate Kieran Hebden’s range and creative development.

title: Dangerous: The Double Album
description: With a 30-song record, the rising country star takes a closer look at Music Row clichés, writing in easy, idiomatic shorthand that plunges you directly into his world.

title: Petrichor
description: The New Mexico musician’s second album has no shouts, no sudden guitar outbursts, no startling tom thwacks. Instead, she layers arrangements so thick it feels like you could lie down in them.

title: Heaux Tales
description: On her fourth album, Jazmine Sullivan contends with all that can be lost and gained through sex and love. She is in full command of her spectacular voice and totally delivers on an ambitious concept.

title: Self Worth
description: After the labyrinthine twists and turns of 2018’s Sorpresa Familia, the Catalan quartet tightens up its songwriting and sharpens its pop-punk attack.

title: Welfare Jazz
description: The subversively sleazy Stockholm post-punk band walks a delicate satirical line between provocation and trolling.

title: Song of Sage: Post Panic!
description: On his second album of 2020, the underground New York rapper reaches a new level. The vibe is calm and bittersweet, as Navy Blue sinks deep into the recesses of his mind.

title: Chain Reaction at Dusk
description: A split EP between the prepared-piano composer and the noise musician explores their shared affinity for sounds that balance beauty with unease.

title: From Gardens Where We Feel Secure
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a bucolic cult classic from 1983, one that taps into a centuries-old tradition of pastoralism in British culture.

title: A Bout De Heavenly: The Singles
description: Formed in the wake of Talulah Gosh, the indie-pop group Heavenly released four studio albums, but this new singles collection shows that their most magical work existed in smaller formats.

title: Come Outside, We Not Gone Jump You
description: On his new album, the Awful Records founder trades his groggy rapping for smooth crooning.

title: Ruff Dog
description: Producer and film composer Mica Levi’s solo debut operates in two modes: blown-out grunge and soporific dream pop, married by a thick layer of fuzz.

title: I Can’t Go Outside
description: Over a woozy mixture of house, funk, and R&B, the Los Angeles rapper-producer recalls the pleasures of life before lockdown.

title: Plastic Bouquet
description: The Canadian folk duo partners with the New Zealand singer-songwriter; together, they mix blues, murder ballads, and Indigenous lore, updating traditional forms in unexpected ways.

title: After Commodore Perry Service Plaza
description: The second album of improvisational jazz from Cloud Nothings’ Dylan Baldi and Jayson Gerycz tones down the bluster, stretching out in slow-moving pieces that rely heavily on space.

title: BRASS
description: On their mesmerizing collaborative album, the gnomic NYC rapper and the avant-garde poet and musician piece together ideas and sounds from history’s jagged shards.

title: it was always worth it
description: The percussionist and composer explores the minutiae of a break-up via a robotic text-to-speech program on her quietly devastating new album.

title: Whole Lotta Red
description: The Atlanta rapper’s third record is both wildly innovative and strikingly consistent. It’s hard, melodic, experimental, and unlike anything else happening in mainstream rap.

title: Real Bad Boldy
description: The Detroit rapper’s fourth album of 2020 is yet another unalloyed success. It’s pure genre fare delivered by an artist with a refined, almost clinical approach to storytelling.

title: No Driver
description: They’re still cooped up and bummed out, but the Swedish emo revivalists’ third album also boasts longer songs with stronger verses and a keener grasp of sequencing and flow.

title: Landwerk/Landwerk No. 2
description: Inspired by The Caretaker’s corroded loops of antique 78s, the Kentucky guitarist creates hypnotic dialogues with the past by mining and responding to his own vast collection.

title: Tim Melina Theo Bobby
description: After more than 20 albums in the past two decades, the idiosyncratic Chicago rock band takes a final bow. As always, their songs are welcome and familiar, yet a surprise every time.

title: Second Wave
description: Long a collectors’ holy grail, this 1975 session is the keyboardist and bandleader’s only known recording: a fierce half-hour that pushes the limits of jazz, funk, and R&B to their breaking point.

title: Good Guess
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter’s second solo album brings the haze of a previous life into focus, making a methodical survey of the vagaries of memory.

artist: Jahari Massamba Unit / Madlib / Karriem Riggins
title: Pardon My French
description: This joint project between Madlib and drummer Karriem Riggins sounds like experimental jazz and feels like a beat tape.

title: First Take
description: Recorded over a period of just 10 hours, the future star’s breakthrough 1969 debut captured her idiosyncratic mix of soul, jazz, and folk and her singular vision as a bandleader.

title: Untitled (Black Is) / Untitled (Rise)
description: Drawing on funk, Afrobeat, and spiritual tradition, two beautifully crafted albums from the elusive UK group passionately consider the entirety of the Black experience in this moment.

title: McCartney III
description: The third installment in McCartney’s home-recorded series is less adventurous and revelatory than its eponymous predecessors, but still contains moments of genuine wonder and weirdness.

title: PlanetMµ25
description: Mike Paradinas’ groundbreaking electronic label celebrates its 25th anniversary by looking not back but forward, presenting a daring selection of footwork, braindance, and experimental beats.

title: The New OK
description: On their second album this year, the hardworking Southern rockers pair The Unraveling outtakes with songs written during lockdown, taking advantage of the record’s looseness to show off their range.

title: Zooropa
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit U2’s daring 1993 album, a staggeringly weird and strangely intimate political pop experience.

title: Long Haired Locusts
description: After years on the DIY circuit, the Philly group condenses its freaky energy into 14 art-punk vignettes about Stevie Wonder, satanic snakes, and a hallucinatory Virgin Mary.

title: Everything Will Change
description: On this live album, based from a 2014 concert film, you can hear the Postal Service transform from an idea to a band.

title: No Explanations
description: While the Oakland rapper still has a knack for melody and easy charm, her album’s larger-than-life narrative is more mechanical and generic than it is fun.

title: Holographic Universe(s?)!
description: Angel Marcloid’s vaporwave side project trades the electronic screamo fusion of her Fire-Toolz alias for glistening smooth jazz inspired by the Weather Channel.

title: What to Look for in Summer
description: The band’s new live double LP is an exceptionally accomplished and generous look back at their evolution from shy indie darlings to touring powerhouse.

title: Weird!
description: The upstart English pop-punk star’s second album buries his charm in clumsy genre experimentation, clichéd lyrics, and unearned bluster.

title: Ravening Iron
description: The power metal band’s second album is full of fallen kings and cosmic deities, intricate world-building and violent action sequences. Every second of the music aspires to be the show-stopping climax.

title: Man on the Moon III: The Chosen
description: The latest, underwhelming installment of the rapper’s cosmic album series arrives 11 years after the original and coasts on a legacy built a lifetime ago.

title: ANTI-ICON
description: The nu-metal heir apparent's latest album is a tremendous step forward while still remaining an acquired, uncompromising taste.

title: Evermore
description: Working again with Aaron Dessner, Swift challenges herself to find new dimensions within the moody atmosphere: fingerpicked ballads, colorful pop music, and her first country songs in years.

title: Live at Tubby’s
description: Back in early March, the New York group swelled to a septet for an intimate, unrehearsed gig at a Hudson Valley bar. Their intricately textured grooves have rarely sounded more dynamic.

title: We Will Always Love You
description: The Australian group’s ambitious third album overflows with ideas, samples, guests, and sheer stimuli. In their sparkling music, every sound feels like a treasured memory.

title: Pieces of a Man
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Gil Scott-Heron’s 1971 album, a sorrowful and prescient appraisal of the Black experience.

title: Feeling Lucky? EP
description: The London jazz-pop musician is at her most opaque on a new three-song EP, yet these tracks are as evocative and affecting as any in her catalog.

title: Think of Spring
description: The singer-songwriter’s latest—a loose reworking of Billie Holiday’s 1958 album Lady in Satin—is made with affection, curiosity, and care.

title: Ground Aswim
description: Songwriter Caleb Cordes’ third LP sets aside big hooks for a different kind of immediacy, scaling back reverb and elaborate riffs in favor of a renewed appreciation for taking life as it comes.

title: Ways
description: The Bay Area producer’s debut—an unconventional blend of footwork, IDM, ambient, and bass music—is lively, dynamic, and above all, original.

title: Live at the Royal Albert Hall
description: Captured in 2018, this live set leans heavily on the band’s last two albums but still plays like a greatest hits.

title: Hardwood Classic
description: The Detroit rapper's second mixtape of the year is like a compilation of leftovers, with enough meticulously told tales to justify the experience.

title: Origin of the Alimonies
description: The black metal firebrands achieve a rapturous synthesis of Hunter Hunt-Hendrix’s philosophical pontifications and musical obsessions.

title: Fuubutsushi (風物詩)
description: On violin, guitar, saxophone, percussion, and keys, the quartet pieces together a carefully arranged mixture of jazz, ambient, folk, and classical minimalism.

title: Nightmare Vacation
description: On her official debut, the electric rapper-singer is by turns deliriously chaotic, full of ambition, and unfocused as she tries a little of everything that’s made her a star.

title: Wonder
description: The pop heartthrob’s lovestruck fourth album comes across like your friend who just got into a relationship and won’t shut up about it: You’re happy for them and also tremendously bored.

title: El Último Tour del Mundo
description: Reggaetón’s biggest star closes a career-making 2020 with an album imagining his music in 2030: It’s morose, introspective, and pulls from post-punk and rock en español as much as it does hip-hop and R&B.

title: The Hustle Continues
description: On his fifth solo album, the Memphis legend invites guests like Jay Rock and Megan Thee Stallion, splitting the difference between coasting and staying fly.

title: Late Night Tales
description: A mixtape from Houston’s worldly psych trio digs deep into funk classics, spiritual jazz, and unusual finds from South Korea, Belarus, and Nigeria.

title: Lesions of a Different Kind
description: The Rochester band’s debut is a vicious and nauseating blast of classic death metal: catchy, impenetrable, and masterfully executed.

title: Force Majeure
description: Holed up in their East Harlem apartment, the bassist and harpist express the early days of lockdown intimately and beautifully with one mic and a set of mostly covers from John Coltrane to Kate Bush.

title: Sand Like Stardust
description: The experimental Chicago musician expands his already broad instrumental palette for a lonesome album that fuses folk and electronic music without succumbing to the tropes of either.

title: The Fink
description: Toronto musician Daniel Lee’s second solo album delivers a dark and relentlessly funky set of proto-industrial grooves with a sleek dystopian edge.

title: Odin’s Raven Magic
description: The Icelandic post-rockers waver between exuberance and heavy-handed melodrama on the first official recording of an 18-year-old operatic work based on a centuries-old medieval poem.

title: Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the singular comedic thrill of the Los Angeles rap group’s debut.

title: Be
description: The K-pop superstars’ second album of new material in 2020 fixates on the frustration and grief of life in quarantine, sifting through the blurry days to construct a new form of intimacy.

title: AYA
description: On her third album, the French-Malian singer artfully slides between lingo and genres—Afrobeats, zouk, R&B—to create a far-reaching pop experience about life, love, and freedom.

title: Tripping With Nils Frahm
description: Recorded at Berlin’s historic Funkhaus in 2018, this live album sounds uniformly gorgeous and features the composer and his passel of gear working dutifully as a well-oiled machine.

title: New Vanitas
description: As the instrumental guitarist’s work develops, it has moved further away from something resembling instrumental Americana and toward ambient soundscape.

title: Mamalarky
description: The Atlanta indie-rock quartet’s debut album stands out from their contemporaries’ laid-back melancholy with complex instrumental interplay that inspires lean-forward listening.

title: Just Dropped In (To See What Condition My Rendition Was In)
description: A collection of the late soul singer’s covers of songs by Janet Jackson, Prince, and others reveals her remarkable ability to reinterpret classic sounds while refusing to be relegated to the past.

title: Spilligion
description: The octet’s latest group album, full of vibrant theatrics and polished posse cuts, is at times representative of Dreamville Records’ reductive homages.

title: Strum & Thrum: The American Jangle Underground 1983 - 1987
description: The inaugural release in a new Captured Tracks compilation series surveys a generation of college-rock bands that drew sustenance from the chiming guitars of R.E.M. and the Byrds.

title: Holy Palm
description: The far-reaching sound collage of the electronic musician’s sprawling album consists of gorgeous ambient tones and textures that feel more composed than found.

title: Translate
description: On his first album in six years, the UK producer spins freeform modular-synth improvisations into shaggily hypnotic psychedelia.

title: Plastic Hearts
description: Stepping confidently into her “rock era,” Miley offers a genuinely pleasing, though sometimes hamfisted record that staves off the awkwardness and missteps that plagued her previous albums.

title: The Great Dismal
description: On their fourth record, Dominick Palermo leads his dream-pop shoegaze band in a claustrophobic album about his upbringing, and how his music career has brought hope and horror in equal measure.

title: Spontaneous Order
description: Dutch producer Bas Bron abandons the understated cool of his cult hit “What’s a Girl to Do” for bright ’80s synths and Daft Punk melodrama.

title: III
description: A decade after their last album together, the Norwegian space-disco producers pick up where they left off, bringing new emphasis on structure and rhythm to their heady, atmospheric vibes.

title: Dimensional Stardust
description: The Chicago jazz composer stitches together an album of big, unanswerable questions and gorgeously orchestrated music from a host of local heroes.

title: CYR
description: Billy Corgan reenlists the creative core of James Iha and Jimmy Chamberlain for a lengthy synth-pop excursion that is clinically competent and rarely as thrilling—or thrillingly weird—as their previous work.

title: Shadow of Fear
description: The post-punk/proto-industrial group is now down to just founding member Richard H. Kirk, who fills the first Cabaret Voltaire album in 26 years with invitingly rough-hewn sounds.

title: Musick to Play in the Dark
description: Newly reissued, the duo’s 1999 magnum opus queers ambient music in a psychedelic journey through sex, death, and gardening.

title: No Panic No Pain
description: The long-awaited debut from this hotly tipped South London rapper fails to meet its astronomical expectations but shows glimmers of real brilliance.

title: Il Quadro di Troisi
description: Italian electronic musicians Donato Dozzy and Eva Geist team up on a bewitching album of opulently appointed songs rooted in the country’s disco and synth-pop traditions.

title: The Concert for Bangladesh
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit 1971’s Concert for Bangladesh, an era-defining event and live album that set the template for the large-scale benefit concert as we know it today.

title: Live in Maui
description: Near the end of his life, Jimi Hendrix recorded two concerts in Hawaii for an ill-fated film. A new reissue reveals him elevating above an earthly debacle to offer a glimpse of transcendence.

title: Copycat Killer EP
description: The songwriter’s new EP reimagines four tracks from her recent album Punisher with devastating orchestral arrangements that bring her voice into dramatic focus.

title: Sin Miedo (del Amor y Otros Demonios) ∞
description: On her first Spanish-language LP, the Colombian American singer eclipses crossover appeal with a moody, hopscotch pop take on the boleros, reggaetón, and Latin soul of her youth.

title: ALIAS EP
description: The South East London singer’s latest EP is a glittering portal into the future that offers up brief glimpses into a glamorously dirty life.

title: A Drill Story: Music, Trial & Trauma
description: The London drill rapper ventures beyond his chosen style in order to offer a fuller picture of what he’s gone through. At his best, he runs laps around the album’s skeletal beats.

title: My Life
description: Twenty-six years after its release, the R&B stalwart’s occasionally tedious sophomore effort remains a lovable album whose flaws only deepen its charms.

title: Good News
description: Amid a pandemic, and while recovering from a gunshot wound, the superstar rapper made an album that purposefully celebrates life. Her beats are playful, and her rapping is as sharp as ever.

title: Mt. Marci
description: On his latest, the Long Island MC exults in the kingdom he’s created within underground rap.

title: Hey u x
description: The 20-year-old New Zealand singer follows up her ironic TikTok smash “Supalonely” with a surprisingly sincere album that only stumbles when it lapses into conventional pop.

title: Preyer
description: The sludgy death-metal group draws inspiration from the story of the satanist Sean Sellers on their roaring latest LP.

title: While the World Was Burning
description: After an illegal remix made him a TikTok hit, the Brooklyn rapper-singer struggles to create an identity on his debut,  enlisting high-profile guests like Kanye, Lil Uzi Vert, and Future in the effort.

title: LIVE DRUGS
description: The first live album from the Philadelphia band feels loose and sounds immaculate, cementing their status as one of the premier live bands of their generation.

title: Confessions
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Usher’s 2004 album, a jam-packed icon of R&B and one of the most flawless executions of mythmaking in pop.

title: Self Help
description: Alongside a roster of guest vocalists including Jennifer Castle and Meg Remy, the psychedelic Toronto outfit allows their exploratory and pop-focused impulses to work in tandem.

title: Home for Now
description: On their debut album, the UK duo nudges classic British bedroom indie toward a fuller, richer sound, while singer Nancy Andersen discovers the potential of her understated voice.

title: Staunch Honey
description: The Nebraska guitarist and songwriter strips his music to its raw, noisy core, revealing how his favorite records might have sounded when they were still being hammered out in rehearsal.

title: Welcome to O’Block
description: The debut album from the uncompromising rapper was released one week before his untimely death. It delivers a concentrated dose of his tense, menacing take on drill.

title: Idiot Prayer: Nick Cave Alone at Alexandra Palace
description: Cave performed these 22 career-spanning songs alone in a deserted concert hall, reworking them into haunted piano sermons that glow with unnerving intimacy.

title: Muvaland EP
description: With saucy charm and ruthless takedowns, motor-mouthed Brooklyn rapper Cakes Da Killa claims center stage on a collaborative EP of house bangers with producer Proper Villains.

title: Hill, Flower, Fog
description: The soft and luminous six instrumental tracks on Sprague’s latest release convey a sort of serene estrangement from the everyday.

title: Point the Flashlight and Walk
description: Felix Walworth’s third album of skewed indie pop is solitary but inviting, setting songs about the pitfalls of intimacy against the most accessible sonics of their career.

title: People
description: On their fourth LP, the Hamilton, Ontario garage punks step up with a more ambitious and accessible sound without sanding down their raw edges.

title: Beautiful Havoc
description: The West Palm Beach rapper tones down the intensity of many of his fellow Floridians, favoring more polished beats and a relaxed, casually charismatic tone.

title: Time Makes Nothing Happen
description: Originally self-released during lockdown’s first wave, these unpredictable modular-synth pieces toy with rhythmic convention while perpetually throwing time out of joint.

title: FlySiifu’s
description: The two students of J Dilla consolidate their skills to create a free-spirited project around joy and fellowship, with a few meandering moments.

title: Songs to Yeet at the Sun EP
description: The revolutionary Philadelphia hardcore band expand the genre’s possibilities on their new EP, which feels cruelly short at only 12 minutes.

title: Stolen Car
description: The veteran avant-garde composer’s third album in two years places him alongside a new generation of collage artists, tying a dizzying array of stylistic signifiers into complex knots.

title: Pluto x Baby Pluto
description: The two rappers show great chemistry on their collaborative mixtape, even if Future sounds like he’s dragging slightly.

title: Monument
description: The Belarusian new wave band’s latest album is an austere gothic dream with no interest in pandering to the audience attracted by their improbable TikTok breakthrough.

title: Send Them to Coventry
description: On his debut mixtape, the British-Gambian rising star breaks away from the UK rap mold and establishes himself as a voice for the marginalized.

title: Código de Barras
description: On his sophomore LP, the Manchester-based electronic producer again pushes batida into hazy new territory with an unusually subdued interpretation of the sound of his native Lisbon.

title: Because of a Flower
description: The California ambient musician’s debut LP pulls from new age, dream pop, Medieval choral music, and Hindustani singing for a hypnotic and tender meditation on gender, identity, and self-love.

title: COA
description: Loud, playful, and full of smoldering angst, the hyperpop rapper’s new album feels emblematic of the moods and textures that this scene aspires to capture.

title: DISCO
description: The Australian pop icon has made several decades’ worth of great disco—yet her new album is a polyester-thin fabrication that sounds as if she’d only just heard of it recently.

title: It Serve You Right to Suffer
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the singular sound and the one-chord wonder of the iconic bluesman’s 1966 album.

title: Spirit World Field Guide
description: On his new album, the verbose rapper’s fascination with creatures widens into a cosmology, resulting in the most joyous album he’s ever made.

title: The Angel You Don’t Know
description: With a distinctive singing voice and confidence in spades, the breakout Afropop star swoops through a pacesetting fusion of alté, R&B, Southern rap, mall-rock, and Top 40 pop.

title: Gone Glimmering
description: The indie rock band made two filler-free albums full of primal thrills and then disappeared. This reissue feels more like a reintroduction than a reassessment.

title: People on Sunday
description: The mysterious electronic musician, now a solo artist, scores a whimsical soundtrack to a 90-year-old German silent film. Soft, gentle, and sparse, his music is imbued with a quiet sense of wonder.

title: Share the Wealth
description: After two relatively tame records for Blue Note, the fearless guitar innovator renews his focus on the atonal and edgy with an ambitious, astonishing work.

title: Stock Child Wonder
description: The agile singer-songwriter smoothly transitions from the effortlessness of his 2017 debut to a sophomore record rich with complexities.

title: Didn’t You Hear? // Lucifer: Black Mass // Ataraxia: The Unexplained // Music From Patch Cord Productions
description: These reissued electronic works by the ’70s Moog pioneer marry the fantastical and the everyday, the whimsical and the occult.

title: FICTION EP
description: Even in its brevity, the Montreal four-piece art-rock band stage a foray into something more instinctive and assured.

title: Lamentations
description: The ambient composer goes back to raiding his decades-deep personal archives for vintage tape to revive with new perspective and fresh feeling.

title: Book of Curses
description: This blistering punk-rock debut from a 55-year-old veteran of the scene delivers urgent music for evergreen unease. These are weary, angry songs, crafted with an insatiable verve and an almost triumphant fury.

title: Alive in the Hot Zone
description: On his latest album, the singer-songwriter documents the tumultuous months of late spring and early summer 2020, occupying a sweet spot at the intersection of folk, punk, country, and Americana.

title: Ephemera
description: The Los Angeles producer’ upbeat second LP is a short, feature-heavy collection that emphasizes his charmingly loose funk and synth-pop arrangements.

title: Shabason, Krgovich & Harris: Philadelphia
description: In drifting arrangements for saxophone, keyboards, and contemplative vocals, thetrio invents a singular style of shipwrecked yacht rock that’s well suited to the strange pace of 2020.

title: Don’t Shy Away
description: The group’s second album skates between rhythmic, mechanical churn and abstracted instrumental sweeps, seeking the boundaries between natural, artificial, and supernatural.

title: Everything U Need EP
description: On their latest EP, the UK dance duo amp up their latent melancholy, luxuriating in a rather British strain of pastoral electronica.

title: Pylon: Pylon Box
description: A 4xLP box set pays tribute to the influential Athens band, who in the early ’80s pioneered a stripped-down post-punk sound that was raw, minimalist, brainy, and danceable.

title: Pegasus
description: The Ohio rapper’s new album sounds like a randomly generated playlist: tons of options, very little soul.

title: LIVE
description: This revelatory and confrontational live album centers around Angel Bat Dawid’s prowess as a bandleader. With her eclectic band, it is a brilliant document of how free jazz functions as both exploration and exorcism.

title: the hum of your veiled voice
description: The Berlin-based electronic musician collages vinyl samples and field recordings into sensually inviting soundscapes infused with a powerful sense of mystery.

title: Sam Amidon
description: Amidon’s self-titled record continues his polyglot blending of folk, classical, and jazz, drawing a resounding personal statement out of songs in the public domain.

title: Long Hot Summers: The Story of The Style Council
description: Collecting both hits and tangents, this double-disc anthology of Paul Weller’s post-Jam project has a concise narrative punch lacking in 1998’s more thorough box set.

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou? (Original Soundtrack)
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the original soundtrack to the Coen brothers’ 2000 film, one that primed a generation for a modern folk revival.

title: Made In Lagos
description: The Afrobeats star balances the formula to unite home and abroad with big pop songs that can compete across cultures and an underlying theme that embraces his roots.

title: May Our Chambers Be Full
description: On their collaborative debut, the Louisiana sludge band and the Kentucky songwriter funnel gothic majesty and charred metal into moments of unlikely wonder.

title: The Edge of Everything
description: On his first album in 14 years, the drum’n’bass innovator blurs the edges of the genre, putting masterful sound design and playful pacing in the service of cinematic aims.

title: Hot Wet & Sassy
description: On his fifth Tobacco album, Thomas Fec doubles down on both the most alluring and unsettling aspects of the project.

title: Summerteeth (Deluxe Edition)
description: This reissue stays true to the darkness and exuberance that defined the band’s revelatory 1999 album.

title: A Japanese Horror Film
description: The introspective St. Louis rapper builds a self-contained world with his magnetic monotone and intricate, evocative raps.

title: BLP 2020 “King of the Night” EP
description: On his first project under his DJ Blackpower alias, the Bronx rapper’s beats grow colder and his lyrics become more heartfelt as he continues to grieve the loss of his mother.

title: Fading
description: Inspired by his mother’s Alzheimer’s, the German ambient-dub musician crafts a masterfully melancholy lament that takes his signature crackle and pop into unsettling new terrain.

title: Love Goes
description: The pop crooner’s third album is at times freer, queerer, and more enlivening than anything Sam Smith has done before, and yet too cautious to make what could’ve been a career-defining leap.

title: Hey Clockface
description: Alternating between loud, sumptuously produced rock and softer, Tin Pan Alley-inspired songs, the British singer-songwriter delivers a brooding set of songs about time’s ceaseless march.

title: Closer Than They Appear
description: On her breakthrough project, executive produced by Phonte, the polymath rapper-singer displays her love of classic hip-hop and tries to soothe the sting of survivor’s guilt.

title: Seven Storey Mountain VI
description: The first installment of the trumpeter’s ecstatic series to be recorded in a studio is its most beautiful, and somehow the most convincing document of the cycle’s in-person grandeur, too.

title: Fires in Heaven
description: On their second full-length in a decade, the despondent witch house pioneers return with an alluring invitation to join them in the depths.

title: Positions
description: Her third album in two years searches for peace, tracing the quiet work of piecing yourself together and delighting in giddy new romance at the same time.

title: De Chamaquito Siempre Cabezu
description: The first full-length project from the Bronx’s Sie7etr3 collective showcases its leader’s elastic flows and artful delivery over minimal but effective beats.

title: E3 AF
description: Three years after making an ostensible but half-hearted return to his roots, the grime icon more convincingly reconciles underground instincts with pop ambitions.

title: America the Beautiful
description: The Chicago percussionist, bandleader, and composer offers a moving, frequently ebullient album that doesn’t shy away from the terrors of America’s past and present while managing, somewhat incredibly, to find hope in the country’s future.

title: Tigermilk
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the debut album from Belle and Sebastian, a little-heard school project that defined the sound of one of indie rock’s most beloved acts.

title: American Beauty / The Angel’s Share
description: Reissued for its 50th anniversary, American Beauty is undoubtedly the Dead’s most beloved studio album, a pure and potent representation of their style and philosophical outlook.

title: Maya
description: The longtime Red Hot Chili Peppers guitarist swaps the acid-house influences of his Trickfinger project for a loving tribute to ’90s jungle and drill’n’bass.

title: Lift It Down
description: The 2018 Nicolas Cage vehicle Mandy featured a bargain-brand messiah figure named Jeremiah Sand. Now, Sacred Bones is releasing an “unearthed album,” supposedly recorded in the  mid-’70s by the fictional cult leader.

title: Magic Oneohtrix Point Never
description: Daniel Lopatin’s latest doesn't swerve in a new direction but instead serves as an overlook for his career, highlighting his skill at splicing the old and the new in continually fascinating ways.

title: Forgotten Days
description: After fumbling slightly on their last record, the doom apostles recover their grave, soaring majesty on an album that find a new way forward by refining their past.

title: Lovey
description: Thirty years after alt rock reshaped the mainstream, Evan Dando and co.’s major-label debut feels like the product of a bygone era—a snapshot of rock regionalism on its last legs.

title: Nirvana
description: After a shaky debut project, the 18-year-old Atlanta rapper gives her punk spirit more space to breathe on her latest mixtape.

title: acts of rebellion
description: The Brooklyn-based producer, vocalist, and drummer underlines her frosty club cuts and wordless, tranquil interludes with a message of dissent.

title: III
description: On their first record in five years, Ty Segall’s proto-metal power trio dig into the fundamentals of their sound, captured in crisp audio-verité style by Steve Albini.

title: Getting Into Knives
description: Recorded in Memphis before lockdown, the Mountain Goats’ second album of 2020 is lush and loose, full of stories about personal fulfillment, in whatever form it takes.

title: Wachito Rico
description: Three years after a brush with the YouTube algorithm turned him unexpectedly into a minor indie-pop star, Nicolas Muñoz still sounds unsure about what to do next.

title: Three States: Rarities 1997-2007
description: The indie pop band's reissue of loosies and cover songs captures their story in thoughtful strokes and further cements Katy Davidson’s role as an influential songwriter.

title: JP4
description: Against a blend of narcotized trip-hop and uplifting R&B, the New York rapper’s fourth LP flips all traces of self-doubt into a source of power and independence.

title: Featuring Ty Dolla $ign
description: On his latest, Ty asserts his mastery over 25 lush, intricate tracks. With a wide-ranging guest roster including serpentwithfeet and Thundercat, Featuring is a capital-A Album, designed to be consumed in an hour-long gulp.

title: Under the Spell of Joy
description: Harnessing the allure of the occult and the power of self-help, the Los Angeles garage rockers break free from their roots and ascend to the realm of spiritual psych-jazz rockestra.

title: Monarch Season
description: The Canadian songwriter blends into the atmosphere of her piano and acoustic guitar, presenting her exceedingly intimate music as an inventive and subtly visceral experience.

title: This Place Sucks Ass EP
description: The pop-punk band’s six-track follow-up to last year’s Morbid Stuff invites listeners to sit with pain of their own, to study it, and, of course, to scream through it.

title: Moveys
description: The self-produced debut from the Chicago-based band recalls the downcast, hazy vibe of Alex G and Soccer Mommy.
On his third album as Call Super, Joe Seaton’s compositions feel more casual, introverted, and low-stakes than previous efforts.

title: Visions of Bodies Being Burned
description: The sequel to There Existed an Addiction to Blood extends the trio’s bristly noise and gory horrorcore rap with a sense of terror that’s more academic than frightening.

title: Love Is the King
description: Released in conjunction with his book How to Write One Song, the Wilco frontman’s response to the pandemic is a mellow, easygoing collection of songs stressing the importance of human connection.

title: The Menswe@r Collection
description: This 4xCD retrospective of a group synonymous with Britpop’s worst excesses captures their pop peacocking and genuine charm, accompanied by a lingering feeling of trying too hard.

title: Songs the Lord Taught Us
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the debut album by the Cramps, true believers who recast rockabilly in their own outrageously camp image.

title: Floral Prince
description: Kevin Patrick Sullivan’s latest is a patchwork of new and old material with some gorgeously off-the-cuff strummers and unvarnished folk songs that start to detail his curious shape as a singer-songwriter.

title: Cuttin’ Grass Vol. 1: The Butcher Shoppe Sessions
description: Accompanied by some of the best players in the scene, the country maverick performs bluegrass versions of highlights from his back catalog, revealing the hidden roots of his idiosyncratic songwriting.

title: songs / instrumentals
description: Across two albums that function as one stunning piece of music, the Big Thief singer approaches familiar themes of loss, solitude, memory, and regret in some of the most vivid songwriting of her career.
Once a famously fractious noise band, the trio continues its slow transformation into an unpredictable and surprisingly tender rock group.

title: Anime, Trauma and Divorce
description: On his bleakly comic new album, Open Mike Eagle surveys the damage of one terrible year, using anime mythology as a lens for examining real-life pain.

title: Sen Morimoto
description: The Chicago multi-instrumentalist and jazz-rap artist’s self-titled double album conceals a reflective sorrow within its blissful swirl of beats and blips.

title: Burden of Proof
description: On his latest project, the Griselda Records rapper reflects on old battle scars and new riches over luxury beats helmed by Hit-Boy. Though he occasionally steps into cosplay, the result is ambitious.

title: Letter to You
description: Riding the E Street Band’s familiar uplift, Springsteen grapples with the complexities of nostalgia, a tension that animates his writing and manifests in the sound of the music itself.

title: First Fire • At Dawn
description: Trading his High Aura’d alias for his own name, the Providence experimental musician finds evocative depths in the small, transitory details of slowly evolving drone pieces.

title: The L.I.B.R.A. (The Legend Is Back Running Atlanta)
description: T.I.’s eleventh album is more concerned with sprinting alongside Atlanta’s new generation than with cementing his legacy or exploring his politics.

title: Someone New
description: The Montreal singer-songwriter’s debut album addresses the strangeness of nascent love, channeling feelings of derealization and disconnect in intricately detailed electronic pop miniatures.

title: Shiver
description: The Sigur Rós frontman’s muddled attempt at a pop album is a cathedral of feelings without referents: beautiful, boring, generically uplifting, and deliberately meaningless.

title: Roped In
description: This duo of guitarist Patrick McDermott and pedal steel player Barry Walker meld country-folk instrumental composition with ambient sonics, creating a languid and colorful world.

title: Apolonio
description: For the first time in his brief career, the triple-threat singer is running on more than just potential. On his latest project, he brings youthful charm, optimism, and curiosity to his most fully realized work yet.

title: Fake It Flowers
description: Inspired by rom-coms and Kimya Dawson, Gen Z songwriter Bea Kristi uses the slanted melodies and flannel-loving aesthetics of ’90s alternative rock in service of massive pop hooks.

title: Stay Alive
description: The Against Me! frontwoman intended to record these bracing songs with her main band before the pandemic sidelined that plan. Her austere solo version feels like a pale shadow of the real thing.

title: Serpentine Prison
description: The National frontman’s solo debut unwinds the nervous energy in favor of something more laid-back. The music is gorgeous and unfussy, but his performances and lyrics feel nondescript.

title: skins n slime
description: Running his instrument through a bevy of effects, the virtuoso cellist summons a powerful, mesmerizing sound variously evoking shoegaze, classical minimalism, drone, and doom metal.

title: Streams of Thought, Vol. 3: Cane & Able EP
description: On the third volume in his solo series, Black Thought once again demonstrates the power of his dense, winding freestyles and stretches into new, more vulnerable territory.

title: Sundowner
description: An indie folk record with tinges of country rock, the songwriter’s latest album pays tribute to his Kansas City home with a vision of the Midwest that feels mythical and enormous.

title: lil kiiwi
description: The pop singer’s debut is a promising reintroduction that shows her emotional and melodic strengths if she can avoid the clichés of influencer culture and the digital age.

title: TOCSIN
description: With a title invoking alarm bells, this ambitious collection of the New York composer’s work is turbulent and disorienting, suggesting cycles of crisis and change.

title: Listen Like Thieves
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit INXS’s fifth album, a pivotal and underrated moment for one of music’s most formidable, hit-making pop-rock bands.

title: Wildflowers & All the Rest (Deluxe Edition)
description: The new reissue of Tom Petty’s benchmark 1994 solo album has a sprawling quality inherent to the album that makes it feel less like a curio for obsessives than a deep interrogation into its success.

title: SIGN
description: After a decade of composing increasingly difficult music, the experimental duo offers a reprieve. SIGN is an exceptionally engaging listen: lean, intermittently sedate, even quite pretty.

title: Nobody Lives Here Anymore
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter belongs to a contemporary lineage of classic-rock devotees; his melodic gifts make this double album, recorded in Memphis, exceptionally warm and inviting.

title: Shades
description: Mica Levi’s band, formerly known as Micachu and the Shapes, embraces imperfection, evoking late-’80s indie pop in whimsical ideas, unsteady rhythms, and meticulous detailing.

title: Projections EP
description: Like her debut, Sarah Beth Tomberlin’s Alex G-produced new EP finds her struggling with abandoning the Baptist church she grew up in. The five songs are so intimate they feel like secrets.

title: Dark Hearts
description: Annie’s first album in about a decade, written and recorded in a haunted house, collapses decades into an evocative blur.

title: Gulfer
description: The Montreal band grows up on their third album, crafting well-made, emo-adjacent songs all while trying to summon enough energy to stare down looming adulthood.

title: UPRIZE!
description: The South African jazz ensemble’s improvised soundtrack to a 2017 documentary about the 1976 Soweto Uprising captures a mixture of outrage, injustice, and hope that resonates powerfully today.

title: Pleased to Meet Me (Deluxe Edition)
description: The latest in the band’s series of expanded editions focuses on their second major-label record, the moment in which Paul Westerberg’s punk impulses, pop instincts, and poetic soul came into focus as never before.

title: The Killing of Eugene Peeps
description: The third album from London composer Bastien Keb is a soundtrack to a nonexistent film: a gloomy, dreamlike suite that summons the vintage sounds of 1970s giallo films and French New Wave.

title: As Long As You Are
description: The Baltimore band goes back to the well for another record of languorous, heart-on-the-sleeve synth-pop that hits all its marks but smacks of diminishing returns.

title: AUNTIE
description: The Brooklyn-based funk singer’s latest project strikes a balance between sweet and larger than life, aided by Chromeo’s sleek production.

title: Circuit City
description: In her debut theatrical work, the Philadelphia poet and experimental musician rails against the racist underpinnings of the housing crisis against a backdrop of free jazz.

title: Act II: The Patents of Nobility (The Turn)
