description: Long-delayed and eventually shelved, Jay Electronica’s near-mythical “lost” album finally sees official release after it was leaked. Even slightly unfinished, it is nearly an all-time classic, the kind of record that celebrates an art form while simultaneously pushing it forward.

title: Silver Ladders
description: With Slowdive’s Neil Halstead in the producer’s chair, the Los Angeles harpist swells her gentle ambience with a more strident sound but remains as transporting as ever.

title: Atlas Vending
description: The Toronto band’s pummeling sound still evokes white-knuckled, visceral disgust, but they struggle to take these songs somewhere more interesting than they started.

title: Sleepless Night EP
description: Yo La Tengo’s second EP in recent months finds them resuming their covers jukebox niche, weaving together selections as unlikely as a 1940s blues oddity and as recognizable as a Bob Dylan classic.

title: Soundkeeper
description: In his improv duo with drummer John Truscinski, guitarist Steve Gunn makes purposefully stark instrumental music that remains as challenging and personal as his singer-songwriter records.

title: Nothing EP
description: With corroded sounds and anxious, wistful guest features, the London producer’s new four-track EP breaks new ground in four different directions.

title: Love Touched Time and Time Began to Sweat
description: The rock group evokes Deerhunter while perfecting their own unpredictable way with melody, teetering on the edge of catchiness and constantly teasing and dodging the logical next note.

title: Lament
description: On their phenomenal fifth album, the post-hardcore band work with famed producer Ross Robinson and come away with their most affecting and resonant work yet.

title: Innercity Griots
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 1993 album from the technically dazzling jazz-rap group that changed the national perception of West Coast hip-hop.

title: Hybrid Theory (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: The California band’s blend of rapping, screaming, and circuit-bending defied easy categorization. Their sharpest tendencies meshed on Hybrid Theory, the most popular rock music of the 21st century.

title: The Seeds of Love (Super Deluxe Edition)
description: A 4xCD/Blu-ray box set unpacks the bombast behind the UK band’s sprawling 1989 hybrid of soul and neo-psychedelia, recorded over four years and hundreds of hours of experimentation.

title: Diamond Life
description: On their remarkable 1984 debut, the UK band were executors of spaciousness. Led by singer Helen Folasade Adu—Sade for short—they crafted vintage pop out of simple elements and inspired a new mellow class of musicians.

title: Lovers Rock
description: Sade’s fifth album trades the band’s signature luxuriance for a sparser, knottier sound. They turn up the natural sensuality of a winding breeze and a low, gibbous moon.

title: Promise
description: Promise, from 1985, is the ideal second album, firmly establishing the Sade template without retreading the same material of the band’s debut.

title: Stronger Than Pride
description: Sade’s third album turned the band’s elegant, composed music into meditation, exploring romance as an interior experience.

title: Personal History
description: Balancing a gutsier sound against the restrained emotion of her voice, the Irish singer-songwriter’s debut flits between clinical detachment and startling closeness.

title: Bobby Bare Sings Shel Silverstein Plus
description: Shel Silverstein’s reputation rests on his children’s books, but he also had a long, illustrious songwriting career in Nashville. No one performed his ribald, irreverent songs more than the progressive country singer Bobby Bare, and this box set collects their work.

title: Phoenix: Flames Are Dew Upon My Skin
description: After 2018’s prickly IRISIRI, the Queens experimental musician narrates a personal and artistic rebirth in spare songwriting fleshed out with acoustic guitar, strings, and turbulent sound collages.

title: Shamir
description: The singer-songwriter’s vibrant, self-titled seventh album bridges the gap between his lo-fi impulses and the more conventional pop sound of his debut, without compromising his artistry.

title: Savage Mode 2
description: The sequel to the canonical Atlanta mixtape is meant to be a legacy-defining stamp, but despite all its glossy guest stars (Morgan Freeman!), it never rises above “just fine.”

title: Speed, Sound, Lonely KV EP
description: Recorded at Nashville’s famed Butcher Shoppe, Vile’s lovely and bittersweet new EP mixes covers and originals, including a duet with the late John Prine.

title: May You Be Held
description: Returning with mightier riffs and wilder improvisations than ever, the trio offers a spiritual vision of metal, one well timed to a moment of crisis.

title: For Broken Ears EP
description: The Nigerian singer-songwriter follows up her dynamic hit “Try Me” with a stark and voluble EP that blends the warmth of R&B with contemporary Afrobeats.

title: Giver Taker
description: Though written during the throes of identity crisis and recovery, the official debut from Boston-based indie-folk artist Anjimile Chithambo radiates the happiness and pride that come with stability.

title: Live Forever
description: On his fascinating debut album, the D.C.-based musician moves freely through many different styles—arena-rock, folk, rap—creating an album about that freedom as a Black artist and so much more.

title: mama’s boy
description: The synth-pop group aches with boy-band sincerity over sugary arrangements and even a little pedal steel on their anodyne new album.

title: File Under UK Metaplasm
description: Descended from Yorkshire’s lineage of extreme computer music, the UK producer’s astonishing second album fuses jungle, singeli, acid, dancehall, and more into audacious yet danceable hybrids.

title: Agüita
description: Spanning tender acoustic ballads, silky R&B performance, and contemporary urbano swagger, the singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist’s second LP unites the facets of his own artistic identity.

title: Free Humans
description: The Newcastle band’s oddball indie pop makes a pitch to those unsure whether to fret over civilizational decline or their own minor burdens: Why not both!

title: Róisín Machine
description: On her fifth solo album, the Irish singer finds a new role as a dancefloor truth-teller, infusing house and disco epics with thrilling expressions of desire, regret, and self-knowledge.

title: True Romantic
description: The El Paso, Texas-based performance artist and musician stages an exploration of popular romance with an album that’s as gauzy and enveloping as a fragrance ad.

title: Irons in the Fire
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Teena Marie’s third album, an essential document of R&B that shined a new light on her voice and artistry.

title: Sign o’ the Times (Super Deluxe)
description: With 63 previously unreleased tracks, this newly remastered version of Prince’s groundbreaking 1987 album is a trove of lost songs and dramatic lore, a jaw-dropping look into one of the most creatively fertile times in his career.

title: Floor Seats II
description: With his trailblazing Trap Lord days behind him, the brash former A$AP affiliate returns with a fun, familiar album that is content to chase trends instead of set them.

title: EP1
description: Ivana Carrescia’s latest project blends pop melodies with rich, moody, turn-of-the-millennium deep house. It’s the kind of music that makes you feel like you’re both dancing and floating in space.

title: Clam Day
description: The Brooklyn electronic musician’s punch-drunk and disquieting debut subverts genre tropes to laugh in your face.

title: Men on the Verge of Nothing
description: The storied career of the glammy singer-songwriter continues with a jangly, fuzzy, noisy album of bummer jams that sound like hugs from a pal who’s bummed out about boys.

title: Who Made the Sunshine
description: The Buffalo rapper’s new project is another serving of glamorous beat loops and gaudy raps delivered with the confidence of someone who believes that all of their thoughts belong in the MoMA.

title: Transmissions: The Music of Beverly Glenn-Copeland
description: The new age composer’s late-blooming renaissance continues with a compilation attempting to span the sounds and moods of a long, eclectic career.

title: Ohms
description: Deftones’ ninth album reaches for a plane beyond loud and quiet, where the band is free to indulge its harshest and most gentle impulses at once. For the first time, they make it look easy.

title: Rilo Kiley
description: The indie band’s remarkably self-assured 1999 debut showed them already in possession of the wry, morbid sensibility that would define them.

title: Palo Alto
description: The legendary jazz pianist’s 1968 concert at Palo Alto High School, recorded by a janitor and shelved for decades, captures some of the fiercest, most spirited versions of his quartet’s core repertoire.

title: Only For Dolphins
description: Over a 10-year recording career, the Queens rapper has diversified his bonds and spread himself thin musically. Still, he remains a captivating figure on his most eclectic album yet.

title: Tickets to My Downfall
description: The motor-mouthed rapper’s latest album reboots him as an heir to the early-’00s pop-punk canon, with Travis Barker producing and playing drums.

title: Stateless
description: The improvising guitarist’s first album for Drag City is restless and unsettling. Building on his idea of improvisation as a non-hierarchical value system, it is also a kind of protest record.

title: Wuddaji
description: As much as the Detroit dance producer’s aesthetic may feel familiar, the improvisatory results plunge into a whole new tributary of club rhythm.

title: Full Wack No Brakes
description: The northern England crew specializes in dance music at its most juiced and jacked up. Like the best nights out, their new album passes by in a blur.

title: Daughter
description: On her fifth and best full-length album, the Ohio singer-songwriter follows the rangy contours of her electric guitar playing with heartbreak stories and searching questions.

title: By the Fire
description: Refining the sound of last year’s sprawling Spirit Counsel into more focused riffs and songs, By the Fire suggests a renewed dialogue between Moore’s experimental instincts and his desire to rock.

title: Sundry Rock Song Stock
description: On his latest album, the Canadian psych-pop auteur expresses something deeply solitary in his music, a textured and overgrown world of the mind.

title: ACR Loco
description: On their first new album in over a decade, Manchester’s funkiest post-punk band offer an imperfect distillation of their 40-year legacy, updating their classic sound with nods to contemporary beat-driven music and political strife.

title: All Thoughts Fly
description: The Swedish composer sidelines the gothic pop of previous releases in favor of lush and sorrowful wordless soundscapes, performed entirely on the pipe organ of a local church.

title: Ultra Mono
description: The Bristol punk band’s third album goes for fist-in-the-air righteousness but stumbles over itself at nearly every turn, resulting in a broad and unfocused attempt to speak to the moment.

title: Hyper Romance
description: As they shed their masks and streamline their sound, the UK psych-pop duo sound like they’ve found their voice but not yet something significant to say.

Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Adele’s earth-shattering 2011 album, granting the British torch singer entrée into the pantheon of iconic pop vocalists.

title: Finds You Well
description: On an album blending downtempo beats and ambient textures, many of the strongest moments skew toward the Canadian producer’s softer side, with slight arrangements that meditate on a single mood.

title: New York: Deluxe Edition
description: A new reissue highlights the ongoing relevance of Lou Reed’s opus about his hometown in the era of AIDS and Reaganism, a protest album unlike any other

title: Renegade Breakdown
description: In self-imposed exile from the international club scene, Marie Davidson teams with two close collaborators for a self-consciously odd collection of Lynchian lounge music and digitized funk.

title: Haunted Painting
description: On the second album under her solo alias, the Speedy Ortiz frontwoman uses maximalist electronic pop to explore youth, self-perception, and a reckoning with her past.

title: The Reinvention of Romance
description: In an engrossing 87-minute piece in which cello and percussion circle each other through passages of sweetness and strife, the American composer explores the daily experience of intimacy.

title: The Ascension
description: Exhaustive, dense, and detailed, Sufjan Stevens’ electro-opus is another huge artistic leap that speaks plainly to complicated emotions and attempts to rebuild his sound from the ground up.

title: Apple
description: One month after releasing 7G, the PC Music founder refines his synthesis of futurist pop and experimental electronic music, flirting with cerebral schmaltz and information overload.

title: Find the Sun
description: Angel Deradoorian’s second LP is darker, less polished, and openly meditative. Even in its most psychedelic moments, the fuzzy aesthetic gives her music an earthy, grounded feel.

title: Risking Illness
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter navigates the aftermath of grief on his gentle new record.

title: Virgo World
description: On the 18-year-old New York rapper’s debut album, a pocketful of catchy melodies and bubbly rhythms don’t make up for a lack of anything interesting to say.

title: The Liz Tape
description: Griselda’s newest signee alternatingly embraces and cuts against the Buffalo collective’s throwback Mafioso rap.

title: The Studio Albums 1978-1991
description: As heard on this 6xLP box set, the UK classic rockers were artier than their reputation suggests, with a subdued sense of adventure that propelled the group throughout its career.

title: Shore
description: On his fourth album, singer-songwriter Robin Pecknold refines and hones Fleet Foxes’ crisp folk-rock sound, crafting another musically adventurous album that is warm and newly full of grace.

title: The Times EP
description: The iconic songwriter offers a selection of tunes from across his catalog, performed live in his house and recorded with an iPad. It sounds as starkly homemade as you’d expect.

title: BC
description: The low-profile Houston producer and singer utilizes elements of contemporary trap music as a jumping-off point for R&B at its most abstract. His blurry portraits offer uncanny clarity.

title: Host
description: Ten years after “Go Outside,” the New York duo find solipsistic charm in revisiting their past, bolstering their classic sound with the tactile verve of live instruments.

title: BREACH
description: After the heavy-hearted indie folk of her debut, the Bristol singer-songwriter returns with a scruffier, more far-ranging record about developing a self in your twenties.

title: A Day in a Yellow Beat
description: The young English singer and songwriter’s funk-inspired synth pop is appealingly goofy, but too often, he sounds caught in a bland impersonation act of his own making.

title: &&&&&
description: A new reissue of Arca’s 25-minute mixtape from 2013 highlights its prophetic, trailblazing qualities. It remains an unfathomably skillful and multi-layered piece of music.

title: Orca
description: The songwriter’s self-produced second LP is an introduction to the psyche beneath the quirky bowl cut. But its self-imposed pop formulas and strained symbolism reveal little.

title: So Glossy and So Thin
description: This Chicago trio makes the rare free-jazz album that goes down easy, playing with a grace that makes even the farthest-out moments feel accessible.

title: Down to the Lowest Terms: The Soul Sessions
description: On his first proper comeback album, the funk legend displays his unmatched vocal chops over polished, modern production.

title: Keyboard Fantasies
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Beverly Glenn-Copeland’s masterwork from 1986, a hermetic and wondrous new age album that contains worlds beyond worlds.

title: Mandinga Times
description: On her first album in a decade, the Dominican iconoclast delivers an explosive comeback full of horror scenes, metal sounds, and post-colonial politics.

title: Harvest Vol. 1
description: The first compilation from electronic Bangkok label More Rice is a solid collection of chugging dancefloor weaponry from South Korea, the Philippines, Thailand and beyond.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: The American DJ, known for her breathtaking, hyperkinetic club anthems, delivers a wide-ranging, shape-shifting set of techno, breakbeats, and leftfield pop.

title: Apparition Paintings
description: The veteran British composer, improviser, author, and scholar assembles a dreamlike, mercurial album of sonic collage that doubles as a philosophical treatise on sound and memory.

title: Cantus, Descant
description: The minimalist composer-performer’s slow, patient works demand and reward close attention; give them time, and their secrets will rise slowly to the surface.

title: Takuya Kuroda: Fly Moon Die Soon
description: The Japanese trumpeter’s dense and cosmic sixth album blends jazz with Afrobeat, hip-hop, neo-soul, and funk.

title: How Ill Thy World Is Ordered
description: The Ontario musician caps a prolific year with his tenth album of 2020: a rip-roaring rock record that draws on a hodgepodge of styles and sounds, from blustery horns to roadtrip folk-rock.

title: voyage au soleil
description: The debut from this instrumental trio has the air of a purifying ritual, blending psychedelia with a loose-limbed minimalism.

title: Hard Luck Stories (1972-1982)
description: An eight-disc box set tells the complete story of the talented yet star-crossed UK folk-rock duo, tying up loose ends and illuminating areas previously shrouded in darkness.

title: Sunday Painter
description: Joined by players including percussionist Mauro Refosco and guitarist Dave Harrington, the New York bassist takes atmospheric cues from classic ECM productions while evoking relaxed, low-key vibes.

title: GMTO, Vol. 1 (Get Money Take Over)
description: On his debut mixtape, the Brooklyn drill rapper performs with hungry urgency, as if prosperity is around the corner for everyone except him.

title: Proboscidea EP
description: On the latest in a series of EPs, the unique Atlanta rapper creates his own cocoon in which to hone his craft.

title: Goats Head Soup
description: In 1973, Goats Head Soup marked the end of the Stones’ imperial era, capturing them as they transitioned from the World’s Greatest Rock‘n’Roll Band to just a really good one.

title: Angelheaded Hipster: The Songs of Marc Bolan & T. Rex
description: An all-star cast pays tribute to the glam-rock icon, but their interpretations too often read angst and torpor in place of the singer’s pomp and frivolity.

title: The Fifth Season
description: Following her brash and confounding debut, the singer-producer slows everything down, recreating the sparse magnetism of her live show.

title: No era sólida
description: As though channeling supernatural energies, the Colombian experimental musician uses eerie electronics and vocal treatments to imbue unsettling world-building with a mystical sort of grace.

title: Lessons
description: The underrated titan of West Coast gangsta rap stays true to his classic formula on an LP featuring guest verses from spiritual descendants Conway the Machine and Dave East.

title: Spell My Name
description: The masterful R&B singer returns with more creative control on a project where her voice, style, and swagger are well preserved.

title: From King to a GOD
description: On his latest album, the Buffalo rapper and member of the tough-talking trio Griselda makes his first bid for a bigger audience.

title: The Universal Want
description: The Britrock survivors’ first album in 11 years is the sound of men in their 50s channeling the memories of their teens through the music of their 30s.

title: PHONE PHREAKER$ PHREAK BACK
description: Producer Bryant Canelo’s latest album is filled with ambient memories, distorted house skeletons, and spoken-word rants. It’s not so much exhausting as it is exhaustive.

title: Electr-O-Pura
description: In 1995, the indie rock trio lurched headlong into its own sound with Electr-O-Pura. Now, newly reissued on vinyl, the pop-focused and densely referential album remains a monument in the band’s catalog.

title: Pod
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the Breeders’ debut album, a warped and indispensable piece of the ’90s alternative canon.

title: All That Emotion
description: Produced with the National’s Aaron Dessner, the introspective Canadian singer-songwriter’s stately fourth album evokes an atmosphere of quiet loveliness.

title: Comma
description: On his third album created primarily with modular synthesizers, the longtime Sea and Cake frontman makes fascinatingly abstracted music about the act of listening itself.

title: The Fire Still Burns
description: Following the recent rediscovery of his 1975 album Valley of Search, the saxophonist releases a quintet set of all-new compositions that nod to jazz history while rocketing off to points unknown.

title: pop songs 2020 EP
description: Michelle Zauner (a.k.a. Japanese Breakfast) and Ryan Galloway of Crying form a socially distanced, easy-going pop duo whose music offers a brief respite from the times.

title: Re-Animator
description: The latest from the Manchester cult favorites lacks the overwhelming chaos of their best music, but it’s their most thoughtful work yet.

title: American Head
description: At the top of their fifth decade, the Lips rekindle their past romance with Neil Young’s piano ballads, the Beatles’ psychedelic guitar tones, and Bowie’s stargazing anthems on a deeply personal album.

title: C’mon Les’ Go EP
description: Chaz Bear (of Toro y Moi) teams up with New York club producer AceMo for a fun, spirited, spontaneous debut EP.

title: Detroit 2
description: On his fifth solo album, Big Sean gets personal, leans on a slate of high-profile guests to provide most of the entertainment, and struggles to deliver anything that isn’t fundamentally embarrassing.

title: Western Swing & Waltzes and Other Punchy Songs
description: The Canadian country singer trades his solitary fare for a new set of stories, and a backing band that cuts in and out like a dance partner.

title: Autogenesis
description: Covering Bill Evans and riffing on Moroccan gnawa and classical minimalism, the 10-piece Harlem band embraces a global vision infused with jazz’s searching spirit.

title: Renaissance
description: With her solo debut, AlunaGeorge’s Aluna Francis explores dance music in many forms—pop-house, dancehall, funk, Caribbean and African dance—as a personal refuge and an industry corrective.

title: Muthaland
description: On her debut album, the Chattanooga rapper balances raunchy sex talk with reflections on trauma. It’s a deliriously entertaining, ambitious project from an artist operating at her peak.

title: Zeros
description: Nodding to Bowie and the Beatles on songs about climate change and capitalism, the 21-year-old songwriter roots his political critique in the rich tradition of British protest rock.

title: Ten Billion Angels
description: Channeling an eerily affecting cyborg tenderness, the Austrian producer and digital nomad writes post-club anthems that sound like pop hits from a parallel universe.

title: Hannah
description: The stunning, open-hearted new album from indie rock singer-songwriter Hannah Read renders personal crises with a deft and delicate touch.

title: Solo / Solo II
description: The collected solo recordings from a veteran of three of krautrock’s fundamental groups—Kraftwerk, Neu!, and Harmonia—walk the line between mesmerizing riffs and wistful, cinematic gestures.

title: 12th House Rock
description: Behind their overt shoegaze and grunge revivalism, the Houston rock band finds careful guitar melodies, sensitive vocal deliveries, and earnest earworms.

title: Awake in the Brain Chamber
description: One of rock music’s former Next Big Things returns with a propulsive, stream-lined album that has the modest charm of fan service.

title: Diva
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Diva, an album that captures Ivy Queen’s legacy as an ardent lyricist and vocalist, a forceful defender of women, and a torchbearer for reggaetón’s subversive—and commercial—promise.

title: The Quiet City
description: The Swedish minimalist composer David Wenngren specializes in soft, evocative miniatures. The songs on his latest album pass by quickly, like fortuitous weather that can hold for just so long.

title: Fall to Pieces
description: After a string of misfires, the UK musician’s 14th album translates unimaginable loss into some of his most darkly moving music in years.

title: Gold Record
description: On his latest solo record, the singer-songwriter continues his quiet excavation of self and the tumultuous world around him, exploring how a supposedly ordinary life is often anything but.

title: Zap the Planet
description: The funky and hypnotic fourth album from the Canadian trio coats a suite of warped synth-pop grooves in the lead singer’s slow-talking sleaze.

title: Plum
description: With glowing synths and lyrics about labor and death, the New York duo’s fifth LP is a tastefully small reflection on modern anxieties.

title: Born Again
description: The NYC rapper YL’s music is full of slice-of-life details that capture the feel of aimless youth.

title: Greenhouse
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter’s music is measured, slow, and focused, allowing space for complex emotions to bloom.

title: Mama, You Can Bet!
description: The third installment of Georgia Anne Muldrow’s solo jazz project is a powerfully resonant and spiritual record, a call-and-response between herself and a history of Black music.

title: The Baby
description: On her first full-length, the singer-songwriter navigates the trappings of young adulthood with subtle, poetic writing and a sardonically sunny indie-rock sound.

title: Got to Be Tough
description: The Reggae legend returns in full force on his latest album, displaying the indomitable spirit he has cultivated throughout his career.

title: Agora
description: Although recorded in the shadow of tragedy, the Brazilian singer-songwriter’s first album in six years is characteristically delicate in tone and full of charm.

title: All These Perfect Crosses
description: With a collection of outtakes, demos, and acoustic reworkings from his three previous solo records, the Hold Steady frontman re-examines familiar characters from new angles.

title: Club Future Nostalgia
description: Packing 15 producers into 50 minutes, the fun but overstuffed Future Nostalgia rework hopscotches between piano house, Baltimore club, and the kind of dance remixes that power Chelsea gay bars.

title: The Room
description: Ricky Reed, the producer behind Lizzo’s “Truth Hurts” as well as hits by Jason Derulo and Fifth Harmony, offers a solo debut made via livestream and defined by a hazy, late-night melancholy.

title: Whole New Mess
description: Recorded in Anacortes, Washington, the stark original version of the songwriter’s 2019 album All Mirrors makes the experience of solitude sound metaphysical. The songs are spare, but still feel electric.

title: Holy Wind
description: The Queens-based producer Alex Dadras has worked with artists as diverse as A$AP Rocky and Show Me the Body. On Holy Wind, he leaves the city behind for an otherworldly record with ecological themes.

title: Inner Song
description: On her second album, the Welsh electronic musician leans into both her loops and her lyrics, seeking something spiritual in the act of repetition.

title: S&M2
description: Two decades later, Metallica reunite with the San Francisco Symphony for a chiefly fans-only document that adds more needless orchestration to already orchestral metal songs.

title: Undercurrent
description: The latest from the pair of Italian experimental musicians marked by its simplicity, distilling their music down to its most lyrical and affecting form yet.

title: ENERGY
description: The Lawrence brothers’ third album of glossy yet gritty disco pop suggests that their true lineage is the Y2K chart-house sound once ubiquitous on UK airwaves.

title: Knot
description: The former members of Krill return with a slower pace and a heavy political conscience. The effect is one of careful deliberation in place of what once seemed to come so naturally.

artist: Vladislav Delay / Sly Dunbar / Robbie Shakespeare
title: 500-Push-Up
description: The Finnish experimental electronic producer and legendary Jamaican rhythm section team up in search of an elusive balance between their distinctive styles.

title: Pussy Cats
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the infamous 1974 album Pussy Cats, produced by John Lennon, the moment a would-be titan consigned himself to a tragic cult figure.

title: Papi Juancho
description: The Colombian pop star’s latest is low stakes, neither offensive nor remarkable, the sound of a reggaetonero you’d expect to find on a mood board for a fashion campaign.

title: Mi specchio e rifletto
description: Inspired by poet Alda Merini, the Italian violinist and vocalist composes a nuanced investigation of the divine feminine, illuminating complex emotional specifics of motherhood and life.

title: Smile
description: Katy Perry’s bubbly, cliché-ridden pop feels especially unsuited for life in a pandemic. But despite all her garbled platitudes, she remains a master at executing chart-topping formulas.

title: Crabs in a Bucket
description: On the UK road rapper’s heavy third album, Nines ably explores the conflict between his old life and his new one with typical flair.

title: Shabrang
description: On her sophomore album, the singer examines good and evil through a series of spare, cryptic parables.

title: Primal Forms
description: The Polish clarinetist Wacław Zimpel blows away the cobwebs from Sam Shackleton’s often shadowy psychedelia, adding a celebratory force to the English electronic musician’s hypnotic minimalism.

title: Load It Up, Vol. 01
description: The latest from the incarcerated L.A. rapper, stemming from the same frenzied recording period just before he went to prison, is an hour of lived-in, reliable street rap that continues to shape and contour the psyche of a rapper in his final days of freedom.

title: Well Groomed (Original Score)
description: The rainbow-colored pups of Rebecca Stern’s documentary are in concert with the Dan Deacon’s score, which teases out the heart underneath the ostensibly garish world of creative dog grooming.

title: King’s Disease
description: The Queensbridge legend’s 13th album marks a retreat into a nostalgia-act comfort zone, one that suits him even as it yields diminishing returns.

title: Motherhood
description: On their fearlessly creative, beat-heavy new record, the Montreal band spikes their dream pop with trip-hop, nu-metal, and other ’90s signifiers.

title: APOLLO
description: The rising Nigerian singer is on the vanguard of the hybrid “Afro-life” sound and his latest album is the peak of his vision so far, a melodious, detailed, and effortless album of feel-good pop and R&B.

title: Eno Axis
description: With spacious live takes and poetic lyricism, the North Carolina songwriter’s second album brings order to the chaos of the day. Step inside Eno Axis and things immediately fall into place.

title: The Dirt and the Stars
description: Three decades into her career, one of country music’s most reliable and empathetic songwriters offers a profoundly intimate record, full of hushed revelations.

title: In Sickness & In Flames
description: The New Jersey duo’s seventh album sacrifices some of the group’s youthful spark, blurring emo nostalgia with contemporary pop polish.

title: Freeze, Melt
description: The Australian electro-pop veterans return with a climate-change album both as chilled as an upscale boutique and as politically engaged as your Instagram feed.

title: eeeeeeep! EP
description: The analog master’s first all-digital release is a compelling document of a veteran artist learning new tricks.

title: The Consuming Flame: Open Exercises in Group Form
description: This striking release from the eclectic duo brings together 99 collaborators to create an enthralling picture of the present moment.

title: Source
description: On her stunning debut, the tenor saxophonist and rising member of the London jazz scene meditates on her humble family heritage, the continuum of jazz history, and the power of collective action in our present moment.

title: SUGAREGG
description: Reintroducing her band as a solo project, Alicia Bognanno follows the tried-and-true: sticky hooks, shoutalong lyrics, and walloping, caffeinated riffs.

title: Happy Birthday
description: The post-punk rebel incorporates elements of house and hip-hop while retaining the swagger and rawness of her early work.

title: Touch the Sound
description: The debut from the Chicago trio tempers grandiose experiments with a keen drive for melody and structure, pushing the further reaches of psychedelia without ever losing its footing.

title: In a Dream EP
description: The Australian pop singer finds freedom in the EP format, breaking the family-friendly veneer of past releases and serving up his most idiosyncratic music yet.

title: Crazy Ex-Girlfriend
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the stellar rise of Miranda Lambert with her second album, one that laid the groundwork for an artist destined for country superstardom.

title: everything means nothing
description: Matthew Tyler Musto’s latest album feels like a time capsule for this cursed year, a nauseating sludge of every “Study Beats” playlist and every TikTok influencer’s attempt at writing a hit.

title: Bent Arcana
description: Oh Sees leader John Dwyer indulges his jammiest tendencies alongside a new cast of powerhouse players, channeling a distinctly 1970s sort of communal exploration.

title: Spinner
description: The newly reissued collaboration between Brian Eno and bassist Jah Wobble from 1995 is an outlier in both their catalogs, which is part and parcel of its allure.

title: The Neon
description: The UK synth-pop duo’s 18th studio album attempts—but doesn’t quite attain—the electric thrill of the material that first made them pop sensations.

title: Show Pony EP
description: The enigmatic masked country singer follows up his debut with more songs about lonesome souls alone together—and one standout duet with Shania Twain.

title: Imploding the Mirage
description: Led by the exquisite brio of Brandon Flowers, the Las Vegas band returns with one of their biggest and best albums, a marvelously absurd collection of synth-rock gems and arena anthems.

title: Down in the Weeds, Where the World Once Was
description: Conor Oberst and company have not lost their taste for grandiosity on their first album in nearly a decade, setting familiar woes against a dazzling collage of sounds.

title: Blush
description: The Stranger Things actor’s move into music is refreshingly thoughtful and understated, with emotionally incisive songwriting and a featherlight voice wrapped up in Laurel Canyon arrangements.

title: Songs for the General Public
description: Classic-rock magpies, brothers Michael and Brian D’Addario construct a fabulously campy pastiche from the spangled castoffs of the 1970s.

title: Twice as Tall
description: The Nigerian superstar’s latest LP can feel heavy under the weight of his personal reflection and Pan-African crusade. It is a load worth carrying.

title: Ho, why is you here ?
description: The brief, playful project from the Alabama rapper is one of the breeziest records of the year, a clinic on nimble shit-talking that’s as effortless as it is brash.

title: Multiply Intentions
description: The Russian electronic experimentalist creates a world without borders, singing in four languages across ambient soundscapes that evoke imaginary lands.

title: Articulation
description: Producer and composer Ryan Lee West continues his practice of turning real-life sketches into ambient techno as ever-shifting moments dip, dive, and refuse to settle.

title: Luminous
description: A seven-track accompaniment to the brothers’ album Mixing Colours—released as both standalone EP and digital add-on—highlights the nuances of their playing and the limits of the attention span.

title: FIXTAPE
description: The dancehall superstar’s latest mixtape is the best of every facet of his work, from slow-wine ballads to summery head-bangers. It’s a testament to his place at the forefront of the genre.

title: Candid
description: Though no song on the Chicago rock band’s all-covers album is particularly wild or ambitious, the collection is faithful, fine-tuned, and thoughtfully curated.

title: Welcome to Conceptual Beach
description: Fusing influences from improv and minimalist composition with its customarily exploratory post-rock, the L.A. band sounds more assured than ever: playful, funky, even willing to flex a bit.

title: I Must Be Living Twice EP
description: The synth-pop soloist recaptures the moody appeal of his earliest releases on this low-stakes collection of covers.

title: Non-Secure Connection
description: The late-career renaissance of a great American troubadour continues with an eclectic album featuring Jamila Woods, James Mercer, Vernon Reid, and others.

title: Total Freedom
description: After a self-imposed exile from the music industry, the Ottawa singer-songwriter is clear-eyed and serene, writing just for the thrill of discovery.

title: Mach's Hard Lemonade
description: The clandestine and engrossing Newark rapper’s latest is a seamless continuation of a long string of reliable records; it is also one of his strongest yet, engrossing despite its brevity.

title: Ridin’ Dirty
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Pimp C and Bun B’s 1996 masterpiece about a weekend in Houston that became a touchstone for Southern rap.

title: Crave
description: After a car accident derailed her life, the pop singer returns with her second album, compacting emotional and romantic upheaval into tactile electro-pop packed with splashy synths and soaring melodies.

title: To Feel Embraced
description: After spending decades creating music out of undiscovered noises, avant-garde composer William Basinski lets his hair down on this joyful, funky release.

title: The Versace Tape
description: On his third album of 2020 and first for Griselda Records, the Detroit rapper continues to pry open windows onto his past, soul, and psyche.

title: What Could Possibly Go Wrong
description: The rising 24-year-old Florida rapper surfs affably on TikTok trends and sounds exactly like a label executive’s idea of the future.

title: Unity
description: The South Sudanese star reflects and celebrates the liminal life of a refugee on his first album recorded in Australia, where he's lived in asylum from his home country's civil war since 2014.

title: Shutting Down Here
description: The experimental polymath looks back on key musical influences in a 34-minute piece that seamlessly melds noise and melody into one of his most personal recordings yet.

title: 7G
description: The PC Music mastermind’s debut solo album is a 49-song extravaganza of sketches, covers, and fully realized pop songs that purports to reveal the inner workings of his creative method.

title: Prole Art Threat
description: The grime producer teams up with a host of rising MCs for a bleak and energizing album that tries to imagine a better future.

title: Lickety Split EP
description: Filled with ruthlessly efficient grooves, the latest EP from the Montreal producer is his most assured work yet.

title: Last Year Was Weird, Vol. 2
description: The second installment of a planned trilogy is a fleet-footed journey throughout many styles and moods, yet frames the 23-year-old artist fully as herself.

title: Goodbye, Nowhere!
description: The Minnesota trio’s forlorn second album holds up alongside distorted post-shoegaze classics but stays true to its chilly slowcore roots.

title: Harbors
description: Ellen Fullman’s imposing Long String Instrument and Theresa Wong’s cello create harmonically complex chord clusters that seem to place you within the belly of the composition itself.

title: Boots No. 2: The Lost Songs, Vol. 1
description: Quickly recorded in 2002 to fulfill a publishing contract, this archival trove cements the singer-songwriter and her steadfast partner, David Rawlings, as modern masters of American folk.

title: Eight Gates
description: The late songwriter recorded the unreleased Eight Gates in the ’00s. The posthumous version sounds by turns haunting and unfinished.

title: Limbo
description: On his new album, the Portland rapper rediscovers the appealing lightness that made him famous.

title: Help
description: On his ruminative and memory-haunted new album, the pianist and singer explores community and the ties that bind us.

title: The Jacknife Lee
description: The Irish modern-rock producer, best known for his work on records by U2, Snow Patrol, and Kasabian, opts for an idiosyncratic electronic melange featuring a surprising roster of guests.

title: Live at Goose Lake: August 8th, 1970
description: Newly unearthed audio of the Stooges’ infamous final original lineup performance highlights their masterful album Fun House and sheds light on their raw, druggy, unhinged stage show.

title: The Hijinx Tape
description: The latest signee to the $uicideboy$ label is an Atlanta skater-turned-rapper with a voice that’s as aggressive as it is gleeful. His new tape isn’t that serious, but his rapping is.

title: Dreamland
description: The UK psych-pop band stretches out to embrace hip-hop production and personal biography. It comes across like a guy trying to tell you his life story in a packed Coachella tent.

title: Cover Charge: NC Artists Go Under Cover to Benefit Cat’s Cradle
description: Featuring artists like Superchunk, the Mountain Goats, and Iron & Wine, this 25-song benefit compilation for the beloved North Carolina venue Cat’s Cradle boasts far more riches than a charity project requires.

title: Purple Noon
description: Ernest Greene floats back into the slipstream with an album of innocuous, Balearic-influenced makeout jams that sound lush but are mostly empty on the inside.

title: The Battle of Los Angeles
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the third album from the radical rap-rock band, their sharpest revolutionary screed dropped into the dead zone of 1999.

title: This Devastating Map
description: As a member of Duster and Built to Spill, Jason Albertini was often in the background. The latest album from his own band feels like a chance to come up for air.

title: Everlasting
description: The Los Angeles singer-songwriter’s debut album is an ambitious, bilingual record that hops between influences, echoing the liminal state of a 26-year-old immigrant in America.

title: Duma
description: The Kenyan noise band’s debut is inventive and abrasive, a timely distillation of global chaos and techno-dystopian dread.

title: Heart’s Ease
description: The English folk maven sounds spry as ever, leading a light-footed exploration of traditional forms that also tips toward classic psychedelia.

title: Microphones in 2020
description: Phil Elverum resurrects his beloved Microphones alias for a 45-minute song about art-making, self-mythologizing, and the endless search for meaning.

title: Jaguar
description: Monét claims the spotlight on her debut project, a sleek cocoon of funk-tinged R&B that excavates what it means to be in control.

title: Such Pretty Forks in the Road
description: On her first album in eight years, the iconic singer-songwriter continues to take the lyrical road less traveled on a vulnerable, sedate, ballad-heavy album.

title: Impenetrable Cerebral Fortress
description: The fast-rising Santa Cruz hardcore band attack their new LP with a murderous intensity, transforming genre tropes into killer hooks.

title: Detuned Reworks
description: Experimental electronic musicians including Loraine James, Rupert Clervaux, and Oliver Coates tackle the spooky, microtonal source material of last year’s Music for Detuned Pianos.

title: Songbook EP
description: The London-based singer-songwriter takes a leap forward with a nuanced and meticulous set of electro-pop.

title: B7
description: The “vocal bible” of pop R&B returns with her first album in eight years, sounding poised and warm but lacking some spark.

title: Actual Presence
description: Featuring habitual collaborators like Jamael Dean and Miguel Atwood-Ferguson, the L.A. percussionist and producer’s sprawling, shape-shifting seventh album finds joy in unexpected connections.

title: Distance
description: On her solo debut, the L.A.-based singer and songwriter taps members of the War on Drugs and Warpaint for winning songs about finding delight in despair.

title: Voices
description: The composer turns to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948 for inspiration in his bittersweet new orchestral work.

title: On&On
description: The second nominally solo album from the former Yuck frontman uses improvisation, repetition, and group interplay as ways of breaking free of traditional modes of songwriting.

title: Sun Piano
description: Recorded in a Brooklyn church as the first installment of a trilogy, the new age pioneer’s latest shows him returning to his first instrument—the piano.

title: Couldn’t Wait to Tell You
description: Short and fleeting yet bound by a shared aesthetic vision, these 20 songs capture in-between feelings—anticipation, longing, eagerness, hesitation, indecision—with sensitivity and specificity.

title: Triz
description: The enigmatic Philadelphia producer’s latest release submerges vocals in dark interiors, suggesting that the truth may lie just under the surface of our perception.

title: Indistinct Conversations
description: Low-key emotional intensity abounds in Elizabeth Powell’s stark, sketch-like reveries, and the new album’s few-frills production exposes just how gut-wrenching their songwriting can be.

title: Muddbruddas
description: The two Chicago rappers form an alliance possibly out of convenience or shared circumstances, but their opposing styles meld into a project that can work surprisingly well.

title: The Zombies / I Love You / R.I.P.
description: A trilogy of reissues tells the story of a brilliant, unconventional, yet luckless British Invasion band let down by an industry that didn’t know what to do with them.

title: No Horizon EP
description: On this EP recorded with the Brooklyn Youth Chorus, the group shows that their capacity for new ideas and reinvention has yet to fail them.

title: Knock Knock
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Bill Callahan’s masterful 1999 record as Smog, a breakup album about discovering new ways of being in the world.

title: Flaming Pie
description: On his tenth studio album, now reissued with rarities and B-sides, McCartney grappled with emotions too big to neatly fit inside a pop record.

title: Made of Rain
description: The British band’s first new album in 29 years is a rare commodity: a comeback record that’s refreshingly free of nostalgic gestures.

title: A Hero’s Death
description: Heady, funny, and fearless, the Dublin band’s second album is a maudlin and manic triumph, a horror movie shot as comedy, equal parts future-shocked and handcuffed to history.

title: Sucker’s Lunch
description: Co-produced by Wye Oak, the singer-songwriter’s new album reckons with a past of self-doubt and a present of intense uncertainty in order to shape something like a satisfying future.

title: KIND
description: The Montreal-based singer-songwriter and violinist’s music feels like an invitation to reflect. Each song recounts not just stumbling and uncertainty, but a sense of motivation.

title: Miles: From an Interlude Called Life
description: Blu & Exile finally offer a worthy spiritual successor to their seismic 2007 debut with a sprawling double album about the cultural forces that shape us.

title: Long Lost Solace Find
description: The Purling Hiss frontman teams with Kurt Vile for a record of simple folk songs pairing blissful sounds with plainspoken sentiments.

title: Mafia Bidness
description: The buzzing L.A. rap group flattens some of its personality with its major-label debut, a mix of party cuts and bland compromises.

title: Totally Crushed Out / Retreat From the Sun
description: Reissues of the L.A. band’s mid-’90s albums capture how they brought girl-group yearning, three-part harmonies, and virtuoso violin lines to the era of Sassy mag and 120 Minutes.

title: Trasslig EP
description: The Swedish singer and producer Thea Gustafsson’s latest EP creates a singular, cosmopolitan pop mood that is at once stylish and vulnerable.

title: Indigo Dream
description: Displaying an atmospheric sensibility reflecting her soundtrack work for fashion campaigns and short films, the UK producer balances ’80s-inspired synth epics and contemporary, club-adjacent sounds.

title: Capricorn
description: The former Youth Lagoon songwriter’s second album under his own name is almost wordless, a quest for ego death that explores the beauty of the natural world with a lingering disquiet.

title: We Have Amnesia Sometimes
description: The New Jersey trio’s latest consists of five formless, comforting drones, recorded with a single microphone placed in the middle of their Hoboken practice space.

title: Manger on McNichols
description: The Detroit rapper teams with the producer Sterling Toles for his most forward-thinking, experimental, and personal album.
Nine years after the Rapture’s final album, the group’s singer/guitarist returns with his debut solo album, grappling with fatherhood and legacies of trauma in adventurous, ambient-infused art rock.
The Rio de Janeiro MC deftly uses a grime framework to explore a wide range of emotional textures that are part of living in Rio—its pleasures and its hardships.

title: Skullcrusher EP
description: The debut EP from Los Angeles-based ambient folk musician Helen Ballentine is short but captivating. Even without specific details, her words are deeply felt.

title: Witness
description: On his debut album under his own name, the artist formerly known as Deadboy captures a cross-section of recent UK dance-music history, spanning 2-step, breaks, sunrise anthems, and dub techno.

title: George Clanton & Nick Hexum
description: The unlikely collaboration between the vaporwave producer and the 311 frontman feels as natural as a wedge of lime and a bottle of Corona—equal parts basic and deeply satisfying.

title: N_O CALLER ID
description: The East London rapper/singer is mostly successful in creating a portrait of late nights out by using the sounds he grew up with as the backdrop for his free-wheeling ruminations.

title: Folklore
description: Made from afar, primarily with the National’s Aaron Dessner, Swift’s eighth album is a sweater-weather record filled with cinematic love songs and rich fictional details.

title: I Against I
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the hard-fought third album by the D.C. hardcore icons who played faster and better than everyone else.

title: Garbers Days Revisited
description: Anchored by a punishing and timely take on Neil Young’s “Southern Man,” this unexpected covers collection finds the audacious Southern band cutting loose.

title: Seeing Through Sound (Pentimento Volume Two)
description: On the sequel to last year’s Listening to Pictures, the octogenarian trumpet player slips into memoirist mode, allowing old tropes from his past to flicker back to life.

title: mydata
description: The Australian singer-songwriter eases up on her customary digital glitches, manipulated vocals, and sudden cuts for a warm record about the difficulty of forging intimacy through technology.

title: FREE I.H.: This Is Not the One You’ve Been Waiting For
description: Sarah Tudzin’s boundless enthusiasm and bottomless bag of studio tricks dispel the tension of a DIY “mixtape” self-released in part to fulfill the obligations of a label breakup.

title: All the Time
description: Recorded shortly before her move from New York to San Francisco, the Canadian club-pop musician’s third LP with Junior Boys’ Jeremy Greenspan sounds sensual, understated, and effortless.

title: Wu Hen
description: The London jazz musician’s latest stakes out a middle ground between spiritual fire and smooth jazz.

title: Rift ONE
description: On this charity compilation, the Swedish label best known as the home of rappers like Yung Lean and Bladee dives deeper into electronic music and the golden-hour euphoria of trance.

title: Welcome to GStarr Vol. 1
description: The Brooklyn rapper follows in the footsteps of A Boogie Wit Da Hoodie and Lil Tjay, crafting sweetly melodic songs about pain and young love.

title: Lianne La Havas
description: Paring her sound back to little more than her skillful guitar-playing and deep, husky voice, the London songwriter explores the aftermath of a breakup with confidence and repose.

title: Ugly Is Beautiful
description: The debut from this 27-year-old artist-turned-“living meme” chases shock and bombast but winds up surprisingly tame.

title: Die 4 Ur Love EP
description: After a tumultuous label break-up, Valerie Teicher shakes off resentment and disappointment with an upbeat set of light, breezy dance pop.

title: Half Price at 3​:​30
description: Under his oddball alter ego, Here We Go Magic’s Luke Temple presents himself as an Auto-Tune balladeer, Afrobeat enthusiast, and skilled craftsman of moody synth pop.

title: Brightest Blue
description: With her fourth album, the pop songwriter reaches a welcome sense of self-assurance. But if this was supposed to be an introspective record, that’s not what’s happening musically.

title: Gaslighter
description: The trio’s first album in 14 years is a genuinely compelling new take on the punchy country sound that’s always made them stand out. But its links between the personal and the political are foggy.

title: Hate for Sale
description: Chrissie Hynde brings back some old bandmates for a brisk record that acknowledges The Pretenders are best when they’re direct and unadorned.

title: Species
description: The minimalist composer trades his usual chamber ensemble for the comparatively monochromatic tones of the Farfisa organ.

title: Pain Olympics
description: This art-punk collective’s utopian first LP illuminates the joy, camaraderie, and compassion that can exist in even the most unforgiving, isolating circumstances.

title: Flower of Devotion
description: Recording in a studio, the Chicago DIY trio sound newly airy and lush, but no less direct and sincere. Their confidence in their concision is the best part.

title: Yes
description: Continuing a remarkable run of post-comeback releases, the secretive Japanese producer trades chilly dub techno for warm, almost chipper house music.

title: Telas
description: The Chilean American musician’s third album this year is a nominal successor to 2015’s ambient film score Pomegranates, but where that album sprawled, Telas is taut and exhaustively balanced.

title: African Rhythms 1970-1982
description: A landmark anthology originally released in 2001 documents how James “Plunky Nkabinde” Branch and his groups connected jazz, R&B, and funk through Afrocentric rhythms and spirituality.

title: Ultimate Success Today
description: On their fifth album, the Detroit post-punk band recruits a woodwind section for its most expansive statement yet.

title: XOXO
description: The long-running Minnesota band’s 11th album is a distillation of their manifold strengths, largely comprised of pastoral accounts of American beauty curdling into something coarser and sadder.

title: Youth of America
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the gnarly, psychedelic, and insurrectionary sound of the Portland punk band’s best album.

title: American Advertisement
description: The talented young Seattle band plays sly and uncommonly melodic odes to ’70s sleaze-rock on its self-released debut.

title: Violence in a Quiet Mind
description: In a vaporous swirl of voice and emotions, Massachusetts songwriter Woodson Black asks a profound question: Music can always make you feel better, but can it ever make you healed?

title: Life on Earth EP
description: Summer Walker’s follow-up to her 2019 debut album offers a quick tour through the Atlanta singer’s world—a couple sultry strip club joints, a couple guitar-led ballads, and a playful reunion with PARTYNEXTDOOR.

title: Disheveled Cuss
description: Tera Melos guitarist Nick Reinhart turns to grunge and power-pop, embracing the limitations of verse-chorus structure with some of his best songwriting to date.

title: До Свидания / Goodbye
description: Couching politically brazen lyrics about police repression and state hypocrisy in a highly stylized goth maximalism, the high-concept Moscow duo is one of Russia’s most exciting bands.

title: Beyond the Pale
description: The debut album from the Pulp frontman’s new band uses a novel approach to recording that aims for the wild abandon of live music but only occasionally reaches it.

title: Isolated From Exterior Time: 2020
description: On their first release since 2013, the avant-rock group forego the escapism of their past work in order to provide a score for our present chaos.

title: Coriky
description: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina have a new band with an old friend—Fugazi bassist Joe Lally. Their debut is a shrewd distillation of some of the United States’ most insidious issues.

title: Recumbent Speech
description: The guitarist and composer leads his adventurous backing band through immersive instrumentals, creating a tranquil atmosphere from classical minimalism, ambient synth, and nimble fusion.

title: Legends Never Die
description: The Chicago artist’s first posthumous release doesn’t feel like a final goodbye, but instead a continued look inside his world. It’s bleak and beautiful.

title: None of Us Are Getting Out of This Life Alive
description: On the Streets’ first album in nine years, the UK rapper returns to the simple snark of his early music, but his youthful misadventures have been replaced by the jaded pronouncements of middle age.

title: Dialectic Soul
description: Blending free jazz with South African protest music and rigorous academic study, the Cape Town drummer connects jazz tradition to contemporary oppression, and points a way forward for the music.

title: Healing Is a Miracle
description: Juliana Barwick’s revelatory new album asks us to picture healing at a moment when the task feels impossible.

title: That’s How Rumors Get Started
description: With country as her foundation, the versatile singer and songwriter pivots toward classic rock. She sounds less like the honky-tonk rebel and more like the Nashville professional.

title: Barnacles
description: The weirdest of all ATL weirdos returns with more songs about hippos and sex.

title: 1000 gecs & The Tree of Clues
description: On this guest-crowded remix album, the duo continues its wild, swerving path through memes, genres, and decades, making some of its originals sound like demos in the process.

title: Terrain
description: In a collaboration with the stunning singers Theo Bleckmann and Jodie Landau, the sharp young composer processes poems and strings into surprisingly magnetic meditations on time.

title: Skinned
description: In songs as slick and futuristic as the screens that surround us, the Danish electro-pop musician uses technology as a frame for deeply human feelings.

title: The Avalanche
description: Mike Kinsella’s latest is his most relentlessly morose and objectively gorgeous work as Owen to date.

title: Is It Selfish If We Talk About Me Again
description: The singer and former G.O.O.D. Music signee returns with a palette of adult contemporary synth-pop and early-’10s R&B. It’s bright and open, built with sounds that move and breathe with the artist.

title: The Waterfall II
description: When they recorded 2015’s late-career highlight The Waterfall, MMJ wrote enough material for two albums. If the original was about conflict, the new volume concerns the healing that comes after.

title: GLOW
description: Working with a stripped-down palette of synthesizers and almost no drums, the UK producer reconnects with the fundamental sense of strangeness that runs through his best music.

title: Jump Rope Gazers
description: On their second LP, the New Zealand indie rockers downshift into a muted, sleeker sound, sacrificing some of the energy that made their debut special.

title: Meddle
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Pink Floyd’s conflicted and brilliant album from 1971.

title: Workingman’s Dead
description: Newly reissued with bonus material for its 50th anniversary, the Dead’s fourth album returned them to their folk-blues roots and transformed the trajectory of their career in the process.

title: One Year
description: The experimental D.C. duo’s latest album is made up of slabs of textured noise and decayed vocals, but they use their DIY chaos as a radical force against all hierarchies.

title: Kite Symphony, Four Variations
description: Lange, better known as Helado Negro, teams with the visual artist Kristi Sword for a sprawling and inspired project paying tribute to the Marfa, Texas sky.

title: As God Intended
description: The Buffalo-area MC is a savvy and earnest lyricist, pairing a violent streak with a clear-eyed gaze at the conditions behind her grisly scenarios.

title: Proof
description: On a companion EP to last year’s Information, the New York house producer continues to experiment with new styles, but the prevailing mood is one of late-night weariness.

title: As We Suffer From Memory and Imagination
description: The Los Angeles group’s second album is a soul-scouring emotional purge that sets a new bar for screamo—and confirms the genre as one uniquely suited to a year as harrowing as this one.

title: Unfollow the Rules
description: Rufus Wainwright’s first original album in eight years isn’t so much a reinvention as an opulently crafted highlight reel, a career-spanning sampler of the singer’s many styles and guises.

title: The Black Hole Understands
description: Rather than lean into the gimmick of a “bedroom” record, Cloud Nothings’ quarantine album disguises relatively amateur equipment behind clean melodies and power-pop nostalgia.

title: Symphonie Pacifique
description: The prolific British pianist-keyboardist-composer’s work is centered on place, partnership, and circumstance. Mostly abandoning jazz, he crafts an idiosyncratic, pastoral opus.

title: So Icy Summer
description: Buried somewhere in this overstuffed, 80-minute crew compilation is Gucci’s best album in years.
Surviving under capitalism is a drag—it’s the oldest story in rock’n’roll—but No Home captures the weight of its dehumanization in a uniquely visceral way.

title: Source
description: The Hungarian producer’s first album for Planet Mu picks up the deconstructive thread of recent left-field electronic music, splitting the difference between academic inquiry and rave hedonism.

title: Moonlit Navigation
description: On their beautiful second LP, the Minneapolis duo conjure the grandeur of Scandinavian extreme metal with reverence.

title: Massey Fucking Hall
description: This live album, recorded in 2017 at the venerated Toronto concert hall, shows the duo sounding reliable and downright professional. The wild utopian energy that characterizes their albums and their best performances is missing.

title: Black Nationalist Sonic Weaponry
description: DeForrest Brown Jr.’s most ambitious release yet is a 49-minute suite that brings together fractured, shuddering drum programming with spoken-word poetry, collage, and noise.

title: NO
description: On their most compelling album in more than a decade, the discursive metal trio folds their broad musical interests into a relentless series of hardcore oddities.

title: Futuro Conjunto
description: A speculative-fiction multimedia project imagines the future sounds of South Texas’ Rio Grande Valley, using an apocalyptic future to pay tribute to the border region’s resilience.

title: Both of Us / Are U Down
description: The London-based producer’s nostalgic, two-track EP is a love letter to classic house and the tender, unspoken, human connection found on a dance floor.

title: Shoot for the Stars Aim for the Moon
description: The 20-year-old rising star was the voice of Brooklyn drill when he died. On his debut album, executive-produced by 50 Cent, his voice shines through despite a raft of unnecessary features.

title: City on Lock
description: Finally reunited, Yung Miami and JT bring their signature amped-up party jams, while also making space to acknowledge what they’ve survived.

title: National Freedom
description: In a 2014 session with the late Richard Swift, the Alabama sculptor and blues man builds on the foundation of American roots music, reshaping his influences into works that transcend genre.

title: I’m Allergic to Dogs!
description: The Los Angeles singer’s whole songwriting vibe is magnetic, blending future pop, bedroom pop, and funk into a new and colorful swirl.

title: Tactics EP
description: Two-thirds of The Comet Is Coming, plus poet and saxophonist Alabaster DePlume, offer ecstatic anthems for battling fascism, capitalism, and catastrophe.

title: Seo Taiji and Boys
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 1992 debut from Seo Taiji and Boys, a canny synthesis of rap, techno, and rock that would soon be seen as the dawn of K-pop.

title: 6pc Hot EP
description: On his laid-back and locked-in new EP, the Atlanta singer-rapper sounds more subtle and assured than ever.

title: EarthSeed
description: Like Octavia Butler’s Afro-futurist science fiction, which inspired the piece, this experimental septet performance can seduce, challenge, and unnerve in the span of a few measures.

title: The Passion Of
description: Mixing art-punk, industrial, and techno, the outstanding New Orleans four-piece emerge with a blistering vision of punk as possibility.

title: Ungodly Hour
description: On the slinky follow-up to their carefree debut, the R&B sisters take greater risks with their production and their writing.

title: Flight Tower EP
description: Dirty Projectors are once again a group effort. Their new EP is helmed by singer Felicia Douglass, whose smooth voice is an antidote to the unrelenting weirdness of Dave Longstreth’s arrangements.

title: Our Two Skins
description: On her sparse and riveting second album, the singer-songwriter examines the personal cost of embracing difficult emotional truths.

title: Red Cross EP / Phaseshifter / Show World
description: A trio of reissues from Merge and Third Man capture the L.A. punk veterans at two very different points in their career, tracking their growth from scrappy dilettantes to swaggering glam rockers.

title: Country Westerns
description: This world-weary garage-rock trio’s music is tailor-made for a pre-pandemic era of basement shows.

title: You’re a Crusher / drocan!
description: The Massachusetts-based drummer and producer buries pop music in experimental chaos using studio wizardry and a deft compositional touch.

title: Inlet
description: The inscrutable shoegaze legends return with a towering reunion album, their first in 22 years. Unexpectedly, it is their most emotionally accessible music yet.

title: ISS005 / ISS006
description: A pair of new EPs splits the German producer’s work down the middle: ISS005 is reserved strictly for big, bruising club tracks, while ISS006 trades the drums for pure, beatless ambient.

title: New Grass
description: The tenor saxophonist’s beguiling and divisive 1969 album attempted to cross-wire free jazz with rock, funk, and soul. It remains his most misunderstood record.

title: KiCk i
description: On the first album of a four-part series, the Venezuelan-born, Barcelona-based artist offers her most accessible music to date, channeling her signature sounds into sharply focused avant-pop.

title: Everything’s Strange Here
description: The Oakland rapper’s quarantine album is meant to portray a radically different artist. More often, he just finds new ways to telegraph the same stories he’s told all along.

title: Sing the Snow Away: The Chunklet Years
description: A collection of catchy, lo-fi 7"s on Athens’ Chunklet shows off the Philadelphia musician Jason Henn’s bedroom-pop prowess and surreal, often funny songwriting.

title: A New Found Relaxation
description: The Big Thief drummer excels at creating ambient worlds, and his second release under his own name evokes the spine-tingling sensations of ASMR as well as a persistent anxiety.

title: What’s Your Pleasure?
description: On her disco-inspired new album, Ware sounds bolder, looser — and frankly, more fun — than she has in a near-decade.

title: The Shadows and the Light
description: The outstanding Chicago-based drummer incorporates ideas from the city’s iconic forebears and ever-evolving jazz scene into his own fluid style.

title: How can I
description: On her second EP, the South Korean producer branches out from the house music of her debut, touching upon juke, trap, and techno while sing-rapping in a mixture of English and Korean.

title: Pure Moods, Vol. 1
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the famous ’90s compilation that bottled the essence of commercial new age music.

title: GREEN
description: The Japanese ambient pioneer’s well-deserved revival continues with a reissue of this 1986 cult classic, which feels like an inviting frame in which to project your own feelings.

title: Weight of the World
description: On his wonderful and grief-stricken new album, the Bronx rapper pays tribute to his late mother and proves that his voice grows stronger even in sorrow.

title: ROSETTA EP
description: Named in honor of Sister Rosetta Tharpe, the Minneapolis-based musician’s shadowy EP is an imaginative investigation of religious and sexual tensions.

title: Mordechai
description: On their third album, the dubby band’s feel for a groove remains intact, but they often render vibrant sounds from all over the world as impeccably stylish mood music.

title: A Portrait of an Ugly Man
description: The Minneapolis emo band broke through in 2017 with a giddy pop-punk sound; two albums later, they are taking bigger chances but falling flatter.

title: False Spring
description: Returning after a five-year absence, the Brooklyn musician slots into a tradition of cryptic, pastoral singer-songwriters; more than his lyrics, it’s the peaceful mood-setting that stands out.

title: Mia Gargaret
description: Following the loss of her voice while out on tour, the Chicago singer-songwriter turned to her synthesizers as she recuperated, building loops out of glowing, meditative tones.

title: Women in Music Pt. III
description: The third album from the trio is far and away their best. Intimate, multidimensional, and wide-ranging, the songwriting shines with personality and a great curiosity for melody and style.

title: Kitchen Sink
description: The best songs on the singer-songwriter’s excellent fourth album invoke the surreal melodramas of Björk and the wry social commentary of Pulp.

title: Naujawanan Baidar
description: Reworking a trove of cassettes filled with decades-old songs from Kabul, the Arizona native explores his Afghan heritage by collaging traditional melodies, entrancing loops, and psychedelic noise.

title: Young & Turnt 2 (Deluxe)
description: The whistling, shit-talking Detroit rapper has found nationwide appeal without abandoning the core elements of his city’s homegrown style.

title: Somewhere
description: The duo of guitarist Courtney Garvin and drummer Connor Mayer make deranged twee psych-pop, anxious and sometimes goofy songs fit for isolation in unfamiliar surroundings.

title: Bigger Love
description: The R&B star’s latest ode to the power of love bursts with positive energy, but there’s an emptiness beneath.

title: Homegrown
description: After 46 years, Neil Young unearths a lost but highly consequential album, a collection of humble, stripped-back love songs he began writing at what was arguably the artistic zenith of his career.

title: Son of a Gun
description: With his gorgeous, cocksure flow and odd ear for beats, the Memphis rapper asserts his position as a singular rising star.

artist: Roy Ayers / Adrian Younge / Ali Shaheed Muhammad
title: Roy Ayers JID 002
description: As pleasant and groovy as it is, the collaborative album never feels like a true Roy Ayers work.

title: The Album
description: Teyana Taylor regains control of her art across a long and complex album, one that deftly recontextualizes classic R&B and better represents the fierce persona she has honed in public.

title: Little Dominiques Nosebleed
description: On his fourth solo LP, the indie rapper shifts from scattered journal entries to focused autobiography, telling the story of his family and his neighborhood with intimacy and warmth.
With battering-ram drums and cavernous bass, the producer’s second album is a high-energy drama about planetary destruction that almost dares you not to take it seriously.

title: Shadow Offering
description: On their fourth album, the Montreal trio begins a new chapter, one robust enough to hold the intense emotions in frontwoman Raphaelle Standell-Preston’s vocals.

title: Kern Vol. 5
description: In a mix for Berlin nightclub Tresor’s mix series, the Hamburg DJ doles out more than two hours of industrial-tinged techno and electro, all delivered with her typically punishing panache.

title: Punisher
description: On her marvelous second album, Phoebe Bridgers defines her songwriting: candid, multi-dimensional, slyly psychedelic, and full of heart. Her music has become a world unto itself.

title: Maggot Brain
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a monument psychedelic funk, a defining document of Black rock music in the early ’70s.

title: Tearless
description: The Finnish duo’s deconstructed club music grapples with life in the Anthropocene, drawing from nu-metal and hardcore in songs that feel burned out and overwhelmed.

title: South Somewhere Else
description: The jangle-pop band’s latest is a deceptively cheery-sounding reckoning with the violence of white American history.

title: Reality Tunnels
description: Thirteen years after his debut album helped open up new possibilities for UK bass music, the Bristol fixture returns with an LP meant to probe the various corners of his musical universe.

title: on the tender spot of every calloused moment
description: On the jazz trumpeter’s fifth album, Akinmusire and his extremely tight band are after your immediate emotional response. It’s music that seeks peace not just despite a world of unrest, but within it.

artist: Bessie Jones and the Georgia Sea Island Singers
title: Get in Union
description: The reissued compilation from the great American folk and gospel singer is a generous introduction to a historically muted view of Black life in the South.

title: Rough and Rowdy Ways
description: Six decades into his career, Bob Dylan delivers a gorgeous and meticulous record. It is the rare Dylan album that asks to be understood and comes down to meet its audience.

title: Providence
description: The Oakland trio’s understanding of the art of death metal continues to deepen and spiral off into unexpected territory.

title: Out in the World
description: The new album from multi-instrumentalist Jay Watson (Tame Impala, POND) is his most ambitious to date, imbuing his mad-scientist home-recording project with some fleeting glimpses into his life beyond the console.

title: Room for the Moon
description: Alongside a cast of musicians who help bring her kaleidoscopic world to life, the Russian avant-pop artist emerges with a visionary record that offers an escape from gloom.

title: I Love You Say It Back
description: Braiding together searching raps, fizzy beats, and charming pop hooks, the underground Atlanta rapper’s new album is a swirl of conflicting emotions animated by near-constant ad-libs.

title: Annual
description: The group’s new mini-album is their most consistent and focused, but by drawing their sound down to its essence, they dampen the anything-goes spirit that made them so appealing.

title: TO LOVE IS TO LIVE
description: With livewire intensity, the Savages singer-songwriter’s ambitious and experimental solo album explodes with life from every corner as an epic display of contrasting themes and emotion.

title: S/T EP
description: Just weeks after releasing a new album and accompanying 7", the Portuguese batida producer completes the triptych with a dynamic and defiant four-track EP of tough, percussive club cuts.

title: Zoom
description: Invoking the playful spirit of classic IDM, the Dutch producer’s debut full-length is an ode to reveling in the beauty of life’s tiniest details.

title: The Godfather 3
description: After a protracted battle with Stormzy and a scrapped crossover album, the grime veteran regroups and offers what he calls his final album.
