title: Muzak pour ascenseurs en panne
description: Pépé Bradock made his name crafting immaculate deep house, but for more than a decade he has delighted in flouting expectations. Guitar in hand, he does just that on this album under a new alias.

title: MTV Unplugged
description: After infamously bailing out right before Oasis’s 1996 MTV Unplugged performance, the irascible, charismatic Britpop anti-hero gets a second chance.

title: Startisha
description: Naeem Juwan steps away from the Spank Rock persona on an album that drifts between manic experimentation and somber fury. It’s the work of a freer musician, one unburdened by internet hype.

title: Drug Dealing Is a Lost Art EP
description: Months after his country-rap video went viral, the purposefully mysterious artist releases an EP with all the personality of a wiped smartphone.

title: So Tonight That I Might See
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a dream pop classic, a spare and gauzy outpouring of feeling that still ripples through modern music.

title: Built to Spill Plays the Songs of Daniel Johnston
description: Following a tour together in 2017, Doug Martsch & co. tackle an album’s worth of the Texas singer-songwriter’s work, but they fail to capture the strange and messy spirit that animates his music.

title: Like Water
description: The Australian producer trades the moody house of his breakout hit, “Winona,” for big-room techno suggestive of the kinds of clubs he has gotten used to playing in recent years.

title: Up All Nite With Prince: The One Nite Alone Collection
description: This reissued box set from Prince’s unloved early-’00s period provides proof of his astounding skill as a performer and the depth of his catalog even in its shallow end.

title: Songs We Sang in Our Dreams
description: In collaboration with singer Xan Tyler, the musician and producer Kramer offers a thoughtful, cavernous-sounding counterweight to a mischievous career.

title: Nomad
description: The latest album from the meditative duo is an impressionistic portrait of life spent in transit.

title: Your Hero Is Not Dead
description: The British songwriter’s excellent debut mines the gentle and detailed sounds of soft rock’s past, while his lucid yet uncomplicated lyrics interrogate the uncertainty of the present.

title: Madison Tapes
description: On her intimate and assured new album, the Brooklyn R&B singer eagerly seeks deliverance from bad sex, bad vibes, and the pulsing anxiety of dead-end jobs.

title: Meditations Mixtape, Vol. 1
description: A devotional prayer for ill relatives inspires some of the Baltimore ambient musician’s most engulfing and moving songs yet.

title: The Freelancer’s Blues
description: The cosmic country of the Brooklyn singer-songwriter is both wry and heartfelt, offering a kind of tongue-in-cheek spiritual audit for a modern age.

title: hybtwibt?
description: The dub techno of the Manchester duo’s latest mixtape attempts to capture the violent energy vibrating through the world at this particular moment in history.

title: Shrines
description: The fourth album from the NY duo composed of Elucid and billy woods is freer, lusher, and brighter than anything they’ve done before.

title: Thank You for Using GTL
description: Recorded in jail over a crackly phone line, Drakeo’s mesmerizing album is a remarkable feat: a stark rebuke of the justice system and an unparalleled achievement for a rapper and his producer.

title: Songs From Northern Torrance
description: The Torrance, California band’s new and allegedly improved rarities collection is the punk record they always wanted to make, and a chance to redefine their legacy for newer listeners.

title: Sleepy For President
description: On his new solo mixtape, the Flatbush rapper spits with the kind of ease and flash that starts block parties.

title: The Prettiest Curse
description: On their third album, the Spanish garage rockers swing for the fences with a big, arena-friendly new sound.

title: Shades of Flu: Healthy Remixes For an Ill Moment
description: With a daring assortment of reverential and playful remixes, the drummer and producer carves a niche for himself in the world of contemporary jazz.

title: All Things Being Equal
description: On his first proper solo album in 30 years, the Spacemen 3 cofounder ruminates on mortality and transcendence over a glowing bed of analog synths.

title: My Heart Is An Open Field
description: The Chicago singer-songwriter’s debut LP appears at first to be fairly straightforward, but it quietly eludes convention and expectation, creating its own hermetic world.

title: Goons Be Gone
description: Fifteen years into their career, the duo are still finding ways to make discord feel utopian.

title: Fantasize Your Ghost
description: The Chicago duo experiments with how many wayward impulses fit inside conventional pop structures on their expansive and thrilling second album.

title: Sideways to New Italy
description: The Melbourne quintet’s second album strolls through familiar territory with good guitar work and good songwriting that never quite peaks where it used to.

title: The Bowie Years
description: A new boxed set documents Iggy Pop’s formative years working alongside David Bowie in Berlin, the moment Pop left the sound of the Stooges behind and came into his own as a lone icon.

title: Wicked City
description: Georgia Ellery and Taylor Skye’s head-spinning vocal processing and unusual fusion of influences form a well of deep feeling, even when the meaning is obscured.

title: In Fabric OST
description: Spanning 35 tracks in nearly two hours, the Stereolab spinoff’s first foray into film soundtracks balances playful electronic mood pieces with drones and nameless dread.

title: My Favorite Mistakes
description: On this covers EP, the country singer digs into the roots in some of her favorite dark love songs, from Sheryl Crow to Nick Lowe to Hank Williams.

title: Welcome to Bobby’s Motel
description: On their debut, the Montreal art-rockers come off like a cootie shot against self-seriousness and boredom.

title: RTJ4
description: On their fourth installment, Killer Mike and El-P are back to tune up the ruling class and the racist police state, this time streamlining the process and settling into their most natural rhythm.

title: Head Above the Water
description: The Irish folk singer’s third album fills out her sound to incorporate elements of jazz, country rock, slowcore, and psychedelia.

title: Flamagra (Instrumentals)
description: The instrumental edition of last year’s cosmic jazz-funk odyssey brings Flying Lotus’ detailed compositions and soundscaping to center stage.

title: Muzz
description: Bringing together members of Interpol, the Walkmen, and Bonny Light Horseman, the indie supergroup’s debut album is a carefully crafted pastoral travelogue.

title: Hit to Hit
description: The Philly indie pop band’s second album keeps things hooky and whimsical across 24 tracks of mostly light fare and dynamic songwriting.

title: The Volume of Things
description: Sarah Howells’ latest project is simple and sweet; its lower stakes fit an album about finding peace of mind amid sensory overload.

title: Alfredo
description: The gruff-voiced rapper and dusty-groove producer are a perfect match as they connect for a seamless ride to the heart of the gangster.

title: Pop Music / False B​-​Sides II
description: Will Wiesenfeld’s second collection of odds and ends revamps old sketches with new lyrics, revealing a deepening interest in pop songcraft.

title: Future Teenage Cave Artists
description: On their 15th album, the indie-rock institution goes apocalyptic with their first concept record.

title: Island
description: With assistance from the London Contemporary Orchestra, the prolific Canadian composer’s arrangements propel dense, elliptical mythologies that unravel like fantasy novels.

title: Pacific Breeze 2: Japanese City Pop, AOR & Boogie 1972-1986
description: Light in the Attic’s latest foray into Japanese easy-listening pop has plenty of summery charm, but it offers few discoveries for those already familiar with the genre.

title: Beginners
description: With the help of Phoebe Bridgers, Conor Oberst, and others, this career collaborator steps into the spotlight with a stunningly empathetic study of human frailties.

title: Contact
description: On his third solo album, the New York drummer sheds his earlier records’ conceptual frameworks, marshaling percussive chaos into increasingly controlled forms.

title: Neon Cross
description: The country singer was “raised on heartache,” but her latest album is a triumphant testament to the way that Wyatt has outpaced her demons.

title: Chromatica
description: With incomparable flair, the pop diva returns to her dance-pop days with a fabulously fun and deeply personal album that is at turns bizarre, theatrical, and ambitious.

title: Ghetto Fabolous
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the New York rapper’s debut that was spun

title: Diplo Presents Thomas Wesley Chapter 1: Snake Oil
description: Trickled down from the success of “Old Town Road” and the meme-level pervasiveness of the yeehaw agenda, the ubiquitous producer’s purported country album suffocates in treacly kitsch.

title: El Androide
description: The rising Dominican star carries dembow into the mainstream on this mammoth double album, sanding down some of the grimy genre’s rough edges in the process.

title: Methods Body
description: The drums-and-electronics duo’s debut album is a gnarled hybrid of free improv, minimalist composition, and dance music that advances in fits and starts.

title: Dedicated Side B
description: With big hooks and breathless romance galore, Carly’s leftovers from last year’s Dedicated show off her range, even when the songs start to lose their spark.

title: EVERYTHING YOU HEARD IS TRUE
description: The rising star’s effortlessly sexy new album offers a startlingly modern take on the R&B coming out of Nigeria.

title: Pantayo
description: The innovative Toronto kulintang ensemble’s debut album is a hybrid of traditional Philippine gongs, electronic production, and Western pop influences.

title: Domesticated
description: The idiosyncratic electro-pop singer-songwriter (and Eurovision contestant) turns his pen to the mundane magic of household chores, but it too often looks like he missed a spot.

title: Wunna
description: The 26-year-old sounds reinvigorated on his latest—the flows are crisper, his puns are more colorful, and the beats are pristine.

title: Cold Water
description: On his latest project, the Brooklyn rapper realizes his vision. His forceful and focused bars are just one aspect of the highly skilled emcee’s community-focused and spiritually rewarding music.

title: Taken Away
description: Following a 2019 episode of police harassment in front of his own building, the Detroit house legend’s latest goes hard on depth and funk, but there’s often an ache where the fun used to be.

title: Introduction, Presence
description: The synth-pop group offers a remarkably assured debut, with 10 pristine pieces that eschew dramatics for concision.

title: NO DREAM
description: New York’s most anxious punk delivers hook after hook on an album that deals with evergreen sociopolitical concerns yet sounds like it could’ve been written 30 minutes ago.

title: Não Fales Nela Que A Mentes
description: The Lisbon batida producer’s second LP is more spacious than her hard-charging debut, but infused with ambivalent emotion; the ghosts of good times seem to hover anxiously in the wings.

title: Survival
description: On her second album as Wares, Cassia Hardy sings of rage, joy, and transformation on a dynamic and euphoric rock record.

title: Strange to Explain
description: The New York psych-folk band makes a welcome return to form with a dreamy, unsettling, Mellotron-filled album that feels especially appropriate right now.

title: Both
description: The experimental guitarist who made his name on collaboration steps into the spotlight with a meditative, ominous solo LP. Each of these eight pieces is like a pitch-black room, easy to enter but tricky to navigate.

title: For You
description: The UK producer arranges classic dance tropes into a roadmap of euphoric self-actualization, creating some of the year’s giddiest, most assured electronic music.

title: The World I’m Going to Hell For
description: The Berlin-based producer swaps his habitually trance-fueled club anthems for an unusual fusion of filmic chamber strings and emotive bass music.

title: Acquiesce
description: The synth compositions of Chicago experimentalist Natalie Chami are deep and romantic, uniquely designed to pull you into them.

title: Elliott Smith
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Elliott Smith’s self-titled solo album, a darkly beautiful record whose spare arrangements conceal worlds.

title: High Off Life
description: The Atlanta icon releases another hour of music rendering tortured hedonism with painterly detail, meticulous production, and melancholy melody.

title: Sheeesh
description: The Australian beatmaker has an ear for silky West Coast sounds, and his debut evokes Roger Troutman, P-funk, and G-funk with wide-eyed sincerity.

title: Runaway Dog
description: Avery Springer and her bandmates grow into a bigger, bolder sound on their second album, pushing beyond obvious hooks and taking new risks with their songwriting.

title: Figures
description: The long-running Belgian avant-garde band explores complicated gender dynamics on their ambitious new double album.

title: Rain Shadow
description: The bass clarinet and synthesizer duo and the Oakland guitarist collaborate on an immersive quartet of tracks that feel like still-life paintings of the same object from slightly different angles.

title: Consummation
description: With virtuosic arrangements and cavernous production flourishes, the Brooklyn songwriter’s second full-length is an ambitious record that miraculously does not feel like it’s taking on too much.

title: Notes on a Conditional Form
description: Matty Healy, the enfant terrible of pop-rock, pushes his band all-in with a long, messy experiment that just so happens to peak with some of their sharpest songs ever.

title: How Do You Feel About Getting Married?
description: Los Angeles singer and songwriter Dijon Duenas’ solo debut takes a polyglot approach, setting his yearning, falsetto-laden vocals against synthy digital textures and folk-inflected guitars.

title: All Visible Objects
description: Richard Melville Hall is back to doing what he does best: making soaring electronic music for billboard-sized emotions. Introspection? Not so much.

title: The Goat
description: The Chicago rapper’s follow-up to his riveting debut LP argues for him as an adaptable and unmissable talent, an unlikely star in a new major-label system.

title: Starz
description: On his new album, the sad-boy pioneer regresses into empty flexing, content to remain stagnant while the rap world passes him by.

title: Hair of the Dog
description: The Philadelphia-based experimental pop musician nails a sunny, carefree vibe somewhere between creepy and sweet.

title: The Mosaic of Transformation
description: Channeling new age spiritualism, the California synthesizer musician’s new album is a tender and warm-hearted offering, well-suited as an ointment for the dullness of life in isolation.

title: All That Glue
description: The British punk-hop duo’s career-spanning collection shows their unlikely ascent from ranting on sidewalks to ranting at Brixton Academy.

title: Atlantico
description: Drawing on the music of his youth, Buenos Aires-born songwriter Juan Zaballa’s second album cleverly illuminates Latin America’s rich musical heritage.

title: how i’m feeling now
description: The British electro pop artist sings of love, loneliness, and solo partying across an album built in and made for this very moment.

title: Beneath
description: Urgent even at its sludgiest tempos, the Fredericksburg, Virginia band’s second album draws on a bleak palette to create illusions of infinite depth and vastness.

title: Becoming (Music From the Netflix Original Documentary)
description: Soundtracking Netflix’s Michelle Obama documentary, the Los Angeles saxophonist trades the sprawl of his albums for a more concise approach, wrapping pop-friendly motifs in big arrangements.

title: Quickies
description: The sharp wit of veteran songwriter Stephin Merritt thrives in brevity across a collection of short songs that range from 12 seconds to an epic two-and-a-half minutes.

title: Every Sun, Every Moon
description: Following an accident that took the life of their tour videographer, the California emo band finds new meaning in old ideas, while J. Robbins’ production nudges them toward newfound confidence.

title: The Quickening
description: The Dirty Three drummer and expansive guitarist collaborate on a freely improvised album that glows with ease.

title: WILL THIS MAKE ME GOOD
description: The Brooklyn musician stretches the boundaries of his psychedelic soul sound, yielding a record that alternates between hypnotic and languorous.

title: Set My Heart on Fire Immediately
description: Mike Hadreas’ fifth album glides between sublime melodies and grimy, guttural dissonance, embracing the joys and burdens of the human body and its innumerable, intangible yearnings.

title: Dare
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the high-art synth-pop of the Human League’s Dare, a prismatic album that all pop music would soon pass through.

title: LAS QUE NO IBAN A SALIR
description: With most tracks pulled from the cutting room floor of the *YHLQMDLG* sessions, Bad Bunny shows he’s in full command of his music, even when it’s a little rough around the edges.

title: Nehruvia: My Disregarded Thoughts
description: The New York rapper attempts to be all things to all people, but in his efforts to split the difference between bar god and pop rapper, he ends up proving he is neither.

title: Sorceress
description: The Texas singer-songwriter’s fourth album sounds older and wiser, casting her mystical interests as a foil to the bittersweet, ordinary moments that add up to earthly life.

title: Josey in Space
description: Connecting disparate styles, eras, and moods, the London DJ’s mix tells a story of black dance music from both sides of the Atlantic, an ongoing dialogue that transcends genres and borders.

title: State Of Emergency
description: Across a mostly fun, guest-filled 22 minutes, the young New York rapper does what needs to be done and puts on for his city.

title: græ
description: The sprawling second album from the crystal-voiced singer-songwriter is a riot of moods. Moses Sumney widens the scope of his work and takes full account of his self, warts and all.

title: One and Only
description: The boisterous rapper’s latest is mellower and more muted than its predecessor, breaking from the maximalist bluster of conventional Brooklyn drill.

title: ORCORARA 2010
description: Dedicated to an incarcerated man who spent years fighting wildfires in California’s Sierra Nevada, Crampton’s latest album confronts the systems of oppression hidden in plain sight.

title: Reunions
description: The alt-country singer-songwriter’s new album moves steadily and carefully, lingering on the conflicted emotions of his finely-etched tales and the band’s textured, elegant understatement.

title: Just Cause Y’all Waited 2
description: On his latest sorrowful dispatch, the drill veteran walks the line between reporter and preacher, gangster and citizen.

title: Good Intentions
description: Rap’s perennial kid brother makes his best album yet—adjusting for expectations.

title: III
description: Producer Joel Shanahan expands his palette, mingling shades of ’90s ambient techno with distant echoes of the Cocteau Twins. Even at the record’s mellowest, muted rhythms knock like a racing heart.

title: Slime&B
description: Rap’s trickster god and R&B’s least tolerable person collaborate on a mixtape with no discernible upside.

title: Descendants of Cain
description: The Brooklyn rapper moves carefully between knotty verses and blunt lines to make some of the most immersive and exhilarating songs of his career.

title: Drop 6 EP
description: Stuck at home on lockdown, the London rapper returns to her long-running mixtape series with a gloomy, affecting meditation on self-reliance that feels as claustrophobic as a one-room apartment.

title: Regresa
description: The Puerto Rican duo moved back to the island in the wake of Hurricane Maria, and their joyful and melancholic new album takes stock of their changed home.

title: Shadow Talk
description: The Chicago band’s third album brings wiry new energy to their fuzzed-out rock songs. The individual pieces are all a notch stronger, but their sum is a ton stronger.

title: What’s New Tomboy?
description: Channeling stripped-back pop songs into hushed folk arrangements, the Seattle singer-songwriter’s 15th album confronts life’s impermanence in terms tender yet unsentimental.

title: Petals for Armor
description: The Paramore singer’s debut solo album is emotionally vulnerable and musically ambitious, one that seeks catharsis and enlightenment in tangled corners of pop music.

title: Music for 18 Musicians
description: Eighteen musicians? In this economy? The Michigan post-minimalist recasts Steve Reich’s landmark composition as a solo project with a sleek, dark-hued electronic palette.

title: It Was Good Until It Wasn’t
description: The cloudy grooves of the Oakland singer’s second full-length album showcase both her voice and her clear-eyed approach. These are love songs about all the forces that make and break romance.

title: Yeo​-​Neun
description: Accompanied by bass, piano, and harp, the New York cellist refracts traditional Korean influences though an avant-garde lens, yielding an album as surprising as it is elegant.

title: They Call Me Disco EP
description: The Chicago rapper’s collaborative EP with the L.A. producer Terrace Martin is a jubilant six-song burst of summertime grooves and throwback funk.

title: Attica Blues
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the landmark 1972 album from the legendary saxophonist, responding loudly and passionately to the tragic outcome of a prison uprising.

title: Forever
description: Denver slowcore artist Madeline Johnston’s memorial to a late friend is full of barren dream-pop and hypnotic, nearly wordless ruminations on the pain of loss.

title: Beyond Bulletproof
description: The Sacramento rapper’s new release doesn’t compromise on his bleak worldview, but the music feels warmer and more accessible.

title: Apparition EP
description: On his new three-song EP, the Baltimore artist uses his sinuous, stunning voice to navigate a dark night of the soul.

title: Huellas Entreveradas
description: The Argentinian electro-acoustic composer has been exploring hidden worlds of sound since the 1960s; these three pieces, all from the 21st century, showcase her playful side.

title: Mutable Set
description: On his fourth album, the expert producer comes into his own as a solo artist with a hushed, finely tuned album that showcases his unassuming voice and impeccable songcraft.

title: Rainbow Bridge
description: On her third LP for Hausu Mountain, the Chicago experimental musician amps up the extremes of her work: It’s more crushing than ever, yet it features moments as tranquil as anything in her catalog.

title: Eastern Flowers
description: On his debut, this Swedish artist submerges psych-rock instrumentals into one low, bubbling groove.

title: Old Blues
description: The Boston lo-fi songwriter’s latest project is a poetic and intensely personal rumination on selfishness, self-loathing, and self-forgiveness.

title: Invisible People
description: The eclectic, party-starting Southern California band make their most accessible record, with big hooks matching definitive statements.

title: Roundelay
description: On their ninth album, the Pacific Northwest mainstays push past their folksy twee inclinations towards the avant experimentations of early Stereolab.

title: Pure X
description: The Austin band’s druggy, wall-of-sound escapism put them on the map, but their first album in six years sounds more confident without it.

title: HiRUDiN
description: Katie Stelmanis’ fourth album swings for big, embodied pop moments without shying from the strangeness and discordance that’s animated the project since the beginning.

title: Instrumental Relics
description: This collection gathers the cloud-rap pioneer’s earliest and most seminal recordings, in danger of being lost to the digital ether.

title: 800 B.C.
description: Coasting on the success of last year’s “Big Drip”—which finds new relevance now that the phrase “demon time” is trending—the Brooklyn drill rapper shows personality but lacks focus.

title: Sogni
description: The Melbourne quartet’s catchy, plainspoken post-punk songs speak to the drudgery of life under capitalism, marrying poetics and politics without an ounce of pretension.

title: The Mother Stone
description: The film actor’s musical debut is full of shadowy theatrics and cryptic gibberish. Rarely do you encounter music this bombastic and unreasonable.

title: Dark Lane Demo Tapes
description: Drake’s new project is a mixtape of glossy “demos” from the recent past. It showcases his precise delivery, sticky flows, and arena-sized hooks, but comes with a fair amount of well-tread material.

title: Frozen
description: Slipping between stark realism and meditative reflection, this is the South London experimental musician’s most intensely introspective album yet.

title: Quiet Bloom
description: Created in a period of grieving, Danish electronic composer Villads Klint’s second album mimics the messiness of feelings in flux, pairing everyday sounds with hints of trance and Baroque.

title: Harkin
description: After a few years as an indie-rock hired gun, the former Sky Larkin singer assumes center stage on her solo debut, chronicling the push-and-pull between blurry days and electric evenings.

title: Chaotic Good
description: The Oregon-based singer-songwriter's taut fifth album channels the wounded spirit of Elliott Smith.

title: Oh Yeah? / Brave Rats EP
description: With a joyous new album, the New York jazz-punk quartet responds loudly and triumphantly to existential terror. Its follow-up EP lets their true feelings show.

title: Shall We Go On Sinning So That Grace May Increase?
description: Matmos member Drew Daniel has put together a gorgeous album that carries itself with the strength of a soft prayer, masterfully fusing jazz, deep house, and minimalism into an enormous, featherlight shield.

title: Mellow Gold
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Beck’s ramshackle 1994 album, a quintessential piece of alternative rock, experimental folk, and hip-hop that felt magically displaced in time.

title: Roaches 2012-2019
description: The singular experimentalist’s first official solo compilation traverses the universes that make up his discography, rejecting genre and attribution in an album-length argument for mongrel pop.

title: Midnight Moods
description: This south London rapper and King Krule associate evokes the carefree heyday of ’90s UK garage.

title: ALPHABETLAND
description: On their first new album featuring all four original members since 1985, the Los Angeles punk icons return to the sound of their heyday on a highly formidable comeback.

title: Making a Door Less Open
description: On his odd and ambitious new album, singer-songwriter Will Toledo dons a gas mask, adds electronic textures, and tries to separate himself from the indie fame of Car Seat Headrest.

title: Cape Cira
description: The British producer’s bubbly, refreshing latest record is a celebration writ small, music for a barnburner in a dollhouse.

title: Modern Bliss
description: Playing spacey techno sounds off breakbeats and inventive percussion, the Australian producer’s debut album has a psychedelic undercurrent that’s more Burning Man than Berghain.

title: Ache of Victory EP
description: On her promising debut EP, the New York singer-songwriter searches for ideal settings for her stunning, intimate voice.

title: farawayfromeveryoneyouknow
description: With garbled singing, shuffling electronics, and fragments of conversation, the Brooklyn band’s new album dwells on ordinary and universal moments of alienation.

title: Pain Mop Girl 2020
description: In the wake of Main Pop Girl 2019, Jaime Brooks delivers a patchwork of dense, often cartoonish reimaginings of those songs, exploring pop’s fluidity with a deft, funny, and heartfelt touch.

title: Thug Luv
description: On the followup to his explosive major-label debut Edgewood, the Atlanta rapper tries to show us his heart but trips over his own painfully limited writing.

title: Paradise Gardens
description: Canadian songwriter Crystal Dorval melts away the haze of dream pop for her most clear-eyed and expansive music to date.

title: Sie7etr3 EP
description: The Bronx-based Dominican crew offer a more lighthearted take on the drill sound with their debut EP.

title: Shadows in Blue
description: Nestling heavy-hitting cuts inside a protective ambient cushion, the Bristol producer’s debut builds on his dancefloor sensibilities while making good on his experimental tendencies.

title: Scacco Matto
description: The Italian electronic producer and arch conceptualist finds a new flamboyance in astoundingly ornate, song-like pieces of deconstructed trance and video-game chirps.

title: 38 Baby 2
description: The Louisiana rapper’s latest is typically blunt, anguished, and unsettling.

title: Good Souls Better Angels
description: Drawing as much from punk as roadhouse blues, Lucinda Williams’ loud and unsparing new album is some of the heaviest, most inspiring music of her career.

title: Thousand Year Stare
description: The Bristol native, now a London resident, maps the links between the two cities’ dance-music traditions in a four-track EP that infuses club energy with headphone-friendly nuance.

title: Selbstportrait Wahre Liebe
description: Returning to the series of instrumental self-portraits he began in 1979, the German experimental rock pioneer, now 86, sounds reflective and at times melancholy, braiding peacefulness and pain.

title: What Kinda Music
description: The second album from Tom Misch, the London-based musician and producer, is an expansive and fruitful collaboration with drummer Yussef Dayes, one that brings out the best in each other.

title: Flowers on the Weekend
description: Welcome to the frat-rap perpetrator’s wokeness parade.

title: My Garden
description: The Los Angeles pianist, a collaborator of Solange and Frank Ocean, sinks back into spare soul-jazz and meditative new age, occupying a middle ground between deep and easy listening.

title: Agitprop Alterna
description: Bearing a distinct resemblance to My Bloody Valentine, the Brooklyn shoegaze band’s second album is a patchwork of brainy indie-pop influences with its own absurdist charm.

title: BLQLYTE
description: The enigmatic Los Angeles rapper-producer's latest is a journey of discovery within a world of shadows, and his best and most stimulating music yet.

title: Skylarking
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the masterful chamber-pop of XTC’s 1986 album Skylarking and the fraught story behind the bucolic songs.

title: ChangesNowBowie
description: This set of cozy, stripped-back rehearsal recordings, later broadcast in a 1997 special, finds Bowie in a valedictory mood.

title: Antarctica
description: Even with help from Ty Segall and Steve Albini, the Los Angeles garage-rock trio’s second album reaches for a grand analogy its cookie-cutter post-punk can’t support.

title: SXTP4
description: Terius Nash digs into his songwriting vault for a leisurely stroll through his single favorite subject.

title: Peaceful as Hell
description: The Canadian noise-pop duo’s music conjures a psychotic slumber party, or a Second Life rave, but remains grounded in the bittersweet beauty of lifelong friendship.

title: Innocent Country 2
description: The bohemian Detroit rapper’s latest collaboration with producer Chris Keys feels as blissful as a beer buzz on a hot summer afternoon.

title: Oneiric Formulary
description: The acclaimed solo guitarist sets aside his beloved instrument for nearly half the tracks on his new album, seeking new routes to convey familiar moods.

title: Cinema
description: The North Carolina singer-songwriter has a voice that attracts metaphors about hypnotism. Her second album reveals a subtle, complex staging of femininity that resists easy resolutions.

title: Fear of Music
description: Today on Pitchfork, we are taking a critical look at Talking Heads with new reviews of five albums that chart their journey from New York art punks to a voracious and spectacular pop group.

title: Little Creatures
description: Talking Heads’ most approachable album embraced love, family, and pop music, celebrating the same simple joys they’d once approached with a sense of fear and alienation.

title: More Songs About Buildings and Food
description: Talking Heads’ second album expanded their sound and took them to the dancefloor, marking the beginning of their career-defining collaborations with Brian Eno.

title: Speaking in Tongues
description: Talking Heads’ fifth album is an inky passport of sounds—art-rock, funk, pop, Afrobeat—meticulously mapped for the collective yet informed by the movements of the individuals.

title: Talking Heads: 77
description: On their debut, the art-punk legends had already arrived at the tunefully agitated sound they’d carry through their career, but weren’t yet attempting to craft a major statement.

title: Duality
description: Seven years after his breakout hit, the UK house producer’s debut album aims to bridge generation-defining dance sounds with more emotive electronic fare, but mostly struggles to find its way.

title: A Muse in Her Feelings
description: After two albums of insular restraint, the elegant R&B duo takes an expansive turn, embracing club sounds and multiple guest stars.

title: Forever, Ya Girl
description: The Chicago-bred singer and producer’s homegrown R&B meditates on hurt, longing, and self-protection, embracing the kind of resolute realness that can only happen outside the major label gaze.

title: Ajai
description: The absurdly detailed new album from the Chicago rapper delves into the compulsions of its titular sneakerhead character over rich production from Kenny Segal.

title: Blame It on Baby
description: The North Carolina rapper’s third album in 13 months is stacked with the same regurgitated phrases and flows from earlier projects. This time, they’re starting to go stale.

title: Earth
description: Unlike his bandmates’ forays in electronica or contemporary classical, Radiohead guitarist Ed O’Brien’s solo debut looks fondly back at the kind of British rock his own group abandoned.

title: Different EP
description: The Ghanaian producer and DJ’s debut surveys contemporary African electronic music, uniting a breadth of influences and guest vocalists in a shadowy, clubby musical world.

title: Pray for Paris
description: The Buffalo rapper continues his unlikely ascent into hip-hop stardom with an album of feverish excess and the best raps of his career.

title: SAWAYAMA
description: The Japanese-British pop singer’s debut is a Y2K flashback that’s as reverent of Evanescence and Korn as it is of Britney and Christina.

title: The Don of Diamond Dreams
description: Ishmael Butler, the MC of the futurist hip-hop duo, looks in a new direction for inspiration on his latest project: his own son, emo rapper Lil Tracy.

title: Viewing
description: The Brooklyn band’s debut is one of the most confidently executed emo debuts of recent vintage, a bracing fusion of brutality and elegance.

title: Knuckleball Express
description: With the Royal Trux once again in his rearview mirror, Neil Hagerty returns to his own group. In place of the genre mashups of 2013’s Best Of, he’s back to making satisfyingly ragged rock’n’roll.

title: Born To Do It
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Craig David’s debut, a UK garage hit parade which became a poisoned chalice for its creator.

title: Safe (Exits)
description: The New York-based electronic musician tries his hand at collage in an appealingly loose, rangy record that's ideally suited to his magpie tendencies.

title: Miss Colombia
description: The Colombian and Canadian musician’s second album is a symbolic reclamation of her crown. On one level, she’s recollecting intimate relationships; on another, she’s calling entire countries to task.

title: In Another Life
description: On his first release in five years and his major-label debut, Pat Grossi offers his cinematic anthems as a sort of spiritual balm.

title: Garden of Lucid
description: The 19-year-old singer’s debut exudes confidence and experience. Her style of R&B is mystical and moody, lavishing in wonky, washed-out guitar, sticky basslines, and fuzzy background vocals.

title: Varispeed Hydra
description: The Los Angeles musician, formerly of Barn Owl, fuses synthesizers and processed guitar into ominous, inky atmospheres that bridge experimental music and ambient dub.

title: Fetch the Bolt Cutters
description: Fiona Apple’s fifth record is unbound, a wild symphony of the everyday, an unyielding masterpiece. No music has ever sounded quite like it.

title: Exeter
description: The enigmatic Swedish rapper strips back his hypnotic music until it’s nothing but AutoTuned crooning and chanted slogans.

title: Born Again
description: The Canadian songwriter’s full-length debut is sentimental and melancholy, allowing even songs with ambiguous, conflicted meanings to be subsumed into echoey haze.

title: Songs for Pierre Chuvin
description: Recording on the same boombox that launched his career, John Darnielle returns to his lo-fi roots for an album of alienation, ancient pagans, and making it through the year together.

title: Songs from The Golden One
description: The comedian and musician's breakthrough HBO special is full of songs about familial trauma that work just as well in an album format.

title: Growth & Development
description: 22Gz attempts to chase a hit on a melodic but stale mixtape that struggles to keep up with the drill scene the Brooklyn rapper helped originate.

title: Perception is/as/of Deception
description: On their eighth album, the married duo spout off defiant one-liners over prickly basslines and noise spirals, sounding as dry and self-aware as ever.

title: Ever-Roving Eye
description: On the follow-up to his 2017 debut, the Chicago guitarist ventures beyond his folk roots, sounding looser and freer than ever. Despite the solo billing, he sounds more like a bandleader here.

title: Negro
description: The rapper’s second full-length is intense and riotous, tapping into the anger at the heart of Black America for an eclectic and captivating record.

title: Ritorno
description: This is the Italian electronic producer’s debut album for Munich’s Ilian Tape label; for a record coming out of post-industrial Turin, its aesthetic is surprisingly luminous.

title: Mas Amable
description: The smooth and hypnotic tracks on the Queens-based producer’s new album share a single tempo and palette—part tropical strut, part moonwalk.

title: The Loves of Your Life
description: The former Walkmen member wrote each of these songs about a specific person, forming an archive of memories that comes alive in his elevated songcraft and dynamic voice.

title: Lost in the Country
description: On his solo breakthrough, the former LVL UP singer comes to terms with hard times by fully embracing the indie rock he loves.

title: Annual Flowers In Color
description: Originally released as a limited-run cassette, this collection of synth pieces from the former Emeralds member is a staggeringly beautiful career highlight.

title: Jacqueline
description: Circuit Des Yeux’s Haley Fohr recasts her alter ego as a long-haul trucker against ambitious, synthetic soundscapes that evoke the near-spiritual loneliness of the solo traveler.

title: Migration Stories
description: The dusty twang of M. Ward’s guitar and his whispered singing paint a picture of souls in transition, hinting at the reasons people choose to leave their country for another.

title: Live in Paris (1975)
description: Pharoah Sanders’ group rolled up all the best qualities from his early-1970s LPs into a newly reissued set that bursts with joy and discovery. It’s a set that sounds more like a party than a seance.

title: Shine
description: In its day, this 2007 album felt like a response to turbulent times. Revisiting the newly reissued LP, its songs feel untethered to any political moment: protest songs delivered as solemn premonitions.

title: Song for Our Daughter
description: The starkly beautiful seventh album from the venerable singer-songwriter reveals more of her aged wisdom through winding narratives rich with humor and despair.

title: Rock Sutra
description: One of the best access points to Cameron Stallones’ eclectic discography, Rock Sutra imagines his act as a band playing together, reacting to the instincts of its members in real time.

title: Friday Forever
description: XL founder Richard Russell’s collaborative project brings out an unfiltered, unrehearsed freshness in its guests that the album can’t quite manage for itself.

title: Self Hate Wraith
description: The Baltimore rapper-producer’s sprawling project seesaws across genres, from emo rap to drum’n’bass to indie rock, with mad-scientist abandon.

title: T.V. Sun
description: New York psych rocker Ryan Jewell channels the subterranean sounds of the ’70s—kosmische, prog folk, space rock—into infectious, wildly inventive songs.

title: The New Abnormal
description: The NYC band’s first album in seven years is sluggish and slight, rendering their signature sound as background music.

title: Fodder on My Wings
description: Long considered an outlier in her catalog, Nina Simone’s newly reissued 1982 album is an intimate and immense portrait, a culmination of Nina Simone’s frustrations molded into a jarring personal statement.

title: BRAT
description: The Chicago singer and multi-instrumentalist leaps fearlessly between voices and sounds. His constant dissatisfaction leaves no question that his true colors are loud and clashing.

title: Sigma Oasis
description: Phish’s instinctive new studio album is a pleasant surprise, a small joy, and an unlikely course correction.

title: Southside
description: The Nashville star blends genres with charm and style on his first new album in five years, a marker of what modern commercial country can do at its heights.

title: Hot and Flustered
description: The Perth punks are more interested in recording immediate, energetic punk rock than becoming experimentalists, and they’ve certainly nailed the former.

title: I’m Your Empress Of
description: Lorely Rodriguez’s third album, largely written and produced alone, refocuses her voice into an emotionally and aesthetically rich album of heartbreak, family history, and pop delights.
The L.A. producer’s music is a fog of samples and clips warped into peculiar shapes that defy recognition but prickle with familiarity, like memories from a past life.

title: Pray 4 Love
description: Even as the Floridian crooner becomes a breakout star, his music remains bleak and filled with pain.

title: If You’re Dreaming
description: The Detroit singer-songwriter’s second album is sparser, lonelier, and more patient, allowing the candor of her lyrics to shine through.

title: Window In
description: The Chicago guitarist and sound artist tucks worlds of deep feelings into these four immersive pieces, which seem to shift with your own mood.

title: It Is What It Is
description: Three years after his 2017 opus Drunk, Stephen Bruner returns with more fleet-fingered jams and abstracted musings, this time a little more unpolished.

title: I Feel Alive
description: At their best, this Montreal quartet locate the aching sincerity in pop clichés.

title: Second Language
description: Angus Finlayson’s first LP is shot through with concussive kicks, writhing basslines, and finely tooled drum work. But even at their most powerful, these songs are remarkably nimble.

title: WOMB
description: The electro-pop duo’s first album in five years muses on bodies, blood, and a girl’s coming of age; it benefits from the group’s newfound musical maturity and more exacting editorial eye.
The London band’s deeply self-aware debut is worthy of being taken seriously even when it’s not serious.

title: What We Drew
description: Yaeji’s first full-length mixtape is a subtle, more insular turn for the producer. It plays like a self-issued challenge to strip away the fluorescence, to find what’s underneath pop catharsis.

title: Head Hunters
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Herbie Hancock’s jazz-funk masterpiece, a celebration of all that is modern and ancient.

title: In Bank We Trust
description: A posthumous album showcases the late Atlanta rapper’s head-spinning dexterity without attempting anything more than that, both grounded and limited by its avoidance of the usual pomp.

title: You’ll Be Fine
description: The second album from the Michigan emo band feels like a product of another era: itching to cross over, but without anywhere to cross over to.

title: Paris Hilton
description: The celebrity socialite’s alluringly empty 2006 debut gets a vinyl reissue. It’s a concept album whose concept is: What if Paris Hilton made an album?

title: New Me, Same Us
description: The Swedish electro-pop group’s first album for Ninja Tune is a welcome departure, finally infusing their own studio work with the creative energy of their collaborative sessions.

title: PITH
description: The Chicago band’s second album strikes a balance between the spartan chaos of noise rock and the soft melodicism of bedroom pop.

title: Three
description: More than 30 years into their career, the Australian experimental trio can still make the mundane feel miraculous.

title: Heaven to a Tortured Mind
description: The iconoclastic artist moves to a plush and magisterial kind of rock music for a gratifying and intense record, one whose pleasures are viscerally immediate.

title: Forever Just Beyond
description: This comeback album, assisted by Scott Avett, feels both charmingly at ease and refreshingly ambitious, grappling with life’s big questions over understated, easygoing production.

title: Yene Mircha
description: The Ethiopian cult musician returns with a collaborative full-band exploration that is no less hypnotic than his celebrated earlier work.

title: Before Love Came to Kill Us
description: The powerhouse singer’s voice is chameleonic and present in every guise. Her debut is most satisfying not because she whizzes across multiple genres, but because of the skill she displays at each.

title: PARTYMOBILE
description: The Toronto singer’s writing lacks the specificity that animates his best music this time around.

title: The Caretaker
description: Synth-pop auteur Nandi Rose renders a nuanced, deeply compelling portrait of a woman turning away from the world just when she needs help the most.

title: Snapshot of a Beginner
description: Gathering newfound lyrical confidence, the Halifax slack-rockers trade the sparseness of their early material for gentle guitar chords and gleaming Mellotron harmonies.

title: Ghosts V: Together / Ghosts VI: Locusts
description: Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross strike a tone similar to their soundtrack work, alternating between hope and dread in sprawling ambient meditations released in response to the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Love Is An Art
description: On her sixth studio album, the former TRL star writes and sings with worldly wisdom and plaintive abandon.

title: Walking Proof
description: On her fourth album, the Nashville singer-songwriter moves beyond the unadorned Americana of previous albums to arrive at new sounds, moods, and emotions.

title: Devotion
description: Without the self-assurance of her debut, the New York songwriter’s second full-length is an album in search of an identity.

title: Cenizas
description: The Chilean American producer’s latest album is his most probing and existential, taking influences from all over his career and placing them into grim atmospheres that slip in and out of reality.

title: Abolition of the Royal Familia
description: Alex Paterson and his band of merry pranksters pay tribute to the golden age of ambient house with subtlety, occasional silliness, and a slyly subversive edge.

title: Far Enough
description: The Australian punk trio, birthed out of Melbourne’s feminist punk scene, are at their best channeling their political rage into small moments

title: Hold Space For Me
description: The Philadelphia R&B singer’s stark, lightly poetic songs splay out the intimacies and contradictions of her raw emotions.

title: Aporia
description: Eleven years after Music for Insomnia, Stevens and his stepfather reunite on a collection of warm, improvisatory synth-wave epics; intimate and unvarnished, they double as a testament to the power of found family.

title: Allegiance and Conviction
description: Turning their atmospheric soft focus on everyday life, this is as close as the Detroit dream-pop duo has come to making a pop record; it’s an ideal entry point into their sprawling catalog.

title: Return to the 36 Chambers: The Dirty Version
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit ODB’s debut classic, a masterclass in winging it.

title: Gigaton
description: Eleven albums in, a band that has become an industry unto itself attempts an artistic rejuvenation that still seems out of reach.

title: City on My Back
description: After a year flooding the internet, this Michigan rapper collects 15 of his colorful and brutal raps, which split the difference between deadpan and dead serious.

title: We Are Sent Here by History
description: The British-Barbadian jazz saxophonist and his South African players narrate the apocalypse from a distant future, suggesting that in order to build anew, some things will first need to burn.

title: Illusion of Time
description: On their full-length debut together, the UK techno producer and the Italian synth guru conjure a mood of pulsing electronic grandeur.

title: Future Nostalgia
description: The ascendant singer’s star-making second album is a collection of sophisticated, hard-bodied pop-funk that gives way to slick, Kylie Minogue-inspired disco.

title: Colores
description: Already a global star, reggaetón’s reigning hitmaker tries his hand at becoming an auteur with an audiovisual album.

title: Saint Cloud
description: With a shift in tone and tempo, Katie Crutchfield creates a vivid modern classic of folk and Americana. It’s the sound of a cherished songwriter thawing out under the sun.

title: Let It All In
description: The long-running Baltimore folk-rock band has never sounded so at ease, or so electrifying.
Donald Glover’s got big hooks and big ideas, but his spiritual largesse is weighed down by impulses carried halfway to their endpoints and moments of frustrating pretense.

title: Empty Country
description: Former Cymbals Eat Guitars frontman Joseph D’Agostino’s solo debut is rangier and more intimate than his former band, but taps similar wells of grief and pain.

title: Through Water
description: The UK singer refines her sound into something moody and aquatic, trading a narrowly escaped adult-contemporary fate for narcotic electronic pop with ASMR undertones.

title: Who Sent You?
description: Led by the poet and musician Moor Mother, the jazz ensemble evokes our American topography, both physically and psychologically, by capturing what’s in the news and what’s underneath that surface.

title: It’s Just Like All the Clouds EP
description: The Brooklyn musician, a member of Palberta and the duo Lily and Horn Horse, crafts whimsical, minimalist indie pop with a slippery lyrical sensibility.

title: Fountain
description: On her debut album, the American musician works entirely with recordings of her own voice, processing and layering largely non-verbal sounds to explore the very fiber of her being.

title: I Am Not a Dog On a Chain
description: Mildly captivating, occasionally repetitive, and frequently ridiculous, the 13th studio album from the fabulous sulk turned red-pill pharmacist is Moz’s vision of radical truth-telling.

title: Lapse in Passage
description: The Chicago duo makes slow and wide-open instrumental music for drums and pedal steel guitar, creating its own lane and rarely straying from it.

title: After Hours
description: Abel Tesfaye finally delivers on his long-running vision, leveraging a self-loathing villain into an irresistible, cinematic narrative with his most satisfying collision of new wave, dream pop, and R&B.

title: Rejoice
description: Two years after the South African trumpeter’s death, this 2010 studio session with the legendary Nigerian drummer documents their unique fusion of Afrobeat and jazz.

title: RIVEN
description: The Discwoman co-founder’s keen understanding of space and dynamics makes just a few overlapping rhythms and melodies feel unexpectedly expansive.

title: Birthmarks
description: The Irish singer and composer’s second album of intimate, experimental folk is at its best when it is quiet and tempered.

title: Vernal Equinox
description: The trumpeter and composer’s 1977 solo debut, reissued on remastered vinyl, retains its uncanny narcotic power and elemental beauty decades on.

title: Let’s Call It A Day
description: The pieces on this reissued 2006 album blend techno’s forward motion with the swirl of ambient.

title: LESS IS MOOR
description: Eight years after “Ima Read,” the club rapper’s debut album channels the ferocity of that breakout single across a maelstrom of different styles while keeping his central shit-talking identity intact.

title: Funky Kingston
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Toots and the Maytals’ 1975 classic, which captured the country soul of roots reggae at its creative peak.

title: Calypso
description: Inspired by the tranquility of the Greek island of Gavdos, the Italian ambient musician luxuriates in leisurely synth passages and gentle piano melodies.

title: Music for Detuned Pianos
description: The British composer works with multiple detuned pianos on this hauntingly elegant record of dreamlike miniatures.

title: Oasis Nocturno
description: Producer Jennifer Lee’s latest album is darker and more introspective, but the innovative beats frequently take a back seat to her guest vocalists’ voices and personalities.

title: LUV vs. The World 2
description: The Philly rapper’s Eternal Atake victory lap feels like a collection of outtakes, but the high points are thrilling.

title: A Little Rhythm and a Wicked Feeling EP
description: Citing Gwen Stefani and Grimes as influences, the L.A. duo’s heartfelt take on bubblegum is a sensitive sort of bombastic pop that wants you to be sensitive, too.

title: Heartbreak Weather
description: For his catchy but charmless second solo album, the pop singer offers a loose-concept record that explores every angle of a breakup through the most pitiful of conversation starters: the weather.

title: Mixing Colours
description: The ambient icon and his younger brother, a well-known pianist in his own right, reveal the results of an intimate musical conversation stretching back 15 years.

title: Heaven or Hell
description: The melodic Texas rapper attempts to step out of Travis Scott's shadow with a debut that mimics Scott at every turn.

title: Rainbow Doll
description: The New Jersey producer’s third album is the first to extensively feature his own voice, which sounds nothing like the buttery crooning that often populates house music.

title: Ricky Music
description: On his latest record, Aaron Maine explores the feelings of confusion and numbness that follow the end of a relationship. It’s an ambitious record that can get a little lost in itself.

title: Sister
description: The second album from producer Nigel Godrich, drummer Joey Waronker, and singer Laura Bettinson is immaculately composed electronica that never really leaves a strong impression.

title: Put the Shine On
description: The Casady sisters’ first album in five years marks a return to their maximalist tendencies, piling on drum machines, chintzy synthesizers, over-the-top raps, and nu-metal guitars.

title: Sixteen Oceans
description: Kieran Hebden’s latest album of club-ready barnstormers and downbeat daydreams feels like a companion to 2017’s New Energy.

title: Origens Da Luz
description: Following Music From Memory’s Outro Tempo, a collection of Brazilian obscurities, the label turns the spotlight on a forgotten composer who fused cello and guitar with the sounds of the rainforest.

title: Truth or Consequences
description: The New Zealand band’s best songs are what one might call picnic disco: lazy in the best way, like stretching out under a hot sun with only the occasional drum loop to gently poke you awake.

title: Underneath
description: At the edge of crossover success, the hardcore stalwarts sputter out with an overstuffed album of weak modern-rock imitations.

title: A Written Testimony
description: After years of waiting and mounting hype, Jay Electronica’s fantastic debut is a mystical, distinctive work that nearly lives up to all the lore surrounding the rapper.

title: Satin Doll
description: On his Nonesuch debut, the innovative saxophonist reinvents jazz standards with a psychedelic hip-hop touch.

title: Sorry You Couldn’t Make It
description: Billed as a country album, the latest LP from the idiosyncratic soul artist born Jerry Williams Jr. examines grief from a distance, taking time to savor life’s little sweetnesses.

title: Hunted
description: The singer-songwriter revisits highlights from her magnetic 2018 LP with the help of guests like Charlotte Gainsbourg, Courtney Barnett, and Julia Holter.

title: Melee
description: The thrilling debut from the Michigan rock band burns hot and bright. It’s a record that’s as melodic as it is physical, where pent-up aggression turns into physical liberation.

title: Kiss My Super Bowl Ring
description: Fusing ’80s-inspired hardcore with playful electronics, the Shears brothers’ bass-and-drums duo enlists a handful of high-profile collaborators in their mission for “total freedom of expression.”

title: Music From First Cow
description: Guitarist William Tyler crafts a spare and meditative soundtrack for filmmaker Kelly Reichardt's quiet frontier story.

title: Tragic Kingdom
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit No Doubt’s 1995 record, an icon of the ska revival and the auspicious beginning of Gwen Stefani’s pop stardom.

title: Free Drakeo
description: The West Coast rapper’s first release since his incarceration is profile-raising look at his rise to folk hero status, culled mostly from scattered loosies released online from 2016 to 2018.

title: The Common Task
description: Horse Lords songs are intricate, methodical patterns that seem to pulse and shift the longer you stare. Their tension is rooted in anticipation, the only relief the relinquishing of control.

title: La Vita Nuova
description: The former Lone Justice singer’s history is the stuff of great rock memoirs, but on her first album in 13 years she looks ahead, celebrating her new life as an out queer woman.

title: the One EP
description: The classically trained 19-year-old musician stands out less for her bars than for intricate melodies and lush soundscapes that push the boundaries of popular rap and R&B.

title: It’s Easy to Feel Like a Nobody When You’re Living in The City
description: The revered and ridiculed DIY legend makes a brisk power-pop record about loving what you do but hating the toll it takes.

title: Every Bad
description: The second album from the Brighton four-piece is the sound of a band mercilessly digging into itself with a stunning, dynamic performance from singer-songwriter Dana Margolin.

title: Purple Moonlight Pages
description: R.A.P. Ferreira (formerly milo) makes his most free-spirited project yet, rapping gleefully over lively and wayward production.

title: Youth Pastoral
description: With his vulnerable, keening voice as the primary emotional vessel, the New York-based songwriter reckons with his break from evangelical Christianity.

title: CHILOMBO
description: Where her last album explored grief, the R&B singer’s latest is more grounded, exploring the ups and downs of a failed relationship.

title: Silver Landings
description: The former teen-pop star’s rueful new album explores who you become when the life around you falls apart and you have to build a new one from the ruins of the last.

title: The Long Goodbye
description: While walking a tightrope across a daring concept album, rapper Riz Ahmed offers compelling, unapologetic account of what it truly feels like to be brown and British in 2020.

title: ~how i’m feeling~
description: Pop singer Ari Leff advocates powerfully for being forthright about your feelings, but his album’s whopping 21-song tracklist is underwhelming and repetitive.

title: Wave Pack
description: This 26-song compilation surveys the brief period, between 2007 and 2009, when the Harlem rapper remolded rap in his wavy image.

title: Suga
description: The relatively short project from the Houston rapper reasserts her absolute domination on the mic and takes her to new melodic spaces to mixed effect.

title: Ceremony
description: The duo foreground their most conventional pop sounds on their fourth album, but remain at their best at their strangest.

title: Eternal Atake
description: The Philly rapper has evolved into an untouchable pop artist in sound and style. With deliriously good rapping and immaculate production, Uzi makes an event album live up to its name.

title: U-Void Synthesizer
description: Relentlessly smashing together bits of punk, grindcore, rave, industrial, and more, the Pittsburgh duo’s maximalist music echoes the cruel momentum of the modern world.

title: Conference of Trees
description: With strings, xylophone, and homemade wooden percussion in addition to his usual synths and bells, the German musician ponders the secret life of trees.

title: Mother’s Finest Compilation
description: On a new label spun off from the eponymous Berlin party series, Franklin De Costa and Hodge curate a strong selection of formidable bass/techno hybrids from acts like Laurel Halo, Batu, and Violet.

title: Not Fire
description: The Berlin-based songwriter’s bleak and coruscating new album feels like a call to hold fast and love hard.

title: Songs & Melodies, 1973-1977
description: A New York minimalist reaches into his archives, turning up solo pieces for piano and saxophone along with shape-shifting ensemble performances featuring Arthur Russell and Julius Eastman.

title: Heavy Light
description: Only the mind of Meg Remy can take the trauma inflicted on Earth and our childhoods and create something as wonderful as Heavy Light, another vivid and highly affecting album of experimental pop music.

title: Don’t Let Get You Down
description: The virtuosic beatboxer and comedian Reggie Watts teams with techno legend John Tejada for a loose, punchy set of house anthems.

title: Post
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Björk’s second album, the foundation for one of the most consequential careers in pop history.

title: We Had a Good Time
description: The Lisbon-based producer’s soft, contemplative pop centers around everyday memories, embracing repetition as a technique to reveal the novel in the ordinary.

title: Superstar
description: The New York songwriter’s fourth album sacrifices spontaneity for the sake of a character-driven concept, but her sense of humor remains as strong as ever.

title: Flood Dream
description: The Brooklyn-based duo of harp and violin make ambient music that’s eerie, beckoning, and tinged with horror.

title: Your Life Is a Record
description: The country singer-songwriter’s sharp and conversational third album transforms everyday pathos into widescreen dramas.

title: I Think I’m Good
description: The drummer/producer blends personal mental-health struggles with the subjugation of black America in a many-voiced, trap-jazz singer-songwriter opus.

title: Traditional Techniques
description: The former Pavement frontman—never someone who seemed interested in making a straightforward acoustic album—releases an unexpectedly deft and learned folk record.

title: Anyways
description: The Atlanta rapper shows off his ear for vivid imagery and counter-intuitive production on his new project.

title: YHLQMDLG
description: Bad Bunny’s second album is outstanding. It’s a big party record that pushes boundaries and pays homage to reggaetón’s past and future, all made by a swaggering star with absolutely nothing to prove.

title: World War
description: The producer also known as Mincemeat or Tenspeed collides the feverish energy of contemporary noise and techno for his shortest and most potent release yet.

title: PTSD
description: The drill legend stays true to his core: tales of trauma and paranoia that feel like watching him argue with a therapist through a crack in the door.

title: Rushing EP
description: On her beguiling debut release, the UK musician joins the atmosphere of ambient music with the structure of choral composition and the seeming effortlessness of pop.

title: My Turn
description: The Atlanta rapper tries to tell the story of his rise to fame on his guest star-packed new album, but the music is all work and no inspiration.

title: The Main Thing
description: As they enter their second decade, the indie-rock veterans gently expand the borders of their suburban ennui with plush arrangements and new voices.

title: Simulcast
description: This instrumental companion to the San Francisco electronic musician’s 2019 album Weather is unfailingly mood-stabilizing and office-friendly, like a desktop screensaver of an ocean.

title: Rakka
description: After selling his gear and nearly abandoning music, the Finnish producer returns from the Arctic tundra with a terrifying portrayal of nature’s violence.

title: La vita nuova EP
description: The singer and producer’s dazzling new EP is a subtle gesture about grace and interiority and the illusion of effortlessness, the same attributes that mark Chris as a true star.

title: Expectations
description: With stately ballads and choruses to shatter glass, the Nashville singer-songwriter’s debut builds into a record that feels deeply thoughtful and unified.

title: Everlasting Spring
description: The solo guitarist’s latest album on the prolific Flower Room label is subtly progressive. It’s celestial without being sleepy, and rarely stays still.

title: Ordinary Man
description: On his best album in decades, the most famous man in metal reaches again for big hooks and big statements, with help from new friends like Post Malone.

title: Suddenly
description: Dan Snaith’s latest is as sly and layered as ever, but he finds ways to be more direct with his songwriting. There are no bum notes, no wasted motions, no corners of the audio spectrum left untouched.

title: The Weather Up There
description: Assisted by Jeff Parker, Tomeka Reid, and Makaya McCraven, the Chicago drummer pays tribute to his late brother with an innovative fusion of jazz composition and spoken-word memorial.

title: Printer’s Devil
description: The Chicago band moves past its early twang into raucous alt-pop on an album that captures childhood confusions and adult yearning.

title: Fungus II
description: Ty Segall’s collaboration with Lightning Bolt’s Brian Chippendale has the same risky yet satisfying quality of watching acid burn through steel.

title: F♯ A♯ ∞
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Godspeed You! Black Emperor’s debut album, a despairing and sweeping document of post-rock.

title: Milkteeth
description: On his third and richest album, the English singer-songwriter probes the mysteries of childhood, family, and memory.

title: Full Hand
description: The Indiana musician Kevin Krauter makes sunny, nostalgic shoegaze with some pleasing arrangements but not a lot of specificity.

title: Everything Is Beautiful / Everything Sucks
description: On a double-set of albums, the New York rapper stakes a claim to life’s dualities, exploring the many layers of her personality with style and vulnerability.

title: Everyday Nothing
description: The British singer and songwriter finds her niche, setting her voice at the center of modest, forthright songs that celebrate self-sufficiency and restraint.

title: Red Paint Reverend
description: The Oak Park rapper’s new album is one of his meanest and funniest, cementing him as a fresh voice in California rap.

title: Companion Rises
description: After several years digging into hushed oddities and esoteric songwriting systems, Ben Chasny resurfaces with his most immediate batch of songs yet.

title: color theory
description: The second album from singer-songwriter Sophie Allison is piercing and unpredictable. In contrast to its bigger and brighter sound, the mood is grimmer, the emotional truths darker.

title: Cape God
description: Inspired by a documentary about the opioid crisis, the pop singer and songwriter dreams up a fictionalized shoreline town where decadence is fueled by deep-rooted melancholia.

title: Got It Made
description: Free of her stifling major-label contract, the Bay Area rapper sounds rejuvenated, delivering fiery screeds on self-reliance of all sorts.

title: Full Circle
description: The mesmerizing Brooklyn rapper's latest release finds him disappearing further into his singular style: gritty samples, low-key rhymes, no real hooks.

title: The Allegory
description: The latest from the Detroit rapper is impressively self-produced and features as many showy passages as clunky stumbling blocks.

title: Myopia
description: The Danish songwriter’s ghostly chamber pop experiments form their own foggy landscape, inviting you into a creeping mist where vocals and piano smear together.
The Venezuelan artist's latest single-track piece contains some of her most delicate and astonishing work.

title: Look At Us Now Dad
description: Martha Brown goes from Charli XCX band member to pop singer on her debut, tackling intergenerational trauma and the painful path to self-understanding with a melodic bubblegum sound.

title: Slap Happy
description: The Los Angeles producer sticks to his habitual turf, crafting lo-fi drum workouts rooted in vintage house.

title: A New Dawn
description: Rising New York fixtures AceMo and MoMA Ready team up on a collaborative album that pays homage to the fast-and-loose aesthetics of ’90s underground dance music.

title: Map of the Soul: 7
description: The K-pop group’s latest is part memoir, part fan service, and part amateur psych eval. They can still tap into something enchanting, but the glimpses of personality here are fleeting.

title: Wild Wild East
description: The composer and jazz multi-instrumentalist explores the myth of the American cowboy through an immigrant's lens on his genre-blending latest.

title: Kulør 006
description: The Danish DJ Courtesy’s label pivots from Copenhagen’s fast-techno sound to a more nuanced and mysterious snapshot of the city’s electronic sounds.

title: The Price of Tea in China
description: On their latest collaboration, the Detroit rapper and the Beverly Hills producer turn out one of the year’s most immersive rap albums.

title: The Rising / Devils & Dust / Live in New York City / Live in Dublin / 18 Tracks
description: The latest in Springsteen’s vinyl reissue series provides a few lost gems for record collectors and completists. But for these odd years, even for the uninitiated, there’s plenty of gold to discover.

title: Before the Age of Mirrors
description: Marco del Rio’s songs are full of riffs that become more nauseating the longer you listen. It all sounds wrong, in the most menacing possible way.

title: Salvador
description: On his solo album, the London producer cloaks his self-doubt in deceptively danceable electronic beats that fuse elements of rap, pop, and UK bass in unexpected ways.

title: Bloody Kisses
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Type O Negative’s third album, a brooding and influential reinvention of goth metal from 1993.

title: Always Tomorrow
description: The band’s new LP is a rosily optimistic record that showcases Bethany Cosentino’s expanding range as a vocalist and songwriter.

title: I Let It In and It Took Everything
description: On their second album, the metalcore band widens the limits of its genre, incorporating nu-metal, shoegaze, and even early-’00s emo.

title: Soakie
description: The hardcore quartet’s 13-minute debut skewers abuses of power, unchecked male privilege, and capitalist complacency at tornado speed.

title: White Ladder (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: The UK singer-songwriter’s 1998 album remains a phenomenon that defies explanation: a modest collection of love songs recorded in his bedroom by an Everyman who was suddenly Everywhere.

title: Random Desire
description: The Afghan Whigs leader's debut solo album balances guitar-slashing catharsis with candelabra-lit elegance, taking inspired tangents from his signature nocturnal sensibility without departing from it entirely.

title: Miss Anthropocene
description: Grimes’ first project as a bona fide pop star is more morose than her previous work, but no less camp. Her genuineness shines through the album’s convoluted narrative, and the songs are among her finest.

title: Molocular Meditation
description: Assisted by the Fall’s late Mark E. Smith, the German experimental musician explores a fusion of abstract electronics and spoken word that has little precedent in his work with Mouse on Mars.

title: Demonstrating Visible Differences of Height EP
description: Maya Bon’s diaristic bedroom rock charts attraction, loneliness, neuroses, and late capitalism in winsome, pointillist detail.

title: Man Alive!
description: The lanky London outlaw with cement-mixer lungs delivers his most anguished album yet, in which impending fatherhood collides with his habitual torments.

title: Duo Exchange: Complete Sessions / First Time Out: Live at Slugs 1967
description: Two archival releases highlight the range of John Coltrane’s late-period drummer: one a fiery free jazz duo album, the other a newly unearthed concert recording that captures him in a more relaxed mode.

title: Swimmer
description: The duo continue their drift from lo-fi throwbacks to crisp modern pop, while maintaining the preoccupation with marital love that has animated their records since the beginning.

title: Planet Swajjur
description: After a mixtape staking his claim to the Woah, a viral dance, the Dallas rapper looks to present himself as a bona fide pop artist with an aesthetic universe of his own.

title: Fluids of Emotion
description: The veteran DJ’s first solo EP confidently navigates a full spectrum of emotion, imbuing her tracks with a sense of wonder.

title: Sea to Sea
description: Using a fanciful palette of chintzy synths and other new-age-adjacent sounds, the Latvian producer pays tribute to the moon’s seas—and humans’ capacity for wonder.

title: Mercy
description: With its mix of rustic lullabies and blown-out rockers, the Men’s eighth album is the work of a proudly counter-intuitive band pushing to new extremes.

title: The Storm Sessions
description: The instrumental duo go all-in on the possibilities of their raw steel-string chemistry, publishing an unplanned session straight to wax.

title: LP5
description: The Oklahoma roots songwriter expands his increasingly experimental and genre-resistant songbook without sacrificing his empathetic, poetic core.

title: Changes
description: The popstar returns with a grown-man album about domestic love that has all the glow and eroticism of an airport terminal.

title: NEVAEH
description: The New York City-based conceptual and visual artist’s experimental club tracks channel the legacies of black women icons into visions of utopias.

title: Chill Out
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the KLF’s sample-heavy dreamscape, one of the most influential records in ambient house music.

title: Fuck the World
description: The Maryland crooner’s dreamy R&B portrays a world where sex is a game and there are no consequences for anything.

title: And It’s Still Alright
description: Setting aside the retro R&B vamping of his group the Night Sweats, the Denver singer-songwriter returns to the sad-sack folk of his roots.

title: What’s Tonight to Eternity
description: On their fourth solo release in three years, the former Women member strikes a provocative balance of ’60s pop bliss and horror-show unease.

title: Loom
description: On her second album, the L.A. musician grapples with the death of her mother, placing her playfully experimental approach to sampling and sound design in the service of a more meaningful vision.

title: The Slow Rush
description: On his fourth album, Kevin Parker takes a breath and eases into a smoother psychedelic sound. Even without the adrenaline-filled highs, the compositions are as rich and thoughtful as ever.

title: Ecstatic Science
description: A new-classical sextet known for pop-adjacent collaborations tackles a set of pieces that highlight its mission to convert new listeners to contemporary composition.

title: Honeymoon
