description: Chicago’s Lili Trifilio writes about heartache and insecurity with the wistful, plainspoken honesty of power-pop.

title: Unlocked
description: On his collaboration with Kenny Beats, the Miami rapper pays tribute to unbridled rap personas like DMX and ODB.

title: Meet the Woo Vol. 2
description: The rising Brooklyn rapper’s new mixtape gets over on sheer maximalism just like its predecessor, with enough deft touches to keep things exciting.

title: soaring wayne phoenix story the earth
description: Originally recorded a decade ago, these contemplative sketches are full of the complicated wisdom that only comes with time.

title: Workaround
description: The debut from the London musician is a culmination of her eclectic journey to the vanguard of electronic music. It is a marvelous paradox: Despite the music’s rigidity, it breathes like a living thing.

title: i am gambling with my life
description: On his debut solo album under a new alias, Spirit of the Beehive’s Zack Schwartz runs with his band’s genre-agnostic ethos, applying his hyperactive style to chillwave, rap beats, punk, and more.

title: Àdá Irin
description: The enigmatic rapper’s debut LP is an honest and optimistic coming-of-age story about overcoming pain with the guidance of loved ones.

title: No One Else Can Wear Your Crown
description: The London pop duo’s impulse to pare down seems admirable, but the songs can be monotonous.
Nicolas Jaar returns to his dancefloor alias, swapping out the mid-tempo crowd-pleasers for a set of surprisingly stern techno that bristles with distortion.

title: Countless Branches
description: The singer-songwriter’s third album since returning from his decades-long obscurity is his sparest and most tender.

title: The Unraveling
description: On their dark and impressionistic new album, the long-running Southern rock band turns their political anxiety inward.

title: Houses
description: On an album created entirely using iPhone and iPad apps, the UK singer and producer trades his customary futuristic soul for the house and techno of his youth.

title: Yellow Tape
description: The Memphis rapper offers hard truths and effortless swagger on his uncompromising new mixtape.

title: Try Again
description: The Earl Sweatshirt collaborator’s curated, understated mixtape fits a wealth of words into a small space. Even when rapping, he thinks like a producer, as concerned with texture as he is with text.

title: Deep Listening
description: In 1989, Pauline Oliveros coined the term Deep Listening to describe a practice of radical attentiveness. This double LP collects the famed original record with selections from her Deep Listening Band.

title: All or Nothing
description: The disco-punk trio’s new record leans more heavily on synthesizers and drum pads, but stops just shy of redefining the group as a synth-pop band.

title: Illuminations
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Buffy Sainte-Marie’s cosmic, groundbreaking 1969 album, an ecstatic invocation of pain, pleasure, and divinity.

title: Live at the Royal Albert Hall, 1974
description: With cover songs and a couple of originals, this solo live performance captures the prolific Roxy Music leader in top form: the weirdo conduit for a generation’s teenage pop dreams.

title: Texas Sun EP
description: After touring together, the psych-funk trio and the soul singer head into the studio for an EP that's both tantalizing and a little half-baked.

title: We’re New Again: A Reimagining by Makaya McCraven
description: The Chicago drummer and producer transforms Gil-Scott Heron's final album into a masterpiece of dirty blues, spiritual jazz, and deep yearning.

title: 27 Miles Underwater
description: Alongside producer Gil Norton, whose work defined commercial alt-rock, the Leeds hardcore band reanimates the sound of 1995 with eerie accuracy.

title: Crashed My Car
description: Working with Lil Peep collaborator Nedarb, the Riverside rapper makes 10 songs feel like a great house party right before someone calls the cops.

title: Which Way Is Forward? EP
description: The Nigerian-born, London-based artist returns with his strongest work yet, celebrating black selfhood in expansive, richly textured songs rooted in Afrobeat and electronic soul.

title: Father of All...
description: The pop-punk stalwarts resist political commentary in lieu of making the most convincingly carefree Green Day record of the new millennium.

title: There Is No Other
description: On her first solo album in 14 years, the former Belle and Sebastian singer indulges a gently psychedelic fantasy of California fleshed out with gospel vocals and a Tom Petty cover.

title: Treat Myself
description: The pop star attempts to be all things to all people, offering an overstimulating mix of sounds and a message of self-flagellation disguised as empowerment.

title: Some Music for Robby Müller
description: Jim Jarmusch and Carter Logan’s tribute to the late Dutch cinematographer Robby Müller is a meditation on the meeting of music and film.

title: Likewise
description: The Philadelphia musician’s first record under her own name eschews the blown-out euphoria of her band Hop Along, but her voice remains an instrument of rare expressive power.

title: Parasite: Original Motion Picture Score
description: With unexpected musical contrasts that evoke a constant sense of uncertainty, composer Jung Jae-il’s score hints at what lies beneath the characters’ superficial appearances.

title: Walls
description: The latest One Directioner to go his own way tackles big themes, but the music is filled with that same dead-eyed vocal delivery, lazy drumming, strumming, and writing that all pop stars fear.

title: The World at Night
description: On his poignant new solo album, the former Walkmen member fondly remembers his old friend and collaborator Stewart Lupton, who died in 2018.

title: Funeral
description: With his big legacy album Tha Carter V out of the way, Weezy is back in the booth and cruising, experimenting with an array of styles and a dizzying maze of wordplay.

title: When We Stay Alive
description: On the band’s fifth album, singer-songwriter Channy Leaneagh grapples empathetically with the daily life after a terrible accident, but the band behind her can’t keep up.

title: LSD
description: The hardened Detroit traditionalist finds a surprising foil with the New Zealand producer Leonard Charles.

title: Laughing Gas
description: A handful of tracks recorded during the Indigo sessions suggest an artist more concerned with creating a vibe than conjuring sincere feeling.

title: Mystic Familiar
description: On the Baltimore musician’s first album in five years, he finds inspiration in his daily meditation practice, but his songwriting sounds as antic as ever.

title: I Was Born Swimming
description: The indie rock singer-songwriter Ella O’Connor Williams’ debut album is poetic, ethereal, and slightly distant.

title: Silver Tongue
description: Mackenzie Scott’s fourth album is both her most intimate and eclectic. Its best moments are the sound of someone powering through uncertainty until they find their direction again.

title: Interplay
description: On her latest release, the Canadian electronic producer approaches emotional turbulence from a place of spiritual calm.

title: Laundry Service
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Shakira’s big crossover record that revealed her fascinating, idiosyncratic songwriting and created a rift among her fans.

title: Land of No Junction
description: The Irish songwriter’s voice shines like a headlight in fog. Her debut abounds with deceptively serene serenades and surprising lyrical shifts.

title: High Road
description: The celebrated pop star’s fourth album attempts a return to the carefree party pop that defined her early career.

title: Scis
description: The glitch pioneer’s new album takes his music to new levels of density and playfulness.

title: Keeping Up Appearances
description: Scottish indie-pop musician Patrick Doyle died in 2018, just 32; this posthumous recording with bassist and tourmate Helen Skinner offers a poignant snapshot of his “bent music for bent people.”

title: Have We Met
description: On his masterful new album, Dan Bejar moves like a ghost through his familiar and inscrutable universe.

title: If I Am Only My Thoughts
description: The debut LP from this Canadian folk-pop trio radiates immediacy and approachability.

title: Be Up a Hello
description: On his first proper album in five years, Tom Jenkinson patches together a passel of vintage hardware to revisit the breakbeat mayhem and drill’n’bass hijinks of his early years.

title: The Neon Skyline
description: The Canadian singer-songwriter uses the concept album to recreate the quietly stirring scenes of a dead romance. The Neon Skyline unfolds into a wistful, funny, and heartbreaking world of its own.

title: Desire
description: Moving beyond FAKA’s gqom influences, the South African musician pairs experimental club styles with operatic falsetto in a multi-sensory exploration of the nature of the divine.

title: the first glass beach album
description: The Los Angeles band’s idiosyncratic debut is a whirlwind of post-emo maximalism, fusing mid-aughts pop-punk with synthy, sugarcoated chiptune.

title: Hotspot
description: On their 14th studio album, the best-selling duo in UK pop dampen the euphoria; the result is a tuneful, wan album that lands somewhere in the middle of their rich catalogue.

title: Bonny Light Horseman
description: The folk supergroup subtly recasts centuries of standards for our fractious and uncertain present.

title: Speed Kills
description: These unruly British punks sound like hardcore kids playing pub rock, and their debut comes alive with liberating energy.

title: Big Conspiracy
description: The London rapper’s second album is smoother, preciser, and more measured. We see J Hus as a lost son of Gambia, an adult-in-progress, a talented pop polymath, and just a guy who has a lot of sex.

title: Invisible Ritual
description: Returning to the duo format, the MacArthur grant-winning experimental percussionist teams up with an elite classical violinist for an album of wide-ranging improvisations.

title: Big Baby Earnhardt
description: The tracks on the Florida rapper’s latest tape overflow with jubilant maximalism and have a proudly Southern bounce.

title: Watch This Liquid Pour Itself
description: The second album from the mercurial singer lets listeners in on another intimate journey of self-reflection, this time drawing on laconic folk, downtempo rock, and upbeat disco.

title: Brolik
description: The Detroit rapper channels the lawless energy of mixtape Nicki and Wayne on his latest.

artist: Terry Allen & the Panhandle Mystery Band
title: Just Like Moby Dick
description: With the help of collaborators, the 76-year-old songwriter takes what would be another great, narrative album set to the familiar rhythms of a country waltz and brings it to new places.

title: Joyful
description: Suffused in romantic piano flourishes, winsome synth leads, and drums that race like a teenaged heart, these seven tracks pursue pure, unadulterated delight.

title: Concrete and Glass
description: The French musician’s solo album is full of blissed-out vocoder ballads that would have slotted effortlessly onto his duo Air’s Moon Safari.

title: Black Sarabande
description: This contemporary classical pianist’s music proves more unsettling the more you disturb its placid surface.

title: Thin Mind
description: Wolf Parade’s latest album plays like the big leap the band could have attempted last decade—without ever quite recapturing the odd, jittery intensity that made them so beguiling.

title: Home
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a pure  and quiet record from 2002, when the Dixie Chicks were the most righteous band in country music.

title: A Change in Diet
description: On his poignant second album, the multitalented singer-songwriter gives voice to the self-doubts that manifest in the wee hours of the morning.

title: Music to Be Murdered By
description: It is not, strictly speaking, a good record—Eminem hasn’t made one of those in a decade—but his latest boasts enough technical command and generates just enough arresting ideas to hold your attention.

title: Death of the Neon
description: Though the Pennsylvania band favor post-rock swells, tricky song structures, and off-kilter time signatures, their restrained maximalism defies expectations.

artist: ...And You Will Know Us by the Trail of Dead
title: X: The Godless Void and Other Stories
description: Pared back to a duo, the storied Austin band sounds unexpectedly winsome on their revelatory tenth album.

title: Suite for Max Brown
description: The veteran guitarist has created an effortlessly detailed album, full of tradition and experimentation that spans generations. It lives at the vanguard of new jazz music.

title: Scanning Backwards
description: Tapping his background in industrial and EBM, the Berghain resident delivers a steely set of cuts tailored for maximum impact inside the club.

title: RICH YOUNGIN
description: DaBaby’s hypeman manages to make money sound boring on his first solo outing.

title: Everything Else Has Gone Wrong
description: After a long hiatus, the big-tent UK pop band returns with a joyful but middling album that’s a little bit of everything they’ve always been.

title: Manic
description: Written from her own perspective, Halsey’s third album flips lonely self-awareness into a kind of strength. But some of its most compelling moments are overpowered by the tedium of modern pop.

title: The Comforts of Madness
description: The 30th-anniversary reissue of this dream-pop landmark includes a second disc of demos, capturing a celebrated band already eager to move onto new sounds.

title: Please Daddy
description: Ever attuned to the nuances of grief, the Melbourne singer-songwriter tackles somber subjects with her typical gravity, but there’s a newfound lightness in her step.

title: Debris
description: On her arid and beautiful debut, the dancer, actress, and composer charts her climb out of paralyzing depression.

title: R.Y.C.
description: The London artist’s surprising second album pivots from twinkly, futuristic electro-pop to nostalgic guitar anthems for the bummer generation.

title: Marigold
description: On their fourth album, the indie-folk band still possess their signature warmth, but the charm of their heartfelt confessionals has dimmed.

title: Swirlings
description: Daryl Groetsch’s style is distinguished by its deeply expressive sensibility. Few ambient composers can fit quite as much feeling into such a small curlicue of tone.

title: Modus Vivendi
description: The heavy-hearted G.O.O.D. Music debut from the young singer is a refreshingly new take on eclectic, lovesick soul music.

title: Football Money
description: With easy hooks, surprise structural twists, and a gift for non-sequiturs, the Canadian quartet’s debut is a vivid portrait of the big-city struggle. Pavement’s influence is impossible to ignore.

title: The Professionals
description: The preeminent crate-digging producer teams up with his younger brother, the rapper Oh No, for a soulful, topical, but reserved project that simmers just below the surface.

title: nijimusi
description: Boredoms drummer YoshimiO returns to the long-running, shape-shifting project that represents the other major pillar of her career, consolidating the strengths the band has developed over the years.

title: Coke Wave
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the high-stakes saga of Max B and French Montana’s 2009 mixtape, a modern classic of New York rap.

title: Munich 2016
description: A newly released date from the pianist’s 2016 European tour toggles between dizzyingly athletic avant-garde jazz, foot-stomping ragtime, and a few tender standards.

title: UR FUN
description: Setting doomy lyrics atop blissful melodies and wispy psychedelic production, Kevin Barnes’ latest album wields his habitual twee escapism like a shield.

title: Shall Not Fade - 4 Years of Service
description: After four years of releasing pioneering and transcendent techno, the UK label offers a new comp full of charm that looks ahead to its promising future.

title: There Is No Year
description: Grounded in historical horrors and gesturing darkly at personal demons, the gospel-punk band’s third album is shot through with dread.

title: You Can Never Have a Long Enough Head Start
description: They may still be stuck in their apartments, false nostalgia, or dead-end service gigs, but the upstart Seattle emo band’s revelation of a second album goes places.

title: Losst and Founnd
description: On the first posthumous album from the famed singer-songwriter, his renowned talent often feels lost in the glut of over-the-top arrangements, flashy production, and cheesy songwriting.

title: Circles
description: The first posthumous album from Mac Miller plays like a companion piece to Swimming. It’s an optimistic epilogue to the life of an aspirational artist.

title: Purple Haze 2
description: Resurrecting a strand of mid-2000s New York hip-hop built on tightly wound samples and a reduced emphasis on bass, Purple Haze 2 is forged in the spirit of the original.

title: in case i die first
description: The short EP from the Philly rapper might not be essential but it reveals more of the fascinating dark side of her artistry.

title: Making a New World
description: The English art-rock duo’s concept album about history post-World War I isn’t worth taking half as seriously as it takes itself.

title: The Circus EP
description: On what he’s called a “prelude” to his next album, the Chicago rapper sets aside the big themes of previous records and luxuriates in letting his mind wander.

title: Lina_Raül Refree
description: A Portuguese singer and a Spanish guitarist (and one-time Rosalía collaborator) pair up to translate fado icon Amália Rodrigues’ songs into subtly experimental contemporary forms.

title: I Disagree
description: The cryptic YouTuber’s new album is the first to fully embrace the upsetting qualities of her video works, folding elements of nu-metal and grindcore into her seasick melange.

title: A Jump From the High Dive
description: The East Coast songwriter’s college-rock melodies and boyish vocal delivery waver between charming and cloying.

title: Mogadisco - Dancing Mogadishu (Somalia 1972–1991)
description: Drawing on the archives of Radio Mogadishu, Analog Africa’s latest archival compilation tells a story of openness that is at stark odds with the past few decades of Somalia’s history.

title: Le Piano Englouti
description: Brunhild Ferrari, the longtime partner of Luc Ferrari, is a powerful creative force in her own right. Jim O’Rourke assists on two new realizations of her work, interpreting them with rare sensitivity.

title: Dreamin’
description: The third album from the Philadelphia-based quintet, led by Dan Wriggins’ spare and transparent songwriting, creates a warm and disorienting mood.

title: Rare
description: Selena Gomez’s third album is a smooth and confident pop record that delves deep—but not that deep—into heartbreak, resilience, and self-love.

title: And I Revel
description: Chewing the foundations of rock into gritty sludge, the New York quartet proudly makes music that sounds loud, messy, and wrong.

title: Existential
description: The New York producer tailors his overdriven techno epics to unusually introspective ends, sculpting stripped-down arrays of synth and drums into spare, expressive forms.

title: Garden Party
description: A gathering of jazz avant-gardists and a new generation of players produces a tossed-off album with a spirit of celebratory tradition.

title: Música Esporádica
description: A rediscovered gem from the prolific new age composer conjures the dreamy polyrhythms of Steve Reich to blissful and kinetic results.

title: Vanquish
description: The dancehall artist’s first act at OVO is not to push forward but to look back. The mixtape is a bit like a recent Popcaan retrospective that sounds simply like a companion piece to his last album.

title: Enema of the State
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit blink-182’s third album, a defining moment in both pop-punk and immaturity writ large.

title: Winter/Time
description: The interwoven guitars, synths, and cymbal crashes of Amy Klein’s second solo album are gale-force, but its opaque lyrics and muted vocals are indirect and timid.

title: Watchmen (Music from the HBO Series)
description: The duo’s three-part score for showrunner Damon Lindelof’s sociopolitically fraught story of vigilantism is their strongest and most direct since The Social Network.

title: Somebody Else’s Song
description: The Brooklyn duo of Rachel Brown and Nate Amos follow their whims to make experimental pop that combines the freedom of exploration with poignant introspection.

title: Nature, Man & Woman EP
description: Max Turnbull’s newest group takes its name from a song co-written by Eric Clapton and George Harrison—then stretches it from a three-minute pop song into a 14-minute improvisatory mission statement.

title: Seeking Thrills
description: The second album written, produced, and performed by Georgia Barnes is the work of a budding pop mind finding her own space on the dancefloor.

title: Multiquest Niveau 1: Camouflé
description: The Canadian electronic musician’s globe-trotting work mingles the familiar and the strange, mixing colorful influences from around the world and somehow landing close to trip-hop.

title: High Line
description: On the New York ensemble’s second album, their arid ambient-country landscapes take on a different tone, sounding less like a vacation than a dinner bell for the apocalypse.

title: The Deadbeat Bang of Heartbreak City
description: The Philly band's rousing punk anthems lose a little luster on an album that feels more motivated by desperation than starry-eyed conviction.

title: Heavy Rain
description: The dub innovator reworks 2019’s Rainford, stripping the original down into a form that is warmer and weirder.

title: Networker
description: The Atlanta duo’s Sub Pop debut examines the mundane anxieties of modern life with caffeinated post-punk that recalls Parquet Courts or Wire.

title: Walking Like We Do
description: The UK quartet pairs glowing synth pads and layered harmonies with a distinctly millennial approach to the possibility of total annihilation.

title: Resonance
description: The Finnish producer continues his streak of luminous electronic releases with an ecstatic, body-moving, and curiously serene collection of techno bangers.

title: Jesus Is Born
description: Kanye West’s executive-produced gospel album is the most realized music to come from this era of his career. The production and the choir’s dynamic power creates an almost hallucinatory effect.

title: Flock
description: The Swedish violinist’s first album-length recording as a solo artist confirms both her uncompromisingly experimental instincts and substantial musical gifts.

title: Impossible Journey of My Soul Tonight
description: Produced by Beau Sorenson and recorded at John Vanderslice’s Tiny Telephone, Melissa Ann Sweat’s fourth album under the alias is a searching work of elemental folk minimalism.

artist: A Winged Victory for the Sullen
title: The Undivided Five
description: The neoclassical ambient duo’s first proper album in nine years pays tribute to the mystical painter Hilma af Klint in stirring strings, melancholy fanfare, and a winking hint of self-awareness.

title: k bye for now (swt live)
description: Ariana Grande’s live album is both a capsule and a capstone, encompassing a nine-month, 102-show tour at what might be the peak of her career.

title: New Ways
description: Conceived as a companion piece to 2017’s Twin Solitude, the Canadian songwriter’s fourth album is a dialogue with the person he’s been.

title: La Luz de la Esperanza
description: The Latinx artist reimagines traditional Mexican ranchera folk songs with a goth edge and a lavish, telenovela-style production.

title: E
description: The debut album from this Swedish multi-hyphenate, an associate of Yung Lean and Yves Tumor, trades hip-hop for an expressive—and surprisingly pretty—take on contemporary pop.

title: JACKBOYS
description: The newly minted rap superstar’s obligatory label compilation is more merch bundle than album.

title: Super Enthusiast
description: The Long Island emo outfit pushes the classic poison-pen sound into brightly colored power-pop territory.

title: Hymn to Moisture
description: Operating under the alias Rrose, the Californian Seth Horvitz deploys the time-honored materials of techno to produce something destabilizing and new.

title: So
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Peter Gabriel’s 1986 art-pop masterpiece, a turning point in the commercial globalization of pop music.

title: Remember the Silver
description: The New York singer-songwriter deftly captures indie-pop longing, though her musical gestures can feel a bit lifeless.

title: juneunit
description: The debut album from this New England-based producer blends ambient, techno, and house into a single sumptuous mood, suffused in tape hiss.

title: Salt Water
description: Inspired by Australia’s lush temperate rainforest, the Melbourne producer’s second album emphasizes melody and background texture more than big drops or bass lines.

title: Bite the Burger
description: The Queens rapper-singer continues to refine her joyfully lascivious, sex-positive sound, but her best moments are the quiet ones.

title: Refuge Cove
description: The Melbourne songwriter’s classic influences guide her toward an album that feels proudly out of time. Its nine songs feel like variations on one stark, psychedelic vision.

title: The Ground Our Sky
description: With pedal steel, synthesizer, and a whisper of voice, Marielle Jakobsons and Chuck Johnson create rippling soundscapes as soothing and engulfing as a warm bath.

title: All in Good Time
description: The Australian garage rock band’s first album in eight years is a modest and welcome comeback even if they don’t crash out of the speakers like they once did.

title: Fates Worse Than Death
description: The Pittsburgh band’s throwback emo revivalism casts a hometown identity crisis in the harsh light of climate change. Their debut has the conceptual heft of an album twice its length.

title: Nibiru
description: The urbano star’s third album pushes him beyond his comfort zone as a romantic reggaetonero—and abandons some of the qualities that once made him unique.

title: After Dark
description: Sampling a worn vinyl copy of Debussy’s La Mer, the Chicago musician creates short, impressionistic pieces that fuse ambient, drone, and noise; they’re easy to get lost in.

title: Year One Demos
description: Cleaned up and newly remastered, these demos are bright and captivating, a rare look at the iconic emo band's sketchbook.

title: Improvement (Don Leaves Linda) / Automatic Writing
description: Two reissues of the late composer’s work highlight the attention he paid to the malleability of language and the way its sound often conveys more than its substance.

title: Duster
description: The slowcore icons’ new album bears all the hallmarks of their classic records: plodding drums, skeletal basslines, and guitar work that sparkles in the darkness like dew on a cobweb.

title: Plunge Remix
description: An adventurous, globe-spanning collection of remixes embraces the hungry and curious spirit of Fever Ray’s 2017 album Plunge.

title: Free Nationals
description: The funky retro-soul band aims to set itself apart from leader Anderson .Paak on a solo debut packed with guests, including Syd, Kali Uchi, and the late Mac Miller.

title: Tapestry
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Carole King’s Tapestry, the second act that turned a master songwriter into a music legend.

title: Nina Kraviz Presents Masseduction Rewired
description: The Russian techno DJ Nina Kraviz enlists Jlin, Buttechno, Midland, and others in remixing all 13 songs from Annie Clark’s 2017 album, to sometimes scattershot effect.

title: Sing the Melody
description: While the band’s new live-in-studio album doesn’t radically reinvent any songs, trimming some of their more frivolous elements grants new clarity and focus.

title: Slipping EP
description: The London producer’s latest EP is both his least dancefloor-minded release and his most satisfying by design.

title: OCCULTING DISK
description: After a long hiatus, the solo electronics master returns with a mesmerizing, terrifying, and emotionally nuanced “anti-fascist ritual” of an album.

title: MONTANA
description: The double album from the Bronx rapper is a bloated, grab-bag of singles made for Hornblower cruises and thirty-second timeouts at Madison Square Garden.

title: Upsurge
description: Following in the path of his label-mates Skee Mask and the Zenker Brothers, the Italian producer’s debut album continues to provide a loose-limbed counterargument to more rigid strains of techno.

title: Heavy Is the Head
description: As he ascends from grime rapper to generational spokesperson, the charismatic UK star tries to figure out where to go next.

title: Bubba
description: With an exceptional collaborative spirit and a highly refined sound, Kaytranada blesses this woeful decade with one last great dance record.

title: WT_PRT15.
description: In the latest installment of his anthology, Glen Boothe continues dipping rap verses in warm, nostalgic loops.

title: Uncut Gems (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: The Safdie brothers’ Adam Sandler vehicle is replete with outsized personalities, but Oneohtrix Point Never’s anxiety-stoking score makes a confident bid for a supporting role in its own right.

title: LP1
description: The former One Direction member’s solo debut is just another pop star flailing to find his identity amid trend-hopping production and half-baked lyrics.

title: The Chronic
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the timeless 1992 debut from Dr. Dre, a historic moment in hip-hop that redefined West Coast rap.

title: Romance
description: The pop singer’s second album captures the thrilling feelings of experiencing love, but it becomes so universalized that it blurs it out of focus.

title: Bad Vibes Forever
description: His purported final posthumous album is more of monument to XXXTentacion’s brand rather than his artistry.

title: Fine Line
description: Harry Styles hides himself inside of a mystic pop-rock record that keeps us away from who he is as a songwriter and fledgling rock star.

title: Glacial Pace
description: Singer-songwriter Brian Collins joins the Woodsist camp with a light, loose collection of songs built for placid and rudderless afternoons.

title: Grime MC
description: The London grime star has made the strongest record of his career, chock full of nimble, intricate raps that seamlessly integrate the nerdiest of signifiers.

title: Puck
description: This collage work by the Los Angeles composer weaves together stray chamber compositions, ambient recordings, voices, and more, yielding a mesmerizing sound both dense and diaphanous.

title: Ism
description: The Chicago bassist’s solo debut—featuring guests including Makaya McCraven, Isaiah Spencer, and Tomeka Reid—ranges widely, from free jazz to post-bop to meditative tone poems.

title: Please Excuse Me For Being Antisocial
description: This Compton chameleon borrows flows from anyone and everyone but gets away with it thanks to his sturdy songwriting.

title: Oderbruch
description: The techno artist discovers a softer, warmer side in an album named for his childhood home.

title: Island Alchemy
description: The Copenhagen composer’s second album this year, and her first for Oakland’s Constellation Tatsu, offers a dynamic take on ambient music, one meant for active listening.

title: Echo Earth
description: Gentle but full of motion, the Portland, Oregon producer’s seemingly uncomplicated music brings the language of left-field ’90s dance to the great outdoors.

title: Pleaser
description: The lead singer for the barn-burning punk act Camp Cope shifts into synth-pop and romantic love for her solo debut.

title: Blood Transfusion
description: The Los Angeles singer-songwriter’s music gets a beat-oriented makeover in a collection of remixes from Skrillex, Omar S, Lafawndah, and other club producers.

title: HERstory Vol. 1
description: In the ’90s, Blige prophesied a future in which hip-hop would be baked directly into pop music. The hits on this collection show her just getting started.

title: Andrés IV
description: Eight years after his last album and seven since the crowd-pleasing “New for U,” the Detroit house and hip-hop staple shows off his encyclopedic knowledge of soul, disco, and Latin music.

title: MTV Unplugged Live in Melbourne
description: The Australian singer-songwriter uses the Unplugged format as a showcase for the community of musicians she’s cultivated.

title: Still Young EP
description: Two friends—one a longtime Neil Young fan, one a relative newcomer—team up for a warm, unpretentious covers EP that serves as an unlikely primer.

title: Melly vs. Melvin
description: The incarcerated rapper, awaiting trial for murder, releases an album of second-rate material and third-rate Young Thug–isms.

title: We Are Beat Happening
description: An essential new vinyl box set collects all of the trailblazing Olympia band’s records. It is a monument to the spartan trio’s music and their seismic influence on the indie rock that followed in their wake.

title: To Magnetize Money and Catch a Roving Eye
description: O’Rourke’s latest drone project, running to over four hours, is darker and more dreamlike than his Steamroom series, and one of his most meditative releases yet.

title: Jules
description: The Baltimore music student’s soft-focus popcraft plays like a lost link between the hazed-out aesthetic of chillwave and the smooth precision of sophisti-pop.

title: Until the End of the World (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: A new reissue of the illusory soundtrack to Wim Wenders’ 1991 road film, which featured the final recordings of CAN and Talking Heads, highlights its forlorn and decadent melancholy.

title: Three Cheers for Sweet Revenge
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit My Chemical Romance’s second album, an operatic pop-rock behemoth that became an icon for outcasts.

title: Catastrophic Deliquescence (Music From Fortitude 2015-2018)
description: The Iceland-based composer’s score for the Arctic crime drama shivers with ominous uncertainty that’s better appreciated in its original context.

title: Grapefruit Regret
description: Blawan and Pariah’s hardware-centric techno duo returns with its debut album, trading some of the distortion of early releases for a funkier, slipperier sound that still bangs.

title: Marcielago
description: The gritty and elusive Hempstead MC caps off a decade of profound influence with more photographic narratives, gnarled slang, and evocative soul samples.

title: Tunes 2011 to 2019
description: A 149-minute anthology maps the UK producer’s expanding multiverse, gathering nearly every solo tune he released on Hyperdub in a fertile, eight-year run of EPs full of surprises (and vinyl crackle).

title: Body of Carbon
description: Beneath its sharp edges and heavy drums, the producers’ second collaboration takes a gentle, humanistic approach.

title: Labyrinth
description: The producer and visual artist builds an uncanny, disturbing world on his debut LP that recalls his collaborations with Björk, Arca, and FKA twigs.

title: 20 Years of Fabric
description: The iconic London nightclub celebrates two decades with 20 tracks that survey the house, techno, and bass-music styles synonymous with the venue, with mixed results.

title: Netflix & Deal
description: The incarcerated Watts rapper’s latest is a loosely movie-themed collaboration with producer-of-the-moment Kenny Beats.

title: Ohio River EP
description: On singer-songwriter Caroline Sallee’s latest EP, everything is transitory—especially life itself.

title: The Hood Dictionary
description: The Alabama rapper’s second project of the year is a mixtape-length “First Day Out” that serves as a timestamp of this moment in his developing career.

title: No Treasure But Hope
description: The latest album from the long-running English band is one of their most sensuous and sunlit, playing on new shades of hope, love, and melancholy.

title: Heliopause
description: The loops and layers of the Berlin-based cellist’s solo album evoke resonant emotions that could afford to linger.

title: WWCD
description: The Buffalo trio’s Shady Records debut doesn’t sacrifice an ounce of their gritty and ruthless throwback aesthetic.

title: Songs for You
description: After freeing herself from a bad record deal, the multitalented R&B singer celebrates with an effortless LP that fully displays her range.

title: Hyperswim
description: Kode9’s Hyperdub label celebrates its 15th anniversary by moving confidently beyond the London club music’s conventions.

title: Hyperspace
description: On his 14th album, Beck roams across a pleasant, gently psychedelic landscape looking for something new.

title: Information
description: The rapper-producer’s third album answers the exhaustion of contemporary life online by stripping down and buttoning up, yielding a newly disciplined take on his trademark deep house.
With their skate-punk shout-alongs and double-tapped guitar heroics, this D.C. duo embodies the sound of emo in 2019.

title: Cotillions
description: The cantankerous Smashing Pumpkin embraces his vision of country music, but the lightest, breeziest songs of his career come with their own peculiar Corganian paradox.

title: Get Bleak EP
description: The Toronto quartet writes lilting, throwback jangle-pop for the isolated and the underemployed.

title: The Envoy
description: The New York electronic musician fashions an evocative tribute to Ursula K. LeGuin’s 1969 novel The Left Hand of Darkness, conjuring the flux of gender and desire in shape-shifting sounds.

title: Reflections
description: Heavy on vocal processing and maximalist A. G. Cook production, the PC Music star’s first full-length can’t help feeling a little anticlimactic.
This five-disc set, which includes concert footage, B-sides, and demos, delivers what box sets of this kind almost never do: the thrill of discovery.

title: Tattoo You
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the Rolling Stones’ 1981 album, a blueprint for how to exist as an aging, internationally famous rock band.

title: Queen & Slim: The Soundtrack
description: Vince Staples, Ms. Lauryn Hill, Megan Thee Stallion, and more come together for the soundtrack to the modern-day Bonnie-and-Clyde parable, set against a backdrop of police brutality.

title: Merry Christmas: Deluxe Anniversary Edition
description: Mariah Carey, the cultural attaché of Christmas, offers a reissue of her 1994 album, which sounds as timeless as possible for music passed through the innocuous filters of mid-’90s adult pop.

title: Ballet Slippers
description: Pieced together from four Merriweather Post Pavilion-era sets, this live album reinforces the weirdness of the band’s pop heyday.

title: Hidden History of the Human Race
description: On their psychedelic and virtuosic second album, the Denver quartet brings death metal to new and exalted places.

title: The Legendary Riverside Albums
description: Five albums recorded in the late 1950s capture the skill and the frailty of an acclaimed jazz trumpeter on the brink of disaster.

title: Supernatural
description: On their second album as a duo, Detroit techno titan Robert Hood and his daughter Lyric sharpen their focus on the fusion of house music and gospel.

title: Chixtape 5
description: On the latest installment of his mixtape series, the rapper/singer invites a truckload of guests to flip ’00s R&B hits.

title: A Good Time
description: On his second album, the Nigerian pop artist provides not just an integrated sound all his own but a clear vision for its future. It is a buoyant, unsinkable record, one of the genre’s finest ever.

title: A Private Picture
description: Chicago singer and songwriter Maria Jacobson ambles into notes from unexpected angles, emboldening the question marks behind interrogative, introspective lyrics.

title: Love Beyond the Intersect
description: Inside producer Jack Hamill’s sci-fi odysseys, Detroit futurism meets ’80s disco in the neon glow of the chillout room.

title: La Linda
description: On her second album, Valerie Teicher explores the nuances of her voice, luxuriating in the comedown of emotional excess over spacious, immaculately produced R&B.

title: Everyday Life
description: On the 52-minute vision quest that is their new double LP, the world’s most earnest arena band sound looser than they have in years.

title: Our Pathetic Age
description: The Bay Area turntablist and producer delivers a mammoth double album—half instrumentals, half rap collaborations—aimed at the decade’s widespread feeling of creeping dread.

title: The Oldest Sons of the Oldest Sons
description: Darkside’s Dave Harrington and Benoit & Sergio’s Benjamin Jay join forces on an introspective album that fuses treated guitar and ambient electronics with obliquely confessional lyrics.

title: Singles 1986-1991
description: They would go onto greater fame with Velvet Crush, but the duo of Ric Menck and Paul Chastain first reached indie pop perfection with the Springfields.
The Berlin-based musician reconceives ambient music as an urgent, deeply embodied project interrogating the experiences of black Africans in the West.

title: Hockets for Two Voices EP
description: A 10-minute EP presents an ambitious solo exploration of hocketing, a musical technique with a long and curious history.

title: Everybody’s Everything
description: Released to accompany the documentary of the same name, this compilation tells the story of Peep’s evolution through his collaborations.

title: Tangerine
description: Balancing unassuming ambient and downtempo experiments with lush, floor-filling house and electro, the London DJ’s debut album sounds refreshingly carefree.

title: WXAXRXP Sessions
description: A collection of radio sessions by 10 of Warp’s defining artists is an alternate-history crash course in a boundary-pushing label’s breadth of vision.

title: BABY GOAT
description: The younger brother of YNW Melly is only 12 years old, and his debut is sure to have middle school dances on smash.

title: Black Space Tapes
description: The young pianist makes an impressive debut as bandleader, with an expansive sound that folds elements of hip-hop, R&B, and ambient into the broad outlines of spiritual jazz.
The Bloc Party frontman attempts a blazing indictment of institutional racism on his latest solo effort, but too often reaches for stock characters and sloganeering.

title: Thanks for the Dance
description: After the grand farewell of 2016's You Want It Darker, Cohen's son gathers his father's scraps and unfinished ideas and lovingly fleshes them out with help from collaborators like Beck, The National's Bryce Dessner and Feist.

title: More Brilliant Is the Hand that Throws the Coin
description: The self-assured debut EP from the 20-year-old singer-songwriter deals with those pure and devastating first loves.

title: Aja
description: Today on Pitchfork, we are taking a critical look at Steely Dan—from their early classic rock staples to their latter-day studio sleaze—with new reviews of five of their most influential records.

title: Can’t Buy a Thrill
description: On their debut, Steely Dan brought pop instincts and studied musicianship to rock radio, putting a smooth spin on several hits that would prove to be a Trojan Horse for their esoteric ideas to come.

title: Gaucho
description: Steely Dan entered the ’80s with something elegant and arid—immaculately conceived malaise-age bachelor-pad music. In these songs, everyone’s alone, or together in a way that’s worse than being alone.

title: Katy Lied
description: Steely Dan’s fascinating fourth album, from 1975, lives at the midpoint of the band’s first act. It’s messier, less sure of itself, besotted neither with youthful confidence nor veteran polish.

title: The Royal Scam
description: By 1976, Fagen and Becker pushed their music to feel as grotesque as their words. The result is the bleakest and most narratively vivid album of their career, as well as their most misunderstood.

title: Iowa Dream
description: The latest posthumous album from the groundbreaking artist feels like one of his truest, 19 “demos” that reveal his elegant songwriting, his disregard for genre, and his boundless mind.

title: H.A.Q.Q.
description: With a new rhythm section, the notorious black metal experimentalists deliver their most aggressive and radical album yet.

title: Sunchokes
description: The scrappy indie-punk band reissues its beloved and long-out-of-print first album.

title: ATØ
description: Skillfully switching between forward momentum and deep reflection, the Berlin electronic musician’s latest album proves her to be a master storyteller.

title: Mind in Camden 2
description: RAP’s Guy Gormley weaves together field recordings, ambient sketches, and club beats in a way that feels provocatively out of step with contemporary dance music.

title: Exhaust
description: In part two of a trilogy of releases focused on “capitalist semiotic pollution,” the UK producer juggles abrasive club-music tropes with field recordings and ominous scraps of advertising.

title: II EP
description: After bowing out at the peak of the trap wave they helped usher in, Hudson Mohawke and Lunice return for their first EP in seven years, sounding as irreverent and unruly as when they started.

title: Bachelor No. 2 or, the Last Remains of the Dodo
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Aimee Mann’s third album, a world-weary showcase of independent spirit and expertly tuned songwriting.

title: It Should Be Us
description: The Manchester producer’s latest songs take us deep into the catacombs to explore a vision of club music at its most damaged.

title: New Hell
description: The second album from the Michigan rock trio is alternately brutal and transcendent, like heavy machinery coming up against the stubbornness of nature.

title: Trophy
description: A former jazz prodigy emerges with a clever and heartfelt indie rock debut that pays winking tribute to adolescence in all its agonies and small glories.

title: OOFIE
description: The NYC rapper, having left his label, shakes off the pressure of his tumultuous last few years with a set of straight-ahead, grimy rap songs.

title: I Made a Place
description: Will Oldham’s first collection of new songs as Bonnie “Prince” Billy in several years focuses on simple pleasures and persistence.

title: King of R&B
description: The self-appointed (and much-derided) new King of R&B attempts to live up to his own hype with a slick and ambitious new LP.

title: Matthew J. Rolin
description: The Columbus, Ohio-based musician approaches fingerstyle guitar with first-take energy and unassuming home-recorded production.

title: Becoming Peter Ivers
description: A new collection of the late songwriter’s work celebrates the wit, range, and unpolished charm of his oddball pop.

title: Hot Pink
description: On her first full-length release since her viral breakout, the rapper-singer and songwriter proves that her real gift is her versatility.

title: No Other
description: The Byrds frontman’s deliriously opulent solo work was misunderstood upon release, but this lavish repackaging restores a spiritual singer-songwriter classic.

title: 2019 EP
description: The singer-songwriter, inspired by seven national holidays (including Bruce Springsteen’s birthday), finds love, death, and wry humor in a few spectacular originals and a collection of covers.

title: Mummer Love
description: The experimental troupe gathers Patti Smith, Philip Glass, and Mulatu Astatke for a sometimes-glorious, sometimes-chaotic attempt at attaining spiritual rapture.

title: Lost Wisdom pt. 2
description: After two heart-rending albums about the death of his wife, Phil Elverum documents a new kind of heartbreak in a set of duets with Julie Doiron.

title: Ghetto Gospel
description: The Floridian singer-rapper delivers tender anthems about his pain and inner demons on his debut LP, executive produced by Kevin Gates.

title: Thousand Knives of Ryuichi Sakamoto
description: Released shortly before his group Yellow Magic Orchestra’s historic debut, the Japanese synthesizer icon’s first solo LP balances kitsch, complexity, and a critical geopolitical perspective.

title: Leaving Meaning
description: Michael Gira reshuffles his famous band's lineup, inviting collaborators like the Necks and Ben Frost for a record that emphasizes elegiac beauty over raging catharsis.

title: Sea of Worry
description: Beneath the metallic sheen of goth rock, the cult band’s third album addresses the disquieting anxieties of adulthood with vengeful indignation.

title: A Fossil Begins to Bray
description: Fueled by existential dread and exacting sound design, the New York electronic musician’s second album for Dais is gratifyingly menacing and masterfully executed.

title: Own Pace
description: The young Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE collaborator makes deeply internal and contemplative rap.

title: Down in Jamaica – 40 Years of VP Records
description: More than a simple greatest-hits collection, this box set commemorating Jamaica’s powerhouse independent label offers a well-rounded portrait of the iconic imprint’s role in reggae history.

title: One of the Best Yet
description: It’s thrilling to hear them again, but once the glow wears off, there’s a hollowness to this posthumous project, cobbled together from unreleased Guru vocal takes.

title: In the Court of the Crimson King (50th Anniversary)
description: The perennially reissued debut from the prog rock giants doesn’t offer much memorable bonus material, but the album itself remains a towering pillar of musicianship, wonder, and menace.

title: Analog Fluids of Sonic Black Holes
description: The Philadelphia poet and experimental musician gives voice to implacable rage and impending cataclysm.

title: Hitler Wears Hermes 7
description: The Buffalo rapper continues to build his grimy, boom-bap brand, one endearingly straightforward release at a time.

artist: ...And You Will Know Us by the Trail of Dead
title: Madonna
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Trail of Dead’s second album, a keystone in the aggressive indie-rock boon of the late ’90s.

title: Supermoon EP
description: These outtakes are less determined to deliver neatly packaged hooks, but there are still moments where the band strikes with full vulnerability and force.

title: Moon Trip Radio
description: On his second album, the cloud-rap innovator hones the decaying instrumentals of his mixtape series to make some of his warmest-sounding music to date.

title: Call for Location
description: The South Florida native’s second album is a tribute to the regional raves of her youth, filtered through the wide array of global club styles that defines her style as a DJ.

title: Travelin’ Thru, Featuring Johnny Cash: The Bootleg Series Vol. 15
description: Dylan's latest installment in his long-running Bootleg series is one of the shortest, the highlight of which is his collaboration with Johnny Cash.

title: Cartas Na Manga
description: The Lisbon producer returns to his hometown’s Príncipe label with nine new tracks of hyperkinetic, defiantly experimental club music.

title: The Juice Vol. II
description: On their second project, the group’s hazy R&B sounds pristine and precise, but the care and craft stop short of their lyrics.

title: Magdalene
description: With limitlessly innovative songwriting and production, the cinema of twigs’ music has never been more affecting. Magdalene is not just on the vanguard of pop, it’s in a breathtaking class of its own.

title: One Life
description: The ambient, five-track mini-LP from the French producer further accentuates the wide-eyed rapture of her early work.

title: A Life of Crime
description: Winston Cook-Wilson’s second album of sly, extravagant sophistipop is sleek music for a cursed place, and a heartfelt cry for lonely city strivers.

title: Athena
description: The L.A.-based singer and violinist makes her boldest and most fully formed statement yet.

title: Charlie's Angels (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: Ariana Grande executive produces the latest entry into the pop-camp franchise, but the collection feels warmed over, too glossy, and only remedially empowering.

title: [USA]
description: Six years after their breakout album, the Brooklyn chiptune veterans turn inward and re-assess their hedonism.

title: Bin Reaper
description: The Detroit scam rapper doesn’t overthink his music: This is just 13 funky instrumentals punched up with funny pop-culture references.

title: badtrip
description: On a double EP for Nina Kraviz’s Trip label, the Russian producer delivers punishing techno shot through with happy pandemonium.

title: Myths 004
description: The Deerhunter frontman and the cryptic singer-songwriter draw out each other’s playful sides on this one-off collaboration.

title: FIBS
description: On her second album proper, the Scottish producer/composer/singer-songwriter dials up her rock band’s dynamic power, creating a nervy, chaotically controlled embodiment of contemporary uncertainty.

title: Boundary Road Snacks and Drinks EP
description: The London post-punk band’s lists and non sequiturs expose the absurdity of modern life from the inside.

title: Feet of Clay
description: A woozy, raw, magical, and extremely short album from hip-hop’s most tantalizingly inscrutable rapper.

title: Saints and Sebastian Stories
description: Combining folk instrumentation and found sound, the Norwegian duo’s debut fosters a sense of familiarity, even when the music meanders.

title: GOTH ANGEL SINNER EP
description: These three tracks come from the last project the beloved emo rapper worked on before he died. They remind us how good he was, but don’t yield new insights.

title: Inside Unsolved EP
description: The Montreal producer pays tribute to the classic sound of two bygone Canadian techno labels, yielding some of the liveliest music in his catalog yet.

title: Monster (25th Anniversary Edition)
description: R.E.M.’s long misunderstood 1994 album isn’t clarified by the bonus material on this new reissue, but the original songs remain strangely oblique, full of glam rock poses and sly subterfuge.

title: Altogether
description: The Virginia emo trio try to keep things as simple and accessible as possible on their fourth album.

title: Let’s Get Free
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Dead Prez’s debut, an iconoclastic rap record built around the politics of liberation.

title: Spring
description: Los Angeles folk musician Kayla Cohen turns a two-month spell in the New Mexico desert into a meditation on place, nature, and the passage of time.

artist: The World Is a Beautiful Place & I Am No Longer Afraid to Die
title: Assorted Works
description: This compilation of rarities shows the beloved emo band growing into their status as a generational voice.

title: Kiwanuka
description: The London singer-songwriter's Danger Mouse and Inflo-produced latest feels like an easy listen at first, but eventually reveals its mournful and even despairing heart.

title: Wildcard
description: With her seventh album, the country star cheerfully exposes her sometimes-chaotic inner life, wearing her heart on her sleeve as she reaches for another shot of tequila.

title: Thanks to You
description: The indie-pop band’s first album in 13 years summons the same mix of erudition, introspection, and intense emotion that has inspired cult-like devotion since the late 1990s.

title: ISS004
description: Continuing his run of dancefloor-focused records, the German breakbeat specialist tilts his rearview mirror toward grime’s nascent stage.

title: Respires
description: The New York musician’s trance-inducing studies for drums and voice, breath and heartbeat, are laid bare as the sources of all expression.

title: Seeker
description: For his fourth solo album, the southern California rocker retreated to a cabin and wrote songs full of doubt and existential anxiety.

title: Three Chords and the Truth
description: On his 41st album, Van Morrison splits the difference between nostalgia, impassioned gripes, and spiritual yearning.

title: GUV II
description: On a new double album from his indie-pop project, Fucked Up guitarist Ben Cook cycles through dozens of styles without losing sight of the primacy of the song.

title: Underground / Loverboy / Odditties Sodomies Vol. 2
description: A new “definitive” reissue series begins with the bedroom artist’s earliest Haunted Graffiti records, which now sound more prescient and ghostly than ever.

title: Days B4 III
description: The Chicago rapper reflects on a bleak personal year and starts to recapture the optimism of his earlier music.

title: a tangle of stars
description: In their duo debut, these guitarists step outside of free jazz and indie rock to offer a dozen surprisingly accessible and warm instrumentals.

title: Colorado
description: Young’s fourth album of the century with his most famous band is simple and heartfelt, gritty and tender.

title: Four of Arrows
description: The indie rock quintet’s second album is more spacious, folksy, and adroit, centering on the evocative voice of lead singer Alex Menne.

title: Jesus Is King
description: Christianity is the unwavering focus of Kanye’s gospel album, a richly produced but largely flawed record about one man’s love of the Lord (and himself).

title: Sleepmoss
description: Field recordings and ambient synthesizers combine to paint an evocative picture of the English countryside and its natural cycles of rot and rebirth.

title: Pyroclasts
description: Recorded in the same sessions as April’s excellent Life Metal, the drone metal band’s new album is a rich, fundamentally life-affirming experience.

title: Hello, I’m Doing My Best
description: With frank lyricism and clean production, the Australian songwriter and guitarist channels the confidence and immediacy of 2000s pop-rock.

title: Cry
description: Greg Gonzalez has a lovely voice and a convincingly atmospheric take on dream pop, neither of which is well served by his two-dimensional fantasies.
Clocking in at almost 100 minutes, the Italian producer’s latest is a muted effort that was originally designed as a sound installation for a bridge in Rome.

title: Cheap Queen
description: The viral phenom’s full-length debut cuts her modern pop sensibility with doses of historicism, embracing opposing energies with effortless swagger.

title: (GI)
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Germs’ (GI), a touchstone of California punk.

title: Trinity
description: A mixtape made with half a dozen New York producers tilts the experimental producer’s left-field tendencies toward full-on dance music, but her signature oblique vocals remain a slippery presence.

title: Surviving
description: The beloved Arizona emo band’s latest is a solid, self-aware effort, missing only a few risks.

title: Tremble Under Boom Lights
description: While fame and fortune may’ve eluded them, the before-their-time New York City rockers’ influence is incalculable. Two decades on, their 1996 mini-LP sounds like a hiccup in the timeline.

title: Nicole Kidman / Anne Hathaway
description: The 19-year-old singer-songwriter’s dual EP branches out from bedroom pop in a set of songs that consider the nuanced ways acting is tucked into our everyday lives.

title: Pony
description: The 21-year-old songwriter’s latest album is irritating enough to activate the mildest allergy to sincerity.

title: The Decalogue
description: This score for Justin Peck’s 2017 ballet, performed by the pianist Timo Andres, is a knotty but welcome addition to the singer-songwriter’s growing set of compositions for dance.

title: Hometown: Detroit Sessions 1990​-​2014
description: A document of the Detroit jazz collective’s later years captures a cast of dozens balancing local community with cultural staying power.

title: Bigger Than Life
description: The synth-pop act’s third album, a rumination on loneliness in L.A., is its cleanest and most melodic, uncovering a previously obscured accessibility.

title: Woptober II
description: The Atlanta legend’s latest continues his consistent streak of mostly-good, sometimes-awkward new material.

title: Mechanical Fantasy Box
description: Accompanied by a newly published journal, this collection of synth odds and ends offers the rare opportunity to hear directly from an undersung icon of San Francisco’s gay disco scene.

title: Anicca
description: Mtendere Mandowa, a veteran (and cult favorite) of the L.A. beat scene, gathers fresh collaborators for a set of effortless, shape-shifting tracks that make time stand still.

title: Everything Not Saved Will Be Lost Part 2
description: The English band’s second album this year isn’t a complement to its predecessor so much as just another iteration on a now-standard formula.

title: Dusty
description: The Queens rapper’s ninth album is full of the dizzyingly technical wordplay he’s made his trademark.

title: The Order of Nature
description: The My Morning Jacket frontman collaborates with his hometown orchestra on a spiritual set of covers and originals over symphonic arrangements.

title: Coconut Grove
description: After years of kicking against dance music’s strictures, Daniel Martin McCormick delivers something close to a pure techno album. A product of turmoil, it’s a satisfyingly confident statement.

title: AXIS
description: The self-described “mutant” reps the New York underground at its freakiest on a fast-past, collage-heavy album of club rhythms, noise blasts, and unsettling humor.

title: Coin Coin Chapter Four: Memphis
description: In the fourth volume of a proposed 12-part suite, the saxophonist fuses free jazz and folk spirituals into an ecstatic confrontation with American history at its darkest.

title: All Encores
description: The adventurous musician and composer takes a step back toward a simpler, sparer sound.

title: You Deserve Love
description: With harmonized guitars, spring-loaded rhythms, and snotty hooks, the Louisville band’s major-label debut is a well-earned success that doesn’t quite feel like a triumph.

title: Juice B Crypts
description: Now down to a duo, the busy instrumentalists recruit Tune-Yards, Shabazz Palaces, and the singer of Yes for their aggressive fourth album.

title: There Existed an Addiction to Blood
description: Despite being based on a ’70s vampire film, the rap trio’s album is somehow their most bloodless project to date.

title: Crush
description: After a run of dates playing “obtuse, strange” music as a warm-up act for the xx, Sam Shepherd translates that experimental energy to an album of mischievous, melodic, stripped-down electronic music.

title: Deborah
description: The Montreal synth-pop duo explore an alternate ’80s where ethereal, post-goth dream pop sounds almost indistinguishable from lush, adult-contemporary soft rock.

title: Beauty and the Beat
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the debut album by the Go-Go’s, a ’70s punk band that beat the odds to become ’80s pop superstars.

title: Lasakaneku / Tomo
description: The Kenyan producer occupies his own switchbacking lane, blending global bass music and regional African rhythms with bits of grime, trap, and drum’n’bass.

title: Use Hearing Protection
description: A new box set of the legendary post-punk label’s first two years gathers chestnuts from Joy Division and the Durutti Column alongside rarities, oddities, dead ends, and some stunning graphic design.

title: Vagabon
description: On her self-titled sophomore effort, Laetitia Tamko leaps with both feet into new sounds and new horizons.

title: Pang
description: The former Chairlift singer-songwriter centers her sweeping solo debut on her powerful voice, crafting love songs about the moment of surrender, the pain preceding it, and the euphoria after.

title: Heavy Lifter
description: The duo’s third album is a nostalgic indie-pop rumination on suburban teenhood that thrums with hopeful energy. The best songs are like dispatches from a cracking cocoon.

title: No Holiday
description: The final album from the punk trio captures everything that was bratty, tender, and unforgettable about its leading force, Kim Shattuck, who passed away earlier this year.

title: Screamer
description: On the band’s sixth album, frontman Stephan Jenkins Peter Pans his way through an improbably infectious set of would-be hits.

title: As If It Were Forever
description: The idiosyncratic singer mixes R&B, ambient, and acoustic soul on her most accessible and fully-formed record, one that still feels like an open mic.

title: Dawn Chorus
description: Pushing beyond his customary dancefloor focus, the French-Canadian producer twists club influences and collaborative input into a textured, exploratory sound, both intimate and immense.
On his dense but meticulously rendered new album, the British folk singer uses grander pop arrangements to wade into the barbarism of modern life.

title: Singles Too
description: One of indie rock’s more consistent guitar bands charts its evolution with a career-spanning collection of non-album singles, B-sides, and cover songs.

title: Metal Galaxy
description: After fusing J-Pop and heavy metal to great fanfare, the duo recruit international guests to expand their sound into even more unlikely hybrids.

title: Neighborhoods
description: A newly reissued private-press curio from 1975 captures the bygone sounds of daily life in Portland, Oregon, in dreamy, proto-ambient form.

title: My Diary
description: The Pittsburgh-based producer makes undeniably heavy music, combining hardcore techno, drum’n’bass, and footwork and sprinkling it with a bit of frivolity and chaos.

title: Broken
description: The prolific Maryland rapper is alternately serious, silly, and soulful.

title: Blood Dust
description: Malcom Lacey’s long-running electro-acoustic project feels like a window into someone’s private world.

title: The Ra(w) Material
description: Two figures of underground rap—Philly’s Sadhugold and Virginia’s Ohbliv—team up for a politically blunted, cult rap record in the making.

title: True Love
description: With his intense baritone voice, Devon Welsh travels deep into the feelings of isolation and introspection with grace and beauty.

title: Let the Sun Talk
description: The latest tape from the 20-year-old rapper is dense and mystic. MAVI delivers revelations from the shadows, concealed and mysterious, in search of fresh air and sunlight.

title: FLY or DIE II: bird dogs of paradise
description: The New York trumpeter and bandleader’s second album is darker, denser, and more experimental than its predecessor, but no less resonant.

title: No Home Record
description: After 38 years of making music, Kim Gordon’s thrilling solo debut lives at the vanguard of sound and performance, shot through with the beautiful, unsparing noise that has always defined her art.

title: True 2 Myself
description: The breakout NY rapper’s emotionally affecting, piano-heavy street tales start to run together at 17 tracks.

title: My Star
description: Chicago’s least-relaxed band doubles their personnel and scales up their sound for a set of unnerving new wave.

title: For Your Pleasure
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Bryan Ferry and Brian Eno’s glam-rock, art-school masterpiece.

title: Closer to Grey
description: Chromatics set their surprise “seventh” album at the witching hour, telling a sometimes-muddled tale of heartbroken lovers reaching out to the spirit realm.

title: Sonic Citadel
description: The noise duo’s seventh album is the most life-affirming and accessible music they’ve ever made.

title: Movimiento Para Cambio
description: Velvety, ’90s-inspired deep house and industrial-punk sing-shouting make for a surprisingly complementary contrast.

title: Two Hands
description: The second landmark album this year from Big Thief is raw, tactile, and essential. The intimate songs zoom in on a band that feels, at this moment, totally invincible.

title: Odds Against Tomorrow
description: Stepping away from the overt historicism of previous recordings, the guitarist opts for a subtler—but just as expressive—investigation of folk and blues.

title: Terror Management
description: On his bleak new album, woods doubles down on the misery that snakes through all his music.

title: On a Clear Day I Can See You Forever
description: The Scandinavian synthesizer maven pays dusts off dozens of arcane vintage machines in an all-hardware studio recording meant to summon the spirit of bygone circuitry.

title: Phantom Rhythm 幽靈節奏 (幽霊リズム)
description: The Beijing-based post-punk duo stack garage instrumentation, Ali Farka Touré melodies, and dissonance without a whiff of the baroque.

title: Tell All Your Friends
description: The newly reissued landmark debut from the Amityville emo band takes heartbreak, jealousy, and depression to an operatic intensity, but does so with sharp wit, a knowing wink, and oh so many hooks.

title: Old LP
description: The ’90s alt-rockers’ first new album in more than 20 years has the vibe of a beloved record that was, for whatever reason, sitting on a shelf.

title: Hello Exile
description: What does it mean to get older in punk? Were the good old days ever that good? Though the titles change, the Pennsylvania band’s song remains the same.

title: Signal
description: The trio’s debut is an exercise in post-punk and no-wave galvanism crafted from throbbing bass, tight-zipped drumbeats, and buzzing synths.

title: Ghosteen
description: Forty years into his career, Nick Cave emerges with one of his most powerful albums yet, an endlessly giving and complex meditation on mortality and our collective grief.

title: Fuck Yo Feelings
description: Throwing open his studio doors, the pianist aims for a loose, mixtape-like vibe, but the stacked guest list yields a scattershot party that only ends up overstaying its own welcome.

title: Over It
description: The 23-year-old Atlanta singer’s slow-groove R&B plays out like a telenovela, feeling irresistibly fresh, messy, and human.

title: Look Up Sharp
description: The Australian multi-instrumentalist and songwriter’s second album finds a home in the shadowy space between post-punk, trip-hop, and lo-fi folk.

title: Deceiver
description: The shoegaze band’s third album is another portrait of addiction and recovery, but this time there’s no suggestion of a victory lap. The lyrics may wallow, but the music soars.

title: Diatom Ribbons
description: Aided by Nels Cline, Marc Ribot, and Esperanza Spalding, the New York pianist and her band mix lyrical song form, turntablism, and avant-garde strategies in unusually fluid fashion.

title: Ode to Joy
description: Wilco’s 11th album is direct and spacious, centering on the beauty of quiet revelation.

title: uknowhatimsayin¿
description: On his fifth album, executive-produced by Q-Tip, Danny Brown ascends to a sort of hip-hop classicist nirvana and remains one of the most inventive and dimensional rappers working today.

title: The Third Ascension
description: The celebrated avant-garde composer’s final work is a shrine to ecstatic disorientation.

title: Carnage Hall
description: Building atop a wobbly foundation of post-punk totems, the Glaswegian sextet make complicated songs sound fun.

title: So Removed
description: The Queens band Wives channel the bygone squalor of NYC’s Y2K rock renaissance.

title: Room for Squares
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the auspicious debut that sent a 23-year-old guitarist into the stratosphere.

title: Make Yourself at Home
description: The 20-year-old singer-songwriter’s clear vocals and candid lyrics feel at home in the Philadelphia DIY scene that raised her.

title: Moments
description: The New York-based composer’s third album spotlights piano and vibraphone, as attuned to the notes struck as to the overtones produced and their natural decay.

title: The Unluccy Luccy Kid
description: The Brooklyn drill artist follows up his two-year-old hit “No Suburban” with a grim and terse debut LP.

title: All Mirrors
description: The breathtaking songs of Angel Olsen’s fifth album are fleshed out by a 12-piece string section and deliver grand gestures about romance, authenticity, and being simply at the mercy of how we feel.
After nearly breaking up and instead making their best album in years, the once-restless Japanese trio become something new again: self-satisfied.

title: Abundance Welcoming Ghosts
description: Animated with a new intensity, the Cornwall band’s fifth album may be its most ingenious and immersive mix of folk and rock yet.

title: Losing, Linda
description: On her alluring and unnerving new album, the Melbourne singer-songwriter adopts a digital alter-ego to explore real-life human strife.

title: Love From the Planet Gong: The Virgin Years 1973-75
description: A mammoth box set of Daevid Allen’s prog-rock project makes a virtue of its excesses, capturing the band’s monumental strangeness.

title: Terms of Surrender
description: Working without his longtime collaborator Scott Hirsch, M.C. Taylor enlists guests Jenny Lewis and Aaron Dessner as he explores the heaviest questions and realizes there are no answers.

title: The Afterlife
description: The cosmic fusion group skewers the jazz-trio format as it’s typically understood, flipping the minimalist palette into an electrifying, apocalyptic sound.

title: Herstory in the Making
description: The New York rapper’s highly anticipated debut album is another big, long flex from one of the most skilled rappers to emerge in the last five years.

title: KIRK
description: The Charlotte, North Carolina rapper's debut finds him in his sweet spot—which is to say, demolition mode.

title: I’M HIM
description: The follow up to 2016's revelatory Islah offers another showcase for the Baton Rouge rapper's fully formed and gloriously weird personality.

title: In the Morse Code of Brake Lights
description: Though a sense of doom lurks at the heart of the venerable band’s eighth album, they remain determined to keep classic guitar-pop alive by slyly twisting and expanding the form.

title: The Adornment of Time
description: A live recording from New York’s the Kitchen captures a rare kind of improv synergy between the versatile composer-percussionist and a pianist who rose to fame in Anthony Braxton’s quartet.

title: Prison on a Hill
description: The Boston rockers’ third album wears its radicalism with confidence, and the untimely death of the band’s guitarist lends their late-capitalist protest unfortunate urgency.

title: SOUND & FURY
description: The fourth album from the country outlaw is another left-turn with synth-rock at its scuzziest, boogie-rock at its cheesiest, all held together by Simpson’s fearless songwriting.

title: Dreams Are Not Enough
description: The electronic outfit’s exquisitely bleak new record, the first since bandmate Charlie Cooper passed away, often feels like the very stuff of music is being torn apart.

title: Legendary Member
description: The Thailand-born and Sweden-raised rapper offers a dreamy, melancholic, and abstracted take on mumble rap.

title: Blue World
description: Long-lost soundtrack recordings by the saxophonist’s powerhouse quartet, made shortly after 1964’s Crescent sessions, capture the band at the peak of its cohesion.

title: Face to Phase
description: The Berlin producer is unafraid to throw a wrench into her steady grooves, and her latest disregards clubland’s status quo for more imaginative terrain.

title: Reservoir 1: Preservation
description: Assisted by the pianist Phillip Bush and her colleagues in the percussion ensemble Meridian, the American composer tests conventional notions of musical narrative.

title: Weeping Icon
description: The Brooklyn band skewers our collective relationship with social media—as well as their own—in noisy punk thrashers that are clever, incisive, and frequently very funny.

title: Gold: Greatest Hits
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit an essential greatest hits album, one that brought ABBA indefinite fame.

title: NINE
description: The shiny, beat-heavy sound of nu-blink-182 works in starts and stops, but feels half as fun as the band used to be.
The genial Louisville rapper doesn’t have much of an identity, but he has a natural, low-stakes charm.

title: Swoon / From Langley Park to Memphis / Jordan: The Comeback / A Life of Surprises
description: Four new vinyl reissues offer a thrilling survey of Paddy McAloon’s idiosyncratic journey as a pop songwriter.

title: Chastity Belt
description: They’ve abandoned the crude wit of their debut, but the Seattle band’s fourth album still maintains the closeness of hanging out with friends in your living room.

title: The Talkies
