description: The Italian synthesizer composer explores new dimensions of her algorithmic, arpeggiated sound, playing with tempo, duration, and pacing to toy with listeners’ sense of perception.

title: STFU II EP
description: Picking up where his DJ-Kicks mix left off, the L.A. funk auteur’s newest release explores peace and love through body-rock.

title: We Fall
description: On her debut solo album, the Breeders’ original bassist blends her signature instrument with minimalist electronics and rippling pools of piano, Mellotron, and acoustic guitar.

title: Fever
description: Megan Thee Stallion’s debut is steeped in sex, pimpin, and power; it sounds like a once and future Houston rap classic.

title: Father of Asahd
description: DJ Khaled has ranged from summertime hitmaker to self-help guru, and neither are all that interesting on his latest guest-filled album. There are plenty of voices but no clear message or intention.

title: Injury Reserve
description: The oddball Phoenix rap trio traffic in wild, boundary-pushing production and playfully anarchic bars.

title: A Fine Mess EP
description: Culled from last year’s Marauder sessions with Dave Fridmann, there’s still a sense that the production actively tries to disrupt what Interpol does well.

title: Radiant Dawn
description: Crosswiring ’80s-Springsteen valor with contemporaneous synth pop, the second album from Dan Boeckner’s disco power trio channels the crushing fear of imminent collapse.

title: Galazy EP
description: On the first release on his new label Young Ethics, the Swedish producer steps outside his hazy comfort zone.

title: 13th Floor
description: With hard-nosed bars and ominous beats, the Canadian rapper’s debut is her most cohesive and narratively ambitious project to date.

title: I Am the Last of That Green and Warm-Hued World
description: Within an album that often sounds like an alien world, small moments of familiarity become breadcrumbs leading to a shared musicology.

title: Nothing Great About Britain
description: The Bajan-British rapper’s debut tackles the UK’s pressing crises—a looming Brexit, class hostility, widening poverty—with great jokes and writerly candor.

title: Origin EP
description: The New York pianist’s stripped-back companion piece to her electronic-tinged 2018 album Ultraviolet is an engrossing ode to the act of creation.

title: Living Theatre
description: The Brooklyn group’s second album frames heavy questions in lovely, deceptively serene psych rock.

title: Igor
description: Tyler, the Creator’s sixth album is impressionistic and emotionally charged, the result of an auteur refining his style and baring more of his soul than ever before.

title: Pacific Breeze: Japanese City Pop, AOR & Boogie 1976-1986
description: This compilation of extra smooth, funky, and sometimes very odd songs from the heydey of Japan’s technological boom is a broad yet nuanced introduction to the genre of city pop.

title: Spice
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the sleek pop, British nationalism, and commercial girl power of the Spice Girls’ debut.

title: Le personnage principal est un peuple isolé
description: STROOM, a Belgian label whose releases are not so much reissues as alternate histories of avant-garde pop, surveys the dreamlike soundscapes of a fringe figure from the 1980s.

title: Natty Light
description: This collection of 7"s and compilation tracks documents the band’s formative years, in which frenzied hardcore and proto-screamo was rapidly churning toward more radical strains of noise.

title: The Movie
description: The Gothenburg emo band specialize in commiseration rock, crafting combustible rallying cries for the overwhelmed and underemployed.

title: Spirit
description: Playing a baby grand piano, Mike Milosh’s eight-song album reflects a sense of ritualistic quiet; it’s intimate without being heavy-handed.

title: The Best of Luck Club
description: The Australian pop-punk musician’s second album is a welcome and wide-open look at mid-twenties inertia and queer romance.

title: Sombrou Dúvida
description: The Brazilian psych band transition from the oft-playful homage and stage-ready jams of previous releases to a serious attempt at tight, kaleidoscopic grooves.

title: Dedicated
description: On her fourth album, the Canadian pop star is doing what she does best, calibrating lovesick or lovelorn synthpop that’s neither too hot nor too cold—and sometimes, regrettably, only lukewarm.

title: Ryan Pollie
description: The L.A.-based singer-songwriter recorded the first album under his own name from the trenches of chemotherapy and a breakup, but the result is an exercise in gentle vulnerability and winsome grace.

title: Matchy Matchy
description: With their first album in six years, New York City indie-pop duo the Ballet question the complexities of modern queer life but offer no easy answers.

title: Beauty Marks
description: The singer’s seventh album moves between frothy pop-R&B and stale empowerment anthems that leave her talents largely underused.

title: Water
description: The Chicago indie-rock trio scrape away 90 percent of what goes into a guitar album and come away with something effortless and uncomplicated.

title: Sings Music for Daydreaming
description: Sam Cook-Parrott returns to his beginnings as a solo artist, an experiment that yields playful piano compositions and introspective lyricism.

title: I Am Easy to Find
description: With a cast of female vocalists guiding and redirecting the songs, the National’s eighth album is their largest, longest, and most daring.

title: Shea Butter Baby
description: The debut album from the neo-soul singer-songwriter is driven by warm funk and soul and has the healing familiarity of hanging out on the couch commiserating with a best friend.

title: LEGACY! LEGACY!
description: The Chicago artist marries political commentary with deep introspection, resulting in a richly composed R&B album about the echoes of the past and the promise of the future.
The Memphis post-punk band’s third album wages guerrilla warfare against the patriarchal surveillance state.

title: Age Hasn’t Spoiled You
description: On their first new album in three years, the Toronto punk band tear down everything they’ve ever known about making music and rebuild themselves for the better.

title: PROTO
description: Created with a choral ensemble and a nascent AI, the Berlin-based electronic musician’s third album is a meditation on community, technology, and the future of, and beyond, the human species.

title: Hexhammaren
description: Eighteen years into its existence, the Swedish band continues to find ways to make a familiar fusion of melodic death metal, crust punk, and d-beat sound fresh.

title: Divided by Darkness
description: Led by young oracle Nate Garrett, the second album from the Arizona heavy metal band carries the torch of their forebears and revives the genre with impressive songwriting and ambition.

title: Young Enough
description: The Brooklyn band’s second record is bigger and darker, amplifying their ’80s new-wave sparkle into ecstatic triumph.

title: Wheeltappers and Shunters
description: The art-punk eccentrics’ first album in six years is a woozy celebration of Britain’s sleazy past, and it sounds like nobody other than Clinic.

title: LOVE&JETT
description: On their 13th album, the Japanese rock’n’rollers reaffirm what they do best: making the once-rebellious sounds of surf, rockabilly, and CBGB punk seem dangerous again.

title: Phantom Forest
description: The ever-ambitious Toronto composer tackles big themes on her environmentally minded song cycle, but keeps things refreshingly immediate and small-scale.

title: Stolen Youth
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Mac Miller and Vince Staples’ 2013 mixtape, a fledgling but important document of freeform creativity.

title: DOLO 4
description: The Washington D.C. producer’s drum tracks are bold, burly numbers that move with abandon. Even without melodies, no two sound remotely alike.

title: are SING SINCK, SING
description: This joint project from Efrim Manuel Menuck and Kevin Doria has an overwhelming radiance to match Menuck's work in Godspeed You! Black Emperor.

title: Failed Entertainment
description: The O.C. hardcore band level up their sound on their second album but remain gruff, guttural, and ferocious.

title: Emerald Valley
description: The second album from Corin Tucker and Peter Buck’s alt-rock supergroup can’t match the urgency of pre-apocalyptic protest.

title: Here Comes the Cowboy
description: The latest from the indie rock rapscallion is an often pretty, occasionally frustrating record that was recorded quickly, but still sounds labored over.

title: Eat My Pussy Again
description: On the sequel to last year’s Eat My Pussy, the Chicago rapper’s songwriting is at times more brazen and at others more introspective.

title: Anoyo
description: The follow-up to last year’s Konoyo—recorded, like its predecessor, with a Japanese gagaku ensemble—functions as a counterbalance to that album: a kind of photo negative, more subdued but no less overwhelming.

title: A Thousand Leaves
description: After a string of surprisingly and contentiously accessible albums, SY attempted to balance their pop curiosity with its experimental instincts.

title: EVOL
description: The core elements of Sonic Youth were still scattered all over their 1986 album, but its dark and sordid sound brilliantly captured the essence of an “underground” band coming to life.

title: Experimental Jet Set, Trash and No Star
description: Somewhere between a sorta-pop stab and pointedly hook-free, SY’s eighth album is ambivalent and shaggy by design.

title: Sister
description: At turns paranoid and explosive, Sister marks a climactic finish to the early albums that carved the New York band’s sound into punk and alternative culture.

title: Washing Machine
description: SY’s ninth record marked a new era for the band. While they didn’t leave the freaky stuff behind entirely, they started serving it up with a spoonful of sugar.

title: The Dots
description: The English six-piece’s debut is a high-wire act combining jazz fusion, disco rhythms, and high-gloss art rock.

title: KOD
description: The BandGang crew is at the center of Detroit’s rap renaissance, and Lonnie Bands’ latest is a great showcase of its sound and energy.

title: Poltergeist Slim
description: The Baltimore rapper switches between singing, rapping, mumbling until there's almost no difference between the words and the beats.

title: there is no Other
description: The singer and multi-instrumentalist joins jazz musician Francesco Turrisi for a thoughtful and ambitious album that spans opera, Appalachian bluegrass, gospel, and traditional Italian music.

title: Sli’merre
description: On one of the best rapper/producer collaborations of the year, the Atlanta MC remains a perfect fit for Pi’erre Bourne’s weird and heavy beats.

title: Enderness
description: On his first album in eight years, the Alabama singer-songwriter turns from folk music to synths, drum machines, and internet speak, but the sorrow at the heart of his music is timeless.

title: Active Listening: Night on Earth
description: The Philadelphia quartet’s full-length debut showcases their defiant brand of noise-pop, a big rainbow of chaos.

title: YU
description: The smoky-voiced R&B multi-instrumentalist charts the ups and downs of a relationship with the help of guests like Jay Electronica and Floating Points.

title: Voicemails
description: The Chicago singer/rapper known for her diaristic, relationship-dissecting R&B builds her new mixtape around inherently private and frequently drama-filled voice messages.

title: U.F.O.F.
description: The third album from the Brooklyn quartet is an intimate and surreal experience, a true masterpiece of folk music from a band working together at the highest level.

title: Useless Coordinates
description: The ferocious Leeds trio treat post-punk like a game of Tetris, joyfully flipping and rearranging the elements into new patterns.

title: Your Need
description: Crafted in tandem with the Gost Zvuk affiliate Flaty, the Moscow producer’s second album balances streamlined electro pop with a hint of rave mayhem.

title: This Mess Is a Place
description: The Seattle band’s fourth record, their first for Sub Pop, is forward-thinking pop-punk that successfully—albeit narrowly—manages to dodge the obvious pitfalls.

title: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit an album that changed ambient music forever.

title: KingMaker
description: The 23-year-old vibraphonist shines on his debut album with an approach that feels sly and mysterious; he also proves himself a sharp bandleader attuned to the importance of group dynamics.

title: Night Pass
description: After being dropped from their label, the Portland duo flout despair with a wall of nostalgic, over-the-top sound.

title: Anger Management
description: Just 18 minutes with Kenny Beats shows Rico Nasty evolving. She remains one of the heaviest hitters in the no-rules arena of rap.

title: Covered N Blood
description: As with all of his best work, the D.C. rapper’s latest finds him grappling with trauma, haunted by the specter of death at every turn.

title: Scatter the Rats
description: The grunge act's first LP in 20 years fails to summon the revolutionary fire that made them such a force of nature in the mid-'90s.

title: Violet Street
description: The L.A. band has long carried the flag for a particular strain of SoCal indie, but the follow-up to 2016’s fashionably yearning Sunlit Youth sounds both more personal and more timeless.

title: Preacher to the Streets
description: The Sacramento rapper spends most of his second album conscience-stricken, trying to explain the difference between being immoral and being corrupted.

title: Green and Gray
description: The seventh album from the Boston noise-rock band revels in a heightened level of studio ambition without losing its snarling ferocity.

title: Father of the Bride
description: Vampire Weekend return with a shaggy, sprawling double album all about rebirth, contentment, and the reclamation of light.

title: Music for Donuts EP
description: The Mississippi punk four-piece celebrate slugs, butter, lard, chewing gum—the important things.

title: ARIZONA BABY
description: The BROCKHAMPTON star’s latest solo album is an often powerful document by a queer artist who has weathered life’s bruises.

title: Run Fast Sleep Naked
description: The second album from the musician formerly known as Chet Faker is at once overstuffed and underwhelming.

title: Mettavolution
description: The Mexican duo’s first album in five years applies their customary virtuoso fusion of classical guitar and contemporary rock to six short originals and a 19-minute cover of Pink Floyd’s “Echoes.”

title: What Life
description: The Oakland quintet’s debut album is a spirited indie-emo blend driven by intricate underlying themes, channeling a slew of influences even as it exists in a space of its own.

title: Take Off Mode
description: As he returns to the intricate polyrhythms and hypnotic vocal chops of footwork, the Chicago producer’s approach remains almost single-minded in its focus.

title: LuvHz
description: The Mexican American electro-pop artist’s debut EP, produced with Panda Bear collaborator Rusty Santos, is a restless patchwork of genre-smashing sounds.

title: Oh My God
description: Morby's spare fifth solo album conjures memories of gospel-phase Dylan.

title: Organism EP
description: The Chicago producer plays with oceanic imagery and a collage-like swirl of influences on a four-track EP that spills over the limits of club music’s conventions.

title: You Can't Sit With Us
description: On their first project in five years, Saba's crew sounds like a bunch of friends at the lunch table trying to out-rap each other for fun.

title: CrasH Talk
description: The L.A. rapper’s latest is comforting if not entirely exciting. It finds Q and host of guests in a good place with nothing to prove.

title: In League With Dragons
description: John Darnielle explores the humanity of wizards, sports legends, Ozzy Osbourne, and other folk heroes and beacons of hope.

title: I Need a New War
description: The Hold Steady frontman's solo work continues its twilit exploration of frail hopes, wasted lives, and quiet battles against despair.

title: Love + Fear
description: Marina Diamandis’ first album since shedding her “Marina and the Diamonds” identity slides from affecting poetry to cold calculation.

title: Itekoma Hits
description: The Kyoto punk quartet unleashes a tornado of defiance at the prospect of romance, monotonous office work, and people who feel entitled to women’s time.

title: For the Throne (Music Inspired by the HBO Series Game of Thrones)
description: Instead of nerding out or having any kind of fun, a host of pop stars turn in a dour, stone-faced compilation inspired by the ubiquitous fantasy saga.

title: The Jewel in the Lotus
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a confluence of jazz’s past and present, an unsung modernist classic from 1974.

title: Seeing Other People
description: The troubled outfit's latest album bitterly recounts the Decline of Foxygen.

title: The Secret of Letting Go
description: The veteran trip-hoppers once stood out by virtue of their idiosyncratic sound, but two decades later, they’ve resorted to playing things frustratingly straight.

title: Exit
description: Always one for gender subversion, the Toronto songwriter invites a cast of men to sing her songs, resulting in some of the project’s most deviously playful music ever.

title: Fly Times, Vol. 1: The Good Fly Young
description: One of the most quietly influential rappers of the last ten years maintains cruising altitude.

title: Designer
description: The third album from the impressionistic New Zealand singer-songwriter eludes easy classification, which makes her delicately built and beautifully rendered songs all the more alluring.

title: Truck Music
description: Christopher Taylor’s genre-colliding mutant pop proves everything can fit if you don’t give it enough time to sound wrong.

title: Blood
description: Featuring collaborations with Skrillex and Jamie xx, the West Coast transplant’s debut album flips the chamber-folk cello of her debut EP into a contemporary, decidedly Los Angeles hybrid sound.

title: Fishing for Fishies
description: The idiosyncratic Australian band’s most streamlined album to date is risky only in that it is their first to be downright boring.

title: 2nd
description: The Queens-based songwriter offers nervy lo-fi synth pop that buzzes with everyday anxiety.

title: Jade Bird
description: The British singer-songwriter’s debut fortifies her early promise as a confident young voice of country-charred rock

title: A Quiet Farwell, Twenty Sixteen to Twenty Eighteen
description: The New York producer’s ambitious album is a dark, surreal, jazzy collage about resistance and hope.

title: Life Metal
description: The titanic drone metal duo returns with Steve Albini for an enormous, meticulous, back-to-basics album that shows just how compelling those basics can be.

title: Still Summer in the Projects
description: The incarcerated Watts rapper’s latest release, a collaboration with Mustard, is exultant and Dionysian.

title: Wooh Dang
description: The hermetic Swedish bedroom-pop auteur spins out songs of electric uplift and dreamy solitude on his first international release.

title: Internet Arms
description: On his third release as the genre-bending alter ego Diane Coffee, Shaun Fleming explores the trap of online intimacy.

title: Stockholm Marathon
description: The Swedish producer’s second full-length album is streaked with bright, bold melodies yet marked with a lightness of touch that’s unusual in dance music.

title: Absolute Zero
description: Jazz fusion, chamber pop, modern classical—if your awareness of Hornsby stops at the lite-FM radio dial, prepare to be disoriented.

title: Family Not a Group
description: The Bay Area rap crew’s collaboration with Hit-Boy catches them in a moment of furious flux.

title: I Love You. It’s a Fever Dream.
description: As he explores the banalities and oddities of tour, Kristian Matsson seeks answers to a bigger question: How best should he move through the landscape of his life?

title: Industrial Accident: The Story of Wax Trax! Records
description: The soundtrack to a documentary about the flagship indie label features early material from Ministry, My Life With the Thrill Kill Kult, and other industrial icons.

title: Covert Contracts
description: On their debut album, the anarchic Philly hardcore trio muster a raw, thrilling assault against complacency.

title: Raw Honey
description: L.A.-based auteur Michael Collins crafts a pristine portrait of early-’70s AM radio by taking inspiration not only from the period’s definitive artists, but its discarded pop detritus, too.

title: Cuz I Love You
description: The shiny soul-pop of Lizzo’s major label debut is something of a thesis on internalized and externalized confidence—so much so that the music can feel like a means to a greater end.

title: Akron, Ohio
description: The Black Keys’ Patrick Carney and longtime indie-rock journeyman John Petkovic team up on a graceless, unsubtle pastiche of rock’n’roll indulgence.

title: Floral Shoppe
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the banal ennui of vaporwave with its pioneering document from 2011.

title: ~~~ EP
description: The Los Angeles-based ambient musician’s EP is restful and restorative, using lo-fi tones and textures to create a work that subtly transcends.

title: Orange
description: The Pulitzer Prize-winning composer returns with a wild and free-ranging collection of chamber pieces.

title: Intellexual
description: The Social Experiment members reintroduce themselves as earnest singer-songwriters, but their post-genre mashup production produces more vibes than actual songs.

title: A Black Market Album
description: The Belgian beatmaker ups his game, roping in guest vocalists Siifu, Spote Breeze, and Mamoyo on a breezy, 22-minute album that, at its best, recalls golden-age Slum Village.

title: Homecoming: The Live Album
description: Beyoncé’s historic Coachella set is preserved as a stunning live album that captures an artist at her peak, flexing her catalog and shining a light on the genius of Black artists that came before her.

title: High Highs to Low Lows
description: Don’t be fooled by the of-the-moment pop sound: The 24-year-old singer’s debut album is the showcase for a refreshingly original perspective.

title: No Dados
description: The North Carolinian singer comes roaring back from multiple strokes to deliver a raw and thrilling solo debut.

title: Utopía
description: The Dominican bachata king follows his chart-topping Golden with a celebration of the genre's rich history, lifting up his forebears and revealing his musical DNA.

title: Grim Town
description: On her second album, the Northern Irish musician graduates from lonesome singer-songwriter to bold art-pop auteur; her growing confidence translates to emotionally probing songs of startling candor.

title: Let’s Try the After Vol. 2 EP
description: On the second half of their paired EPs, the Toronto collective settles into comfortable territory that soon proves stale.

title: Where Polly People Go to Read
description: The debut from the it-boy bedroom pop auteur manages to feel both excitingly personal and a bit disingenuous.

title: Invitation
description: Three albums in, the Oregon-based multi-instrumentalist still sounds as though she’s composing music en plein air.

title: Laughing Matter
description: As they pare away at their sound, Wand move further away from psych-rock and closer to true psychedelia.

title: Dogrel
description: The steely Dublin post-punk band infuse the bitterness and rage of The Fall with punch-drunk romanticism.

title: Rose Gold
description: With low-stakes dance-pop that simmers just beneath the surface, the artist formerly known as Kitty Pryde attempts to transcend her internet bubble.

title: I Must Be the Devil
description: The former múm frontwoman steps out with a set of airy, orchestral folk that resembles early Kate Bush or Joanna Newsom.

title: LSD
description: Diplo, Sia, and Labrinth combine forces for an album of truly forgettable pop music that is too tired to be wired.

title: Song Feel
description: Nearly a decade after helping revolutionize the sound of UK bass, the veteran Night Slugs producer struggles to maintain the radicalism of his early music on his debut album.

title: WARMER
description: Recorded at the same time as last year’s WARM, the companion album showcases Tweedy’s aged songwriting that continues to be humble and revealing.

title: Imperial Flood
description: A pioneer of what he once termed “weightless” bass music moves toward the outer fringes of club aesthetics on an album imbued with the apocalyptic overtones of sci-fi and speculative fiction.

title: Everybody Split
description: The unassuming Melbourne five-piece build garage-jangle guitars and blunt-edged harmonies into strangely hypnotic arrangements that feel simultaneously long and short.

title: MAP OF THE SOUL : PERSONA
description: The biggest K-pop group in the world try to move their sound forward but spend too much time leaning on their past.

title: All Time Present
description: Accompanied by a handful of his Solar Motel Band collaborators, the Philadelphia guitarist seeks the third path between classic-rock peaks and floating experimentalism.

title: Sulphur English
description: The Richmond metal quintet’s fourth album is its most intense and most rewarding: a virtual symphony of pummeling, dissonant riffs sculpted with unrelenting precision.

title: Mandatory Reality
description: The Chicago bassist and guimbri player turns in a minimalist mountain of an album, one whose slow pace and gradual changes prove unusually mesmerizing, even sublime.

title: Who Is Jill Scott?: Words and Sounds, Vol. 1
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the 2000 debut of Jill Scott, a neo-soul chronicle that brought love and sex to the everywoman.

title: El Chan
description: Indie rock’s preeminent classical composer offers a selection of piano pieces from minimal, to rousing, to a heroic concerto for two pianos backed by a full orchestra.

title: Only You Can See It
description: The Brooklyn-based pop polymath writes, performs, records, mixes, and engineers her most ambitious and electrifying collection of songs to date.

title: Personal Rock
description: Twenty years ago, the German electronic musician Jan Jelinek’s tools were rustier, his loops lumpier, yet his vision for a transcendent music of digital failure was very much intact.

title: Essentials
description: The Brooklyn post-punk trio’s debut full-length reveals an instinct for scrappy, empathetic songwriting.

title: Ventura
description: After the hard left turn of Oxnard, Paak sinks back into the bubbly smooth grooves that got him noticed.

title: Ribbons
description: After drifting into ambient drone on his last album, Stephen Wilkins returns to his chill, bucolic stomping grounds.

title: Long Story Short
description: With a nonchalant flow, Eto paints a grim and familiar world where only survival-of-the-fittest tactics prevail alongside sumptuous production from Superior.

title: No Geography
description: Blending psychedelic sensory overload with riotous club bangers, the shape-shifting electronic duo’s ninth album is their most entertaining in years.

title: Brutalism
description: The latest album from the Drums—now just frontman Jonny Pierce—is his most honest and most unvarnished.

title: Kill This Love EP
description: The K-pop girl group’s enjoyable but weirdly dated EP offers a mishmash of EDM styles ahead of their big Coachella debut.

title: Signals Bulletin
description: The German experimental musician teams up with a Japanese organist prone to taping down the keys of his instrument; together, they conjure massive, buzzing slabs of drone.

title: Even in the Tremor
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter’s third album takes a microscope to the messy business of being human, finding revelatory moments of empathy in the smallest everyday details.

title: What a Boost
description: Like a half-forgotten dream, the English singer-songwriter’s combination of minimalist blues and free-floating jazz feels just out of reach.

title: Just Another Gangsta
description: A decade-plus after splitting from Cash Money, Juvenile reunites with Birdman for a shockingly strong late-career-reunion record.

title: Pantame
description: The unclassifiable Spanish duo span 1990s-inspired alternative rock, glitching electronic percussion, mournful Andalusian flamenco, and the dread empty spaces of post-punk.

title: Free Spirit
description: The second album from the historically inoffensive singer is another genreless collection of safe choices for a pop star in the making.

title: Saturday the 14th EP
description: The Canadian power-pop duo take underappreciated micro-genres for a test drive in a bid to make music that’s as funny as their lyrics.

title: The Shape of Your Name
description: With a delivery as authentically conversational as her songwriting, the Toronto-based musician treats even the broadest themes on a person-to-person scale.

title: Haunted Items
description: Four short EPs from Greta Kline feature the singer-songwriter at a piano singing her detailed and deeply felt songs with newfound conviction.

title: وين كنيت بي ١١​/​٩؟? “Where Were You on 9​/​11​?​” EP
description: The New York agit-punks’ latest EP is another menacing, distorted call to arms.

title: Ambitions
description: The Norwegian producer rediscovers the simple joy in his space-disco sound on his most cohesive LP in years.

title: Hiding Places
description: On his bracing collaboration with L.A. producer Kenny Segal, woods gets painfully real about his fears, his doubts and irritations, and even his mortality.

title: The Seduction of Kansas
description: The Washington, D.C. band’s second album is dense with ambiguities, sacrificing their debut’s quotable one-liners in favor of character sketches about the everyday banality of evil.

title: Dog Whistle
description: The hardcore trio grapples with the ongoing death of their NYC home in their most cohesive work to date.

title: We Need to Talk
description: A songwriter best known for her work penning hits for Ariana Grande, Khalid, and Panic! At the Disco claims the spotlight for herself, but she struggles to define what makes her unique.

title: The Slider
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the peak of Marc Bolan’s career, the extravagant and near-perfect The Slider.

title: Autoclave
description: Mary Timony and Christina Billotte’s early band operated for less than two years, but the appeal of their jagged, math-rock-adjacent punk has lasted decades longer.

title: Natural Facts
description: The second album from these New Jersey-based Grateful Dead devotees is still indebted to familiar reference points, but finds the band pushing to expand.

title: Thalassa
description: The Io Echo singer’s debut solo album expands on the gothy, mythical undertones of her earlier work.

title: Deserted
description: The legendary band's first full-length in eight years is a besotted concept album about the desert, once again revealing the depth of their imagination.

title: Crackheads Live Longer Than Vegans
description: The prolific Chicago rapper’s recent project is his loosest, funniest, and most invigorating to date, full of hard left turns and sly wit.

title: In the Shape of a Storm
description: The singer-songwriter’s intimate 14th studio album strips down to spare acoustic guitar, lingering on the moments when the buzzing world around all but fades away.

title: Morbid Stuff
description: On their long-awaited follow-up to their breakthrough sophomore effort, the pop-punk band embraces the liberating power of anger.

title: Triad
description: On his second album with producer Palmistry, the elusive London vocalist delivers a surreal blend of singing, rapping, and voiceover narration.

title: Titanic Rising
description: Natalie Mering’s fourth album is a grand, sentimental ode to living and loving in the shadow of doom. It is her most ambitious and complex work yet.

title: Fucking Bliss
description: The album Sam Ray envisioned as his last begs close listening, but punctuated with impenetrable harshness, it is almost prohibitively scattered.

artist: Beth Gibbons / Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra / Krzysztof Penderecki
title: Henryk Górecki: Symphony No. 3 (Symphony of Sorrowful Songs)
description: The Portishead singer and conductor (and film-music icon) Krzysztof Penderecki deliver a surprisingly disquieting take on Henryk Górecki’s canonical symphony, a piece so familiar that it’s often taken for granted.

title: Spying Through a Keyhole
description: This assemblage of strange outtakes and demos—including what may be the first demo of "Space Oddity"—find Bowie in his tentative folkie phase, about to blast off.

title: Supermarket
description: From clumsy stadium rock to unacceptable ska, Logic’s overly ambitious album is a painful slog.

title: Lifelike
description: On their second release, the Disappears alums turn mercurial, whipping their habitual post-rock into more impressionistic, unpredictable forms.

title: The Big Freeze
description: On her fifth solo album, the New York musician both evolves as a singer-songwriter and grows in confidence, addressing heavy emotional themes with candor and grace.

title: You’re the Man
description: Recorded in 1972, this largely unreleased “lost” album is a fascinating glimpse into what one of the great 20th-century artists strategically allowed the culture to see.

title: Crux
description: The Long Island prog-metal band bursts with enthusiasm and rabid energy, as if Mastodon's apocalyptic visions were replaced with cosmic wonder.

title: Tuez-Les Tous
description: The cryptic and elusive New Jersey rapper teams with DJ Muggs, who is enjoying a career renaissance as the go-to producer for glowering, throwback East Coast street rap.

title: Agora
description: The experimental musician’s sweeping, ambient album works in small, fascinating ways from moment to moment but has a cumulative force that is unlike anything he’s done in years.

title: The State Between Us
description: The producer and DJ’s guest-packed “Brexit album” conjures a great sprawl of humor and tragedy that makes for Herbert’s richest album in years.

title: A Guide to Being a Partying Freshman
description: With its tinny mix, infectious chant raps, and Fruity Loops-style beats, this Texas dance rap king's debut has a refreshingly unforced charm.

title: English Rose
description: At turns soulful and spirited, the debut album from the British singer balances rabble-rousing political energy with a nonchalant chumminess.

title: Mise En Abyme
description: French-British producer Jean Cousin draws despair and wonder from within the vast unfeeling of digital communication.

title: Ilana (The Creator)
description: The Tuareg musician’s first full-band studio album is an incandescent set of guitar music with a spontaneous, celebratory air—and a latent urgency reflecting the region’s very real difficulties.

title: Guns
description: Quelle Chris examines how words, fear, and skin color are weaponized, and how one’s community can dictate their relationship to firearms.

title: Damita Jo
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Janet Jackson’s 2004 album, a lush and preeminently sex-positive album that deserves a reappraisal.

title: Late Night Tales
description: The UK DJ and producer taps the depths of his record collection in a gorgeous, moody mix that runs through ambient, jazz, psych pop, and vintage soul.

title: The Quanta Series
description: The Syrian American producer lingers with grief and horror on her past while the music accelerates into the future.

title: Deforming Lobes
description: Taken from a three-night stint in L.A. and recorded by Steve Albini, this live album disavows almost all the rules of the form.

title: Cruising OST
description: The soundtrack for William Friedkin's controversial and problematic 1980 thriller features a stunning array of hardcore punk and hard funk, including rare songs by the Germs.

title: When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?
description: The debut album from the meteoric pop star lives in a world of its own: gothic, bass-heavy, at turns daring and quite beautiful.

title: It's Real
description: The second album from Mary Timony's band suggests that the hard rock of debut Rips was no dalliance: This time, they mine the denim-clad AOR of Billy Squier and Foreigner.

title: Cosmic Wind
description: The second album from the singer/producer duo aims for laid-back but stalls out at sleepy.

title: Antidotes 1 EP
description: On her debut solo EP, the cellist and vocalist explores a vaporous middle ground between R&B and chamber pop.

title: The World Is Yours 2
description: The perpetual Atlanta B-lister sounds like a guest on his own albums, outshone by features from Gunna, Young Thug, Offset, Big Sean, and more.

title: Ancestral Recall
description: The New Orleans trumpeter and composer’s latest album continues to stretch the language of jazz, further embracing electronics and an increasingly broad approach to rhythm.

title: This (Is What I Wanted to Tell You)
description: Kurt Wagner uses restraint with a masterful touch on his latest record, applying a light vocodor touch to his voice to illuminate the intimacy of his understated songwriting.

title: New Rain Duets
description: On their collaborative record, Superchunk frontman Mac McCaughan and harpist Mary Lattimore lead each other through misty, evocative improvisations.

title: Bad Habits
description: The Punjabi-Canadian MC returns from his eight-week retirement with a droning collection of listless would-be bangers.

title: Cows on Hourglass Pond
description: Dave Portner’s latest solo excursion stakes out a middle ground between the exterior and interior, between direct melodies and the oblique music they float on.

title: Capsule Losing Contact
description: Duster’s debut was barely a blip on the radar—and then, like a comet, they reappeared. A comprehensive box set from Numero Group revisits the spacey, unassuming band with new perspective.

title: Ancestor Boy
description: The singer-producer’s debut album splits the difference between proudly rootless and profoundly lost.

title: We Wanna Be Hyp-No-Tized
description: Clunky lyrics and inept political analysis hinder Scott Kannberg’s most enjoyable solo album to date.

title: Bodyguard
description: The co-founder of Oakland’s Club Chai merges samples of Turkish and Middle Eastern music with club beats on an EP that casts a skeptical eye on club culture’s promise of personal liberation.

title: Le Mal
description: On their second proper album, the already-bizarre Quebec experimentalists splice and reformulate their DNA to become even more aggressively strange.

title: Hi This Is Flume
description: The Australian electronic-music producer and streaming behemoth signals a shift in his approach with a surprise mixtape featuring appearances from JPEGMAFIA and SOPHIE.

title: Eraserland
description: Fusing post-punk touchstones with his heartland-rock heroes, a reinvigorated Timothy Showalter comes back to the light.

title: My Finest Work Yet
description: After a string of releases that sometimes felt like hearing Bird think himself in circles, the singer-songwriter relaxes into his most plainly and darkly funny album in a long time.

title: Songs of Faith: Aretha Gospel
description: The very first recordings of Aretha Franklin, captured in Detroit when she was all of 14 years old, are remastered and offer a window into the early sounds of a genius.

title: Significant Changes
description: The Canadian DJ, producer, and marine biologist bridges worlds on her debut album, weaving orcas’ songs and conservationist messages into deep-diving tracks aimed at inclusive dancefloors.

title: On the Line
description: The fourth album from the California indie rock icon features some of her strongest songwriting, sung gorgeously and told with piercing detail.

title: When the Pawn...
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Fiona Apple’s second album, full of diamond-sharp writing that mines the depths of her psyche and emotion.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: On her first commercial mix album, the producer crafts an unbroken stretch of shapeshifting grooves and psychedelic fireworks.

title: I Trawl the Megahertz
description: This lost Prefab Sprout album, previously issued as a Paddy McAloon solo LP, finds the singer receding into a vivid dream world unlike anything in his catalog.

title: Dreaming the Dark
description: On her new album, Tamaryn aims for sky-high '80s-goth melodrama.

title: Matamoros
description: USA/Mexico are sludgy, nasty, and unclassifiable, meaning they fit perfectly into Austin's coterie of noise-rock misfits.

title: Electric on the Eel
description: A new six-disc box set featuring performances from the late ‘80s and early ‘90s offers the definitive document of the latter-day Jerry Garcia Band.

title: Miss Universe
description: The rapturous debut from the British singer-songwriter takes adventurous pop-rock crucibles to new heights with her illusory songwriting and stunning voice.

title: Inside the Rose
description: On their fourth album, the visionary English experimenters conjure a sinister and beguiling new world.

title: Run Wild Run Free
description: After snagging everyone’s ear on Kendrick’s “LOVE.,” the 22-year-old TDE signee Zacari struggles to hold our attention.

title: American Football (LP3)
description: The dazzling third album from the stalwarts of Midwestern emo does away with the band’s self-mythology and takes bleary, bold steps toward a new dawn.

title: Confetti in the Sky Like Fireworks (This Is Bate Bola OST)
description: On his soundtrack for the film This Is Bate-Bola, the Chicago cornetist, keyboardist, and composer summons the dread and excitement of the lesser-known Rio festival.

title: Jag Trax
description: Gold Panda’s Derwin Dicker adopts a new alias and a new sound, trading his typically lush, sampledelic style for clean-lined house music with a dry sense of humor.

title: LIL BIG MAN
description: The L.A. rapper grapples with uncertainty and depression over warm, creamy, lo-fi beats.

title: GloToven
description: It isn’t really in Keef’s nature to be sentimental, but even Zaytoven has a way of getting to the hardest rappers.

title: Crazy But It’s True
description: The Atlanta rapper’s new project stumbles around in search of a hit and comes very close to finding one.

title: Bubble Universe!
description: A new project from the Chicago vaporwave maven eases off the aggression of her Fire-Toolz alias, finding new inspiration in the clash of new age, smooth jazz, prog rock, and video-game soundtracks.

title: The Devil You Know
description: The punk trio’s unfussy production and precise vocal harmonies are a testament to their well-earned longevity.

title: Make a Wilderness
description: Jonny Nash draws on the otherworldly sounds of the Baschet brothers’ experimental instruments to sculpt a gently haphazard ambient mirage.

title: Plastic Anniversary
description: Recorded using only plastic material, the concept of the latest Matmos album is undergirded by the compositional integrity, the quality of the sound, and the sickeningly beautiful idea of it all.

title: Komachi
description: Blending modern techniques with deep reverence for history, producer Meitei sets out to recapture a “lost Japanese mood.”

title: ATAXIA
description: The UK producer’s debut album fashions a distinctive aesthetic out of asymmetrical machine beats and dabs of electronic melody, balancing academic concerns with rave-tested thrills.

title: Lux Prima
description: Karen O and Danger Mouse have concocted a lush, vivid world on their dreamy and poignant collaboration.

title: High Anxiety
description: The Chicago noise-rock/thrash/punk/metal/etc. trio continue to hate you, your band, and most other things.

title: Rapture EP
description: The young Jamaican singer shows off her versatility on her debut EP, slipping between rapid-fire ragga grit and conscious reggae styles, and maintaining an unwavering focus on memorable melodic hooks.

title: Trust in the Lifeforce of the Deep Mystery
description: The cosmically minded group featuring rising jazz saxophonist Shabaka Hutchings dances to the apocalypse and pleads for humanity.

title: Let There Be Eve...Ruff Ryders’ First Lady
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Eve’s 1999 debut, a hard-bodied and self-determined showcase.

title: Cry 4 Help EP
description: The L.A. singer and rapper’s intimate EP confronts trauma and healing in smooth, unflinching songs.

title: Downer Edn
description: The Sydney punks comb through society’s sludge on a deadpan collection of mosh pit anthems and glistening new wave synthesizers.

title: Many Any
description: The D.C. dance-music vet and Future Times honcho drops a freeform set of free-spirited club tracks that show off his keen beatmaking abilities.

title: Groove Denied
description: The indie-rock icon fires up his laptop and lays down a set of quasi-electronic jams that owe more to late-1970s post-punk than to the Berlin nightlife that supposedly inspired the record.

title: PUNK
description: The Japanese quartet devote their second album to enthusiastic, maximalist pop with a bluntly feminist message.

title: Psychodrama
description: On his debut album, the talented South London rapper Dave explores family and identity with the unguarded catharsis of a therapy session.

title: Panorama
description: On their Epitaph debut, the Grand Rapids post-hardcore band ruminates on the small stuff—death, grief, life, love.

title: Sucker Punch
description: On her debut, the Norwegian pop phenom offers a patina of fresh-faced authenticity and not much else.

title: Egowerk
description: More than two decades in, the Omaha electro-rock band finds new reasons to stay angry and keep dancing.

title: PURGE
description: The tempestuous debut by producer and vocalist Felicia Chen is an emotionally tense album that whips between violent outcries and quiet pockets of respite

title: Knife + Heart (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
description: On his third outing composing music for film, Anthony Gonzalez breaks from his own soundtracking habits with a welcome sense of playfulness.

title: EXPORT
description: The UK duo’s ambitious second album has an alluring and unclassifiable sound. Rarely has a hybrid of new wave and experimental electronic music led to such an introspective place.

title: The Transitory Poems
description: Two celebrated jazz pianists bring contrasting, complementary approaches to a set of improvised pieces that pay tribute to Cecil Taylor, Geri Allen, and other titans of the instrument.

title: I Don’t Know How to Be Happy
description: The industrial noise-punk duo Deli Girls’ I Don’t Know How to Be Happy is a vengeance document built on industrial mutant rage.

title: Still on My Mind
description: The UK goddess of lite pop still sounds serene, unbothered, and preternaturally confident.

title: Death Race for Love
description: Over 72 minutes, the emo-rap star explores drugs, heartbreak, and the drugs that lead to heartbreak.

title: On Time Out of Time
description: The ambient composer turns his attention to the skies, sourcing an epic, heart-stirring sound from gravitational waves emanated by two massive black holes that collided 1.3 billion years ago.

title: Everything Not Saved Will Be Lost Part 1
description: The UK rockers summon all their crowd-pleasing, arena-sized ambition on the first half of a double album but lack the panache to really pull it off.

title: Hyperion
description: The second album by the French producer Gesaffelstein brings in big pop collaborators like Haim and Pharrell.

title: Dead Man Original Soundtrack
description: A vinyl reissue of the atmospheric guitar score for Jim Jarmusch’s 1995 film reveals a spare and intuitive performance unlike anything else Neil Young has recorded.

title: Toothsayer EP
description: On a five-song EP accompanying the British National Maritime Museum’s “Polar Worlds” exhibit, the Inuk experimental musician joins landscape, culture, and resistance.

title: Dusty Notes
description: Meat Puppets’ 15th album mirrors the Kirkwood brothers’ ethos: earthy and out of time, casual and familiar, and wholly at ease with itself.

title: Nick Waterhouse
description: The Southern California rocker cobbles together a pastiche of 1950s rockabilly, 1960s pop, and old-school soul. At its best, it’s a shot of pure joy, but it never quite transcends its inspirations.

title: Beware of the Dogs
description: The Australian singer-songwriter’s debut album brings her captivating voice and keen eye to songs that demolish expectations. Fierce, funny, and unsettling, her music is empathetic to the core.

title: Sky Blue
description: A posthumous 1973 solo album from the Texas singer-songwriter, released the week he would’ve turned 75, displays his careful sense of craft across a set of covers, favorites, and unheard songs.

title: If I Could Only Remember My Name
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit David Crosby’s solo debut, a foggy dream of psychedelic folk-rock.

title: archipelago
description: Having traded K-pop’s regimented model for an experimental sound merging modular synthesis with vocal manipuation, the Tokyo-based Yeohee Kim finds a new degree of artistic freedom.

title: Girl
description: On her second album, the country-pop singer remains a powerhouse talent who can sing the hell of out every middle-of-the-road style going.

title: Inferno
description: 13 years after the death of his Go-Betweens partner Grant McLennan, Forster offers reflections with a spring in his step.

title: The Same but by Different Means
description: The home-recording savant stitches together micro-epics into a sprawling expanse that feels both intimate and grand.

title: Baby On Baby
description: The irreverent and charismatic Charlotte rapper's Interscope debut is just as wild as his mixtapes.

title: This Is How You Smile
description: Roberto Carlos Lange’s sixth and best album as Helado Negro deepens and expands upon the imagistic nature of his lyrics and cosmic synth-folk. It is a sublime, masterful piece of music.

title: Posthumous Humiliation
description: On their second album, this proudly gratuitous Philadelphia quartet dives headlong into extreme gore and extreme sonics, making a real-life mess of death.

title: SASAMI
description: Sasami Ashworth’s debut union of synthesizer decay and guitar reverb that embodies shoegaze’s supernatural ability to conjure sadness from the void.

title: I Also Want to Die in New Orleans
description: Mark Kozelek’s latest 90-minute dispatch frames his unedited ramblings as a kind of... free jazz?

title: GREY Area
description: The third album from the 25-year-old UK fire-spitter is a wickedly assured, highly entertaining, coming-of-age marvel.

title: M for Empathy
description: The Texas songwriter examines empathy in a series of probing and gemlike miniatures.

title: Sofia Kourtesis EP
description: The Peruvian-born, Berlin-based musician’s debut EP is the kind of house music that skirts convention and renounces rote functionality without ever forgetting that its purpose is to make people move.

title: Westkust
description: On their first LP following another bout of lineup changes, this Gothenburg band pushes against shoegaze confinement with songs meant to feel good.

title: Rap or Go to the League
description: The Atlanta rapper rewrites the rulebook on winning on his most thoughtful album.

title: Wasteland, Baby!
description: The man who took us to church tries to take us to the same church, again, 14 times, six years later.

title: Fantasy & Facts
description: The UK singer weaves in and out of reality and make-believe on her debut album of lush, experimental R&B. It’s a transparent look into her swelling heart and wistful imagination.

title: 1UP
description: The Auto-Tune crooner catches everyone’s attention and promptly squanders it again.

title: American Love Call
description: If this Indiana soul band’s debut was the party, the strings come out for these songs about heartbreak and the hope in resilience.

title: SNAFU
description: Six years after their scrappy debut, the pop-punk band Potty Mouth return with an arena-sized follow up that sounds like a major-label effort without all the compromises.

title: When I Get Home
description: Solange’s fourth album is unhurried, ambient, and exploratory. Using everything from spiritual jazz to Gucci Mane, Solange conjures her hometown with exceptional songcraft and production.

title: Girls
description: On her first full-length album, the versatile Atlanta artist explores the alternate identities of girls and women, finding solidarity in a cast of striking friends.

title: Death Becomes Her
description: On her full-length debut, the provocative producer also raps, smartly using her voice as a tool in her quest to dislodge gender binaries and power hierarchies.

title: White Stuff
description: Perhaps their reunion is already doomed, but for the first time in almost two decades, this haywire tandem goes wild with their singularly subversive rock’n’roll.

title: Good at Falling
description: On her debut album, the British singer-songwriter Amber Bain lets go of her self-consciousness and, with some help from the 1975, makes the transformation from hesitant outsider to unlikely pop star.

title: Weezer (The Black Album)
description: Weezer reflects on their own capricious history, using a blunt force the likes of which they’ve never deployed before.

title: Walking Wounded
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the intersection of pop and trip-hop and love and memory in a stellar record from 1996.

title: Pretty Face
description: The 22-year-old Queens rapper offers a tape of thoughtful and weighty heartbreak hymns that slowly reveal more of his layered personality.

title: This Land
description: Leaning into both his songwriting and his studio experimentation, the Texas guitarist proves his eagerness to move beyond the confines of modern blues.

title: BTTB (20th Anniversary Edition)
description: This restrained collection of solo piano instrumentals evokes Satie, but the often-overlooked experimental touches presage Sakamoto’s subsequent work.

title: Eminent Domain
description: Showcasing the darker, noisier side of Ron Morelli’s industrial-electronics label, this collection creates a cohesive whole out of jagged contrasts.

title: A Long Red Hot Los Angeles Summer Night
description: Evoking the golden age of LA hip-hop with rapid-fire rhymes, vivid set pieces, and sample-centric beats, the rapper finally offers a proper follow-up to an ill-fated opus.

title: All My Relations
description: The Dap-Kings saxophonist assembles a sizeable, percussion-heavy ensemble on a set that draws inspiration from a search for his ancestral past.

title: placeholder
description: Anxiety swirls through these songs about non-normative relationships, the unease countered by a bucolic mix of pleasing melodies, soft guitars, and gentle vocals.

title: Tasmania
description: The eighth album from the Australian psych-rockers is their most melodically realized of their career. The strains of pop offer a lovely imprint of a band in a constant state of flux.

title: Gangster Music Vol. 1
description: A hip-hop head’s presumptive fantasy, this compilation by the Gangster Doodles illustrator gathers loosies from cult favorites and a few new artists.

title: Europa EP
description: Despite trending toward pop in recent years, the globetrotting producer turns to European and African rappers to help him find new inspiration—or at least try.

title: Big Bad...
description: The London rapper’s fifth album reinforces his dominance of the UK scene and marks his increasing cachet in international waters, but the decision to sing might be the wrong kind of risk-taking.

title: Swervvvvv.5
description: On her supposedly final mixtape before she issues her full-length debut, the “urban jazz” rapper and singer adds intrigue with bits of her backstory and elliptical flourishes.

title: Harverd Dropout
description: Having abandoned his lo-fi roots in the South Florida rap scene, Lil Pump has become a caricature of himself. His second album is sometimes fun but mostly unnecessary.

title: Drip or Drown 2
description: The drowsy Atlanta rapper polishes his style and submits some of his best songs, but the same thing that makes Gunna dependable also makes him predictable.

title: Crushing
description: On an album that mines failed relationships for self-discovery, the Australian singer-songwriter shows her talent at distilling complex situations into searing couplets.

title: Father of 4
description: Though it’s undermined by its inertia and lack of focus, Offset’s solo debut offers glimpses of the rapper as a compelling storyteller and bluesman.

title: Second Language
description: The second album from the experimental Korean rap/production duo really starts to come together. They find a catchy, powerful zone to serve up their invective.

title: Sunshine 3
description: Using a bespoke tuning system, the Finish producer builds his songs inside an otherworldly ecosystem of sound using the pulse of electro, funk, and classic IDM. It is simply alluring.

title: Fabric Presents Bonobo
description: In the first installment of the London nightclub’s relaunched mix series, an artist best known for soulful, worldly downtempo tries his hand at upbeat house.

title: Helium
description: The former Mac DeMarco guitarist shifts to tepid synths and limp beats on his fourth album, a pastiche of references beyond his reach.

title: While We Wait
description: The Oakland R&B singer’s latest project is a shining example of both her emotional intelligence and her balmy, lucid songwriting.

title: Silences
description: Even if the second album from this Nashville singer doesn’t sound like the blues, she embodies the spirit, squaring up to her demons without fear.

title: Lung Bread for Daddy
description: Beth Jeans Houghton’s second album as Du Blonde sorts through the messiest aspects of desire and revulsion with cathartic finesse, purging her past while leaving her strange, spiky magic intact.

title: 808BB EP
description: Following last year’s thrilling Compro, the Ilian Tape label’s breakbeat-techno renegade returns with a three-track EP of club cuts that cleverly flip dancefloor expectations.

title: Los Angeles
description: A powerful, iconic document of West Coast punk is reissued, warts and all.

title: MTV Unplugged in New York
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit Nirvana’s transcendent live acoustic album recorded in 1993.

title: Serpent Power
description: Completing the move from hard club music to phantom ambient music, the producer escapes pixel-pocked logic for something more like nature.

title: Brilliant Trees / Alchemy: An Index of Possibilities / Gone to Earth / Secrets of the Beehive
description: After the breakup of Japan, this reluctant star retreated into a series of four albums—including his masterpiece—built on noir balladry, instrumental abstraction, and an abiding sense of distance.

title: You Will Not Die (Deluxe Version)
description: The strikingly intimate debut from the London-via–South Africa singer showcases an exciting new talent despite its occasionally lead-footed pacing and stilted theatrics.

title: Modern Sounds in Country & Western Music Volumes 1 & 2
description: At last available digitally, these quietly revolutionary albums still break one of music’s deepest-held genre orthodoxies.

title: Post Earth
description: The LA quartet’s second album is more musically focused and emotionally unsettled, its once shaggy sound sculpted into post-punk precision.

title: Love Is Love
description: On her second full-length album, the Baltimore rapper indulges in the time-honored queer tradition of plotting a great escape from it all.

title: Mazy Fly
description: Tia Cabral’s second album retains the great mysticism of her songwriting. The unsettling synth textures and soundscapes fly around her soulful voice, making something beautiful out of sheer terror.

title: Illegal Moves
description: Calling back to the insurgent sociopolitical jazz from another era of national unrest, these ecstatic instrumentals are urgent and purposeful.

title: Steals
description: On his second album for Nicolas Jaar’s label, the Russian producer continues to move away from footwork, building a gloomy world that is strangely welcoming.

title: Freewave 3
description: The latest project from the 22-year-old Chicago rapper is dour and affecting, a dispatch from a young man able to diagnose his wounds but unable to repair them.

title: Kankyō Ongaku: Japanese Ambient, Environmental & New Age Music 1980-1990
description: Visible Cloaks’ Spencer Doran curates an appealingly cohesive compilation of Japanese ambient music that, while decades old, feels uncannily suited to contemporary listening habits.

title: Mujeres
description: During this whirlwind of dream pop, folk, and jubilant dance music rendered in Spanish and English, Luz Elena Mendoza steps forward as a singer and bandleader like never before.

title: ALL
description: Best known for his music’s starring role in films like Amélie, the composer aims to become the auteur here—maybe a little too much.

title: Hello Happiness
description: Co-produced by UK dance mainstay Switch, this comeback album largely ignores all the qualities that made the Queen of Funk a legend in the first place.

title: New Atlantis
description: Berlin’s Phillip Sollmann strikes a balance between dancefloor techno and avant-garde experiments; his tracks slip into the cracks between common melody and rhythm.

title: Volume One: Dilemmas of Identity
description: On his first solo LP in six years, the noise architect lingers inside a series of haunted scenes, animated by the surreal sounds of homemade instruments.

title: Crush on Me
description: Kelsie Hogue’s debut album is likely to be among the year’s most extra albums, but behind its excitable homage to Britney and “TRL” lies an even more intriguing spin on ’90s alternative.

title: Head Above Water
description: Though an interesting showcase of her powerful and newfound voice, the Canadian pop star’s comeback too often lapses into the rote, the stale, or the uninspired.

title: Cherushii & Maria Minerva
description: Chelsea Faith Dolan perished in Oakland’s Ghost Ship fire in 2016; this EP of left-field dance music made with her 100% Silk labelmate Maria Minerva is a moving testament to her talents and legacy.

title: Another Kind of Revolution
description: On her Thrill Jockey debut, this Basque multi-instrumentalist ties together political and personal revolutions with atmospheric and even cinematic ballads.

title: An Attempt to Draw Aside the Veil
description: On their first album in seven years, the experimental guitarist and lutist craft surprisingly accessible and candid instrumentals from esoteric topics.

title: TNT
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the wondrous alchemy of performance and technology found on Tortoise’s third record.

title: Elder Mantis
description: On the sort of record that would have once sparked a minor bidding war between Stones Throw and Ninja Tune, hip-hop, IDM, and ambient music drift into a waking dream.

title: The Language of Injury
description: The debut from the UK melodic hardcore band shows their passion for experimentation in a genre where that is desperately welcome.

title: Cast
description: Leaving behind the singer-songwriterly stylings of his previous project, Coldair, Tobiasz Biliński taps the pristine sonics of 1980s sophisti-pop, but it’s often too bloodless for its own good.

title: Powder in Space
description: On her first official mix album, the Tokyo DJ unveils an intricate, inspired playing style whose value system differs from the typical dancefloor mix.

title: Let’s Try the After Vol. 1 EP
description: A pleasant palate-cleanser after the nourishing Hug of Thunder, the Canadian collective’s latest EP tackles familiar modes in capable fashion, while offering moments of life-affirming beauty.

title: Solitude
description: Now a duo, Kevin Martin and Roger Robinson strip away all the excess and most of the reggae, yielding a desolate snapshot of heartbreak framed in stark, largely beatless drones.

title: Ladytron
description: A dystopian band for dystopian times, Ladytron return with an angry, pitiless, evil-sounding record whose nihilism presents them as sirens of the apocalypse.

title: In a Galaxy
description: On her second album, the Dutch-Zimbabwean musician feeds off the energy of a move from Amsterdam to Peckham, England, turning the minutiae of daily life into bold, 1980s-inspired synth pop.

title: Rosa Parks: Pure Love. An Oratorio of Seven Songs
description: The jazz trumpeter’s meditation on the legacy of civil rights and the heroism of Rosa Parks is formally inventive and emotionally gripping.

title: After its own death / Walking in a spiral towards the house
description: The new project from Grouper’s Liz Harris contains some of her most beguiling work. Spread across two long, contrasting ambient compositions, her music remains in an enigmatic class of her own.

title: Living Tomb
description: On their debut album, this Portland quartet demonstrates their old school death metal bona fides, even when they’re more interested in evolution and atmosphere.

title: Bad Influence
description: A producer with a knack for matching any rapper’s flow and a rapper at his best when embracing his regional flair are, turns out, good influences.

title: Fyah
description: A player in Shabaka Hutchings’ Sons of Kemet and a key figure in London’s vital jazz scene, Cross brings new energy to the tuba, an instrument long neglected in jazz and hits offshoots.

title: Zandoli EP
description: The Belgian-Caribbean musician’s breakout EP, co-produced by Soulwax, channels Guadeloupean influences into striking, playful electro pop with a sly sense of humor.

title: Main Pop Girl 2019
description: The wonderful second album from James Brooks’ project uses breakbeats, samples, and beautiful rave-pop motifs to tell stories about the bruising power of memory.
The ostensible sequel to How Fly offers a few fleeting glimpses of the easygoing, unruffled, and effortlessly cool rap produced by the duo 10 years ago.

title: Girl With Basket of Fruit
description: The duo’s latest speeds between fragmented beats and mournful balladry but rarely makes an impression beyond its sound and fury.

title: Empire EP
description: Following last year’s mesmerizing Stadium, this three-track EP is as spacious and richly textured as experimental percussion gets.

title: What It Is
description: After a solemn post-divorce album, the Nashville-via-Texas songwriter works his endearing wit back into songs about loving someone new and abhorring social trends.

title: Gangway for Navy
description: Built on loud, low-bit-rate samples, the New York rapper uses a relaxed, almost deadpan flow to nestle deep in his own consciousness, drawing you in close to his words.

title: Buoys
description: Noah Lennox finds solace in solitude on his sixth solo album as Panda Bear, stripping the instrumentation down to just a handful of sounds to create an unusually unified listen.

title: AJ Tracey
description: The debut from grime’s rising star is a mixed bag but still peppered with hits, inviting elements of dancehall, pop, trap, and garage to the same house party.

title: thank u, next
description: Released five months after the catharsis of Sweetener, these songs of affirmation feel lighter, freer, and more fun, carried effortlessly by Grande’s undeniable voice.

title: A Different Forest
description: With more straightforward performances and compositions, the album has its flat spots, but it hints that Bertelmann might have as much to say as his piano does.

title: VOL. 4 :: SLAVES OF FEAR
description: The Los Angeles band used to make lithe, multifaceted songs that wrapped daring pop melodies in bristling noise; now, they seem content to complain into a murky hybrid of trip-hop and metal.

title: A Prince Among Thieves
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit an ambitious, righteous piece of hip-hop storytelling from 1999.

title: Tip of the Sphere
description: On his ninth album, the reserved bandleader incorporates more classic rock references than usual, but they’re the frames for subtleties and surprises within.

title: Unseen Worlds
description: Reissued at last by the label that borrows its name, the second album from the computer music innovator is less predictable, with dark moods rising to a captivating surface.

title: Severance
description: On their second album, the Irish duo Mikron—brothers Michael and Ciaran Corcoran—make promising strides toward defining their own patch of techno turf.

title: Olympic Girls
description: After an extended search for inspiration, the New Zealand singer/songwriter uses color and newly adventurous song structures to explore definitions and limits of freedom.

title: Oh Boy
description: In 2010, no band seemed to be having more fun with scrappy garage rock than this one. On their first album in nine years, they forget to replace that spark with anything else.

title: Quiet Signs
description: The Los Angeles folk musician’s third album is her best yet—a collection of hushed reveries that unspool like daydreams.

title: Live in London
description: Ten years after her last live record, Live in London feels like a valedictory statement.

title: Bobbie Gentry’s The Delta Sweete Revisited
description: A half-century after the release of Bobbie Gentry’s imaginative second album, the art-rock band revisits it as if in a daze but with the help of over a dozen brilliant singers.

title: Pursuit of Momentary Happiness
description: On their second album, this unruly British trio make the rare garage rock-informed record that aims for the upper reaches of Royal Albert Hall.

title: The Oracle
description: The debut from the Chicago-based composer and clarinetist serves as a vibrant, spiritual, free-jazz document of black life as it stands today.

title: Astronoid
description: On their second album, these metallurgists again find an awesome intersection of black metal pummel and shoegaze luster—then remain there, in its thrall.

title: Electric Lady Sessions
description: The version of the band that toured behind 2017’s American Dream gathers in the legendary New York studio, giving old songs new life and additional oomph.

title: True North
description: On his second album produced by Steve Gunn, the underground folk icon sings about age and regret with authority and grace.

title: Sunshine Rock
description: After a stretch of dark, searching records, the former Hüsker Dü and Sugar leader uses the familiar power trio configuration to find a little peace.

title: Big Dreez
description: After a quiet few years following her 2016 debut, the Chicago rapper returns sounding self-assured, wrapping her sharp flow in lush yet punchy beats.

title: Drift Code
description: Former Talk Talk bassist Paul Webb finally steps to the microphone on his first album in 16 years, a meticulously arranged wonder steeped in English folk and proggy vibes.

title: Music Inspired by the Film Roma
description: The curious, sometimes effective, sometimes bizarre music collected here features contributions from Beck, El-P, Patti Smith, DJ Shadow, Billie Eilish, and more.

title: Stuffed & Ready
description: Leading her thorny rock trio, Clementine Creevy keeps her themes broad and her anger specific as she reflects this moment’s feelings and fatigue.

title: Pure Imagination, No Country
description: With a group behind him that recalls the electronic jazz splatter of ’90s New York, Dave Harrington’s guitar work becomes a psychedelic, soft-hued quest for transcendence.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: The British house producer’s contribution to the longstanding series offers a broad cross-section of his tastes, mostly letting his selections, and not his mixing, do the heavy lifting.

title: Emergency Raps Vol. 4
description: When emcee Fly Anakin and producer Tuamie connect inside a sound infatuated with the hip-hop of the past, it becomes a launch pad to new life.

title: Gallipoli
description: Zach Condon reunites with his old Farfisa on his fifth album, but otherwise he remains cozily ensconced in his twee wheelhouse.

title: Careful
description: A decade after minimal wave seemed to reach its peak, the Massachusetts duo proves the style’s continued vitality.

title: On the Other Ocean
description: Over 40 years after its initial release, the composer’s pioneering work pairing computers with live players feels not only prescient but also refreshingly optimistic.

title: This Is Not the End
description: On their debut LP, the Norwegian trio emboldens their customary celebration rock by adding emphatic stretches of post-rock and power pop.

title: Journey in Satchidananda
description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit a marvel of spiritual jazz, an album overflowing with transcendence, harmony, and grief.

title: Tatizo Pesa
description: Jay Mitta adds an incredible amount of detail to the frenetic and kinetic sound of singeli, a blisteringly quick style of dance music from Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania.

title: Michael O’Shea
description: Originally released on the UK post-punk group Wire’s label in 1982, this long-lost one-off spotlights a singular busker who made magical music out of a stringed wooden door.

title: Mystery Hour
description: This baroque pop record is pleasant and roomy, but peer inside to find a fragmented portrait of heartbreak shared by the band’s cofounders.

title: Internationally Unknown
description: The fashionable UK punk-rap frontman has been made into an icon, but his second album is too often a pale and rote imitation of rebellion.

title: Scenery
description: The New York singer-songwriter’s third album maps life’s changes to sleek, vibrant R&B that’s packed with 1980s soundtrack flourishes and big moments; it’s the perfect frame for her extraordinary voice.

title: What Chaos is Imaginary
description: Weaving in and out of concrete, direct, indie-rock songwriting and meditative, impressionistic dream pop, Girlpool’s third album features their most expansive and surreal songs to date.

title: Hueco Mundo
description: The solo debut from one of the Dublin rap group NUXSENSE’s core emcees, backed by ghostly beats from producer Sivv, represents the clearest iteration of the group’s aesthetic yet.

title: Bartier Bounty
description: Already an all-time-great shit talker, the Detroit rapper reaffirms his reputation as a fun-loving rapper who repurposes familiar topics in new forms.

title: Comp x Comp
description: As the Tokyo experimental musician’s work is finally made available digitally, this compilation offers an introduction to the artist’s critical perspective on capitalism, gender norms, trans identity, and more.

title: Isa
description: The sixth album from Loke Rahbek’s experimental industrial project is his most cohesive to date, dissecting pop for parts and refiguring melodic elements into something truly other.

title: Almost Free
description: A little Gary Glitter, a little Kid Rock, even a little Smash Mouth—the third album from these former California party kids holds nothing back.

title: D A Y S
description: Perhaps familiar from her time in Okkervil River, the multi-instrumentalist builds fascinating webs of sound around skeletal songs on her solo debut.

title: Everything’s for Sale
description: The Compton rapper’s debut is smart, technically dazzling, and thoroughly sullen.

title: Epitaph
description: On what is billed as his proper debut LP after several years’ worth of cassette releases, the Greek producer fashions a wide-ranging attempt to move beyond his dub influences.

title: Nectar
description: The lo-fi, art rock project from Yung Lean is every bit as dazed as his rap music, while otherwise sounding almost nothing like it.

title: Signals Into Space
description: After 30 years, the London duo sounds more refined than ever, though their mix of ethereal jazz, ambient electronics, and mechanized drums has rarely been harder to define.

title: Goes West
description: The solo guitarist’s fourth album is soft and subtle, approaching the strains of pop while still basking in the solitude of Americana.

title: La Onda de Juan Pablo
description: On his first album sung entirely in Spanish, the Uruguayan-American singer-songwriter finds poetry in small moments, with low-key craftsmanship that matches his songs’ quotidian subject matter.

title: La Maison de la Mort/Minimal Cuts EP
description: The Russian producer better known as Buttechno applies his gonzo sonics to psychoactive ambient miniatures and joyfully off-kilter club tracks.

title: Nighttime Birds and Morning Stars
description: After first gaining attention for representational acoustic beauties, the guitarist digs deeper into abstraction, until the physical trappings of her instrument largely melt away.

title: All the Young Droogs
