description: Jim James' new solo album contains some of his most psychedelic music, as well as his most directly topical lyrics, offering new ways for him to wield his otherworldly voice.

title: Apocalypse Fetish
description: Following the solemn elegance of his last album Brace the Wave, Lou Barlow's new ukulele-heavy EP feels incomplete.

title: Romantic
description: Philadelphia’s Mannequin Pussy thrash swiftly from the playful to the chaotic. Their latest LP combines punk, shoegaze, death metal, and more, with the ferocious push-pull energy of a mosh pit.

title: Arrival
description: At their best, as on Arrival, ABBA were as mysterious as Bowie, as rococo as Phil Spector, as unbearably sad as the Smiths.

title: Blunted on Reality
description: On their underrated commercial-flop debut album, the Fugees searched energetically for the voice they would find on The Score.

title: Liberation
description: oddCouple, a Chicago producer who has worked with Jamila Woods, Joey Purp, Saba, Kweku Collins, and others, gathers his most talented friends for a warm, relaxed affair full of pleasantly hazed beats.

title: Strange City
description: The constant and destructive waves of noise make this decisively a Merzbow record, but its cosmic mood and rhythms prove that Sun Ra lives in its DNA.

title: The Deaner Album
description: Dean Ween's solo debut is missing the sincerity and surrealism of Ween, but its bizarre chaos feels like you are in on a longstanding inside joke with an old friend.

title: You Know What It’s Like
description: Smoky and ominous, Australian singer/songwriter Carla dal Forno's You Know What It's Like simmers, both musically and thematically, while she inhabits the gloom of her arrangements like a ghost.

title: Black America Again
description: Common’s dissonant, politically-charged new album Black America Again finds him angry and off-balance—which feels like it’s exactly where he should be.

title: Keep Flexin
description: Rising Atlanta rapper and Migos affiliate Rich the Kid drops a bubbly, if not uninspired new tape with features from Young Thug, Desiigner, Migos, and Jeremih.

title: Talk to You Soon
description: The latest from the experimental producer/songwriter dives into the warrens of memory and trauma with a collection of anxiety-ridden and often beautiful vignettes.

title: QTT4
description: Producer Huerco S.'s latest ambient release feels like something heard from the other end of a long, dark tunnel that you no longer remember how to find your way back across.

title: Live at the Whiskey A Go Go: The Complete Recordings
description: This essential six-CD set captures Otis and his blazing ten-piece band at a vital time in soul music, where a young showman was trying to cross over to the white rock'n'rollers on the Sunset Strip.

title: xxx
description: In a season where “pussy” has become a household word again for all the wrong reasons, Pussy Riot return to exact their vengeance. At least, that’s the narrative for Nadya Tolokno’s xxx EP.

title: The Olympians
description: This self-titled debut on Daptone Records follows a tried-and-true formula for the records: Hire incredible musicians and get out of their way.

title: Disclosure
description: Leipzig's Gunnar Wendel, better known as Kassem Mosse, abandons his house music background for thorny synthesizer sketches—fistfuls of gurgle and ping, sometimes beatless, and maddeningly absorbing.

title: DC4
description: On the fourth installment of his Dreamchasers mixtape series, Meek struggles to figure out exactly where he belongs, caught between his old life and his new one, between superstar and street rapper.

title: Freedom Jazz Dance: The Bootleg Series, Vol. 5
description: A glimpse inside the studio for numerous outtakes and illuminating dialogue from the legendary “Second Great Quintet” sessions that would spawn Miles Davis' Miles Smiles, Nefertiti, and Water Babies.

title: Dissociation
description: The famously technical New Jersey band ends their career with one final album of squealing riffs, dizzying musicianship, and plenty of nostalgia for their heyday.

title: ONEderful
description: The Chicago-bred, now Brooklyn-based beatmaker DJ Rude One's ONEderful is a grubby set of blood-in-your-mouth street raps, featuring Roc Marciano, Your Old Droog, Mr Muthafuckin eXquire, and more.

title: Hunted
description: Denver’s [Khemmis](http://pitchfork.com/artists/33397-khemmis/) traffic in longform doom metal, letting their anger spread gradually rather than unleashing it all in one torrent.

title: FLOTUS
description: The stalwart and defiantly odd Nashville band Lambchop's latest reinvention finds them embracing a Vocoder-drenched, largely electronic sound. It is as lush and gorgeous as any of their past work.

title: All the Right Noises
description: Roman Flügel has explored hard techno, acid trance, willfully lunkheaded electro-house, and lyrical deep house over his prolific career, but this is the furthest he has strayed from the dancefloor.

title: Tumblers From the Vault (1970–1972)
description: All but unknown in the US, the adventurous trio Syrinx was among the first groups to embrace the Moog. RVNG has reissued their two albums along with a stunning live document.

title: Blood on the Tracks
description: Bob Dylan’s moody 1975 epic is often referred to as his “breakup album,” but it might be his most welcoming LP, its music projecting an undeniable warmth.

title: Secret Path
description: Tragically Hip singer Gord Downie, diagnosed with a terminal brain tumor, offers an affecting album with Broken Social Scene's Kevin Drew about the plight of Canada's indigenous population.

title: Rage & the Machine
description: Joe Budden's latest album, produced almost entirely by AraabMUZIK, offers a concentrated dose of his usual fare: complex lyrical raps, bitter contempt for current hip-hop, and a list of grievances.

title: Candida Cosmica
description: The latest unearthed work from San Francisco disco innovator Patrick Cowley is a woozy, fascinating synth experiment with Candida Royalle, the feminist porn director and actress.

title: R M H Q: Headquarters
description: In the early ’80s, New Zealand’s Roy Montgomery was part of foundational Flying Nun band the Pin Group. His first solo work since 2001 is a 4xLP set that, at its best, plays like a shadowy dream.

title: Beyond Now
description: After helping David Bowie realize his harrowing final statement Blackstar, saxophonist Donny McCaslin offers a bracing record with two Bowie tunes and a pair of covers of electronic acts.

title: Big Baby D.R.A.M.
description: After a string of EPs and some offbeat hits, rapper/singer D.R.A.M. arrives with his first full-length, a record filled with funny asides and sharp details and its fair share of memorable hooks.

title: Dreamt Takes
description: Queens-based beatmaker Luis summons early Warp-era IDM, when acts like Autechre, Speedy J, and Polygon Window crossbred hardcore and rave with the introspection of Tangerine Dream and Pink Floyd.

title: Running Out of Love
description: The latest from Swedish indie-pop stalwarts the Radio Dept. is the sound of a band rejecting indie-darling complacency for riskier, more mature territory, and the gamble pays off.

title: Lighthouse
description: Working with Michael League, the leader of the Brooklyn-based jazzy jam outfit Snarky Puppy, David Crosby releases his second solo record since returning from a 20-year hiatus.

title: Mad Love.
description: After a decade of record label turmoil, the pop singer JoJo—of “Leave (Get Out)” fame—returns with a sincere third album, featuring guest spots from Alessia Cara, Wiz Khalifa, and Remy Ma.

title: Nordic Mediterranean Organization / Numerous Miscommunications Occur
description: On their full-length debut, the Norwegian and Spanish experimental duo N.M.O. deliver a zig-zagging array of unnerving forms, evoking militarization and irreverent playfulness in equal measure.

title: Lazarus (Original Cast Recording)
description: In the last year of his life, David Bowie completed his remarkable final album, Blackstar, as well as this curious jukebox musical for which he wrote a few new songs.

title: American Football
description: Coming after a 17-year hiatus, the second LP by American Football* *might be the most highly anticipated emo album ever made.

title: Beyond the Fleeting Gales
description: The indie rock trio Crying folds the bombast of mainstream '80s rock into their sound, and the results feel like a grinning inversion of the hetero-masculinity that’s often baked into such fireworks.

title: After Hours
description: On her debut LP, the Miami-born, NYC-based DJ and producer Jessica Gentile honors the nightlife that raised her. She draws on dancehall, Miami bass, and trap, with enough space to breathe and glitter.

title: T.C.R. EP
description: On their latest EP, the misanthropic British duo Sleaford Mods allow some air into their sound and frontman Jason Williamson turns some of his acrid tirades towards himself.

title: Moving Still
description: On his second album as a bandleader, the jazz trumpeter Jonathan Finlayson finds an exciting meeting ground of exploration and approachability. It’s the work of a composer on the rise.

title: Joanne
description: Now that her peers have caught up to her visual provocations, Lady Gaga seems less like an audacious pioneer than one among many, and Joanne feels tentative, an affront to the Gaga of yesteryear.

title: Popp
description: On his fifth record since returning from hiatus in 2010, Oval's Markus Popp shows a side of, well, pop to his music that has often dwelled below the surface but never so overtly above it.

title: Retribution
description: Throat-singer Tanya Tagaq could be Canada’s unlikeliest crossover act. At a time when Canada is reckoning with the historic mistreatment of its indigenous population, her new LP demands retribution.

title: Everything Feels Better Now
description: From Indian Lakes’ fourth LP is mood music for the hopeless romantic, overwhelmed by the desire to connect but pining for the confidence to make the first move.

title: You Want It Darker
description: Leonard Cohen's 14th studio album feels like a pristine, piously crafted last testament, the informed conclusion of a lifetime of inquiry.

title: Headache
description: Male Bonding's surprise-released third LP is another album about wounds that won’t heal. But at its best it brings a wizened new perspective to those same themes.

title: Whatever Forever
description: Oozing Wound capture the energy of classic Slayer, Entombed, and punk-metal like Suicidal Tendencies, but it's hard to escape the feeling they are making fun of these guys as much as celebrating them.

title: Savoy Motel
description: Savoy Motel recreate the sounds of the ’70s using the ’90s pastiche techniques of Beck, Ween and Royal Trux, compacting glam-rock, southern boogie, and Stax sax stabs into 8-bit videogame proportions.

title: Self Restraint
description: Self Restraint, the latest album from rapper Gods Wisdom of the New England-based Dark World collective, arrives feeling strangely dated, as if it’s an artifact from 2011 or 2012.

title: Woptober
description: On his second LP since being released from prison, Gucci revisits the darker, weirder style of his classic period but keeps the clear-eyed outlook of his new, healthier lifestyle.

title: EP A
description: This solo EP from Katie Alice Greer, singer in lauded D.C. punks Priests, mixes industrial textures and synth-pop. Her talent for composing moody collages of unraveling sound is a pleasant revelation.

title: These Systems Are Failing
description: These Systems Are Failing is Moby’s most furious album in twenty years, a return to his hardcore days, but it's still oddly cold and routine.

title: Every Now & Then
description: On their second album, the Australian outfit go bigger and broader, unapologetically mining Primal Scream and the Madchester scene for inspiration.

title: Color
description: On her Tri Angle debut, sound designer and producer-turned-musician Katie Gately twists odd, outré samples into big pop shapes.

title: WALLS
description: *WALLS *mostly finds Kings of Leon back in that mode of offering up fast-food “whoa-oh” singalongs and guitars that chime as distinctly as wallpaper.

title: Fires on the Plain
description: Matt Kivel's patient, close-miked folk music opens up slowly, revealing painful secrets the more time you spend listening to it.

title: Sport
description: The punk electronic music Powell makes is crude, queasy, sometimes shockingly ugly, and often quite funny, in a madcap, slightly threatening way. It thrills and it mystifies in equal measure.

title: Thirst 48 Pt. II
description: The Compton rapper’s latest is a sequel to his 2014 debut mixtape. Boogie steps into the California sun, embracing a brighter sound with a flow that sharpens year after year.

title: Front Row Seat to Earth
description: The third full-length from singer/songwriter/producer Natalie Mering overflows with the misty sounds of late '60s folk and '70s AM radio, but her presence in these songs is modern and slyly knowing.

title: Standard Nature
description: Whether making black metal as Altar of Plagues or electronic music as WIFE, James Kelley has a taste for subversion, and his new WIFE EP surprises again by sounding downright joyful in spots.

title: Arctic Thunder
description: Darkthrone’s seventeenth studio album, Arctic Thunder, is a seamless, genre-hopping lexicon of death growls, doom dirges, and thrash runs as immediate as they are all-encompassing.

title: Yermande
description: German techno giant Mark Ernestus delves deep into African music, and the result is drum-drunk and gorgeous, both techno-fast and dub-slow.

title: Yes Lawd!
description: Yes Lawd! is another accomplishment in Anderson .Paak’s continued rise, a beautiful beat tape made with the producer Knxwledge that nods to classic Stones Throw duos.

title: Remember Us to Life
description: Regina Spektor’s latest album takes the unabashed earnestness that has always marked her music and rewrites it in a somber, minor key.

title: Building a Beginning
description: On Building A Beginning, Jamie Lidell unplugs his laptop for the most conventional R&B album of his career.

title: Requiem for Hell
description: Mono's ninth album looks to nothing less than the mother of all epics, Dante's The Divine Comedy, for inspiration.

title: Lubbock (on everything)
description: The artist Terry Allen made outlaw country from the vantage of the art world. Paradise of Bachelors have lavishly reissued his 1979 double album, a dreamscape that sways between country and folk.

title: America’s National Parks
description: Trumpeter Wadada Leo Smith's latest is an expansive and politically charged suite that pays tribute to official national parks as well as cultural zones not yet recognized by government decree.

title: super low
description: Atlanta art-punks Warehouse build a tightly controlled chaos, relying on improvised collaboration to forge gems from dischord.

title: Good Old Boys
description: Randy Newman’s Good Old Boys is nothing less than a tour of Southern bigotry and pride in the 20th century. It remains as shocking, pristine, and regrettably relevant as the day it was released.

title: Coconut Oil
description: *Coconut Oil, *Lizzo's first release under Atlantic, is her ode to body positivity, self-love and the trials of getting to the point where you believe you deserve it.

title: Adieux Au Dancefloor
description: Marie Davidson is a spoken-word poet and electronic artist who is also one half of the duo Essaie Pas. Her third solo release, examining club culture, shows near-exponential growth in her abilities.

title: High Bias
description: At his best, Purling Hiss frontman Mike Polizze simultaneously embraces, tweaks, and subverts all kinds of vintage garage, punk, and grunge moves. This is their most classic-rock record so far.

title: COW / Chill Out, World!
description: C**OW has some of the Orb’s most gentle moments to date, eschewing ambient house for ambient music, pure and simple.

title: Outer
description: After perfecting anthemic dancefloor fantasies with fine-tuned tracks like “Yoohoo,” Dusky offer a sentimentalist hodge-podge designed to prove that their mettle extends beyond the dancefloor.

title: Home OST
description: Made for a Belgian coming-of-age tale, Home is the latest film soundtrack by Johnny Jewel. It features new Chromatics and Symmetry music, plus eight ambient tracks, but is strangely mild-mannered.

title: Coming Home (Original Ghanaian Highlife & Afrobeat Classics 1967-1981)
description: This two-disc retrospective touches on several phases of Ghanaian vocalist Pat Thomas' career, pulling highlife, swing jazz, Afrobeat, psychedelic rock, reggae, funk, and disco into his joyful orbit.

title: Philosophy of the World
description: The Shaggs' Philosophy of the World became an enduring classic for its beguiling amateurism. But in its 2016 reissue, it's easier to hear the darkness and sadness behind the Wiggin sisters' story.

title: Complete Third
description: Big Star's never-completed third album is enshrined in a triple-disc box that contains all known recordings from the 1974 sessions and finally makes sense of all the chaos.

title: Marked for Death
description: Rundle has made her name performing mournful, minor key compositions, swelling with gothic drama, and her latest is her heaviest and most uplifting work yet.

title: Cashmere
description: The transatlantic duo of Heems (ex-Das Racist) and Riz MC (actor Riz Ahmed) link up for an album of politically-charged rap that's both thought-provoking and genuinely fun.

title: There Is No Right Time
description: The debut album from Yorkshire house producer Ewan Smith is a collection of daydreamy mood pieces. Stepping up the sound design, these melancholy tracks highlight Smith’s expressive sensibility.

title: The Altar
description: Banks' The Altar has a lot in common with the alt-R&B singer's breakthrough Goddess, including its fatal flaw: its attempts to position her as edgy or dangerous, despite all evidence to the contrary.

title: Ruminations
description: *Ruminations *is a record like none other in Conor Oberst’s catalog, stunning for how utterly alone he sounds.

title: NOTU_URONLINEU
description: Working under his new alias DVA [Hi:Emotions], Leon Smart smears the edges of the human and artificial, the organic and the electronic, as if trying to sketch out the dimensions of a digital self.

title: Cody
description: The California foursome follow their pop-punk breakthrough Never Hungover Again with the more grown-up and measured Cody.

title: Throwback to the Future
description: Producer Prince Paul and Digable Planets rapper Ladybug Mecca contribute to this fusion of NYC-style hip-hop and Brazilian music.

title: Shit Don’t Stop
description: In a crowded—and excellent—year for West Coast hip-hop, G Perico stands out as one of the most promising newcomers.

title: Heart Like a Levee
description: On his sixth album as Hiss Golden Messenger, M.C. Taylor's lifelong theme remains intact: What happens when you feel a distance from the thing that’s meant to sustain you?

title: Day Breaks
description: The restive jazz star, who went on to work with Jack White, Danger Mouse, and others after her multiplatinum debut, returns with a no-frills record that fades into the background without much fuss.

title: While They Were Sleeping
description: The eighth album from the wildly experimental Brooklyn metal group doesn't quite blaze trails on par with the band's classic catalog, but they are still genuinely searching for new expressions.

title: Sonoran Depravation
description: Arizona’s Gatecreeper stand out not by aping one particular style of death metal, but by acting as a polyglot of various classic bands. Sonoran Depravation is their unwavering debut LP.

title: Requiem
description: The ritualistically anonymous GOAT return with a double album of psychedelia rendered primarily with acoustic elements. Though still veiled, they reveal more of their heart and personality than ever.

title: Revolution Radio
description: Over the course of 26 years, Green Day have gone from pop punks to rock stars. Their latest, however, has little effect on their legacy and lapses into pandering, embarrassing lyrical misfires.

title: Root/Void
description: The latest from the prolific psych-folk duo comes courtesy of Woods' Woodsist imprint, and the higher profile coincides with some of their more memorable tunes.

title: Rhythm Nation 1814
description: After her 1986 album Control and its assertion of her identity as an artist, Janet Jackson was thinking big. Rhythm Nation 1814 is a thrilling mix of social messaging and dancefloor pleasure.

title: Private Energy
description: The latest from Roberto Carlos Lange's electronic pop project is a melodic and beautifully produced meditation on identity and the difficulty of connection.

title: Cold Summer
description: In the wake of some professional tumult, the snap and ratchet producer stages a solid comeback with more varied production and plenty of celebration.

title: Be Here Now
description: Oasis’ third album from 1997 was always more circus than substance. The bloated and indulgent remaster only reinforces it as one of the most agonizing listening experiences in pop music.

title: Sorceress
description: On their 12th full-length album, the Swedish metal institution have never sounded more comfortable with their full-on prog transition, which works both for and against them.

title: Lamentations
description: Moses Sumney has a gorgeous voice that is as intricate as it is intimate. His latest EP comes and goes too fast, but is still a welcome window into the electro-soul folk singer's private world.

title: Three
description: As Sarah Barthel and Josh Carter inch toward the mainstream, their plaintive and gloomy* Three* feels less like an album and more like postcards from the eye of an emotional hurricane.

title: Big Boat
description: Phish is not known for their studio work. But for a group of musicians whose sole value has always been the simple pleasure of making music, everyone here sounds noticeably vacant.

title: Everywhere at the End of Time
description: This new LP is the first in a six-album series from ambient artist James Leyland Kirby. It’s an extreme continuation of the concept—memory loss—that guided his 2011 masterpiece, An Empty Bliss...

title: Farewell, Starlite!
description: After big-name co-signs for the smooth, self-made producer and vocalist Francis Farewell Starlite, his latest album doesn't quite live up to expectations.

title: Fires Within Fires
description: The heavy Bay Area band’s eleventh and latest full-length is also their briefest by a sizable margin. It sags often, but Fires With Fires ends with a staggering exhibition of quiet power.

title: Head Carrier
description: While not as egregiously baffling as Indie Cindy, the latest from the ’90s indie icons is nonetheless a middling effort missing all kinds of dynamics the Pixies used to offer.

title: Serpent Music
description: Like James Ferraro or Dean Blunt, the Turin-based artist uses unsettling percussive loops and field recordings to create a mood as if lost in a strange urban landscape.

title: Light We Made
description: Following 2013’s bludgeoning The Things We Think We’re Missing, the Doylestown, P.A. band returns with a cleaner, efficient, and more stylish sound.

title: The Electric Lucifer
description: In the 1960s and ’70s, Bruce Haack led a double life. By day, he made children’s music. By night, demonic electronica. This reissue presents his most accomplished work in all its end-times glory.

title: A Seat at the Table
description: Solange’s new record is stunning, a thematically unified and musically adventurous statement on the pain and joy of black womanhood.
With 13 albums under their belt, the Norwegian experimentalists continue to haunt the dark, underexplored basements of electro-improvisational music.

title: Monologue
description: The session musician and leader of Nat Turner goes big on his first official LP, creating a spiritually rich and soulful autobiographical story.

title: Red Horse, White Mule / Opium Musick / Raag Manifestos / Jack Rose / I Do Play Rock and Roll / Dr. Ragtime and His Pals
description: Vinyl reissues of six albums from the late Jack Rose further solidify his place as a brilliant steel string guitar innovator.

title: Blood Bitch
description: The Norwegian avant-gardist’s most atmospheric and filmic album draws on several traditions: vampire movies, the cross-hairs of art and pop, and the lineage of artwork made of menstrual blood.

title: Fio da Memória
description: It's been six years since the Brazilian singer's debut. Now she returns with an album that both utilizes and breaks free of samba and bossa nova classicism with deep, downtempo beats.

title: Rheia
description: Rheia not only transforms the Belgian metal band's own abilities, but the breadth of the much heralded—and derided—black metal-shoegaze fusion.

title: Atrocity Exhibition
description: Atrocity Exhibition can be seen as the third work in a trilogy that began with XXX. Here, Danny Brown's songs of pain and release are accompanied by dense sonics from all over the musical map.

title: Real Enemies
description: Darcy James Argue's big band meets “The Daily Show” in an ambitious, wholly fascinating look at American politics and propaganda.

title: Quebec Place
description: The young Maryland rapper presents a deft, stylish, and unique introduction to his career.

title: Schaum
description: Experimental electronic producer Jan Jelinek partners with vibraphonist Masayoshi Fujita to create gorgeous clouds of shifting sound.

title: Alien Lanes
description: In the mid-’90s Guided by Voices were a mysterious outfit from Dayton, Ohio, that the music press didn't know what to do with—a rumor as much as a band. Their Matador debut was a turning point.

title: 22, A Million
description: Bon Iver’s first album in five years takes an unexpected turn toward the strange and experimental. But behind the arranged glitches and processed voices are deeply felt songs about uncertainty.

title: Expert Knob Twiddlers
description: Manage your expectations: This record may combine the electronic music giants Richard D. James and Mike Paradinas, but it's really just a playful, occasionally inspired time capsule of the 1990s.

title: Alienist
description: With two covers and two originals, the psych rock band of Genesis P-Orridge expands rather than fortifies the definition of classic rock'n'roll.

title: A 1000 Keys / A Certain Degree of Stasis
description: On an album of brutalist, MIDI-driven piano fugues and a double CD of languid ambient drones, the German electronic musician shows off two distinct sides of his musical personality.

title: Masculin Féminin
description: The Masculin Féminin box set is a scrapbook made from early records that already felt like scrapbooks, but collectively they form a rich and vibrant portrait of the ’90s indie rock icons.

title: Fetish Bones
description: Camae Ayewa channels the politics of noise music and Afrofuturism for a deeply confrontational and affecting album that makes real and visceral the trauma of the past.

title: Sirens
description: Sirens is a thoughtful study in contrasts, both musical and political. It's only Nicolas Jaar's second LP, but it is the mark of an enduring electronic composer.

title: Heads Up
description: Warpaint’s new album is said to be informed by recent hip-hop and R&B but it ultimately hews closely to the moody downtempo rock they’re known for.

title: If You See Me, Say Yes
description: On her bright and self-assured solo debut, Wye Oak’s Jenn Wasner offers the most all-encompassing document of her tastes yet, incorporating dreamy indie rock and digital pop.

title: Return to Love
description: On their Sub Pop debut, LVL UP's more unhinged, existential bent gives a new weight to their songwriting.

title: The Healing Component
description: The Chicago rapper’s debut LP is a daring and expressive album that explores the American web of love, faith, violence.

title: Campaign
description: On his new trap- and hyphy-inflected mixtape, Ty Dolla $ign stumps for Hillary—and he's pretty psyched on Jack Johnson, too.

title: Legends Never Die
description: Chinx's second posthumous album misses the mark, but these scraps and drafts are still a reminder of his promise.

title: Ape in Pink Marble
description: Devendra Banhart’s ninth LP continues on with the wispy, low-stakes coziness of 2013’s Mala, though it’s much darker. Its best moments are a reminder of why Banhart touched a nerve in the first place.

title: Open to Chance
description: Kaya Cohen's third guitar-and-voice album is a sprawling fascination with the natural world and the nature of people.

title: Human Energy
description: Travis Stewart has bobbed and wove through many styles du jour, but his latest closes the gap between glitch and pop by using Dawn Richard, MeLo-X, and Jesse Boykins III on his euphoric compositions.

title: I Remember
description: Aluna Francis and George Reid's sophomore album globe-trots through bass and sass-heavy dance tunes that occasionally stall out at their peaks.

title: A Loud Bash of Teenage Feelings
description: Beach Slang's earnest angst still makes for an excellent group therapy session.

title: Mirage
description: Mirage nixed any suggestion that intra-band drama was their sole animating force, and flourished in the emotional void they occupied: heartbroken, strung out, and alone at the top.

title: Care
description: Tom Krell teams with collaborators like Jack Antonoff and dancehall producer Dre Skull on his most polished album yet. But it turns out the professional sheen doesn't suit him.

title: A Corpse Wired for Sound
description: If Merchandise weren't a rock band before, they certainly are now. They've gotten a little more earnest and shoot for a bigger sound. It's a mixed bag, but it's hard to hate them for it.

title: Mama’s Gun
description: Erykah Badu's second album is dense with ideas and sounds that draw from the past and look toward the future. Released in November 2000, it embodies the millennial tensions of that pivotal year.

title: Shape Shift With Me
description: Laura Jane Grace leads her Florida punk band into uncharted waters with a densely packed, vicious, and heartbreaking album about sublimation and transformation.

title: Crooked Man
description: The legendary British DJ has been around the block. He returns with his Crooked Man project with pedigree, craftsmanship, and, delightfully, zero aspiration to the “new.”

title: Dang
description: One half of Tonstartssbandht, Eola is a vocal-only project with loops and blues. Dang is charming, weird, and extremely sincere.

title: Instrumentalepathy
description: After a scooter accident almost killed him, William Bensussen returns with a more nuanced album, full of spiritual revelations and electro-psych affirmations.

title: Departed Glories
description: The Norwegian ambient musician Geir Jenssen plumbs the mind of a medieval queen on his beautiful, gripping new album.

title: I Had a Dream That You Were Mine
description: The pairing of the Walkmen's Hamilton Leithauser and former Vampire Weekend producer/instrumentalist Rostam Batmanglij turns out to be an inspired one.

title: Sunlit Youth
description: The California indie-pop band goes bigger and broader, leaving behind some of the more intricate songwriting of their past.

title: Mykki
description: On her studio debut, Mykki Blanco shines with both her lyricism and radicalism.

title: We Are the Halluci Nation
description: The trio of Canadian DJs’ unique “powwow step” turns the pulse of First Nations music into a modern electric dance soundtrack that is politically thrilling and immediate.

title: Chapter and Verse
description: This companion to Bruce Springsteen’s memoir traces his development as a songwriter and a person. Most notable is the inclusion of five previously unreleased songs from before he signed with Columbia.

title: Mount Ninji and Da Nice Time Kid
description: Across the South African rap duo's fourth album, their iconoclastic rave-rap fades into shallow humor and belabored production.

title: Up Against the Bricks
description: Sadie Switchblade of G.L.O.S.S. steps out with a solo album that touches on the hardcore of her main band and adds elements of country music and acoustic folk.

title: Feature Magnetic
description: The legendary MC has made a career out of evading definition, which he continues to do alongside an array of guests who are all here to simply and inimitably just rap.

title: Fear and Fury
description: The Arkansas doom metal band's stopgap EP features a Black Sabbath cover, a Type O Negative cover, and one original that reinforces their place among the best of them.

title: The Randy Newman Songbook
description: The four-LP box containing everything Newman recorded for his Songbook series is a self-made and ever-shifting canon from songwriting's most charming cynic.

title: Hard II Love
description: On his eighth album, Usher sounds better than he's sounded in ages, proving he will not go gentle into that quiet stormy night.

title: Love Means Taking Action
description: As another moniker for Danish musician Loke Rhabek, Croatian Amor finds him at his most ambient, exploring the ugly beauty of love and human connection.

title: Furfour
description: The fourth album from the London duo recalls Brian Eno's post-psych, pre-ambient albums from the mid-’70s and explores how modern media interacts with musical transcendence.

title: The Complete BBC Sessions
description: Newly remastered by Jimmy Page, the three-disc set featuring recordings from ’69-’71 captures a vibrant and liminal phase of the band's career that shows who they once were and who they would become.

title: Imaginational Anthem Vol. 8 : The Private Press
description: The latest issue from the always idiosyncratic Tompkins Square series features songs from guitarists who released their warm and surreal folk ragas and finger-picked fantasias to private press.

title: Body Wash
description: Los Angeles beatmaker Ringgo Ancheta engages with classic ’80s R&B and boogie funk, pairing his adventurous sound with themes of self-actualization and human connection.

title: Preoccupations
description: The artists formerly known as Viet Cong return with a harrowing, ferociously alive rock record that nods to Swans and Echo and the Bunnymen.

title: ArtScience
description: By keeping things mostly in-house, Glasper's Experiment band present their most realized album yet.

title: Sumerlands
description: On the debut LP from his band Sumerlands, producer Arthur Rizk (Title Fight, Prurient) establishes himself as a keen student of early ’80s American metal and a songwriting behemoth in his own right.

title: Another Green World
description: Brian Eno has done everything from producing huge pop stars to creating tiny art installations to touring with rock bands to inventing ambient music. Another Green World remains his definitive album.

title: Transpecos OST
description: Moonlighting from their gig in the National, the Dessner brothers deftly transpose their rock acumen to a subtle and detailed film score.

title: The Tonite Show
description: The two Bay Area presences come together for a short but supremely fun trip on the latest in the *Tonite Show* series.

title: Femenine
description: This 1974 performance of Femenine is a marvel of open-form minimalism, a rare recording of the undersung avant-garde composer and pianist that heralds the powerful voice of the black, queer artist.

title: The Divine Feminine
description: As a loose concept record about the many subtleties of love and distance, the Pittsburgh rapper’s new release is the most surprising, concise, and accomplished album of his career.

title: Pretty Years
description: Following up their remarkable LOSE, the Staten Island rockers try to fight grief with dense, hook-filled songs about the intrinsic value of being alive.

title: Cactus
description: On this fully-improvised session, the jazz duo of drummer Bobby Kapp and pianist Matthew Shipp lock in and never lose focus.

title: Clinging to a Dream
description: On this new album, Simeon Coxe rewires 1960s underground space poppers Silver Apples (again) and makes far-out sounds and sweet left-field songs.

title: Stage Four
description: A harrowing and unrelenting record, Stage Four is a glowing testament the post-hardcore band's melodicism, honesty, and unconditional empathy.

title: Lady Parts
description: This collab between the fun-loving Boston rapper Michael Christmas and the fractious IDM producer Prefuse 73 has flashes of fun and brilliance, but their styles are often incompatible.

title: Sunergy
description: Electronic music pioneer Suzanne Ciani and composer Kaitlyn Aurelia Smith come together for two lengthy slices of ambient bliss as part the RVNG label's *FRKWYS *series.

title: The Wink
description: Tim Presley's solo debut reteams him with producer Cate Le Bon for a stark, stream-of-consciousness odyssey.

title: Light Falls
description: Featuring members of Godspeed You! Black Emperor, J.R. Robinson's chamber-doom project coheres beautifully into a meditation on the banality of evil.

title: The Assistenz
description: The Chilean-born, UK-raised producer continues his work to breathe life into techno and meticulously break down the division between texture and rhythm.

title: KoKoro
description: Sarah Assbring's global influences bring her to bright new places with inspiring albeit uneven results.

title: E2-E4
description: After Ash Ra Tempel dissolved in the mid-’70s, the krautrock band’s leader Manuel Göttsching explored ambiance and minimalism. Improvised at home in an hour, E2-E4 became an electronic music landmark.

title: Skeleton Tree
description: Nick Cave has always played with death. Now, he confronts it.

title: Orphée
description: Based loosely on Ovid’s interpretation of the Orpheus myth, the Icelandic composer’s latest work reveals the grandeur of his music outside of scoring films.

title: AIM
description: M.I.A. returns with a politically charged but confusing album that lacks bite and bounce, presenting only glimmers of what once was.

title: Time Fades Away/Zuma
description: Neil Young's troubled, long-fabled "Ditch Trilogy" is finally released in full alongside an unexpected, mercurial coda.

title: Desconstrução
description: A new compilation celebrates the grey but lush “samba sujo” of São Paulo, with strands of native samba, post-punk rumble, Afrobeat, and blasts of avant-jazz.

title: Pearls to Swine
description: After almost a decade, the gorgeous voice of singer-songwriter Adam Torres remains the spotlight, but his songs have grown wider and more elemental.

title: Afro-Cuban Electronics
description: Producers Armando Martinez and Rey Rubio focus on electro's Latin roots with an album that's all about percussion.

title: Acoustic Recordings 1998-2016
description: A career compilation that highlights the gentler side of White, some in a stripped-down Detroit setting and others in a homespun Nashville setting.

title: Rub Out the Word
description: Steve Buscemi reads the cut-up passages of William Burroughs while backed by the drones of Elliott Sharp. It rarely works.

title: Arvo Pärt: The Deer's Cry
description: The Estonian composer's ecclesiastical music is masterfully produced, bolstered by a powerful interpretation from the vocal ensemble Vox Clamantis.

title: Caetano Veloso
description: In 1968, the Brazilian pop singer began a Tropicália revolution against a newly installed military government. It's a vibrant, cheeky, agitprop album that purred and glided past the martial censors.

title: Twin Peaks OST
description: The timeless score to David Lynch’s television show doesn't need any visuals to achieve the same sense of unsettling beauty.

title: Anything But Words
description: RZA and Interpol's Paul Banks come together for an overwrought pop-rap record either for die-hard fans or for those who think Chris Martin might just the best part of Graduation.

title: Deserts of Youth
description: Maine-based songwriter Liza Victoria’s proper debut album is a work of intimate beauty—a self-contained world that feels like a long song cycle rather than a collection of various pieces.

title: Away
description: Okkervil River’s Will Sheff approached Away like a solo record, collaborating with jazz, folk, and classical musicians. It contains the thrill of listening to a person take risks.

title: Goodbye to Language
description: Using only pedal steel, lap steel, and effects, Lanois turns traditional sounds into ambient and effortless music, brilliantly masking the complexity of its source.

title: The End of Comedy
description: For his latest psychedelic pop record, Michael Collins enlisted Ariel Pink, Weyes Blood, and members of the Mac DeMarco band, among others. It’s Collins’ most focused effort yet.

title: We Move
description: With the help of some producers du jour, the Irish singer-songwriter expertly blends his deep love for acoustic soundscapes and hip-hop on his fully realized third record.

title: Schmilco
description: Wilco's 10th album is a largely acoustic affair laden with sweet melodies, autumnal production, and childhood memories that stop just short of nostalgic.

title: The Serious EP
description: Bibio smartly reteams with Olivier St. Louis for a brief, effervescent, if somewhat canned retro R&B homage.

title: Circle 1: Live in Germany Concert / Circle 2: Gathering
description: Available for the first time digitally, these two albums from the free-jazz supergroup featuring pianist Chick Corea and saxophonist Anthony Braxton offer a singular display of musicianship and chaos.

title: False Readings On
description: On his striking new LP, the pop-ambient composer Matthew Cooper, aka Eluvium, marshals his sound into sweeping maximalist splendor.

title: The Sun’s Tirade
description: The Tennessee rapper and TDE associate really finds his voice on his second album, one filled with the tensions caused by a cycle of self-loathing and self-discovery.

title: Splendor & Misery
description: The L.A. rap deconstructionist trio, which features Hamilton’s Daveed Diggs, has released their highest-concept work yet: a hip-hop space opera.

title: Here
description: The Scottish quintet’s 10th album, and first in six years, is full of quiet revelations. The hushed production and contented lyrics make for their warmest and subtlest effort to date.

title: Patientness
description: The delicate songs of the nomadic singer-songwriter have the ability to turn the wildest emotions into something calm and centered.

title: Ultra
description: The fourth full-length from the hermetic UK electronic wizard is his most confident in ages, a fully-formed showcase for his singular ear and audacious production.

title: A Rainbow in Curved Air
description: A fixture of the minimalist canon, these two singular psych-classical compositions snuck into '60s counterculture at just the right time.

title: Science Agrees
description: The Smiths' Andy Rourke and Cranberries' Dolores O'Riordan team up with producer and singer Olé Korestsky for an album that doesn't lean too much on everyone's bona fides.

title: and the Anonymous Nobody...
description: The hip-hop legends return for their first album in 12 years and turn a comeback story into more of a claim to their legacy.

title: Existentialism
description: Recorded last summer in Brooklyn, this kinetic live album collects new politically-charged songs from the British art-punk O.G.s—a call to arms for all those pushing against the tides of modern life.

title: Cosmetic
description: The Nots' second album finds the Memphis band moving beyond minute-long blasts of hooky punk and experimenting with new textures and art-damaged noise.

title: My Woman
description: Angel Olsen's latest is her best record yet, a bracing mix of sounds and styles congealing around songs of pain, sadness, and hope.

title: Kiss Me All Night EP
description: Just six months after their seismic Big Black Coat, the Canadian electronic duo shifts into a lower gear but stays on the vanguard.

title: blisters
description: The hybrid pop collaboration between Josiah Wise and Haxan Cloak is a sly and personal exploration of the queer experience, boiling with personal energy and fantastically operatic in scale.
This reissue of William Basinski's 2009 album finds the composer doing what he does best, creating haunting loops and drones that have a way of burrowing into your life.

title: Funk Factory
description: Known for housing a famous Beastie Boys sample, the reissue of this 1975 funk and fusion classic brings peerless Polish and American players together for a groovy, eccentric journey.

title: One Nite Alone, The Aftershow: It Ain't Over!
description: Originally released as part of a three-disc set, Prince fires on all cylinders at these live recordings from the early ’00s, a testament to his late-night blues and funk reveries.

artist: Soundwalk Collective, Patti Smith, Jesse Paris Smith
title: Killer Road
description: Soundwalk Collective is an electronic group featuring vocals by Patti Smith and percussion by her daughter, Jesse. Here, they use field-recordings from Ibiza to rework the poetry of Nico.

title: JEFFERY
description: The rap iconoclast returns with his best album since Barter 6, daring and chameleonic, filled with hooks about identity, love, and that undefinable future swag.

title: Opalescent
description: This reissue of the electronic composer’s first album, made in his early 20s, rings thin and hollow compared to the dark genius of his later work.

title: The Party's Over EP
description: The new Rage Against the Machine/Public Enemy/Cypress Hill supergroup is a harmless if not crass experiment that amounts to a bad cover band playing songs they actually wrote.

title: Becoming the Beach Boys: The Complete Hite & Dorinda Morgan Sessions
description: A collection of spartan demos, false-starts, and practice runs of early Beach Boys songs recorded in 1961-62 amounts to a curious, often campy origin story for hardcore fans only.

title: Trouble
description: Though they’ve been releasing music since the late ’80s, the New Zealand noise trio remain as vital, corrosive, and challenging as ever.

title: Amnesty (I)
description: The first Crystal Castles album without vocalist Alice Glass is also the first safe album from an act that once would have recoiled at such a thought.

title: Whole & Cloven
description: Bowles has the power to transform the sound of a banjo—and traditional folk music—into something transcendental, often bringing the spirit of Americana to new heights.

title: Water EP
description: The eight-track *Water* EP collects preliminary sketches from Aaron Maine’s best album, the spring release *Pool*. These rudimentary demos are filled with their own attractions and surprises.

title: Prima Donna
description: Pushing his versatility, ear for production, and lyricism in new directions, Vince Staples' hot streak continues.

title: Mangy Love
description: On his eighth album, the singer-songwriter connects his gentle, acerbic soul to his most politically charged, well-stated, and funniest songs.

title: GucTiggy EP
description: Gucci Mane and Zaytoven give a quick five-song salute that recaptures a few sparks of their former fire.

title: Motion Graphics
description: Joe Williams' first solo project is a breath of fresh air for vaporwave.

title: For this We Fought the Battle of Ages
description: On their fourth full-length, the Salt Lake City doom band SubRosa take inspiration from a 100-year-old dystopian novel about a modern surveillance state. The resulting album is their best yet.

title: Things Fall Apart
description: Things Fall Apart was a turning point for the Roots, the record where they figured out what kind of band they could be. Both its themes and its eclectic mix of sounds resonate in the current moment.

title: Larva Lumps and Baby Bumps
description: Perennial Long Island noise-rockers return with their first album in 14 years, as detailed and cacophonous as they've always been.

title: Take It, It’s Yours
description: On this collection of classic punk covers, La Sera’s Katy Goodman and the Hush Sound’s Greta Morgan defang purposefully messy music with honeyed duets and pleasant arrangements.

title: The Bells
description: The Swedish producer in charge of bringing capital-F Fun back to the dance floor succeeds in a multitude flying colors across his ebullient and wildly dynamic debut album.

title: 4th of July
description: On his second solo album, the My Morning Jacket guitarist finds comfort in the slow lane of life, eschewing guitar fireworks for easy-chair folk.

title: Ibifornia
description: The French duo resurface with their first album in 10 years, slamming together the Balearic reverie of Ibiza and the pop-chart tank-top vibe of California, not always to great effect.

title: Nexus
description: On his sophomore EP, DJ/producer Caleb Halter positions his music between ambient atmospheres and clubby bombast—this time pulling in opposing directions rather than seeking balance.

title: Instinctive Drowning
description: On his second solo LP, the Detroit MC Chris Orrick, aka Red Pill, raps about alcoholism and depression. Instinctive Drowning is largely devoted to the persistence of a tormented mind.

title: Blade of Love
description: The avant-garde tenor saxophone quartet returns with three adventurously dense movements, yet they maintain a focused sense of restraint and melody throughout.

title: Blonde / Endless
description: Four years after the landmark Channel Orange, two new releases from Frank Ocean find him writing richly emotional songs for a quieter, more meditative space.

title: Partners
description: What starts as an homage to John Cage, soon shifts into an increasingly honest and heartfelt album of solo piano by the young composer.

title: Atomic Bomb Compilation Vol. 4
description: A juke-filled, global set of songs compiled in Japan reflects the fear and uncertainty of the atomic age, recontextualizing the joy of footwork into ominous, often unsettling compositions.

title: Home Wrecking Years
description: On his third solo album, Broken Social Scene’s Brendan Canning offers tentative experiments that ape other bands’ styles. It feels like a guy just filling downtime.

title: CDW EP
description: The Toronto singer's debut EP arrives fully formed, a short mix of quiet storm R&B and dark pop for doomed lovers.

title: "Fantasy Live 1999"
description: An extended dance music composition from the Japan-based analog-synth trio audaciously tries to recreate a long-lost live session with contemporary global grooves.

title: I Told You
description: On his debut album, the Toronto artist provides his origin story, and proves just how hard it is to escape from the long shadow of Drake.

title: Star Core
description: On the Bay Area electronic musician’s second solo album, the minutest vibrations are as expressive as the most sweeping gesture. Its mood exquisitely balances melancholy and hope.

title: Skiptracing
description: Mild High Club is the solo act of Alex Brettin, a tourmate and disciple of Mac DeMarco’s sunny sound. On his sophomore album, Brettin finds a voice more distinctly his own.

title: Miss Sharon Jones! OST
description: The soundtrack to the Sharon Jones documentary isn’t quite a career-spanning compilation, but provides the unflinching honesty and ceaseless vitality that abounds in her life and music.

title: I.B. Tree
description: With the help of producer I.B. Classic, the Chicago trap-soul rapper delivers the most defining and unifying record of his career.

title: Phase Zero
description: On his Sub Pop debut, deranged psych-pop bedroom auteur Morgan Delt cleans up his sound considerably.

title: Blue Rider Songs
description: On his debut solo album, the Hiss Golden Messenger member finally lets out his voice—a cool, soulful thing filled with deep reverence for the road, if some cynicism about the myths it’s spun.

title: The Childhood of a Leader OST
description: The avant-garde icon Scott Walker scored this film about a fictional 9-year-old dictator, and it's one of the best things Walker has done since the still-unsettling The Drift.

title: Sélébéyone
description: The international jazz-rap project Sélébéyone is a rare case of the two genres mixing at their most far-out, abstract corners.

title: Songs in the Key of Life
description: *Songs in the Key of Life *was the culmination of a historic period of creativity for Stevie Wonder. Its ambition and scope were unprecedented, and he never approached its caliber or impact again.

artist: Atticus Ross, Leopold Ross, Bobby Krlic
title: Almost Holy OST
description: Atticus Ross (Trent Reznor's film-scoring partner) and Bobby Krlic, aka The Haxan Cloak, soundtrack this documentary about a priest who rescues drug-addicted youths from the streets of the Ukraine.

title: In Summer
description: The experimental ambient musician Jefre Cantu-Ledesma's In Summer is some of the most emotionally evocative noise music of the year.

title: Honor Killed the Samurai
description: With his latest, the Brownsville rapper cements himself as a preeminent stylist, his voice hushed but vicious, his production a grim rabbit hole of found sounds, minor keys, and few drums.

title: Rattle
description: The all-drum band Rattle's self-titled record has an admirable sense of freedom and unwillingness to mimic the tropes of conventional songwriting.

title: Open Your Eyes
description: Open Your Eyes, the first set of new tracks released on Teklife's eponymous label, features collaborations with Oneohtrix Point Never and a host of footwork veterans.

title: Spinhead Sessions
description: Titled after the studio where the band rehearsed for a movie-soundtracking job, these purely instrumental pieces from 1986 offer another look at the Sonic Youth who had just recorded EVOL.

title: Crappin’ You Negative
description: The mid-'90s Memphis band Grifters wrote songs that sounded like smart conversations you wished you could contribute to, inside jokes you wanted to be let it on. This was their most bracing statement.

title: Radiating Light: Orchid Tapes & Friends
description: Radiating Light is the second compilation from Orchid Tapes, a sequel to 2014's *Boring Ecstasy. *Like the first, it gives you hope that people still make magic in their apartments behind closed doors.

title: Fishing Blues
description: The Minneapolis rapper-producer duo Atmosphere over-share on their sloppy and tedious new album, though it still contains a few gripping moments.

title: Paramount
description: Fury’s debut LP is a proud revival of the Orange County youth crew hardcore tradition. It is a devastating work of emotional and philosophical inquisitiveness that, yes, you can totally punch shit to.

title: Callus
description: Gonjasufi's Callus is an album that's disorienting at its catchiest, harrowing at its ugliest, and more than willing to run both of those modes at the same time.

title: Boronia
description: On *Boronia*, the Australian duo Hockey Dad are a 2016 version of the Wyld Stallyns, if Bill and Ted had been hypnotized by surf rock instead of metal.

title: Jumping the Shark
description: The Australian musician Alex Cameron paints quick, affecting character sketches of losers and creeps, bolstered by elementary synth programming and Cameron’s confident, warm baritone.

title: Official
description: On this new mixtape, Oakland rapper and former Das Racist member Kool A.D. collaborates with the producer Trackademicks to focus on a looming Bay Area influence: hyphy.

title: Stranger Things OST, Vol. One
description: The soundtrack to the runaway-hit Netflix sci-fi series evokes some of the ‘80s touchstones of the show, but in a more restrained way.

title: 5TARB01
description: Lexxi worked on Elysia Crampton's excellent July release *Demon Cit*y. Where *Demon City* stretched to encompass both past and future, the producer's debut EP* *takes place in a single wide-eyed moment.

title: For Mark, Your Son
description: On his Mello Music debut For Mark, Your Son, the Chicago-born rapper, singer, and producer Lando Chill comes to grips with the death of his father.

title: Kiid
description: On Kiid, her first full LP, Mal Devisa’s voice is raw, collected, and honest, scaling heights that you may have forgotten were there.

title: PARTYNEXTDOOR 3 (P3)
description: Drake affiliate and OVO signee PARTYNEXTDOOR follows up his biggest hit, penning Rihanna's summer jam “Work,” with his most assured and confident work yet.

title: Convenience
description: The no-wave inspired Brooklyn punks Pill pair controlled chaos with darkly funny, incisive political commentary.

title: The Get Down OST
description: The soundtrack for the Netflix drama The Get Down, which tells the story of the birth of hip-hop in '70s NYC, mixes disco classics with contributions from Nas, Miguel, Kamasi Washington, and others.

title: SremmLife 2
description: SremmLife 2, the follow-up to the turbocharged rap duo's joyous debut SremmLife, is stranger, artsier, and flat-out ballsier than its predecessor.

title: Roosevelt
description: Roosevelt's debut is a cocktail of disco, French touch, Ibiza house, yacht rock, and electropop that evokes some crowded Tiki-torch dancefloor lost on the Mediterranean coast.

title: One Day All of This Won't Matter Any More
description: The British duo Slow Club traveled to Virginia’s Spacebomb Studios to record their latest LP. The songs are dressed in easy listening costumes, but they seethe with disconnect and sorrow.

title: More Better Days
description: The Japanese DJ/producer Chee Shimizu curates a two-volume selection of obscure Japanese pop that runs the gamut from jazz fusion to New Age and prog rock.

title: Dry
description: On her debut, Polly Jean Harvey matched Patti Smith’s incandescence with Bessie Smith’s lasciviousness, outplayed everyone on the British indie circuit, and became an instant star.

title: Daniel Son ; Necklace Don
description: On his third project of 2016, 2 Chainz continues to show the way to rap successfully past the age of 40: He has some of the most enduring, daring, and funny verses in the game.

title: Golden Sings That Have Been Sung
description: The first song on guitar wunderkind Ryley Walker’s fourth album might be the best thing he’s ever done. Then there are the other seven songs.

title: Chronicles 1
description: In the ‘90s, the heady, ethereal techno made by 7th Plain had no peers. The best of this out-of-print and previously unreleased material still sounds otherworldly, all these years later.

title: Kaleidoscope World
description: In early ’80s Dunedin, the Chills were at the forefront of an extraordinary little guitar-pop scene. This reissue of their debut—a major document of their early era—extends the album to 24 tracks.

On their second LP for DFA, Factory Floor’s post-punk past has dissolved into hardware dance pieces of monomaniacal repetition and stiff precision. It’s tirelessly energetic, but often in a brute way.

title: A Weird Exits
description: On their latest, Thee Oh Sees show an eagerness to drift away from their foundational ’60s psych-pop and garage-punk roots into more cosmic realms.

title: Summer Camp
description: R&B singer/producer theMIND’s debut project Summer Camp is a low-stakes surprise, the late-night stoner’s LP we didn’t know we needed.

title: Live from Trona
description: Toro Y Moi's Live From Trona is an odd concert album: It was performed in front of no one, amidst the beautiful landscape of Trona—three hours away from Los Angeles.

title: Encore
description: DJ Snake is best known for his endless sugar high “Turn Down For What.” His solo album has a few successfully ridiculous tracks but mostly makes you question the need for its existence.

title: Way Down in the Jungle Room
description: Tracked at Graceland in 1976, the recordings on this double-disc compilation show that Elvis never stopped believing in the power of music, that he never stopped searching for the right song to sing.

title: Innocence Reaches
description: After a run of increasingly fussy, exhausting records, Kevin Barnes has started making direct and inviting music again. Innocence Reaches dips its toe into contemporary EDM.

title: Verschiebung
description: The producer Roman Flügel has spread his work across genres and a number of aliases, and on Verschiebung he explores misty, muted techno.

title: What Now?
description: The experimental soul musician's adventurous debut album draws as much from free jazz and IDM as it does funk and R&B, from the Dirty Projectors as much as D'Angelo.

title: Flood Network
description: Part of the appeal of Melbourne bedroom-pop artist Katie Dey’s latest is the voyeuristic thrill of hearing knotty music made to satisfy nobody but its author, sometimes at the audience’s exclusion.

title: Interior Architecture
description: This expansive double LP from Los Angeles producer M. Geddes Gengras collects four modular synth compositions with a lush, liquid sound. They are rewarding in their instability.

title: The Land OST
description: Nas executive-produced the film and soundtrack The Land, the sort of coming-of-age tale that hip-hop once produced in abundance. The soundtrack features Nas, Erykah Badu, Kanye, Pusha T, and more.

title: Well Worn
description: The Australian duo Kllo is consistent in its commitment to moodily lit, immaculately appointed spaces—to stylish understatement at all costs.

title: Sweatbox Dynasty
description: Thomas Fec (aka Tobacco) has trafficked over the years in the weird, the uncanny, the not-quite-right. His new album tries for a slightly less confrontational, still-unconventional take on synthpop.

title: Start Your Own Fucking Show Space
description: *Start Your Own Fucking Show Space *is a loving and lovable tribute to the Brooklyn DIY space Death by Audio

title: Suicide Squad: The Album
description: Featuring Skrillex, Rick Ross, Grimes, Kehlani, Lil Wayne, and many (many) others, the Suicide Squad OST feels as grim and stapled-together as the movie.

title: Generationwhy
description: Zhu first gained attention with massive 2014 last-call club hit “Faded,” but his debut album is bloated with bland, often downright bad dance music.

title: Cluster Ensemble: Plays Philip Glass
description: The Cluster Ensemble tackles some of Philip Glass's iconic early works, playing them more crisply and clearly than perhaps any other recording in history.

title: Phantoms of Dreamland
description: Each cut on the obscure British-born, Swiss-based musician Michal Turtle's Phantoms of Dreamland presents a strange-yet-charming self-contained little sound world.

title: Boy King
description: Wild Beasts' Boy King replaces the ornate detail of its predecessors with machine-tooled funk and pitch-shifted gasps. It's by no means a disaster, but it is a disappointment.

title: Dangerous
description: At the time of Dangerous, Michael Jackson's universal popularity was on par with pizza and the polio vaccine. It was the last time that Michael Jackson was Michael Jackson.

title: Cam & China
description: Cam & China, twins from Inglewood and veterans of L.A.’s jerkin’ scene, are uniquely attuned to one another,  resulting in some of the year’s fiercest, most viscerally exciting rap music.

title: Lovers
description: Romantic “mood music” isn’t what most listeners expect from Nels Cline, but on his Blue Note debut, the Wilco guitarist delivers a chamber-orchestra set that visits some American songbook standards.

title: Revisions of the Past
description: Revisions of the Past reissues two albums by Panopticon, the solo vehicle of Minnesota-via-Kentucky black metal musician Austin Lunn, here remastered by Colin Marston of Krallice, Gorguts, and others.

title: How It Feels to Be Something On
description: Sunny Day Real Estate admired Fugazi's ethics, but dreamed of being Led Zeppelin and U2, bands that aspired for total transcendence—something they finally achieved on How It Feels to Be Something O**n.

title: Circle of Light
description: Delia Derbyshire was an unsung early pioneer in electronic music, and her score for the 1972 film Circle of Light is the longest single piece of recorded music of hers to see release yet.

title: Major Key
description: Major Key is DJ Khaled’s ninth studio album in 10 years, and it’s undoubtedly his best. Depending where you stand on the Khaled spectrum, that may mean nothing or everything.

title: Night Melody
description: Electronic musician Ryan West's latest release as Rival Consoles has a level of warmth and humanity missing from his earlier records. This is his most expressive and emotional music yet.

title: 1-800 DINOSAUR Presents Trim
description: Grime outsider Trim teams up with James Blake and other members of the British electronic music scene for an intriguing, somewhat-cluttered collaborative mixtape.

title: No Beer, No Dad
description: Portland band Blowout's exuberant debut conveys the sense of being so overwhelmed by frustration, excitement, or any feeling really, that it must be acted on, coordination be damned.

title: Hypercaffium Spazzinate
description: *Hypercaffium Spazzinate *is the first LP in over 12 years from the California pop-punk icons, and it relies on the same humor, honesty, and personal experience that has always powered their music.

title: Impossible Dream
description: Haley Bonar’s Impossible Dream is a brisk half-hour of barbed power-pop tunes that sting so sweetly that it’s only after the fact you consider you might need a tetanus shot.

title: The Perfect Luv Tape
description: Lil Uzi Vert's latest mixtape comes at a moment of fever-pitch buzz for the young rapper, reaffirming his talent for synthesizing trends into a catchy melodic soup.

title: Spend the Night With...
description: Cheena is composed of members from noise and hardcore outfits like Pharmakon and Anasazi, but on their debut, they are a rock band, pure and simple, channeling the New York Dolls.

title: Hangin’ At the Beach
description: Producer Delroy Edwards combines the faded ‘80s vibe of Ariel Pink and John Maus with a sharp eye toward what moves bodies on dance floors today.

title: Give a Glimpse of What Yer Not
description: The latest from the re-reconstituted Dinosaur Jr. proves the equilibrium they discovered on their 2007 comeback Beyond remains intact.

title: Jaguar Mirror
description: While only four tracks and under 20 minutes of music, the Swedish duo Thunder Tillman’s debut EP spans continents.

title: For All We Know
description: On For All We Know, Nao autopsies various relationships—with friends, lovers, outgrown versions of herself—and, having decided what went wrong, calmly takes down the perpetrators.

title: The King of Whys
description: Mike Kinsella expresses ugly sentiments with inverse beauty in Owen's acoustic-heavy return.

title: Shy Layers
description: Shy Layers’ debut is one of the year's great, unexpected pleasures: a deeply engaging, effortlessly listenable collection of Balearic pop with overtones of yacht rock, Kraftwerk, and Graceland.

title: 4OKI
description: Steve Aoki’s latest EP, 4OKI, is a cheap, placebo imitation of a party.

title: The Disco’s of Imhotep
description: The Disco’s of Imhotep is dance-music outsider Jamal Moss's most approachable collection to date while not diluting his music’s signature oddity.

title: Music Inspired by Philippe Garrel’s Le Révélateur
description: Harpist Mary Lattimore, who has worked with Thurston Moore and Sharon Van Etten, teams with mult-instrumentalist and War on Drugs producer Jeff Zeigler for a hypnotizing, semi-improvised score.

title: 25 Years of Musical Deviance
description: This box packages most of Meshuggah’s recorded work—7 studio albums and 3 EPs—and offers an overview of how this extreme metal band pushed the entire genre head-first into the future.

title: Take Down
description: With the debut of his new project Metronome, Mikel Rouse reaches the rarified level of production ambition he first achieved in the ’80s, as he weaved together classical, electronic, and indie rock.

title: S+@dium Rock: Five Nights at the Opera
description: This raucous, epic live album compiles several nights' worth of shows at the Brooklyn venue Shea Stadium, where Titus Andronicus celebrated the release of 2015's The Most Lamentable Tragedy.

title: Blood Sugar Sex Magik
description: On their 1991 breakthrough album, the Red Hot Chili Peppers were the partially-clothed id, barreling toward the funk and stumbling across inclusiveness along the way.

title: The Philips Years
description: The Philips Years is a humble title for a collection that contains some of the most important, moving documents of American history. Nina Simone’s Philips records remain her most essential.

title: Drool Sucker
description: The unpredictable Drool Sucker kicks off a series of EPs from the transcontinental band No Joy in which they attempt to shake off the “shoegaze revival” tag once and for all.

title: Stranger to Violence
description: The Queens, New York-based outfit Psalm Zero explore the fertile territory between metal and new wave on their sophomore album.

title: Sky Girl
description: Two French DJs evoke heartbreak and desolation in a compilation of little-heard gems.

title: A Mulher do Fim do Mundo (The Woman at the End of the World)
description: 79-year-old samba icon and Brazilian national hero Elza Soares offers a searing, surging fusion that combines Afro-Brazilian styles with wiry, dissonant strands of punk and noise-rock.

title: Boleros Valses y Mas
description: The Los Angeles producer's first Stones Throw release takes the bolero, the valse, and other traditional Latin forms and plays them on a solitary Oberheim synthesizer.

title: D.T.S.N.T.
description: The quietly virtuosic Parisian producer STWO worked on Drake’s “Weston Road Flows” from VIEWS, and his debut EP is chock-full of impressive guest vocalists, testifying to his ear for talent.

title: Let Me Hang You
description: Let Me Hang You is the result of long-shelved sessions from the 1990s, during which Burroughs recited some favorite riffs from Naked Lunch. The album conjures only a portion of the book’s wild power.

title: Late Nights: Europe
description: Reportedly recorded in 2 weeks, Late Nights: Europe is a polished, 14-track libertine manifesto, wrapping up a trilogy of odes to the grown and sexy. Featuring Ty Dolla $ign, Wiz Khalifa, and more.

title: Lil Durk 2X
description: After a forgettable Def Jam debut, 2x realizes Durk’s full potential as drill’s last major-label hope.

title: The Bird & the Rifle
description: On her Dave Cobb-produced latest, country singer/songwriter Lori McKenna shows her remarkable facility for conveying the inner lives of women trapped in soured relationships.

title: Noise Patterns
description: Composer, designer and programmer Tristan Perich uses very small objects—microchips—to pose very big questions about art, music, and the state of the “album.”

title: Unfinished
description: On his sixth release, lo-fi techno producer Florian Kupfer creates music as airy and pleasantly rudimentary as a papier-mâché sculpture.

title: Dead Revolution
description: John Cobbett is one of modern metal’s premier guitarists. In Hammers of Misfortune, he reinvigorates ’70s progressive rock and the hard rock of Deep Purple, Rainbow, and Uli Jon Roth-era Scorpions.

title: Summer Songs 2
description: On his latest mixtape, the divisive Atlanta rapper sounds best when chasing fresher, weirder, spacier styles instead of trying to live up to hip-hop’s storied traditions.

title: Guidance
description: There's an organic and unforced feel to the latest album by Chicago-based post-rock trio Russian Circles, as if songs were allowed to grow wild rather than carefully cultivated.

title: Command Your Weather
description: The duo Big Business’ latest is an anxious and adventurous little record, too eccentric and playful to be accepted as metal but too loaded and loud to be taken as most anything else.

title: This Is Gap Dream
description: Gap Dream's morose new record documents a music nerd's midlife meltdown, over junk-littered garage rock, rudimentary synth-pop, and no-budget prog flourishes.

title: Everybody Looking
description: Emerging from prison clean and sober in May, Gucci Mane releases an album looking to capitalize on his massive influence. Featuring Kanye West, Young Thug, and Drake.

title: Young Jefe 2
description: On the sequel to his breakout 2014 mixtape, the Washington, D.C. rapper Shy Glizzy is simply a joy to listen to, one of the most distinctive and technically adventurous rappers working today.

title: Titans in the Flesh
description: With their second collaborative project, this rapper/producer duo offer a well-studied paean to hip-hop’s past. You could call it a boom baptism.

title: Love & Hate
description: Singer Michael Kiwanuka’s new album* *is a sprawling soul opus full of longing and self-assessment.  It's a bittersweet offering, growing more melancholy as it plays.

title: Songs and Jams Vol. 1
description: Few post-punk outfits deliver their most accomplished album 36 years after putting out a debut single. Yet the story of Philadelphia’s Notekillers has rarely been a typical one.

title: Coolaid
description: On Snoop Dogg’s 14th studio album Coolaid, he returns to hip-hop as both a resident and a tourist.

title: Sound Signature Presents: These Songs That Should've Been Out on Wax By Now
description: Theo Parrish might have gotten screwed over at the vinyl-pressing plant, but as a result, we got two volumes of this very-bluntly-named collection of moving, diffuse, spare, soul-deep jams.

title: Buhloone Mindstate
description: De La Soul’s knotty and brilliant third album is a fever dream of shared memories, historical touchstones, geographical landmarks, first-person pronouns and six feet-deep self­-actualizations.

title: Savage Mode
description: On Savage Mode, the dry-voiced and deadpan trap rapper 21 Savage recounts a life that has known nothing but violence. It's his strongest release, thanks to sleek production by Metro Boomin.

title: Cistern
description: Composer and songwriter Jherek Bischoff's third record is an oceanic song cycle that encourages listeners to drop down into their own mind, a safe space in the dark where they are comfortably alone.

title: Ambulance
description: On their gloomy new record, the psych-rockers the Amazing grab hold of a small range of emotions—depression, regret, angst, longing—and hang on for dear life.

title: Call by Night
description: Fresh & Onlys guitarist Wymond Miles cultivates an arch air of high drama in his solo LPs. The songs on Call By Night touch on the exhilaration that sometimes accompanies sadness and uncertainty.

title: No Hard Feelings
description: Chicago rapper Dreezy is a drill-adjacent upstart from the South Side, and her major-label debut is a fully-formed offering that seamlessly balances rugged raps with pristine pop songs.

title: HEAVN
description: With the assistance of fellow Chicagoans Chance the Rapper, Saba, and Kweku Collins, R&B artist Jamila Woods makes vital, resonant protest music that sounds like a children’s playground.

title: Mono No Aware
description: The British punk band Johnny Foreigner’s songs often seem made up of components of older emo and pop-punk songs, but remembered wrong, reversed and compressed into anxious nodes.

title: Horror Zone
description: Though 40 years have passed between albums, roots reggae legend Max Romeo's latest picks up right where the classic Lee “Scratch” Perry-produced War Ina Babylon left off.

title: PRINCESS
description: The Atlanta singer/producer Abra makes vintage, '80s-sounding R&B with the production values and aesthetic of bedroom pop.

title: Centres
description: Ian William Craig's Centres is a swirling and alchemical blend of drone, keyboards, and manipulated vocals. The more time you spend with it, the further you will want to get lost in it.

title: Community Service 2!
description: Chance the Rapper compatriot Towkio sometimes raps great, vivid tales about his life in Chicago. Sometime’s he’s funny and weird. And sometimes he falls victim to cruddy trap beats and generic lyrics.

title: Indifferent Rivers Romance End
description: The California duo Wreck and Reference strip away the basics of metal, redefining the genre even as they sit outside it. On their new album, their songcraft catches up to their uncompromising gloom.

title: IV
description: On their fourth record, the succinctly titled IV, BADBADNOTGOOD rein in their jam-band impulses, delivering a velvet-crushed portrait of an effervescent lounge act in the 21st century.

title: Operator
description: More than any other MSTRKRFT release, *Operator *sounds like the work of a band — one with punk DNA coursing through its army of analog synths.

title: Pylon Live
description: The Athens, Georgia group Pylon were one of the great unsung heroes of '80s post-punk, and Live captures them in December 1983 at the peak of their local popularity.
The Berlin- and London-based photographer Wolfgang Tillmans has long had ties to music and club culture, and now he has released a musing and quizzical techno release of his own.

title: Camp Cope
description: This Melbourne trio's effusive, empathic, and emphatic indie-rock debut examines shame the way 69 Love Songs x-rays love.

title: 32 Levels
description: The influential hip-hop producer's debut album, 32 Levels, has two distinct sides: a uniformly strong rap side and a pop side that’s not nearly as engaging or distinctive.

title: Elysia Crampton Presents: Demon City
description: Demon City, Virginia producer Elysia Crampton's follow-up to her sumptuous debut American Drift, is a wonder of concision and represents another massive leap forward in her growth.

title: Caramel
description: Konx-om-Pax is the project of electronic musician Tom Scholefield. His second LP Caramel fondly invokes nostalgia for the rave era, playing like the faded tracers and seared after-images that remain.

title: Devotional Songs
description: Shackleton, who has made himself a genre of one with his dark, dramatic dub-inspired work, takes a turn toward the operatic.

title: Tusk
description: Fleetwood Mac’s beautiful and terrifically strange 1979 LP, Tusk, poses the question: What happens when love dissipates, and you have to find a new thing to believe in? What if that thing is work?

title: Sketches from an Island 2
description: The British-born producer Mark Barrott played a big role in establishing the Balearic sound. Sketches from an Island 2 is the rare sequel that improves on the original.

title: 3 Way
description: Migos found the perfect moment to drop their short but potent EP 3-Way.

title: Hit Reset
description: The Julie Ruin’s second album, Hit Reset, is bandleader and punk icon Kathleen Hanna's most commanding release since her manifesto-writing days.

title: Eleven into Fifteen: a 130701 Compilation
description: Eleven Into Fifteen: a 130701 Compilation is a new anthology pulling unreleased work from 130701’s roster, celebrating not just the label but the hazily-defined genre of “post-classical.”

title: The Columbia Years 1968-69
