He disappeared in the late 90s, but returned last year: Drained of Connotation, a collection of solo pieces he made in 1982 using a synth and a drum machine, shows his recent beat-oriented mindset didn't come out of nowhere.

title: Divine Ecstasy
description: Chicago production duo Supreme Cuts' Whispers in the Dark was a strikingly trendy and sometimes engrossing stew of bass beats that seemed more eager to confound than galvanize. Alongside a number of vocal collaborators on their new album Divine Ecstasy, Supreme Cuts shoot for the anthemic but come up measurably short.

title: The Green EP
description: Electronic producer Bibio's new Green EP collects outtakes from last year's Silver Wilkinson. Like the album from which it was derived, the Green EP is pleasantly moody.

title: Nixon
description: When Nixon was released in 2000, it was immediately enshrined by the British music press, though most people in America continued to have no idea who Lambchop were. Merge's 2xCD reissue of the Nashville country/soul troupe's sumptuous fifth collection also offers the White Sessions 1998: How I Met Cat Power, a set by singer Kurt Wagner on French radio.

title: 20th Adversary of Emptiness
description: Just as rock'n'roll has its shadow canon, the Trout Mask Replicas and SMiLEs that offset the Revolvers and Blonde on Blondes, extreme metal has an alternate-universe hall of fame. The 1993 collection Nespithe, the only LP released by the eccentric Finnish death metal band Demilich, is one of these. This 3xLP/2xCD retrospective packages it with everything the brainiac obsessives ever recorded.

title: Wedding Bells EP
description: On the second EP from Cashmere Cat—the alias of Norwegian electronic producer Magnus August Høiberg*—*he ramps up the twinkly, diaphanous, twee elements in his arsenal.

title: Innocence
description: Though by no means a "comeback" record, the latest from Blue Ridge rockers Pontiak, Innocence, does have a whiff of rejuvenation about it.

title: Ghettoville
description: Darren Cunningham's fourth album as Actress is a record that takes his fascinations—Detroit techno, Chicago ghetto house, rap—and repeatedly kicks them in the ribs. After three collections that played Jenga with genre rules, Ghettoville is content to wallow in the ruins of the musics its predecessors so fascinatingly deconstructed.

title: Thirtysixtwentyfive / Misnomer / Glasshead / Dialogue
description: Earlier this year Kieran Hebden opened a Bandcamp account, offering streams and downloads of three early Four Tet EPs and the full-length Dialogue. The material dates to the late 1990s, when Four Tet was more of a side project for Hebden, and when his attention fell mostly on his three-piece band, Fridge.

title: Malleus Maleficarum
description: On their second LP, Malleus Maleficarum, the Knoxville, Tenn., trio Argentinum Astrum aim to bridge the gap between doom and black metal. The DIY production values are subterranean, blanketing the recording in a thick miasma of distortion and soot.

title: Morgan Delt
description: California native Morgan Delt is a homegrown musician whose debut evades convenient pigeonholing. The collection is a carefully built mosaic of jangly power pop, fuzzed out martian rock, and did-it-myself B-movie soundtracking that dissolves into a melted mess.

title: Trouble
description: On their second album, Hospitality move beyond the catchy indie-pop of their 2012 debut. With Trouble, the Amber Papini-led Brooklyn trio make a point of showing their listeners the difference between "beautiful" and "cute.

title: Come to Life
description: Memphis rapper Cities Aviv continues to exist outside neat genre lines, mixing spacey production and rock aggression into a distinctive and personal style.

title: Too True
description: Dum Dum Girls mastermind Dee Dee has been flirting with, and stepping tentatively back from, full-fledged stardom ever since she introduced herself to us. Her well-crafted third album is sparkling and beautiful, a glittering glaze of guitars and keyboards.

title: Lord Steppington
description: The Alchemist and Dilated Peoples' Evidence bring their shared understanding of the history and context of rap (and a guest list that includes Domo Genesis, Action Bronson, Styles P, and Blu) to their new project Lord Steppington, a welcome addition to the collection of solid boom-bap rap albums that Alchemist has helmed over the last few years.

title: Drowners
description: On their self-titled debut, the New York-based post-punk band Drowners, fronted by Welsh male-model/musician Matt Hitt, recall early Strokes and Arctic Monkeys. Their willingness and ability to sound like two and only two bands is actually kind of impressive.

title: Where Shine New Lights
description: Tara Jane O'Neil's first solo LP in five years finds the ex-Rodan bassist, painter, constant collaborator, and tireless solo experimenter carving scenery out of sound. It's quite possibly the finest merging of the chameleonic O'Neil's song-based work and her more experimental side.

title: Abandoned Apartments
description: Jeremy Jay, who's been signed to Calvin Johnson's K Records for years, has an ongoing fascination with dreams and cinema, and an aesthete's ear for perfect little sounds. His newest collection, Abandoned Apartments, is more nocturnal and forlorn than 2011's Dream Diary.

title: Transgender Dysphoria Blues
description: On their sixth album Transgender Dysphoria Blues, Laura Jane Grace and Against Me! draw a hard line between “identity” and “ideology.” Produced by Grace and put out on her own label Total Treble, the band splits the difference from old and new into a compact sound that skews more Sex Pistols than Foo Fighters.

title: Michael Lee Yonkers / Borders of My Mind
description: As new albums from Minneapolis cult hero Michael Lee Yonkers have come to light, it seems as if his breakthrough Microminiature Love’s raving, avant-garage inclinations were just a blip. The new Drag City reissues of two of his early-70s albums show just how much country and folk were part of Yonkers’s idiosyncratic musical worldview.

title: From All Purity
description: The Chicago blackened doom band Indian's fifth album wields as much power from a distance as it does in close quarters. With ex-Wolves in the Throne Room guitarist Will Lindsay re-enlisting to split guitars and vocals, and Bloodyminded mastermind Mark Solotroff adding sheets of  noise, it's an album whose every layer seems customized and every crease deliberate.

title: Brothers and Sisters of the Eternal Son
description: Damien Jurado’s 11th album, Brothers and Sisters of the Eternal Son, is the third piece in a Richard Swift-produced triptych that began with 2010’s St. Bartlett and continued on 2012’s Maraqopa. It's yet another leap into territory that Jurado has only touched on previously.

title: Spaces
description: The Berlin-based composer Nils Frahm's Spaces is a live album patchworked together from various recordings, containing songs both old and new, some shortened, some lengthened, some radically different in approach. It's a mesmerizing and beautiful work.

title: Have Fun With God
description: Have Fun With God is Bill Callahan and his mixer Brian Beattie's dub version of last year's excellent Dream River. It feels like a live, real-time dub, and in addition to this sense of spontaneity, the arrangements lend themselves well to the treatment.

title: Shy Boys
description: Kansas City indie pop trio Shy Boys' self-titled debut is a triumph of ramshackle aesthetics and homespun hooks. Instrumentally, Shy Boys is far from dazzling, but that doesn't seem to hold the group back.

title: Sanctuary: The Complete Discography
description: The relatively unheralded UK outfit Vex was an anarcho-punk band that sounded far more dark, desperate, raw, and apocalyptic than anything at the time. A new reissue of their lone release, 1984's Sanctuary, showcases a band throbbing with ominous, semi-industrial precision.

title: Light Show
description: Enigmatic L.A. musician Jack Name—who has also recorded as Muzz, Fictional Boys, and John Webster Johns—creates his own world on his new Light Show. It's Name's attempt at a rock opera, and even though it features catchy, immediate songs, it's an album that asks for focus and thought.

title: Tuck Box
description: The posthumous marketing of Nick Drake's music has been arduous and fitful, a decades-long attempt at setting right what everyone agreed went horribly wrong the first time. His new box set Tuck Box, the latest and possibly final repackaging, includes studio albums Five Leaves Left, Bryter Layter, and Pink Moon as well as two compilations of rarities.

title: Warpaint
description: The Los Angeles band Warpaint's three-years-in-the-making second album, featuring cover art from acclaimed video director Chris Cunningham, was produced by Flood and mixed by Nigel Godrich.

title: Edges
description: While peers adjusted from "post-dubstep" to techno and house, Toronto electronic duo Graze offered a fully-formed and distinct aesthetic on their self-titled debut. Its follow-up LP, Edges, strips their sound down to its bare essentials.

title: Shelter
description: The French outfit Alcest has been slowly turning away from the corrosive, ambient metal of their early work—a sound that’s influenced many, most notably Deafheaven—toward an unbroken dreamscape of cushiony shoegaze. Their fourth album, Shelter, produced by Birgir Jón Birgisson and featuring vocals from Slowdive’s Neil Halstead, marks that clean break.

title: Strong Feelings
description: On Doug Paisley's third album Strong Feelings, featuring guest vocals from Mary Margaret O’Hara, the Toronto alt-country artist seeks refuge in the beauty of the romantic lyrical metaphors that have populated the country genre since at least the heyday of Hank Williams.

title: Post Tropical
description: Irish singer James Vincent McMorrow's sophomore effort Post Tropical is an album that seems suited to winter. It features lyrics about “elements of frost” and “cold air” and taut, pensive songs that carry a pristine stillness.

artist: Thee Silver Mt. Zion Memorial Orchestra
title: Fuck Off Get Free We Pour Light on Everything
description: The orchestro-punk Godspeed offshoot Thee Silver Mt. Zion's excellent seventh album examines the difficulties of keeping one’s moral compass steady in a society that’s becoming ever-more indifferent to the things you value. The songs are more outwardly anthemic and viscerally rocking than Godspeed’s slow-surging, side-long epics.

title: Gay Disco
description: Led by vocalist Kassie Carlson, who evokes a tuned-up Kathleen Hanna or Molly Siegel of Ponytail, the Boston band Guerilla Toss channel the fractured funk of pre-Echoes Rapture, Black Dice's anti-grooves, and the tinnitus-beckoning mania of Lightning Bolt.

title: Fabriclive 73
description: On Pangea's Fabriclive 73 mix, Kevin McAuley uses the platform to articulate a compelling case for the state of UK techno in 2014. Fabriclive 73 is complex and confrontational but resolutely unshowy.

title: The Invention of Animals
description: The legendary Lounge Lizard and no wave filmmaker/actor John Lurie has always had a big personality, but he's also a consummate collaborator. The Invention of Animals is a collection of live recordings and studio tracks used for episodes of his "Fishing With John" series that he made with drummers Billy Martin and Calvin Weston.

title: Killed by Deathrock: Vol. 1
description: Sacred Bones' new odds-and-ends compilation Killed By Deathrock, which unearths bizarre modern punk bands who produce oddities and competent facsimiles of more popular bands, is pure fun.

title: Rave Tapes
description: Mogwai's eighth album outside their soundtrack and remix work has been framed in terms of its increased use of electronics. The instrumentation has indeed shifted, but Rave Tapes digs hard into a place they've consistently circled back to throughout their career.

title: Alternate / Endings
description: Lee Bannon broke through as one of the most promising producers associated with Joey Bada$$'s Pro Era crew, offering potent updates of beats forged by the likes of RZA and DJ Premier. Since then he's gotten weirder, and his drum and bass-inspired second album, Alternate/Endings, seems more interested in atmosphere than rhythm.

title: Eighteen Hours of Static
description: Throughout Eighteen Hours of Static, arty Brooklyn post-punkers Big Ups' howling debut LP, vocalist Joe Galarraga and company put the world on notice. For 28 minutes, no grievance goes unaired, and no blood's left unlet.

title: Chiaroscuro
description: Swedish electronic duo I Break Horses' sophomore LP Chiaroscuro finds a band deliberatly slowing down and simplifying their sound. But for all this reduction, I Break Horses are left with little that they can call their own.

title: Has God Seen My Shadow?: An Anthology 1989-2011
description: Even when he’s stealing the spotlight, Mark Lanegan still seems like he’s lurking in the shadows, not so much singing a song as haunting it. So it’s appropriate that Lanegan’s now receiving a tribute that most don't receive until they're dead, the career-spanning collection Has God Seen My Shadow?: An Anthology 1989-2011.

title: Bad Debt
description: Songwriter M.C. Taylor—who records as Hiss Golden Messenger—wrote Bad Debt in 2009, months after his son was born, and recorded it in his North Carolina kitchen. Destroyed in a warehouse fire and just now seeing wider re-release, Bad Debt is an album deeply concerned with the nature of faith and man’s relationship with his Maker.

title: Mr. Jones
description: In 2013, the Russian electronic producer and DJ Nina Kraviz was the focus of discussions on feminism and raw sexuality in club culture. Mr. Jones, her first material in 18 months, is a 54-minute double EP.

title: Audion X
description: Matthew Dear's dancefloor-oriented side project Audion was introduced in the middle of the last decade to provide an outlet for his baser desires. Audion X, offered up 10 years after the release of Audion's sole album, Suckfish, collects 18 tracks from a dozen-plus EPs and that album, and adds two new tracks in anticipation of a sophomore LP, due later this year.

title: The State vs. Radric Davis II: The Caged Bird Sings
description: On this Bandcamp release, Gucci gets ample assists from his usual Brick Squad brethren Young Thug, Peewee Longway, and Young Scooter as well as production help from 808 Mafia and Zaytoven.

title: Keep Doing What You're Doing
description: The Orlando emo band You Blew It!’s sophomore LP, Keep Doing What You’re Doing, is a deeply satisfying “airing of grievances” record. The group's poised to fill a role for frustrated listeners who can no longer find loud, angsty rock'n'roll via traditional indie channels.

title: White Light/White Heat
description: When the Velvet Underground's second album descended on the world in January, 1968, nobody was ready for it. As the story goes, it was a relentless, screeching, thudding, scoffing assault on the pop sensibilities of its time. For its 45th anniversary it's been reissued in expanded, remastered form, and listening to White Light/White Heat now, it doesn't quite fit the template of its legend.

title: The Soul Tape 3
description: Fabolous' The Soul Tape 3 is the third and final installment in his trilogy of soul-sample-heavy mixtapes, and it attempts to reinforce his status as a go-to for those in search of comfort food rap.

title: Cartography for Beginners: A Best of the Lucksmiths
description: Australian trio the Lucksmiths were exemplars of a certain kind of deliberately anti-macho indie-pop that would have made sense on Sarah Records or as part of the C86 scene. Their 16-year artistic evolution meant a slow, steady improvement in craft, making this the rare decade-plus retrospective where the later songs beat the early ones.

title: Broken Swenglish Vol. 1 EP
description: The four English-sung power-pop songs on Broken Swenglish were originally recorded in Swedish and found across a pair of Peter Morén solo albums he released outside his main gig in Peter Bjorn & John. The music's nearly identical to the originals, but the lyrics have shifted.

title: NOT O.K.
description: The amount of material Victor Vazquez has made in the year since Das Racist called it quits tops the total output of his previous gig. But despite being a collection of outtakes from his upcoming proper album, Not O.K. features the kind of roster (Toro Y Moi, Del Tha Funkee Homosapien, Ladybug Mecca from Digable Planets, etc.) that makes it feel like the biggest event of  his post-DR career.

title: Give the People What They Want
description: Even if the title of Sharon Jones and the Dap-Kings' fifth album invokes one of the more state-of-the-art slices of 70s soul as delivered by the O'Jays, Give the People What They Want finds the group staying in their late 1960s lane. It's an album built less on advancement than resilience.

title: The Shaw Tapes: Live in Detroit 5/27/88
description: Detroit punks the Gories' new archival release, The Shaw Tapes: Live in Detroit 5/27/88, showcases a slapdash snapshot of a young, feral gang of throwbacks reinventing a genre by uninventing it.

title: Forever
description: Forever, the debut LP from the San Francisco psych-pop duo Painted Palms, crafts a balmy sound that showcases their refind melodicism. However, its 39 minutes often run together.

title: Iller Than Most
description: Bay Area hip hop vet Del tha Funkee Homosapien's unexpected return—the low stakes, free mixtape *Iller Than Most—*is both ridiculously goofy and ridiculously fun.

title: Enter
description: Cybotron’s 1983 album, Enter, is widely considered to be where Detroit techno began. The collection's obsessed with the future as co-creators Juan Atkins and Richard Davis saw it, a vision dominated by the notion that human life would become so intertwined with technology that they’d be essentially inseparable.

title: Settle: The Remixes
description: Settle: The Remixes features Hudson Mohawke, Baauer, Totally Enormous Extinct Dinosaurs, Flume, DJ Premier, Larry Heard, and others remixing tracks from Disclosure's instant classic debut, along with two new originals.

title: Until the Colours Run
description: UK indie rockers Lanterns on the Lake’s second album Until the Colours Run is borne of loss, turmoil, and doubt on every level. The group expresses faded glory and missed opportunities while exhibiting potential with many rich sounds and potent concepts.

title: Grassed Inn
description: From the dense psych of 2010’s Headless Ark, to the damaged rock of 2012’s Go Easy, Aussie noise rockers Blank Realm have been tracing an arc toward accessibility. Their latest, Grassed Inn, is their most structured, tune-heavy album to date—as well as their best.

title: Marci Beaucoup
description: Over the course of his first two albums, New York rapper Roc Marciano established himself as one of the foremost purveyors of classicist New York slick-talk. His latest release, Marci Beaucoup, finds Marciano stepping out of the spotlight and focusing on his production chops.

title: Early Live Recordings
description: Early Live Recordings is a 2xCD set that digs into Ariel Pink’s earliest material, and while there are no exact dates to peg to these 36 tracks, the recordings appear to predate Pink’s inspired 21st century spurts. They are lo-fi recordings to say the least, heavy on detuned bass, lackadaisical tambourine rattles, and feral growls, all of it couched in tape murk.

title: High Hopes
description: Bruce Springsteen’s 18th record, High Hopes, is a collection of new recordings of songs he's been playing for 10 or 12 years. They're essentially outtakes from The Rising, Magic, and Working on a Dream*,* but Springsteen re-recorded them with producer Ron Aniello—often with Tom Morello on guitar—and sequenced them into an album.

title: Terminal Teen Age
description: Sick Thoughts is the garage punk project of Baltimore teenager Drew Owen. His exciting, impressive debut, Terminal Teen Age, delivers bug-eyed weirdness, screaming intensity, and a seemingly effortless knack for crafting hooks.

title: Battlefields Forever
description: After the demise of their longtime label Hydra Head, the Los Angeles heavy rock/light metal trio Big Business decided to release Battlefields Forever, their excellent fourth album, on their own. It turns out they're better at making records than marketing them.

title: Try Me
description: Over 10 years and dozens of releases—under their current name and as End of a Year—Self Defense Family have built themselves out of perversity, mixing black humor, jarring turns of phrase, and pop-culture references with open-hearted hardcore. Their official full-length debut, Try Me, strays even further from emo fundamentalism.

title: Dirty Gold
description: No one will come away from New York-via-Detroit rapper Angel Haze's major label debut doubting her natural talent, but Dirty Gold lacks the spark and distinct personality of a proper coming-out.

title: EP-2
description: The resurrected Pixies' EP-2 dates from the same recording sessions as last year's EP-1. The four new songs here are less blank than the four on the first, but the gulf between the feel this music has on the mind and the name on the cover remains jarring.

title: Dr. Stokley
description: Dr. Stokley represents a synthesis of Stones Throw rapper and singer Dudley Perkins’ career, combining his relatively grounded early days as Declaime with the funk, soul, and afrocentric mysticism that he’s embraced in his later years.

title: River of Souls
description: Tim Cohen wrote the songs for River of Souls with backup singers in mind. He’s said the only thing that separates his Magic Trick material from his work with the Fresh & Onlys are the two bands’ personnel, but this breezy collection is all about beauty and sheen.

title: Dell'Universo Assente
description: As one might expect that with a title like 'The Absent Universe," the reissue of style-sampling Italian composer Luciano Cilio's Dell'Universo Assente is a spare album, its pleasures revealed through careful listening rather than quick snippets. Not a single note or gesture feels out of place.

title: Spezmodia EP
description: Jettisoning most of the 2012 "comeback" LP Parastrophics' sonic jumble for something more explicitly streamlined, Spezmodia represents one of Mouse on Mars' sharpest left turns in the past decade. On these five-songs, they shape their taste for aggressive textures into new, more dancefloor-ready molds.

title: The Abstract And The Dragon
description: The new collaborative project from New York Native Tongue veterans Q-Tip and Busta Rhymes, The Abstract and the Dragon, features a handful of interesting exclusives but mostly revised older work. The new cuts, in particular, showcase a madcap chemistry unblemished by the passage of time.

title: Clapper Is Still
description: Each homespun song on "pastoral punk" duo Way Through's new Clapper Is Still >plots a course through England's history. It's a noisy, warm record filled with chaos and constant upheaval.

title: The Ancient Tonalities Of…
description: The best tracks from this Finnish producer fall somewhere in the middle of Kompakt's crushed-ice prettiness, Border Community's glowing pastoral techno, and the enveloping analog warmth of Warp's ambient outposts.

title: Wind In Lonely Fences 1970 - 2011
description: Harold Budd's music exists somewhere between ambient, new age, and minimalism. Wind in Lonely Fences is a 2xCD retrospective of the prolific composer—with as many albums as Budd has to choose from and no responsibility to things like radio hits, the job of the compiler becomes an unusually creative one.

title: Drilluminati 2
description: Though Chicago drill veteran King L has splashed around in other styles, his new mixtape Drilluminati 2 emphasizes his music is very self-contained.

title: Instrumental Tape 3
description: Producer Mike Volpe, aka Clams Casino, released his third instrumental mixtape for free on Twitter just before 2013 came to a close. This final installment in the series features beats for A$AP Rocky, Mac Miller, Mikky Ekko, DOOM, a remix, and three previously unreleased originals.

title: Retrieval
description: Mamiffer's Faith Coloccia runs SIGE Records with husband and frequent collaborator, ISIS co-founder Aaron Turner. Her debut with Chicago multi-instrumentalist Alex Barnett of Oakeater offers warped AM radio transmissions comingling with soporific beats, Motorik clicks riding beneath keyboard nightmares.

title: Justus Köhncke & the Wonderful Frequency Band
description: Although the new album from Kompakt Records tentpole Justus Köhncke boasts a characteristic mix of mid-tempo house, techno, disco and kitschy pop, it’s hardly a definitive statement.

title: There’s A Dream I’ve Been Saving: Lee Hazlewood Industries 1966–1971
description: The four-disc box set There's A Dream I've Been Saving chronicles the output of Lee Hazlewood’s California-based LHI label during the prime of the hippie era, and it’s steeped in the bright, balmy Hollywood atmosphere from whence it came.

title: L.I.E.S. Presents: Music for Shut-Ins
description: The title of L.I.E.S.' two-and-a-half-hour second label-summating compilation, Music for Shut-Ins, may or may not playfully allude to the forward thinking dance imprint's reputation for fringe-originating dance music. But the collection approaches a perverted accessibility.

title: Wig Out at Jagbags
description: Most of Stephen Malkmus' newest solo effort, Wig Out at Jagbags, sounds like 70s guitar-rock rendered as some kind of ergonomic desk toy: compact, brightly colored, unlikely to stir the depths of the soul but nifty nevertheless. He's never resisted age but has never seemed younger.

title: Hallelujah All the Way Home / Juvenilia
description: Captured Tracks' reissues of the Flying Nun catalogue continue with two releases by New Zealand's the Verlaines. Hallelujah All the Way Home is the post-punk band’s first album from 1985, and Juvenilia is a 1987 compilation.

title: A Fallen Empire
description: The music of Berlin-based Brit Samuel Kerridge bears a pitch-black complexion that firmly positions it alongside an entire strain of current electronic music. However, on his new A Fallen Empire, Kerridge incorporates different electronic shades than his peers, making the release stand apart.

title: Journey of the Deep Sea Dweller IV
description: This is the fourth and final volume of Dutch imprint Clone’s Drexciya reissue series, which gathers out-of-print music from the difficult-to-classify Detroit electronic music project. This set contains some of the group's spikiest electro, as well as music that has the raw spirit of punk.

title: The Block Brochure: Welcome To the Soil, Pt. 4, 5, & 6
description: Making great rap music is a reason to live for Bay Area legend E-40, whose fierce new The Block Brochure: Welcome To the Soil installments act as a fountain of youth.

title: Beyoncé
description: Beyoncé’s fifth album, surprise-released on iTunes in December, finds the singer hitting a new peak. Working with a large cast of collaborators, she shifts gears to pull off her most explicit and sonically experimental music to date, exploring sounds and ideas at the grittier margins of popular music.

title: Saâda Bonaire
description: Saâda Bonaire, the model-esque non-singers Stefanie Lange and Claudia Hossfeld, released their lone single in 1984. This unexpected reissue from Captured Tracks under their Fantasy Memory subsidiary reveals that the project was the concoction of Ralph “Von” Richtoven, a Bremen club DJ, and produced by dubmaster Dennis Bovell in Kraftwerk’s Cologne studios.

title: Fair
description: This six-track debut album from the Brooklyn-based producer Bryce Hackford might look like an EP on the surface, but it explores the trancey side of house music at great length, creatively mixing in rock dynamics along the way.

title: The First And Last Days Of Unwelcome
description: Lumbar is the doom metal trio of Aaron Edge, Yob’s Mike Scheidt and Tad's Tad Doyle. They took their name in honor of the three spinal taps Edge endured for a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, a diagnosis that may mean this remarkable debut is their last.

title: BOOT!
description: Swedish/Norwegian trio the Thing—who've covered the Cramps, the Sonics, and PJ Harvey and collaborated with Jim O’Rourke, Peter Brötzmann, and Merzbow—play free jazz you can stage dive to. Their sixth album, Boot!, is among the group’s finest efforts at pairing bludgeoning physicality with heady free jazz chops.

title: Rival Dealer EP
description: Burial's new EP, Rival Dealer, arrives almost exactly a year after the release of Truant/Rough Sleeper, but the stylistic leaps made on this release are wider, more jarring and revelatory, than anything in Burial's catalog. It's unquestionably the strongest release of his since 2012's Kindred, and his most satisfying statement of purpose since 2007's Untrue.

title: Blue Rider
description: On singer-songwriter Zachary Cale's fourth album, Blue Rider, you're forcefully reminded that acoustic solo music is only as simple as you make it. It's a misty, gorgeous collection, offering a space that feels wonderful to roam around in.

title: Patricidal Lust
description: On Patricidal Lust, one of the strongest metal releases of the year, the Bay Area death metal group Vastum deliver a record about sex that takes a grisly look at erotic tension at its most extreme.

title: The Love Champion
description: NYC singer Ian Isiah's The Love Champion features beats that would turn Tricky Stewart's head, guest spots from Le1f and Mykki Blanco, and charismatic vocals drowned in AutoTune. Backed by producers like Sinjin Hawke, Brenmar, and ShyGuy, it's hard not to see parallels with Kelela's Cut 4 Me.

title: Remainderer EP
description: Despite the leftovers its title implies, The Remainderer EP is being touted by the Fall’s label as “a bridging point” between 2013's spirited if sloppy full-length, Re-Mit, and another new album coming in 2014.

title: Because the Internet
description: The onetime 30 Rock writer and Community star Donald Glover’s newest Childish Gambino album is a multi-platform project that includes guest spots from Chance the Rapper, Azealia Banks, Problem, Mystikal, Miguel, and Jhené Aiko, among others.

title: Omen Ex Simulacra
description: On their second album Omen Ex Simulacra, the Oregon/Illinois duo Ævangelist create an aural monster, a horrific re-imagining of black/death metal coupled with harsh electronic noise and industrial mechanization.

title: Spit
description: Ron Morelli has spent the last three years building his L.I.E.S. label into a paragon of noisy, Made-in-the-U.S.A. club music. Spit, the first music under his own name released on Dominick Fernow's Hospital Productions, defies the type of romantic, back-to-basic engagement L.I.E.S. inspires.

title: School Daze
description: Sex was the thematic preoccupation of producer Patrick Cowley, reflecting the strong connection between disco and gay bathhouses in late-70s San Francisco. Fittingly, the first concrete attempt to canonise Cowley as an electronic music auteur is a compilation of his soundtrack work for gay pornographic films.

title: Nina
description: Here Xiu Xiu takes on the Nina Simone songbook, offering covers of songs like "Don't Explain", "Wild Is the Wind", and "Four Women". While the concept looks intriguing on paper, the execution leaves something to be desired.

title: Live at the Cellar Door
description: This 1970 solo acoustic set at D.C.'s Cellar Door catches Neil Young in a bleak, hollow mood, rudely awoken from the hippie dream his audience still wants to believe. Amidst an accumulation of dark, druggy vibes, Live at the Cellar Door shows Young peeking over the edge of the 60s into the dark chasm of the next decade.

title: Kok EP
description: Norwegian house producer Bjørn Torske builds enveloping shapes from the merest scraps of musical information and in recent years has been making loose disco edits of his own instrumental recordings. His new Kok EP feels like a concise alternate version of 2010's excellent Kokning mixed with headphones in mind.

title: Soundtracks for Takeshi Murata
description: Until now, Hair Police's Robert Beatty, who also records as Three Legged Race, has never released a collection under his given name. He made the abstract music on Soundtracks for Takeshi Murata to accompany the films of “digital video glitch pioneer” Takeshi Murata.

title: David Novick
description: As a member of San Francisco Water Cooler, David Novick plays abraded, candy-colored garage rock. But last October he released a muffled, strangely beatific self-titled psych-folk collection that's now being reissued by God?, a subsidiary of Drag City.

title: I Heard The Angels Singing: Electrifying Black Gospel
description: I Heard the Angels Singing: Electrifying Black Gospel from the Nashboro Label, 1951-1983 collects important songs from the catalogue of the Nashville gospel label Nashboro, painting a picture of a scene that was vital both musically and financially.

title: Black Panties
description: R. Kelly's 13th solo album Black Panties tosses aside the classic soul of his previous two albums in exchange for a deep dive into the sounds of contemporary bumping and grinding.

title: Step Brothers 2
description: Two years after their collaborative debut Step Brothers, Southern rappers Starlito and Don Trip present the for-retail sequel, a release that reveals two of the most honest writers in rap working together at maximum comfort and confidence.

title: Obscure Verses for the Multiverse
description: The Seattle black metal duo Inquisition's first album for major metal indie Season of Mist follows 2011's excellent Ominous Doctrines of the Perpetual Mystical Macrocosm. It's another impressive collection, one that's about as catchy as a pure black metal record has any right to be.

title: Syndrome Syndrome
description: On Syndrome Syndrome, the debut album from Australian electronic duo Gardland, there's a freeform feel that has more in common with the more experimental FRKWYS work than RVNG's regular releases.

title: Blazing Gentlemen
description: Robert Pollard's 2013 included a fine Guided by Voices EP, an okay GBV album, an unfailingly sweet solo collection, and a public fight with drummer Kevin Fennell. He closes the year with Blazing Gentlemen, a headier, rockier solo offering*.*

title: 7 Days of Funk
description: 7 Days of Funk is Snoop Dogg recording in laid back mode as “Snoopzilla” and Dâm-Funk revamping the classic synthesizer melodies, electronic basslines, and digital drums that coursed through funk both before and after they attached the “g-” to it. It was home-recorded and assembled quickly, and the easygoing nature shines through.

title: Within The Walls
description: On Bloodyminded's first album in seven years, the Chicago raw noise collective plows through harrowing drones, feedback bursts, mutated screams, static blitzes, and circuit collapses. There are imprecations hurled in English and Spanish and floods of sound so caustic and strong they rattle both brain and core.

title: No Dreams
description: On Noveller's new No Dreams, experimental musician Sarah Lipstate has added synth, beats, and other instrumental elements to her effect-heavy guitar soundscapes without dampening the impact of her cinematic music.

title: The Constant One
description: On the surface, Long Island emo outfit Iron Chic is cut from the same cloth as style forefathers like Saves the Day, but underneath the pop-punk veneer is one of the most flat-out fun indie rock guitar records of the year.

title: Cosmic Machine
description: The new compilation Cosmic Machine: A Voyage Across French Cosmic & Electronic Avantgarde (1970-1980) documents the roots of acts ranging from Daft Punk and Justice Todd Terje. At its most interesting, it shows the mercenary-like tendencies of these European musicians, changing from tweed to chiffon to tinfoil as the trends occurred.

title: Live at Brixton
description: Captured at a February 2012 gig in London, Live at Brixton, available both as an audio-only release and with video of the full concert, finds Mastodon barreling through 23 choice cuts from their five good-to-classic LPs, 2002's Remission through 2011's The Hunter.

title: Non-Drowsy
description: Physical Therapy's new Non-Drowsy is a free, seven-track EP that finds the producer mining the abundant melodicism of early 90s house and garage.

title: EOLIAN INSTATE EP
description: On London producer patten's new EP, his Warp debut, his sound remains much the same—a pulverised form of electronica tempered with a subtle melodic glow. However, these tracks are a touch more incisive than those on his debut GLAQJO XACCSSO.

title: Dominae
description: Ejecta is the slinky synth pop project of Neon Indian's Leanne Macomber and Joel Ford of Ford & Lopatin. Their debut builds a complex world out of an imagined narrator’s deepest longings.

title: Harmonie du Soir
description: Seminal downtown N.Y. composer Rhys Chatham's latest release, Harmonie due Soir, includes three pieces—his first ensemble of six guitars and drums since the mid-80s, a work for a 70-piece brass ensemble, and the screeching, clawing Drastic Classicism Revisited.

title: A Christmas Album
description: Bright Eyes' A Christmas Album, originally recorded in 2002, is a reissue that marries Yuletide memories with nostalgia for a time when Saddle Creek’s roster was still operating as a vibrant and prolific artistic community.

title: The Missing
description: The NY band Vaura features members of Gorguts, Dysrhythmia, Kayo Dot, Blacklist, and Religious to Damn. Their, at times, surprisingly poppy second album, The Missing, blends post-punk and black metal with feathered atmospherics and cavalier dexterity.

title: Re-Engineering
description: For his new album Re-Engineering, producer and artist Steve Warwick—who records as Heatsick— draws on a wide range of influences, be it his own art exhibition in Berlin, avant-garde dance music, or an overheard snippet of a street busker belting out an Oasis cover.

title: ARC of Fire EP
description: Following two LPs and a split with Grimes, Montreal singer/producer Chris d'Eon's debut EP as Kallisti is loaded with breakneck moments derived from 'ardkore and jungle's heyday. It's a million miles away from the glistening synth-pop of his previous releases.

title: Like A Dream EP
description: Save for production work on Drake’s Thank Me Later and the occasional performance piece, it’s been a quiet couple of years for Francis and the Lights. The Wesleyan-born pop R&B band's new EP is a brief outing, but it serves as a satisfying end to the silence.

title: SUM/ONE
description: Gang Gang Dance multi-tasker Brian DeGraw's debut LP under his bEEdEEgEE moniker features vocals from bandmate Lizzi Bougatsos, Hot Chip's Alexis Taylor, and others. His fondness for splicing up musical juxtapositions is executed with the same feel of floaty optimism that pervades the most recent GGD records.

title: CAPS LOCK
description: Since beginning his career in the late 90s, Japanese producer Yasutaka Nakata's maximalist take on electro-pop has gained favor with his some of his country's largest pop acts. His sparse new Caps Lock isn’t the easiest entry into his music, but features enough great moments to make people revisit his past.

title: Wot
description: Separated from his now defunct band, Sic Alps' frontman Mike Donovan and friend/collaborator Eric Park make acoustic rock influenced by the likes of Dylan and Haggard. The result, Wot, is a well-crafted record that's lyrically dwarfed by the old emoting masters.

title: Blood/Lines
description: Blood/Lines is California singer/songwriter Emily Jane White’s fourth album in four years, a recording pieced together from sketches that sprawls and stretches, prizing sustained melancholy over concise arrangements.

title: Lockjaw EP
description: After Chet Faker contributed vocals to “Left Alone”, a song from electronic producer Flume’s self-titled debut last year, the two Australians holed up for a week of recording that culminated in the three-track Lockjaw EP.

title: What The...
description: The new seventh Black Flag LP appears after a yearlong mire of dueling reunions, media mudslinging, a failed lawsuit and—less than a week prior to the record's street date—a fallout with vocalist Ron Reyes, who appears on the album. Amid all that, it's easy to forget it's the first new music in 28 years from one of the great American rock bands.

title: Everlast
description: The debut LP from singer Perera Elsewhere has the kind of breathy, sighing tone that complements trip-hoppy electronic music—the kind you'd expect to hear in the background at a public place. But laid naked on Everlast, the effect is beguiling and spooky.

title: Moods of Future Joy
description: Bristol producer Guido's 2010 debut Anidea succeeded by being graceful, accessible, infectious, and above all immensely fun. On his sophomore album Moods Of Future Joy, he settles for a middle ground, diluting a winning formula.

title: Harlem River
description: Kevin Morby, who played bass in Woods and the Babies and now resides in Los Angeles, offers a collection of intricately textured songs that function as a love letter to New York City.

title: Nothin’ to Look at Just a Record
description: Minimalist composer Phill Niblock asks a lot of you: most of his albums are long, and so are the individual pieces. The music itself is demanding, comprising held tones without percussion or anything conventionally used to mark time. But as the reissue of his 1982 debut, Nothin' to Look at Just a Record, and his new album, Touch Five, illustrate, it's also moving.

title: Live From KCRW
description: Live From KCRW was recorded last April during the week separating the Bad Seeds’ two appearances at Coachella before a small studio audience at the station’s famed Santa Monica studios. The Bad Seeds discography is hardly lacking for concert documents, but this something of a wild card among them.

title: Echoes
description: After a promising 2010 single, the Brooklyn-based duo CREEP surfaced only intermittently over the last three years, often as remixers, but also with occasional advances on their own take on trip-hop. Their oft-delayed debut album features Tricky, Sia, Planningtorock, the xx's Romy Madley Croft, Alejandra Deheza of School of Seven Bells, and others.

title: Desert Skies
description: Sixteen years after the initial sessions that birthed L.A. alt-country outfit Beachwood Sparks' new Desert Skies, they remain a surprisingly divisive band. Though strides are made, they don't have much of an answer for the detractors accusing them of imitating rather than innovating.

title: Fellow Travelers
description: This new 10-song collection, Fellow Travelers, finds Shearwater covering Xiu Xiu, Coldplay, Clinic, St. Vincent, Folk Implosion, and others. Interestingly, the title seems to let you know who Jonathan Meiburg and company see as their role models and their peers.

title: Event of Your Leaving
description: Raum is the collaborative project of Grouper's Liz Harris and Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, a solo artist and member of San Francisco post-rock band Tarentel. Both produce emotionally overwhelming drone abstractions with unconventional beauty, and their debut, Event of Your Leaving, is damaged and euphoric.

title: Singles Collection Volume Three
description: San Francisco garage icons Thee Oh Sees' latest Singles Collection serves as an excellent tasting-platter way to engage John Dwyer's prolific output. On this 10-song volume, Dwyer showcases a mixture of mania and stasis, a way of pacing while standing still.

title: Dorner vs. Tookie
description: Cali rapper Nocando’s Hellfyre Club is an assemblage of West Coast art rap luminaries connected to Project Blowed. On their new compilation Dorner vs. Tookie, the collective showcases a penchant for tongue-in-cheek self-flagellation and confessional storytelling.

title: Nun EP
description: The dance duo Teengirl Fantasy's new EP *Nun*, released in anticipation of their third full length due out this Spring, finds Nick Weiss and Logan Takahashi subtly tweaking their sound, offering their most colorful, futuristic work to date.

title: Shine Your Light
description: Gap Dream frontman Gabe Fulvimar lives inside the Fullerton, Calif., record store that also happens to be his label's office. Fittingly, his debut collection of loner power pop spans the gamut of styles you’d expect from a record store guy, i.e., Beach Boys, Eno, Can, Velvet Underground, and the forgotten bands that were influenced by them.

title: Don't Tell the Driver
description: On Australian guitarist and Dirty Three member Mick Turner's new album Don’t Tell the Driver, Turner favors listing rhythms and loose meters. Over eleven carefully yet imaginatively arranged songs, its music suggests unrehearsed spontaneity but also tribulation and peril.

title: Jetlag
description: Michael Milosh, the Toronto-based singer/producer who fronts Rhye, has been releasing his own music for nearly a decade. If you discovered Milosh via Rhye, don’t expect to hear his unmistakeable voice surrounded by the same kind of silky soul on this chilly solo offering.

title: Stealth of Days
description: In a dance music scene striving for experimentation, Nasvhille electronic duo Jensen Sportag’s debut album Stealth of Days is a sonic hybrid that stands out for its audaciousness.

title: A/B til Infinity
description: On his 2011 debut, Toronto-based producer David Psutka, aka Egyptrixx, took a widescreen approach to mining the fertile ground of the London dance music label Night Slugs. His second album focuses on a specific realm and comes off like a soundtrack pointing to a space between film noir and dystopian sci-fi.

title: Yours to Discover
description: Death From Above drummer/vocalist Sebastien Grainger's new solo effort Yours to Discover is an album of love songs, a release that's catchy for the wrong reasons and confined by its narrow scope.

title: Purple Snow: Forecasting the Minneapolis Sound
description: Numero Group's Purple Snow: Forecasting the Minneapolis Sound gets to the foundation of one of the most vital scenes in funk lore. Here are the roots of the chart-topping, synth-heavy pulse pioneered by Prince and the songwriting/production juggernaut of Jimmy Jam Harris and Terry Lewis.

title: Five Spanish Songs EP
description: Dan Bejar's Five Spanish Songs proves that his peculiar presence is unmistakeable even when he’s singing someone else’s songs in a foreign tongue. The EP also serves as a North American introduction to Seville songwriter Antonio Luque, a prolific cult hero whose band Sr. Chinarro originally recorded the tracks Bejar covers here.

title: Sail Out EP
description: The recent adoration of artist like Ciara and Cassie may have provided a perfect incubator for a singer like Jhené Aiko, the feather-voiced Def Jam signee. However, it's hard to decipher whether the songs  on her new *Sail Out* EP are more appealing than the mere atmosphere they create.

title: Spring Songs EP
description: On Kingston, Penn., punk outfit Title Fight's ambitious new Spring Songs EP, the group softens their sound without forfeiting the hooks or energy of their previous releases.

artist: Okkyung Lee, C. Spencer Yeh, Lasse Marhaug
title: Wake Up Awesome
description: Experimental musicians C. Spencer Yeh, Okkyung Lee, and Lasse Marhaug's collaboration as part of Software’s SSTUDIOS series is a bubbling, restless sonic fun house, filled with comic samples, oddball turns, surreal transitions, and enough activity to power a jet engine.

title: Across Six Leap Years
description: The songs from Tindersticks' new collection of reworkings, Across Six Leap Years, don't stray far from the original pieces, instead acting as tasteful updates that add a dab of cohesion.

title: The Rise & Fall of Paramount Records, Volume One (1917-1932)
description: The Rise and Fall of Paramount Records: Vol. 1 (1917–1932), released on Jack White's Third Man imprint and Revenant, is a 22-pound set that comes in a thick cardboard box. At the center of the collection is a drive containing 800 songs from Paramount’s first decade, a period that shaped the landscape for the rise of a recording industry anchored on jazz, rock'n'roll, and country music.

title: Land vs Air
description: William Burnett, an affiliate of the L.I.E.S. label who pushes out a broad array of electronic oddities at a frantic clip, gathers tracks from his various aliases on this compilation. For 14 obtuse pieces smeared across five aliases, there is a peculiar unity to Land vs Air that belies Burnett's scattershot approach.

title: As Iron Sharpens Iron, One Verse Sharpens Another
description: Compared to his previous releases, the eight songs on electronic musician Ricardo Donoso's new double EP As Iron Sharpens Iron, One Verse Sharpens Another are a bit generic, though there are many memorable moments.

title: Cold Mission
description: London-based producer James Parker, aka Logos, makes grime music that unfolds with an almost meditative calm. The songs on his excellent debut, Cold Mission, could be moody jungle breakdowns shorn of context, left to mark time in a state of infinite suspense.

title: Memorial
description: Chicago instrumental trio Russian Circles' fifth album, Memorial, builds off 2010's Empros, but these songs, one featuring Chelsea Wolfe, feel bigger and more polished, and somehow more intimate.

title: Direct Hits
description: The Killers' greatest hits collection, Direct Hits, includes singles from their four studio albums along with new songs (the M83-produced "Shot at the Night" and "Just Another Girl", produced by Stuart Price). Taken as a whole, it proves the band has fewer actual hits, let alone great ones, than you thought.

title: Remember Your Black Day
description: In the past three years, Vatican Shadow—the techno racket of Prurient mastermind  Dominick Fernow—has released more than a dozen aesthetically coherent cassettes, EPs and singles. On Remember Your Black Day, however, the meticulously upheld image of Vatican Shadow starts to feel more rigorous than the music itself.

title: FINS
description: Running six songs and 19 minutes, Connecticut punks Fins' new mini-LP FINS registers on first contact like a clawing blur, just like a punk tape should.

title: One Breath
description: Anna Calvi's new One Breath is a shade darker and angrier than its precursor, alternately haunting and just a bit more disarming than you’d expect. However, the quickly recorded release is too disparate in spots.

title: Christisland
description: Brooklyn experimental veterans Excepter's new Christisland EP may ultimately rank as an intriguing side-step, but when it’s playing, it sounds like feet firmly planted in new turf.

title: Screaming Life / Fopp
description: In the early days of what would become grunge, Soundgarden had the catchiest songs, the sexiest frontman, and the most conventional approach to making music. Twenty-five years later, Sub Pop has reissued their 1987 debut EP, Screaming Life, along with its 1988 follow-up, the Fopp EP, this time with a Jack Endino remastering job and bonus track.

title: Serpents Unleashed
description: After a decade as a band, five albums, and enough miles logged in tour vans and planes to have circumnavigated the Earth several dozen times, Athens, Ohio, metal diehards Skeletonwitch have released their best collection to date.

title: Get There
description: Minor Alps is the new pop rock project of Juliana Hatfield and Nada Surf’s Matthew Caws. It's a true collaboration: on their debut, Get There, they co-wrote all the lyrics, played all the instruments (minus some drums), and usually sing at the same time.

title: Watching Dead Empires in Decay
description: The new album from the Stranger—the latest project from electronic musician James Leyland Kirby—continues his fascination with memory, arguably taking it even further out into the abstract than he has before, sonically and structurally.

title: I Want to See Pulaski at Night
description: Andrew Bird fashioned I Want to See Pulaski at Night around “Pulaski at Night”, a song he wrote but didn't want to hold until he had enough for a full-length. He composed a handful of instrumentals to form prologues and epilogues around it, comparing it to soundtracking a film.

title: Government Plates
description: Death Grips' fourth album Government Plates loudly reestablishes the band as a group freed by having no ideals whatsoever, making music without a past about a present with no future. It isn’t defined by dissonance, volume, or abrasion so much as discomfort, Death Grips trying to figure out how to advance a sound that won’t stay still.

title: How to Stop Your Brain in an Accident
description: How to Stop Your Brain in an Accident, Future of the Left's fourth studio album, is built on political, pugilistic rage. It's their toughest, meatiest record to date.

title: Preparations EP
description: One one level, New Zealand producer Olly Peryman’s music as Fis is an offshoot of contemporary drum and bass, but he's also a singular figure whose avant-garde rhythmic constructs have converged only briefly with a wider movement. His new EP, and Tri Angle debut, further complicates matters.

title: Surrender to the Fantasy
description: Magik Markers' first album in four years was recorded in J Mascis’ attic, in vocalist/guitarist Elisa Ambrogio's dad’s basement, and at a number of East Coast practice spaces. For all the different environments, Surrender to the Fantasy takes the focused quality of the noise trio's recent output and adds warmth and melody.

title: Saint Heron
description: The Solange Knowles-curated compilation Saint Heron feels like the Flex Your Head or No New York of ambitious minimalist R&B. Although most of the songs here from the likes of Kingdom, Kelela, Sampha, and Knowles herself, have been previously released, she’s assembled them into a coherent piece that becomes something of an aesthetic manifesto.

title: Jamaica Plain EP / "it's a big world out there (and i am scared)"
description: The Jamaica Plain EP is an artifact from Kurt Vile's earliest days, a collaboration with Robert Robinson's Sore Eros that offers a brief and fitfully pretty glance backwards. An EP of newer material, it's a big world out there (and i am scared), is a bonus collection dug out of the corners of the masterful 2013 collection Wakin On A Pretty Daze.

title: Clean
description: The Atlanta trio Whores create taut, bass-heavy noise rock for people who love the stuff. Their newest offering, Clean, is a set of songs influenced by AmRep, Pissed Jeans, and the Melvins.

title: Mug Museum
description: Welsh singer/songwriter Cate Le Bon’s understated and modest third album, Mug Museum, is in part a lament to the erosion of memories, all told with remarkable detail.

title: Back to Land
description: Wooden Shjips’ fourth album heads further into the earthier direction of its 2011 predecessor, West, and casts even more radiant rays of Golden State sunshine onto the band’s once-foreboding hypno-drone-rock.

title: Purgatory/Paradise
description: Purgatory/Paradise, Throwing Muses’ first album in 10 years, is an ambitious collection that was also devised as a book with essays by Kristin Hersh and art by drummer Dave Narcizo. Half of the 31 tracks barely make it over two minutes: some are reprises, sometimes the reprises come first, and some tracks are lopped-off bridges or choruses.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: Following last year's astounding debut, ƒIN, the Barcelona producer John Talabot offers an album-length stitchwork of euphoric moments and rich textures in his 75-minute DJ-Kicks isntallment. Amid his sharp selection of glistening melodic dance music, Talabot himself steals the show, including three new cuts he had a hand in.

title: As Plantas Que Curam
description: Fernando Almeida and Benke Ferraz of Brazilian psych pop duo Boogarins spent the duration of their debut album lightly teasing every record in their collections. Their new As Plantas Que Curam is packed with melody, wit, and memorably referential music.

title: Nearest Suns
description: Nearest Suns, like the previous two solo outings from Medicine guitarist and producer Brad Laner, draws its inspiration from the peak of rock’s baroque psych-pop days, with Sgt. Pepper’s and Pet Sounds looming large over most of its inconsistent tracklist.

title: I Am The Center: Private Issue New Age Music In America 1950-1990
description: Light in the Attic’s new age compilation I Am the Center doesn’t try and pretend new age music was something it’s not. Focusing on private presses, it starts in 1950, about 25 years before the term “new age” existed in any kind of widespread way, and leads up to 1990, when the genre had devolved into factory-like repetitions of itself.

title: UZU
description: Operatic rockers Yamantaka // Sonic Titan's new UZU is hazier than their forceful 2011 self-titled debut, but the band has broadened its range.

title: On Air - Live at the BBC Vol. 2
description: The BBC was where the Beatles could perform for an audience of millions without struggling to hear themselves sing over primitive concert-hall P.A.s, and where—via mailed-in requests—they could interact with their many admirers without worrying about being trampled by the mob. Like the preceding Live at the BBC, On Air - Live at the BBC Vol. 2 is a pleasure to behold.

title: The Room
description: L.A. late-hours R&B duo Skin Town recall a number of recent artists in their lane—the Weeknd, for instance. But, for all the hallmarks they borrow, there are plenty of moments on debut The Room that are all theirs, thanks to Hall's singular singing and Nick Turco's scene-stealing synthscapes.

title: Young Chronos EP
description: N.Y. electronic duo Gatekeeper first released their extravagant, operatic new EP as a free torrent on Pirate Bay. The material is tighter and more expansive than what came before it, with their sense of absurdity deliriously heightened.

title: Shulamith
description: The Minneapolis electro-pop band Poliça's second album, Shulamith, is named for late feminist writer Shulamith Firestone, whom vocalist Channy Leaneagh has called her “mentor and muse from the grave.” The collection clears away some of the haze of the band's 2011 debut, while maintaining its predecessor's bleak depths.

title: Songs for Slim: Rockin' Here Tonight
description: In 2012 the guitarist Slim Dunlap suffered a debilitating stroke. Songs for Slim is a 2xCD tribute to Dunlap’s music outside of his work with the Replacements featuring contributions from Jeff Tweedy, Lucinda Williams, Steve Earle, Frank Black, Craig Finn, John Doe, Patterson Hood, Soul Asylum, and the Replacements themselves, among others.

title: Cupid Deluxe
description: On his second collection of melancholic 80s-inspired pop odes, the 27-year-old singer/songwriter/producer Devonté Hynes, aka Blood Orange, channels vagabond emotions into something universal and inviting. His Cupid Deluxe is an album that tenderly details heartbreak through the language of longing.

title: Rap Album One
description: L.A. MC/producer Jonwayne's formal Stones Throw debut Rap Album One is a dense affair. While the rapping on Rap Album One can feel bogged down in thought, the production benefits from the almost mathematical approach.

title: Pastel and Pass Out EP
description: Over the course of the three songs on Montreal noise rock trio No Joy's new EP Pastel and Pass Out,  they extend the accessibility of this year's Wait to Pleasure into a surprising playfulness with structure, brevity, and dynamism.

title: Small Sound EP
description: With their third release, the five-song Small Sound EP, Tennis complicate the easy breezy beautiful schtick with some positive results. Some of that is up to producer Richard Swift, who gives their throwback sound a few new wrinkles.

title: Julia with Blue Jeans On
description: Featuring nothing but piano and his voice, Julia With Blue Jeans On is Spencer Krug's starkest, most gripping Moonface record to date. It's also one of the finest LPs of his prolific, unpredictable career.

title: The Magnolia Electric Co.
description: Songs: Ohia's best and most pivotal album, 2003's The Magnolia Electric Co., showcased the late Jason Molina's strong shift toward rock populism. Imbued with a dust-under-the-fingernails weariness, the album is so representative of Molina’s sound and spirit, he subsequently took Magnolia Electric Co. as his new band’s name.

title: Harmonie
description: The German duo Musiccargo's 2009 debut emphasized electro with a krautrock drive beneath it courtesy of sequencers and hardware. On their second album, Gordon Pohl and Klaus Dinger student Gerhard Michel favor austerity, and there's a clarity and intensity to every track.

title: Caramel
description: New Zealand psych pop virtuoso Connan Mockasin's latest, Caramel, creates a stainless world that is both unsettling and fitting. Each new instrument seems to come out thick and globby, gradually dribbling out with an adult contemporary sheen.

title: Good Mood Fool
description: Luke Temple's new solo album Good Mood Fool is more playful and less particular than anything Temple's done in years. Though frequently gorgeous, the album's everything-in-its-right-place presentations occasionally outshine the songs' underlying melodies.

title: Pre-Human Ideas
description: Though his catalog may paint him as a Thoreau figure who draws mana from the trees and moss, Phil Elverum is a man wild with contradictions. See, for instance,  *Pre-Human Ideas*, a collection of songs made entirely on GarageBand with all the vocal parts filtered through an Auto-Tune setting.

title: Shields: B-Sides
description: Grizzly Bear have a history of putting out non-album releases that are much better and more meticulously arranged than they need to be. Culled from an intense recording session in Marfa, Tex., Shields: Expanded collects the best of these previously unheard tracks, which amount to captivating sketches, rather than scraps.

title: Magic Hour
description: It's been 14 years since the last Luscious Jackson album, and the world mostly hadn't been clamoring for a reunion. Their new Magic Hour is just a return to very familiar territory without the urgency and mystery of Luscious Jackson's 90s-era music.

title: Who Is William Onyeabor?
description: Luaka Bop’s Who is William Onyeabor? posits the mysterious late 70s/early 80s Nigerian funk musician William Onyeabor for a 21st century audience. Listening to the nine-song compilation, it makes sense that the likes of Four Tet, James Holden, and Caribou have already been buzzing with their accolades for him.

title: Aheym
description: Bryce Dessner's day job as a guitarist in the National requires him to work in big, sweeping rock-song arcs, but his solo work displays a furiously complicated musical mind chattering to itself. On his new collaboration with the Kronos Quartet, Aheym, Dessner produces vivid, fierce chamber pieces.

title: Aleph
description: On his relentless debut, Aleph, French producer and Yeezus collaborator Mike Levy proves to be the sort of transcendental figure who can fill festival EDM tents with drop enthusiasts while also appealing to listeners who consider themselves nuanced consumers of contemporary electronic music.

title: Not Here/Not Now
description: Compiled from the band’s 2012 world tours, Not Here/Not Now is the fourth release and second double-live album Michael Gira has issued since reviving the Swans name in 2010. Of the songs featured, only three have appeared on previous recordings, and the lone 80s-era track that figures offers an idea of where Swans are heading on their upcoming album.

title: The Second Album
description: Bay Area indie rappers Latryx—the duo of rappers Lyrics Born and Lateef the Truth Speaker—waited sixteen years to release their The Second Album, a record that feels scattered and frantic compared to its breezier predecessor.

title: Skycell
description: The Los Angeles duo Nguzunguzu have had success as producers, recently writing beats for the likes of Le1f and Kelela. On their Skycell EP, they let their headier ambitions run free, allowing songs to unfold gradually and settle into organic-feeling configurations.

title: COIN COIN Chapter Two: Mississippi Moonchile
description: Mississippi Moonchile, the second installment of saxophonist Matana Roberts' Coin Coin series, focuses on the life of her grandmother, a poor Southern girl who grew up in an era of keen turbulence that spanned the Great Depression, World War II, and America’s crawl toward civil rights.

title: Confection
description: Sébastien Tellier is still best known in the States as the louche, besunglassed Frenchman whose 2008 album Sexuality layered the electro-disco sound that was big in Paris at the time. His new Confection is a similarly decadent experience.

title: Blue Chips 2
description: On Blue Chips, Queens rapper Action Bronson and producer Party Supplies struck a balance that was both tonally perfect and ridiculously fun. With the just-released Blue Chips 2 they don’t tinker with the formula, and the result is a sequel nearly as good as its predecessor.

artist: Wooden Wand & The World War IV
title: Wooden Wand & The World War IV
description: James Jackson Toth's new album as Wooden Wand, Wooden Wand & the World War IV, is arguably his most consistent yet. The best songs on the record combine easy power with an undercurrent of tension.

title: My 1st Chemistry Set
description: With a production assist by LA producer Alchemist, Boldy James' new My 1st Chemistry Set reveals an artist who has been steadily deepening, as a writer and rapper. Guests like Action Bronson, Earl Sweatshirt and Freeway breeze through, but none overshadow Boldy.

title: Process
description: Brooklyn industrial rock band Yvette are a two-piece, but sound like an army. Process, their excellent full-length debut, feels like a series of fragmented outbursts compacted together into a 33-minute piece that shifts course and reanimates into new shapes without warning.

title: Transatlanticism
description: On Transatlanticism, Chris Walla was expanding his scope and ambition as a producer, intersecting with Ben Gibbard, who was doing the same as a writer. A decade after its release, Death Cab For Cutie's fourth and finest album is being reissued on limited vinyl (and MP3) with demo versions of all 11 tracks.

title: The Marshall Mathers LP 2
description: The Marshall Mathers LP 2, featuring Rihanna, Kendrick Lamar, and executive producers Dr. Dre and Rick Rubin, offers a second helping of the celeb-hating, self-deprecating juvenalia of Eminem’s beloved third album peppered with samples of and references to the source material. It also revels in its predecessor’s worst behaviors.

title: Allegoria
description: Kinuko Hiramatsu of Sapphire Slows is part of a small Tokyo-based scene of producers mixing house music beats with the breathless longing of bedroom indie pop. Her debut full-length album, Allegoria, wonderfully captures the shadowy essence of this corner of music.

title: The Swamps EP
description: Brooklyn indie rock outfit Widowspeak's new The Swamps EP was inspired by a tour itinerary through the Southern United States, a region whose hazy, bluesy music proves to be a tangible and versatile anchor for Widowspeak’s songwriting.

title: NYC, Hell 3:00 AM
description: Experimental musician James Ferraro's bleak new album NYC, Hell 3:oo AM inverts the druggy nocturnal glamor that’s become avant's default mode.

title: MellowHigh
description: The new album from MellowHigh—Odd Future's Hodgy Beats, Left Brain, and Domo Genesis—shows that the trio have figured out how to consistently deliver, but they've also lost the edge of unpredictability that made their breakthrough BLACKENEDWHITE so compelling.

title: Matangi
description: M.I.A. has hyped her long-delayed fourth collection as her "spiritual album." While Matangi is not as abrasive or hook-averse as its predecessor ///\Y/, much of its sensibility feels dated, limp, or just plain perplexing.

title: Antiphon
description: Midlake's fourth album, the first since the departure of singer-songwriter Tim Smith, finds the Denton, Tex., band revisiting the sound of their earlier work, including the folky soft-rock of 2006 sleeper hit The Trials of Van Occupanther and the burlier psychedelia of 2004 debut Bamnan and Slivercork.

title: Just In Case
description: Doley Bernays is a promising Bronx rapper, but the star of his debut EP is producer MP Williams, probably best known for LongLiveA$AP's "Ghetto Symphony". Williams supervises this project, draping the record in a thousand glorious rippling harps and interstellar synths.

title: Surfing Strange
description: Fronted largely by Allison Crutchfield, Swearin' ripped through 12 hook-heavy songs in 28 minutes on their 2012 debut, battling unattractive realities with calls for jubilant bodily motion and youthfully existential shout-alongs. On their heavier second album, Surfing Strange, that jubilation is almost gone, but the foursome's restlessness still persists.

title: The Regal Years: 1997-2004
description: The Regal Years combines the Beta Band’s entire recorded output into a seamless, six-disc listening experience. The collection arrives with both a very reasonable price point and a wealth of bonus material: Comprising key transitory non-album singles, B-sides, demos, radio sessions, and concert recordings, these add-ons will be equally revelatory to long-time enthusiasts and tourists alike.

title: Free Your Mind
description: Australian electronic outfit Cut Copy never sounded like a band that had a problem getting to the point. On Free Your Mind, though, their most overtly fun and least dynamic music restates the obvious over and over again.

title: Mercury
description: Miracle are a self-described “boy band” featuring Steve Moore, an American synth wizard known for his droning epics, lush dance tracks, and italo-aping band Zombi, and UK singer Daniel O’Sullivan, who's worked with any number of left-field rock outfits from Sunn O))) to Guapo, the band he fronts. It’s moody, serious, rather beautiful stuff.

title: Sunset Blvd.
description: J Dilla’s younger brother, Illa J, follows his 2008 Yancey Boys collection with Sunset Blvd., a record that features old Dilla associate Frank Nitt, a whole gang of Dilla-ites (Common, Talib Kweli), and another bumper crop of previously unreleased Dilla beats. It's the most joyous record we’ve seen from Dilla’s disciples since the producer’s death in 2006.

title: Overdue
description: On her early albums, Haley Fohr, aka Circuit Des Yeux, distanced her somber tones with thick distortion or hissy echo. Over time her work has become clearer, and the darkly hypnotic *Overdue*, her fourth full-length, is the most direct, immediate record she’s made.

title: Rapor EP
description: Indie rock songwriter Pat Grossi's latest release as Active Child, the Rapor EP, trades the pristine spaces of his previous work for louder beats and synths, and generally shifts from stained glass preciousness to neon pop.

title: Nonfiction
description: Nonfiction, the first full length from electronic producer James Hinton (aka the Range), is a meticulous record filled with pretty sounds: soft pianos, fake strings, bass that stretches like taffy, and synth blips that twinkle like itsy bitsy stars. Even at its busiest, it feels tidy and compact, like the gears of a prewar pocketwatch.

title: Retrash
description: Chicago band Oozing Wound's debut Retrash has been called crossover due to its punk influence, but it's also got grittiness and snottiness more thrash bands could use. The collection is one of the year's most notable thrash mutations.

title: Black Moon White Sun
description: Before the self-titled space-disco gem that put Black Devil Diso Club on the map 35 years ago, Bernard Fevre worked in the production music library trenches. On the new Black Moon White Sun, the music stumbles its way through an uneven if reasonably fun back catalog.

title: Double Exposure
description: Matt Kivel's acoustic Double Exposure is a small masterpiece of humble virtues: warm, patient, calm. It is beautifully, pristinely recorded, finely wrought; its twelve songs represent some of the least insistent music you will be spellbound by all year.

title: Chance of Rain
description: Electronic musican Laurel Halo's releases since 2012's Quarantine can be read as a reaction to that album and its reception, as she has steadily retreated from that album's vocally oriented post-pop into the harsh instrumental strictures of techno. Her second album, the dynamic, bracing Chance of Rain, continues this transition.

title: Peace Sword EP
description: The Peace Sword EP originated as another one of the Flaming Lips’ one-off larks: they were asked to contribute to the soundtrack of the upcoming science-fiction epic Ender’s Game. *Peace Sword—much like Ender's Game itself—*is thus a proverbial fight test, a space where the Lips’ light and dark energies square off in battle, sometimes within the same song.

title: Horrible Chamber
description: New York noise metallurgists Gnaw are a five-piece band, but they churn around one clear and inarguable point of darkness—ex-Khanate vocal torturer Alan Dubin. Horrible Chamber, the band’s much-improved second album, pushes their tirades and tales to the point where actual destruction seems just beyond the door.

title: She's Gone
description: Upset features former Best Coast/Vivian Girls drummer Ali Koehler, occasional La Sera guitarist Jenn Prince, and onetime Hole drummer Patty Schemel. Their first full-length, She's Gone, produced by by Kyle Gilbride of Swearin', is a collection of uncomplicated, sticky-catchy pop punk songs.

title: Lanterns
description: Son Lux's new LP Lanterns isn't piecemeal beats or hastily assembled instrumental clutter, rather it begs to be heard as the lingua franca of the past and the future, something that connects the analog and digital realms. And sometimes it totally gets close.

title: No Blues
description: Los Campesinos!’s fifth album, No Blues, is their strongest release since the staggering 2008 two-fer *Hold On Now, Youngster.../*We Are Beatiful, We Are Doomed. In a strange way, it also ends up sounding like the happiest LC! record, or at least the most implicitly hopeful.

title: Night Time, My Time
description: At barely 21, Sky Ferreira’s had a musical career burdened—and bolstered—by so many warring external forces that the sheer existence of her debut album is a minor miracle. It’s both a relief and a bit of a shock that Night Time, My Time is not only here, but that it’s one of the most pleasing pieces of pop-rock to come along this year.

title: The White Goddess (A Grammar of Poetic Myth)
description: The epic German heavy metal band Atlantean Kodex's sophomore album plumbs the depths of imagination and mythology to create something special. There's a studied seriousness about their songwriting that ensures headbangers will leave with more than just a sore neck.

title: Joko sinä tulet tänne alas tai minä nousen sinne
description: The Finnish group Paavoharju's first album since 2008 was conceived and recorded in a variety of abandoned buildings, including a self-built sauna deep in a swamp. The music's a dense weave of submerged tape loops, crackly field recordings, and disembodied snippets of voice and shadowy instruments.

title: Butter Knife
description: On their third full-length, the longtime Fullerton, Calif., garage rockers Audacity prove they've perfected the art of the party-rock anthem. Butter Knife also proves there's only so far the band can take that deftly honed identity.

title: L-event EP
description: English electronic duo Autechre work operates at a high level of engagement, requiring a commitment from the listener that's as great as the detail poured into the music. Their new EP, L-event, includes beautiful moments but returns to ground they've already covered.

title: Reflektor
description: Arcade Fire's lush, imaginative 85-minute fourth album is a triumph, but not a victory lap; the band never sounds content enough for that. Instead, Reflektor is an anxious, occasionally downright paranoid album that asks big, barbed questions aimed not just at the man who may or may not be upstairs, but the more terrestrial gods of rock history, too.

title: Obsian
description: On their stubborn and excellent second album*,* New York math-metal-madman Castevet, featuring Krallice bassist Nicholas McMaster, hint at climaxes they refuse to deliver and misdirect their redirections. The underlying draw of Obsian is that ability to sound incredibly visceral and obviously convoluted at once.

title: Milk Money
description: The multi-instrumentalist and Andrew Bird drummer Martin Dosh's first album in three years features six slight, impressionistic pieces as well as the most ambitious and surprising moment of his entire repertoire.

title: Kid Is Gone
description: Numero Group begins their ambitious series of box sets documenting the history of Pacific Northwest mainstays Unwound. This first volume showcases the rougher, noisier, rawer, punkier version of the band, as found on early albums, 7"s, tapes, and radio sessions.

title: Wenu Wenu
description: Syrian singer Omar Souleyman’s Wenu Wenu is technically his first proper recording, having been cut in a studio in Brooklyn rather than on site at one of the thousands of weddings he’s performed over the past two decades. Four Tet's Kieran Hebden, who produced, made the wise decision not to try and improve on a sound that doesn’t need fixing.

title: Love's Crushing Diamond
description: Throughout the seven gorgeous, baroque-folk songs from Boston outfit Mutual Benefit’s proper debut LP Love’s Crushing Diamond, the music can be described in a number of simple ways: loving, patient, warmhearted, and unfailingly hopeful.

title: Grand Blood
description: Doomriders are largely known as the rockier side project of Converge bassist Nate Newton, who handles guitars and vocals here. Their Kurt Ballou-produced third album, Grand Blood, is the band's first collection of new material since 2009.

title: Boardwalk
description: Los Angeles indie duo Boardwalk make music eerily reminiscient of Beach House or Widowspeak and definitely have a good ear for melody. The problem is it doesn't sound like their own.

title: Soul Music
description: As Special Request, UK producer Paul Woolford aimed to honor his teenage years of listening to pirate radio, hearing the sounds of first-generation jungle and rave through his speakers as rave culture was forming. The project's proper debut, Soul Music, is one of the most exciting dance records of this year.

title: ilp
description: On his debut LP ilp, producer/singer Kwes’ gentle songwriting sensibilities are unable to keep up with his exploratory beat making and the result is too often a mismatch.

title: Guilt Trips
description: On wide-ranging Canadian producer Ryan Hemsworth's first solo LP and second major release of 2013 after the Still Awake EP, he remains stylistically daring, but shows off a newfound focus. The material still meanders, though with more purpose, sharper hooks, and lusher instrumental textures.

title: Whales and Leeches
