description: Under the name "Melvins Lite," Buzz Osborne and Dale Crover pull away from the younger half of their band, adding double bassist Trevor Dunn (Mr. Bungle) to cover Macca, improvise, and turn plenty-weird songs into still-weirder jams.

title: There's No Leaving Now
description: The Swedish folkie's third album is the first to feature multi-tracking. He's still driven by his wandering spirit, but these songs have the feel of someone exploring a nature trail in his own backyard.

title: Triple F Life: Friends, Fans & Family
description: Featuring Nicki Minaj, B.o.B, Drake, Ludacris, and airy, stroboscopic beats, Waka Flocka Flame's second album exchanges his debut's antisocial charisma, grim ambience, and seismic street impact for something more amenable to pop stardom.

title: Ursprung
description: Merging live instruments with editing software, Hendrik Weber, aka Pantha du Prince, teams with Stephan Abry of Krautrock-as-indie-pop act Workshop for a collection that largely abandons Pantha's bright and glacial digital palette.

title: Love Me Oh Please Love Me EP
description: The London producer Nathan Jenkins, who once successfully combined Pet Sounds and the music of J Dilla, offers a frequently vocal-led EP of five original tracks and a Robert Wyatt cover.

title: Do Things
description: For his second album on Animal Collective's Paw Tracks label, the Oxford, Miss., musician replaces his ukelele with spritely synths, airy acoustic guitars, and hints of psychedelia.

title: Synthetica
description: Emily Haines spends much of Metric's fifth album pondering the way the human mind is transformed by artificial versions of natural experiences. She also duets with Lou Reed.

title: In Our Heads
description: Hot Chip's fifth full-length, a meditation on positivity, is their most playful and colorful record to date.

title: Blood Speaks
description: On their sophomore album, the London-based blues and folk duo of Katherine Blamire and Jessica Davies found a sympathetic ear in longtime PJ Harvey collaborator Head.

title: Dub Egg
description: On their second album, the first for Matador, Austin four-piece the Young dial down their psych-rock impulses to focus on classic songcraft.

title: Bat Chain Puller
description: Captain Beefheart's 1976 album Bat Chain Puller was a record that, for many, existed only in promising snatches through subsequent albums, a fragmented text never quite assembled. The tapes have finally found release in an edition available through a subsidiary of the Frank Zappa estate.

title: Umskiptar
description: Without Varg Vikernes, the black metal story doesn't happen, or at least it doesn't merit a book deal. But how do you treat the legacy and output of someone who's done so much to build a sound, yet is also a murderer and a bigot?

title: 1991 EP
description: The Harlem-based MC's long-delayed first official release finds her standing at a number of interesting junctions, if not yet having committed to a solid path.

title: Radlands
description: The Brit rockers' fourth album finds the band leaving behind the glitzy rafter-reaching attitude of 2010's Serotonin in favor of countryish melodies, acoustic guitars, and gospel choirs.

title: Hope in Dirt City
description: The Edmonton MC has served as the official poet laureate of his hometown, so it's surprising the strength of his third album doesn't lie in his writing or his rapping.

title: A Painting of a Painting On Fire
description: The Band of Horses member's debut solo LP was recorded by Chris Testa (P!nk, Matchbox 20) and features a hyperactive brand of 1970s rock full of big, shiny melodies and eager riffs.

title: Lex Hives
description: On the Swedish garage rock group's fifth album, their proper followup to 2007's The Black and White Album, it sounds like they're still figuring things out.

title: Quarantine
description: Veering from claustrophobic sci-fi dioramas to meditative synth drones to nakedly expressive confessionals, Laurel Halo's Hyperdub debut is unified by an underlying perspective and personality that commands attention yet still leaves plenty to the imagination.

title: LP
description: Following last year's split with Grimes, the Montreal musician releases an LP, a sprawling collection that explores extremes of spirituality in a digital world.

title: Aimlessness
description: Jimmy Tamborello, best known for his work in the Postal Service, releases a third album of new material, a collection that mixes instrumentals and collaborations with guest vocalists like Baths and Nite Jewel.

title: Endless Flowers
description: The 1960s-nodding San Diego noise-pop band's third album is their best and also their most frustrating.

title: The Stoned Immaculate
description: Curren$y's latest album features Big K.R.I.T., Pharrell, 2 Chainz, Estelle, Young Jeezy, Wiz Khalifa, and a buzz-harshing Wale, among others.

title: Banga
description: Patti Smith's new guitar-driven album, her first since 2007's Twelve, is a meditation on exploration and adventure.

title: Taranta
description: The 28-year-old Parisian born singer-songwriter's debut LP was inspired by madness, spider bites, and the hellish melancholy of early Cat Power records.

title: All of Us, Together
description: Though Teen Daze is intent on calling himself a producer, it's helpful to view the British Columbia artist's debut LP within the frame of rock music.

title: Reverberations: Tape & Electronic Music 1961-1970
description: This monumental box set collects the work of the 80-year-old composer, teacher, and electronic music pioneer: Reverberations fills a dozen discs in almost as many hours, laying substantial groundwork for every electronic drone artist and harsh noise terrorist to come.

title: >>
description: While retaining the eerie, claustrophobic atmosphere of its predecessor, the second LP from Portishead mastermind Geoff Barrow's krautrock project boasts a brisker, more purposeful sequence.

title: Control System
description: The least visible member of the Black Hippy collective, who Schoolboy Q has called a "human dictionary" and Kendrick Lamar "a wizardish genius," releases his exhilarating debut.

title: Trust EP
description: Joel Ford, who plays bass in Tigercity and records as as one half of Ford & Lopatin, offers a five-track solo EP that finds him widening his scope and edging away from outright pop.

title: Lillie: F-65
description: Saint Vitus' first album in 17 years, the first to feature original vocalist Scott "Wino" Weinrich in 22 years, finds the hugely influential Los Angeles doom band flush with renewed energy.

title: Odd Renditions Vol. 001 EP
description: On the eve of a new full-length, the D.C. rapper releases an EP featuring reworked cuts by Bon Iver, Metronomy, Marvin Gaye, and k-os. They're remixes in the loose sense, but Oddisee treats them like duets.

title: A Joyful Noise
description: Following 2009's Rick Rubin-produced Music for Men, the Portland trio's fifth album was handled by UK pop mastermind Xenomania, perhaps best known for helming Sugababes and Girls Aloud's clever post-millennial bubblegum.

title: WIXIW
description: Co-produced by Mute founder Daniel Miller (Depeche Mode, Yazoo), Liars' dark, largely electronic and sample-based latest album is a return to their adventurous, experimental roots. It's also the group's most human and fragile album to date.

title: Embracing the Lightless Depths
description: On their excellent second album, the Portland funeral doom band make every ounce of their weight count by knowing exactly how to counter it.

title: Sex, Drugs & Video Games
description: The Mississippi rapper's latest album, his first since 2008, features Big K.R.I.T., A$AP Rocky, 2 Chainz, Chris Brown, Bun B, Snoop Dogg, and Lil Wayne, among others.

title: Here Comes Everybody
description: The Wake, who recorded for Factory and Sarah, mixed nervously funky post-punk with bedroom synth-pop. After repressing two singles for Record Store Day, Captured Tracks has reissued the Glasgow band's 1985 sophomore LP along with non-album tracks from the era.

title: Among the Leaves
description: Mark Kozelek's sprawling, cathartic fifth album as Sun Kil Moon feels like the work of a songwriter clearing his palate.

title: Americana
description: Neil Young's latest studio record, his first with Crazy Horse in nine years, isn't so much a covers collection as it is a concept album in the vein of Nick Cave's Murder Ballads.

title: Merciless
description: After more than a decade of noise and drone made in small editions, the Ohio-based artist-- with the help of Marina Peterson, C. Spencer Yeh, and Jason Zeh-- offers his richest LP to date.

title: Generals
description: Laura Burhenn's second LP, again produced by Richard Swift, is a stylistically diverse collection of openhearted, politically engaged pop.

title: Journey of the Deep Sea Dweller II
description: The excellent second installment of Clone's four-part Drexciya retrospective continues in much the same manner as Vol. 1: short tracks of spackled, analog funk dominate, offering occasional clues about the Detroit duo's sci-fi mystery.

title: The Sister
description: Marissa Nadler's second full-length by way of her own Box of Cedar imprint is her most narcotic album to date.

title: Max Payne 3 OST
description: The L.A. noise-rock band's original score for Max Payne 3 replicates the third-person shooter action game's slow-motion frenzy.

title: A Monument
description: Fronted by Corrina Repp and Joe Haege (Menomena, 31 Knots), the Portland quartet creates darkly lovely music-- and actual songs-- on its second LP.

title: Here
description: The onetime frontman of Ima Robot offers the next chapter in the ever-evolving mythology of Edward Sharpe with a surprisingly humble, homespun sophomore album.

title: What We Saw From the Cheap Seats
description: Now six albums into her career, Regina Spektor presents both her sentimentalism and her more childlike qualities with a certain defiance.

title: This Is PiL
description: For a band that built its name on ripping up the rule book, what do Public Image Ltd. sound like 20 years since their last album, and over 30 since their first?

title: Valtari
description: The Icelandic post-rock band's longest-gestating LP abandons both the pop leanings of more recent releases and the volcanic dynamics of their earliest material but still sounds like the work of no other group.

title: Spirits
description: The latest from this project from Eternal Tapestry guitarist Dewey Mahood is easily his warmest, most approachable record, filled with pastoral drones and swirling psychedelia.

title: King Tuff
description: After making an album under the name Happy Birthday, Kyle Thomas returns with a new moniker and sharper songwriting chops, resulting an album that is long on distortion and short on subtlety, but still manages to transcend lo-fi.

title: Magic Hour
description: Scissor Sisters' latest features collaborations with producers like Diplo, the Neptunes, and Boys Noize, but despite these club-friendly ringers the album is heavy on the ballads.

title: Diver
description: Four years after their big and bombastic self-titled debut, Lemonade return with an album that functions in more pop-economical four-minute bursts, with tracks tempering the big-beat ballast with stripped-down slow jams.

title: Celebration Rock
description: The Vancouver's 2009 debut Post-Nothing was an emotional blast and also a sonic blur; the follow-up finds everything hitting louder and clearer than before, along with making a huge leap in songwriting technique.

title: Classical Curves
description: After two EPs and a big single, this young English electronic producer steps out with his debut full-length on Night Slugs, an album that feels more like one long, continuous idea than a series of discrete tracks.

title: Time Team
description: Offering dubstep filtered through a g-funk lean, the UK producer has never sounded further askew from his generation than on his bold, manic debut LP.

title: Alien Tentacle Sex EP
description: This Toronto R&B singer shares a lot with the Weeknd, including a producer (Illangelo), subject matter, and vibe, in addition to the eerily similar vocal melodies.

title: The Plot Against Common Sense
description: On his latest for his post-Mclusky band, Andy Falkous still manages to serve up a healthy amount of bile, but some of his targets are questionable.

title: Heaven
description: On their sixth record, a gloriously pretty collection that features guest vocals from Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold, the Walkmen have made a bewildered, giddy paean to their own happiness.

title: Body Faucet
description: The Athens, Ga., band uses its debut LP as a vat in which to hastily dump the past five years of top-shelf indie into some kind of frat party-stoking jungle juice.

title: A Shut-In's Prayer
description: Released on Red House Painters/Sun Kil Moon mastermind Mark Kozelek's Caldo Verde label, the debut LP from Owen Ashworth's post-Casiotone for the Painfully Alone project is the most wistful work he's committed to tape.

title: Passage
description: On their audacious, ambitious Secretly Canadian debut LP, the Brooklyn duo of Aleksa Palladino and Devon Church show there's a bigger hook to their band than their romantic backstory.

title: Empyrean
description: After some solid EPs, the Brooklyn black metal band's debut LP finds a way to reinvigorate the old-school black metal template with a sound that's stately and epic, but booze-soaked, filthy, and feral.

title: Ram
description: Paul McCartney's Ram is a domestic-bliss album, one of the weirdest, earthiest, and most honest ever made. What 2012's ears can find is a rock icon inventing an approach to pop music that would eventually become someone else's indie pop.

title: Silfra
description: The classical violinist Hilary Hahn holed up in Iceland for two months to record with German pianist and indie classical composer Hauschka. The result is a record about fiddling around happily with music's guts.

title: Music for Neighbors
description: All five current members of the Feelies were involved in this 1980s N.J. band at some point, but the Trypes were more than an offshoot. Acute's reissue collects their sole release, 1984's The Explorers Hold EP, plus demos, live performances, and previously unheard practice sessions.

title: Deep Thuds
description: Jason Killinger of the Philadelphia lo-fi rock'n'roll band Birds of Maya, the group that also birthed Purling Hiss, delivers a compulsively listenable, spaced-out set.

title: Go! Pop! Bang!
description: On her long-delayed debut, the 21-year-old rapper proves she was ahead of the curve as a young teenager performing in Baltimore, and that M.I.A. was smart to recruit her when she assembled her N.E.E.T. team.

title: Words and Music by Saint Etienne
description: The English electronic pop band's first proper album since 2005 is a sterling affirmation that relating music to your life doesn't have to grow more difficult as you get older.

title: Rhine Gold
description: The Copenhagen group's second album is a hook-laden prog-pop opus that bridges whatever currently falls under the heading of "post rock" with the past five years of flannel-wearing American indie.

title: Unpatterns
description: The English duo's latest studio album backs away from the darkness of 2010's Delicacies and moves toward the pleasure principle once again.

title: Internal Logic
description: There's evidence all over Grass Widow's third album that the San Francisco post-punk band has spent the two years since its last album tightening its sound. It's an approach that feels more personal and self-contained than it does trendy.

title: Masterpiece
description: Based on his most recent London club night, the English DJ/producer's 3xCD contribution to Ministry of Sounds's "Masterpiece" series is a collection of remixes that showcase his idiosyncratic way of forging links between the underground and more populist fare.

title: Clear Moon
description: Phil Elverum recently took an extended break from touring to record two albums in a studio he built in a deconsecrated church. The first of these albums makes a vast, cool sanctuary of itself and quietly beckons you into it.

title: Pinkish Black
description: Formed after the suicide of the bassist from their previous group, Texas duo Pinkish Black offer a dark blend of death-rock, metal, punk, and synthesized drone on their self-titled debut.

title: Majenta
description: The Detroit producer and fashion photographer's first album for Scuba mastermind Paul Rose's Hotflush label might make you want to take a shower.

title: Sunburn EP
description: The Vampire Weekend bassist's first solo outing feels connected to his playing in his usual band but also extends far from anything on Vampire Weekend's records.

title: Natural History
description: The Baltimore noise-rock quartet's sophomore album, their first for Drag City, finds them softening their sound but still nailing the sweet spot between savagery and self-awareness.

title: Cancer for Cure
description: Featuring guest spots from Mr. Muthafuckin' eXquire, Danny Brown, and a snarling Killer Mike, El-P's first album since putting Def Jux on hiatus in early 2010 marks a break from the old order and another call to arms.

title: Civilization
description: The dot-connecting Atlanta bass producer's first album for Tectonic feels like a rapid succession of new-direction singles gathered together as an overarching summary of a growing artist.

title: RØSENKØPF
description: Drawing from goth and industrial, this promising Brooklyn noise-rock trio creates rhythmic, surprisingly accessible music that hits with brute muscle rather than harsh abrasion.

title: Dreamchasers 2
description: On the Philly rapper's first mixtape to reflect his heightened profile-- a collection featuring guest spots from Drake, Wale, Big Sean, Fabolous, and Kendrick Lamar, among others-- he doesn't so much step out of his own world as merge it with the one he's about to enter.

title: The Visitors [Deluxe Edition]
description: A fifth reissue of a 30-year old album needs something remarkable to make fans bite, and EMI promised just that for this edition of ABBA's risk-taking final record, which hosts their first piece of unreleased material since 1994, along with a set of uniformly terrific bonus tracks.

title: Ufabulum
description: The English electronic musician's newest is in many ways a return to his earliest material. If people have forgotten the whimsical-yet-punishing pleasures of Squarepusher's breakbeat chaos, might it be a good a place to get onboard?

title: Dismania
description: The N.Y. sludge-punk band, featuring former Black Lips member Jack Hines and Golden Triangle's Vashti Windish, offer buckets of blood and bile on their aggressive sophomore LP.

title: Heavy
description: The visceral N.Y. string quartet's third solo album is a collection of dark thoughts and relentless pressures: Ethel function as a living affront to the misconception that chamber music is polite, white-napkin stuff.

title: A.C.R. 1999
description: Recorded in a 1999 session, A.C.R. 1999 includes previously unreleased tracks as well as songs that were re-made for the Baltimore post-punk legends' ninth album, Necrophones, heard here in sharper, more muscular form.

title: Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde: The Singles Collection Music Box
description: This limited singles box for the 1992 debut LP from the L.A. rap group Pharcyde highlights their dizzying mix of SoCal 420 culture, jazzy bohemianism, and self-conscious rap smarts.

title: Not Your Kind of People
description: For their first release in seven years, Garbage faced a conundrum similar to that of many artists who found success in the alt-rock 1990s: Do you update your approach to conform to a more contemporary sound, or do you keep partying like it's 1998?

title: Live
description: The Carl Craig-nodding German techno duo's first full-length since their 2004 eponymous debut is an 80-minute DJ set that presents a potted history of the group's last eight years.

title: Into the Trees
description: The London-via-Chicago psych-folk songwriter's sophomore LP, produced by Four Tet's Kieran Hebden and released on his label, features guest spots from Radiohead's Colin Greenwood.

title: True
description: Jorge Elbrecht moved his shape-shifting post-Lansing-Dreiden pop band to Slumberland for their sophomore LP, a collection that incorporates the roar of first-wave shoegazers into the mix.

title: Shot Forth Self Living / The Buried Life
description: The Los Angeles noise-pop band's early-1990s catalog gets an extensive work-through courtesy of Captured Tracks.

title: The Only Place
description: Best Coast's Jon Brion-produced second album finds the band leaning toward alt country and working in a more stripped-down mode, with Bethany Cosentino's voice front-and-center.

title: I Feel So Far Away: Anthology 1974-1998
description: This 2xCD collection, which draws from four albums and other material the Velvet Underground drummer recorded over two decades, includes guest spots from her VU bandmates as well as Daniel Johnston and members of Half Japanese, the Violent Femmes, and Sonic Youth.

title: V
description: The first album in three years from the international drone-doom duo of Sunn O)))'s Stephen O' Malley and Pita's Peter Rehberg offers a surprising junction of various musical outfields.

title: Köima
description: The Malian folk-blues singer recorded his first Thrill Jockey LP in his sister's house in Gao with a string of collaborators, often in one or two takes. His second, Koïma, is a more structured, subtly arranged offering.

title: Neck of the Woods
description: In the age of downloading and streaming, the L.A. alt-rock band still makes albums like it needs to take full advantage of a CD's storage capacity.

title: R.A.P. Music
description: On R.A.P. Music, Killer Mike hooks up with El-P and Adult Swim subsidiary Williams Street for the 2012 equivalent to Ice Cube and the Bomb Squad's similarly inspired bicoastal union on AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted.

title: Super Vague EP
description: The Baltimore quartet, led by Denny Bowen of the recently defunct post-punk trio Double Dagger, revives the fuzz and feedback-laden churn of early-90s indie rock without so many of the bad vibes.

title: Prophet
description: The ex-Menomena multi-instrumentalist returns with his second full-length, and it's another production wonder, vast and symphonic one moment, stark and intimate the next.

title: Motion Sickness of Time Travel
description: Though often gentle and reflective, there's a forcefulness to Rachel Evans' drone-based music. Her newest double LP as Motion Sickness of Time Travel is her most definitive statement to date.

title: Fear Fun
description: On his eighth solo LP, his first as Father John Misty, ex-Fleet Foxes drummer Josh Tillman has shaken his lonesome, somber tone in favor of something more gregarious, engaging, even funny.

title: Bloom
description: Two years ago, Teen Dream felt like such a complete realization of Beach House's potential that it had to make you wonder where they could possibly go from there. By just about every measure, the Baltimore duo's fourth album is stronger than anything they've done before.

title: Versions
description: Though it came from the same improvised studio session, David Daniell and Tortoise/Eleventh Dream Day player Douglas McCombs' second LP is a marked improvement on their first collaboration.

title: Gallery EP
description: Justin Vallesteros follows Craft Spells' Idle Labor with an EP of six songs-- essentially makeout music for loners-- that could have easily served as deep cuts on that promising 2011 debut.

title: DROKK: Music Inspired by Mega-City One
description: Started as the soundtrack for Pete Travis' forthcoming Judge Dredd adaptation, Portishead's Geoff Barrow teamed with Emmy-nominated composer Ben Salisbury for this tribute to the fictional setting of the comic book series.

title: Royal Headache
description: This Australian garage-rock band's vocalist is several shades more complex and adaptable than your typical throat-shredding truth-teller: His warm, soulful voice pilots his group's promising 26-minute self-titled debut.

title: Isn't Anything / Loveless / EPs 1988-1991
description: My Bloody Valentine's output during the band's miracle years between 1988 and 1991 still feels like a gift.

title: Family Perfume Vol. 1 / Family Perfume Vol. 2
description: White Fence's recent collaboration with Ty Segall sounds hi-fi in comparison to this paisley-tinted pair of fuzzed-out records, which leader Tim Presley pieced together from a year spent crouched over a 4-track.

title: Deathless Master
description: Dropping the crust punk of their earlier offerings, the San Francisco band is committed to old-school death metal on its brutal, surprisingly catchy latest LP.

title: A Different Ship
description: Here We Go Magic's latest turns songwriter Luke Temple's anxiety of non-commitment into an aesthetic of sorts, with the results proving strangely medicated.

title: Dopesmoker
description: Almost 20 years after it was recorded and rejected by London Records and then made public as unofficial bootlegs or unagreeable edits, stoner-rock legends Sleep's storied one-song, hour-long third album is finally available through a remastered, re-illustrated reissue.

title: OFF!
description: OFF!'s debut LP, which comes in just shy of First Four EPs' runtime, again finds Keith Morris venting spleen at anything and everything. This time out, though, his targets seem softer and a little harder to pin down.

title: Oh Holy Molar
description: On the minimalist English chamber-pop band's second album, vocalist/pianist Lucinda Chua filters raw emotion through pith and poetry.

title: Posthuman
description: Touted as a return to his Godflesh days, Justin K. Broadrick's newest project steps away from Jesu's dreaminess to a dark, brutal electronic realm.

title: The Electronic Anthology Project of Dinosaur Jr.
description: J Mascis and Built to Spill bassist Brett Nelson offer a collection of Dinosaur Jr. synth-pop covers, culled mostly from the band's 1987 SST classic, You're Living All Over Me.

title: Complete Discography
description: This reissue of the Maryland post-hardcore group Moss Icon's Complete Discograpy is essential because, like Fugazi, Slint, or any other wondrous butterfly nourished in hardcore's cocoon, they were a band that forged their own universe.

title: Galaxy Garden
description: With his fifth album since 2007, dance producer Matt Cutler has released his most complete statement: Each track on Galaxy Garden is a maximalist marvel in minimalist disguise.

title: Memory
description: On its first album for Modeselektor's Monkeytown label, the L.A./Berlin bass duo further develops its tendency to put together one subgenre's tracks by another subgenre's rules.

title: Hoyas EP
description: Blending mumbled folk and bleary-eyed blips, the Bon Iver percussionist's new solo EP feels like the soundtrack for an ice-slicked, insomniac winter drive.

title: Death Dreams
description: On its second LP, the Canadian fuzz-rock duo drowns its sorrows with very loud and brash songs about very small and internal breakdowns.

title: Urban Turban
description: Three years into a remarkably prolific second phase, Cornershop release a playful 12-song collection that finds them teaming up with an international cast of vocalists.

title: We Rose From Your Bed With the Sun in Our Head
description: Focusing on new material, this live 2xCD collection from Swans' first tour in more than a decade finds the loud, mean, and complicated Michael Gira-led sextet beating past successes with the purpose of the present.

title: Heirlooms
description: Taking his late father's jazz trumpet legacy as source material, Marc Barrite's second LP as Dave Aju is a deeply affecting work that channels house, funk and the messages of George Clinton.

title: Half Blood
description: Frostbitten Scandinavian black metal and rustic U.S. roots music harmonize on Horseback's second proper LP to create a sweeping mix of ugliness and beauty. It's post-rock at its most spartan and hard rock at its most out-there.

title: In the Belly of the Brazen Bull
description: The UK band's Dave Fridmann- and Steve Albini-produced fifth album goes full-blown 1990s Buzz Bin. Fortunately, the Cribs write better hooks than C-level revivalists.

title: Club Rez EP
description: Almost two years after the release of the astonishing single "Wut", the UK producer is back with a new EP for Night Slugs: Can he make lightning strike twice?

title: Dr Dee
description: A departure from his recent work with Gorillaz and Rocket Juice & the Moon, Dr Dee is the stately, melancholy soundtrack to the opera Damon Albarn wrote for director Rufus Norris.

title: The Diver
description: On their second album, and Sacred Bones debut, the Wierd-affiliated N.Y. band is obsessed with wringing genuine emotion from decrepit electronics.

title: Electra Heart
description: Marina Lambrini Diamandis' second album is a high-gloss record made with Dr. Luke, Stargate, Greg Kurstin, and Liam Howe, and dressed in layers of philosophy, mythology, and blonde wigs.

title: The LHI Years: Nudes, Singles & Backsides (1968-1971)
description: This set from the late singer-songwriter and producer collects tracks cut for his own LHI label. His biggest hits as a songwriter were behind him, but Hazlewood still had plenty of weirdo ambition.

title: Mondo
description: The buzzed-about L.A. band's Danger Mouse-produced debut is a cautionary tale of what happens when a "hit record" forgets to actually include hits.

title: Hair
description: Garage-rock wunderkind Ty Segall's collaborative album with Tim Presley of White Fence is an absorbing maze of detours. They're the sort of people who seemingly enjoy pulling support beams out of songs to see how they hop along without them.

title: Damned
description: Four years after their last release, the Swedish crust punks Wolfbrigade return with a vicious Southern Lord debut and, one may hope, a new lease on life.

title: Loot
description: Political in the non-dogmatic way of someone open to new experiences in a world hostile to difference, the Barcelona-via-Los Angeles producer's third LP presents a vision of global bass culture that goes down smoothly without blanding.

title: Live in Detroit 1986
description: The Nigerian Afrobeat pioneer performed this hypnotic, four-song, two-and-a-half-hour set less than a year after being released from prison, and his pointed, usually funny monologues about that wrongful imprisonment are a large part of this 3xCD collection's charm.

title: Exercises EP
description: With this chilly, quietly compelling EP of piano ruminations, Montreal producer Mike Silver unveils his most intriguing material to date.

title: World, You Need a Change of Mind
description: On his debut Kindness LP, the buzzy UK songwriter Adam Bainbridge offers washed-out new wave, strobing disco, lite funk, atmospheric balladry, and a couple unexpected covers.

title: Echoes and Rhymes
description: The UK indie pop band's first LP in 21 years is a collection of covers of 196os obscurities, but Echoes & Rhymes is more than a curio.

title: Art Dealer Chic, Vols. 1-3
description: Armed with a diverse bag of tricks, the 25-year-old L.A. singer offers some of the best R&B of the year on these three fearless EPs.

title: Strange Land
description: Yellow Ostrich's first album as a trio opens up Alex Schaaf's bedroom-pop sound: He's a lonely soul, but on Strange Land, he's in good company.

title: Aufheben
description: Recorded in East Berlin with a cast of session musicians and a couple of longtime collaborators, Aufheben is Anton Newcombe's most consistent, sonically lustrous album in years.

title: Master of My Make-Believe
description: Four years after her genre-blending debut, Santigold offers a polished assortment of global pop tunes produced by the likes of Q-Tip, TV on the Radio's Dave Sitek, Boys Noize, and Yeah Yeah Yeahs' Nick Zinner.

title: The Ghost in Daylight
description: Continuing to explore themes of "compulsion, degradation, and the possibility of transcendence," the Bristol musician's first LP since 2007 adds an icy despair to his earlier folk-oriented releases.

title: I Predict a Graceful Expulsion
description: The 24-year old Canadian singer's transfixing voice brings warmth to her chilly debut, a collection that subtly tugs against the big, major-network-drama payoff for which it feels custom-built.

title: Black Is Beautiful
description: The debut Hyperdub LP from the duo once known as Hype Williams feels like a trip through the fragments of their collective psyches.

title: Blow Away Your Troubles / On Any Normal Monday / Midnight Cleaners
description: Cleaners From Venus, the lo-fi pop project of the English musician Martin Newell, offered a mix of rough edges, distanced vocals, definite hooks, and unexpected mixing choices. This box set features the first three 1980s cassette-only efforts with liner notes, flyers, buttons, and unreleased tracks and photos.

title: Nootropics
description: Incorporating synths, ambient drift, and stark percussion, the Baltimore band, fronted by onetime folk eccentric Jana Hunter, widens its sonic palette and scope on this richly detailed sophomore LP.

title: Concatenating Fields
description: The Akron, Ohio, husband-and-wife duo's newest, an album of "nighttime grass thoughts," finds ambient sounds and loops coexist quietly together.

title: Dark York
description: The NYC queer rapper Khalif Diouf's dark, sleek debut mixtape, featuring production work from Nguzunguzu, feels animated by the force of its own movement.

title: Light Asylum
description: The Brooklyn electro-goth duo of Shannon Funchess and Bruno Coviello has personality and style to spare, but is that enough to carry this full-length debut?

title: Meantime EP
description: The London producer's new EP is an unabashedly beautiful, even sensuous 17 minutes of music: He's a startlingly clear new voice, and here, he's just clearing his throat.

title: Fevers and Mirrors / There Is No Beginning to the Story EP
description: A dozen years after its release, Fevers & Mirrors, Bright Eyes' defining LP, is reissued by Saddle Creek, along with 2002's There Is No Beginning to the Story EP.

title: Mohn
description: The lastest collaboration by German techno heroes Wolfgang Voigt and Jorg Burger is essentially an ambient record, though it manages to avoid the sterility of actual background music.

title: First of My Kind EP
description: The young Paul Weller- and Oasis-approved Liverpudlian, who records as one half of the Last Shadow Puppets with Arctic Monkeys' Alex Turner, offers a four-song EP.

title: Pluto
description: On his debut album, the Atlanta rapper/singer makes his strongest case yet that he is one of the foremost sources of rap that's as peculiar as it is pop. He also miraculously shows that it's still possible for Auto-Tune to be an interesting artistic tool.
Recorded in Oakland with a heavy presence of Bay Area producers and rappers, the Das Racist member's highly listenable second mixtape of 2012 is a testament to his heretofore untested malleability.

title: Mermaid Avenue: The Complete Sessions
description: All three installments of Wilco and Billy Bragg's tribute to Woody Guthrie are collected in this compilation, which lovingly-- and in timely fashion-- shows there was more to the Okie folkie than protest music.

title: Valot Kaukaa
description: Finnish producer Olli Aarni explores the boundaries between repetition and the unpredictable, analog and digital, clarity and warble. His new album makes a strong argument for distortion as a reverie-inducing narcotic.

title: Seven Bells
description: On their Tom G. Warrior-mixed fifth album, the German black-metal band Secrets of the Moon have defrosted their Satanic hymns and amped up the swagger.

title: Poor Moon
description: Initially out last year on a small vinyl-only edition, this collection of skewed country-soul greatness deserves to be heard by more ears.

title: You Know You Like It EP
description: The London duo's debut EP is a full-bodied, slinky embrace of the weirder end of R&B trailblazed by Timbaland and the Neptunes a decade ago.

title: R.I.P.
description: Darren Cunningham is a dance producer who references extroverted, populist music to create a meditative, introverted, immersive experience.

title: Lifetime of Romance
description: With his latest, the young Bloomington, Ind., electronic artist moves on from the abstract sonic adventures of his earlier work to a collection of unabashed synth pop.

title: Cynic's New Year
description: For Horse Feathers' latest album, Justin Ringle brought in scores of Portland musicians to add flourishes of piano, reeds, banjo, and horns. He's expanding his band's palette, not necessarily its sound.

title: Sentenced to Life
description: The Seattle death- and thrash-influenced quintet draws members from Shook Ones, Go It Alone, Blue Monday, and Get the Most, and their second Southern Lord LP is proudly in the hardcore tradition.

title: Ugly
description: The fifth disc from the New Brunswick, N.J., punk trio builds off the group's reputation as shred-oriented SST revivalists, with a refined focus on songwriting.

title: All Hell
description: The onetime trucker and drummer of the stoner metal band Pearls and Brass releases a solo album that finds him crooning, beautifully, over country-music samples.

title: Golden Rhythm/Ink Music
description: Showcasing a knack for marrying the absurd to the sublime, the eccentric English band offers its first album in five years.

title: True Predation
description: This Columbus, Ohio, quartet finds a way to infuse familiar punk templates with subtle progressive elements, resulting in an album that feels like a thick swamp of crust, muck, piss, and bile.

title: What Kind of World
description: The Raconteurs member's fifth solo album finds him playing the rock'n'roll loser once again, and occasionally meriting the Alex Chilton haircut he sports on its cover.

title: June 2009
description: Chaz Bundick reached into his archives for this collection of singles written around the time of his debut, Causers of This. It allows you to think "big picture" not only about Bundick, but the role of production and atmosphere in general.

title: The Money Store
description: Death Grips are angry. It's unclear why. But on their major label debut, the Sacramento noise group's monomaniacal desire to rain down fiery destruction on the powers-that-be is crystal-clear, even if nothing else is.

title: Da Mind of Traxman
description: The veteran Chicago producer's Planet Mu debut is an album more concerned with footwork's past than its future: it's a loving musical history set on loop.

title: This Machine
description: Given its promising start, you might be inclined to place the Dandy Warhols' ninth LP on the level of the alt-rock band's first three records. But then it keeps going.

title: Candy Salad
description: On their sophomore album, the Yeasayer and MGMT-associated Brooklyn chamber-pop band leave every sound tweaked or otherwise troubled.

title: Harmonicraft
description: The Miami sludge-pop band's third album feels like an attempt to make a break with the past, but they might not be able to, at least not yet.

title: Blunderbuss
description: Following the dissolution of the White Stripes and his marriage to model/singer Karen Elson, Jack White releases his first solo LP. Rife with songs about fear and loss, Blunderbuss feels unusually personal.

title: Diamond Rugs
description: Deer Tick's John McCauley and Robbie Crowell and members of the Black Lips, Dead Confederate, Los Lobos, and Six Finger Satellite kick up dust on Diamond Rugs' self-titled debut.

title: Love Is the Plan, the Plan Is Death
description: The gifted 12-string guitarist's latest album-- featuring guest vocals from Geneviève Beaulieu of drone/black metal outfit Menace Ruine-- is a continuation of his tinkering with a variety of instruments as well as a return to his past solo work.

title: Everything EP
description: Following a string of interesting genre detours, Manchester producer Rupert Taylor's house-centric new EP is his most consistently pleasurable release to date.

title: Blackwater Park [Legacy Edition] / Deliverance [Reissue] / Damnation [Reissue] / Lamentations [Reissue]
description: The Swedish band, which mixes psychedelia, prog, and extreme metal, reissues three ambitious studio albums and a live DVD from the early years of the millennium, records that found it transitioning from death growls to cleanly sung acoustic compositions.

title: The Flaming Lips and Heady Fwends
description: This Record Store Day round-up of collaborations conducted over the past year features a cast that includes Ke$ha, Chris Martin, Nick Cave, Yoko Ono, Bon Iver, Neon Indian, and Lightning Bolt, among others. Amazingly, it hangs together well as a front-to-back album.

title: Woods / Amps for Christ
description: This split release sees Amps for Christ's Henry Barnes in as messy a mood as ever, with his taste for roughness rubbing off on Woods' rustic offerings.

title: Netherwards
description: The Seattle death/doom band's bleakly elegant debut album is powerful, complex, and overwhelmingly dense.

title: 2 RMX
description: Grinderman's final release is a collection of remixes by Yeah Yeah Yeahs' Nick Zinner, Factory Floor, QOTSA's Josh Homme, UNKLE, and Robert Fripp, among others.

title: Savage Journey to the American Dream
description: Rick Ross' latest protégé does his thing over a collection of impeccable beats, courtesy of the Neptunes' Chad Hugo and Block Beattaz, among others.

title: Essential Mix
description: The manic, unclassifiable Glasgow producer's overstuffed, expertly curated contribution to the BBC's Essential Mix program pulls together threads from across the musical spectrum.

title: Brass Tactics EP
description: This Bellingham math-punk trio's riotously complex three-song EP is the mark of an exhilarating new voice that's fun, ferocious, and exhausting in the most satisfying kind of way.

title: Lissy Trullie
description: The John Hill (Santigold, M.I.A.) and David Sitek-produced follow-up to 2009's Self-Taught Learner EP arrives fashionably late, and clad in halfway-convincing post-punk attire.

title: The Block Brochure: Welcome to the Soil 1, 2, & 3
description: Not everything works on the Bay Area rapper's sprawling three-volume, 60-track offering, but not only are none of these songs bad, two-thirds of them range from good to mind-blowing.

title: Out of the Game
description: Rufus Wainwright's Mark Ronson-produced seventh album represents the singer's return to more formal song structure, but it also marks a break from the florid, operatic pop that defined his first five albums.

artist: The Congos, Sun Araw, M. Geddes Gengras
title: Icon Give Thank
description: For the most rewarding installment in RVNG's FRKWYS series, Sun Araw and M. Geddes Gengras traveled to Jamaica to collaborate with legendary reggae vocal group the Congos on this psychedelic gospel album.

title: In Between
description: No longer smothered in fuzz, the San Franciscan shoegazers' second album makes up for what its predecessor lacked in hooks and vocal distinction.

title: History
description: The Swedish-born, Berlin-based John Maus collaborator's fourth full-length is a collection of power ballads and off-kilter dance-pop, carried by her commanding, almost Nico-like voice.

title: Europe
description: Improving on its promising debut, the London-via-Australia indie pop band offers a bolder, more lyrically and instrumentally beguiling second album.

title: Sees the Light
description: This second, much improved La Sera collection finds Katy Goodman translating what she brings to Vivian Girls into top-shelf songwriting.

title: Dross Glop
description: With contributions from Hudson Mohawke, Kode9, the Field, Gang Gang Dance's Brian Degraw, and Eye from the Boredoms, this varied remix set plays up the humorous and party-starting aspect of Battles' personality.

title: Plateau Vision
description: Having come to the fore via mash-ups back in the mid-2000s, Raj Haldar continues to investigate contrasts between disparate genres on this original release.

title: Consignment: Favor For a Favor, the Redi-Rock Mixtape
description: The Detroit rapper's subtle poetic gifts and unflinching descriptions of the drug dealer's day-to-day make for a consistent, confident 26-track second album.

title: Spring EP
description: Working under a new name for a new label, producer and songwriter Laurel Halo crafts a rich EP that touches on many sounds but manages to feel whole.

title: With Siinai: Heartbreaking Bravery
description: Continuing his recent forays into more literal storytelling, Spencer Krug's collaboration with Finnish prog-rockers Siinai is a swirly, molten rumination on heartbreak.

title: Sweet Heart Sweet Light
description: Spiritualized's best album since the defining 1997 monument Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space is not so much a drastic transformation as much as an acute refinement, and it also happens to be the most uplifting album of Jason Pierce's career.

title: 120 Days II
description: The Norwegian electro-rockers' first album in six years focuses on larger-than-life electronics, relegating the guitar to a more supportive role.

title: Armor On EP
description: Free of Diddy's Dirty Money project, the vocalist releases a remarkable EP that eschews traditional R&B, contrasting human sympathies with harsh mechanical sounds.

title: Violet Replacement
description: Violet Replacement, a 2xCD-R Liz Harris released to support a Grouper tour of the same name, features extended ambient recordings with few vocals.

title: Ruin 3
description: The conceptually minded Minneapolis electronic duo invited six artists to remix three of its tracks, contributing to an ongoing project that feels outward-looking and communal.

title: Mr. Impossible
description: There's an infectious sense of discovery in Black Dice's latest album as the Brooklyn band finds ways to make bizarre music into something tightly structured and fun.

title: Time Capsules II
description: Brad Oberhofer and co.'s Steve Lillywhite-produced debut finds a once-modest indie band swinging for the fences in hopes of cracking the big leagues.

title: Monnos
description: The British doom trio locates the perfect guitar tone on its crushing new LP.

title: Accelerando
description: Pianist Vijay Iyer returns to the trio format for a collaboration with Stephan Crump and Marcus Gilmore that includes jazz interpretations of Michael Jackson, Duke Ellington, and Flying Lotus.

title: Back From the Dead
description: Chief Keef's breakthrough mixtape, is loud, rough, and unrelenting, but the 16-year-old Chicago rapper's calm, dead-eyed delivery is its most unsettling and intriguing element.

title: MTV Unplugged
description: It's hard to imagine a voice more equipped to puff new life into "MTV Unplugged" than Florence Welch's, but the series' stripped-back approach doesn't do her any favors.

title: No1 2 Look Up 2
description: The 21-year old Queens MC's first release for the label run by Das Racist's Heems works best when he drops the implausible pose as a hip-hop savior and raps as himself.

title: Live 1976
description: This rare 1976 live recording shows the experimental folk musician in uncharacteristically lucid form, tying together unlikely influences into fluid, unusual compositions.

title: The Lost Entrance of the Just
description: Following last year's excellent Eleven Fingers, the mysterious Finnish duo trades the frisson of black metal, post-punk, and pop for a subtle union of gorgeousness and ghoulishness.

title: Split Cranium
description: Aaron Turner of Isis and Jussi Lehtisalo of legendary Finnish shape-shifters Circle join forces for a collection of full-throttle crust punk.

title: Quakers
description: Portishead's Geoff Barrow assembles a 40-plus-person cast ranging from hip-hop vets to obscure MCs for an indie rap recording that's engaging in spite of its heavily fractured structure.

title: Rock and Roll Night Club EP
description: The artist formerly known as Makeout Videotape releases an EP of unsettling soft rock that mixes freaky sleaze with a surprising dose of swooning sensitivity.

title: Strange Grey Days
description: On its self-titled debut, this Vancouver "garage soul" band does a faithful, playful recreation of 1960s girl-group sounds, filtered through proudly grimy production.

title: Nightmare on E Street
description: The rising D.C. rapper's newest bears some worrying marks of encroaching industry bullshit, but by and large, it's a generous helping of what made Fat Trel noticeable in the first place.

title: Let the People Speak
description: Violet Clark has described her second album with husband Frank Black as "doggystyle," but it doesn't even qualify as masturbation.

title: A Wasteland Companion
description: M. Ward's seventh album sounds as gloriously refined as ever, but pairs uncharacteristic sweetness with a mismatched bitter streak for a record with a shaky sense of self.

title: Much Ado About EP
description: The San Franciscan jangle-poppers' final release significantly peps up their previously downtrodden approach for a winsome EP.

title: Dusk | Subside
description: The Melbourne metal band forges a strong bridge between two of its members' past in cultish doom group diSEMBOWLMENT and a more rock-oriented focus on the future.

title: Harmony, Melody and Style: Lovers Rock and Rare Groove in the UK
description: Soul Jazz's latest compilation focuses on British lovers rock, the softer, more feminine counterpart to the politicized roots reggae that soundtracked radical social and racial events in 1970s and 80s Britain.

title: Our Love Is Hurting Us EP
description: On his second EP in as many years, Christopher Dexter Greenspan goes for another swim in witch house's corpse-laden waters.

title: Boys & Girls
description: The much-hyped, Jack White-feted Alabama garage band's debut finally arrives a significant amount of time after its completion, working to their benefit and detriment.

title: Transistor Rhythm
description: On his debut LP, UK juke/bass producer Antony Williams is still taking cues from Chicago's South Side veterans, but for the first time it feels like he's building something of his own.

artist: Janka Nabay and the Bubu Gang
title: An Letah
description: Two years after his Bubu King EP, the N.Y.-based Sierra Leone musician offers a whiplash set of electrified bubu backed by NYC locals like Highlife's Doug Shaw and the band Skeletons.

title: Songs
description: The Leeds producer's sophomore LP is a nasty carnival of electronic pop that giddily hops between styles like a broken radio.

title: De Vermis Mysteriis
description: Following the glossy sheen of 2010's Snakes for the Divine, High on Fire get back to doing what they do best: sweaty, thrashing, chipped-tooth stoner metal.

title: Pink Friday: Roman Reloaded
description: Much of Nicki Minaj's ambitious second LP sweats with a too-big-to-fail desperation. At its best, she innovates with the playful abandon of prime-era Missy Elliott or Busta Rhymes. But in her quest to avoid becoming just another female rapper, she settles for being just another pop star.

title: I Don't Want to Die
description: The Burlington, Vt., singer-songwriter's new album finds him refining his pop vision, splashing it with touches of New Age pensiveness and moments that topple into dissonance.

title: Vattnet Viskar
description: This small-town New Hampshire black metal band's auspicious debut EP manages to marry ambition and efficiency without a misstep.

title: Iradelphic
description: Deciding he was "bored of computers," the restless English producer's latest album (featuring guest vocals from Martina Topley-Bird) offers his most drastic shift to date.

title: I Love You, It's Cool
description: The Brooklyn trio follows 2009's Beast Rest Forth Mouth with a record that's admirable in large part because its ambitions are as subtle and difficult to quantify as its pleasures.

title: A+E
description: On his raw and visceral eighth solo LP, Graham Coxon takes us back to when he was revered as Blur's experimental weirdo.

title: Other People’s Problems
description: The London band, four filmmakers-turned-musicians named after the founder of Surrealism, offer ambiguous politics on their buzzed about debut.

title: New Wild Everywhere
description: The Canadian folk-rock band's fifth record introduces a semi-permanent lineup and marks the first time the Tony Dekker-led group's recorded in a proper studio.

title: Young Man in America
description: The ambitious Vermont-born folk singer and Bon Iver collaborator offers "a meditation on a theme" that pulls off the difficult feat of feeling political without ever being didactic.

title: lowFLOWs: The Columbia Anthology ('91-'93)
description: This collection assembles the post-Minutemen trio's two albums released on Columbia, an EP, and an assortment of extras, offering a generous overview of the group's loose-limbed, slightly lopsided rumble.

title: Wonky
description: Orbital's first album in eight years, featuring a collaboration with Zola Jesus, finds the Hartnoll brothers doing what they've always done best.

title: Locked Down
description: Dan Auerbach of the Black Keys produced the New Orleans legend's newest, a weird-ass mix of grotty funk and R&B.

title: H.N.I.C. 3
description: A year after his release from prison, Mobb Deep's Prodigy offers his latest and most high-profile attempt at finding his footing in A$AP Rocky's New York.

title: Mouseman Cloud
description: The beyond-prolific Guided by Voices frontman's first solo LP since January's Let's Go Eat the Factory was recorded with an emphasis on wordplay.

title: Year Zero OST
description: Combining edits of their best songs with five new pieces, the Vancouver psych-rock band offers a nine-song soundtrack for the post-apocalyptic surf film Year Zero.

title: Kill for Love
description: Chromatics' first album since 2007's stunning Night Drive is a 90-minute tour-de-force that gives their nocturnal foreboding a new sense of grandeur. Though long, Kill for Love is lushly atmospheric and replayable, with expansive interstitial tracks balancing its impressive clutch of gorgeous synth-pop singles.

title: Milo Goes to Compton
description: Naming her first LP after the 1982 debut by the Descendents (who she also covers), the one-woman Oakland band offers an amalgam of punk, garage, and 1960s girl group harmonies.

title: Lightships
description: On his solo debut, Teenage Fanclub's Gerard Love offers a lush, cerebral rendering of his other band's pop ethos with the help of past and present Fanclub members.

title: Both Lights
description: Luke Wyland's latest endlessly resituates itself between towering chamber-folk, cyclonic Marnie Stern-style spazz, and orchestral psych.

title: Acousmatic Sorcery
description: The gifted Chicago singer-songwriter and self-identified outsider artist makes his full-length debut with an often impressive collection of home-recorded material from the last several years.

title: Spooky Action at a Distance
description: The Deerhunter guitarist/songwriter's fantastic second solo LP is unerringly tuneful and immediate, the sort of thing that seems unambitious until you step back and ask yourself just how many records actually manage to pull this off.

title: Grief Pedigree
description: Read Nate Patrin’s review of the album.

title: Come the Thaw
description: Featuring Agalloch's Aesop Dekker on drums, this Bay Area band moves between doom metal and gentler 4AD-adherent epics on its sophomore LP.

title: Happy To You
description: The Swedish trio, including the production duo Bloodshy & Avant (Britney Spears, Kelis, Kylie Minogue), offer springy electronic pop on their sophomore LP.

title: Hundred Waters
description: The Gainesville, Fla., quintet composes bewitching digital folk on its immersive debut.

title: Zammuto
description: Following the breakup of the Books earlier this year, Nick Zammuto's self-titled debut finds him singing and playing his heart out through an array of computer dressing.

title: Ariettes Oubliées...
description: On their second album, Alcest's somber comrades Les Discrets blend post-rock, dusky goth-pop, and the faintest shadow of black metal to create their own take on "French shoegaze metal."

title: Choreography
description: The London power pop band's debut recasts the exuberance of mid-1960s Beatles and Byrds as a manifestation of modern-day social anxieties and sleep-depravation-induced paranoia.

title: awE naturalE
description: This Seattle neo-soul duo lent forcible female vocals to Shabazz Palaces' 2011 LP Black Up. Following a handful of self-released mixtapes, awE naturalE marks their proper debut.

title: Taylor Allderdice
description: Now a legitimate star, Wiz Khalifa offers a free mixtape named for his high school that attempts to reclaim what he sees as his.

title: LateNightTales, Vol. 2
description: The LateNightTales series asks artists to create a "late night" mix from their record collections. Belle and Sebastian's second contribution leans heavily on the 1960s and early 1970s, with occasional glimmers of modernity.

title: Transverse
description: This live recording from an improvisational performance by Throbbing Gristle's Chris Carter and Cosey Fanni Tutti and Factory Floor's Nik Colk Void has an unusual transformative energy.

title: Broda
description: On Broda, the Portuguese group Gala Drop and Six Organs of Admittance's Ben Chasny make like a crack 1960's instrumental band wailing freely.

title: Illusion EP
description: This Seattle band, featuring members of Fleet Foxes and Crystal Skulls, debuts with a five-song EP of tumbling acoustic fingerwork and gauzy group harmonies.

title: Seeds
description: The restless R&B auteur offers one of her most captivating statements, a deeply spiritual collection produced by Madlib.

title: Viva Hate
description: Morrissey's fascinating 1988 solo debut is the perfect subject for a deluxe reissue package, but Morrissey being Morrissey, that isn't what we got.

title: Listen, Whitey! The Sounds of Black Power 1967-1974
description: Focusing on the music and rhetoric of Black Power music at street level, this set places songs by artists like Gil Scott-Heron and the Last Poets alongside spoken word pieces from Stokely Carmichael and Dick Gregory.

title: The Revolution EP
description: The more visceral side project of Alan Sparhawk's Low dips its toes into arena-ready 80s corporate rock with strange results.

title: Kenny Dennis EP
description: The rapper who recently collaborated with Sufjan Stevens steps out with a concept EP that finds him rapping in his Kenny Dennis alter-ego, a character who loves to riff on Chicago sports and sausage and not a whole lot else.

title: Folila
description: With contributions from Santigold, the Yeah Yeah Yeahs' Nick Zinner, and members of TV on the Radio, the Malian duo clearly have genre fusion in mind on their latest.

title: Don't Think
description: This riveting DVD/CD set captures the energy and sensory overload of a Chemical Brothers show. It also showcases many of the finest moments from their catalogue.

title: Mirel Wagner
description: On her self-titled debut, the Ethiopian-Finnish singer-songwriter's stark doom-folk is in permanent flux between concerns of the soul and the desires of the flesh.

title: Earth
description: Marc Richter's fondness for altered records marks him as an evil twin of Philip Jeck or Leyland Kirby. His latest record as Black to Comm began as a film soundtrack, and the audio is a natural fit for a fabulous landscape full of piled corpses.

title: Sonik Kicks
description: On Sonik Kicks, the legendary English songwriter makes use of electronic toys and a variety of production tricks.

title: Mixed Emotions
description: Following an EP and various singles, the sunny Brooklyn synth-pop duo's full-length debut aims for the heart and the gut.

title: MDNA
description: Madonna's 12th studio album, featuring collaborations with M.I.A. and Nicki Minaj, is the product of both a merger and a divorce.

title: Queen of the Wave
description: The sample-happy Finnish electro-pop duo compose an "esoteric pop opera in three parts."

title: Blu Tops EP
description: This free five-song EP finds stalwart NYC producer Ski Beatz (Curren$y) teaming with Cam'ron, Vado, and upstart vocalist McKenzie Eddy.

title: Voices From the Lake
description: As Voices From the Lake, Italian producers Donato Dozzy and Neel reinvent typical techno structures wholesale. Rarely can an album be this intimidatingly detailed, warmly inviting, and totally indifferent.

title: Beak & Claw
description: Sufjan Stevens, the New York composer Son Lux, and the Anticon rapper Serengeti form an oddball trio on this EP.

title: Blue Chips
description: Over the last six months, the Flushing native made the leap from promising character to one of the most hilarious and creative writers in rap. On Blue Chips, he's eminently quotable and savagely funny.

title: Rooms Filled With Light
description: The London baroque-rock band's sophomore album-- produced by Ben Allen (Merriweather Post Pavilion, Halcyon Digest)-- finds the group aspiring to darker and difficult territory.

title: Ice Level
description: The genre-bending New York synth-funk septet create a glorious mess on their full-length debut.

artist: Oren Ambarchi | Keiji Haino | Jim O'Rourke
title: Imikuzushi
description: This ecstatic third installment of Keiji Haino, Jim O'Rourke, and Oren Ambarchi's annual live meeting features ear-filling noise-rock that conjures metal, psych, and stoner rock.

title: Foreign Body
description: Liz Harris (Grouper) and Jesy Fortino (Tiny Vipers) collaborated on this collection that effectively and purposefully combines their respective sounds.

artist: Odd Future Wolf Gang Kill Them All
title: The OF Tape Vol. 2
description: Incorporating all of Odd Future's members with surprising ease (not an easy task considering all the stylistic differences at play), The OF Tape Vol. 2 is the first thing in well over a year that will remind people of why they liked the L.A. skate punks in the first place.

title: The Host
description: Under a new alias, the Irish producer Barry Lynn (aka Boxcutter) abandons beat-driven aggression for short, wafting pieces, and something more personal and psychedelic.

title: Leaving Atlanta
description: Four years after his debut, the Atlanta power-pop songwriter returns with a sing-along sophomore LP dedicated to five friends who died in quick succession, most way too young.

title: Give You the Ghost
description: Gayngs mastermind Ryan Olson produced the debut from this double-drumming Minneapolis art-rock band fronted by ex-Roma di Luna singer Channy Leaneagh.

title: God's Father
description: Lil B's newest is a 34-track opus that demands several sessions to take in. It's the latest proof that he hasn't finished telling us his peculiar story.

title: Between the Times and the Tides
description: The biggest solo production of the Sonic Youth co-founder's career features contributions from SY bandmate Steve Shelley, Wilco's Nels Cline, jazz organist John Medeski, guitarist Alan Licht, and former bandmate Jim O'Rourke.

title: Pipe Dreams
description: This Bay Area shoegaze outfit features Nick Bassett of the black metal group Deafheaven. On their latest, they manage to establish a distinctive identity in a style that often relies on blurry facelessness.

title: Yesterday Was Lived and Lost
description: New Build is the London trio of Hot Chip's Al Doyle and Felix Martin with engineer Tom Hopkins. On their debut, they capture the rare alchemy that first made Hot Chip so appealing.

title: Canto Arquipélago
description: Antwerp-based collagist Lieven Martens makes contemporary New Age music that ripples with oceanic calm. This 35-minute collection is barely perceptible in places.

title: Lover Motion EP
description: The Cut Copy bassist's first solo EP includes synth work from Cut Copy vocalist Dan Whitford and production by members of Architecture in Helsinki.

title: Silent Hour/Golden Mile EP
description: The Grizzly Bear and Department of Eagles member's first solo EP is a brief, majestic song cycle.

title: Trevor Jackson Presents Metal Dance: Industrial/Post-Punk/EBM Classics and Rarities 80 to 88
description: The man behind Playgroup lends his curatorial ear to music from the stiffer, meaner, moodier, fuglier world of 1980s industrial and its various offshoots, from the club-ready to the floor-clearing.

title: Decade
description: Having broken through in the beat-driven sphere under his Ital alias with his excellent album Hive Mind, Daniel Martin-McCormick returns to the serrated edges of his noise-rock project Mi Ami.

title: Valentina
description: Though they are touring playing their 1991 album Seamonsters in its entirety, Leeds indie stalwarts the Wedding Present also have an album of new material, their first in four years.

title: Wreck
description: Unsane's sound is anti-evolutionary, almost masochistically so. For the past 20-odd years, both in their gruesome album covers and their often monosyllabically titled songs, they've explored only shades of grey, with spatterings of red. Their latest is one of their better ones.

title: Port of Morrow
description: Five years after the moody Wincing the Night Away and two releases by his Broken Bells project, James Mercer returns to the Shins energized and with his songwriting prowess intact.

title: Baby
description: The debut album by this Camden quartet demonstrates a studious appreciation of Clinton-era guitar rock. At times, they seem to want nothing more than to channel a 45-minute MTV rock block from 1995.

title: Everyday Grace
description: Incorporating elements of industrial music and a dissonant strain of early-1980s computer funk, producer Elon Katz explores themes of over-consumption, isolation, and claustrophobia.

title: Eternal Turn of the Wheel
description: Controversy regarding politics has followed this mysterious Ukrainian band since its inception, and its latest LP offers no easy answers. But the album finds them at a musical peak, splitting the difference between Burzum worship and their folk-music leanings.

title: Bogota Rich: The Prequel
description: This 13-song mixtape from the Maybach Music Group associate is disappointingly brief but also serves as a showcase for the rapper's fiendish creativity and technical ability.

title: Weed Forestin'
description: Lou Barlow's 1987 home-recorded indie folk cassette album is re-released yet again in a variety of formats with an hour of bonus material, and once again under the original Sentridoh name.

title: Form & Control
description: This NYC disco-pop outfit is indeed a band, and they do make occasional use of handclaps. Two out of three ain't bad.

title: Pretty Ugly
description: Leon Smart's debut for Hyperdub offers an approach to dance music that looks askew, glances awry, and always moves out of kilter.

title: Frying on This Rock
description: White Hills' third LP for Thrill Jockey in as many years finds these purveyors of brain-warping psychedelia arriving at Martin Bisi's studio with a few things worked out.

title: Closer EP
description: Cities Aviv collaborator steps out with an EP that pulls together many of-the-moment sounds-- quiet-storm R&B, Chicago house, 1970s funk, hypnagogic fuzz-pop-- in service of a concept album about getting it on.

title: 4Eva N a Day
description: The rapper's self-produced followup to last year's Return of 4Eva is heavy on the Southern rap exercises that point you away from his music and towards his heroes.

title: Phédre
description: Toronto's Phédre zig-zag through the sounds of classic rock, disco, post-punk, and gothed-out rockabilliy. They never stay in one place for long, but their melodic sensibility provides the thread.

title: Noctiluca
description: On their ambitious debut LP, past members of Finally Punk, Mika Miko, and Talbot Tagora make expansive music that's decidedly not punk.

title: The Shadow Gallery
description: The Brooklyn hardcore/metal quintet's debut LP fuses the grandeur of Isis with the precision of Dillinger Escape Plan and injects it with unavoidable catchiness.

title: Where the Sands Turn to Gold
description: Jason DiEmilio, the Philadelphia musician behind Azusa Plane, took his own life in late 2006. This 2xCD + DVD collection offers an extensive look at the delicate, powerful guitar-derived drone work he created.

title: Always
description: You know what you're in for when you put on a new Xiu Xiu album, and the band's latest is a well-executed sampler of the magnified pain and horror we've come to expect from them.

title: Limo
description: This Brooklyn-via-Chicago electro duo's Limo consists of eight "movements" that bleed into one another and features vocals from Brazilian Girls' Sabina Sciubba.

title: Father Creeper
description: The South African-born rapper/singer's second album, his first for Sub Pop, attempts to make a virtue of its own messiness.

title: Kingdoms
description: The debut release from UK electronic artist (and La Roux keyboardist) Mike Norris is a collection of lush, deep DIY house music.

title: Muscle Car Chronicles
description: The New Orleans MC's experiment with rapping over a live funk-rock band stands as the first notable misstep of his rejuvenated career.

title: Rocket Juice and the Moon
description: Damon Albarn, former Fela Kuti drummer Tony Allen, and Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist Flea are the core of this album of West African-style funk and psychedelia.

title: Brain Pulse Music
description: Ghost ringleader Masaki Batoh realizes a long-held dream to control music via brain waves, offering two such compositions amidst several improvised pieces.

title: Spaced Out
description: The Calgary garage-pop band's warbly and reverb-heavy debut sounds like it was fueled by a sugar high.

title: Jewelry
description: This free beat tape from Los Angeles sound collagist Matthew McQueen feels tailor-made for the unconscious.

title: Medicine Show #13: Black Tape
description: A bit like the bookend to the original dozen installments of his Medicine Show series, Black Tape fuses rap a cappellas to Madlib's own hazy, no-fi dub-of-a-dub aesthetic.

title: We All Raise Our Voices to the Air (Live Songs 4.11-8.11)
description: This 2xCD collection, the Decemberists' first live full-length in their decade-plus career, sets all their heady concepts, genre nods, and oddball experiments side by side.

title: Shangaan Shake
description: This 2xCD compilation features Theo Parrish, Demdike Stare, Ricardo Villalobos, and others doing remixes of 2010's Shangaan Electro: New Wave Dance Music from South Africa.

title: Faithful Man
description: The soul veteran builds out every song with towering horn arrangements, strings, and background vocals on an album focused on love, loss, and longing.

title: The Chap
description: The North London pop quintet follow last year's tongue-in-cheek greatest hits album We Are the Best with a collection that finds them immersed in feelings of insecurity, isolation, and anxiety.

title: Zoo
description: The Bay Area quintet's first record for Matador feels a long way from its powerviolence beginnings, with a cleaned-up sound and a focus on garage-rock hooks.

title: Ssss
description: Three decades after "Just Can't Get Enough", Depeche Mode's Vince Clarke and Martin Gore are back with 10 tracks of fierce, instrumental, no-bullshit techno.

title: Dispossession
description: The Brooklyn singer-songwriter weaves together British folk, improvised jazz, Indian raga, psych-rock, and a strange, unforgettable voice on his sophomore album.

title: The Aberrant Years
description: The Australian noise-punk trio made compelling music from repetitive elements and narrow sonic parameters. The Aberrant Years collects the 1978-1989 lineup's complete output, including rare bonus tracks.

title: Careless World: Rise of the Last King
description: Does the 22-year-old Compton-born MC have any other songs as good as his breakout "Rack City"? His sophomore album tries its damndest to answer this question in the affirmative.

title: Milk Famous
description: The Brooklyn-via-Columbia, Missouri sextet's Mike McCarthy-produced third album finds the group overestimating their ability to be interesting instead of likeable.

title: Love at the Bottom of the Sea
description: The record that marks the end of Magnetic Fields' self-imposed "no synth trilogy" is also the first Magnetic Fields album in a more than a decade that isn't organized around a formal limitation.

title: Scum.Collapse.Eradication
description: The vicious Canadian black/death metal band's fourth album is a challenge and a triumph.

title: King Con
description: The New York singer-songwriter's debut is catchy and well-produced, but she rejects the ice-cream gloss and ambiguity of many other contemporary pop artists.

title: Untitled EP
description: Featuring production work from Juicy J, Flying Lotus, and the Alchemist, this is the first major release from the Odd Future camp to rely almost wholly on collaborations from outside its circle.

title: The Clearing
description: Recorded in Bon Iver's Wisconsin retreat, the North Carolina duo's third LP is broad and ambitious, documenting a challenging year with unprecedented studio gleam.

title: Wrecking Ball
description: Bruce Springsteen's 17th studio album is an overtly political affair, with songs that tackle hypocrisy, greed, and corruption set to a musical backing of Civil War snares, gospel howls, and chain-gang stomps.

title: Best Behavior
description: The promising Brooklyn "synth-punk" trio's sophomore album is more accessible and enjoyable than their debut, but is it a legitimate leap?

title: Ain't Ain't Ain't
description: Tim Fite's first album for ANTI- in years finds the Brooklyn-based singer-songwriter confusing being nice with being interesting.

title: Fatherland EP
description: On this seven-song EP, the New York trio replaces the post-Nevermind feel of its debut with a purposefully regressive sound that brings to mind a mid-1980s Homestead Records signee.

title: All of Me
description: On her third record, Estelle's more focused on hitmaking than crafting a cohesive album statement.

title: Break It Yourself
description: Andrew Bird's latest album, which includes a duet with St. Vincent, finds the multi-instrumentalist working more collaboratively with a band than he has in a long time.

title: The Minimal Wave Tapes Vol. 2
description: Compiled by Peanut Butter Wolf and Minimal Wave founder Veronica Vasicka, The Minimal Wave Tapes Vol. 2 offers a second gleaning of tracks from the cloistered minimal wave universe.

title: The Belbury Tales
description: By welcoming in a couple of guest players on a number of tracks, the meticulous Welsh electronic musician Jim Jupp creates his most pleasingly open-ended release to date.

title: bell hooks
description: On this DJ Benzi-hosted mixtape titled after the pen name of black feminist thinker Gloria Jean Watkins, the Chicago hip-hop crew throw a party without toning down their fiery rhetoric.

title: One Second of Love
description: In the context of her catalogue, this feels like a coming out party for Ramona Gonzalez's Nite Jewel. Compared to the electro-pop project's more lo-fi beginnings, the music here is forthright and clear.

title: Open Your Heart
description: The Brooklyn quartet's excellent new LP treats the last four decades of rock music like an amusement park rather than a museum.

title: Killing Time
description: Featuring three members of Magic Bullets,the Troggs-inspired Bay Area trio balances an aggressive delivery and melodic, relatively reserved vocals on their debut LP.

title: Into the Waves
description: The solo debut from Sophia Knapp, also a member of Cliffie Swan (formerly Lights), features a couple of duets with labelmate Bill Callahan.

title: Possession
description: Frontwoman Christine Davis leads this Olympia metal quintet through no-frills proto-thrash, grandiose classic rock, and smoky doom on the band's sophomore LP.

title: Personality
description: Berlin-based UK producer Paul Rose eschews dubstep on his third Scuba LP, using prog house, trance, big beat, rave, old techno, and synth pop to create something stylishly retro.

title: Ekstasis
description: On her second album, the California singer and songwriter pulls in references and sounds from everywhere and shapes them into music that's both haunting and life-affirming.

title: Silica Gel
description: James Ferraro drops much of the hip-hop inspired material of his last free mixtape on this follow-up released under his new Bodyguard moniker.

title: Pre Language
description: The Chicago band's third LP features Sonic Youth's Steve Shelley as full-time drummer, and it's their most concise, commercial music to date.

title: Sounds From Nowheresville
description: On the English duo's genre-hopping sophomore album the only common thread is how uniformly bad everything is.

title: Ghostory
description: Since their debut, School of Seven Bells have continuously pared down song length, sonic clutter, and personnel. On their third LP, the duo of Alejandra Deheza and Ben Curtis come across like they've achieved Zen perfection.

title: Sorrow and Extinction
description: The debut album by this young doom metal outfit from Arkansas is startlingly well realized, with deep, sludgy guitar textures and proggy songs that are complemented by a sparkling melodic sensibility.

title: When You're Gone EP
description: UK producer Stuart Howard's Brainfeeder debut offers sparkling pop deconstructed with avant-garde abandon.

title: Beard, Wives, Denim
description: Sharing two members with Tame Impala, this Australian psych trio blends indulgent chunks of far-outness with fundamentally solid rock'n'roll tunes.

title: The Keychain Collection
description: On his debut, Will Ozanne combines the low-end physicality of bass music with the care and caution of cocktail-lounge fare.

title: Vee Vee (Remastered)
description: Seventeen years after its release, Archers of Loaf's sophomore album gets reissued as a 2xCD collection, remastered by original producer Bob Weston, and including 16 bonus tracks, liner notes, and new cover art.

title: How About I Be Me (And You Be You)?
description: The title of Sinéad O'Connor's first album in five years might seem self-exploitive if it didn't so thoroughly comment on and confound her recent controversies. It's been ages since she's released a record this devastating.

title: The End of That
description: On their third LP, the Montreal indie rock trio attempt to take unsparing inventory, offer sincere amends, and confront the responsibilities of adulthood.

title: TRST
description: On their rich, room-filling debut, the Toronto electro-goth duo of Robert Alfons and Austra's Maya Postepski make malevolent, sexy synth-pop.

title: A Victim of Stars: 1982-2012
description: This engaging compilation of work by the former Japan vocalist begins begins with a version of a song from his old band, moves through material from his solo LPs, and closes with a new song.

title: The Slideshow Effect
