description: Gonjasufi's multi-faceted vocals get the remix treatment from Oneohtrix Point Never, Broadcast and the Focus Group, and others.

title: Lucky Shiner
description: London bedroom producer follows a slew of excellent EPs and remixes with his much-anticipated Ghostly debut LP.

title: Matador at 21
description: Matador celebrates 21 years as a label with an eclectic limited-edition box that collects highlights plus a disc of live material.

title: Foreign Landscapes
description: German pianist/composer follows his excellent 2008 album, Ferndorf, with an album of chamber and piano pieces inspired by various locales.

title: Duppy Writer
description: UK hip-hop star gives over his catalog to dub producer Wrongtom for a radical makeover.

title: Sound of the Police
description: Famed underground hip-hop DJ here blends the sources, influences, and echoes of Mulatu Astatke's 1960s and 70s Ethio-jazz scene into a winning mix.

title: To Dreamers
description: Stoltz's latest for Sub Pop finds him dressing down his pocket symphonies, throwing a little more grease and glam at his well-oiled tunes.

title: The Age of Adz
description: Sufjan returns with a welcome change-up, as he moves away from bookish detail, experiments with electronics, and writes from a more personal perspective.

title: Graffiti Composition
description: The experimental craftsman teams here with Elliott Sharp for an improvised concert based on an abstract score, one crafted by graffiti on blank music sheets.

title: Holkham Drones
description: Following fellow Border Community producers James Holden and Nathan Fake, this UK producer gently, effectively recalls Oval, Seefeel, and Cocteau Twins.

title: Last Day of Summer
description: Austin band celebrates the end of summer with a free online release full of experiments, detours, and well-taken chances.

title: Blue Water White Death
description: Xiu Xiu's Jamie Stewart and Shearwater's Jonathan Meiburg come together for a new project.

title: Write About Love
description: Settling into a chiming, mod-inflected version of 70s AM pop, the indie pop legends put the focus here on their ensemble playing and intricate arrangements.

title: Marcberg
description: Rapper associated with Busta Rhymes' Flipmode Squad steps out with an album that combines early 1990s boom-bap with an impressive flair for storytelling.

title: Sailors With Wax Wings
description: Helmed by Pyramids' R. Loren, this crew also features Prurient, James Blackshaw, Marissa Nadler, and members of Unwound, Slowdive, Swans, and Current 93.

title: An Ark for the Listener
description: One of experimental music's current stars, Jeck expertly mixes, loops, and layers passages from old records into an instantly identifiable aesthetic.

title: 1,000 Years
description: Sleater-Kinney's banshee-wailing singer retreats to creating a record of surprisingly muted, slow-burning intimacy.

title: King Night
description: The witch house poster band's brand of slowed-down, blown-out, culturally mishmashed electronic music has proven divisive, but it was always meant to be.

title: Past Time
description: San Francisco-based post-punk group makes a solid second album thanks to its three distinct and spirited vocalists.

title: Wolfpack Party
description: Bloghouse-rap holdovers the Pack return after an unusally long layoff, bearing no resemblance to the meme-generating solo career of group member Lil B.

title: Epic
description: Sophomore album from this Brooklyn-via-Tennessee singer-songwriter improves on her debut with classical songwriting and a confident, ethereal delivery.

title: A Swedish Love Story EP
description: This sonic continuation of Heartland is a reflection of Pallett's new live setup, where the once solo star is now augmented by a multi-instrumentalist.

title: Marnie Stern
description: Still balancing earnestness and technique, Marnie Stern's songs here are darker, the lyrics lingering on loss, regret, doubt, and failed love.

title: Fuck Dance, Let's Art: Sounds From a New American Underground
description: !K7 compilation attempts a lo-fi electo scene overview with tracks from Toro Y Moi, Balam Acab, Animal Collective, and others.

title: Solo
description: One of the most inventive and vital men in contemporary jazz, expert collaborator Vijay Iyer finally gets around to doing a solo piano LP.

title: BXI EP
description: One of the world's best, most interesting rock bands, the Japanese noise group Boris, teams with the former singer of 80s hard rock heroes the Cult.

title: Ring
description: Alongside Bat for Lashes, Fever Ray, and Zola Jesus, Glasser is in the upper tier of those making quasi-mystical, swirling electro-pop.

title: Caribou Vibration Ensemble
description: Dan Snaith captures a rare performance by the 15-person band he assembled for ATP NYC; guests include Four Tet and members of the Sun Ra Arkestra.

title: oOoOO EP
description: Witch-house/drag producer's debut EP drops a pin at the crossroads where commercially viable hip-hop gravitates toward left-field electronic influences.

title: Shadow Temple
description: Raw, unrestrained psych-rock band releases its fourth album, and first for Animal Collective's Paw Tracks label.

title: Meet Me at the Muster Station
description: The full-length debut from this Ontario duo finds them putting a forceful and funny spin on the sound of 1980s indie rock.

title: Best Bless EP
description: This project from Sleepy Doug Shaw of White Magic draws inspiration from the African highlife style with surprisingly engaging results.

title: I Am Not a Human Being
description: A clearinghouse of pre-jailtime work, Weezy's latest album is neither a hint of what's to come nor a clear reminder of why we care so much in the first place.

title: Males
description: Former A Frames drummer Lars Finberg continues to put his hyper-caustic wit and knack for garage-punk to good use with this In the Red project.

title: Losing Sleep
description: Five years ago, brain hemorrhages left the former Orange Juice singer unable to read, write, walk, or talk; here he makes a courageous return to form.

title: Metallic Spheres
description: Over the past few years, the Orb have been nudging their sound back toward its techno-hippie roots; now they team with Pink Floyd's David Gilmour (!).

title: Telephantasm
description: One of grunge's founding fathers and leading lights has its career compiled in multiple ways, none of them satisfactorily.

title: Forget
description: Twin Shadow's consistently compelling and refreshing debut nods to 80s new wave but doesn't forget the songwriting; Grizzly Bear's Chris Taylor produces.

title: Warp Riders
description: On their third full-length, the Austin retro metal band teams with producer Matt Bayles (Isis, Mastodon).

title: TSOL
description: Kenya-born, Ontario-raised rapper's Polaris Prize-nominated album is being pegged by the faithful as a new standard for positive rap.

artist: Working for a Nuclear Free City
title: Jojo Burger Tempest
description: Manchester band returns with a blend of live drumming, textural guitars, skittering electronics, and wistful harmonies.

title: Bubblegum
description: UK cult band Clinic continue to make dependably good music, here continuing their ongoing exploration of vintage psychedelia.

title: Le Noise
description: After an unpredictable decade, the rock vet starts off a new one with a near-solo record helmed by famed producer Daniel Lanois.

title: Eskmo
description: After a two-year burst of activity that includes tracks on Warp and Planet Wu, rising electronic producer Eskmo issues his debut LP.

title: Good Things
description: Reinventing himseld as a full-on neo-soul singer, Aloe Blacc follows his inspired and often-innovative 2006 LP, Shine Through.

title: The Game of Monogamy
description: Cursive and the Good Life frontman again effectively takes his music to the edge of emotional catastrophe.

title: Public Strain
description: For their sophomore effort, the Calgary post-punk band offer a bleak but beautiful record, full of subtly skewed melodies.

title: Klavierwerke EP
description: Few artists are stretching the boundaries of dance music wider than this UK producer, who follows CMYK with another excellent EP.

title: Tidelands
description: This rootsy band aims for the harmony-heavy sound of Neil Young or the Band, and their second album is more deliberate than its shaggy predecessor.

title: AM/FM
description: The producer with an ear for plunderphonic-style cut-ups returns with a remix album drawing from his previous LP, Radio.

title: Blood Under the Bridge
description: With veterans of 90s indie rock stalwarts Silkworm and Seam amongst their ranks, Bottomless Pit unsurprisingly value unflinching resolve and ambitious sprawl.

title: Safehouses EP
description: Like Burial or James Blake, this producer uses vocal samples to build gorgeous, unsettling post-dubstep; in his case with nods to many sub-genres.

title: Station to Station [Deluxe Edition]
description: Bowie issues a new version of his most immaculately constructed album, the most important tactical transition in a career built upon aesthetic reinvention.

title: The Hundred in the Hands
description: NYC duo nail all the crowd-pleasing, familiar signifiers of buzzy, dancey new wave but fail to distinguish themselves from their peers.

title: Return II Space
description: This South London duo takes a classicist's approach to dubstep here, leaving behind influences from the pop world and sticking with the dark and heavy basics.

title: Help Me Name Melody
description: Austin band continues to create open, exploratory music that evokes the authoritative nuance of Low.

title: Ninja Tune XX: 20 Years of Beats and Pieces
description: One of the longest-running labels to come out of the late-80s/early-90s explosion in dance and hip-hop celebrates 20 years in the game with a 6xCD set.

title: Everything in Between
description: L.A. dream-punks' second LP matches a new, nuanced approach to their expansive noise with their sturdiest set of songs yet.

title: From the Cradle to the Rave
description: After a lifetime in the dance underground, Marcus Lambkin, a longtime DFA fixture, finally issues his debut LP. Hot Chip's Alexis Taylor and Juan MacLean guest.

title: Postcards From a Young Man
description: Energized by the success of Journal For Plague Lovers, the Manics return with an album that's grandiose even for them, but they make it work.

title: Mixed Race
description: Another tentative comeback album from the 90s giant, Mixed Race's best moments look back to Tricky's bleak peak-period work.

title: The Trip
description: After two decades fronting Stereolab and her side project Monade, Laetitia Sadier makes a strong solo debut.

title: Halcyon Digest
description: Deerhunter make a record about the joy of early music discovery, and in revisiting that youthful enthusiasm, they brilliantly rekindle it.

title: Phosphene Dream
description: Austin psych-rock band's third LP finds them peeling back the psychedelic murk and tempering their bad vibes with a hint of flower-power homage.

title: The Princess Is Here
description: One of the 00s' best singles artists continues to struggle with LPs and her label; this mixtape is a look at what could be next for her.

title: Singing Ax
description: Fleet Foxes member releases another muted, grave solo folk album-- this one even more bleak than usual.

title: Beast Rest Forth Mouth Remixed
description: One of indie's best post-Animal Collective bands enlists the Field, Justin Broadrick, High Places, and others to remix the songs from their 2009 LP.

title: Love Remains
description: The debut full-length from this hazy R&B-leaning lo-fi project is the terrific culmination of a year of heavy recording activity.

title: Drawing Down the Moon
description: Orenda Fink and Maria Taylor continue their second life as Azure Ray, with Crooked Fingers/Archers of Loaf's Eric Bachmann back as producer.

title: Elf Power
description: The Elephant 6 vets dial down their pop hooks for a record dedicated to their late friend, frequent collaborator, and fellow Athenian Vic Chesnutt.

title: You Are Not Alone
description: Working with Jeff Tweedy, the soul veteran sounds energetic and artful on a collection of covers and re-imagined hits from her past.

title: Fields
description: José González reconvened his pre-fame band Junip for an excellent EP earlier this year; now they release their first LP in almost a decade.

title: Sit Down, Man
description: They came on the scene with online novelty hit "Combination Pizza Hut and Taco Bell", but there's a lot more to this New York rap outfit on their new mixtape.

title: The Traveller
description: A techno record without many of techno's signifiers, the latest from Shed is a difficult, slippery, beautiful collection of short, fragmented compositions.

title: In Live Concert at the Royal Albert Hall
description: Epic metal band celebrate their fertile, eclectic catalog with a 3xCD, 2xDVD set that documents one career-expansive three-hour show.

title: My Father Will Guide Me Up a Rope to the Sky
description: Michael Gira reunites his epochal band, retaining its bleakness and melodrama but presenting it now via his love for apocalyptic country blues.

title: To All My Friends, Blood Makes the Blade Holy: The Atmosphere EPs
description: Returning to the EP format that served them so well on Lucy Ford all those years ago, the emo-rap O.G.s offer their best release in some time.

title: Business Casual
description: Blog-house leftovers jump to Atlantic and continue to demonstrate a love of and appreciation for squelchy chart pop.

title: Fission
description: On their fourth full-length, the California band returns with some new wrinkles that expand their shoegazing sound.

title: Frankie Rose and the Outs
description: Member of Crystal Stilts, Vivian Girls, and Dum Dum Girls abandons the lo-fi M.O. of those groups for a harmonically driven, high-fidelity throwback pop album.

title: Moon Deluxe
description: Former Titus Andronicus guitarist crafts a record that seems homespun but muscular, recalling Phil Elverum's defunct Microphones project.

title: Barking
description: The 90s electronic totems have seen their classic work age extremely well, yet oddly struggled to sort out a clear identity in the here and now.

title: Majesty Shredding
description: Nearly a decade since their last album, Superchunk crank out snarky bruised-romantic pop-punk anthems without any dip in energy level or quality control.

title: Our Cubehouse Still Rocks
description: Bob Pollard's new Spaceships LP is not only rife with stuff for megafans to pore over but could catch on with those who'd forgotten about the man as well.

title: Faults
description: One of the great forgotten bands of the 1990s reconvenes at a time when their neo-shoegaze meets rave meets ambient sound is all the rage.

title: Heretofore EP
description: The N.C. folk-pop trio follow their breakthrough LP Gather, Form & Fly with an easygoing yet tightly structured set of songs.

title: One Club
description: Herbert pays homage to DJ culture on his latest record, composed from sounds recorded during one night at the Robert Johnson nightclub in Frankfurt.

title: Pattern + Grid World EP
description: Following the dense and ambitious Cosmogramma, the L.A. producer returns with a short and more accessible EP that extends his creative streak.

title: Sleep Forever
description: Though they're still slavishly devoted to their influences, Crocodiles expand their sound on their second LP with help from Simian Mobile Disco's James Ford.

title: Old Punch Card
description: The Sea and Cake leader returns with a very different kind of album from his two song-based solo LPs, releasing a contemplative, loose electronic record.

title: Crush
description: L.A. punk band completes the transformation into goth and cold wave, with an emotive, dramatic record that still unmistakably sounds like their work.

title: Expektoration Live
description: Considering his off-the-charts negative live reputation, DOOM has some big balls to release a concert recording.

title: Hurley
description: Weezer return to basics on their eighth album, and first for Epitaph Records.

title: Alibi Coast
description: Painter and founding Black Dice member makes his solo debut with a bold, bittersweet folk-pop album commemorating his late brother.

title: Skit I Allt
description: The Swedish prog-psych outfit slows down the tempo and experiments with a more expansive sound.

title: Songs for Singles
description: Miami underground-metal trio follow-up 2008's excellent Meanderthal with this stopgap eight-song release that has an intense focus on brevity.

title: Sometimes the Blues Is Just a Passing Bird EP
description: Neither a sequel nor a satellite to this year's The Wild Hunt, the Tallest Man on Earth's new EP is slightly darker, muted, and meditative.

title: Grinderman 2
description: Nick Cave's schizophrenic and sloppy mid-life crisis project, Grinderman, returns with another album of feral urges and ferocious guitar work.

title: Lights From Paradise
description: Less stoner rock than stoned rock, QFF's sophomore album is raucous, texturally rich, and whimsical.

title: Man Alive
description: Future Mercury Prize contenders continue to make it difficult for us to take UK hypes very seriously.

title: Album of the Year
description: Detroit underground hip-hop star comes to grips with his particularly difficult 2009 on this deeply determined LP.

title: Pop Negro
description: A huge influence on the summery and Balearic sounds in indie over the past two years, Barcelona's El Guincho returns with his sophomore album.

title: False Priest
description: Kevin Barnes delivers more ambitious psych-pop in the vein of Hissing Fauna or Skeletal Lamping, here with help from Jon Brion and Janelle Monáe.

title: This Alone Above All Else in Spite of Everything
description: Welcome back to another record from doom-folk machine Mat Sweet's morally ambivalent universe of violence, despair, and loveliness.

title: The Vaselines: Sex with an X
description: The Glasgow duo of Frances McKee and Eugene Kelly-- feted by Nirvana, backed here by members of Belle and Sebastian-- release their first LP since 1989.

title: Memphis
description: Memphis indie pop band follows top singles "Hey Boy" and "Superball" with an album of first kisses and Brian Wilson-like melodies.

title: Penny Sparkle
description: Longtime NYC band suspends its Sonic Youth and MBV worship and makes a record of all pillowy electro-balladry.

title: Interpol
description: Interpol re-group on Matador and record a bleak, depressive album about disillusionment and being at the end of one's rope.

title: Fin Eaves
description: The drone-pop band returns with its fourth proper album, which mixes blasts of noise with more melodic elements.

title: On the Bright Side
description: Sasu Ripatti (Luomo, Vladislav Delay) issues a record of the analog, bleeps-and-bass sound that characterized UK rave at the start of the 90s.

title: 7AM
description: Creators of one the songs of the year, "Cheaters", this duo-- like James Blake or How to Dress Well-- craft hazy, homemade versions of pop, R&B, and dance.

title: Senior
description: Just 18 months after the effervescent electro-pop of Junior, Röyksopp return with an all-instrumental follow-up.

title: Lisbon
description: On their sixth studio LP, the Walkmen use mariachi horns and echoes of 1950s production styles to realize their wounded, anxious, and affecting songs.

title: No Ghost
description: On their latest the Canadian folk-rockers show a flair for ballads and an ear for textures but struggle to articulate an original voice.

title: Tomorrow Morning
description: E returns with another exercise in self-referentiality and self-indulgences.

title: Pope Killdragon
description: Confessional singer-songwriter abandons the personal tragedies that inspired his debut in favor of an astoundingly original twist on the loner-folk template.

title: Bitches Brew [Legacy Edition]
description: One of the most unfuckwithable records of the 20th century gets another pair of reissue releases, the better of the two being this Legacy Edition.

title: Body Talk Pt. 2
description: Robyn releases the middle part of her Body Talk trilogy, here tabling some of her forays into the offbeat and sticking with her pure pop wheelhouse.

title: The Soft Wave
description: After pre-dating the rise of artists like Emeralds and Oneohtrix Point Never, Arp's drone gets a shot of songcraft and traditional instrumentation.

title: Live at Roadburn 2007
description: The epic kings of doom and sludge, a huge influence on this century's metal, release their first official live record.

title: Kilimanjaro
description: One of Kompakt's cornerstone artists returns to making slow, bleary, moody, spooky sounds just as they find favor in the U.S. electro-pop underground.

title: Wilderness Heart
description: Stephen McBean's boogie outfit makes a more concerted effort to reconcile the band's inner darkness and light, leaning as much on pop as psych.

title: We Have Remixes EP
description: The electro-pop band has tracks from One Life Stand reworked by house hero Todd Edwards, Caribou's Dan Snaith, and techno hotshot Osborne.

title: Afro-Beat Airways: West African Shock Waves, Ghana & Togo 1972-1978
description: The tireless Analog Africa label heads to Ghana and Togo to explore the area's tight-knit 1970s funk scene.

title: We Can't Fly
description: Apparently, "artistic differences" wasn't a bullshit reason for this potentially giant dance duo's recent breakup: Their debut LP is all over the place.

title: The Last Call
description: Mixtape star and B.o.B. associate fortunately hasn't switched up his style, or lost his creative spark, on his latest release.

title: Minotaur
description: The UK cult act continues to draw from 60s soft-pop yet adds off-kilter twists-- a spoken-word, musique concrète ghost tale-- on this mini-LP.

title: Personal Life
description: The pop-punkers are a bit less frantic as they turn their attention from politics to affairs of the heart, and the results are mixed.

title: Machines Hate Me
description: L.A. hip-hop producer combines 80s chiptunes with the -bumper hip-hop breaks that are currently his hometown sound.

title: O
description: The deluge of material from the long-dormant electronic experimentalist continues with a 2xCD set that builds on the new sound unveiled on his Oh EP.

title: The Capitol Years: 1995-2007
description: This sporadically successful glam-pop band's stint on a major label is traced from start to finish.

title: I'm Having Fun Now
description: Sure to garner comparisons to She & Him, Jenny Lewis' collab with boyfriend and folk troubadour Jonathan Rice is rougher, tougher, and more rock'n'roll.

title: All Delighted People EP
description: Ahead of his October LP, Sufjan Stevens issues an hour-plus "EP" that seems to accommodate a grab bag of disparate ideas and familiar sounds.

title: Nothing Else
description: Lorn's debut on Flying Lotus' label is 30 minutes of beat-driven bangers with very few zeitgeist-capturing gimmicks to be found.

title: Modern Rituals
description: NY-via-California band exhibits a bicoastal sound that keeps them from being beholden to any single style.

title: Hood Pass Intact EP
description: This four-song EP from the prolific producer features re-worked cuts from the Toeachizown series along with new material.

title: Jewelry Selection
description: After a relatively sedate, lyrics-focused tape, Gucci Mane returns to the more musically dynamic, multi-dimensional approach of his 2007-09 work.

title: Familial
description: Radiohead drummer goes acoustic guitar-strumming singer-songwriter, putting his sticks down to pen Nick Drakesian songs about family.

title: Ullakkopalo
description: Finland's Fonal, a leading label in the psych and freak folk worlds, releases another dense tapestry of electro-acoustic sound from Jan Anderzén.

title: The Metallic Year
description: UK guitarist/tape manipulator Alexander Tucker and New Zealandic cohort Daniel Beban explore intersection of drone and doom metal for Thrill Jockey.

title: The Waves
description: This Bay Area duo that recalls Glasser and Wild Nothing makes an assured Mexican Summer debut.

title: Jesu: Pale Sketches Demixed
description: Justin Broadrick's latest EP finds him adopting the Pale Sketcher alias in order to remix his Jesu odds-and-ends compilation of the same name.

title: Surfing the Void
description: Nu-rave avatars follow an oddly overhyped and underrated LP by shaving some pop and art leanings and coming across as a fully formed rock band.

title: Disko
description: Rune Grammofon and Smalltown Supersound associate Kim Hiorthøy enlists a full band for a project that recalls his previous work.

title: Barbara
description: Popular in the UK and basically ignored at home, We Are Scientists have now enlisted a Razorlight member for their latest LP of lukewarm indie-dance.

title: Total 11
description: Kompakt's flagship compilation series returns with new tracks from the Field, Jürgen Paape, Superpitcher, and Michael Mayer.

title: 1,000 Grams Vol. 1
description: Coke-rap star's latest high-profile mixtape is characterized primarily by a potential feud brewing between himself and Rick Ross.

title: The Electronic Anthology Project
description: Built to Spill have a little fun with their own catalog by covering their own songs in the style of 1980s synth-pop. Seriously!

title: Scott Pilgrim vs. the World OST
description: The big-screen adaptation of the popular comic enlists Beck, Broken Social Scene, and Metric to stand in for its fictionalized bands.

title: Without Why
description: Former Pipettes singer trades girl-group conceits for lovelorn and wistful indie pop, with help from backing band the Distractions.

title: That Mystic EP
description: Rave throwback producer branches out to explore dubstep and R&B on his new EP and keeps up his perfect hit-to-miss ratio in the process.

title: The Orchard
description: Pals from Vampire Weekend's Class of '08, the similarly preppy band returns with a sophomore album that pushes their stylistic range at the cost of hooks.

title: Thank You For Your Love EP
description: Antony Hegarty returns with a teaser from his new album, covers of Bob Dylan and John Lennon, and two other originals.

title: Keraaminen Pää
description: The Finnish psych-folk singer embraces electronics-- icy synth tones, crunchy samples, and abstract gurgles-- on her latest record.

title: Gambling With God
description: Toronto band's sound is a throwback to the alt-rock 1990s and they get in just enough catchy riffs to pull it off.

title: DJ /rupture Presents CIAfrica
description: DJ /rupture handpicks and mixes the best tracks from Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, rap group CIAfrica.

title: Year One / Extra Width/Mo' Width [Deluxe]
description: The JSBX reissues continue with a collection of early recordings and an expanded version of 1993's Extra Width.

title: Special Moves
description: Mogwai's first live package-- a concert recording and DVD companion, Burning, with a different tracklist-- finds them in typically outstanding form.

title: Proximity One: Narrative of a City
description: More of a scene overview than a label one, this collection of L.A. instrumental hip-hop takes cues from g-Funk, dubstep, and Oxnard breaks.

title: Cloak and Cipher
description: Loosely related to Broken Social Scene, this Montreal band traffics in the same brand of anthemic, proficient indie rock. Arcade Fire's Jeremy Gara guests.

title: All We Grow
description: Bon Iver's classically trained percussionist crafts a debut solo record of austere folk and lush sonics.

title: My Name Is Hannibal
description: The debut album from the promising Chicago-based comic gets over on his conversational tone and bizarre observations.

title: Strange Weather, Isn't It?
description: Warp's dance-rock lifers return to basics after the at-times ham-handed, at-times highly effective rockism of 2007's Myth Takes.

title: Royal Toast
description: Combining elements of post-bop jazz and chamber music, the Claudia Quintet have found a unique and engaging hybrid.

title: Consolamentum
description: Former Oceansize guitarist works with broken-backed dirges for guitar, piano, and tape that skulk between ambient, noise, and pure sound art.

title: Sand & Lines: The Georgia Theatre Sessions, May 20th–24th 2008
description: Scaling back instead of simply piling on, this Georgia chamber-pop band's live document is their most well-crafted record yet.

title: Knoxville
description: All-star composer/producer Christian Fennesz issues another of his low-key collaborative LPs, here with guitarist David Daniell and drummer Tony Buck.

title: The Week Never Starts Round Here [Deluxe Edition] / Philophobia [Deluxe Edition]
description: The unparalleled Scottish band has its first two LPs reissued and expanded, with Peel Sessions and live performances added.

title: Catching a Tiger
description: L.A.-based folkie's debut sees her collaborating with producers of Tom Waits, Modest Mouse, and Band of Horses fame.

title: House of Tongues
description: Well traveled and practiced indie pop veterans, including former Luna guitarist Sean Eden, share a keen sense of pop history and a kitchen-sink aesthetic.

title: The Budos Band III
description: The dependable retro funk outft compacts Afrobeat, Latin soul, and James Brown into brief but highly danceable instrumentals.

title: More About Nothing
description: After his major-label flop, Wale returns to the scene of his greatest mixtape success with another "Seinfeld"-referencing collection.

title: Hawk
description: Three albums in, this pairing of ex-Belle and Sebastian and Screaming Trees members still feels unlikely, and still sounds quite good.

title: Sad Sour Future
description: Iowa indie rock band harkens back to the kind of hooky, brainy indie traditions of Superchunk, Pavement, and Beulah.

title: Kaleide
description: UK band with a taste for North American indie rock enlists producer John Goodmanson (Sleater-Kinney, Death Cab For Cutie) for their second record.

title: Church With No Magic
description: Formerly known as Pivot, this Warp act also pares back the atmospherics and drift that often blighted their records.

title: Melvins/Isis
description: Isis' final recordings turn out to be contributions to a split 12" with the resurgent Melvins.

title: Shangaan Electro: New Wave Dance Music From South Africa
description: An almost wholly unrooted and original dance music, this emerging South African sound marries hyper-quick, cheap electronics with soulful vocals.

title: Boy EP
description: Indie YouTube covers star aims to branch out with his own material on this, his first Frenchkiss EP.

artist: Oren Ambarchi | Keiji Haino | Jim O'Rourke
title: Tima Formosa
description: Three of the world's best sound artists combine for an absorbing record of electroacoustic improvisation.

title: Natural Selections
description: Longtime L.A. rock vet (Savage Republic, Medicine) explores his long-loved themes of juxtaposition and electronic exploration on this solo record.

title: Am I Real? EP
description: Latest from Ramona Gonzalez, a buzzed-about, L.A.-based musician who records ephemeral, homemade dreambeat music.

title: All's Well That Ends EP
description: Welsh indie band reward their sizable cult with a digital-and-vinyl release that pulls together alternate versions of Romance Is Boring tracks.

title: Berghain 04
description: Famed Berlin club continues its mix series with a set constructed by one of its residents, and one of the tech-house/minimal axis' leading lights.

title: Atalanta (Acts of God) Volume II
description: A 20th century composer who should be namechecked along with Terry Riley and Steve Reich, Robert Ashley often turns the marginal and mundane into magic.

title: High and Dry
description: The versatile and prolific drummer crafts a raucous sound akin to a free jazz take on math-tinted groups like Breadwinner or Shellac.

title: All Is Falling
description: Latest from the UK twentysomething, already a renowned figure in the space between folk, classical music, minimalism, and experimentalism.

title: Black City
description: The versatile, prolific techno and pop artist crafts a dark, funk-driven record that may be the best of his career.

title: The Cradle
description: Following the departure of three band members, the Oxford, Miss., band re-groups and tries to make a new start.

title: House With a Curse
description: For their third full-length, Coliseum move from metal-oriented Relapse to Temporary Residence and add guests including Will Oldham.

artist: Someone Still Loves You Boris Yeltsin
title: Let It Sway
description: Blog-rock survivors continue to knock out trend-resistent power-pop. Death Cab for Cutie's Chris Walla produces.

title: See Birds EP
description: An impressive early step from Alec Koone, a 19-year-old college kid crafting slow, gloomy tracks all from samples located online.

title: Root For Ruin
description: The veteran band takes a victory lap on its latest record, which walks the same path as 2007's relatively polished Let's Stay Friends.

title: Failing Lights
description: Mike Connelly of Wolf Eyes and Hair Police trades harsh noise for tense and shadowy atmosphere.

title: Sugar
description: Athens band tours with Dinosaur Jr. and the Meat Puppets, and sounds like it on their latest throwback 90s alt-rock record.

title: Light Chasers
description: The eighth proper album from the environmentally-minded indie rock band from Minnesota showcases them in quirky and eccentric form.

title: Are You My Mother?
description: Debut solo effort by Neko Case's New Pornographers substitute Kathryn Calder puts the spotlight squarely on her singing, often at the expense of songwriting.

title: Trill O.G.
description: Former UGK great continues to plug away as a solo artist after the untimely death of his musical partner, Pimp C.

title: Full House Head
description: The "boogie" is ok; the "endless" is a serious problem.

title: Laugh Tracks
description: The Fresh & Onlys singer extends his prolific songwriting run of fuzz-psych earworms into solo album territory.

title: Outside the Box
description: The dubstep originator experiments further with pop form, adding collaborations with artists like Murs and La Roux to bass-heavy instrumentals.

title: Transit Transit
description: Despite fans ranging from Trent Reznor to Thom Yorke to the Coen Brothers, this L.A. neo-shoegaze band never crossed over. Six years later, they finally return.

title: All the Waters of the Earth Turn to Blood
description: Though they work in the field of doom metal, this Rhode Island-based duo add gospel choirs, harsh noise, and industrial rock to their terrific second LP.

title: Beachcomber's Windowsill
description: Taking cues from the Kinks and Belle and Sebastian, this Oxford band craft delicately arranged, pastoral guitar pop.

title: Four More Years EP
description: With a tone palette as rich as anyone working in chillwave, this bedroom producer crafts a promising debut.

title: Alive As You Are
description: After two LPs of neo-shoegaze, Darker My Love dump the delay pedals and noise for acoustic guitars and harmony vocals.

title: Seu Jorge & Almaz
description: Like The Life Aquatic David Bowie tie-in, this project began a soundtrack collaboration, but Jorge asked the band to assist on an entire covers album.

title: Maximum Balloon
description: TV on the Radio's Dave Sitek opens his address book and recruits bandmates Kyp Malone and Tunde Adebimpe, Karen O, David Byrne, and more for this project.

title: Tiger Flower Circle Sun
description: Through self-designed software, Willits is more a manipulator of guitar tones than a guitarist, and his latest is an ode to tones from Tortoise to Fripp.

title: Shannon Stephens
description: The debut LP from the folky singer-songwriter who made her start with Sufjan Stevens in the 1990s band Marzuki is given a re-release.

title: Gold on Gold
description: Recalling Junior Boys, Hot Chip, or Cut Copy, this is as satisfying a take on indie-dance as you'll hear until one of those pacesetters drops a new album.

title: #Zero With a Bullet
description: Veteran singer-songwriter and key influence on Conor Oberst continues to have success elude him, a topic he frequents on his new record.

title: Rated R [Deluxe Edition]
description: QOTSA's second full-length, originally released in 2000 and now available in a deluxe reissue, stands as one of the last great modern hard rock records.

title: Puutarhatrilogia
description: Finnish dance-pop band can evoke Stereolab or Lykke Li but mostly work with oblique techno references within the framework of numerous sounds.

title: Drifts
description: The tables turn on this prolific remixer, as his Continent LP is re-worked by a roster of fellow Canadians, including Junior Boys.

title: Jungle Music: Mixed With Love: Essential & Unreleased Remixes 1976-1986
description: This 2xCD set collects remixes from the disco producer (including tracks by sometime collaborator Arthur Russell) that helped to define the 12" dance single.

title: Hidden Lands
description: The appealing second album from this Colorado group is a pastoral in the extreme, with drifting textures, whispered vocals, and lyrics about the forest.

title: Str8 Killa EP
description: After two urgent mixtapes, the Indiana rapper releases his first-ever commercially available record, an EP that finds him more comfortable than ferocious.

title: Fortress
description: No-frills indie-pop band incorporates outside elements into its sound, but their style-appropriation can come off as posturing. Neon Indian and Chris Chu guest.

title: Where the Messengers Meet
description: Punishingly monochromatic and near-depressive, the record sounds like someone sitting and dutifully picking at his meal.

title: On the Ones and Threes
description: The quintessential 90s indie rock band returns with its first LP in a decade.

title: The Singles, Vol. 9: 1973-1975
description: Some of the era's best funk singles are greeted here by mercifully cancelled releases on a comp characterized as much by interesting failures as hits.

title: Jane Birkin et Serge Gainsbourg
description: Featuring the scandalous hit "Je T'aime", this 1969 LP from the brilliantly original singer-songwriter has aged beautifully.

title: Obadiah
description: Be Good Tanyas singer strikes out on her own, releasing a quietly ambitious record that tiptoes between soft jazz, smoky soul, and austere country.

title: Mind Altar EP
description: Pairing two EPs originally released on the Deastro blog, the latest from the electro-pop project heads in a noisier and more psychedelic direction.

title: Spur of the Moments
description: Drag City unearths material from this lost 1960s combo, whose eclectic work highlights how quickly and rapidly rock was growing at the time.

title: Teflon Don
description: His first two records were lousy, but Rick Ross has found his niche by presiding over a luxurious rap fantasy out of step with the current moment.

title: Weareallgoingtoburninhell-megamixxx3
description: Indie hip-hop great strings together experimental asides, self-contained pieces, and pre-established material into an instrumnetal sonic arc.

title: Dealing in Antiques
description: This odds-and-ends compilation from the Finnish indie-pop band contains demos, B-sides, covers, and a couple of new tracks.

title: Let Me Shine for You
description: Ascendant outré-dance imprint Tri Angle pays tribute to jailed starlet Lindsay Lohan with a mixtape covering her pop songs (remember those?).

title: K-X-P
description: Annie producer and cohort Timo Kaukolampi heads a trio making delightfully dark disco.

title: Candle to Your Eyes
description: This shape-shifting band is at its best when synthesizing art-rock and R&B, but they're confident and thoughtful at crafting other sounds as well.

title: The Suburbs
description: On their third LP, Arcade Fire prove they can make grand statements without sounding like they're carrying the weight of the world.

title: The Low Hanging Fruit
description: Singer-songwriter Jesse Rifkin draws inspiration from religion, mixing tales inspired by the Bible with Qawwali drones and Hindu chants.

title: Cloud Seed
description: Aggressive and haunting, Jamie Vex'd makes post-dubstep dance music that could soundtrack dystopian Hollywood sci-fi films.

title: That's How We Burn
description: This indie rock grab bag makes for an impressive Sub Pop debut for this veteran Milwaukee band.

title: Moses on a Snail
description: After a recent hot streak, the GBV singer's latest is dusky, dour, and a bit of a retread.

title: Pilot Talk
description: The New Orleans rapper's long and strange career path leads to this lush, languid, and inviting LP.

title: Again and Again
description: Following the "Drugs in My Body" single, synth-pop band Thieves Like Us issues their sophomore LP.

title: Hunting My Dress
description: Rising folkie moves from California to Manchester and blends British pastoral folk into her American blues and roots music. Elbow's Guy Garvey guests.

title: Constellations
description: Bedroom indie-pop outfit returns with more studio polish but a lyrical plainness that sadly keeps the band from matching their peers just yet.

title: Neu! Box Set
description: This vinyl-only set contains the influential German band's three original albums plus some rarities, including sessions from an aborted 1986 reunion.

title: Angel Echoes Remix
description: Bundling all the recent remixes of Four Tet into one digital package, this set features work from Caribou, Joy Orbison, Floating Points, and Mosca.

title: Come Hell or High Water
description: The large trans-continental project led by Greg Jarvis returns with an evocative album that balances stately chamber pop with noise and drone.

title: Pink Graffiti
description: Fargo, N.D., band all but sends mash notes to the 90s rosters of K, Merge, or Matador throughout this throwback indie rock record.

title: The Runaway
description: Third album from the UK indie band finds them experimenting with a wider array of sounds to mixed effect.

title: Villa Manifesto
description: The Detroit crew returns with their first full-length since the deaths of producer J Dilla and founding member Baatin.

artist: Tony Da Gatorra vs. Gruff Rhys
title: The Terror of Cosmic Loneliness
description: Super Furry Animals singer teams with a Brazilian VCR repairman/peace activist to craft a record on a homemade synthesizer/drum-machine.

title: Fields Within Fields
description: Like Robedoor, Heavy Winged prove long-form jams on traditional rock instruments can still produce forward-looking drone.

title: XXX
description: Discovered in his teens by Warp, Edgar grows up, moves to !K7, and seems to like strip clubs (and strip-club music).

title: Dual Identity
description: Two of the finest saxophonists going collaborate on this album that serves as a great entry point into contemporary progressive jazz.

title: United Nations of Sound
description: Richard Ashcroft responds to the failure of the Verve v. 3.0  with an album of excitable, populist electro-soul.

title: Crazy For You
description: California's Bethany Cosentino delivers on the promise of her noisy early singles with a richer-sounding album that highlights the power of her voice.

title: Blue Giant
description: The principals from Portland's Viva Voce team with members of Golden Bears, Swords, and the Decemberists for a more rustic take on indie pop.

title: Pestilence & Joy
description: One of the more intriguing and unclassifiable acts in experimental music releases a consistent record that deals in a kind of symphonic minimalism.

title: Somewhere on the Golden Coast
description: Often called the Californian Hold Steady, HCP combine the easy guitar-pop of Weezer and Pavement with detail-rich lyrical acumen.

title: On Patrol
description: Sun Araw's muggy psych-trance is given space and time to stretch out, simmer, deepen, and the results move from mesmeric to narcotic.

title: Mines
description: On their third pop album, Menomena dial back a bit, focusing as much on conventional songwriting as jamming, looping, and editing, to very good effect.

title: Contoured Heat
description: Chicago pysch-rock band bows out with an album that pairs their raw, visceral music with lengthy instrumental excursions.

title: Rural Route No. 2
description: Rising drone artist reminiscent of William Basinski and Stars of the Lid finds new shades of emotion and intensity in his overcast compositions.

title: Record: The Best of Zero 7
description: Downtempo kingpins round up their hits and somehow have gathered remixes from Dilla, Joker, Justus Kohncke, Fred Falke, and others for a Disc Two.

title: Welcome Home/Diggin' the Universe
description: Woodsist offer ramshackle rock plus forays into twee and pop-punk on this label comp. Woods, Fresh & Onlys, Ducktails, and Skygreen Leopards appear.

title: Crooks & Lovers
description: After two stellar EPs, this post-dubstep duo again turns club and R&B influences into something, like Boards of Canada or James Blake, best enjoyed alone.

title: The Long Shadow of the Paper Tiger
description: Chicago band enlists guest musicians, trading the peaks and valleys of its previous albums for overall danceable consistency.

title: Butterfly House
description: Working with producer John Leckie, the Merseyside band soldiers on after the departure of guitarist Bill Ryder-Jones.

title: Beyond the Valley of Ultrahits
description: Best known for minimalism, noise, and avant-folk, Richard Youngs created this CD-R of "proper pop" music on a dare. Jagjaguwar now re-releases it.

title: Twin-Hand Movement
description: Jana Hunter teams up with a new band that provides her with unhinged, dreamy rock more often in the service of atmosphere than her voice.

title: Archives 2003-2006
description: Grizzly Bear's Daniel Rossen issues a collection of rich, revelatory material recorded between his other group's two albums.

title: Art School Girls
description: It's like ironic hipster rap and blog-house never ended.

title: Interpretations: The British Rock Songbook
description: The soul veteran puts her own spin on songs by the Who, the Beatles, Led Zeppelin, and more.

title: Made the Harbor
description: Vermont trio builds on its blog buzz with an album of old-timey music highlighted by the group's lovely bell-toned voices.

title: Infra
description: The latest from the electro-acoustic composer with a flair for slow, aching beauty was originally commissioned for a multimedia performance piece.

title: Lazers Never Die EP
description: Diplo and Switch supplement their 2009 dancehall record with this EP, a summertime's worth of originals and reinterpretations. Thom Yorke and M.I.A. appear.

title: Flaws
description: The UK band goes from teenage post-punk acolytes to Nick Drake- and John Martyn-loving folkies in one move.

title: Serotonin
description: On their third LP, and first for Rough Trade, the UK former prog-pop band now essentially fully strips the "prog" from its music.

title: Libraries
description: After a lo-fi triumph, Stuart McLamb records his second LP in a proper studio, supplementing his melodic gifts with reverb and colorful arrangements.

title: Kicking at the Perfumed Air
description: The late ex-Wilco man has his mostly completed record of stalwart, sad, often quite affecting pop-rock songs posthumously released.

title: The Way Out
description: The Books' fourth album and first full-length in five years finds their knack for finding strange and wondrous samples intact.

title: Apparitions
description: Chicago indie rock band serves up big choruses and post-Arcade Fire grandeur on its first LP.

title: Man Forever
description: Oneida drummer Kid Millions enlists members of Yeah Yeah Yeahs and Sightings for his first solo record.

title: Of Seismic Consequence
description: Chicago metal band reaches for, and often locates, something mysterious and elemental on virtually every track of its new LP.

title: Learning
description: A strikingly intimate and affecting debut full-length from Seattle singer-songwriter Mike Hadreas.

title: Piratas de Sudamérica, Vol. 1
description: Following his successful LP Alegranza!, the Spanish producer returns with an EP containing re-workings of pre-rock songs from Latin America.

title: Unheard Ofs & Forgotten Abouts
description: This evangelical for old-timey music crafts a mixtape of global folk songs-- Scotland to Nairobi; China to Appalachia-- from his record collection.

title: Fabulous Diamonds II
description: The Aussie duo stretches their murky and zonked-out stoner vibes even further on their latest album, which drafts elements of dub, repetition, and minimalism.

title: LA Vampires Meets Zola Jesus EP
description: This collaboration between Zola Jesus leader Nika Rosa Danilova and Pocahaunted member Amanda Brown is the polar opposite of polished.

title: Night Light
description: Delicate synth-pop act gets remixed by Neon Indian, Jens Lekman, and the Dirty Projectors' Angel Deradoorian.

title: Move of Ten
description: Their second LP in a matter of months, Move of Ten is a beat-driven complement to Oversteps' dubstep-nodding ambiance.

title: Wildwood
description: North Carolina Americana band continues to impress, colliding their bluegrass more than ever with other strains of country music.

title: Scared
description: The overcast moods and broken tempos of this dance vet are informed by Villalobos and Pantha, but also come off like kin to the xx and witch house.

title: They'll Only Miss You When You Leave: Songs 1996 - 2003
description: Former beloved local Seattle band-- a stepping stone for virtually every early Band of Horses member-- has its best moments collected and released.

title: Disconnect From Desire
description: This collaboration between Secret Machines and On! Air! Library! members returns, again with shoegaze motifs married to assertive pop melodies.

title: Fables of the Reconstruction [Deluxe Edition]
description: R.E.M.'s overlooked and transitional third album from 1985, produced by Joe Boyd, receives the deluxe reissue treatment.

title: Fuck Winter / Regolith Vol. 1 / Patient Sounds Sampler V. 1
description: Three comps from under-the-radar labels issuing cassettes and vinyl in limited quanities highlight a range of strange sounds from all over.

title: New Sounds
description: In 1974, Bob Desper released his only album-- limited to a 500-copy pressing on a local Christian imprint. Discourage reissues it now.

title: Part II: The New December
description: Liars cohorts and tourmates locate that band's sense of rhythmically obtuse and dense appeal yet often make almost whimsical pop out of it.

title: Admiral Fell Promises
description: Working alone with just a nylon-string guitar, Mark Kozelek takes a new tack under his Sun Kil Moon alias.

title: Love King
description: On his third album, the influential R&B singer/songwriter comes into his own as an album artist, getting over on his impeccable sense of craft.

title: No Great Lost: Songs, 1979-1985
description: Following recent reissues of Pylon and Method Actors, another great lost Southern new wave artist has his work unearthed.

artist: David Karsten Daniels, Fight the Big Bull
title: I Mean to Live Here Still
description: Pairing with the Virgina jazz ensemble Fight the Big Bull, the singer-songwriter has found an intriguing new setting for his somber tales.

title: Mystery Tape EP
description: Denver-based instrumental psych band has a real feel for dark mood and atmosphere on their latest.

title: Can't See My Own Face - The Eternal Love 2
description: Promising newcomer Tom Krell marries the intimacy of cheaply recorded bedroom pop with lush melodicism and a tinge of R&B.

title: / \ / \ / \ Y / \
description: After two game-changing LPs and the surprise 2008 success of "Paper Planes", M.I.A. returns with an album heavy on noise and light on memorable songs.

title: Palenque Palenque: Champeta Criolla & Afro Roots in Colombia 1975-91
description: This engaging comp from Britain's Soundway documents the evolution of a unique scene that grew from a mix of Colombian and West African pop.

title: En Fin Tid
description: The Norwegian producer with an ear for bubbly summer dance music builds on that sound and experiments with some new moods.

title: Spirituals
description: Mixing recordings of free jazz ensembles with electronics, Portland's Tyler Tadlock mines the tension between efficient technology and messy humanity.

title: The Story of an Artist
description: This 6xCD box collects Johnston's earliest releases, including Songs of Pain and two volumes of The Lost Recordings*.*

title: Cerulean
description: L.A. producer Will Wiesenfeld incorporates the woozy pitch-shifted samples of local beatmaking peers into surprisingly affecting songs.

title: Privilege
description: The Cologne-based producer crafts a minimal techno world so repetitive and stark it begins to feel like ambient.

artist: Jack Rose, D. Charles Speer and the Helix
title: Ragged and Right
description: This EP finds the late guitarist working with No-Neck Blues Band's Dave Shuford on a set of loose, energetic covers of tunes by Link Wray and Merle Haggard.

title: Treasure State
description: The New York-based new music ensemble teams with the sample maestros on a highly tactile album that draws inspiration from the American landscape.

title: Funstyle
description: The veteran singer-songwriter surprise releases a new album, and it's a baffling mix of wacky beat-driven tunes and more conventional songs.

title: Flesh Tone
description: Focusing more than ever on dance music with an album the flows like a DJ set, the left-field R&B diva has made her most consistent record in years.

title: Taste the Sin
description: Savannah's Black Tusk mix metal and hardcore in a way sometimes reminiscent of Weedeater or Baroness but with an approach all their own.

title: Bonjour
description: The Algerian-born bandleader with a knack for mixing rock, reggae, techno, raï, and Arab pop tries a new producer and a dialed-down sound.

title: Chapter Ahead Being Fake EP
description: This split 10" shines due to Boris' contribution, which finds them mixing black metal and shoegaze into a sound that resists categorization.

title: Touched EP
description: On their debut EP, this promising Brooklyn duo offers up a homemade take on Lindstrøm-style space-disco.

title: Mount Wittenberg Orca
description: Dirty Projectors and Björk self-release a folksy, dressed-down, and appealing song cycle for charity that was written and assembled quickly.

title: Roachy Balboa
description: The young Bay Area rapper returns with his second album that nicely balances acrobatic rap style, storytelling, and humor.

title: Fantision
description: Prolific producer who has released almost 50 albums in the last 10 years doesn't rush his electro-acoustic soundscapes here.

title: Reservoir Songs II EP
description: Eric Bachmann releases his second covers EP, here tackling the Kinks, Merle Haggard, Waylon Jennings, Glen Campbell, and Thin Lizzy.

title: Immer 3
description: The Kompakt proprietor releases the third volume in his flagship mix series, featuring tracks by Cortney Tidwell, Massive Attack, and more.

title: Sir Lucious Left Foot: The Son of Chico Dusty
description: After years of label drama and leaked tracks that hinted at something great, the OutKast MC exceeds high expectations on his proper solo debut.

title: Lustre
description: Following his 2007 best-of, the British singer-songwriter returns with an album that finds him trying his hand at some new styles.

title: O.M.G.!
description: Dubstep producer does crossover on his debut album for Mad Decent, including collaborations with Amber Coffman and Gucci Mane.

title: Shut Up, Dude
description: Following on the success of the novelty song "Combination Pizza Hut and Taco Bell", Das Racist return with a smart, funny, and engaging mixtape.

title: Mr. Zone 6
description: After another stint in prison, the rapper is back on the mixtape circuit and he hasn't lost a step.

title: Fabric 52
description: The Scottish duo's club night of the same name is no more, but their partnership continues with this mix, among the most techno-heavy of their career.

title: Listen for the Clues
description: Drew Patrizi of What Made Milwaukee Famous returns with a new band with some seriously maximalist orchestral pop tendencies.

title: Addicts: Black Meddle, Part II
description: Extending beyond black metal to incorporate more synths and studio polish, Nachtmystium hold on to their crushing heaviness.

title: Base World, Pt. 1
description: This recent mixtape from the madly prolific YouTube rapper and member of the Bay Area crew the Pack gives a good overview of his off-the-dome style.

title: Night Work
description: Latest from the NYC band beloved across the pond shifts thematic focus from camp to overt sexuality and has a darker, more 1980s-informed sound.

title: King of the Beach
description: On this strong return after a tough year, Nathan Williams enlists Jay Reatard's backing band, polishes his sound, and embraces pop-punk clarity.

title: Fever
description: California band with a classic rock lean mixes British folk, stoner metal, and more into a swirling psych stew.

title: Swung From the Branches
description: This promising project from Toronto is indebted to the atmospheric dream pop of Atlas Sound but manages to carve out its own identity.

title: Earth vs. the Pipettes
description: Initially dreamed up as a modern girl group, the Pipettes took the exercise one step too far with a revolving-door membership and and an emphasis on conceit.

title: Square Shells EP
description: A between-albums EP from the psych-folk singer-songwriter continues his winning streak.

title: White Magic
description: Eric Berglund of the Tough Alliance steps out with a solo project that combines effortless electro-pop with lush orchestral pieces to dazzling effect.

title: We Are All One, in the Sun: A Tribute to Robbie Basho
description: American primitivist Robbie Basho is honored on this comp, with contributions from Espers' Meg Baird, Helena Espvall, and more.

title: Catoptric
description: After the disappointing Mirror Eye, the psych-droners return with a more expansive and engaging record cut around the same time.

title: Cosmology
description: British hardcore band enlists Diplo to craft their latest record of frenzy and fractal math rock.

title: Outlaster
description: The singer-songwriter embellishes her sparse, haunted folk sound with strings and woodwinds to superb effect.

title: Expo 86
description: On their third full-length, the indie supergroup led by Dan Boeckner and Spencer Krug sounds more unified as their songwriting voices bleed together.

title: Ramadanman EP
description: Breaking post-dubstep into detours such as glitchy, out-of-step rhythms and breakbeat hardcore creates an inviting record.

title: Perch Patchwork
description: Chicago band leaves the math-rock musicianship of previous releases behind, turning their quirks into something diverse and accessible.

title: Dansette Dansette
description: Indie pop vets whose work dates back to late-1980s twee-punk band Talulah Gosh return to find a revival of what they've been doing all along.

title: Peoples Potential Family Album
description: The Peoples Potential Unlimited imprint assembled this impressive collection of ultra-obscure early-1980s disco and funk.

title: Mare
description: Former Ridgewood, NJ-based singer/songwriter takes a major creative leap, refining his eclectic collage-pop aesthetic while retaining its emotional tug.

title: Chicago
description: The Berlin techno producer crafts a lengthy and austere album filled with psychedelic touches and odd bits of humor.

title: Jazeera Nights: Folk and Pop Sounds of Syria
description: Another excellent Sublime Frequencies collection of Omar Souleyman's work, these very modern electronic Arabic folk songs were recorded live.

title: Get Him to the Greek OST
description: Russell Brand's fictional band from the film sends up British rock, with songwriting help from Jarvis Cocker and the Libertines' Carl Barât.

title: Magic Bullets
description: San Francisco band draws from some obvious indie pop touchstones and manages a solid batch of convincing and affecting songs.

title: How I Got Over
description: The Roots' latest is also their leanest and most stylistically cohesive LP to date. Guests include Joanna Newsom, Dirty Projectors, Phonte, Blu, and Jim James.

title: All Creatures Will Make Merry
description: Edinburgh band combines tricky drumming, string swells, banjo solos, and rousing refrains on a compelling record with serious emotional pull.

title: Dagger Paths
description: On this impressive record, the UK producer's haunted sound evokes faded memories, ghostly auras, and dream states but also remains grounded and forceful.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: Hyperdub boss and dubstep star crafts a mix that includes usual suspects like Zomby and Ikonika, plus excursions into R&B and South African house.

title: Life Magazine Remixes EP
description: Not simply a quickie remix collection, Cold Cave get heavyweights Optimo, Arthur Baker, Pantha Du Prince, and Delorean to re-imagine their recent single.

title: The Boxer
description: Like the Strokes' Julian Casablancas before him, the Bloc Party singer explores electronic textures on his solo debut.

title: Against Love
description: In the midst of a 90s revival, this actual 90s band looks back and re-traces some of its earliest ambient-pop steps as a group.

title: Star Tiger Star Ariel
description: Undersung UK guitar pop act puts its head down and rocks out for the first time in its career.

title: Allo Darlin'
description: London-based foursome-- with ties to Hefner and Amelia Flecther-- issue the first excellent no-frills twee-pop record in a few years.

title: Time Flies
description: The absolutely enormous rock band reminds us that they got that way by simply communicating basic truths and basic melodies. Over and over and over again.

title: Disco2
description: The second album-length remix collection from HEALTH finds artists like Pictureplane, Crystal Castles, and CFCF re-working songs from Get Color.

title: Martian's Bloom
description: Ambitious indie rock band works in the same vein as the Bad Seeds, Tindersticks, or the Dirty Three.

title: Southern Gothic
description: Trying to be for Atlanta what Lou Reed or Brian Wilson are for NYC or California, this gothic rock band enlists Cee-Lo and Asher Roth on their debut LP.

title: The Threshingfloor
description: On their latest, Wovenhand mix traces of Indian, Celtic, and Middle Eastern folk into songs delivered with a preacher's fervor.

title: Splazsh
description: Nominally working under the umbrella of dubstep, this London producer has called his music "R&B concrète"-- a celebration of the abstract and the pop.

title: Cocainism, Vol. 2
description: More upbeat and loose than Cuban Linx II, this mixtape is simply a display of Raekwon's oft-overlooked, masterful technique.

title: The Offending Party
description: Former Grifters members recall that band's soulful lo-fi cacophony with a record that nicely dovetails with today's penchant for slop and chaos.

title: Sinister Devices
description: Promising Florida dream-pop outfit debuts with an album that finds the right balance between gossamer and grit.

title: About to Choke [Reissue]
description: The late singer-songwriter has his dark, death-obsessed major-label debut reissued.

title: Homeland
description: The Downtown NYC fixture's first album in a decade is an exquisite state-of-the-union dispatch from a darkly comic conscience.

title: The Five Ghosts
description: The Toronto indie pop veterans follow their theatrical, big-room work with a more muted, grayer record.

title: We Are Born
description: Sia migrates from understated R&B to energetic pop with a few refreshing results.

title: Oh EP
description: Marking his return as Oval after a 10-year absence, glitch pioneer Markus Popp issues a sharp, prickly, and finely detailed EP.

title: Bang Goes the Knighthood
description: Neil Hannon continues to quietly and effectively operate his own one-man niche, thanks to impeccable arrangements and tightrope-walking songwriting.

title: Go! Common Classics
description: Common already readies his second best-of record-- and unfortunately this one focuses on the nadir of his fruitful career.

title: Recovery
description: The rapper's next comeback LP, this is meant to trace Em's journey out of depression and drug addiction and back into the peak of his powers.

title: Two Agents
description: Now a duo, Signaldrift continue to meld IDM, krautrock, and post-rock with often schizophrenic results.

title: El Che
description: On the endlessly delayed follow-up to the overlooked Blue Collar, the Chicago hip-hop vet aims to put his career back on track.

title: Something For Everybody
description: Despite a shaky start, Devo's first LP in 20 years turns out to be more than a marketing and conceptual gesture.

title: Freiland Klaviermusik
description: The Kompakt mainstay-- who has recorded as Gas and Studio 1, and as part of Burger/Ink-- creates a strange, drum-less, almost monastic take on techno.

title: Further
description: Scrapping big-name guests and harnessing the live fury they've shown in recent years, the Chems make their best LP in more than a decade.

title: Homemade Extacy
description: This duo from Denton, Texas, make electro-infused noise that sometimes recalls HEALTH and Fuck Buttons.

title: Baby Style EP
description: Lefse band in debt to Panda Bear follows its excellent "Yellow Wings" single with this EP.

title: Chasing After Shadows... Living With the Ghosts
description: Hammock have a unique sound that lies between the deep ambient of Stars of the Lid and the anthemic rock of the Church.

title: American Slang
description: Rockers in the mold of Springsteen and Strummer are not just a band simply awash in nostalgia; their songs are about the very concept of nostalgia.

title: Lazerproof
description: Diplo and Switch take a risk, building a mixtape of modern rap, R&B, dancehall, and dubstep rhythms around the icy synth-pop of La Roux.

title: Melted
description: In the wake of Jay Reatard's passing, this San Fran garage-punker is one of rock's better razor-sharp throwback tunesmiths.

title: False Lights From the Land EP
description: The modern-day crooner highlights Truelove's Gutter epic "Remorse Code" on an EP that also features a pair of covers and a new song.

title: Tacklebox
description: For the third year in a row, the Chicago hip-hop duo celebrated Memorial Day by issuing a mixtape of retro-minded boom-bap.

title: Future Breeds
description: Hot Hot Heat return to an indie (Dangerbird) and make their best album since 2002's Make Up the Breakdown.

title: Thank Me Later
description: Inspired by rap and R&B in equal measure, Drake becomes the first of the post-Kanye, emo-y rappers to fully deliver on his debut LP.
Despite attempts to outlaw rock, Indonesia became a hotbed of pop and R&B as two new compilations from Sublime Frequencies prove.

title: Goodbye, Killer
description: After a four-year break, Joe Pernice's band returns, a little stripped down but still crafting pop nuggets in hock to the pop nuggets of the past.

title: Wild Smile
description: Brooklyn art-rockers build on the promise of their 2009 EP with a record of wheelhouse emotionally nourishing indie rock.

title: Fuck a Mixtape
description: On his latest mixtape, T.I. again proves how good a rapper he is-- perfectly in control of voice and flow and meter and cadence.

title: How to Destroy Angels
description: Trent Reznor returns, emphasizing plaintive downtempo ballads and ceding vocal duties to ex-West Indian Girl singer Mariqueen Maandig.

title: My Neighbor/My Creator
description: Bold new EP from the dream-folk band embraces negative space, hip-hop, and fingerpicking and somehow make them all work.

title: Walls
description: Banjo or Freakout's Alessio Natalizia and the guy behind the Allez-Allez podcast craft ambient-pop for Kompakt.

title: Becoming a Jackal
description: Irish folk-pop artist Conor O'Brien is getting a lot of NPR/mainstream attention for his emotionally nourishing music.

title: Champ
description: After their shaky 2008 full-length debut, Elephant Shell, Tokyo Police Club return with an album that recaptures some of their early promise.

title: Returnal
description: After the sprawling Rifts, one of drone's top new artists returns with a more focused yet more complex album.

title: ...And They Have Escaped the Weight of Darkness
description: The young Icelandic composer who has toured with Sigur Rós continues to develop and refine his string-and-piano-heavy sound.

title: Broken Hearts & Dirty Windows: Songs of John Prine
description: Chicago folk legend is honored by Conor Oberst, Bon Iver, Drive-By Truckers, Lambchop, and more.

title: Assume Crash Position
description: Five years since Congotronics introduced Konono to a broader international audience, the Congolese band releases its second studio album.

title: Rope and Summit EP
description: José González reforms his old band, nicely amplifying both his sound and the underlying rhythmic force in his solo material.

title: Disintegration [Deluxe Edition]
description: The Cure's 1989 album, released during what was arguably the band's peak period, receives a lavish reissue with some terrific bonus material

title: Living
description: The busy Virginia band return with another album of dense, rumbling blues-rock heavy on the instrumentals.

title: Topp Stemning På Lokal Bar
description: The fine debut from this Norwegian dance-pop band is a satisfying blend of the tropic and the cosmic.

title: Twistable, Turnable Man: A Musical Tribute to the Songs of Shel Silverstein
description: The famed children's author and songwriter is honored by My Morning Jacket, Andrew Bird, Frank Black, Kris Kristofferson, and more.

title: The Shape of Punk to Come: A Chimerical Bombination in 12 Bursts [Deluxe Edition]
description: The legendary LP from the Swedish hardcore band is given a deluxe reissue with a live album, video, and a documentary.

title: Does It Look Like I’m Here?
description: Prolific drone act follows last year’s What Happened with a zoned-out epic in the vein of ’70s space-rock giants Tangerine Dream and Ash Ra Tempel.

title: A Memory Is Better Than Nothing
description: The legendary Dan Treacy reconvenes his band for an album about hurting so badly that it's no longer possible to express the pain clearly.

title: The Jayhawks
description: The alt-country forebears finally have their almost mythical debut LP, nicknamed The Bunkhouse Album, released.

title: Into the Great Wide Yonder
description: Creator of a string of excellent singles, and remixes for the Knife and Röyksopp, the versatile techno producer unveils his latest LP.

title: The Drums
description: One of indie pop's most promising bands navigates the tension between its populist and insular tendencies on its sure-to-break-out LP.

title: LP4
description: Crafted from leftovers from the *LP3* sessions, Ratatat's latest is another take on their signature sound-- slick electro-pop heavily infused with hip-hop.

title: Heavy Ghost Appendices
description: Singer/songwriter collects covers, B-sides, remixes, do-overs, and other odds and ends from the past year. Bibio and Rafter are among the remixers.

title: Year of Panic
description: Brooklyn's Captured Tracks unveils an excellent record from a one-man German band in the spirit of Vivian Girls and caUSE co-MOTION!

title: Eccentric Breaks and Beats
description: Reissue label supreme Numero Group loved this bootleg collection of their samples (created by Shoes) so much they released it officially.

title: Pigeons
description: Luke Temple hires a band and, led by the outstanding "Collector" single, expands upon the promise of his debut as Here We Go Magic.

title: Before Today
description: After a decade of home recorded releases on smaller labels, Ariel Pink jumps to 4AD and makes the best record of his career.

title: The Black Dirt Sessions
description: Downcast roots rockers led by John McCauley return with album number three.

title: The Bride Screamed Murder
description: The grunge mainstays return with another record full of unexpected twists, turns, jokes, diversions, and ideas.

title: Dirty South Dance 2
description: The second volume of A-Trak's Southern hip-hop-meets European-electro-house mash-up series keeps the party going.

title: Tiger Bay / Finisterre
description: The latest deluxe reissues from St. Etienne come from a period when they hit on the right mix of pastoral folk and silvery electronics.

title: Destroyer of the Void
description: Portland band continues to explore the rugged late-60s roots-rock of Bob Dylan and the Band while also spreading out and displaying their eclectic nature.

title: See You on the Moon
description: Alt-country songstress finally takes full advantage of her gift for intimate, fragile songwriting on her latest LP.

title: The Champ Is Here 3
description: After a few lame actual records, Jadakiss responds with a surprisingly taut and triumphant mixtape.

title: Callin' All
description: The much-loved Liverpool band has its brief career stretched to four CDs by including singles, B-sides, demos, radio sessions, and live stuff.

title: Shadows
description: Veteran Scottish band shrug off their midlife crisis record, 2005's Man Made, returning to their classic Byrds-esque sound.

title: Gemini
description: Wild Nothing's achingly beautiful reflection of 80s dream-pop carves a tunnel from Ibiza's beaches to Manchester's rain-soaked fairgrounds.

title: Trash Kit
description: Introducing a UK female trio faithfiul to the small-scale, distortion-free punk of the Slits and the Raincoats.

title: Suite #420
description: Yup, that title is a weed reference, and rapper Devin the Dude is still the self-deprecating stoner everyman.

title: Be Yourself: A Tribute to Graham Nash's Songs for Beginners
description: Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold, Bonnie "Prince" Billy, Brendan Benson, and others pay tribute to Graham Nash's most personal solo album.

title: Long Distance
description: Parisian producer rolls together current trends-- broken beats, woozy aural effects, vintage funk and R&B-- into another great post-Dilla record.

title: Anidea
description: A pianist trained in jazz and classical, this post-dubstep producer is both methodical and highly melodic on his often stunning debut LP.

title: Dominant Curve
description: On their latest album, the new music ensemble interprets Debussy, John Cage, and others in unusual and compelling ways.

title: Me Oh My
description: First released on Gruff Rhys' label, the debut from this Cardiff singer/songwriter buries the pop hooks and lets her freak-folk flag fly.

title: Curtis Lane EP
description: Prodigious talent Pat Grossi displays an aptitude for the grandeur and grace of M83, OMD, and Animal Collective on this new EP.

title: Say It
description: After a promising debut, Warp's spazz-pop band sounds adrift and unmoored on their second LP.

title: Body Talk Pt. 1
description: Five years after the original issue of *Robyn*, the Swedish singer still has a knack for memorable pop gems.

title: Vespers
description: The debut LP by this instrumental post-rock outfit led by a former member of Antony and the Johnsons is an intriguing mix of drone and improv.

title: Heaps of Nothing
description: The Australian duo's latest makes a small move toward accessibility but they are as noisy and abrasive as ever.

title: Deathbed +4 EP
description: After a lengthy hibernation, Chicago's top garage-rock band returns with a five-song EP.

title: Trap or Die II
description: A-list rapper brings his bulldozing delivery and deft ear for huge, gothic tracks to his new mixtape.

title: Innerspeaker
description: These Australians have crafted an assured and accomplished album that integrates an array of psych rock references into a powerful whole.

title: Peter Wolf Crier
description: Minnesota duo channels the front-porch spirit of M. Ward on this collection of understated, ragged songs.

title: Well Done Europe
description: UK band's manic, meta-pop approach-- think Ray Davies or Jarvis Cocker-- doesn't so much plant tongue in cheek as pierce it right through.

title: K.R.I.T. Wuz Here
description: After being largely unknown throughout most of 2009, this Southern rapper is suddenly the next big blog-rap hope.

title: The Ghost Who Walks
description: Supermodel and wife of the White Stripes' Jack White aims to transcend those two facts on her debut LP of murder ballads and country-rock.

title: Bigger and Blackerer
description: Indie comedy's biggest star issues his first Sub Pop CD in six years.

title: A Thousand Voices EP
description: Chicago duo strike a productive bargain between raw primordial stomp and self-aware homage to 1990s alt-rock.

title: Three Kings
description: The psych-rockers' latest is a multimedia set including a feature-length film that cuts between performance footage and loopy dream sequences.

title: Saint Bartlett
description: The consistent indie rock journeyman makes one of the best records of his career with production assistance from Richard Swift.

title: Love and Its Opposite
description: Everything But the Girl singer continues to play the matriarch of love-lorn electronic music on her latest solo album. Ewan Pearson again produces.

title: Of Light / Shabazz Palaces
description: Ishmael Butler of Digable Planets has a very promising new solo project and he's out of the gate with two fine EPs.

title: Burners
description: Former drone band continues to explore song-oriented material-- here, krautrock, gothic sludge, and Stooges-like pysch-garage.

title: Holy Ground: NYC Live with the Wordless Music Orchestra
description: Ambitious post-rock band further embraces strings by teaming with Wordless Music Orchestra on this live album.

title: The Samps EP
description: Band that includes a sometime member of Ariel Pink's Haunted Graffiti crafts a short, sharp, and satisfying EP of bent pop.

title: Maniac Meat
description: The Black Moth Super Rainbow frontman returns with a more rough-edged and driving record that features two guest-spots from Beck.

title: Revolutions Per Minute
description: Talib Kweli and Hi-Tek reunite under their Reflection Eternal name and continue the good work they've displayed for more than a decade.

title: Spirit Youth
description: Wonderfully produced, this is the latest record from an indie pop band that shares members with Pains of Being Pure at Heart.

title: Splash
description: Jay moves from cinematic cityscapes and brittle indie toward the sloppy guitars and meaty chord progressions from MTV's "120 Minutes" heyday.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: Border Community head provides an alternative look at dance music, mostly avoiding the expected techno for a rich blend of current sounds.

title: Beach Fossils
description: Adopting the atmospherics of the Clientele and Real Esate, this Captured Tracks band manages to be both evocative and technically proficient.

title: CMYK EP
