description: The prodigious London electronic producer, still only 21, crafts intricate music that's both deeply retro and futuristic.

title: Subject to Shift
description: Jason Amm visits darker and more beat-driven territory on his fifth album, but brings elements of his upbeat analog synth sound with him.

title: Dust
description: Bpitch label head and scene linchpin redefines herself as a melancholy techno-pop songwriter with interests well outside her Berlin dance sphere.

title: Now I Got Worry / Controversial Negro
description: The beat-infused mutant blues of Now I Got Worry and the incendiary live document Controversial Negro are reissued with bonus tracks.

title: Distant Relatives
description: Hip-hop and reggae stars follow their excellent "As We Enter" single with a full LP. This summer's jam-band festgoers are going to love it.

title: Compass
description: Stylistically diverse though still identifiably his work, the new record from Jamie Lidell enlists a huge cast-- including Beck, Feist, and Grizzly Bear.

title: Kitsuné Maison 9
description: The latest comp from the French label includes contributions from Washed Out, Holy Ghost!, and Crookers.

title: Eyes & Nines
description: The Sacramento hardcore band captures the fury of their live show in a concise 18-minute blast of an album.

title: Dopeman Music
description: After a pair of bleak so-called retirement records, the Houston rap vet returns limber and energized on his new mixtape.

title: Total Life Forever
description: Eclectic UK band locates an emotional center amidst their mathematically arranged dance punk elements.

title: The ArchAndroid
description: The singer/songwriter's new album is stunningly ambitious, veering from R&B to rap, pastoral British folk, psych rock, disco, and more.

title: Pure Moods EP
description: Chicago band slows their kraut/noise blend down, sounding increasingly more like another set of Can lovers-- Stereolab.

title: Say God
description: Though ostensibly about Christianity, this 2xCD record from the former Lungfish leader is actually more about mind and spirit than scripture.

title: OJ Simpson
description: Cohesive, focused, and flat-out fun, Guilty Simpson and Madlib have crafted one of the best hip-hop records of the year.

title: Brothers
description: After working with Danger Mouse on their last full-length, Black Keys sound re-energized and playful on their loosest record in years.

title: Exile on Main St. [Deluxe Edition]
description: The 1972 classic is given a remaster and a deluxe reissue.

title: Alt Er Tabt
description: Danish group's latest is a dark, tense record full of spartan arrangements and songs built more around moody atmosphere than melodic hooks.

title: In and Out and Back Again
description: Amidst the slew of Velvets/Spacemen 3-indebted garage-drone bands around, Woven Bones continue to come closest to capturing the right mood.

title: Rhizomes
description: Brooklyn band recalls the experimental, krautock-inspired spirit of rhythmic post-punk, expertly synthesizing 15 years' worth of brooding, seismic rock.

title: False Flag
description: This out-rock supergroup featuring Sir Richard Bishop (Sun City Girls), Ben Chasny (Six Organs of Admittance), and Chris Corsano doesn't disappoint.

title: Infinite Arms
description: Jumping from Sub Pop to a major-- and featuring a revamped lineup around linchpin Ben Bridwell-- Band of Horses return for album No. 3

title: Wounded Lion
description: L.A. group's offbeat humor comes off as more honest and unguarded than their garage and lo-fi peers', but without the strong tunes to carry it.

title: Opal Island
description: Another in a recent wave of excellent drone artists-- Emeralds, Oneohtrix Point Never, and Black to Comm-- releases his latest LP.

title: The People's Record
description: Versatile Swedish indie pop band branches out to add dense polyrhythms to their Euro-indie aesthetic.

title: A Small Turn of Human Kindness
description: The Georgia sludge-merchants' latest has almost a black metal-style feeling of desolation to it-- slow and somber but still powerful.

title: This Is Happening
description: On LCD's third LP, James Murphy applies his knowledge of post-punk and studio craft to remake 70s art-rock in his own hyper-modern, self-aware image.

title: Night Train EP
description: Corny Coldplay copycats try to loosen up and project fun on their new EP. Feel-good MC K'naan guests, which actually makes sense.

title: New Slaves
description: The experimental Brooklyn band's latest is a satisfying descent into noisy chaos.

title: Blackjazz
description: The acclaimed Norwegian avant-rock band splits the difference between jazz and metal while still transcending their influences.

title: Latin
description: Having solidified their lineup, this Toronto band's third album is leaner, funkier, and more consistent than its predecessors.

title: Treats
description: The New York duo's debut full-length is a wildly fun noise-pop thrill-ride, delivering on the promise of last year's widely circulated demos.

title: Fabric 51
description: The loose, low-slung disco found on the Get Physical proprietor's Fabric mix isn't up-to-the-minute, but it still resonates.

title: Warm Slime
description: Prolific San Francisco psych band continues to make engagng bite-size garage-pop, like contemporaries Fresh & Onlys and Sic Alps.

title: The Adventures of Bobby Ray
description: Promising hip-hop star hits #1 with a compromised and creatively limp record. Thanks, major-label record industry.

title: No Singles
description: One of 2009's top new indie rock bands compiles two out-of-print EPs (2007's All Lies and 2008's Lullaby Death Jams).

title: Nothing Hurts
description: Male Bonding's full-length debut cleans up the sound of their ultra lo-fi early singles but the music is still fast, noisy, and full of hooks.

title: The Bells
description: Erased Tapes-- home to Peter Broderick and Ólafur Arnalds, among others-- issues this piano improvisation work from Berlin-based composer Frahm.

title: Totaled
description: Houston-based psych band experiments with more song-oriented forms on its latest.

title: Feast of the Hunter's Moon
description: Three-fifths of the Decemberists joined with a few friends to form a string band specializing in bucolic Americana, bluegrass, and cowboy songs.

title: Here's to Taking It Easy
description: After his Willie Nelson-inspired record, Matthew Houck stays firmly in the world of country music rather than the wilderness folk he'd previously crafted.

title: Grey Oceans
description: Hugely successful cult act continues to travel their own love/hate path, now for Sub Pop after years with Touch and Go.

title: Seedbed
description: Following quickly on a late 2009 12", Twin Stumps' latest is a more focused version of the band's grim, grimy, dread-filled post-hardcore.

title: Dettmann
description: The Berlin DJ and producer releases his first LP, with tracks ranging from crisp minimal techno to more dubby and spacious excursions.

title: Boys Outside
description: The Beta Band leader returns with his first record under his own name. Famed electronic craftsman Richard X produces.

title: Li(f)e
description: The verbose indie-rapper recruits Califone as a backing band and collaborates with Chris Walla, Jason Lytle, and the late Mark Linkous on his new LP.

title: Sea of Cowards
description: Jack White takes a stronger, more central role on the second Dead Weather album, sharing vocal duties almost evenly with Alison Mosshart.

title: Deep Tissue
description: Side project of Oneida's Kid Millions and Bobby Matador works a psych rock vein similar to their main band but ramps up the minimalist repetition.

title: Wake Up the Nation
description: The Jam and Style Council vet continues to display relevance and resilience on his latest solo record. Kevin Shields and ex-Jam cohort Bruce Foxton guest.

title: Where Did the Night Fall
description: Incredibly now going into its third decade, James Lavelle's resilient project reinvents itself as a workmanlike, electronically informed rock band.

title: At Echo Lake
description: Lo-fi heroes graduate to crafting country-inflected indie pop that's part Wowee Zowee and part Workingman's Dead.

title: High Violet
description: Returning with a slightly darker and more ornate sound, the National remain masters of widescreen, emotionally engaging rock.

title: Cut and Run
description: Brooklyn trio creates brutal prog à la Lightning Bolt or Orthrelm, but in consistently unexpected ways.

title: East General
description: Fucked Up's Ben Cook's side band issues its debut LP, which leans more to the "noise" end of "noise-pop" than contemporaries Sic Alps and Vivian Girls.

title: Liquid Love
description: The New York synth-pop duo have streamlined their sound, opting for lush, reassuring disco pulses reminiscent of late-era French house.

title: Honest Strings: A Tribute to the Life and Work of Jack Rose
description: This gargantuan, online-only recording is an incredible testament to the life and career of the recently deceased acoustic guitar master Jack Rose.

title: Your Future Our Clutter
description: Mark E. Smith's veteran band teams with indie heavyweight label Domino for this lean, brute-force rock record.

title: In Evening Air
description: Baltimore band mixes its own spin on new wave with highly charged drama courtesy of bellowing lead singer Samuel T. Herring.

title: Everyone Is a Ghost
description: Slowdive guitarist Christian Savill's long-running project returns and sounds freshly energized.

title: The Dogs Are Parading
description: Veteran producer and frequent Steven Soderbergh collaborator gathers his best work and his best remixes and obscurities.

title: Relayted
description: Folkie and electro supergroup-- including Bon Iver, Megafaun, members of the Rosebuds, and leader Ryan Olson-- tackle 80s R&B and Lite FM fare.

title: Cosmogramma
description: The L.A. producer's head music, which pulls from jazz, hip-hop, videogame sounds, IDM, and more, is more dense and rewarding than ever.

title: Victorian America
description: California singer-songwriter mixes folky tales of woe delivered in a stripped-down setting with stately songs backed by lush arrangements.

title: A Little Big
description: Berlin-based F.S. Blumm continues to create understated, austere tunes, often in collaboration. Here he teams with Swedish singer Ellinor Blixt.

title: Bedford Park
description: Underground hip-hop agitator Mike Ladd brings back his Infesticons project for the third part of a high-concept trilogy.

title: More!
description: The famed Berlin techno duo return to their producer-centric roots after a one-album detour into crossover techno-pop.

title: Together
description: The Canadian supergroup continues its shift from urgent, high-velocity rave-ups to mid-tempo tunes with an ornate, cinematic grandeur.

title: Cracked Love & Other Drugs
description: Steeped in Pac NW garage and punk, this wonderful Hardly Art band recalls everyone from the Wipers to the Fastbacks to Mudhoney.

title: Instant Coffee Baby / If You Leave It Alone
description: UK outfit's latest is being released in the U.S. alongside a 2008 LP, introducing a promising band that brings to mind the wit of Art Brut.

title: A Book of Songs for Anne Marie
description: Drag City's other harpist/pianist releases her intriguing second LP, which should earn her notice equal to that of her contemporaries.

title: Omni
description: The indie rock veterans return with a slicker, more radio-friendly album that takes some troubling lyrical turns.

title: Heaven Is Whenever
description: The Hold Steady attempt to balance widespread appeal while remaining embedded in the scenes they've been chronicling for half a decade.

title: MCMLXXX
description: Sharing two members with Mahjongg, this Chicago trio crafts a conceptual album that's actively more enamored of the audience than itself.

title: A Balloon Called Moaning
description: Welsh band's mini-LP, out last year in the UK and now being issued in the States, demonstrates a flair for guitar anthems.

title: The Fear Is Excruciating, But Therein Lies the Answer
description: With conviction and character to spare, the post-rock band crafts another record of soft/loud dynamics.

title: Option Paralysis
description: Blending technical metal and hardcore, the ambitious DEP try to avoid being pulled in too many stylistic directions.

title: Forgiveness Rock Record
description: With production assistance from John McEntire, the Canadian indie rock kingpins return, tighter and more polished than ever.

title: Barefoot Wanderer
description: Multi-cultral dance act makes its BPitch debut, constructing songs from dancehall riddims, glitch-hop, and experimental techno.

title: You Never Did Anything Wrong to Me
description: Former member of M83 picks up where the dark shoegaze of Dead Cities, Red Seas & Lost Ghosts left off.

title: A Mishmash of Changing Moods
description: Preternaturally gifted Dutch techno producer quickly follows his impressive debut with another decent LP that could have been a great EP.

title: Paul's Tomb: A Triumph
description: Carey Mercer and co. follow 2007's triumphant Tears of the Valedictorian with another record of ambitious, high-wire indie rock.

title: Sun Bronzed Greek Gods EP
description: Dom have only been a band for a few months, but they already display an innate understanding of the power of killer hooks-- their debut EP is packed with them.

title: Inter Arbiter
description: Up and coming baroque-pop singer/songwriter flashes plenty of promise on his debut LP. Zach Condon (Beirut) and Angel Deradoorian (Dirty Projectors) guest.

title: Words Are Stupid
description: This extremely limited vinyl-only release is also the first since the sudden death of Black Swans member Noel Sayre.

title: Écailles de Lune
description: French artist Neige finally fits all his component parts-- arching atmospherics, celestial melodies, suffocating roars-- into one dynamic metal record.

title: My Best Friend Is You
description: Following her Brit award-lauded UK #1 debut, the young singer-songwriter hasn't cracked up yet, but her sophomore album is thrillingly schizophrenic.

title: Crystal Castles
description: Crystal Castles return with a second self-titled album, embracing a more direct pop sound while retaining the sharp edges that made their debut so compelling.

title: Little More Lived In
description: Memphis-by-way-of-Athens band drifts away from orchestral pop and incorporates more rootsy Southern flourishes.

title: Trans-Continental Hustle
description: Gogol Bordello again tackle overcoming stigmas against immigrants and America's favoring of bland homogenization. Rick Rubin produces.

title: What We Lose in the Fire We Gain in the Flood
description: Former Georgie James member takes a creative leap forward, trading polite, unmemorable indie pop for full-blown country and soul.

title: Voluspa
description: After a string of promising singles, and even better remixes, the blissed-out electro-pop group make their full-length debut.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: DFA mainstay builds off the massive success of his 2008 single "Happy House" by crafting the latest entry in the venerable DJ-Kicks mix series.

title: Thistled Spring
description: The PacNW band continues to trade in Southern gothic images and themes, adding more complexity and confidence to their sound.

title: Animal Feelings
description: The versatile songwriter/producer streamlines his spazz-pop approach and incorporates influences from modern R&B.

title: Daughters
description: The final Daughters record finds the part of the group that went on to form Fang Island taking the lead, resulting in a more accessible version of the band.

title: Avi Buffalo
description: Like the xx raised on a diet of Built to Spill and the Shins, Avi Buffalo are confident, deft, and lust-obsessed teens making music beyond their years.

title: Nobody's Daughter
description: More than a decade after its last album, Courtney Love's band returns, and its leader attempts to prove she's more than a punchline.

title: III
description: The prolific, talented avant artist completes his "maximalist three-part suite" with its most diverse and engaging entry.

title: Guitar El Chark
description: One of the most legendary figures in Arabic music has the first official compilation of his work-- made in the mid-1970s-- released in the West.

title: Completely Removed
description: D.C. band formed from the ashes of Faraquet take a turn toward melodic songcraft, and the new look suits them.

title: Streetlights
description: After last year's lauded DJ Quik collab BlaQKout, the former Death Row mainstay finds a less fruitful partnership in Snoop producer Terrace Martin.

title: Clinging to a Scheme
description: The Swedish indie pop group Radio Dept.'s third and best LP expands their sound palette with songs that sparkle with a glowing, sun-soaked ambiance.

title: Clay Stones
description: This L.A.-based electro pop outfit's menacing synths and treated vocals owe more than a little to the Knife's gothic techno.

title: The Day the Turf Stood Still
description: Bay Area rapper is making noise with his winning reinvention of not only his own area's sound, but NYC's as well.

title: Secret Agent
description: The famed Afrobeat drummer, one of the pioneers of modern African music, makes his Nonesuch debut.

title: All Days are Nights: Songs for Lulu
description: The talented pop singer flirts with outright self-absorption on his latest record, a solo piano effort on which he bites off more than he can chew.

title: The Chaos
description: After a few records of unwelcome detours, the Futureheads mostly ditch the attempts at anthems and re-embrace some of their eccentricities.

title: The Endtables
description: Drag City unearths yet another worthwhile nugget from the post-punk vault, compiling the work of a group that sounded like an off-kilter Buzzcocks.

title: Lux
description: Chicago band that includes members of the Ponys and Boas brings its jagged rock mix from Touch and Go to Kranky.

title: Kush and Orange Juice
description: Without a major label deal or superstar allegiances, Wiz has turned himself into a hip-hop star by rapping about weed, girls, and smoking weed with girls.

title: Travellers in Space and Time
description: The E6 vets continue their welcome comeback with an album that pairs the usual ELO/Wings pop with dancier, looser tunes.

title: Subiza
description: The band whose Ayrton Senna EP helped define last summer's bright, beachy sound gains momentum with a beautifully surging, shimmering trance-pop LP.
Garage-rock fixture-- whether as BBQ Show, an Almighty Defender, or any of his other numerous projects-- releases a rare LP under his own name.

title: Ear Drums and Black Holes
description: On his second album, Starkey amplifies his gift for matching melodic complexity to forceful rhythms, every bass-heavy beat matched to a soulful melody.

title: Thing
description: The long-running electro-rock band seems over its dull patch from a few years ago, continuing the bump in quality evinced on 2007's Sex Change.

title: The Incredible String Band / The 5000 Spirits or the Layers of the Onion / The Hangman's Beautiful Daughter / Wee Tam and the Big Huge
description: The UK folk group's first four LPs are reissued.

title: I See the Sign
description: This thoroughly modern folk singer continues his stunning recreations of classic folk, with help from Ben Frost, Nico Muhly, and Beth Orton.

title: The Outsiders Are Back
description: Along with Sharon Jones, Lee Fields, and Charles Walker's Dynamites, here's another worthy entry in the 21st century soul revival.

title: Where Is the Truth
description: Former Seefeel man returns at a time when the woozily psychedelic synth-pop he helped pioneer is back in style.

title: Righteous Fists of Harmony
description: The prolific L.A.-based beatmaker releases a new EP for Flying Lotus' Brainfeeder imprint.

title: A Coming of Age
description: One of the most dynamic indie pop and pre-Beatles throwbacks around follows their excellent 2007 debut, The Great Unwanted.

title: Swim
description: After drawing from IDM, krautrock, and sunshine pop, Dan Snaith's project sets its sights on dark and intricate dance music, with dazzling results.

title: It All Falls Apart
description: This Gas-influenced ambient composer teams with an ex-Slowdive member and displays more personality on his latest Ghostly International LP.

title: WHB
description: London dance-punk band with a bit of online buzz offers up their full-length debut.

title: LeftBack
description: This is supposedly the final chapter for Phonte and Pooh's often divisive group, self-proclaimed keepers of the true hip-hop flame.

title: La La Land
description: Montreal band follows its underrated 2008 Laurel Canyon-like debut Parc Avenue with a more plugged-in, boisterous record.

title: City of Daughters / Thief / Streethawk: A Seduction
description: Remastered and reissued editions document Dan Bejar's early period, when he grew into the unique, beloved songwriter he is today.

title: Sucker
description: The eccentric Memphis singer-songwriter and former Cat Power collaborator again crafts narratives tinged with insight and humor.

title: Steal Your Face
description: San Fran trio crafts almost overwhelmingly intense music; stick with its guitar savagery, dub textures, and ricocheting rhythms-- you'll be glad you did.

title: Initiate
description: Wilco's Cline leads one of his may other projects through two discs-- one live, one studio-- of unpredictable electronic rock-ish jazz.

title: The Burrrprint (2)
description: Gucci's record released while incarcerated; despite the name-- the sequel to his best 2009 tape-- it's being treated as much as an LP as a mixtape.

title: Rough Travel for a Rare Thing
description: Bill Callahan's first live album, recorded in 2007, is a 2xLP/download set that captures one of this era's best singer-songwriters in amazing form.

title: Goodbye Falkenburg
description: Welsh band with a flair for music hall, psychedelia, glam rock, and post-punk craft a debut that is both ambitious and immediate.

title: Las Vênus Resort Palace Hotel
description: Brazilian singer pays tribute to the untrendy sounds of exotica, searching for beauty in the stylized approximations outsiders have made of her culture.

title: ForNever
description: After a lukewarmly received major-label record, Murs retreats into a more familiar headspace with frequent collaborator 9th Wonder.

title: City of Straw
description: New York trio continues to explore minimalism and white-hot noise, a fierce blend of seemingly disparate elements.

title: The Wild Hunt
description: Swedish troubadour Kristian Matsson returns as a more confident vocalist and a more nuanced and effective songwriter.

title: Wooden Blankets EP
description: Animal Collective acolytes continue to grow and escape the shadow of their influences on their new EP.

title: Contact, Love, Want, Have
description: A rare full length from Hyperdub, Ikonika's debut is an exciting extension of post-dubstep styles like wonky, funky, and chiptunes.

title: Prior to the Fire
description: After parting ways with RCA, the stoner-metal band regroups and releases their second album the way they intended people to hear it in the first place.

title: Prins Thomas
description: Space disco mainstay and frequent Lindstrøm partner records a solo record inspired by 1970s German music and avant-garde composition.

title: Raw Power [Legacy Edition] / Raw Power [Deluxe Edition]
description: One of the greatest rock albums ever is reissued again, this time in two versions; both useful but less than ideal or definitive.

title: Speculation
description: Berlin post-rockers play nice with a member of Krautrock legends Faust and discover a looser sound.

title: Heart That's Pounding
description: Artist formerly known as New Buffalo-- and the co-author of Feist's "1234"-- traffics again in wistful, just-eccentric-enough indie pop.

title: Gute Luft
description: The versatile German producer returns with music created for a documentary, and the set serves as an excellent survey of his range.

title: Shame, Shame
description: After a gruelingly long run of 1960s rock fetishism and dry, indistinguishable material, Dr. Dog embrace a bigger, more charismatic sound.

title: True Love Cast Out All Evil
description: The inimitable veteran rocker teams with fellow Texans Okkervil River on a record that gathers ideas and songs crafted over the past 40 years.

title: White Hills
description: Thrill Jockey debut from this space-rock band adds urgency to familiar psych-rock templates while displaying a careful layering of sounds and atmospheres.

title: Small Black EP
description: The band currently touring with kindred spirit Washed Out supplements their 2009 EP with two additional tracks in a remastered edition on Jagjaguwar.

title: Slave Riot
description: Madlib again displays his near-unparalleled ear on this smoldering homage to the independent-minded, freewheeling jazz of the 1960s and early 70s.

title: One One
description: The post-modern music maker limits his contextual sampling to a single subject: himself.

title: Congratulations
description: MGMT follow the surprise hit Oracular Spectacular by teaming with Spacemen 3’s Sonic Boom for a leftfield psych-pop LP bereft of obvious singles.

title: Escape
description: Woodsist presents the first full-length from this krautrock-indebted collaboration featuring Wooden Shijps guitarist Erik "Ripley" Johnson.

title: Tommy
description: Stretching his legs beyond his folktronica wheelhouse, Dosh's latest album is a compelling glimpse of potential things to come. Andrew Bird guests.

title: The Bundles
description: Kimya Dawson and Jeffrey Lewis collect some tunes crafted when they first met nearly 10 years ago, fleshed out with a few recent stragglers.

title: High Places vs. Mankind
description: On their second proper LP, High Places move from the wispy optimism that characterized their early work, opting for a darker sound to suit more solemn songs.

title: Wu-Massacre
description: Three of Wu-Tang's top MCs show up together on this 30-minute LP for three whole songs, padding out the rest with skits and guest verses.

title: Bubu King
description: The Sierra Leone-born singer releases a short but satisfying EP containing his native country's minimal and hypnotic bubu music.

title: Extra Wow
description: Portland duo's first Warp album maintains their previous work's eclecticism but aims for a more cohesive listen with a relentlessly sunny, psychedelic feel.

title: No Mas
description: Mixing electro, funk, world music, and early hip-hop, Javelin made waves with mixtapes and singles; now, via Luaka Bop, they offer their scrubbed-up debut LP.

title: The Dark Leaves
description: The New York-based singer/songwriter releases his eighth full-length, and first since 2007's Last Light.

title: Here Lies Love
description: The Talking Head and A-list dance producer gather 22 vocalists-- including Santigold, Tori Amos, and Florence Welch-- for a tribute to Imelda Marcos. Really.

title: Skulltaste
description: Post-hip-hop producer creates an album whose sonic multiple-personality disorder could be aggravating if it weren't so consistently engaging.

title: PUMPS!
description: Former duo adds a third member, shifting the balance of their focus from tones graced by rhythms to rhythms graced by tones.

title: Vol. 2
description: The San Francisco band issues a second set of odds and ends, demonstrating how it streamlines multiple strains of psychedelic rock.

title: Unfun
description: Influential San Francisco punk band's bracing 1990 debut full-length is remastered and, on digital versions, paired with the 1989 Whack & Blite EP.

title: The Places Between: The Best of Doves
description: The former "new Radiohead" has their best moments-- most of them from their first two LPs-- packaged with other highlights, and the requisite new song.

title: New Love
description: Minneapolis producer's self-released debut makes up for a lack of envelope-pushing with a fine-tuned ear for cratedigger-friendly 1970s soul jazz.

title: ...And Then We Saw Land
description: Weirdo UK folk band gets a lot less weirdo on its latest album, sounding here like skewed pastoral groups the Beta Band and the Incredible String Band.

title: The Predicate (Dub Version)
description: Prefuse 73's Scott Herren remixes a Stones Throw release credited to the Predicate Production Guild-- which may also be Herren himself.

title: Hippies
description: A garage band as steeped in Pixies as Nuggets, Harlem's Matador debut is filled with bubblegum choruses flavored with booze and cigarettes.

title: New Amerykah Part Two: Return of the Ankh
description: After the fury of the stunning New Amerykah Part One, Badu returns to creating relaxed, personal funk that feels more like a sketchbook than a record.

title: No Rest
description: Classically trained pianist and self-taught indie guitarist find middle ground through a shared sense of experimentation.

title: The Law of Large Numbers
description: Delgados singer operates outside of her orchestral pop comfort zone, improving on her solo debut.

title: NonStopErotik
description: Pixies singer and guitarist continues his prolific solo career, again connecting his current output with his formative work.

title: I Learned the Hard Way
description: The latest from these funk/soul throwbacks further affirms the validity of working in specific styles, even ones most people stopped exploring decades ago.

title: Go
description: The Sigur Rós singer fights huge with huger on his solo debut, matching the uplift of his full-time band at their most dramatic.

title: Future Factory
description: Ambitious, under-the-radar indie rock band returns to form blending Brit Invasion pop with elements of Krautrock and bossa nova.

title: Outbursts
description: It's the return of Turin Brakes, back with more dewy lead guitar and dewy lyrics.

title: Triangulation
description: The steward of the almost bulletproof Hotflush label, home to nominally dubstep breakouts by Mount Kimbie and Joy Orbison, issues his excellent second LP.

title: I Speak Because I Can
description: Just out of her teens, promising UK songwriter starts to come into her own on her second album, a top five success in her home country.

title: The Wonder Show of the World
description: Will Oldham pairs with guitarist/Cairo Gang chief Emmett Kelly to explore how we tangle ourselves with each other-- as friends, parents, children, spouses.

title: Machines That Listen
description: The Delta Mirror's debut for Lefse works from an unusual concept: Each of its nine tracks takes place in a different room of a hospital.

title: Holy Broken
description: The project of former Red Red Meat bassist Tim Hurley continues writing interesting twists into his former band's noisy Americana legacy.

title: Our Inventions
description: On its first album in five years, the German electro-pop band that includes Markus Acher from the Notwist continues to refine its icy style.

title: Black Tambourine
description: Black Tambourine's sound is all over the contemporary lo-fi scene, and this reissue shows why it has endured.

title: Sisterworld Reinterpretations
description: Liars' bracingly physical rock is given the remix/covers treatment by Thom Yorke, TV on the Radio's Tunde Adebimpe, and Atlas Sound, among others.

title: Wrestling Moves
description: Indiana post-hardcore band with proggy leanings release their debut full-length.

title: Endless Falls
description: Ambient vet Scott Morgan breathes new life into the Loscil project, playing with the idea of water-as-sound and pulling it off. Destroyer's Dan Bejar guests.

title: Mimicking Birds
description: This spectral folk/home recording project from Portland's Nate Lacy was produced by the songwriter's psuedo-mentor, Modest Mouse's Isaac Brock.

title: Nolens Volens
description: L.A. band rebounds from falling off the hype machine with a more direct, foreboding, and ultimately better second LP.

title: I Will Be
description: Former lo-fi star Dee Dee hires a full band and co-producer Richard Gottehrer, making this Sub Pop LP both terrifically fun and occasionally ferocious.

title: White Mystery
description: Chicago garage-rock fixture Alex White forms a drums-guitar duo with her brother to craft a whipsmart record with an almost perverse sense of pride.

title: Africa
description: This 1975 record from Zambia's "Zam-rock" scene, reissued by Now-Again and Shadoks, shows a band that was both behind and ahead of its era.

title: Color Your Life
description: Young NYC band continues to grow on its dynamic second EP, which recalls everything from Stereolab to Björk to Cocteau Twins.

title: Tomorrow Is Alright
description: Like citymates Girls, this group of San Fran all-stars matches wry, easygoing tunes with a far-reaching pastiche of vintage trappings.

title: Today / On Fire / This Is Our Music
description: The brilliant and influential dream-pop band's three studio albums have been reissued again, this time in 2xCD sets.

title: Love & Desperation
description: Cobra Verde's John Petkovic leads a band featuring J Mascis through takes on 70s arena rock and hard-luck tales.

title: And in the Endless Pause There Came the Sound of Bees
description: Consistently outstanding Icelandic composer and producer creates the soundtrack for a film about rodents that doubles as a well-done eco-parable.

title: The Illustrated Garden
description: Jim Putnam re-tools his band's lineup and tweaks its name on the Americana group's latest in a string of Merge releases.

title: Mulatu Steps Ahead
description: The veteran Ethiopian bandleader works with Heliocentrics and Boston's Either/Orchestra to craft a loose and improvisational winner.

title: Roman Candle / From a Basement on the Hill
description: Elliott Smith's first and last albums are reissued, highlighting the remarkable progression of his sadly brief career.

title: Live Recordings, TV-Clips & Roadmovie
description: This 2xCD release unarchives a few moments from the Swiss punk band's past: a Kleenex set from 1979, a LiLiPUT one from '83, unreleased songs, and a DVD.

title: Lux
description: Latest from the Scottish producer whose dark, ornate music seems at odds with electronic music fashion in the best possible way.

artist: Ben Sollee and Daniel Martin Moore
title: Dear Companion
description: My Morning Jacket's Jim James coaxes a modern sound from traditional roots on an album about the ecological challenges facing the trio's old Kentucky home.

title: Missing Deadlines: Selected Remixes
description: A dreamy haze runs across this shoegaze-minded producer's remix collection, for better or worse.

title: Under Great White Northern Lights
description: This lavish box set-- a live DVD, CD, documentary film, and book-- reinforces the White Stripes' mythology and displays the awesome power of their live show.

title: The Optimist
description: Dance-rock stars of minor blog hits like "Ice Cream" and "The Bomb" return with another stab at capturing the aloof cool of Ladytron.

title: Sleep Mountain
description: Once a nervy indie rock band à la British Sea Power, the Kissaway Trail here is basically a Scandinavian Arcade Fire.

title: Manifesto
description: The Wu-Tang MC returns with his first full-length in four years. Kurupt, Raekwon, and Cappadonna guest.

title: Two Thousand and Ten Injuries
description: Disco beats, post-punk sax honking, twee-pop boy/girl harmonies, and lyrics that rip your heart out. Yep, Love Is All is back.

title: Head First
description: Bringing roller-disco synth-pop out of mothballs gives the UK duo their most entertaining album since electro-glam juggernaut Supernature.

title: A
description: Massachusetts out-rock collective again teams with Four Tet, who turns them into an ethereal, electronic version of themselves.

title: Everyday Balloons
description: Portland band effectively translates its once-acoustic slowcore to electric arrangements, with help from producer Adam Selzer (Decemberists, M. Ward)

title: S-M 2: Abyss in B Minor
description: Scandinavian group finally drops a follow up to its debut, with Sufjan once again adding barely perceptible instrumental flourishes to the general maelstrom.

title: Dirty Shirt Rock 'n' Roll: The First Ten Years
description: This survey of the JSBX's first decade holds together remarkably well and gives a good sense of the band's visceral appeal.

title: One Jug of Wine, Two Vessels
description: Conor Oberst resurrects the Bright Eyes moniker on this reissue, which adds four newly recorded tracks.

title: Invisible Violence
description: Montreal dance-punk band mellows out on its latest, and along the way seems to have lost some of its sense of self.

title: Alex Bleeker and the Freaks
description: Real Estate member gathers his bandmaters and friends for a low-key classic rock-like record about spring, summer, and hanging out.

title: Raw Cuts, Vol. 1
description: Stuttgart's Danilo Plessow gathers three 12"'s (and three exclusives) that often sound like dance created by and for people who love dusty, 1990s hip-hop.

title: In the Court of the Wrestling Let's
description: The members of this London rock band are barely out of their teens, which helps explain their uncanny knack for articulating the pain of youth.

title: Greenberg OST
description: On this soundtrack for a new Noah Baumbach-Ben Stiller film, LCD's James Murphy shows his singer-songwriter side, often making like Harry Nilsson.

title: Chant Darling
description: Bella Union uproots another 60s pop-loving artist, releasing the U.S. debut from James Milne, who has played with the Ruby Suns and Okkervil River.

title: Kings Ballad
description: Spiritual singer/producer refocuses for a deeper, more rooted release.

title: This Is Still It
description: A striking collection from the 1980s Athens, Ga., band, which came up in the same scene as R.E.M., the B-52's, and Pylon.

title: Oversteps
description: Warp mainstays and techno pioneers pivot slightly with an album of dark ambience and intriguing textures.

title: Volume Two
description: Zooey Deschanel and M. Ward refine and improve their sound, creating a sequel that actually improves on the original.

title: Fly Yellow Moon
description: Guillemots singer trades his band's stylistic adventurousness and avant-garde impulses for the direct simplicity of 1970s singer-songwriter stuff.

title: Rough Frame EP
description: Woodsist continues to explore San Fran's ascendant art-pop scene, here releasing lo-fi indie pop from a duo featuring Glenn Donaldson (Skygreen Leopards).

title: Settings EP
description: Former Prof Murder and Don Cab guys continue to impress with tropical synth-pop that sounds more like Tough Alliance and AnCo than their former acts.

title: The Martyrdom of a Catastrophist
description: Boston band inspired by the darker end of new wave crafts an engaging concept album about a fringe scientist.

title: jj n° 3
description: Cosmopolitan Swedish group follows a record that took cues from Balearic dance, bookish indie pop, and hip-hop into a heavy-lidded stunner.

title: Masks EP
description: Baltimore trio and Wham City vets bash out often-funny anthems that recall post-punk and alternative rock heroes.

title: Be Brave
description: This raucous Austin band's second album dials back some of the garage rock intensity in favor of introspective songs with a more emotional tug.

title: Sweet Sister EP
description: The North Carolina band's studio work grows increasingly intricate, even here on a self-produced follow-up to their major label debut.

title: Massa Hypnos
description: Ecstatic Peace! band continues to mine sludgy Detroit rock like the Stooges and the Nuge, and now mines classic indie rock as well.

title: Stuck on Nothing
description: James Murphy-produced DFA band bottles the wide-eyed, wild-haired feeling that galvanized Richard Linklater's Dazed and Confused.

title: Polaroid Piano
description: Japanese composer crafts a wistful and gorgeous meditation for minimal piano and field recordings.

title: Message From the Tribe: An Anthology of Tribe Records 1972-1976
description: Soul Jazz reissues the work of this Detroit jazz collective, most striking for its eclectic, without-borders approach.

title: Happy Birthday
description: Sub Pop group marries two of the PacNW's great musical legacies-- twee and grunge-- with surprisingly great effect.

title: Weathervanes
description: Frenchkiss, lately locating quality bands with commercial appeal (Passion Pit, Antlers, Dodos, Local Natives), here offers a crappy one with commercial appeal.

title: Big Echo
description: San Fran baroque-pop group takes a nice step forward on its sophomore album, thanks in part to pristine production from Grizzly Bear's Chris Taylor.

title: Gay Singles
description: True Panther collects 7" tracks released over the past few years by Seth Bogart's homoerotic, rock'n'roll throwbacks.

title: Wildling
description: Tough-to-peg band mixes jazz, classic German psychedelia (think Cluster), and a bendy guitar style familiar from spaghetti Westerns.

title: Who Killed Sgt. Pepper?
description: The latest from Anton Newcombe's band finds him attempting to revitalize BJM's sound with disco rhythms, drum loops, and house-diva wails.

title: Are the Roaring Night
description: Montreal band delivers an edgy, restless set of dark romanticism and muscular guitar.

title: The Big To-Do
description: The DBTs return, focusing on the songwriting of Patterson Hood and refreshingly reconnecting with the macabre and darker corners of the American psyche.

title: PVI006/IBB004
description: This oddly titled compilation rounds up a group of kindred UK garage-rock spirits-- led by Male Bonding, Teen Sheiks, and Spectrals-- quietly making noise.

title: Shaved EP
description: Vancouver artist makes his Warp debut on an EP of ominous mood pieces and dubstep-esque excursions he calls "surf-step."

title: Lay of Pilgrim Park
description: Using just vocals and a small array of traditionally classical instruments, this Chicago band conjures their own unique sound.

title: Rush to Relax
description: Fantastic Australian garage-punk band continues its quick rise on this hastily made but powerfully packed new album.

title: Fang Island
description: This wildly infectious Brooklyn band takes manic musicianship and shoutalong choruses to another level on their self-titled second album.

title: Nigeria Special, Vol. 2: Modern Highlife, Afro Sounds & Nigerian Blues 1970-6
description: Soundway's second Nigeria Special volume gives us a glimpse of what highlife sounded like in Africa's most populous nation during the early 1970s.

title: Be So True EP
description: Another rising chillwave producer, South Florida's MillionYoung creates music that's more synthetic than most current bedroom electronic projects.

title: The Desert of Shallow Effects
description: After six years of almost complete silence, the former Beulah frontman delivers his solo debut to a cult in waiting.

title: Carve Out the Face of My God
description: Sophomore LP from this L.A. noise artist is bolder and more fully realized than his debut, with almost every shoegazey glow countered by a noisy growl.

title: The Monitor
description: Titus' sophomore record, a sprawling concept album loosely about the U.S. Civil War, is packed with anthems and brimming with energy and ambition.

title: Return to Form
description: At their best, this fantastic live band combines tight riffs and chops with a deep, abiding love of joyous guitar slop.

title: Home Acres
description: Aloha continue to invest in woeful tales of anti-social sadsacks set to a pristine mix of Chicago indie-prog and late-90s emo.

title: Kairos
description: Casey Dienel's restless voice detours again on an enveloping album of artful, gauzy pop.

title: Stridulum EP
description: Following on their stirring full-length debut, The Spoils, Zola Jesus return with a terrific EP that applies their gothic drama to more immediate songs.

title: Broken Bells
description: The Shins' James Mercer teams with producer and Gnarls Barkley member Danger Mouse for a melancholy pop record.
Led by a touring guitarist from Titus Andronicus, Dinowalrus create rapidly shifting songs that leap from spazzy guitar-pop to skronky noise.

title: Land of Make Believe
description: Backpacker latecomers shift to make a record that picks up the Kid Cudi rap-pop baton.

title: Strange Keys to Untune Gods' Firmament
description: UK band creates an engrossing 12-track, 2xCD, two-hour-plus marathon of feedback-and-distortion charges for electric guitar and electronics.

title: Beat the Devil's Tattoo
description: One of the original progenitors of the early-2000s "rock is back" ethos reckons with making music well after their original battles have been fought.

title: Plastic Beach
description: Ex-Blur frontman Damon Albarn ditches the idea of writing pop songs a cartoon band might front and makes one of his most gorgeous pop records in years.

title: Wierd Presents: Cold Waves and Minimal Electronics, Vol. 1
description: A satisfying collection of the obscure synth-based music that drew from post-punk and early new wave in a decidedly low-budget and DIY style.

title: Double Jointer
description: Hardly Art band's debut falls in line with the throwback garage-rock of Black Lips and King Khan, as well as the murkier scuzz-pop of Vivian Girls.

title: In Stereo
description: Viennese laptop guru Christian Fennesz, British electronic wizard Peter Rehberg, and American multi-tasker Jim O'Rourke reunite for a third record.

title: The Brutalist Bricks
description: After the slight letdown of Living With the Living, Ted Leo's new LP is hopeful, purposeful, direct-- an improvement on every level.

title: Sisterworld
description: Liars' relentlessly tense new album finds the always excellent band focusing on detail and texture rather than stylistic schizophrenia.

title: Time on a String
description: Produced by Daniel Smith, the debut from this deeply mannered singer finds her backed by members of her family.

title: Between Buildings and Trees
description: Kompakt ambient artist collects patient piano melodies and loops and crafts a quiet, delicate winner.

title: Nerve Up
description: Manchester singer/guitarist Julie Campbell proves the post-punk revival isn't a spent force on this, her debut LP for Warp.

title: The Winter of Mixed Drinks
description: Frightened Rabbit's third studio LP finds them with a bigger, more sophisticated sound to match their newly-expanded band and a slightly sunnier outlook.

title: Quarantine the Past
description: The first career-spanning Pavement comp contains their best-known songs as well as concert staples, fan favorites, and at least a couple of curveballs.

title: Hologram Jams
description: These former Blood Brothers are now a duo with a stronger dance-rock flavor; somewhere along the line, something went very wrong.

title: Lights
description: Hailed as a UK buzz artist for her blend of folk and pop sensibility, this newcomer is more akin to Scandinavians Lykke Li and Jenny Wilson.

title: Jet Lag
description: The WHY? drummer and brother of Yoni Wolf steps out with a solo LP inspired by a breakup.

title: Fight Softly
description: A louder, thicker album from New Zealand-based outfit known for combining live instruments and samples in a swirl of psychedelic color.

title: Oar
description: Beck continues his inspired work leading famous friends in covers of older albums. Wilco, Feist, Jamie Lidell here help him tackle Skip Spence's cult classic.

title: Nigeria Afrobeat Special: The New Explosive Sound in 1970s Nigeria
description: The fifth volume in Soundway's Nigeria Special turns its attention to Afrobeat proper, featuring both Fela Kuti and just some of those indebted to him.

title: Draumalandid
description: Famed Icelandic producer (Björk, Will Oldham) and Bedroom Community boss soundtracks an environmental doc. Sam Amidon, Nico Muhly, and Ben Frost guest.

title: Constellations
description: Austin instrumental ensemble demands patience and attention on this, their best record to date.

title: In the Dark
description: The Athens rockers' third album, produced by Ben Allen, finds them a long way from their scrappy beginnings.

title: A Sufi and a Killer
description: Working with producers including Flying Lotus and Gaslamp Killer, vocalist Gonjasufi has created a fascinating slab of hallucinogenic head-nod music.

title: Back to Light
description: UK producer Tim Simenon continues his comeback as Bomb the Bass, here roping in Gui Boratto as co-producer. Martin Gore and Kelley Polar guest.

title: Elevator Music, Vol. 1 / Sub:stance
description: A pair of compilations-- one from Fabric, one from Scuba's Berlin club-- that serve as mini-anthropologies of dubstep in 2010.

title: Going Places
description: Famed noise/drone duo issue their final record, which transforms a sense of finality and reflection into often incredible instrumental passages.

title: Permalight
description: After a run of bad luck and tragedy, Rogue Wave reconvene for their second post-Sub Pop album.

title: The Creatures in the Garden of Lady Walton / Veil Waltz EP
description: The National's Bryce Dessner's post-rockers return, now focusing on songcraft. Shara Worden frequently guests; Matt Berninger and Sufjan Stevens also appear.

title: Descending Shadows
description: Veteran PacNW garage rockers Fred and Toody Cole, formerly of Dead Moon, record their second LP (and first for Vice).

title: Coconut
description: Marking a transition between their garage rock roots and a new DFA-esque friendly sound, the UK band deliver a record of two very different sides.

title: Close Calls With Brick Walls / Mother of Mankind
description: The once Far East-only-- frequently awesome; sometimes experimental-- Close Calls LP is finally released in the U.S., along with a bonus record.

title: Rat a Tat Tat
description: Broken Social Scenester displays a welcome command of songcraft in an indie-folk field that too often is all about vocals and words.

title: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space B P
description: This new deluxe, limited product is only for hardcore fans; the music, however—both the original LP and this record’s extras—is timeless.

title: Yeah So
description: Sheffield boy-girl duo nail precious, vulnerable feelings over the course of their sweet (but not twee or saccharine) indie pop debut.

title: Mathematics Presents: Return of Wu and Friends
description: The sequel to the Wu family record nobody wanted in the first place explores the post-The W, pre-8 Diagrams Wu dead zone.

title: Snakes for the Divine
description: Five albums in and another awesome, absolutely pummeling record of tough, fast stoner metal from Matt Pike and co.

title: Nitetime Rainbows EP
description: Ambitious Philly band follow their hour-plus opus Ashes Grammar with a second example of what their new-look band sounds like.

title: Tomorrow, in a Year
description: The prominent electro group releases an avant-garde opera about the life of Charles Darwin that's at times impenetrable and rapturous.

title: Trilogi
description: Swedish folk band collects three limited-edition EPs onto a record that has a sneaky, consistent sound that's immediate and yet full of surprises.

title: Maintenant
description: Long-gestating LP recalls the recent soft-pop of Lucky Soul or Camera Obscura, but with guest vocalists that include Owen Pallett, Mirah, and Rose Melberg.

title: Magic Chairs
description: Danish band, who has often intrigued and wowed in the past, chart a more direct path, preferring pop clarity over musical intrigue.

title: Watergate 05
description: Berlin techno linchpin contributes to her hometown club's mix series, featuring tracks by Röyksopp, Matias Aguayo, Luciano, AGF, and Uffie.

title: Dear God, I Hate Myself
description: With Caralee McElroy gone, Jamie Stewart enlists new guests and experiments with 8-bit textures. It's still Xiu Xiu though: look at the title.

title: Landing
description: Wire's Colin Newman and co. keep their original sound-- reminiscent of their first band and very early Stereolab-- mostly intact on album three.

title: Eyelid Movies
description: An aptly titled debut record from a duo with a penchant for lush, moody, and surprisingly affecting trip-hop.

title: The Magician's Private Library
description: Rising singer-songwriter explores nightmares, hopes, and loss on her debut album. TV on the Radio's Dave Sitek produces.

title: Work
description: On their follow-up to 2007's Our Ill Wills, the Swedish band enlists Phil Ek to beef up and sharpen their twee-leaning sound.

title: American Recordings VI: Ain't No Grave
description: The supposed final chapter in the late country star's career-capping sessions with producer Rick Rubin is released and fashioned as a tearjerker.

title: Introducing
description: New noise-pop band fits perfectly into the Slumberland Records aesthetic: washes of reverb, bubblegum melodies, and shoestring-budget production.

title: Minor Love
description: The former Moldy Peaches member eschews dick jokes and pop ditties for Downtown cool and minimalism.

title: Luck in the Valley
description: One of the de facto leaders of the resurgent movement of John Fahey devotees, Jack Rose recorded this triumph shortly before his recent death.

title: Similes
description: Accomplished ambient artist expands his sound to include delicate new elements-- soft percussion, his own voice-- creating distant pop songs.

title: The Golden Archipelago
description: Following career-peak Rook, Jonathan Meiburg and co. return with another excellent record of restrained grandiosity and enigmatic grace.

title: European
description: The Gothenburg, Sweden-based indie pop band demonstrates the virtues of cosmpolitanism, craft, and restraint.

title: Standing on Top of Utopia
description: Scandinavian producer trades in vocal-aided tracks that are odd and disparate and instrumental cuts that are even more schizophrenic.

title: Fabric 50
description: Fabric's top mix series here finds the dubstep A-lister showcasing his increasingly divergent interests, touching on all manners of UK dance subgenres.

title: The Meat of Life
description: After almost breaking up during the recording of 2009's The Hungry Bird, Clem Snide are back, if not exactly re-energized.

title: Have One on Me
description: The full-length follow-up to Ys is no less ambitious, but this 3xLP set also has some of the most inviting and accessible songs of Newsom's career.

title: Animalore
description: Brooklyn band retains its debut's mature, earnestly proficient folk-pop and adds touches of funk, R&B, and humor.

title: The Years EP
description: Chillwave newcomers take a more relatively somber approach to bedroom-produced nostalgia, lending this EP a more classic, polished feel.

title: Tidings
description: London band mixes blues-rock with English folk and bits of glam rock, stitching together the songs with abstract interludes.

title: American Gong
description: Portland indie supergroup focuses on its strengths and boils its songs to their most essential ingredients on their best album in years.

title: Hidden
description: UK post-punk revivalists tear up their own rulebook and start from scratch on this ambitious, darkly experimental second album.

title: Sigh No More
description: West London band's faux family business actually sounds like a business, one supplying value-added products at discount prices.

title: We Are Proud of Our Choices
description: Producer and remixer extraordinaire straddles the pop and the underground on this rhythmically diverse Kompakt mix.

title: Prenuptial Agreement
description: Rising Oakland rapper has a genuine ability to entertain without trivializing the significance of the tragic underpinnings that give his songs their power.

title: Presidence
description: Brooklyn avant-rock collective helms a 130-minute 2xCD set: Put simply, Disc One is mostly classic Excepter, and Disc Two is mostly something else.

title: Black Noise
description: German producer builds minimal techno epic from a beautifully textured sound palette. Panda Bear guests.

title: Planets of Old
description: Hipster metal O.G.s bring their 2009 comeback EP to CD, recalling both their slicker crossover sound and chop-heavy prog roots.

artist: Everybody Was in the French Resistance...Now!
title: Fixin' the Charts, Vol. 1
description: Art Brut's Eddie Argos teams with Dyan Valdés on an LP of "answer songs"; what makes for a mildly amusing MySpace click can lead to a painfully obnoxious album.

title: Tapestry of Webs
description: Former members of Blood Brothers make a clean break from the past by offering an LP marked by quiet tension and gradual builds.

title: We All Got Out of the Army
description: Pollard's first solo album of 2010 is a hefty glam-pop record with a brighter, more nuanced sound reminiscent of GBV's Isolation Drills.

title: The Stimulus Package
description: The former Roc-A-Fella star brings his ferocious voice and unique intensity to Rhymesayers, here teaming on a record with Jake One.

title: Maudlin
description: Team Love band embraces arrested development with a drink in one hand and Dylan's lyrics sheet in the other.

title: Peace & Love
description: Ten albums into her solo career, the alt-rock veteran goes it alone, playing every instrument in a mostly-acoustic setting.

title: The Minimal Wave Tapes: Vol. 1
description: Stones Throw offers an expertly crafted introduction to a label focused on unearthing electronic DIY music from the late 1970s and 80s.

title: Measure
description: After breaking to work as School of Language and the Week That Was, the brothers Brewis return for a new Field Music LP.

title: Causers of This
description: More of a producer than a composer, Toro Y Moi carries the chillwave torch into 2010 and works best when he's exploring sounds instead of songs.

title: Found Songs
description: The young Icelandic composer who has opened for Sigur Rós constructs an album of short but emotionally-charged pieces for strings and piano.

title: XXXX
description: Canadian dance-punk survivors' new album looks like a winking porn reference but it's a moody, melancholy look at another four-letter word.

title: Dream Get Together
description: Ezra Feinberg again gathers the totems and taboos of 1970s rock, exploring the excitable intersection of psychedelia and pop.

artist: Thee Silver Mt. Zion Memorial Orchestra
title: Kollaps Tradixionales
description: Constellation's flagship band continues to evolve from a meditative orchestro-folk ensemble into a politically enraged rock band.

title: Scratch My Back
description: The dignified prog and pop star returns from another long layoff with a covers LP featuring takes on Arcade Fire, Bon Iver, Radiohead, and Magnetic Fields.

title: Mountain Debris
description: Mixing 90s alt rock and of-the-moment lo-fi haze and hypnagogic pop pastiche, this UK auteur is crafting a very now sound.

title: Face a Frowning World: An E.C. Ball Memorial Album
description: Bonnie "Prince" Billy, the Handsome Family, and others cover this itinerant folk-gospel artist, who preached salvation more than damnation.

title: Frauhaus
description: All-female British trio's sophomore effort celebrates their percussive, atonal foremothers like the Slits, the Raincoats, and LiLiPUT.

title: Falling Down a Mountain
description: The veteran UK band continues to re-locate itself on this, its second album since the departure of three of its original six members.

title: Gorilla Manor
description: Local Natives have a familiar sound-- rustic vocals, harmonies, clattering percussion-- but songwriting skill and youthful energy mark their striking debut.

title: Playtime
description: Collaboration between house producer Move D and Spacetime Continuum's Jonah Sharp is a no-seams mix of gliding house music and ambient composition.

title: The Amazing
description: Sharing members with Dungen, this Swedish group alternates between moody acoustic folk rumination and various permutations of stoner-friendly rock.

title: North/South/East/West
description: Warp gathers top artists from four locales-- NYC, L.A., London, and Glasgow-- to create an all-star wonky album featuring FlyLo, Skream, FaltyDL, and more.

title: Renihilation
description: These "Brooklyn hipsters" treat extreme metal with the élan of a ripe young garage rock band or a focused noise artist.

title: Soldier of Love
description: The classic soft-rock band returns with its first album in a decade, and it still seems wholly unique and oddly captivating.

title: Casual Victim Pile
description: Matador boss Gerard Cosloy curates a compilation highlighting his favorite Austin-area bands of the past few years.

title: Frictionalism 1994-2009
description: This 3xCD, 35-track retrospective places many tracks on CD for the first time and sheds light on one of Detroit techno's great, unclaimed dance artists.

title: The Calcination of Scout Niblett
description: Niblett's music has always been lonely, introverted, and anguished, but the stakes seem much higher on this album, like it's a do-or-die scenario.

title: Periphery
description: On her debut LP, Black Moth Super Rainbow member Maux Boyle crafts ambient music using synthesizers and lightly treated piano.

title: Odd Blood
description: A tighter, slicker, poppier sophomore album tries on every imaginable sound and style-- but none is as original or effective as the one they started with.

title: Interference
description: This lost act recorded unreleased music for Glenn Branca's label that split the difference between Swans and ESG. Now Social Registry releases their stuff.

title: Aufgang
description: Blending classical piano, live drums, and techno-inspired electronics, Aufgang's fresh sound is hard to classify.

title: It Was Easy
description: Q and Not U drummer John Davis, formerly of Georgie James, continues the latter band's power-pop lean with his new project.

title: Thin Thin Line
description: The singer-songwriter with a devoted cult following returns with a fine album on Mark Kozelek's Caldo Verde imprint.

title: I'm New Here
description: The influential singer-songwriter returns after many years with a powerful album that mixes spoken word, folk, and blues over roughed-up sonics.

title: Si, Para Usted: The Funky Beats of Revolutionary Cuba, Vol. 2
description: This retrospective gathers songs from Cuba's 1960s and 70s, a time when global pop was blending with the country's traditional music.

title: Raiders
description: Either a doom band with drone overtones or a drone one with doom overtones, L.A. duo Robedoor follow in the footsteps of Double Leopards, Axolotl, and others.

title: AFCGT
description: Former members of the still-underrated A-Frames team with members of Climax Golden Twins for a record of drones and sound collages.

title: Songs About People I Know
description: Delightfully ramshackle, this UK indie pop band works wonderfully in spite of seemingly being another jumble of influences.

title: Heligoland
description: On their first non-soundtrack album in seven years, original member Daddy G returns and Damon Albarn, Hope Sandoval, and Elbow's Guy Garvey guest.

title: Talking to You, Talking to Me
description: The angelic-voiced L.A. folk-rock revivalists add versatility and personality to their sound.

title: Heart of My Own
description: A rare find in the crowded folk-pop world, this Rough Trade singer/songwriter is engagingly versatile and fresh.

title: Daptone Gold
description: Studiosly re-creating the sounds of 1960s and 70s soul, Daptone has gained a deserved cult following; here it collects some of its best recordings.

title: Ali and Toumani
description: The uncommonly beautiful final recordings by Malian guitar pioneer Ali Farka Touré find him once again joined by Toumani Diabaté.

title: One Life Stand
description: Dialing back some of their eccentricities and embracing personal songwriting, Hot Chip have crafted their most consistent album yet.

title: 144 Pulsations of Light
description: Kranky debut from a California artist who sits nicely alongside the meditative sounds of Gas, Boards of Canada, and Stars of the Lid.

title: Good God! Born Again Funk
description: Second in Numero's gospel series is easily as good as the first and funky enough to grab any listener with a taste for rhythm, religious or not.

title: In Search of Stoney Jackson
description: Stones Throw continues to widen its circle of L.A. connections, pairing Madlib's production work with this post-Death Row SoCal crew.

title: The Soft Pack
description: Formerly known as the Muslims, much buzzed-about California band evolves, grafting some finesse and introspection onto their garage-rock template.

title: Dreamland EP: Marimba and Shit-Drums
description: Spencer Krug takes a detour under a new alias, constructing a suprisingly affecting and dreamlike 20-minute track using the instruments in the EP's subtitle.

title: Shape of the Shape
description: Manchester band unexpectedly moves from Pentangle-like folk-rock to a weird and intriguing combination of cosmic country and space-age Moog drones.

title: Sadly, the Future Is No Longer What It Once Was
description: Leyland Kirby, aka V/VM, creates a 3xCD set of anodyne melodies focused on mood, composition, and performance.

title: A Chorus of Storytellers
description: Post-rock veterans and Sigur Rós associates continue to create twinkling, mostly instrumental music with IDM textures.

title: Mind Chaos
description: Portland buzz band sounds like NYC 00s buzz bands-- specifically, like the precise midpoint between the Strokes and LCD Soundsystem.

title: Rebirth
description: He really went ahead and did it: Lil Wayne finally releases his unlikely, unqualified, and quite unbelievable rock album.

title: Leaving on a Mayday
description: Swedish star takes another stab at the U.S. market with her third LP. Björn Yttling produces; Sonic Youth's Steve Shelley and Chavez's Matt Sweeney guest.

title: You & Me
description: Freak folk linchpin, who counts Currituck County and Vetiver among his projects, releases his first LP under his own name. Joanna Newsom guests.

title: Tumbélé! Biguine, Afro and Latin Sounds From The French Caribbean, 1963-1974
description: The Soundway label offers a primer on the musical crosscurrents found in Martinique and Guadeloupe.

title: Ugly Side of Love
description: The Bristol duo championed by Portishead's Geoff Barrow indulge in sample-heavy pop that seems pulled from a UK pirate-radio broadcast from 1973.

title: The Courage of Others
description: The recent breakout band follows its delightful 2006 album, The Trials of Van Occupanther, with a long-awaited new folk-pop record.

title: Ommatidia
description: Boston improv duo deals primarily in slow, sparse sounds-- a form of improvisation known as reductionism-- but the effect is far from minimal.

title: Rifts
description: One of a handful of new artists making exquisitely crafted, ear-opening forays into drone collects his limited-run output onto a 2xCD set.

title: Paper Dolls
description: New Zealand-based indie pop duo continues to strike an odd balance of child-like singsong simplicity and subtle sophistication.

title: The House of Love / The German Album
description: One of modern rock's great should-have-been bands has its two Creation Records LPs reissued in the U.S.

title: Couple Tracks
description: The Toronto hardcore band issues its second singles compilation, which begins with its debut single and leapfrogs around the group's fruitful career.

title: Accelerated Living
description: Oakland band dials down the sludgy thwomp of its previous work in favor of run'n'gun thrash metal.

title: Einzelkämpfer
description: Experimental German producer Antye Greie, who has worked with the likes of Ellen Allien and Vladislav Delay, returns with her sixth solo album.

title: Journal of Ardency
description: Former solo folkie Elizabeth Harper's new dance-pop project features the frosty sonics and compelling vocals that made her 80s influences so memorable.

title: Life Is Sweet! Nice to Meet You
description: Former Test Icicles member recruits Animal Collective producer for an album that plays like a product of his musical restlessness.

title: Romance Is Boring
description: The divisive and highly personal Welsh group continues to grow up, embrace its inner punk, churn out amazing lyrics, and sharpen its edge.

title: Adventures in Experimental Electric Orchestra from the San Francisco Psychedelic Underground
description: Former Manson associate, still imprisoned, has a 2xLP set of "electric symphony orchestra" music issued by Mexican Summer.

title: No Hope, No Future
description: London's Good Shoes lie somewhere between a less insular Arctic Monkeys and a less caffeinated Futureheads, and here they return with album number two.

title: Night Music
description: With help from Detroit techno godfather Carl Craig, former Zombie Zombie member creates a haunted, sinister take on electronic music.

title: To Realize
description: Oakland three-piece continues to create outstanding Liars-like rock that places its faith in texture, atmospherics, and shades of light and dark.

title: Stroke: Songs for Chris Knox
description: An all-star lineup-- Mangum, Oldham, YLT, Callahan, Merritt, Darnielle, Jay Reatard-- pays tribute to the iconic Kiwi singer/songwriter and stroke sufferer.

title: Forge Your Own Chains: Heavy Psychedelic Ballads and Dirges 1968-1974
description: Collecting strains of heavy psych from five continents, this ambitious, thoughtful release is also unsurprisingly erratic.

title: Versions
description: The slippery, underappreciated Portland band reworks its own previous material, and in just about every case improve upon the source material.
The second full-length from the rocking side project of Low's Alan Sparhawk builds nicely on the sound of their debut LP.

title: Turn Ons
description: Following a split with their label, two-thirds of Supergrass team with producer Nigel Godrich and create a stopgap all-covers project.

title: IRM
description: After a 2006 album created in collaboration with Air and Jarvis Cocker, Charlotte Gainsbourg returns with a surprisingly great LP written and produced by Beck.

title: YellowFever
description: Playing girl-group pop drenched in noise, like their pals Vivian Girls, YellowFever offer more surprises and Easter eggs on this hyper-aware record.

title: Together You and I
description: The folk troubadour's fourth album bends musical elements to reinforce his lyrics, which show a strong grasp of character and voice.

title: Pop Ambient 2010
description: A pair of Brock Van Wey tracks, plus new ones from DJ Koze and Dettinger highlight the latest version of Kompakt's annual ambient series.

title: FabricLive 49
description: A hugely diverse and dense mix from the Portuguese outfit includes selections from Zomby, Major Lazer, Crime Mob, and many more.

title: Realism
description: Stephin Merritt explores another aesthetic conceit on his latest record, creating a characteristically self-aware play at a "folk" record.

title: One-Armed Bandit
description: The ambitious Norwegian band with a hard-to-define jazz/ post-rock sound returns with another eclectic album.

title: The Biggest Ragga Dancehall Anthems 2009 / The Biggest Reggae One-Drop Anthems 2009
description: Greensleeves Records issues its two high-profile, annual looks at the past 12 months' worth of the most fruitful types of Jamaican pop.

title: Setting the Paces
description: Pacific Northwest songwriter David Crane beefs up a batch of songs about childhood and innocence with meatier rock production on BOAT's latest.

title: Acolyte
description: The latest attempt to rescue the UK from landfill indie, Delphic are a hotly tipped band that is being branded as a new New Order.

title: Teen Dream
description: Teen Dream is both the most diverse and most listenable of the Baltimore band's three full-lengths, and yet it never seems like a compromise.

title: Five American Portraits
description: With help from Jim O'Rourke and the Raincoats' Gina Birch, Red Krayola and A&L combine classic tunes with portraits of famous figures.

title: Book of Leaves
description: Best known for her stint in chamber ensemble Rachel's, the Louisville pianist's solo debut is in the same neo-classical vein as her old group.

title: The Flexible Entertainer
description: Having previously fed on a diet of everything post-punk, the now-duo is opening up to rhythms and sounds from modern R&B.

title: Sturm
description: Beloved German band releases a soundtrack record so generic that selling it as a Notwist record feels faintly deceitful.

title: There Is Love in You
description: Driven by dance-inspired beats and ghostly sampled voices, the new Four Tet album is the most focused in Kieran Hebden's catalog, and also among his best.

title: Silence
description: Blending techno, dubstep, and ambient into an hour of idiosyncratic drift, this is programmed electronic music at its most sensually expressive.

artist: Franco & le Tout Puissant OK Jazz
title: Francophonic, Vol. 2: 1980-1989
description: The second volume of the Stearns label's anthology of the Congolese bandleader's recordings is thunderbolts and fireworks, start to finish.

title: Black Wooden EP
description: Phil Elverum contributes to a series that asks musicians to create "something spontaneous, collaborative, fun, or experimental."

title: Zephyr EP
description: The house music legends go on an unexpected detour here, offering an EP of synth washes, ethnographic pastiches, and soft-rock jams.

title: Diplo Presents: Free Gucci (Best of The Cold War Mixtapes)
description: Quintessential Atlanta MC Gucci Mane is given an indie reinvention via Diplo and a host of top producers-- Zomby, FlyLo, Memory Tapes.

title: Dimensional Bleedthrough
description: Metal supergroup, led by Mick Barr, creates something for fans of black metal, noise, and drone to all love.

title: What Day Is it Tonight?
description: Trans Am explore a career's worth of 1970s rock cliché and 80s synth-rock cliché on this strong live album and DVD.

title: Up From Below
description: Dude from Ima Robot reemerges as a folk-pop singer, winning over satellite radio and late-night TV producers for some reason.

title: End Times
description: Mark Oliver Everett returns with another record of sadsack self-pity, without even the tinges of humor that typically color his work.

title: Astro Coast
description: The debut LP from this young Florida band is first and foremost a great guitar album packed with sing-along hooks, but there's more going on beneath the surface.

title: You Are the One I Pick
description: Kranky issues the debut album by this UK chamber-pop duo, who counts Erik Satie, PJ Harvey, and Rachel's among their influences.

title: Trust
description: Kompakt producer continues to re-imagine trance as a worthy component of chic modern techno.

title: Make It Sound in Tune
description: Merge leader Mac McCaughan gives his label's acts-- including Spoon, the Magnetic Fields, and Lambchop-- the covers treatment on this charity EP.

title: Intimate Moments for a Sensual Evening
description: Indie comic follows his "Parks and Rec" stardom with a collection of his best stand-up bits, including nine minutes of RAAAAAAAANDY.

title: Real Life Is No Cool
description: After elongating his brand of retro-futurism to great song lengths, the Norweigan producer crafts an achingly stylish and neatly accessible dance record.

title: Carousel
description: The latest instrumental album from the mastermind of the Cocteau Twins' sound delivers the magisterial guitar tones one has come to expect from his projects.

title: Underwater Peoples Winter Review
description: The upstart Underwater Peoples-- the label that birthed Real Estate-- follows its summer 2009 comp with another seasonal collection.

title: Athens
description: The famed progressive house band collect a few of their favorite things.

title: Roy Montgomery/Grouper
description: Grouper follows her outstanding 2008 LP with another mix of submerged instruments and field recordings, on a split with a new Roy Montgomery track.

title: Transference
description: Trading some of their signature groove for a more destabilizing sound, Spoon have created an offbeat, unexpected, but ultimately cerebral record.

title: Climb Up
description: New England post-rock group trades their debut's gloomy swirl for a more linear, prog-leaning take on chugging radio rock.

title: July Flame
description: Neo-folkie takes the best aspects of her two previous records and distills them into her best album. MMJ's Jim James and the Decemberists' Chris Funk guest.

title: Rain on the City
description: The dependable singer-songwriter who debuted in the alt-rock era returns with his first album of new songs in eight years.

title: The Colossus
description: After a foray into singer-songwriter territory, Rjd2 rediscovers mood-setting backgrounds and rattling, rigged-to-explode instrumentals.

artist: The Flaming Lips, Stardeath and White Dwarfs
title: The Dark Side of the Moon
description: Originally conceived for a New Year's Eve show, the Flaming Lips and guests Peaches and Henry Rollins cover the Pink Floyd classic.

title: Hustler's Son
description: Rilo Kiley drummer follows the lead of his bandmates by making a solo record that leans heavily toward the rootsy-- sounding most like 1990s alt-country.

title: All Shall Fall
description: The 1990s Norwegian black metal band is still sharpening its singular sound.

title: Legendary Hearts / New Sensations
description: The two very different paths that Lou Reed traversed after his 1982 comeback The Blue Mask are reissued and remastered.

title: The Little Match Girl Passion
description: Adapting a Hans Christian Andersen fable, the Bang on a Can co-founder has produced the most profound and emotionally resonant work of his career.

title: Heartland
description: After several releases as Final Fantasy, Owen Pallett makes his debut under his own name, and it's his grandest and most assured statement to date.

title: Eddy Current Suppression Ring / Primary Colours
description: Australia's promising young garage rock band finally has its two best bits of minimalist guitar music issued in the States.

title: Fabric 48
description: Radio Slave's blend of lush, hypnotic minimal-into-house is almost like a tribute to the sound of 2007, in the best sense.

title: Is There Nothing We Could Do?
description: The former Next Big Thing dusts off some of his long-dormant qualities for this appealing soundtrack record.

artist: Bonny Billy and the Picket Line
title: Funtown Comedown
description: Will Oldham's latest is a fittingly titled, string-band live LP released digitally and on vinyl with little fanfare during the final bleak days of 2009.

title: Campfire Songs
description: Animal Collective's transitional 2003 album, recorded in one long take on a porch in the Maryland woods, is reissued on their Paw Tracks imprint.

title: Low Tide Digitals III
description: Out-music veterans continue their decade-long collaboration with an album of severe modern classical, harsh noise, and ambient music.

title: A Parallax I
