description: Of Montreal member and frequent E6 collaborator releases a solo debut full of fragments of his day band's genetic material.

title: Judy Sucks a Lemon for Breakfast
description: More than a decade after their peak, the UK band returns with their unique palette of perspective, imagination, and humor still in place.

title: Reality EP
description: Real Estate cap their fruitful first year with a collection of new songs-- many of which are the solo work of chief songwriter Martin Courtney.

title: The Fame Monster
description: Lady Gaga's second record, containing "Bad Romance" and "Speechless", finds her coming into her own as both a songwriter and a pop star.

title: Eggs
description: This Copenhagen band seems to specialize in volcanic sound effects, but it manages to write some pretty compelling songs along the way.

title: Gonna Work Out Fine
description: Jack Dunning aka Untold's final 2009 Hemlock release cements his status as one of post-dubstep's-- hell, electronic music's-- most vital producers.

title: Huntsville International
description: Underdog hip-hop group manages to expertly reimagine trance as a soundtrack for a lonely southern stoner rather than as club anthem fodder.

title: Fela: The Best of the Black President
description: With a full reissue campaign coming-- and a show in his honor on Broadway-- Fela's re-examination year kicks off with this comp.

title: VH1 Storytellers
description: This live set finds Kanye inserting rambling monologues in the middle of his songs, not so much storytelling as a bizarre string of WTF asides.

title: Movies Is Magic
description: Kompakt vet Sebastian Meissner explores cinematic sweep and the notion of film music as home listening on his new LP.

title: Rejoicer
description: New York's Grooms, formerly known as Muggabears, ably and enjoyably channel the spirit and sound of 1990s alt-rock and indie.

title: The Voidist
description: Yeah Yeah Yeahs sideman finally makes a nimble, grandiose album all his own, one that feels like a move towards his own spotlight.

title: The Burrprint: The Movie 3-D / The State vs. Radric Davis
description: Underground rap's biggest breakout of 2008-09 finally releases his major-label debut; plus, a look at the best of his many recent mixtapes.

title: Contra
description: Read Mike Powell’s review of the album.

title: An Exaltation of Laarks
description: Absolutely Kosher band creates a well-crafted document of the 2000s, a time period we're still in the process of digesting

title: The Mantles
description: San Franciscan five-piece churns out sharp, garage-minded jangle-pop with more bite than most of their peers.

title: Gone: The Promises Of Yesterday
description: Buried somewhere down in the footnotes of the story of Stax Records is 24-Carat Black. Numero Group thankfully unearths them.

title: By the Throat
description: Australia-born, Iceland-based producer creates one of the most menacing-- and rewarding-- ambient records of the past year.

title: We Are Young Money
description: In the spirit of work from Dipset and Bad Boy, Lil Wayne creates a clique record, and-- with Drake and Nicki Minaj on board-- pulls it off.

title: Strange Gods
description: Reminiscent of Fuck Buttons or Black Dice, Philly's David Harms combines heavily repetitive rhythms with noisy, thickly textured loops.

title: Triptych / Vice Versa, etc.
description: Important Records reissues two albums from the French drone composer, which were previously unavailable in digital form.

title: Young One
description: Assembling previously released material, this duo-- he from Blank Dogs, she from the Dum Dum Girls-- revels in the contrasts between their music.

title: ATL RMX
description: Free mixtape from Adult Swim pairs Atlanta's top rappers (Jeezy, Cee-Lo, Gucci) with some of today's top indie producers (El-P, FlyLo, Dam-Funk).

title: Gazzillion Ear EP
description: The standout track from Born Like This gets the remix EP treatment, with work from Thom Yorke, Dave Sitek, and Jneiro Jarel.

title: Chimeric
description: A relatively looser, more open approach suits the Austrian electro-acoustic trio.

title: The Dance Paradox
description: As Burial reworked the signifiers of UK Garage into an extremely personal sound, Redshape takes the essential tropes of classic techno and does the same.

title: Alphabet 1968
description: Black to Comm successfully probes the depths of ambient, drone, and modern classical composition with both restraint and imagination.

title: Who Designs Nature's How
description: Arcade Fire members' other band enlists Tim Hecker, Mad Professor, Kid Koala, and more to help craft this remix EP.

title: Enemy of the State: A Love Story
description: Getting back to business, the Chicago MC provides a potent reminder of his sheer technical prowess on this brief yet rewarding mixtape.

title: Of the Body Prone
description: Asheville, N.C.-based trio releases its latest record on John Zorn's Tzadik label, a logical fit for their abstract, surprising music.

title: Milky Ways
description: French producer's latest veers from post-rock jamminess to rock pastiche but its best moments come when he settles into contemplative dance mode.

title: God Is a Twelve-Year-Old Boy With Asperger's
description: Indie comedy vet and "Flight of the Conchords" regular issues his latest Sub Pop stand-up album.

title: The Singles, Vol. 8: 1972-1973
description: The latest set of JB singles finds him making odd decisions in an attempt to be seen as important and socially vital. Most of them work out fine.

title: Prison Break EP
description: This digital-only EP features uniformly solid remixes from El Guincho, jj, and others, plus an incredible one from the Juan MacLean.

title: Slow Attack
description: The former Suede singer finds unlikely inspiration in Talk Talk and makes his best solo album.

title: Kitsuné Maison 8
description: The Paris-based label again shows its range and strong ear, with a comp featuring Memory Tapes, the Drums, and Chew Lips vs. Alex Kapranos.

title: In This Light and on This Evening
description: Album number three from the popular UK post-punk acolytes finds them moving to a more synth-based sound to dreary effect.

title: My Dusty Road
description: A treasure for historians and folk fans alike, this 4xCD set collects more than 50 long-lost mid-1940s performances from the American legend.

title: Untitled
description: After surviving for years in a ravenously young genre (and, of course, his legal battles), this beguiling pop culture oddball finds himself oddly adrfit.

title: Fire in My Bones: Raw + Rare + Otherworldly African-American Gospel, 1944-2007
description: This gospel set covers a wide range of approaches: from contented to contemptuous, sessions to field recordings, fevered shouts to ruminative moans.

title: Xenophanes
description: The latest in a large run of 2009 solo records from Omar Rodriguez-López may be the tightest Mars Volta-related release in years.

title: Echo Kid
description: Once a Be Your Own Pet side project, Turbo Fruits issue their first LP since the dissolution of their day-job band.

title: Klang
description: The UK indie band returns to the spirit and energy of their promising debut, and then unexpectedly breaks up after releasing this record.

title: Neil Young / Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere / After the Gold Rush / Harvest
description: Neil Young's first four albums, remastered and gathered together in a pricey (but impressive) box set.

title: Darkness Come Alive
description: Converge's Nate Newton takes his band's hardcore punk roots and adds Thin Lizzy's guitar harmonies and Motörhead's high-octane grime.

title: Ghost
description: One of rising label Lefse Records' marquee fall releases, the debut from this San Diego three-piece is more about promise than delivery.

title: Television
description: The Senegalese legend returns with his first album since 2001's Missing You (Mi Yeewnii).

title: Fantastic Mr. Fox OST
description: The OST to Wes Anderson's animated tale features the director's faves (the Stones, Beach Boys), plus Jarvis Cocker and composer Alexandre Desplat.

title: Til the Casket Drops
description: Rap's preeminent group returns with their first LP not entirely produced by the Neptunes, and first LP in years without a protracted label battle.

title: Jarvik Mindstate
description: One of dubstep's key producers makes his full-length album debut, with few concessions for non-fans for good or bad.

title: Kids Aflame
description: Ex-Harlem Shakes guitarist offers his first solo album of mostly unvarying, lo-fi instrumentation, which sounds nothing like Harlem Shakes.

title: Zounds
description: Sydney band with prog leanings and widescreen inclinations blows up its sound even further this time out.

title: White Water, White Bloom
description: Swoony, melodic songs delivered with aching sincerity-- no wonder this fit so well on the Twilight soundtrack.

title: Music For Insomnia
description: Asthmatic Kitty co-founder teams with his partner and stepson, Sufjan Stevens, and the National's Bryce Dessner for a record of avant-garde experimentalism.

title: Light: On the South Side
description: Numero Group create their most lavish package yet-- a look at the 1970s Chicago soul scene, complete with a book full of Michael Abramson photography.

title: How to Be a Lady, Volume 1
description: With production by The-Dream and his cohorts, this R&B group's debut features lush slow jams and rococo, information-overload uptempo tracks.
The mysterious and often rapturous Norwegian avant-garde collective releases its first record as a trio.

title: Renaissance: The Mix Collection
description: The German duo put together a history-lesson-cum-slow-burn showcase featuring some of 2009's best dance music, and many classics.

title: Elvis 75: Good Rockin' Tonight
description: To mark Elvis' 75th birthday, Legacy issues a new 4xCD, 100-song box set drawing from the singer's entire career.

title: Endless Bummer
description: Philly disco crew mixes limber dance-punk and funk tracks with dreamier, more contemplative fare, resulting in a varied set that works as an album.

title: Dr. No's Ethiopium
description: Madlib's younger brother continues to develop his own recognizably consistent and characteristic style, here working with Ethiopian music of the 1960s and 70s.

title: New York-Addis-London: The Story of Ethio Jazz 1965-1975
description: This collection of tracks from the Ethiopian bandleader shows the power of his unique fusion.

title: Asleep in the Back [Deluxe Edition]
description: Stately, luxurious sounding, professional-- one of the decade's quietly underrated bands has its best album given a 2xCD/DVD reissue.

title: Lifter Puller / Half Dead and Dynamite / The Entertainment and Arts EP / Fiestas and Fiascos / Slips Backwards
description: The Hold Steady's Craig Finn has the bulk of his cult classic group's catalog digitally reissued.

title: Pyramids With Nadja
description: Toronto metalgaze duo Nadja pairs with the Denton, Texas, outfit Pyramids for an expansive, effects-heavy album of surprising focus.

title: Armonico Hewa
description: Japanese all-female group and Boredoms offshoot continues to refine its unique, experimental voice.

title: Tribute to the Sun
description: His second full-length marks Luciano as a techno producer whose sound-world is uncommonly vast and even more uncommonly fertile.

title: Score! The Remixes!
description: Merge caps its 20th anniversary year with a charity record that finds Four Tet, Caribou, Junior Boys, and more reworking songs from the label's catalog.

title: Dreamin' Man
description: The latest entry in Young's fabled Archives series is a peculiar one: live versions of the songs that eventually were released as Harvest Moon.

title: Cocoon of Love
description: This baroque-pop band comes off as the Left Coast answer to the Vampire Weekend/Grizzly Bear boat-shoe/literary reference set.
The longtime Icelandic collective hooks up with the venerable techno label Kompakt on its latest record.

title: Florine
description: Rising talent Julianna Barwick has her ethereal, gorgeous EP given a well-deserved wide release.

title: Good Evening New York City
description: CD/DVD package attempts the difficult job of capturing a stadium-sized show from the Beatles legend.

title: Felt 3: A Tribute to Rosie Perez
description: The cream of U.S. indie hip-hop-- Murs and Atmosphere's Slug MCing, with production from Aesop Rock-- combine for the first Felt record in four years.

title: The Treatment
description: Indiana shoegaze/slowcore revivalists make a surprisingly crisp, economical record.

title: Dead Zone Boys
description: Formerly Grampall Jookabox, David "Moose" Adamson here crafts an intriguing record about inconspicuousness and civic inattention.

title: The Seventh Seal
description: After 10 years and an aborted Dr. Dre collaboration, the legendary MC releases his comeback album.

title: Toeachizown
description: This 2xCD collection pares down the L.A. producer's 5xCD debut album series, intended as a mission statement for what he calls "modern funk."

title: Rated R
description: The R&B star has described the Rated R sessions as "theraputic," and the vitriolic, rough, raw end product is about as brutal as you'd expect.

title: New Worlds
description: Still best known for playing in other people's bands-- Ash, Client, Bat for Lashes-- Charlotte Hatherley's third solo LP is her most self-assured to date.

title: Echo Party
description: Much-missed underground hip-hop producer returns with an offbeat old-school mix taken from the archives of Traffic Entertainment Group.

title: A Retrospective 1998-2008 or I Was a Christian Emo Twentysomething
description: Menomena's Danny Seim picks through the best tracks from his Lackthereof project, choosing from the self-released albums that preceded Your Anchor.

title: Blakroc
description: The Black Keys combine with many of hip-hop's top stars-- Mos Def, Q-Tip, RZA, Raekwon-- on a surprisingly well thought-out record.

title: The Catalogue
description: Long-awaited box from one of the most important bands of the last 35 years presents their output from Autobahn forward in remastered and repackaged form.

title: Maybes EP / Sketch on Glass EP
description: One of the most promising dubstep producers is also one of those responsible for taking the dance genre places it usually doesn't go: R&B, post-rock, IDM.

title: What We All Come to Need
description: No longer grappling with its identity, this instrumental band now writes efficient, five- to seven-minute songs that, with a few edits, could end up on radio.

title: Buzzrock Warrior
description: Co-produced by DJ /rupture and Shadetek with a roster of collaborators, this Guyana-born Brooklyn MC's debut offers a decent set of global grooves.

title: Stir the Blood
description: After a misstep of a second album, these modern rock survivors return to the synth-pop that got them on the NME's good side earlier this decade.

title: One Fast Move or I'm Gone: Music From Kerouac's Big Sur
description: The Death Cab for Cutie and Son Volt leaders construct songs from Jack Kerouac's prose, all for a doc on the famed writer.

title: Spells
description: Promising L.A. band-- led by the particularly intriguing singer and guitarist Sarah Negahdari-- is another worthy entry in the 90s alt-rock revival.

title: Family
description: We've spent a lot of the decade with a choice of spazzy, lo-fi electro-funk bands from Montreal, but here's one more worth tracking.

title: Arrow
description: On their sophomore album, New York-based indie poppers seem willing to turn an appreciation of the Fab Four into a guiding artistic principle.

title: New York
description: Compiling six previously unreleased New York shows from 1955 through to 1990, this large box is a sequel to Sinatra's similarly themed Vegas set.

title: Fall Be Kind EP
description: Ten months after the release of Merriweather Post Pavilion, Animal Collective return with an EP that finds them still on a creative roll.

title: Seconds
description: The cult songwriter behind the beloved, once-lost folk-rock classic Red Hash makes an inevitable return to writing new songs.

artist: D. Charles Speer and the Helix
title: Distillation
description: No-Neck Blues Band's Dave Shuford continues to find success with his roots-rock offshoot, which trades in twangy guitars and tear-in-beer ballads.

title: Escape 2 Mars
description: The Blackalicious MC makes a comeback on this solo album, which recalls... Blackalicious.

title: Oh, Glory. Oh, Wilderness.
description: Four years after their last full-length, Holopaw seem reinvented, sporting a looser, more melodic sound that moves easily between styles.

title: For Your Own Special Sweetheart
description: The D.C. band's 1994 major label debut, long out of print, has been reissued by Dischord and DeSoto, and it has aged exceedingly well.

title: Trust in Numbers
description: Latest find from Service, the Swedish indie pop label that helped launch the Tough Alliance and Jens Lekman. Studio's Dan Lissvik produces.

title: Ouled Bambara: Portraits of Gnawa
description: This CD/DVD package documents the suite of songs played in Moroccan Gnawa ceremony; it's music that's more spiritual currency than a product or showcase.

title: Idol Omen
description: Brooklyn duo gets assists from Luke Temple (Here We Go Magic) and Joan as Police Woman on its eerie, elusive, late D Plan-like new album.

title: Can You Dig It? The Music and Politics of Black Action Films 1968-75
description: The Soul Jazz label offers an excellent 2xCD compilation of early-70s soul and funk from films.

title: Glitter and Doom Live
description: This live record is a de facto greatest hits of Tom Waits' fourth decade of music, during which his gnarly adventurousness only intensified.

title: Carpet Madness
description: Gallic/English duo mines the coquettish 1960s pop vibe of yé-yé, the precision and throb of UK post-punk, and the syncopation of reggae and tropicalia.

title: Hot Wax
description: A decade after his sadly overlooked Good News for Modern Man, the former Hüsker Dü member finally issues his third solo record.

title: Up to Now
description: The Coldplay acolytes release a deeply overstuffed 2xCD best-of when a crisp singles collection could have done.

title: Live in New York
description: The much-maligned band makes a case for itself on this sprawling 6xCD collection, recorded just before the release of Morrison Hotel.
This lavish vinyl-only boxset includes full albums like Deadringer and Since We Last Spoke along with some impressive unreleased material.

title: Blackout Summer
description: Part of the burgeoning San Diego lo-fi scene that's home to Crocodiles and the Soft Pack, Christmas Island make shaggy, sadsack hymns to heartbreak.

title: Local Currency: Solo 1992-1998
description: Cult guitar pop veteran releases the sort of warts-and-all release that most songwriters would love to call their own.

title: Street Anthems
description: The grime crew that featured Dizzee Rascal, Wiley, and Flowdan gets a welcome retrospective that gathers their raw early work alongside stabs at pop.

title: Do What You Want, Be What You Are: The Music of Daryl Hall and John Oates
description: This too expansive look at the lengthy career of Hall and Oates features two great discs and two not so hot ones.

title: Them Crooked Vultures
description: Led Zeppelin's John Paul Jones, Nirvana/Foo Fighters drummer Dave Grohl, and Queens of the Stone Age's Josh Homme resurrect the hard rock supergroup.

title: Historicity
description: The jazz trio continues its outstanding work, reflecting in their music our age of information and chatter. And they do a mean cover of "Galang".

title: Yankee Reality
description: Freak-folk vets make a leap from last year's self-titled Ecstatic Peace! debut that feels markedly deliberate and completely natural. J Mascis produces.

title: Ask the Night
description: Azure Ray singer trades the full-band sound of her solo debut for a more rustic approach. Modest Mouse's Isaac Brock guests.

title: The Apple and the Tooth
description: The Warp producer collects remixes from his breakthrough album, Ambivalence Avenue, and adds four new tracks on this 2009 punctuation mark.

title: Don't Stop / All Night EP
description: After a long wait and a battle with her former record label, electro-pop should-be star finally issues her second album, plus a bonus EP of older ideas.

title: Continent
description: This young Montreal producer, best known at this point for his remixes and a collaboration with Sally Shapiro, offers an accomplished debut full-length.

title: Sugarland
description: No Wave-inspired band makes its Rare Book Room debut, bringing an increase in clarity and detail to its thick noise.

title: Ultraviolet
description: After three years of work, the once-anticipated Kid Sister album finally sees its release.

title: Space Oddity [40th Anniversary Edition]
description: Celebrating the true first chapter in an often brilliant career, David Bowie's second studio album is reissued, complete with a 15-track bonus disc.

title: Real Estate
description: After several excellent singles, New Jersey's Real Estate deliver on their full-length debut with a rich collection of evocative and haunting songs.

title: Machine Dreams
description: Swedish quartet make dance-oriented electronic-leaning pop that foregrounds ambiance and texture, as Tricky once did so well.

title: Ignore the Ignorant
description: Smiths guitar hero Johnny Marr joins one of the brightest lights of post-Libertines UK rock for their fourth album.

title: Before I Self Destruct
description: After two huge misses and a bleeding of good will, 50 steps back and makes a record designed to appeal to listeners who still might be rooting for the guy.

title: Suitcase 3: Up We Go Now
description: The third 100-song vault-clearing contains unheard demos from Guided by Voices' classic mid-90s era.

title: No Ceilings
description: Weezy returns to mixtape form, where he shows off his digressive, distracted spirit-- still a huge part of what makes him great.

title: Waiting For You
description: With stripped-down, ambient eeriness, the debut LP from this dubstep/dancehall crossover is like a mirror image of the Bug's London Zoo.

title: Rock is Dodelijk
description: Brighton rockers offer a breathless, ripchord performance on this new live disc.

title: Flashmob
description: The influential dance artist unveils his second act-- and first after blog house producers turned overblown feedback and digital grime into exhausting shtick.

title: Get Yer Ya-Ya's Out! The Rolling Stones in Concert [40th Anniversary Deluxe Box Set]
description: The Rolling Stones' go-to-by-default big live album gets a remastering job, but also an odd multi-disc treatment.

title: iTunes Originals
description: This iTunes collection spans YYYs' whole career, and it shows a band willing to adapt and change without regrets or nostalgia for its past.

title: Dog Poison
description: The hyper-prolific garage-rockers manage to put a few new spins on their familiar formula.

title: Belly of the Lion
description: Composer and songwriter David Wingo issues another strong LP whose expansiveness and Americana textures are reminiscent of MMJ or Band of Horses.

title: Solar Life Raft
description: After blowing minds with 2008's Uproot, and working with the Ex's Andy Moor, Brooklyn's DJ /rupture teams with Dutty Artz co-owner Matt Shadetek.

title: Harvest Festival
description: Hot Chip's co-frontman records his debut solo LP, a rippling set full of throbbing synthesizers and thudding drum machines.

title: Stills
description: Belle and Sebastian's Stuart Murdoch follows his soundtrack to an unfinished movie with a new EP from his girl group- and musical theater-leaning project.

title: Islands
description: Heart-on-sleeve Swedes return with another album of 1980s-indebted exquisite melancholy.

title: A Good Year for Hardness
description: After a 10-year hiatus, the hard-to-pin-down, forward-looking indie rock band returns.

title: Extended Vacation
description: The latest from the long-running side project of Wilco drummer Glenn Kotche and upright bassist Darin Gray, two focused, imaginative composers.

title: Rewolf
description: The dream-pop band offers nine stripped-down reimaginings of the duo's music, with a cover of Hope Sandoval's smoky 2002 single "Suzanne".

title: Bleach [Deluxe Edition] / Live at Reading
description: Nirvana's scrappy Sub Pop debut is reissued with a 1990 live show as a bonus, and their legendary 1992 set at Reading is finally given a DVD/CD release.

title: Warm Brother
description: Managed by Jay Reatard, Shawn Foree's project has a predictably rude sense of humor; here, he takes advantage of a full studio for the first time.

title: Visitation
description: This California band blends the ambition of Omaha turn-of-the-millennium emo with tricked-out studio atmospherics.

title: Truce Opium
description: Ambitious Athens collective blend almost everything imaginable-- from drone metal to avant-jazz, Southern folk to classic rock-- into their huge sound.

title: Chomp More
description: An expanded reissue of the Athens post-punks' second album offers some clues to where they could have gone next.

title: Attention Deficit
description: After three mixtapes-- highlighted by 2008's triumphant and savvy The Mixtape About Nothing-- Wale finally issues his debut LP.

title: Horror Disco
description: With one foot in Italo disco and one in Goblin-like 1970s horror soundtrack, this debut LP is one of the more appropriately titled of the year.

title: Performing Parades
description: The Danish art-rock collective records their second album with some of the Danish National Chamber Orchestra, so their already-epic songs become more so.

title: Ghana Special: Modern Highlife, Afro-Sounds & Ghanaian Blues 1968-1981
description: This fine 2xCD companion to the earlier Nigeria Special comp highlights the musical connections between the two countries.

title: World Painted Blood
description: The best album from thrash metal's Big Four (Metallica, Megadeth, Slayer, Anthrax) since the 1990s is fast, finely controlled, and nearly fat-free.

title: Beast Rest Forth Mouth
description: The second full-length from this Brooklyn band is a striking consolidation of the spiky psych-prog tendencies of its 2007 debut into a pop framework.

title: Everything Is New
description: The sophomore full-length from the UK singer-songwriter finds him broadening his palette to include textures from genres like Afropop and Tropicália.

title: Thriller
description: On their third album, loud Londoners Part Chimp slow down, stretch out, and sometimes indulge their metal side a little more.

title: Turning the Mind
description: Mercury-nominated producer with an ear for shoegaze textures returns with an album more invested in lyrics.

title: Broken
description: Mark Lanegan again teams with UK electronic vets, with guest spots from Spiritualized's Jason Pierce, Mike Patton, Richard Hawley, and Gibby Haynes.

title: Warp20 (Box Set) / Warp20 (Chosen) / Warp20 (Recreated) / Warp20 (Unheard)
description: Warp celebrates 20 years in business with a massive box set collection.

title: When the Devil's Loose
description: The second solo album from the one-time Verbena frontman continues his obsession with rough-hewn imagery and earthy song structures.

title: In the Gardens of the North
description: Bandleader Markland Starkie transforms lessons learned from his DIY home-taping years into fully-realized songs of all shapes and sizes.

title: Ay Ay Ay
description: Kompakt star and former Closer Musik member returns with a record of maximal oddity, an album far from his minimal roots.

title: Invisible Girl
description: Shaking off the Almighty Defenders misstep, King Khan and Mark Sultan collaborate for another distillation of Nuggets and Brit Invasion rock.

title: Phrazes for the Young
description: Strokes singer makes his solo bow with a record of post-millennial synth-pop.

title: Midnight Soul Serenade
description: Jon Spencer and Matt Verta-Ray continue to reinterpret the early days of rock'n'roll, emphasizing the rawness and raunchiness of it all.

title: Goodbye Cruel World, Hello Crueler World
description: It's been a long time since you've heard a band pull off this sort of southern-fried slop-pop with such charm, craftiness, and self-deprecating wit.

title: Received Pronunciation
description: The Boston trio continues the tradition of wordy, tuneful, earnest underdogs from Small Factory and the Trashcan Sinatras to the Lucksmiths.

title: Molina and Johnson
description: Magnolia Electric Co./Songs: Ohia's Jason Molina and Centro-Matic's Will Johnson team for a sleepy, evocative record.

title: Raditude
description: Melodic sing-alongs, fuzz-guitar riffs-- Weezer are going back to basics, making music that sounds for (but also often by) 13-year-olds.

title: Unbalance
description: Dave Huismans, aka A Made Up Sound, uses dubstep as the center rather than the totality of his sound as he here also explores techno and broken beat.

title: Eccentric Soul: Smart's Palace
description: A soul music empire from Wichita, Kansas, and nearly lost to history is resurrected by the Numero Group on the latest comp from the imprint's winning series.

title: Blue Record
description: The second LP from this Savannah, Ga., metal quartet finds producer John Congleton coaxing more sound out of the band than they've ever allowed.

title: Greatest Hits
description: Despite missing early single "I'll Stick Around", and including blah new songs, these modern rock survivors prove their singles band cred on this comp.

title: Swords
description: Twenty-track compilation gathers the B-sides of the indie legend's recent comeback years.

title: Under Stellar Steam
description: British multi-instrumentalist mines fertile repetition on the latest compelling record in a compelling career.

title: Entropy
description: Portland dance-rockers offer an album of tightly constructed piano pop nuggets replete with overdubbed, harmonized vocals and loosely jazzy rhythms.

title: Shaft OST [Deluxe Edition]
description: Isaac Hayes' game-changing film score, which launched the soul/funk soundtrack craze in the early 70s, is given a deluxe reissue.

title: Unexpected Guests
description: DOOM has the more scattershot pieces of his already scattershot discography compiled on this LP of lesser-known tracks.

title: The Unforgettable Fire [Deluxe Edition]
description: U2's first collaboration with Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois comes across as a transitional album of the highest magnitude.

title: III
description: Philly collective of freak-folkers-- led by Greg Weeks and Meg Baird-- move toward simplicity and directness.

title: Opiate Sun
description: Stop-gap EP from Justin Broadrick's most pop-oriented project foregrounds his memorable riffs and ringing climaxes.

title: Beak>
description: Portishead's Geoff Barrow unveils an odd, menacing, and even potentially alienating work that sounds more like 1971 than 2009.

title: Sainthood
description: The Quin twins follow their career peak The Con with another eclectic and personal record. Death Cab's Chris Walla produces.

title: What Will We Be
description: The preeminent songwriter and personality of New Weird America moves to Reprise without losing any of his eclecticism or quirk.

title: Smoke the Monster Out
description: UK-born, L.A.-based producer tries to reconcile a penchant for idiosyncratic sample collages with a career based on giving the crowd what it wants.

title: Strict Joy
description: The Oscar-winning duo made famous in the popular indie film Once returns with their first post-film (and post-breakup) record.

title: Let's Build a Roof
description: The Olympia, Wash., group continues quietly to build an impressive arsenal of indie pop songs. Karl Blau produces.

title: Axe to Fall
description: One of the decade's best metal and post-hardcore bands finish the 2000s with one of its best records.

title: Live at the Olympia
description: This 2xCD LP, recorded over a five-night public rehearsal at a small venue in Dublin in 2007, attempts the colossal task of summing up a sprawling career.

title: Let's Just Stay Here
description: One of alt-country's best vocalists and underrated songwriters collaborates with some Toronto-based kindred spirits.

title: Hors d'Oeuvres
description: Annie Sachs, an artistic descendant of Robert Pollard, follows her self-titled 2008 debut with a far more concise and deliberate release.

title: Normal as Blueberry Pie - A Tribute to Doris Day
description: The eccentric singer-songwriter pays tribute to the music of Doris Day, from classics like "Sentimental Journey" to lesser-known songs from films.

title: Kaleidoscope
description: Trance superstar trades voyages into the smiley faced ultraworld for collaborations with Sigur Rós, Bloc Party, Tegan and Sara, and more.

title: 5: Five Years of Hyperdub
description: To celebrate five years in business, the Hyperdub label gathers tracks from Burial, Flying Lotus, and more into a convincing statement on the range of dubstep.

title: Summer of Fear
description: Following a bleak debut produced by Grizzly Bear's Chris Taylor, MBAR's follow-up streams like one long AOR-radio rock block.

title: Let It Die
description: Portland band continues its Beatlesesque pop, here wrapping studies of mid-life anxieties in unfussy, steady-as-she-goes rockers.

title: Wayfaring Strangers: Lonesome Heroes
description: Numero Group's choice Wayfaring Strangers series continues with an LP of wanderlust often inspired by the draft. Ex-NHLer Jim Schoenfeld appears.

title: Investigate Witch Cults of the Radio Age
description: The exceptional avant-pop group combines with the Ghost Box records founder for a mini-LP that highlights their differences as much as their shared vision.

title: Head [Deluxe Edition] / Goat [Deluxe Edition] / Liar [Deluxe Edition] / Down [Deluxe Edition]
description: The first four full-lengths from the hugely influential noise-rock band have been remastered by Steve Albini and Bob Weston and reissued.

title: Transition
description: Viennese duo of Florian Kmet and Radian's Stefan Németh come together for an accessible and appealing album of electro-acoustic instrumentals.

title: The First Days of Spring
description: Laura Marling's former band carries on without her, with a record that reflects her break from both the group and its leader, Charlie Fink.

title: Baghdad Batteries: Orbsessions Vol. III
description: The Orb's new-millennium output has been inconsistent, but here Alex Paterson arrests the slump toward making music that's merely pleasantly familiar.

title: Christmas in the Heart
description: The patron saint of sneering, disaffected poets releases a collection of classic Christmas songs for Feeding America, a leading hunger-relief nonprofit.

title: The Twilight Saga: New Moon OST
description: The massively successful vampire franchise soundtracks its second film with Thom Yorke, Death Cab, Grizzly Bear, Muse, Bon Iver, St. Vincent, and more.

title: Grey-Eyed Girls
description: Prolific Bay Area band offers its latest album of jangly garage-pop, balancing psych-rock swagger with generous dollops of sweetly cockeyed melody.

title: Keep in Mind Frankenstein
description: Ex-Band of Horses member Mat Brooke and co. follow their highly enjoyable debut with their latest Sub Pop release.

title: Break It Up
description: Be Your Own Pet's precocious singer goes solo and grows up a bit, the zombies and pizza parties of yore replaced with predicted "dark days."

title: Other Truths
description: Toronto post-rock band's latest contains four lengthy tracks that add new dimensions and sharper textures to their sound.

title: Tarot Sport
description: The second full-length from this noisy Bristol duo is more accessible than their first but sacrifices none of that record's visceral power.

title: Barn Nova
description: After nearly a decade of small-run releases, Matt Valentine, Erika Elder, and co. bring their act to Thurston Moore's Ecstatic Peace for a third time.

title: Doomsday EP
description: Elvis Perkins punctuates his intriguing In Dreamland LP with a six-song exercise in tinkering with the foundations of American music.

title: Feel Good Together
description: Black Keys' Patrick Carney leads a band of four other fulltime drummers on this guitar-driven record.

title: Trapped Animal
description: The post-punk originals make a long-awaited return, updating their Jamaica/London sound for the digital age.

title: Logos
description: With contributions from Lætitia Sadier of Stereolab and Panda Bear, the Deerhunter frontman continues to expand the parameters of his solo project.

title: Geneva
description: Chicago post-rock band makes its best album yet, both in structure and execution.

title: Black Beach
description: Working better in visual format than on disc, this CD/DVD from the often inscrutable experimental band captures a nice communing-with-nature spirit.

title: Skin and Bones / Mo Beauty
description: The Clap Your Hands Say Yeah frontman returns with two markedly different albums, one recorded with help from Philly pals and one recorded in New Orleans.

title: The Fountain
description: The 1980s legends continue their lengthy second act with a record that aims to remind listeners of the band's past rather than recast it in new light.

title: Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix [Remix Collection]
description: Phoenix have their 2009 tracks remixed by Animal Collective, Passion Pit, Devendra Banhart, Chairlift, and more.

title: At the Cut
description: Working with the same lineup as 2007's North Star Deserter, Chesnutt blends country-folk, Southern soul, and post-rock around dark, existential lyrics.

title: Yeah Ghost
description: Zero 7 return, not with a downtempo album but some sort of omnivorous post-MP3 pop record.

title: CrownsDown
description: Anticon group takes up its rap-saving banner again in a major way, crafting a back-to-basics album.

title: The Real Feel
description: After working for a decade as the Preston School of Industry, Pavement founder Scott Kannberg releases his first album as Spiral Stairs.

title: I Told You I Was Freaky
description: The faux-folk, hipster-doofus duo have their Season 2 music presented on disc, an exercise for fans rather than neophytes of the HBO show.

title: New Clouds
description: Kranky pysch-rocker Adam Forkner indulges his spontaneous side on a heady record that's laid out like a modern classical or classic jazz work.

title: Zebra
description: K Records singer/songwriter embraces African music, crafting an ode to it and the music it prompted stateside.

title: Declaration of Dependence
description: Ignoring calls to fold Erlend Øye's hushed beats into their hushed folk, the Kings of quiet return with their most whisper-soft-- and graceful-- record yet.

title: Celebration
description: Another Madonna compilation: This 2xCD set collects roughly half of her singles, albeit sequenced in almost random order.

title: The BQE
description: Sufjan Stevens' multimedia work inspired by the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway, premiered in 2007 at the Brooklyn Academy of Music, is released as a CD/DVD set.

title: You Can't Take It With You
description: Working within the easily licensed Jeff Buckley-Snow Patrol continuum, this Long Island band makes major-label melodrama.

title: Survival Skills
description: NYC rap vets offer a surprise collaboration, with guests Mary J. Blige, Bounty Killer, Slug, Talib Kweli, and Immortal Technique.

title: Love Is Not Pop
description: After a slight misstep, the Swedish singer/songwriter makes a heartbreaking return to form. Studio's Rasmus Hägg co-produces.

title: Is and Always Was
description: Jason Falkner produces the latest record from Daniel Johnston, giving the iconoclastic singer/songwriter the rich canvas he has so long deserved.

title: Earthly Delights
description: On their first LP in four years, Lightning Bolt offer a record in which most tracks center around growling chords and monolithic beats.

title: The Conformist
description: Thomas Bartlett continues on his quiet musical path, here with contributions from Norah Jones and Matt Berninger of the National.

title: We're on Your Side
description: Latest from Danish experimental chamber-pop group finds the band reveling in the sweet spot between structure and open-ended art-rock exploration.

artist: Thao with the Get Down Stay Down
title: Know Better Learn Faster
description: After a personal, sometimes exuberant debut, Thao Nguyen's follow-up is the post-party comedown, a collection of hard-learned lessons.

title: Dillanthology 3
description: Mostly sourced from his classic 2000s LPs, the latest J Dilla comp is also therefore arguably the most familiar music and least essential intro.

title: Tongue N' Cheek
description: Dizzee's self-released dance-pop record has three UK #1 singles, but it's the album tracks that make this a worthwhile and often enjoyable listen.

title: Wildlife
description: The Polyvinyl band explores how frail, fraught, and difficult it is to maintain the connections between family, lovers, and friends.

title: All the Pleasures of the World
description: Like an indie-pop Kurt Vile, this Aussie artist transforms classic rock touchstones into something affecting and winning-- in this case, charming indie pop.

title: Rio [Collector's Edition] / Live at Hammersmith '82!
description: Duran Duran reissue and expand their one truly great album, plus issue a live document of their ascendancy to transatlantic superstardom.

title: Splitting the Atom
description: Massive Attack preview their new LP with an EP of two new songs and two remixes of songs we've yet to hear-- plus contributions from TVOTR and Elbow.

title: The Life of the World to Come
description: John Darnielle offers up a concept album based on Biblical verses, and the theme leads to an intense collection of songs that yields more with every listen.

title: The Yolks
description: Chicago garage-rockers craft a no-nonsense album of simple pleasures that's direct, unpretentious, and joyful.

title: Imidiwan: Companions
description: Following their 2007 breakthrough Aman Iman: Water Is Life, the desert guitar band from Mali returns with a more communal album.

title: 45 Live
description: Stones Throw head manages the impressive task of artfully mixing 7" singles on this trip down hip hop's memory lane.

title: Live at the El Mocambo
description: Recorded on the 1978 tour for My Aim Is True, this live set captures Elvis Costello and the Attractions at their fierce and funny best.

title: Psychic Chasms
description: Beneath the hazy sonics from this bedroom electro-pop project are well-structured and highly addictive songs, resulting in one of the year's nicest surprises.

title: Abstract Expression
description: Leone's second full-length is an exhilarating, restless, and sometimes downright tiring album of schizoid avant-pop.

title: Good Morning Jokers
description: Finnish duo with a flair for fashion returns with their first album in four years and it's filled with more frosty, slowly developing folk music.

title: Butter
description: Glasgow producer sounds both richer and more restless, serving up pitched-up hip-hop, tripped-up drum patterns, and shorted-out 8-bit melodies.

title: Sunset/Sunrise
description: Seattle duo's sophomore effort balances the darker qualitites of their debut with Jesse Lortz's murkier musings on the birth of his first son.

title: Embryonic
description: In a shocking turn, the Flaming Lips offer their most audacious undertaking since Zaireeka, an unrelentingly paranoid, static-soaked acid-rock epic.

title: DJ-Kicks
description: The 30th entry into !K7's storied DJ-Kicks series comes from Vice's Chromeo, so it's not surprising it's filled with funk and R&B-infused pop.

title: Death Acoustic
description: As its title implies, this is a stripped-down solo album from the former Queens of the Stone Age co-leader.

title: Ciao My Shining Star: The Songs of Mark Mulcahy
description: Thom Yorke, Michael Stipe, the National, and Dinosaur Jr. turn out for this charity tribute to the man best known for the theme song to "Pete & Pete".

title: Never Cry Another Tear
description: Ex-New Order members Bernard Sumner, Stephen Morris, and Phll Cunningham unveil their new project. Blur's Alex James guests.

title: Scars
description: The eclectic dance duo dial it back a bit on the most effective parts of their latest album.

title: Magic Neighbor
description: While characteristically downcast, the eighth album from Germano lifts some of the gauze and exhibits a bit more warmth and playfulness.

title: Zero to 99
description: Robert Pollard quietly continues his excellent 2009 with another often-rewarding Boston Spaceships release. R.E.M.'s Peter Buck guests.

title: Childish Prodigy
description: Drawing heavily on road-weary classic rock and folk-rock, Kurt Vile makes the leap from lo-fi all-star to Matador's impressive class of 2009.

title: Fluorescent Black
description: The caustic, adventurous hip-hop group returns for its first non-collaborative album in seven years.

title: Where the Wild Things Are OST
description: Karen O leads an all-star team (including members of YYYs, Liars, and Deerhunter) on the OST for Spike Jonze's film version of the Maurice Sendak classic.

title: Chicken Switch
description: Sonic Youth's Lee Ranaldo, Matmos, and Boredoms' Eye Yamatsuka are among participants in a remix LP that's more like a comp of excellent experimental music.

title: Goodnight Unknown
description: On his second solo album under his own name, the indie rock veteran does a little of everything he does well and improves on his last outing, Emoh.

title: Bonfires on the Heath
description: Capping off one of the decade's great bodies of mood music, the Clientele continue to conjure and charm through their evocative music.

title: Ghostdini: The Wizard of Poetry in Emerald City
description: Whether as a commercial concession or an experimental detour, Ghost goes full-tilt R&B on his new album.

title: Run Rabbit Run
description: Sufjan Stevens' experimental electronic LP Enjoy Your Rabbit is recast as a modern classic work by Osso and many of NYC's hippest young composers.

title: Family
description: Hardly Art band's sophomore album bears the fingerprints of many of today's top indie bands, including Animal Collective and Grizzly Bear.

title: Where the Action Is! Los Angeles Nuggets 1965-1968
description: Rhino continues its expansion of the Nuggets brand with a 4xCD look at the fertile Sunset Strip and other SoCal musical locales of 1965-68.

title: Dead Man's Bones
description: Oscar-nominated actor Ryan Gosling gets a friend and a children's choir together for a truly unusual and surprising record.

title: In and Out of Control
description: Sticking with the sure-footed, loud formula that suited them on their debut and Lust Lust Lust, these Danish JAMC acolytes are back on a roll.

title: Warm Heart of Africa
description: The full-length debut from this Afropop project rises to the high standard of their 2008 mixtape; guests include M.I.A. and Ezra Koenig of Vampire Weekend.

title: Six
description: Black Heart pull off the delicate task of making legitimately unsettling, spooky music without sounding like a novelty-- perfect stuff for this time of year.

title: Exploding Head
description: The loud New York band with gothic/shoegaze overtones returns with album number two, which tones down the volume slightly and puts more focus on songwriting.

title: Losing Feeling
description: Returning to EPs after their incredible first proper LP, No Age inject more tension and shimmering guitars into their already excellent punk rock.

title: Love 2
description: The Gallic duo aim to dust off the disappointment of Pocket Symphony with their first LP to be written and recorded without a major outside producer.

title: There Is No Enemy
description: Built to Spill arrest their 2000s slide with the unexpected There Is No Enemy, their best album in years.

title: A Strange Arrangement
description: Stones Throw's one-man soul band is almost too sweet for his own good.

title: Threats/Worship
description: Latest from a Toronto band so easy to love they've been released by both the anti-corporate people at Constellation and the trendspotters at Vice.

title: I and Love and You
description: One of the biggest grassroots success stories of the decade makes their well-deserved, Rick Rubin-assisted major-label bow.

title: My Weakness Is Strong
description: Patton Oswalt is now more mature and even grown-up, but everything that makes him the funniest stand-up around is still in place on his new album.

title: Hello Nasty [Deluxe Edition]
description: With 43 tracks spread over two discs, the latest deluxe version from the Beasties catalog suffers from some of the same lack of editing as the original did.

title: Threadbare
description: Like the progeny of California's new folkies and Arcade Fire's euphorics, Port O'Brien still hew to an acoustic guitar/secular spiritual awakening formula.

title: Born Again Revisited
description: Matador band's highest-fidelity album to date, an intentional playing down of the things that made them among lo-fi's leading lights.

title: Milwaukee at Last!!!
description: His second live album, but first covering his own material, this CD/DVD set finds Rufus Wainwright playing the role he was born to play: himself.

title: Man on the Moon: The End of Day
description: After co-writing several tracks with Kanye West and hits with Crookers, Kid Cudi releases his long-awaited debut album.

title: White Lunar
description: Nick Cave and Dirty Three/Bad Seeds member Warren Ellis collect two discs of soundtrack work, including pieces from the new adaptation of The Road.

title: LOVEWORLD
description: U.S.E. finally follow its debut with another LP of post-Daft Punk house music, twee indie rock, and a sort of "Sesame Street"-esque funk.

title: Bright Penny
description: Chicago's hard-luck cult artist finally offers his third album, 11 years after debuting with the exquisite, underrated More You Becomes You.

title: The Spoils
description: Their gothy sound is reminiscent of Siouxsie and the Banshees and Cabaret Voltaire, but on their first proper full-length Zola Jesus show a distinctive voice.

title: All My Friends Are Funeral Singers
description: The remarkably consistent band continues its strong run here, with another album of fine songs that combine earthy instrumentation and artful noise.

title: Seek Magic
description: Producer Dayve Hawk, who has created dreamy electro soundscapes as Memory Cassette, Weird Tapes, and Memory Tapes, arrives with a striking new album.

title: Manafon
description: Former Japan leader strengthens his ties to modern avant-garde, be it jazz, electro-acoustic improvisation, post-glitch electronics, or modern composition.

title: Sing Along to Songs You Don't Know
description: Icelandic band remains pretty obsessed with the kind of childlike innocence that attracts or repels people with equal fervor.

title: I Am the Cosmos [Deluxe Edition]
description: This set from Rhino Handmade augments the former Big Star member's posthumous collection of solo material with an extra disc of alternate versions and mixes.

title: The Sound the Speed the Light
description: The most industrious of their three post-reunion albums, The Sound's songs are so signature-styled you might wonder if you've heard them before.

title: 45:33 Remixes
description: James Murphy's contribution to Nike's intermittent series of one-artist mixes designed for exercise gets a belated remix treatment.

title: Columbus'd the Whim
description: With a name like Holiday Shores, you'd guess this Florida group is part of 2009's fuzzed-out, beach-party vibe. You'd be right.

title: Fool's Gold
description: Foreign Born's Lewis Pesacov has been filtering African music into his songs for ages, but his new project will still attract Vampire Weekend comparisons.

title: Where Were You When It Happened?
description: Grittier than Drag City debut Body Language, the latest from this Israeli band connects the Stooges' pre-punk blues to Mudhoney's grunge.

title: Vapours
description: After the relative darkness of Arm's Way, Islands welcomes back original member Jamie Thompson and makes a welcome return to the sound of their debut.

title: The Sun Came Out
description: Crowded House's Neil Finn leads a number of artists-- members of Radiohead and Wilco, Johnny Marr, and Lisa Germano-- on this ambitious 2xCD project.

title: White Clouds Drift On and On
description: Typically working with dub and ambient music as Bvdub, here Van Wey ditches drums and bass for a full-on, immersive Gas-inspired experience.

title: Through the Devil Softly
description: Former Mazzy Star singer keeps the aesthetic of her former band very much alive on this collaboration with My Bloody Valentine drummer Colm Ó Cíosóig.

artist: The Pains of Being Pure at Heart
title: Higher Than the Stars EP
description: Highlighting the bookish indie pop at their core, this Pains EP still sounds classic and timeless, even if it's more Field Mice than Shop Assistants.

title: Eskimo Snow
description: After the vulnerable masterstroke Alopecia, WHY? unleash a record that's darker in content but often gorgeous in sound.

title: Album
description: Girls have been the subject of a steadily building buzz based on some excellent singles, and they deliver on that promise here in a big way.

title: Colonial Drones
description: Still taking cues from both 1990s lo-fi and ambitious 2000s indie, Hallelujah the Hills continue to expand and improve their sound.

title: Expressions
description: The debut from this Secretly Canadian band is an obvious homage to ABBA, the Carpenters, ELO, and other purveyors of the unironic, sugary pop of 1970s radio.

title: Us
description: What comes across as moralistic sermonizing from lesser MCs here is the work of a rapper with a humane, often-troubled conscience.

title: Forget the Night Ahead
description: Evocative, emo-ish lyrics and Kevin Shields-by-way-of-Thurston Moore torrents of noise once again color the work of this Scottish band.

title: Unmap
description: Justin Vernon of Bon Iver teams up with the post-rock outfit Collections of Colonies of Bees for a loose, weird, and rewarding album.

title: Origin: Orphan
description: Joel Gibb makes his "mature" album, trading the joyful glee of past Hidden Cameras work for increased gravity and seriousness.

title: 69: The Legendary Adventures of a Filter King
description: Detroit techno legend collects lesser-known older material originally created under his 69 moniker, reissuing it as a vinyl-only, 5x12" release.

title: Year in the Kingdom
description: The newest Fleet Foxes member has been crafting hushed folk for years, and he stays prolific as a solo artist with this, his second LP of the year.

title: Between My Head and the Sky
description: The new Plastic Ono Band stays true to the original's friends-and-family vibe, recruiting Sean Lennon, Cibo Matto's Yuka Honda, and Cornelius.

title: Monsters of Folk
description: Bright Eyes’ Conor Oberst, My Morning Jacket’s Jim James, M. Ward, and Saddle Creek’s Mike Mogis create a folk-pop supergroup, our era’s Traveling Wilburys.

title: Marlone
description: Operating with one foot in the avant-garde and the other in the structural, this Kranky band hews closer to Deerhunter or Low than that label's dronier artists.

title: Texas Rose, the Thaw, and the Beasts
description: Raymond Raposa's ramshackle folk and pitch-dark music would sound at home in either a Village coffee shop or a roadhouse.

title: Truelove's Gutter
description: A few years after the outstanding Coles Corner, former Pulp touring member continues his atmospheric, nostalgic work as a singer-songwriter.

title: Live From Home
description: Another in a line of 1990s stalwarts making their recent comeback, these D.C. art-rockers document their 2008 reunion tour on this live disc.

title: Backspacer
description: Former "biggest band on the planet" continues its yeoman's work, making anonymously dependable riff-rock for those who want that sort of thing.

title: DIA
description: Damon McMahon's Locust release recalls other claustrophobic, inner-space travelers like Syd Barrett, Roky Erickson, and Skip Spence.

title: Crayon Angel: A Tribute to the Music of Judee Sill
description: Cult folk artist Judee Sill gets a tribute with contributions from Bill Callahan, Grizzly Bear's Daniel Rossen, Beth Orton, Marissa Nadler, and more.

title: Two Sunsets
description: Scottish indie pop legends team with Japanese duo Tenniscoats to record their first non-soundtrack studio album in 12 years.

title: Central Market
description: In his first post-Mirrored release, the Battles leader enlists the Wordless Music Orchestra to craft a record of ambitious modern classical music.

title: Rain Machine
description: TV on the Radio guitarist/singer Kyp Malone subverts expectations on this solo project, creating both gentle, atmospheric detours and kinetic drama.

title: La Roux
description: This record of unapologetically derivative 80s synth-pop is already a sensation in the UK, boasting a pair of hit singles.

title: Keep an Eye on the Sky
description: Combining studio tracks, live cuts, demos, and unreleased recordings, Rhino' 4xCD compilation is the reissue that finally gets Big Star right.

title: Time to Die
description: Like many ambitious indie bands before them, the Dodos enlist producer Phil Ek to help craft their rise to indie fame.

title: Kamaal the Abstract
description: Q-Tip's long-delayed experimental album, cut at the beginning of the decade with contributions from jazz musicians, is finally given a proper release.

title: The Visitor
description: After years of foregoing recorded music for other pursuits, Jim O'Rourke makes a brilliant return with a subtly complex 38-minute piece of orchestral pop.

title: Black Telephone of Matter
description: Like Kreng before him, Pan Sonic's Mika Vainio is making dark, compelling, almost frightening music.

title: Brooklynati
description: This indie hip-hop group has been lauded as a flamekeeper for a certain time in the early 1990s when the Native Tongues held down New York.

title: So Tough / Sound of Water
description: The expanded 2xCD reissues of the St. Etienne catalogue continue with 1993's terrific So Tough and 2000's Sound of Water.

title: A Brief History of Love
description: A study in the enormity of sound, the debut from this arena-ready UK band delivers on the promise of its early singles.

title: Only Built 4 Cuban Linx... Pt. II
description: The Wu-Tang Clan member's long-awaited sequel to his 1995 classic is finally here, and yes, it's as good as fans have been hoping for.

title: Inglourious Basterds OST
description: Quentin Tarantino's first period piece largely ignores cratedigging pop, rock, and soul, instead offering forgotten B-movie cues or clever cinematic in-jokes.

title: God Is Good
description: Grails' Emil Amos joins Om's former Sleep member Al Cisneros and, despite some fears that he'd busy their sound, he fits right in.

title: The Miseducation of Freddie Gibbs / Midwestgangstaboxframecadillacmuzik
description: With an armful of new Just Blaze and Polow da Don beats, this Gary, Ind., MC and ex-Interscope signee is breathing fresh air into hardscrabble mixtape rap.

title: Life of Leisure EP
description: Highly promising young songwriter continues to show why he's one of chillwave's rising stars.

title: Tribute To
description: My Morning Jacket's Jim James pays tribute to the late George Harrison on this mostly solo acoustic journey through a half-dozen of the quiet Beatle's songs.

title: Hey Friend, What You Doing?
description: We might be getting close to some kind of lo-fi tipping point here, folks.

title: The Broad Street Bully
description: After the demise of Roc-A-Fella, Beanie unearths a collection of "lost" tracks for a free mixtape that doubles as his best work since The B.Coming.

title: Ashes Grammar
description: Philly septet continues its winning streak on this sprawling and ambitious affair, masterfully puzzled together from a wide range of parts.

title: The Resistance
description: Muse are back, with an LP of all-caps, no half-stepping ART-ROCK that closes with a three-part epic so shameless about its size it's billed as a "Symphony."

title: The Velvet Underground & Nico
description: Making great use of his home studio and L.A. friends, Beck kicks off his off-the-cuff, unrehearsed covers of full LPs by taking on VU's debut.

title: Orange You Glad
description: Chillwave fixture releases an album of airy electronics, late-1960s psychedelia, and slow-burn rhythms.

title: Out Into the Snow
description: Like a modern-day Leonard Cohen, Simon Joyner's poetic lyrics and beaten-down vocals gesture as much to characters or melodies as they do articulate them.

title: The Almighty Defenders
description: Black Lips, King Khan, and Mark Sultan spent a week crafting this record in Berlin. And it sounds like it.

title: Crazy Rhythms / The Good Earth
description: Three-chord punk boiled down to two-chord devotionals, these two amazing Feelies records are back, and both are worth a lot of your time.

title: The Blueprint 3
description: More Blueprint 2 than Blueprint, Jay-Z's latest is actually closer to Kingdom Come than either of those others. Unfortunately.

title: Heartbeat Radio
description: Again paying close attention to arrangements and general songcraft, the Norwegian transplant reinforces his pleasant earnestness.

title: Mister Pop
description: The Kiwi Pop giants and lo-fi all-stars return with, incredibly, only the fifth LP in their storied career.

title: Masters of the Burial
description: Stars and Broken Social Scene singer steps out for her second woodsy solo album.

title: Break Up
description: Continuing her high-wire act of a musical career, ScarJo follows her trip into the Tom Waits songbook with an album inspired by 1960s Gainsbourg/Bardot duets.

title: The Stone Roses
description: A badly needed remaster of this landmark LP sounds even fresher than it did 20 years ago-- and thanks to Sony there are now loads of expensive ways to hear it.

title: Past Masters
description: For the first time, the singles/EPs/leftovers compilations Past Masters are combined and sold in one glorious package.

title: Let It Be
description: After the discord of The Beatles, the group sought to get back to basics with a rock LP and a film about its creation. This was the eventual result.

title: Abbey Road
description: The perfect ending to a recording career, this LP shows a band still in its prime, capable of songwriting and recording feats others could only envy.

title: Yellow Submarine
description: The only minor album in the Beatles' catalogue is this soundtrack to a feature-length cartoon, a project with which the Beatles had little involvement.

title: The Beatles
description: Indulgent, sprawling, overflowing with ideas and excess, the White Album became not only a monument to unbridled creativity but a rock archetype.

title: Rock Band
description: Harmonix updates the hugely popular video game for the Beatles-- 45 songs from across their career are represented-- and gives it a markedly different vibe.

title: Magical Mystery Tour
description: The only American release to become part of the Beatles' canon, Magical Mystery Tour combines a soundtrack EP and some brilliant singles.

title: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
description: Though it has perhaps slipped in estimation since its initial issue, the 1967 release that defined the LP format still packs surprises.

title: Revolver
description: As they devoted more time to the studio, the Beatles' individual voices and confidence continued to grow, resulting in the sonic landmark Revolver.

title: Rubber Soul
description: The Beatles' first undisputed masterpiece is their quietest and most folky record, reflecting the influences of contemporaries like Dylan and the Byrds.

title: Help!
description: The Help! soundtrack album is as haphazard as Beatles For Sale, but it lacks that record's glowering intensity; it's a great but confusing record.

title: Beatles For Sale
description: The angriest, most aggressive record in the Beatles catalogue, For Sale finds them reaching back to their Hamburg club days in both attitude and sound.

title: A Hard Day's Night
description: A Hard Day's Night is from an era when pop and showbiz were inseparable-- and if it doesn't transcend that time, it does represent its definitive peak.

title: With the Beatles
description: Released just before eventual U.S. gamechanger "I Want to Hold Your Hand", this quickie sequel doesn't match its predecessor but doesn't cheat fans either.

title: Please Please Me
description: A raw, high-energy run-through of their early live set, the Beatles' debut is also the sound of rock'n'roll finding a suddenly large, new audience.

title: Stereo Box / In Mono
description: In 1987, the Beatles' albums appeared on compact disc for the first time. Considering how much music had already found its way to CD, the Beatles were very late, so the digital rollout was a big deal. The new issues came out in batches and the excitement steadily built, peaking when *Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band* came out on June 1, 1987, the 20th anniversary of its original release ("It was 20 years ago today..." was perhaps the greatest record marketing hook of all time.) In the 22 years since, plenty of bands have had their catalogues reissued a

title: The Entrance Band
description: Guy Blakeslee recruits a rhythm section à la the Jimi Hendrix Experience and adds "Band" to the name of his Entrance project.

title: The Sub Pop Years
description: Galaxie 500's rhythm section went on to make some subtly powerful albums, and this comp draws from their output on Sub Pop between 1995 and 2002.

title: No More Stories Are Told Today...
description: Danish prog-pop maestros, here sporting an absurdly long album title, consolidate everything that's made them interesting to date.

title: Sidetracked
description: Hercules and Love Affair's first commercial mix affords Andy Butler the opportunity to step outside the confines of his group and straight-up DJ.

title: East of Eden
description: The former Concretes singer travels to Pakistan to record her second TbT album. Studio's Dan Lissvik produces; Panda Bear guests.

title: After Robots
description: Pushing against a mountain of hype, BLK JKS' debut LP is hugely ambitious, with a bigness of sound that's hard to approximate and control.

title: Intuit
description: Brent Knopf of Menomena and a huge cast of his friends get together to create a record full of meticulous attention to sonic and compositional details.

title: Temporary Pleasure
description: A grab bag of styles, SMD's latest features Hot Chip's Alexis Taylor, SFA's Gruff Rhys, Jamie Lidell, Beth Ditto, and Yeasayer's Chris Keating.

title: Signal Morning
description: Olivia Tremor Control ringleader Will Cullen Hart and his Circulatory System return after a lengthy absence with their highly anticipated sophomore album.

title: Diary / LP2
description: A template for both emo and modern rock, Sunny Day's original lineup has its two records reissued, with bonus cuts, and they deserve reassessment.

title: Fervency
description: Following in the shadow of William Basinski and Stars of the Lid, this NYC drone artist works in self-effacing quietude, crafting patient, conceptual works.

title: Welcome Joy
description: Pretty Girls Make Graves' Derek Fudesco returns to lead his fellow Pac NWesterners on their second LP of ultracasual back-porch folk music.

title: As Good as Gone
description: After dabbling in electronic ambience, heavy-beat IDM, and fractured funk, this Kranky band has hit upon a winning combination of sounds.

title: Haih or Amortecedor
description: Tropicália legends unite for their first studio album in 35 years, which includes songwriting contributions from Jorge Ben and Tom Zé.

title: Everything Goes Wrong
description: Facing the prospect of following a hyped debut and the backlash against shitgaze in general, Vivian Girls issue their second album.

title: Songs for the New Industrial State
description: A strange record from the early 1970s is reissued, and it combines adult-aimed light music and California pop-psych with anti-consumerist social commentary.

title: Alice and Friends
description: No, they're not named after the Pavement tune; though they are noisy and lo-fi, Box Elders are more enamored of 1960s garage rock touchstones.

title: Red
description: Norwegian dance-rockers return with a collection of songs boiled down to more pop-friendly lengths and their goofy humor still intact.

title: In Prism
description: Math-rock band returns after 11 years with not just a good reunion album, but also the most immediately satisfying record in their entire catalogue.

title: Popular Songs
description: The indie rock perennials return with yet another accomplished album, again reminding us why they're among the most consistently rewarding bands of our time.

title: One Foot Ahead of the Other
description: Dubstep star follows his excellent rave-tinged LP Where Were U in 92? with an EP that veers closer to the kaleidoscopic melodies of his singles.

title: Disconnected
description: Justin Broadrick of Jesu (among others) and Aaron Turner of Isis team up for a record that the former says taps into his aggressive side.

title: Get Color
description: HEALTH follow their apocalyptic debut, arguably better remix album, and thrashing, industrial-disco single "Die Slow" with LP No. 2.

title: The Fine Print (A Collection Of Oddities and Rarities 2003-2008)
description: The Southern rock band culls through its recent archives and compiles a dozen rarities on this odds'n'sods collection.

title: Two Dancers
description: UK quartet follows 2008's fidgety, impulsive baroque-rock debut, Limbo, Panto, with an album that refashions them as a steely art-funk outfit.

title: Quest For Fire
description: Finally available in the U.S., via Tee Pee, this Toronto metal band offers distended riffs, patient drumming, and subtle textures.

title: A Slave's Commitment
description: One of dance's hip young gunslingers, 21-year-old, Amsterdam-based Pascal Terstappen, issues his debut LP on the venerable Traum label.

title: City Limits Volume 1
description: London-based dubstep producer blends jazzy sophistication with the archetypal shuddering bass wobbles on this excellent collection.

title: #1 Hits Explosion
description: This best-of shaves away some of the small gestures that have made the Apples a favorite, but retains their power as a modern pop band.

title: xx
description: Young UK band influenced by modern R&B lands on the scene with a terrific debut, filled with seductive songs set to spare but effective arrangements.

title: Anti-Magic
description: No Age-associated drum'n'vocal band tests listener endurance on its latest collection of loud, spastic, and often complicated music.

title: L'Autopsie Phénoménale de Dieu
description: The latest majestically bleak ambient classical release from Norwegian label Miasmah Records, this LP helps make the world a slightly darker, lonelier place.

title: To Swift Mars
description: Aloha member comes across as a thoughtful, subtly clever musician with an ear for low-key melodies and a mind for cerebral indie rock poetry.

title: My Guilty Pleasure
description: Mysterious Italo-disco singer returns with the follow-up to the exquisite isolation of her debut, Disco Romance.

title: Hail to the Thief: Special Collectors Edition
description: After four LPs that pushed the boundaries of what's expected from a rock band, Radiohead internalized leftfield electronics yet embraced straightforward rock.

title: Wave If You're Really There
description: Like Devo or Hot Chip before them, this Liverpool band aims for nerdy electro-pop and tidy funk on its debut LP.

title: Tummaa
description: Sasu Ripatti returns under his clicks'n'cuts-gone-ambient name for a new album of loops, thwacks, and other micro-sounds.

title: Love Comes Close
description: Moody synth-poppers from Philly, whose contributors include members of Xiu Xiu and Prurient, make an impressive full-length debut.

title: Walking on a Wire: Richard Thompson (1968-2009)
description: 4xCD retrospective of cult-favorite British singer/guitarist's work is the closest thing to the career-spanning greatest-hits album he deserves.

title: Amnesiac: Special Collectors Edition
description: Met with confusion back in 2001, just nine months after the landmark Kid A, Amnesiac can take its rightful place among Radiohead's classics.

title: Posthumous Success
description: The North Dakota troubadour draws from Woody Guthrie's folk wanderlust, Cole Porter's cosmopolitanism, and Jeff Buckley's arty otherworldliness.

title: Infidel
description: Thrash metal veterans return during their sound's revival with a record that feels both retro and contemporary.

title: Awe Owe
description: Guillermo Scott Herren collaborator's project is similarly enamored of Latin American psych-folk, scratchy beats, and warm, homemade production.

title: Cartography
description: The adventurous trumpet player, best known for his work with Supersilent and his solo records on Rune Grammofon, makes a terrific debut for ECM.

title: Kid A: Special Collectors Edition
description: Capitol follows its excavation of Radiohead's 1990s work with new version of the band's first three 2000s LPs, including the landmark Kid A.

title: Conditions
description: Australian band with radio-friendly ambitions follows its "Sweet Disposition" single with a record that shoots for the heights of the Arctic Monkeys or U2.

title: If You Know What's Good for Ya!!
description: DFA partner Rong Music collects this electro-pop artist's post-2005 singles and pairs them with fresh material.

title: Slaughterhouse
description: Hip-hop supergroup (Crooked I, Joell Ortiz, Royce Da 5'9", and Joe Budden) is united by little more than shared failures and a love of bareknuckle rhyming.

title: Landscapes
description: Latest album from the one-man psychedelic pop project of Matthew Mondanile, guitarist for North Jersey up-and-comers Real Estate.

title: Humbug
description: The Arctics expand their sound with the help of producer Josh Homme (QOTSA) on this, their relatively relaxed, confident third album.

title: The Phenomenal Handclap Band
description: New York-area band, joined by guests from TV on the Radio and the Dap-Kings among others, concoct slightly spacy live-band psych-disco.

title: Hard Knox or, "Are You Sure Hank Jr. Done It This Way?" / Born Bad
description: James Jackson Toth (Wooden Wand) continues to be both prolific and promising, with a recent collection of old home demos and a new LP for Ecstatic Peace.

title: Snow Blindness Is Crystal Antz
description: Indie rock Renaissance man Chad VanGaalen offers a collection of 19 electronics-heavy instrumentals that allow him to stretch out and experiment.

title: Ze 30: Ze Records Story 1979-2009
description: The adventurous New York label that helped to define the sound of early-1980s left-field dance music celebrates its 30th with a comp.

title: Wind's Poem
description: Phil Elverum returns with the latest piece in the epic, ongoing existential puzzle he's been constructing for nearly 15 years.

title: Season Dreaming
description: This Florida psych-pop duo's debut owes just about everything to Animal Collective.

title: Lungs
description: Unlike fellow quirky UK songstresses La Roux and Little Boots, Florence Welch moves away from the Lily/Amy template by building her career from the bottom up.

title: We Gave It All Away, Now We Are Taking It Back
description: Maximalist dance duo collect its remixes on a gargantuan 2xCD remix compilation that reveals the group's eclectic nature and considerable talents.

title: I Love You
description: Lady Gaga minus the tunes, ambition, or sense of purpose.

title: Total 10
description: The seminal label celebrates its 10th year with a new Total comp, featuring the Field, Reinhard Voigt, Ada, Gui Boratto, DJ Koze, and Justus Köhncke.

title: Arrivals
description: Leeds duo moves away from its IDM-bolstered post-rock to something more compelling, like Burial for English-lit majors.

title: Silk Flowers
description: This charismatic Brooklyn trio sounds less like a Xerox of classic artists Suicide, Cabaret Voltaire, or PiL and more like one of their minor contemporaries.

title: Fear of Song
description: The former Low bassist issues a new record financed in part by his eBay sales of his ex-band's album art.

title: Memoirs at the End of the World
description: After a delightful debut and a covers album, the Postmarks ramp up their sound on this collection of Mancini/Morricone/John Barry-literate indie pop.

title: Watch Me Fall
description: After two singles comps, the Memphis punk makes his Matador studio LP debut and continues to embrace infectious Kiwi pop as well as 60s garage rock.

title: Destination Tokyo
description: On this Smalltown Supersound EP, Tokyo's Nisennenmondai move past post-punk talking points and pay more attention to their songs.

title: Clubroot
description: The next big dubstep album comes not from the big-name 12" producers around, but this veteran producer with roots in drum'n'bass.

title: Creaturesque
description: After a promising start, TMTS are still struggling to shake a few influences while picking up a few familiar moves from others.

title: Live at the Folklore Center, NYC - March 6th, 1967
description: Recorded when he was just 20, this CD finds the L.A. singer invading the NYC folk scene and exploring jazz, raga, psychedelia, rock, and even schmaltz.

title: Solo Electric Bass 1
description: Tom Jenkinson returns to his "classic" sound, albeit with a twist-- this is a live, solo performance recorded in Paris.

title: Pop Psychology
description: Canadian singer-songwriter offers a self-deprecating look at navigating the crumbling music industry.

title: My Old, Familiar Friend
description: The other Raconteurs singer-songwriter returns with his first solo album in the spotlight enjoyed as an occassional musical partner of Jack White.

title: Luminous Night
description: Latest from the prolific and influential avant-folk artist is something of a summary record, demonstrating most of the range he's shown over the years.

title: King of Jeans
description: Latest from Pennsylvania scuzz-punk revivalists consolidates their strengths, harnessing their fire-extinguisher splatter into shake-appealing rock action.

title: Bay of Pigs EP
description: The rumors were true: Dan Bejar's new two-song EP is boosted by a 13-minute-long slab of ambient disco, complete with footnote-worthy lyrics.

title: The Future's Looking Grim
description: Latest from Chicago MC/producer team finds them coming closer to capturing the charm of their live show.

title: Physical Changes
description: Despite spending time with Pele, Collections of Colonies of Bees, and Volcano Choir, uncompromising percussionist Jon Mueller is arguably best on his own.

title: Dark Rift
description: On his proper full-length debut, Denver's Travis Egedy combines samples and an ear for the best parts of dance pop from an earlier era.

title: The Smith Westerns
